cards.title: Open dimension algebra to user-declared dimensions
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F1 (top-ranked). PHYSICAL_DIMENSIONS is a closed 5-row [i32;3] table (Syntax.rs:261-267); a user #UnitFamily(Mass) gets no algebra — kg * meter is plain E0109 while meter / second derives Speed (live probe). SI needs 7 base dimensions; real programs need domain axes. Fix: families opt in to minting a dimension; exponent vectors become open-length over declared bases; the 5 built-ins become prelude declarations. Pay-up-front: generalize the vector representation before it is serialized into unit facts and snapshots. Ballot D-DIMENSION-OPEN1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-DIMENSION-OPEN1=D — open dimensions plus a full SI prelude written in ordinary Jet, with no compiler table. Derived-name spelling pending D-DERIVED-DIMENSION-CLAIM1 (owner leans A; question q0w4b9xl answered 2026-07-30 — see ballot explainer).

Precision and speed law (answers q0w4b9xl): a derived family's base member is coherent — exactly 1 of the product of its base dimensions' base units (1 newton = 1 kg*m/s/s). Every other unit of a dimension is an exact arbitrary-precision rational scale from that anchor (D-QUANTITY-DECL1). No pairwise conversion tables: any conversion is one ratio of two exact rationals folded at compile time; implicit conversion only when exact, lossy conversion only through the explicit rounded form (D-UNIT-CONV1) — at most one rounding, only on request. Units erase after sema; a conversion is one runtime multiply (plus one add for affine), same-unit math costs zero.

1. Replace the closed PHYSICAL_DIMENSIONS [i32;3] table at Syntax.rs:261-267 with an open exponent map keyed by declared base dimensions. Do this before unit facts and snapshots serialize the old shape; that is the pay-up-front reason this ranked first.
2. Let a #UnitFamily opt into minting a dimension, so a user axis takes part in the same algebra as the built-ins.
3. Move the five built-in dimensions out of the compiler and into prelude declarations, written in the exact surface a user gets.
4. Ship the full default battery in the prelude, all with exact rational scales: all 7 SI base dimensions (Length, Mass, Time, Current, Temperature, AmountOfSubstance, LuminousIntensity); all 22 SI named derived units (hertz, newton, pascal, joule, watt, coulomb, volt, farad, ohm, siemens, weber, tesla, henry, lumen, lux, becquerel, gray, sievert, katal, radian, steradian, degree Celsius); the SI prefix ladder; accepted non-SI units (litre, tonne, minute, hour, day, degree/arcmin/arcsec, electronvolt, dalton, astronomical unit, bar, mmHg); customary units with exact defined scales (inch, foot, yard, mile, ounce, pound, pound-force, psi, gallon, mph). Electronics coverage is mandatory: ampere base; volt/ohm/farad/henry/siemens/weber/tesla/coulomb coherent derived.
5. Nominal sharing then only ever applies to third-party dimensions, because the standard ones live in one shared prelude. State that in the spec entry.
6. Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle.rs, the quantity and unit checking in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/, the prelude source under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/, examples/features/types/.

Proof: targeted tests showing a user #UnitFamily(Mass) takes part in multiplication and division; kg times meter now types; meter over second still derives Speed; an SI derived unit from the prelude checks end to end; 4newton == 4kg*1m/1s/1s type-identity test; pound-force to newton converts by the exact defined ratio with no drift; a lossy conversion is a compile error naming the rounded fix; example golden; independent review closes.

questions.text: Why not b + a? Then we can define all units as part of jet with high precision, so scientists, researchers, students, engineers, physicists, etc. can all do everything out of the box with no hassle, jumping right into calculations, simulation, modeling, etc. But then its's open for them to use custom units. Remember, batteries included magic out of the box is perspective one, perspective two is full expert control. It would be silly to require people to define standard units, we can do that up front, so someone can just jump right into jet and start getting accurate, convenient sim & modeling -> beating stuff like python & matlab
questions.answer: Agreed — and A already contains the seed of B: it turns the five built-ins into ordinary prelude declarations of the same mechanism users get. Your refinement finishes that prelude: ship all seven SI base dimensions plus the standard derived units (newton, joule, watt, pascal, hertz, volt, ...) with high-precision scale factors, written in Jet itself. Perspective one: unit-safe physics, engineering, and simulation work with zero declarations out of the box — ahead of Python-with-pint and MATLAB on day one. Perspective two: your own axes (tokens per second, pixels per point, dollars per hour) are one #UnitFamily(..., dimension) away, and the built-ins are readable prelude source, not compiler magic. The nominal-sharing rule then only ever bites third-party dimensions, since the standard ones ship once in the shared prelude. I added option D — the open mechanism from A plus full-SI batteries in the prelude (B's content without B's closed table) — and moved the recommendation to it.

questions.text: Conceptually I think I like A the most, but it isnt clear to me how this would work with different types of units. Like if we wanted to use measurements that compared pounds force to newtons or speed, but then if you dont have all the conversions directly and precisely then values could be off. We want extreme precision where possible while keeping exceptional speed. REMEMBER, BY DEFAULT WE NEED TO SUPPORT EVERY SINGLE UNIT OF MEASURE THAT IS STANDARD, including support for things like electronics with voltage, amperage, inductance, impedence, resistance, force, pressure, etc. EVERYTHING that would be a standard tool in the domain of ANY scientist, researcher, engineer, mathemetiian, or analyst
questions.answer: A handles mixed units through one coherent anchor, never pairwise conversion tables. A derived family's base member is pinned coherent: exactly 1 of the product of its base dimensions' base units, so 1 newton = 1 kg*m/s/s by construction. Every other unit of that dimension — kilonewton, pound-force, psi — is an exact arbitrary-precision rational scale from that anchor. Pound-force is exact, not approximate: the pound (0.45359237 kg) and standard gravity (9.80665 m/s^2) are exact by international definition, so 1 lbf = 4.4482216152605 N exactly. Nearly every standard unit has such an exact SI definition. PRECISION: any conversion is one ratio of two exact rationals, folded at compile time (already ratified in D-QUANTITY-DECL1); implicit conversion happens only when exact, and lossy conversion requires the explicit rounded form (D-UNIT-CONV1) — so a value rounds at most once, and only when you ask. SPEED: units erase after sema; a conversion is one runtime multiply (plus one add for affine units like celsius) against a compile-time constant, and same-unit math costs zero. COVERAGE: the ratified D-DIMENSION-OPEN1=D prelude ships every standard unit by default — all 7 SI base dimensions; all 22 SI named derived units (hertz, newton, pascal, joule, watt, coulomb, volt, farad, ohm, siemens, weber, tesla, henry, lumen, lux, becquerel, gray, sievert, katal, radian, steradian, degree Celsius); the SI prefix ladder; accepted non-SI units (litre, tonne, minute/hour/day, degree, electronvolt, dalton, astronomical unit, bar, mmHg); and customary units with exact defined scales (inch, foot, yard, mile, ounce, pound, pound-force, psi, gallon, mph). Electronics is fully covered: ampere is a base dimension, and volt/ohm/farad/henry/siemens/weber/tesla/coulomb are coherent derived families. Ballot updated: option A now states the coherent-anchor rule and shows pound-force as an exact scaled member; the explainer carries the precision/speed/coverage model; the card plan enumerates the full default battery.

cards.title: Marker argument types become real prelude enums
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F2. Policy::APPLIED_RULES types every #Rule signature over 14 parameter types (TaintKind, ObligationMode, InlineMode, Maturity, Layout, Target, ABI, FfiLanguage, NamingCase, PolicySetting...) that no user can name; E0930 renders them in type syntax; TypeInfo.markers is strings. Fix: declare them as ordinary enums in a reserved prelude namespace, generated from the registry with a drift-guard test; diagnostics, jet explain, LSP, and TypeInfo read the same declarations. No S26 contact — marker args are already comptime-evaluated values. Ballot D-RULEARG-TYPES1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-RULEARG-TYPES1=A — the fourteen marker argument types become ordinary enums in a reserved prelude namespace, generated from the registry.

Open gate: the namespace name. The ratified ballot calls `core.lang` a working name, and I7 makes the path a user-typeable surface. D-LANGNS-NAME1 is on this card for that pick. Everything below is ready to build the moment the name is chosen.

1. Generate the enum declarations from the `Policy::APPLIED_RULES` signatures: TaintKind, ObligationMode, InlineMode, Maturity, Layout, Target, ABI, FfiLanguage, NamingCase, PolicySetting and the rest.
2. Add the drift-guard test so the generated declarations and the registry cannot fall out of step.
3. Point every reader at those declarations: E0930 and its siblings, `jet explain`, LSP hovers and completion, and the docs.
4. Dot-literals such as `.Track` resolve by the normal expected-type rule, so a marker argument needs no import.
5. Upgrade `TypeInfo.markers` from marker-name strings to typed argument records. Keep the string form during this epoch for compatibility.
6. No new type category. Marker arguments are already comptime-evaluated values, so S26 is untouched.
7. Syntax chores: I7 rows for the namespace path and the generated enum names, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation Policy registry, the generated prelude module, crates/jet-sema (resolution and E0930), Comptime/Reflect.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, tests/ui, docs/spec/.

Proof: the drift-guard test fails when a registry signature changes without a regenerate; a targeted test naming a marker argument type in ordinary code; hover and explain read the declaration; reflection returns a typed argument record; independent review closes.

cards.title: One fact model behind tags, states, taint kinds, effect leaves
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F3. Four mechanisms spell one behavior (erased named facts with set/tree matching): tag, state, taint kinds, effect leaves. D-EFFTREE1 already reuses D-TAG1's subtree matching for effects. Fix layer 1 (ships regardless): one internal fact registry, one subsumption algorithm, one TypeInfo reflection surface. Fix layer 2 (owner picks): (a) facts are comptime-consumed enum declarations reusing D-TAG1 machinery, (b) tree-bodied tags (amends D-QUAL2 'exactly two qualifier kinds'), or (c) internal-only. User taint kinds stay gated on deferred IFC. Ballot D-FACTMODEL1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-FACTMODEL1=A — facts are enums. Four mechanisms spell one behaviour today: tag, state, taint kinds, and effect leaves.

Layer 1 ships regardless of surface:
1. One internal fact registry behind all four.
2. One subsumption algorithm. D-EFFTREE1 already reuses D-TAG1 subtree matching for effects, so there is one algorithm to keep.
3. One TypeInfo reflection surface for facts.

Layer 2 is the ratified surface:
4. States, taint kinds, and declared effect leaves become enum declarations that markers consume at compile time. Enum groups already give trees, subtree matching, exhaustiveness, and payloads, so facts reuse all of it.
5. `#State`, `#Transition`, `#Tainted`, and `#Caps` argument positions resolve against those enum declarations.
6. Amend the S26-adjacent spec text explicitly: facts classify values and erase; they never select types and never drive dispatch.
7. The `tag` keyword stays for flat one-off qualifiers, or retires into the same story once card #1295 lands its surface.

User taint kinds stay gated on the deferred IFC decision. A kind with no sink checks nothing, so do not open that door here.

Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

Owned paths: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/State.rs, the taint and effects checkers, crates/jet-foundation/src/Traits.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, Comptime/Reflect.rs, docs/spec/.

Proof: targeted tests proving one subsumption path serves tags, states, and effect leaves; a reflection test reading facts through TypeInfo; every existing tag, state, taint, and effect test still passes; independent review closes.

cards.title: Unified tags: checking behavior chosen in the declaration
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F4b, generalized by owner question q8jh0b7a: tags and taints are two polarities of one erased-fact mechanism. New ballot D-TAG-UNIFY1 decides whether each tag declares its own checking mode — plain (documentation), strict (positive fact, blessed in via #Blesses), taint (negative fact, spreads by dataflow, blocked at sinks, sanitized out via #Sanitizer) — with built-in taint kinds respelled as prelude taint-mode tags. Supersedes ballot D-TAG-STRICT1 (deleted; strict is now one mode of the unified mechanism). Builds on ratified D-FACTMODEL1=A; depends on card #1289 (undeclared tags must error).
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-TAG-UNIFY1=A and D-TAG-SURFACE1=A. D-TAG-SURFACE1 is the later and wider ruling, so it sets the shipped surface; D-TAG-UNIFY1 supplies the semantics that carry over.

1. Tags declare as a small struct body: `tag Name { deny: [...], from: [...] }`. `deny:` is required and non-empty and lists the effects a tagged value must not reach. `from:` is optional and lists origins whose outputs are born tagged.
2. Entries resolve by ordinary name lookup against effect leaves (card #1299 and D-FACTMODEL1=A) and against module and function paths. Typos get did-you-mean.
3. Spread is D-TAINT1 dataflow: a derived value keeps the tag. `#Scrub(Tag) fn` is the one way to remove it and the one grep an audit needs. `#Scrub` validates that the signature consumes the tagged type.
4. Retail sources apply the marker directly on a field, a return type, or an expression.
5. Retire the old spellings: bare `tag Name` is an error carrying the fix, and strict mode, `#Tainted`, and `#Sanitizer` all go. E0721 and E0722 semantics carry over with "denied at" copy. An empty or missing `deny:` is a teaching error.
6. Respell the built-in taint kinds (Input, PII, Secret, Credential) as prelude tag declarations, so the beginner writes nothing and keeps full protection and the expert reads the prelude as ordinary code.
7. Migrate or retire the existing plain-tag examples. This is greenfield, so migrate where the example still teaches something.
8. User-declared sinks stay gated on the deferred IFC ruling.
9. Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows for the tag body fields and `#Scrub`, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

Blocked on #1289: undeclared tags must error before a tag body can be trusted to name real things.

Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/Traits.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, the tag and taint checkers in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema, the prelude tag declarations, tests/ui, examples/features/, docs/spec/.

Proof: targeted tests for a tagged value reaching a denied effect, a `from:` origin marking a value at birth, a `#Scrub` clearing it, a bare `tag Name` erroring with the fix, and a typo in `deny:` getting did-you-mean; all retired spellings error with teaching copy; independent review closes.

questions.text: Ok now in this case I am starting to fail to see value in tags at all... What are the use cases? Why would you use a tag over a taint other than just for documentation?
questions.answer: Honest answer: today you are seeing it right — a plain value tag checks nothing, so over a taint it buys only documentation. The two also answer opposite questions. Taint is negative provenance, on by default: this value may be dangerous, tracked through the whole program, blocked at sinks, with #Sanitizer as the audited exit door. A tag is positive provenance, opt-in: this value passed X — reviewed, normalized, validated, escaped, canonical. You cannot get positive facts out of taint without inverting the world: every value would have to start tainted for every fact, with sanitizers everywhere. Taint tracks the dangerous minority; positive facts mark the verified minority. The real use cases only appear with option A, where the fact becomes checked: an untagged String cannot reach a #Reviewed String parameter, and the #Blesses fn is the greppable, audited door in — still zero runtime cost, and no wrapping tax, because the value stays a String and works with every String API. That last part is the whole case for a strict tag over distinct: distinct mints a new identity you must unwrap at every boundary; a strict tag is the same type carrying a verified property. TypeScript branded types are this exact pattern hand-rolled at massive scale — the demand proof. If checked positive facts do not earn their place for you, the honest pick is C (retire value tags from type position; distinct carries enforcement). B is the weakest of the three: it keeps signatures that look like checks and are not, which is exactly the trap in the story.

questions.text: Ok, based on your response, it sounds like tags and taints are two sides of the same coin. Why not just call all of them tags, then taints and tags are unified under one banner & users can choose which behavior they want in the definition or at call sites, etc? create a new proposal ballot with this idea, it probably supersedes this but you can decide that
questions.answer: Done — new ballot D-TAG-UNIFY1 on this card, and I agree it supersedes D-TAG-STRICT1, which I deleted (strict is now just one mode of the unified mechanism). The shape: every tag declares its checking behavior — plain (documentation, today's default), strict (positive fact: values must pass through a #Blesses door to enter tagged positions), taint (negative fact: spreads by dataflow, blocked at declared sinks, cleared only through a #Sanitizer door). The built-in taint kinds (Input, PII, Secret, Credential) become prelude tag declarations in taint mode, so #Tainted stops being a special case and taints join the tag namespace users can extend. Two notes. First, this builds on D-FACTMODEL1=A, which you ratified today: one fact registry behind tags, states, taint kinds, and effect leaves, with tree facts declared as enums — the modes here attach to that same model, so nothing is relitigated. Second, on choosing behavior at call sites: I worked it out as option C so you can see it honestly, but it breaks the guarantee — the same signature would be checked at one site and decorative at another, and a security property that holds only where someone remembered to ask is the property that fails. The declaration is the honest home for the mode; call sites interact through the doors. Recommendation is A.

cards.title: States join the type's namespace and TypeInfo
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F5. Typestate checking works (E0150 copy is excellent) but states live in no namespace: Machine.Off is E0107, no completion, no reflection, nothing for tooling. Fix: register the state set as comptime-only members at T.State.Off (qualified plane avoids collisions with synthesized members like D-PATCH1's T.Patch); #State/#Transition arguments resolve by ordinary lookup with did-you-mean; TypeInfo gains .states and .transitions so fn build tooling can render the machine. Erasure unchanged. Ballot D-STATE-NS1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-STATE-NS1=A — states live at `T.State.Name`, a reserved plane, plus TypeInfo.

1. Register the state set as comptime-only members at `T.State.Name`. The qualified plane cannot collide with methods, fields, nested types, or synthesized members such as D-PATCH1's `T.Patch`.

cards.title: TaskGroup becomes a nameable parameter type
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F6. fn f(g: TaskGroup) is E0119 and g.task outside the lexical block is E1110 — structured concurrency cannot be factored into helpers (live probe). Fix: publish TaskGroup as a nameable parameter type with a soundness rule priced honestly: spawns through a group received as a parameter require owned captures (~x moves/copies, no view captures), extending D-DETACH1. Jet has no lifetimes; the lexical rule is what makes view captures safe today, so the parameter path must close that hole itself. Typed Capability<E> handles were considered and demoted to a post-v1 note. Ballot D-TASKGROUP-PARAM1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-TASKGROUP-PARAM1=A — TaskGroup is nameable in parameter position, and spawns through a parameter group must own their captures.

1. Publish TaskGroup as a type that can be written in a parameter. `fn f(g: TaskGroup)` stops being E0119.
2. Spawns through a parameter group require owned captures: move or copy, never a view. Spawns inside the group's own block keep today's freedom. This is what keeps the parameter path safe without lifetimes, so price it honestly in the diagnostic.
3. TaskGroup stays second-class: legal as a parameter, illegal in struct fields, in returns, and in closures that escape. It flows down the call stack only.
4. Escape checking stays lexical per frame. Owned captures cannot dangle, so no interprocedural analysis is needed.
5. Update the E1110 copy to teach the parameter path instead of only refusing.
6. Extend D-DETACH1's owned-capture discipline to cover non-local spawns.
7. Typed `Capability<E>` handles are a post-v1 note, not this card.

cards.title: Ranges become values: one Range type in core
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F7. a..b is legal in exactly five slots (loop source, arm head, slice, view arg, distinct constraint) and no Range type exists — bands :: [0..<10, 10..<100] has no type to be. Fix: one nominal Range over Int; both spellings construct it; the value carries end-exclusivity; .start/.end/.contains(x). No second RangeExclusive type. Loops keep specializing to jumps (zero-cost lowering is codegen, not surface). Accepted asymmetry stated in spec: distinct Int(0..10) stays literal-only. Ballot D-RANGE-VALUE1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-RANGE-VALUE1=A — one nominal Range type in core, over Int, in v1.

1. Add `Range` to core with `start`, `end`, `contains(x)`, and end-exclusivity carried in the value. An inclusive and an exclusive range are the same type with different end behaviour. There is no second RangeExclusive type.
2. Both spellings construct it, so `bands :: [0..<10, 10..<100]` has a type to be.
3. Every position that takes a range today keeps working with literals and also accepts a Range value: loop source, slice, and view argument.
4. Lowering specializes exactly as it does now. No iterator object, no allocation. Zero-cost lowering is a codegen matter, not a surface one.
5. Arm heads keep accepting range literals as today. Range values in arm heads are a later question and are out of scope here.
6. State the accepted asymmetry in the spec: the distinct-constraint position, `distinct Int(0..10)`, stays literal-only.
7. Syntax chores: Syntax.rs row, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

cards.title: Optional effect-leaf declarations kill typo leaves
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F8. Effect roots are a closed 10-set (right call) but leaves are freeform strings: =[FS.Raed]=> silently mints a new leaf; pkg.jet budgets compare the same undeclared strings. The effect keyword is reserved and unminted (D-EFF4/5) — the slot exists. Fix: effect FS.Read declarations; once any leaf is declared under a root, undeclared leaves under that root become resolution errors with did-you-mean; never-declared roots keep today's freedom; the prelude declares stdlib leaves so day-one users get typo protection free. Ballot D-EFFECT-DECL1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-EFFECT-DECL1=A — optional `effect FS.Read` declarations, and a root becomes checked once anything is declared under it.

1. Mint the reserved `effect` keyword into the D-EFF4/D-EFF5 slot.
2. Add the declaration form `effect FS.Read`. Declarations are package-scoped facts.
3. Once any leaf is declared under a root in a package's view, an undeclared leaf under that root is a resolution error with did-you-mean. A root nobody declared under keeps today's mint-on-use freedom.
4. The checked flag is per root, per package view, over the package's own declarations plus its dependencies' declared leaves.
5. `pkg.jet` budgets and `#Caps` and `#Grant` arguments resolve against the same names, so a typo cannot silently mint a budget line either.
6. Declare the stdlib's own leaves in the prelude, so a day-one user gets typo protection on the common roots having written nothing.
7. Tree matching is unchanged.
8. Register the resolution error with what/why/fix text and its UI snapshot (I4). Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows for the keyword and declaration, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

cards.title: Marker/trait name-collision law
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F10. Comparable is a trait, a #Comparable marker, and a capability bundle; #Codable = Encode+Decode; 'tag' means three things (tag keyword, serde #Tag, D-TAG1 enum groups); #Task fn vs Task<T>. Fix: spec states that a type-site PascalCase marker IS a trait/derive reference (one namespace — user derives already work this way), plus a rule for future markers: a rule that derives trait X is spelled #X; a non-derive rule may not take a trait's name. Optional renames for serde #Tag and scheduled #Task if the owner wants them. Ballot D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1=A — adopt the naming law and rename the two offenders.

1. Write the law into the marker-authoring section of the spec: a type-site PascalCase marker is a trait or derive reference, in one namespace, exactly as user derives already work. A rule that derives trait X is spelled `#X`. A non-derive rule may not take a trait's name.
2. Add the registry lint that enforces it, so the next marker cannot break the law quietly.
3. Rename serde's `#Tag` to `#Discriminant`, the standard term for the variant field.
4. Rename the scheduled `#Task` to `#Job`, a scheduled unit of work, distinct from the `Task<T>` handle.
5. Both old spellings error with fix text pointing at the new name. Add retirement rows in the registry and register the E-codes with their snapshots (I4).
6. Switch the D-TAG1 spec prose to "variant groups" in the same pass, so "tag" shrinks to two meanings.
7. Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows for the renames, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/Traits.rs and the marker registry, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, the serde and scheduling checkers, tests/ui, examples/features/, docs/spec/.

cards.title: Vec3 and builtin structs print a different shape on each lens
cards.body: print(Vec3(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)) gives 'Vec3([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])' under jet build and 'Vec3 { 0: 1.0, 1: 2.0, 2: 3.0 }' under jet run. The AOT spelling comes from a hand-written JetShow in the linalg prelude (Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs); the interpreter has no declared fields for a builtin struct and falls back to a generic renderer. Card #1270 removed the user_ mangling from both, so only the shape now differs. Same class applies to Vec2/Vec4/Mat3/Mat4. Pick one spelling and make both lenses use it.
cards.plan:
Two lenses print one value two ways. `jet build` gives `Vec3([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])` from a hand-written JetShow in the linalg prelude; `jet run` gives `Vec3 { 0: 1.0, 1: 2.0, 2: 3.0 }` from the generic interpreter renderer, because a builtin struct declares no fields to it. One compiler, two lenses, and never a difference the user can see.

No ballot is needed: the house shape is already ratified. S55 and D-DISPLAYDBG1 auto-derive Debug for a struct, and a probe confirms a user struct prints `P { x: 1.0, y: 2.0 }` today. Vec3 exposes named fields `.x`, `.y`, `.z`, so the shape that follows the existing law is `Vec3 { x: 1.0, y: 2.0, z: 3.0 }`.

1. Give the builtin math structs declared field names on the interpreter side, so the generic renderer stops falling back to positional indices.
2. Delete the hand-written JetShow spellings in MathTaskMem.rs and let the same derived shape serve both lenses.
3. Cover the whole family: Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Mat3, Mat4, and any sibling builtin struct with the same shape problem.
4. Add a parity test that prints each of them on both lenses and requires the two to match, so this class cannot come back.

Card #1270 already removed the `user_` mangling from both sides, so only the shape differs.

cards.title: Stale example goldens: parallel_scan, returned_views, deadline_context, browser_locked_provision
cards.body: cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run is red on four examples unrelated to any current change. concurrency/parallel_scan counts lines and chars of pipeline.jet, tasks.jet, and json.jet, and those sources were edited without reblessing the golden. memory/returned_views prints two extra lines. concurrency/deadline_context gained a trailing 'panic: a task panicked' on stderr. net/browser_locked_provision has no golden at all and update mode never creates one. Confirmed pre-existing: the same four fail with the compiler reverted to HEAD. The three web/web_wasm_* failures in the same run belong to the in-flight web backend work, not here.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make the four goldens from this card pass in `examples_compile_and_run`, each for a justified reason (no blanket rebless): `concurrency/parallel_scan`, `memory/returned_views`, `concurrency/deadline_context` and `net/browser_locked_provision`. The three `web/web_wasm_*` failures belong to the web backend work.

## Current state
- Criteria 2 and 3 are verified. The reblesses were justified, and update mode now creates a missing golden: `Examples/features/expected/net/browser_locked_provision.out` exists, and `tests/golden.rs:886` asks for `JET_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` plus a scoped filter.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER` is a single substring of `Examples/features/<stem>.jet` (`tests/common/mod.rs:1252-1254`). The earlier comma-list proof never matched. `concurrency/parallel_scan` also pulls in `parallel_scan_expert.jet`, whose generated Rust fails with seven E0308 errors around `jet_err_apply_conversion` and typed list/task values (log 2026-09-22).
- `deadline_context` fails E3403 on `time.sleep` under the MIREval deadline, and task join then reports E3003 (logs 2026-09-15). #1218 (building) owns that parity fix. Its `.out` and `.err.out` exist.
- The conversion is emitted at `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet:2683`. The host helper is `jet_foundation::Outcome::jet_err_apply_conversion` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs:215`), and the route row is `crates/jet-codegen/src/TIR/routes.rs:9146`.

## Changes
1. Run each golden with an exact filter, `…/parallel_scan.jet`, so that `parallel_scan` is judged on its own.
2. Reproduce the `parallel_scan_expert` E0308 errors on the emitted Rust. Fix the argument and return typing of the `apply_conversion` call in the retained rustc emission, and mirror the fix in `Expressions.jet:2683` so the Jet emitter produces the same shape. If that example is not one of the four, file it as its own card and keep this card to the four.
3. `returned_views`: read the two extra lines, and rebless only if the new output is correct.
4. `deadline_context`: once #1218 lands, cancellation under a deadline must not print `panic: a task panicked`. Confirm the result against the existing `.err.out`.

## Proof
Each of these must be green, run one at a time through the memory-capped wrapper:

cards.title: Orphan test binary from a deleted worktree spins at 100% CPU
cards.body: PID 169312 runs target/debug/deps/jet-fcd0d638b91407a3 from .claude/worktrees/e3-1230-close, a worktree that no longer exists. Both its cwd and exe read as (deleted). It has burned a full core since 2026-07-27 13:57 (over 20 hours of CPU) and slows every build in this repo. Kill it. Then find why that test never terminated, because the same hang will strand the next worktree run: a test that cannot finish is a defect even when the worktree is gone.
cards.plan: Confirm that PID 169312 is gone and record its process evidence. Reproduce the orphan through the Linux isolated-worker path in Source/BudgetProviders.rs. Set a parent-death signal in each isolated worker and close the fork race before hostile work starts. Add a focused regression that kills the supervisor, proves the worker exits, and cleans up on failure. Run the BudgetProviders unit tests and performance-budget provider tests. Get an independent process-lifecycle review and rerun the focused proof.

The original worker can exit and the PID can be reused between those operations, so cleanup can still signal an unrelated process. Use a stable process handle for the cleanup signal. Second, host readback found three original workers still running from the deleted e3-1230-close worktree: PIDs 169315, 169317, and 169319. Each uses about 99 percent CPU, has a deleted cwd and executable, and is adopted by the user systemd process. cards.title: One widening law across the numeric menu (implicit lossless widening)
cards.body:
Ratified 2026-07-28. D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F: a whole number moves on its own into a wider whole number that holds every one of its values; nothing ever narrows on its own; a mix with no common wider type stays an error. D-VERDICT-1304-1 extends the same law to decimals: an F32 moves on its own into a Float, amending D-FLOATW1, which today makes that a compile error with a convert fix-it.

This replaces the card's original narrow framing. It started as one red test — tests/cffi.rs cffi_named_pure_callback_has_stable_c_symbol writes `x + 1` where x is an I32 and sema answers E0109 — and the ballot turned it into a language rule. That test is now one of this card's regression proofs, not its scope.

Probed on the current binary 2026-07-28: `I32 + Int` is E0109; `I32 + I16` is E0109; `F32 + Float` is E0109; `U8.{ 300 }` is caught at compile time as E1003; `increment(2)` already compiles, so a numeral already takes the width an argument asks for.

Open gate: D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1 — whether widening crosses between whole numbers and decimals. The ruled law does not say, and read strictly it answers by accident, allowing I32 into Float while refusing Int. Amends S42 (named widths never mix) and D-FLOATW1.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F and D-VERDICT-1304-1. One widening law across whole numbers and decimals. Gated on D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1 for the boundary between the two kinds; everything below is the within-kind work, which the cross-kind pick does not change.

1. Order each numeric family by value containment: a type widens into another when every one of its values is held exactly. Whole numbers: I8 into I16 into I32 into I64, U8 into U16 into U32 into U64, and each unsigned type into the next wider signed one. Decimals: F32 into Float.
2. Apply that ordering as an implicit coercion at operators, at arguments, at returns, and at assignment. The type of a mixed expression is the wider of the two.
3. Refuse a mix with no common wider type, such as U8 with I8, and keep today's E0109 for it with copy that says why neither holds the other.
4. Never narrow on its own, anywhere. Narrowing stays destination-owned and fallible per D-SHAPE-CONVERT1.
5. A numeral takes its narrowest holding type and then widens by the same rule. Keep the compile-time range check: an out-of-range numeral is an error naming the width and the limit, as E1003 already does for a typed head.
6. Leave overflow alone. D-NUMOPS1 traps at every width, and widening never changes where a trap happens, because a widened value is exact.
7. Delete the conversion ceremony this makes unnecessary in the stdlib and the examples, so the corpus teaches the new law rather than the old one.
8. Amend the spec: S42's separation of named widths, D-FLOATW1's F32-with-Float error and its convert fix-it, and the E0109 copy that currently says the two sides must match. Register the amended texts with UI snapshots (I4).
9. Syntax chores: syntax-decisions.md amendment rows with the decision ids, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.
10. Once D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1 is ratified, implement its pick as the one boundary rule and state it in the same spec entry.

Owned paths: crates/jet-sema (numeric typing, coercion, E0109 and E1003), crates/jet-codegen (widening at lowering, both lenses), crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, tests/ui, tests/cffi.rs, examples/features/.

Proof: targeted tests for each widening pair, for a refused mix with no common wider type, for a refused narrowing, and for an out-of-range numeral; cffi_named_pure_callback_has_stable_c_symbol passes without weakening what it tests; a trap test proving overflow still stops at the declared width; both lenses agree; independent review closes.

log.text: Batch closeout complete. Scoped machine proof is green and criteria are independently verified. Fixes landed in 33b34075e, dbea973d5, and 2cc68a838. Final verify-full advanced through the affected batches and stopped only on unrelated allocator_families failures; those do not reopen these scoped closures under repository policy.

[handoff] D-NUMLIT-PEER1 is the open gate. Its failing proof is cargo test --test comptime_diff comptime_matches_runtime: the cases 1000000 * 1000000, (0 - 17) / 5, and (0 - 17) % 5 all trap at compile time because each peerless numeral shrinks to its smallest fitting width. That test is the last comptime_diff failure; the other 24 pass. D-NUMJOIN1=A is implemented in 7c27d8fcc (if-branches, yielding-loop items, list elements all use Type::numeric_join), so nothing else on this card is blocked.

Ballot D-NUMJOIN1 raised: D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F names operators, arguments, returns, and assignments, and gives a numeral its smallest fitting type, but never named multi-branch value joins. So  is E0124 (U8 against Int) and tests/ui_lint/prefer_arm_table.jet no longer compiles. Also fixed a cascade the same rule caused: E0112 no longer follows E0202 on , where the argument was already refused for not being a named binding.

Final reviewer-fix commit 44f76c8fe closes the stale evidence blockers. The claimed typed-binding gap is not a valid surface: D-BIND-BARE1 retired initialized `name: Type :: value` and `name: Type := value`, the parser rejects it with E0003, and initialized local bindings cannot populate Binding.ty; reopening it would contradict ratified authority. Replaced the obsolete valid `1 + 2.5` E0109 fixture with incomparable U8 + I8, regenerated E0109, and repaired stale representative E0108/E0119 pages. Rewrote the numeric reference around the one containment law, corrected the binary inference comment, and removed the unreachable Int/Float never-mix branch. Final proof after commits caae2e5e8, ca8f2af0c, d637e253b, and 44f76c8fe: `cargo test --test numeric_widening -- --nocapture` 8/8 across AOT, resident JIT trace, and forced interpreter; unblessed filtered mixed_numbers UI 1/1; unblessed `cargo test --test gen_errors gen_error_pages -- --nocapture` 1/1; `git diff --check` clean.

Material-fix recheck: d637e253b closes the missing call surfaces (function values, user/static/trait methods, inline/imported calls, fan-out, variadics, builtins), but #1304 remains blocked. CheckerCore/bindings.rs still rejects nonliteral typed-binding widening; the stale never-mix comment remains in CheckerInfer/binary.rs; core-library numeric docs and E0109 reference still teach no widening; mixed_numbers UI still expects 1 + 2.5 to fail although D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1=E makes it compile. Fix typed bindings and replace stale docs/UI with valid incomparable/narrowing cases before re-review.

Reviewer-fix commit d637e253b centralizes non-Write numeric argument coercion across ordinary/static/trait methods, function values, inline and imported modules, fan-out, builtin/variadic and specialized call finishers. Bare operator literals now use a containing typed peer or the narrowest holding integer type, so I8/U8 + 1 stays beginner-friendly while U8 + 256 joins at U16; destination-owned U8.{256} still reports E1003 and lexer limits retain E0007. Added exact E0104/E0109 approx UI snapshots. Resident-tier tests now assert jit_executed=true, fallback=false, deopt=false instead of checking subprocess text. Proof: cargo test --test numeric_widening (8/8 AOT/resident/forced-interpreter) and unblessed filtered approx diagnostic snapshots (1/1) pass. Discovered separate AOT trait-object local-variable boxing bug and recorded #1318.

Final independent review added a second criterion-7 blocker: typed binding initialization in CheckerCore/bindings.rs explicitly refuses nonliteral width widening, so small: I8 cannot initialize wide: I16. The one destination-wide law therefore still changes by syntactic context. Also remove the stale CheckerInfer/binary.rs comment that says widths never mix implicitly. Centralize widening across calls and typed bindings, then rerun the complete matrix.

Review expanded the same systemic blocker: widening is not centralized at the argument-coercion seam. In addition to function-value and user-method calls, inline-module and cross-file/import calls in CheckerCoreLib/imports.rs, trait method arguments in CheckerItems.rs, and fan-out function application in CheckerInfer/expr.rs skip widen_numeric_expr; specialized method finishers may also drift. Surface spelling or module boundary therefore changes numeric meaning. Fix one shared non-Write argument coercion path and prove every call family.

Independent review found a remaining criterion-7 blocker after ca8f2af0c. infer_call_value in CheckerInfer/calls/helpers_call_values.rs and check_method_args in CheckerItems.rs compare got != param_ty directly and emit E0112 without calling the shared numeric widening seam. A function value (x: I16) called with I8 and a user method taking I16 both reject instead of widening. Route non-Write arguments through widen_numeric_expr before assignability/type errors and add tier tests. Current commits are not safe to integrate.

Reviewer finding resolved in ca8f2af0c: sema now consumes the compiler-private approx marker through redundant transparent parentheses at the shared widening seam, covering operators, arguments, returns, and assignments. Focused parenthesized regression passed AOT, resident JIT with no tier0 deopt marker, and forced interpreter (1/1). Complete tests/numeric_widening.rs matrix passed 6/6. git diff --cached --check was clean; commit contains only owned #1304 hunks and test.

Implemented caae2e5e8. Focused numeric matrix 5/5, canonical Prelude test, UI snapshot, grammar no-drift, both examples across AOT/JIT/interpreter, and exact C callback compile/link/threaded runtime pass. Full CFFI has 14 unrelated stale E3201 fixtures tracked on #1317. Ready for batch review.

Coordination: five-card batch is integrated on master as f0b574092. Owner requires .claude/worktrees/core-five deleted before the serial memory wave. Please commit or otherwise preserve #1304's owned numeric/Units changes and release this worktree promptly; do not discard them.
Started implementation in shared core-five worktree. Inspecting existing numeric typing and runtime trap seams before edits.

prep: owner asked how MATLAB and Python behave on cross-kind arithmetic; added MATLAB, Python, and NumPy 2.0 comparisons to D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1 and a new option E (cross everywhere, check the crossings that cannot be proved exact, reusing the D-NUMOPS1 trap path); recommendation moved from D to E
prep: dropped two criteria the rescope made stale (D-INTLIT-WIDTH1 is now ratified; the argument-versus-operand item is subsumed by the widening-law criteria)

Verdict recorded (D-VERDICT-1304-1): Implicit lossless widening covers floats as well as whole numbers. An F32 moves on its own into Float, exactly as a narrow whole number moves into a wider whole number; nothing ever narrows on its own. This amends D-FLOATW1, which today makes mixing F32 and Float a compile error with a convert fix-it. Owner words (2026-07-28): "Ok, again we want beginner magic out of the box and full expert control. So let's go with option f but for both int and floats". With D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F this is the ruled surface: one widening law across the whole numeric menu.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

questions.text: Shouldnt we make literals like this as small as possible so that they can auto widen with no loss?
questions.answer:
Half of it works, half of it backfires, and the good half is bigger than literals. I added both readings to the ballot as options E and F.

Option E is your idea taken literally: give the numeral its narrowest type, then widen it losslessly. Two problems, both found by probing the current binary.

1. "Narrowest" cannot be decided without looking at the other side. The narrowest type for 1 is an unsigned byte, and an unsigned byte does not fit in an I8. So `fn tick(x: I8) => I8 { return x + 1 }` gets refused. Once you consult the other side to avoid that, you have written option A.

2. The out-of-range case gets worse, not better. `U8.{200} + 300` would make 300 a 16-bit number, widen the U8 to meet it, and hand back a 16-bit sum. The mistake is accepted and the expression silently changes width. The error lands later, at the store, instead of on the 300 where you typed it. Today `U8.{ 300 }` is caught on the spot as E1003, and option A keeps that.

Option F is the bigger idea inside your question, and I think it is the real one. Lossless widening implicit everywhere, not just for numerals. `I32 + I16` is refused today (probed) even though every I16 value fits an I32 with nothing lost. F fixes that whole family, not just the literal case, and narrowing stays explicit.

F costs two things. It ends the deliberate separation of named widths in S42. And it splits the numeric menu: D-FLOATW1 keeps F32-with-Float as a compile error with a convert fix-it, so whole numbers would auto-widen while floats would not. If you want F, that float rule should be reopened in the same breath so both halves follow one law.

So: A if you want the argument-versus-operand inconsistency closed and nothing else moved. F if you want the general "no ceremony for a conversion that cannot lose anything" rule, knowing it amends S42 and pulls D-FLOATW1 with it. E is the one I would not take, because it refuses the I8 case and it accepts the 300.

cards.title: Retire comptime: implicit folding + #Known marker
cards.body:
Retire the `comptime` keyword (S57/S26 surface) per owner ruling 2026-07-28 (chat).

Ruled package:
1. Implicit comptime folding is the beginner default: the compiler folds any foldable
   expression silently; if compile-time evaluation would panic or hit an unsupported
   construct, it silently defers to runtime (R12 bit-for-bit parity makes folding
   observationally invisible; tests/comptime_diff.rs battery is the guarantee).
2. The explicit demand form moves to the marker plane as `#Known` (bindings and blocks),
   beside #Track/#Unsafe/#Impure/#Region; `#Track x :: expr` is the marker-on-binding
   precedent. Demand semantics = fail the build if the value cannot be computed now.
   Required at the sites that semantically need compile-time values: `[T#N]` lengths,
   `mem.Fixed.new(size:)`, static assertions, guaranteed baking.
3. `when` as the conditional-compilation spelling is REJECTED. The conditional form
   (today `comptime if`, D-WHEN1) keeps if-based spelling; exact replacement spelling
   still open (leading candidate `#Known if`) — needs owner confirmation before parser work.
4. `fn build` / BuildPlan (D-BUILDENTRY1) remains the separate effectful buildtime
   mechanism; unchanged by this ruling.

Migration scope: KW_COMPTIME in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs (+ decision ID),
parser (bindings/blocks/comptime if), sema in_comptime plumbing and E09xx diagnostic copy,
formatter, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md amendment, every example under
examples/features/comptime/, UI snapshots, fuzz corpus. E0956 wording overlap with #1254
(runtime-tier E0956 must stop saying comptime regardless).

cards.title: Canonical Codable semantics survive TIR deopt
cards.body: Typed CBOR can run resident through generated Decode bodies, but a surrounding tier gap sends the function to the canonical TIR evaluator. That evaluator must preserve the same Encode, Decode, migration, coercion, range, and error laws. Field-name/type tuple walking is forbidden because it ignores user and marker behavior.
cards.plan: Parse CBOR once into DataTree. Dispatch named and custom values through the ordinary lowered Type.encode and Type.decode functions already present in JitProgram. Share primitive and container decoding for Option, List, fixed lists, maps, bytes, F32, sized integers, chars, DataTree, distinct ranges, and exact errors. Carry a compiled migration plan with wire keys and default or converter function names; apply it through the same codec dispatch. Delete typed field-tuple encode and decode shortcuts. Prove forced per-function deopt matches AOT for rename, default, flatten, deny unknown, custom Decode, migrations, enums, maps, F32, bytes, sized bounds, and distinct values.

cards.title: Portable on_click across UI backends
cards.body:
Ratified scope from D-WEB-CLICK-OWN1=D (option B is the destination, not an idea). One portable `on_click` that works the same on the GTK, web, and terminal backends, and on future mobile backends. Card #1274 shipped the interim form: the flagship browser demo binds the click with `web.on` and holds the count in a reactive signal.

This card owns the design of the portable form. It must answer three things.

1. Stable node identity across renders on the DOM backend. A handler is attached to a node in the tree. The tree is rebuilt on every render, so each node needs an identity that survives the rebuild, or the listener is lost or duplicated. The DOM runtime already keys painted elements by render path (`jetDomBoxRegistry` in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js). Decide whether the render path is the identity, or whether the node carries an explicit key.

2. The event dispatch channel from JavaScript to the wasm side. A DOM `click` arrives in JavaScript. The handler is Jet code compiled to wasm. Decide how the event crosses that boundary, how the handler is addressed, and what happens when the handler is gone.

3. The portable event set. Decide which events every backend must support, and what a backend does with an event it cannot produce. GTK, DOM, and terminal do not agree on hover, focus, or key repeat.

Flagship respell: when this card lands, examples/features/web/ui_web_click.jet moves to the portable form. The `web.on` selector call and the manual bind ordering go away, and the button node carries its own handler:

    button :: ui.button("Click me", on_click: () => count.set(count.get() + 1))

The GTK backend already has `on_click` (`GtkBackend.on_click`), so the design must fold that surface into the portable one instead of adding a second mechanism (I8).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship one portable `on_click` on GTK, web, and terminal (D-WEB-CLICK-OWN1 destination B). Fold GTK's existing `on_click` into that one mechanism (I8). Move `examples/features/web/ui_web_click.jet` off `web.on` to node-carried handlers.

## Ratified law
- D-UI-NODE-ID1=C — render path is identity by default; optional author `key` overrides for lists and reorders.
- D-UI-EVT-DISP1=E — default hot path is O(1) node-keyed handler slots (`jet_ui_dispatch`); unmount clears the slot; experts opt the same handlers into the shared UI scheduler for ordered/coalesced drain. Never selector identity.
- D-UI-EVT-SET1=D — portable core is click/activate; richer events require an explicit capability module (for example `ui.web.hover`).

## Build steps
1. Write identity, dispatch, and event-set law into the UI/runtime docs this card owns.
2. Implement Prelude/DOM/GTK marshalling to those rules only. No second click mechanism. No policy re-encoded in an engine (I9).
3. Respell the flagship web example to portable `on_click`. Prove default `jet run` and AOT when the example is runnable. Keep GTK click parity.
4. Add capability-module path for one rich event only if needed to prove D; otherwise document the import rule and leave wider events for follow-on cards.

## Acceptance / proof
- Flagship click demo uses portable `on_click`, not `web.on`, for the counter path.
- Remount after re-render keeps the handler (path identity); a keyed list reorder keeps the keyed handler.
- Unsupported rich event without the capability module is a clear diagnostic or compile gate, not a silent no-op.
- Targeted UI/runtime tests + example golden green on applicable tiers.

## Owned paths
`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js`, `UiGtk.rs`, UI Prelude surface, `examples/features/web/ui_web_click.jet`, related UI docs under `docs/spec/`.

cards.body: Sema and the TIR evaluator recurse per nesting level with large frames. `jet::compile` called from a 2 MB thread aborts with `fatal runtime error: stack overflow` on a ten-line program (`shared_is_the_safe_mutation_control_case`, `composite_lambda_capture_walks_if_prefix_and_fallback_values`, `local_cell_full_surface_runs_through_default_tier`). The `jet` binary survives only because a process main thread gets 8 MB. Confirmed on master both before and after the core-five merge, so it predates that work. tests/dev.rs already works around it by setting RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 for child runs. A stack overflow is an abort, not a diagnostic, so this also violates the spirit of I2/I4: rustc is hidden and every refusal is a product diagnostic. Ballot D-COMPILE-STACK1 attached.

Route each public root entry that loads, parses, checks, lowers, or evaluates through it exactly once. Keep all current synchronous signatures and values. Resume worker panics on the caller thread. 2. Keep hook lifetimes correct across the boundary. Initialize the process-wide `TirBridge` in the worker. Keep JIT native-call and ambient runtime scopes on their execution thread. cards.title: Comprehension surface coherence: loop-header split, labels, map duality
cards.body: Comprehension-surface coherence analysis (owner-requested). Three wobbles found; each has a ballot drafted and waiting in the decide lane: D-LOOP-HEADER3 (loop-header split), D-LOOPLABEL4 (label placement), D-LOOPMAP1 (map/comprehension duality). Implementation is owner-gated: do NOT start until the owner ratifies the ballots in the Tower UI. After ratification, implement the full ruling + acceptance terms (verify skill owns syntax chores). Background: analysis of composition/surface/structure coherence versus Python comprehensions; goals are versatility, flexibility, simplicity, expressiveness, power.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the three ratified rulings on one card. Do not reopen the ballots.

### D-LOOP-HEADER3=D — one meaning for three slots
Header shape is binding; source; step rule. Slot three is an Int stride or a step rule (s => s * 2) on a range source. Retire the old counter form with a teaching diagnostic. Pointer-chase loops use a Core generated-sequence helper (Swift sequence(first:next:) shape); settle the helper name in code and document it. Yield arrows keep working.

### D-LOOPLABEL4=A — no change
Keep binding-as-label for effect loops (Void binding). Optional: suppress unused-binding lint for Void loop labels used as break/next targets. No grammar change required beyond staying compatible with the header work.

### D-LOOPMAP1=B — eager adapters; opt-in lazy
values.map(f) returns a List. Lazy pipelines require values.lazy().map(f).... Iterator sources (files, channels) stay lazy. Eagerness applies to in-memory collections only.

## Acceptance
- Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions.md for each ruling that changes surface law.
- Grammars regenerated; snapshots blessed (verify skill).
- Teaching diagnostic for retired counter form (I4 snapshot).
- Example(s) covering: range+step rule, Int stride, labeled effect loop, eager map vs .lazy() pipeline.
- I9: default jet run and AOT match goldens for new examples.
- No second loop mechanism; no second map plane without .lazy().

## Steps
1. Header rewrite in parser/sema; diagnostic for old counter form.
2. Step-rule lowering on ranges; Int stride unchanged in law.
3. Core generated-sequence helper for pointer-chase; document name.
4. Adapter eagerness + .lazy() entry; update collection method law/docs.
5. Examples + goldens; syntax chores; Sol review.

## Owned paths
parser/sema/codegen loop + collection adapters, Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md, Core sequence helper, examples, snapshots.

questions.text: this is not clear and the options are terrible. Rethink from first principles, consider surface syntax, ontology, isomorphism, logic, psychology to provide a much better list of options
questions.answer: Rewrote D-LOOP-HEADER3 from first principles. The lesson now derives the problem from loop ontology (three drivers: forever, test, source — the C-style counter is not a fourth, it is a test loop plus loop-scoped state and an advance that runs on next), the shape/meaning isomorphism break (slot two flips data/test, slot three flips count/action, cued only by ':='), silhouette-first reading psychology, and a logic hazard the old ballot hid: retiring the counter form makes 'next above the advance' spin forever, because bare test loops retest without advancing. Options are now five genuinely distinct designs: A keep both; B retire plain, with its scope-leak and spin costs stated honestly; C keep the advance clause, drop the init slot (Zig direction); D unify three slots as binding; source; step-rule so 'loop size; 1..<budget; s => s * 2' replaces the counter inside the one source dialect (Swift sequence(first:next:) direction); E keep both but force the counter into a parenthesized head so the silhouettes differ at a glance. cards.title: TIR evaluator diagnostics have no spans
cards.body:
`EvalCtx::span()` in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs returns `Span::new(0, 0)` unconditionally, so every diagnostic the canonical TIR evaluator raises points at line 1 column 1. Since #777 made that evaluator the comptime engine, any comptime runtime failure now underlines the first byte of the file instead of the construct that failed — visible in tests/ui/comptime_panic.stderr and in every E0955/E0956 the evaluator raises.

29c90b639 works around it for build-time IO by running the same law in a sema pre-pass that has the call's span. That trick does not generalize: TIR carries no spans at all, so the fix is to thread them (TExpr or at least TStmt) and have the evaluator report against the node it is running.
cards.plan: Carry source spans as TIR statements through lowering and evaluator state, keep AOT/JIT/web adapters semantics-neutral, and snapshot a real evaluator diagnostic location.

cards.title: Expert view-provenance declarations: stable borrow contracts, trait lending, callback relations
cards.body: D-MEMPROVENANCE2=A made view provenance fully inferred. Three expressiveness walls remain where Rust is more capable than Jet: (1) a library's borrow contract is accidental - it shifts silently when a body is edited, a breaking API change no signature shows; (2) function/callback types have no body to infer from, so view-returning callbacks freeze every compatible non-scalar argument; (3) open trait dispatch returning a view is refused outright (E2305) because no per-body inference is possible. Rust states all three with lifetime annotations; Jet bans that notation. This card ratifies an opt-in expert declaration spelling (inference stays the beginner default) so nothing expressible in safe Rust is inexpressible in Jet. See ballot D-MEMPROVENANCE3.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship D-MEMPROVENANCE3=A: opt-in trailing `from` provenance clauses. Inference (D-MEMPROVENANCE2=A) stays the beginner default.

## Law
- Grammar: `from src (| src)*` after return types, view-typed params, trait-method returns, and function-type returns. Aggregate per-slot: `from (field: srcs, …)`.
- src = param name | `self` | `static.<path>`, with optional projections.
- Check: each return path's inferred sources ⊆ declaration; wider declaration is legal; escape teaches with fix-it.
- Trait clauses bind impls and retire E2305 for declared methods. Function-type clauses quantify per call.
- Type defs never carry owner parameters. API digests flag declared relations.

## Vertical slice order
1. Parse + Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions + example for result `from` (single/union).
2. Sema: attach declared set; check ⊆; keep undeclared = infer-only.
3. Trait method `from self` + retire E2305 on that path; callback function-type clause.
4. Parameter `from` requirements + aggregate per-slot.
5. Grammars, snapshots, golden example (returned_views / new expert example).
6. Independent review; criteria verify; done.

## Out
Pin/self-ref (D-PIN1), variance UI, mandatory notation.

cards.title: Member spread across a shared prefix (jetpack packages and beyond)
cards.body:
Owner instruction in chat (2026-07-31): 'I want to be able to have that spreading for packages and other things in jetpack in particular.'

D-VERDICT-1324-1 removed S75, which was a CALL fan-out: f.[a, b, c] meant [f(a), f(b), f(c)]. jetpack never used that meaning. env.jet and config.jet write default.[git, ripgrep] to mean MEMBER spread: [default.git, default.ripgrep]. jetpack reads the field's source text with Merge::parse_package_list, so S75 only had to parse, never to evaluate. Removing S75 therefore took away a spelling jetpack depends on while leaving its real semantics unspecified.

Scope: choose and ship the member-spread surface. The removal of the call fan-out stands.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship D-SPREAD1=A: `prefix.[a, b, c]` means member spread `[prefix.a, prefix.b, prefix.c]`. Call fan-out stays gone.

## Law
- Sigil `.[` after an expression; entries are bare idents only (E0970 if not).
- In list position: splice into surrounding ListLit.
- Elsewhere: fixed-size `[T#N]` list (S76).
- Desugar in sema before inference. Formatter emits the sugar. Migrate env.jet + jetpack fixtures.

## Steps
1. Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions D-SPREAD1=A; note E0970 (E0963 already S76).
2. Parse Expr::MemberSpread { base, names }.
3. Sema desugar; UI snapshot for non-ident.
4. Formatter + fmt STABILITY; migrate env.jet and fixtures.
5. I9: example AOT + jet run; independent verify; done.

## Owned paths
parser Expressions, AST, sema desugar, Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions, diagnostics, env.jet, jetpack fixtures, formatter, UI snapshot, example.

cards.title: Jet as guest: export native libraries and embed contract
cards.body: Incremental enterprise replacement keeps the legacy application as host for years; teams rewrite leaf modules in Jet and link them back in. Deliver the guest direction: export marked Jet functions as .a/.so/.dylib/.dll with a stable C ABI, generate matching C headers from sema's typed facts, and define the embed contract (runtime init/shutdown inside a foreign process, thread ownership, signals, allocator/TLS policy). Gap G1 in the field audit. Export surface spelling is owner-gated (D-ADOPT-GUEST1).
cards.plan: Apply D-ADOPT-GUEST1=A. Implement the matching #Import/#Export C ABI surface, c-archive and shared-library emission, sema-derived headers, and the foreign-host runtime contract for initialization, shutdown, threads, signals, allocators, and TLS. Prove real C and C++ hosts can link and call Jet, compare results with native Jet execution, and cover ABI mismatch and lifecycle failure. Use focused guest/FFI tests; Epoch 11 closeout owns the full suite.

cards.title: Host-runtime packaging and foreign registry publishing
cards.body: Foreign developers must consume Jet libraries through the tools they already use: pip/npm/Maven/NuGet. Wrap exported Jet C surfaces as Python wheels, Node N-API modules, JVM JARs with JNI loading, and NuGet packages, and publish them with one command. This is how Rust won invisible share (maturin/PyO3, napi-rs). Publishing surface is owner-gated: D-ADOPT-PUB1. Gap G5 in the field audit.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Foreign developers consume Jet libraries through pip, npm, Maven and NuGet. `jet publish --to <registry>` derives each package from the one exported ABI, bundles the host runtime, and publishes atomically. Decision D-ADOPT-PUB1=A is ratified. Field-audit gap G5.

**Current state**
- `Source/main.rs:3741` parses `--to` and hands off to `run_publish`.
- `Source/Publish/ForeignPackage.rs`:
  - :23-49 `ForeignRegistry::{PyPi,Npm,Maven,NuGet}` parse/as_str.
  - :98 `build_foreign_package` (archive into `.jet/build/foreign`) and :121 `publish_foreign_package`.
  - :661-668 per-registry entries (wheel/zip, npm tar.gz).
  - :2395 env endpoints (`JET_PYPI_URL`, `JET_NPM_REGISTRY`, `JET_MAVEN_URL`, `JET_NUGET_SOURCE`).
  - :2428/:2450/:2497 `file://` offline registry.
  - :2453+ network publishers (twine, …).
- There are no `#[test]` items in ForeignPackage.rs and no `tests/*publish*`, so every criterion is unexercised. Blocker #1343 is done.
- Ownership handoff (#3398): use the existing jet-ffi-descriptor-v1 contract and the per-language ABI leaves. #3401 owns C extraction. #3402 owns the native Nixpkgs-to-Jet translation (Jetpack only, Hangar only, no Nix implementation dependency).

**Changes**
1. Jet compiler: none. The export surface comes from the existing descriptor.
2. New `tests/foreign_publish.rs`, which builds a small `#Export(c)` library (scalar, Text, typed error) and runs these:
   - `publish_file_registry_<eco>` for each ecosystem: `jet publish --to <eco>` with `JET_FOREIGN_REGISTRY_URL=file://<scratch>`, then install into a consumer in a fresh dir with PATH stripped of `jet`:
     - `pip install --no-index --find-links`
     - `npm install <tgz>`
     - `javac`/`java` against the jar with its JNI loader
     - `dotnet restore` from the local source
   - Each consumer calls the function and asserts the result and the typed error.
   - Metadata agreement: version, platform tag, license, SBOM, signature/provenance and source identity equal across the four packages.
   - Hostile cases: duplicate version, corrupt artifact (flip one byte before upload), interrupted upload (kill mid-copy), missing runtime, ABI drift (changed export after build) and bad credentials. For each, assert that the registry directory is unchanged, there is no partial file, and the secret never appears in stdout/stderr.
3. Fix every defect found in `ForeignPackage.rs`. There is no second publish path.
4. `Docs/`: the first-minute workflow per ecosystem, in the existing publish reference.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test foreign_publish` → all rows pass. An absent toolchain prints `MISSING <eco>` and fails that row: it does not pass.
- Full-suite proof belongs to the Epoch 11 closeout.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: this is the Source/ CLI publish command and its tests only.

**Dependencies**
None open. #1343 is done.

The blocker #1343 is done, so the clean-consumer and hostile-failure proofs are all that remain. Evidence: Source/main.rs:3741 (`flag_value(&raw, "--to")` → run_publish); Source/Publish/ForeignPackage.rs:34-37 (PyPi/Npm/Maven/NuGet registry parse), :2450-2497 (file:// registry publish). There are no #[test] items in ForeignPackage.rs and no tests/*publish*. #1343 is done. Proof owed: Add focused tests/foreign_publish.rs: for each of pypi/npm/maven/nuget, publish an exported Jet library to a file:// registry. Then, in a clean environment without jet on PATH, install and call it (pip install, npm install, a JVM loader and dotnet restore where available), asserting typed results and errors. Also cover hostile cases: duplicate version, corrupt artifact, interrupted upload and missing runtime all fail atomically with no partial publish and no leaked secret. cards.title: Foreign build hosts invoke Jet: CMake, Gradle, Bazel, MSBuild
cards.body: Large codebases change build systems last. D-BUILDLEGACY1 wraps foreign builds inside Jet's graph; this card is the reverse direction: first-party rules so existing builds compile Jet sources and link Jet archives as one step. CMake toolchain file + find_package(Jet), Gradle plugin, Bazel rules, MSBuild targets, prioritized by target market. Gap G3 in the field audit. No new Jet-side syntax expected; raise a ballot only if one appears.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
First-party CMake, Gradle, Bazel and MSBuild integrations let existing builds compile Jet sources and link Jet archives as one step (reverse of D-BUILDLEGACY1; field-audit gap G3), all through the canonical Jet driver/export path with typed artifacts.

**Current state**
- Adapters exist: Tools/foreign-build-hosts/cmake/{JetToolchain.cmake,FindJet.cmake}, gradle/jet-library.gradle, bazel/jet_library.bzl, msbuild/Jet.Library.targets, shared runner jet-library.sh/.ps1, BUILD.bazel/WORKSPACE.bazel. Fixtures: tests/fixtures/foreign_build_hosts/{bazel,cmake,cmake-cc,gradle,make-cc,msbuild}.
- tests/foreign_build_hosts.rs checks files statically (`adapters_use_one_jet_library_runner_and_fail_closed_outputs` :37, `representative_projects_declare_exact_inputs_and_stay_under_ten_lines` :87, `host_descriptors_are_small_and_route_to_native_library_targets` :123) and runs only the shared runner (`shared_runner_publishes_only_after_a_successful_jet_export` :189, unix).
- No real host build, incremental latency, cancellation or clean-machine proof exists. Canonical ownership after #3398: jet-ffi-descriptor-v1 contract; #3401 owns C extraction; #3402 owns Nixpkgs translation.

**Changes**
1. Add host-gated tests to tests/foreign_build_hosts.rs that drive each real tool on its fixture in a scratch copy: clean build, no-op, Jet source change, API change, target change; assert correct invalidation and record latency.
2. Failure cases: missing/stale `jet`, incompatible ABI, parallel builds, cancellation (kill during export), diagnostic failure, partial outputs — no valid-looking host artifact or stamp remains.
3. Fix adapter defects the runs expose inside the four owned surfaces only; each adapter invalidates on any declared Jet source, tool, target, ABI or receipt-input change.
4. Diagnostics from `jet` propagate to the host tool's error output with file:line.
5. Document usage (≤10 maintained lines per host) in Tools/foreign-build-hosts/README or the reference docs; clean-machine run on a fresh container.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test foreign_build_hosts` passes on a host with cmake, gradle and bazel installed (msbuild on Windows), with the new host-gated tests reporting each tool as run or unavailable.
Full-suite proof belongs to Epoch 11 closeout.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: host build tooling; no compiler change.

**Dependencies**
#1344 (hermetic `jet cc`, building) for the cmake-cc and make-cc fixtures.

cards.title: Mixed-repo developer experience across the language boundary
cards.body: A 95%-Java / 5%-Jet repository must feel first-class: mixed-language stack traces, debugging that steps across the FFI boundary, profiling attributed to Jet symbols inside a foreign host, coverage aggregation, test orchestration, and CI recipes for incremental adoption. UL11 names debugger/source-map integration only; the rest is unowned. Gap G6 in the field audit. UX/DX is the acceptance bar: the boundary should be invisible in daily work.
cards.plan:
## Goal
A repository that is 95% Java (or C/C++, JS/Python) and 5% Jet feels first-class. Mixed stack traces, debugger stepping across FFI, profiler attribution to Jet symbols, coverage aggregation, test orchestration and CI recipes all read one versioned symbol/source/provenance model, and honest "unavailable" states replace wrong locations.

## Current state
- The Jet-consumes-foreign direction is covered on unix by `tests/polyglot_systems.rs`: `mixed_run_workflow` (:625-691), stale-descriptor recovery (:694) and `mixed_repo_edit_test_debug_profile_and_recovery_workflows` (:1089). These exercise check, debug build, `test --coverage`, a debug session, perf capture/view and recovery for C/C++/JVM/JS/Python dependencies. The provenance schema is `jet-ffi-bridge-provenance-v1` (:443).
- Missing: the foreign-host direction (Java/C/Node hosting a Jet export), mixed stack traces, cross-FFI stepping and one shared model feeding debugger, profiler and coverage.
- The debugger host is `crates/jet-debug/src/{Dap,LineMap,Native,EventObservation,Inferior}.rs`. Rust-side source-map emission is in archived `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/{MIRRust,MIRWeb}.rs`. The Jet emitter is `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/`.

## Changes
1. Provenance emission: put the export symbol, source span and ABI identity into the `jet-ffi-bridge-provenance-v1` record from `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit` (Rust and Web emit). Until #218 cuts over, the shipped binary keeps its current emission path. Mirror only the fields the host consumers need.
2. Host consumers read only that record. `crates/jet-debug/src/LineMap.rs` and `Native.rs` get mixed frames and cross-boundary step. The Source/ perf command gets Jet symbol attribution. `jet test --coverage` merges foreign coverage. Stripped, stale, ABI-mismatched or mixed-version artifacts produce an explicit `unavailable` state, never a plausible wrong location.
3. Add a guest-direction fixture: a small JVM or C host plus one Node host loading a Jet export (#1343 contract), with callbacks, a Jet panic, a foreign exception and a second thread.
4. Document the CI recipe for incremental adoption in `Docs/` and add a `tests/suites.txt` entry. Remove any competing mapping.

## Proof
- The added criterion.
- `cargo test --test polyglot_systems -- mixed_repo_edit_test_debug_profile_and_recovery_workflows` and `cargo test --test debug` stay green.
- Hostile cases (stripped binary, attach denial, disconnect, partial coverage) print `unavailable` in the test output.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: debugger, profiler, coverage and test orchestration are host tooling. Emission changes are small.

## Dependencies
None open: #180 and #1343 are done. Full-suite proof belongs to the Epoch 11 closeout.

cards.title: Single write borrow of one place splits AOT from JIT
cards.body:
Split from #1199's third review finding. A lone `&place` write borrow never reaches the split-view planner in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs split_view_plan, because a plan needs two or more candidates. AOT then borrows a temporary clone and silently drops the write; the JIT applies it. Not taskgroup-specific — it reproduces with no concurrency at all.

Measured matrix (run = default jet run, aot = jet build). 'plan' is the one-line gate `group.len() == 1 && candidates[group[0]].write`:

  case                                   no plan (run/aot)   with plan (run/aot)   correct
  ps[0] via +=, plain local list          12 / 10 WRONG       12 / 12               12
  taskgroup child, one borrow             12 / 10 WRONG       12 / 12               12
  a :: &ps[0]; a.position = 42            42 / 1 WRONG        1 WRONG / 42          42
  &w.ps[0] through a &W parameter         1 WRONG / 1 WRONG   E0956 / 42            42
  &grid[0][1] nested index                2 WRONG / 2 WRONG   E0956 / 2 WRONG       42

Planning the lone case is therefore not the fix on its own: it corrects AOT for the simple shapes but makes the JIT wrong for `view.field = v`, and the JIT refuses nested and through-parameter owners with E0956. The gate was reverted on that evidence; the last two rows are wrong on BOTH tiers today and predate #1199.
cards.plan: Fix the JIT split-view path first so a one-region plan is lowered correctly, including `view.field = value` assignment and nested or through-parameter owners, then re-enable the lone-write case in split_view_plan. Close only when every row of the matrix above reads the correct value on AOT and default jet run, with no E0956. Add each row as a case in tests/ownership.rs or a new tier test.

cards.title: Interpolation debug-label shorthand (Python f'{x=}' equivalent)
cards.body: From the 2026-07-31 video-mining audit (Indently Python series): Python's f"{name=}" — printing "name = value" without typing the name twice — was the top debugging ergonomic across six videos. Jet has S8 interpolation and the #-selector rail ({value#Debug}, {value#Fixed(n)}), but no way to print an expression's own source text next to its value. Today users write print("count = {count}"), duplicating the name; the copies drift when the expression changes. New user-typeable syntax -> owner ballot (I7). Ballot D-FMT-INTERP2 on this card presents the options. Acceptance on ratify: Syntax.rs entry, example + golden proving identical output on AOT and default jet run (I9), snapshot for the invalid-use diagnostic (I4).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship D-FMT-INTERP2=A: trailing equals in an interpolation hole prints expression text, then " = ", then the value. Example: print("{count=}") → count = 3.

## Acceptance (ratified)
- Syntax.rs entry for the trailing-equals form (I7).
- syntax-decisions.md log for D-FMT-INTERP2=A.
- Grammars regenerated; snapshots blessed.
- Example + golden prove identical output on default jet run and AOT (I9).
- Invalid use (empty hole, wrong position) gets one diagnostic with a UI snapshot (I4).
- Composes with selectors: {x=#Fixed(2)} labels, then formats.

## Steps
1. Parser/sema: accept {expr=} inside string interpolation; keep # selector rail unchanged.
2. Lowering: emit source text + " = " + Display of the value (same path as a bare hole).
3. Example under examples/features/ (or strings/) with golden; prove AOT + jet run.
4. Diagnostic + snapshot for misuse.
5. Verify skill syntax chores.

## Owned paths
crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, parser/sema/codegen interpolation paths, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, examples + goldens, UI snapshots.
