cards.title: Probe: can a Shared<T> ownership cycle leak in v1?
cards.body: From the 2026-07-31 video-mining audit (weakref video, top comment on C++ shared_ptr cycles). Question: is a reference cycle constructible through Shared<T> (Arc + lock handle, D-SHARED-API1=A) in v1 — e.g. Shared<A> whose payload stores a Shared<B> whose payload stores the first handle — and if so, does anything diagnose or collect it? D-OPTGC1=A's traced collector covers cycles only inside opted GC scopes; Shared<T> sits outside them. v1's no-stored-references rule blocks reference cycles, but Shared<T> is an owned handle value, so the usual argument may not apply. Deliverable: an adversarial example set (attempt cycle construction across struct payloads, lists, task captures); either (a) sema rejects each with a named diagnostic, or (b) a leak reproduces — then file the follow-up design card. No weakref surface is proposed; that would be a second mechanism (I8) vs the GC path.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Answer one question with evidence: can Shared<T> (or similar shared ownership) form a cycle that never frees in v1?

## Best path
This is a probe, not a new feature. Do not invent weak references. Jet already has GC for promoted cycles (see examples/features/memory/gc_cyclic.jet under #Policy(gc)). Shared is a different ownership path — prove whether it can leak.

## Steps
1. Build the smallest reproduction matrix: two Shared boxes that point at each other; a list that stores Shared to a parent; a Shared that captures itself in a closure/task if the type system allows it.
2. Run each case under default jet run and AOT. Watch process memory or a free/drop counter if one exists; otherwise use a finalizer/drop side effect or GC stats the runtime already exposes.
3. Outcomes:
   - If every case frees (or sema rejects the construction with a named diagnostic): keep one regression example + golden, close the card.
   - If a leak reproduces: stop. File a follow-up design card. Do not add weakref here (that would be a second mechanism vs the GC path — I8).
4. No owner ballot unless the follow-up needs a new surface.

## Owned paths
examples/features/memory/ (new probe example), related Shared/GC runtime paths only as needed for measurement.

cards.title: Map merge/union API with explicit conflict rule
cards.body: From the 2026-07-31 video-mining audit (25-tips video: Python dict | union; commenter asked which value wins on key conflict). Jet's [K: V] Map has no confirmed merge/union in the spec; "merge" in code is the struct-Patch method (diff/merge pair) and "union" is the Set method. Deliverable: (1) confirm whether Map merge exists on any tier; (2) if absent, add a Core-lib Map merge with an explicit, documented conflict rule (follow the §6 structural Merge precedent; last-wins like Python unless a stronger reason emerges), full I9 tier parity, example + golden, and doc row in syntax-decisions Core table. Library API only — no new syntax expected; raise a ballot only if a genuine user-typeable surface choice emerges.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Add Core `Map.merge` with an explicit conflict rule. Confirm no existing Map merge on any tier first. Library API only — no new syntax.

## Ratified law
D-MAP-MERGE1=E — one method: `Map.merge(self, other, conflict: ((K, V, V) => V)? = None)`.
- Omit `conflict` → right wins (beginner overlay).
- Pass `conflict:` → callback result per shared key (expert control).
One name, one idea. Full I9 in Prelude; engines marshall only.

## Build steps

cards.title: Function values in collections crash both engine tiers (JIT segfault / AOT ICE)
cards.body:
Sema accepts function values stored in collections, but no engine tier can run them; behavior diverges per tier (I9 violation, I3 acceptance hole).

Repro 1 — list of named fns:
  fn double(n: Int) => Int = n * 2
  fn triple(n: Int) => Int = n * 3
  fn run() { fns :: [double, triple]  loop f, fns { print(f(10)) } }
Default jet run (JIT): works, prints 20/30. jet run --release (AOT): ICE exit 101 — generated Rust fails with 'Box<dyn Fn(i64) -> i64>: Clone' on iter().cloned().

Repro 2 — string->function dispatch map:
  commands :: [String: fn(String) => String].{ "lower": lower, "quote": quote }
  ... commands.get(name) matched with .Val(f) -> f(text)
Default jet run (JIT): segfault exit 139. AOT: ICE exit 101 — Option::cloned() on non-Clone Box<dyn Fn>.

Spec intent (S47, docs/spec/spec.md:1940-1952) says named fns coerce to function values and escaping lambdas may be stored in bindings/struct fields — so these programs are meant to be valid; fix belongs in codegen (e.g. Rc/Arc<dyn Fn> or borrowed access instead of Box + .cloned()), not in narrowing sema. No new syntax, dependency, or carve-out needed — no owner gate.

Found while mining https://youtu.be/d7dhT2cBkJE (Python dispatch-table idiom smoke test), 2026-07-31.

Make function values in lists/maps runnable on every tier with one meaning (I9). Fix AOT ICE (Box<dyn Fn> not Clone) and JIT map-dispatch segfault; keep sema acceptance (S47).

## Law
- Named fns coerce to function values; storing them in collections is valid.
- No new syntax, deps, or I9 carve-outs. No jit_gaps parking.
- Prefer Rc/Arc (or borrow without clone) over Box+cloned in emit; engines marshal only.

## Steps
1. Reproduce both cards' repros on JIT and AOT; capture failure modes.
2. Fix AOT emit for function-typed list/map elements (clone/share strategy).
3. Fix JIT host path for map.get → call through function values.

5. Confirm no jit_gaps entry; independent review + criteria verify; done.

cards.title: Write windows cannot flow out of a callee inside an aggregate
cards.body: A live exclusive window (ViewMut<T> or Pin<T>) cannot be returned from a function inside a struct, nor accepted as a parameter and stored, without the ownership checker reporting E0204 or E0212. Return-view provenance was built for read slices: a 'from owner' clause marks the returned aggregate a read view of the owner, so writing through the stored window is then rejected.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Let a library take a caller-owned place and hand back an aggregate that stores an exclusive window into it, with the same provenance proof read views already get.

## Why now
Card #1200 (Pin<T>) met criteria #1 and #3 but left #2, #4, and #5 open on exactly this. The same limitation blocks any ViewMut-storing library API, so it is one shared fix, not pin-specific work.

## Repro
    fn attach(label: String, node: &Node) => Queue from node {
        return Queue.{label: ~label, head: mem.pin(&node)}
    }

Writing through `queue.head` afterwards is E0212: "queue is a live read view into node". Dropping the `from` clause instead loses the hidden Rust lifetime and rustc rejects the generated signature (I2).

## Owned paths
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs (return-view provenance, call-site composition)
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Validation.rs (declared `from` contract)
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/functions.rs (hidden view lifetime on write windows)
- tests/ownership.rs, tests/pin.rs

## Scope
In: write-access provenance for returned and stored windows; the `from` clause carrying access, not only the owner set; call-site composition for an aggregate that stores a window.
Out: new syntax. The `from` clause and the `Pin<T>` / `ViewMut<T>` spellings are already ratified.

## Acceptance
A library function may accept `&owner` and return an aggregate with a `Pin<T>` or `ViewMut<T>` field; the caller may edit through that field; AOT, Cranelift, and the interpreter agree; provenance escape is still rejected.

cards.title: Reading a place through its owner while a write window is live reaches rustc (I2)
cards.body: Sema allows an ordinary read of an owner while an exclusive window into it is still live. rustc then rejects the generated code with E0503, which I2 classifies as an internal compiler error rather than a user diagnostic.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Reject a read of a place while an exclusive window into it is live, in sema, before rustc sees the code.

## Why
`check_place_change` only fires on changes. A plain read of the owner while a write window is live passes sema and then hits rustc E0503 ("cannot use `x.f` because it was mutably borrowed"), which is an internal compiler error by I2, not a user diagnostic.

## Repro
    node := Node.{payload: 41, hops: 0}
    pinned :: mem.pin(&node)
    if node.payload > 0 {
        pinned.hops += 1
    }
    print("{(pinned.hops)}")

Sema accepts this; rustc rejects the generated Rust. It reproduces with a plain `p :: &node` window too, so it is not pin-specific.

## Owned paths
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs
- tests/ownership.rs, tests/ui/

## Scope
In: a read-while-write-window-live check with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot; the fix should name the window to read through.
Out: relaxing the existing E0212 change rules.

## Acceptance
The repro above is a Jet diagnostic, not an ICE; existing read-view overlap rules are unchanged; a read after the window's last use still compiles.

cards.title: Unify struct field defaults onto `field: T = expr` (retire #Default)
cards.body:
Owner lean (2026-07-31): collapse wire/CLI field defaults from `#Default(expr)` into the same `field: T = expr` spelling used for function parameters (S61). Goal: shorter, clearer surface and free the `#Default` marker slot for higher-value markers/tags on congested paths.

Today (ratified D-SERDE5 / D-CLIFLAG1): field absence defaults use `#Default(expr)`; `=` is reserved for call-site params. Construction literals `Type.{ … }` still require every field.

This card owns the owner decision that amends or keeps that split, then the migration if unify wins (parser/sema/CLI/serde, Syntax.rs, examples, diagnostics, teaching). Construction fill-from-default is in scope for the ballot (whether `=` also fills omitted fields in `Type.{ … }`).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Unify struct field defaults onto `field: T = expr`. Retire `#Default(expr)` for wire/CLI absence defaults. Free the `#Default` marker slot.

## Ratified law
D-FIELDDEF1=C — fields use `=` for absence and for construction fill.
- Same spelling as function parameter defaults (S61).
- Omitted fields in `Type.{ … }` fill from their `=` defaults when every omitted field has one.
- Required fields remain those without `=`.
- Field `=` expressions are compile-time constants, same as today's `#Default`.
Amends D-SERDE5 / D-CLIFLAG1 / construction (E0303).

## Build steps
1. Update `Syntax.rs` and `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`. Run `jet devtools grammars`. Re-bless syntax snapshots.
2. Parser/sema: accept `field: T = expr`; reject or migrate `#Default` with a teaching diagnostic + snapshot (I4).
3. Serde/CLI/construction: absence and partial literals honor `=`. Keep required-field errors for fields without defaults.
4. Migrate examples and Core surfaces that still use `#Default` for field absence.
5. Full I9: same meaning on AOT, default `jet run`, and interpreter when the surface is reached.

## Acceptance / proof
- `#Codable` / `#CLI` structs with `=` defaults work without `#Default`.
- `Serve.{ name: "api" }` fills other `=` fields; missing required fields still error.
- `#Default` on fields is gone or hard-errors with a registered diagnostic + UI snapshot.
- Example + golden green on AOT and default `jet run`.
- Syntax chores from the syntax-group auto-criteria are met.

## Owned paths
`crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs`, parser/sema/codegen serde+CLI paths, diagnostics + snapshots, examples, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`.

cards.title: inspect expand --json: honor the ratified semindex document
cards.body: The cross-facet video mine exposed a concrete D-EXPANDCLI1=A drift. The ruling says the existing global `--json` mode emits a stable semindex-schema document. `Source/CmdExpand.rs` accepts `_json` but always prints human prose. This card restores the ratified contract without adding a command, lens, schema, or analysis path.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make `jet inspect expand --json` truthful and machine-safe under D-EXPANDCLI1=A.

## Work
1. Reuse the canonical semantic-index schema and serializer. Do not invent an expand-only JSON model.
2. Project the selected expand lens or the bare all-lens view from the same checked `ProgramBundle` and sema facts used by human output.
3. Keep human output unchanged. JSON mode emits one document and no human headers or prose.
4. Cover bare, selected, empty, unknown-lens, invalid-program, and deterministic-order cases.
5. Update help, the command spec, snapshots, and tests where the corrected behavior changes their truth.

## Proof
Targeted CLI and schema tests prove valid JSON, stable ordering, exact lens filtering, ordinary diagnostics, and no second analysis or rustc path. A fresh-context reviewer checks D-EXPANDCLI1, I2, I3, I4, and schema reuse.

2. Map every gate and operation span to stable source file, line, and column in human output. Keep mode, reason, policy provenance, obligation state, and nesting readable.
3. Keep one deterministic JSON contract with source provenance and machine positions. Update its schema only when needed for the same navigability facts; do not create a second report model.
4. Cover missing files, unreadable files, malformed source, multi-module gates, missing reasons, tracked and discharged operations, empty reports, ANSI, and `NO_COLOR`.
5. Update CLI help, spec text, snapshots, and examples.

## Canonical surface
- `T.$layout` gets the focused layout object.
- `T.$layout[.field]` gets a typed, rename-safe field fact.
- `T.reflect().layout` returns the same object for full reflection.
- `$name`, `$[ … ]$`, and `T.$layout` are the three contextual `$` forms.
- No alias, fallback parser, compatibility diagnostic, or second fact model.

## Implementation
1. Add the ratified syntax entry in `Syntax.rs`. Accept `$` after member access only for compiler-owned fact names. Do not allow user-declared `$` members.
2. Parse free, chained, and namespaced type expressions consistently. Preserve `$name` splice and `$[ … ]$` expansion parsing.
3. Resolve `T.$layout` in sema as the exact `T.reflect().layout` projection. Keep validation in sema and codegen dumb.
4. Use one `LayoutInfo` and `LayoutField` model. Whole-type and field byte facts are optional when Jet does not guarantee physical layout.
5. Complete `$layout` under a visible Compiler facts group. Complete `[.field]`; support hover, rename, and go-to-definition.
6. Project the same facts through `jet inspect expand --facts layout` human and JSON output. Never query rustc.
7. Replace the rejected layout spelling in active source, docs, examples, tests, help, snapshots, and generated artifacts. Preserve only ratified ballot/history text and unrelated compiler-internal `__name` binders.
8. Regenerate grammars and bless only reviewed snapshots.

## Proof
Test `$name`, `$[ … ]$`, `T.$layout`, chained field selection, unknown compiler facts, user attempts to declare `$` members, source-written dunders, default/C/columnar layouts, optional byte facts, completion, hover, rename, navigation, CLI text/JSON, ANSI, and `NO_COLOR`. Prove every applicable execution tier uses the same semantics. Run a repo-wide search that finds no rejected layout spelling outside Tower history. A fresh reviewer checks the diff and reruns targeted proof.

cards.title: Reconcile S33 generic call arguments once
cards.body: S45 first banned call-site type arguments. D-SERDE6 later authorized `call<T>(...)` as general grammar. cards.plan:

Inference is the default. Any generic free function, namespaced call, or method may use adjacent `call<T>(...)`. Jet never uses Rust `::<T>`. This verdict supersedes S45, D-SERDE6, and D-SHAPE-CONVERT1 call-site clauses.

cards.title: Typed exact-integer and Decimal decoding preserves each valid JSON numeric value
cards.body: Python can parse a JSON number directly as Decimal. Jet turns fractional numbers into Float before typed decode, so exact values can be lost or rejected. The owner must choose one exact number model.
cards.plan:
Scope: D-JSON-EXACTNUM1=A. DataTree keeps its ratified Int/Float meaning (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/JSONDataTree.rs, render_datatree_json line 17); a typed Decimal or BigInt decode target reads the original JSON number token text directly, before any Float conversion, so exact values never round-trip through binary64. One tokenizer feeds two destinations: the existing DataTree builder, and a typed visitor path for Decimal/BigInt fields. json.canonical(json.parse(text)?)? keeps its one-call D-JSONCANON1 contract unchanged (do not amend it, per option A vs B). Blocked on #1394 (edition-2027 DataTree/Codable split) -- #1394 owns creating the edition-2027 tokenizer entry point; do not build a second one against the frozen edition-2026 crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/JSONCodec.rs (its JSONParser/JSON enum at lines 95-296 stay byte-frozen per #1394's own plan step 2).

SEQUENCING AMENDMENT (this audit, 2026-08-06): D-TYPE2-NUM1=A (ratified) folds BigInt into Int -- "the number tower: one grid, and BigInt folds into Int" -- and #1436 (D-INTBIG1=A, also ratified) is the card that makes default Int arbitrary-precision. As of this audit, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:811 still defines a standalone JetBigInt struct and #1436's own criteria are all open (BigInt has not yet folded into Int in the tree). Building this card's typed-visitor path against JetBigInt today is correct FOR NOW, but becomes throwaway/rework once #1436 lands and JetBigInt retires. To avoid two homes for the same exact-integer decode work: block this card on #1436 in addition to #1394, and when both have landed, the "BigInt decode target" in every step below means the arbitrary-precision default Int, not a surviving JetBigInt type. If owner sequencing forces this card to ship before #1436, implement against JetBigInt as scoped below but file the Int retarget as a plain implementation follow-up (no new decision needed -- D-TYPE2-NUM1 already settled the direction).

Approach (execute after #1394 AND #1436 land, per the amendment above):
1. Confirm the exact-number gap first: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingTraits.rs 'impl user_Decode for jet_std::JetDecimal' (line ~202-210) currently only accepts DataTree::Text and DataTree::Int, erroring on DataTree::Float -- meaning a fractional JSON number decoded into a dynamic tree first cannot reach Decimal at all today. Locate #1394's edition-2027 equivalent decode path and confirm the same gap exists there before patching it.
2. In #1394's edition-2027 tokenizer, add a typed visitor mode alongside the DataTree builder: when the destination field is JetDecimal (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs) or the exact-integer destination (post-#1436: the default arbitrary-precision Int; pre-#1436: JetBigInt, CommonTypes.rs line ~800), the number token's raw text (mantissa, optional fraction, optional exponent) feeds JetDecimal::from_str / the integer parser directly -- never through DataTree::Float. Whole-value decode (json.decode<T>) and stream decode share the same tokenizer and visitor.
3. Extend crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingTraits.rs user_Decode impls for JetDecimal and the exact-integer destination to accept the typed-visitor projection path in addition to their current Text/Int cases.
4. Define errors per the ballot: target mismatch (schema expects Decimal/exact-integer but token is non-numeric), overflow (only meaningful pre-#1436, since arbitrary-precision Int has no overflow per D-INTBIG1), non-finite input (NaN/Infinity are not valid JSON tokens -- confirm this is already rejected), unsupported canonical output (a Decimal/exact-integer value that cannot round-trip through json.canonical's existing Int/Float contract), and configured limits (digit count / exponent range) -- reuse the existing EncodingError kind vocabulary in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingTraits.rs rather than inventing a new error type.
5. Hostile test coverage in tests/encoding_corpus.rs and tests/encoding_parity.rs: exponent forms (1e30, 1E-5), scale (12.340 keeps trailing zero, 100 stays whole), large integers beyond i64/i128, adjacent-precision values (0.1 vs 0.10 vs 1e-1), streaming decode, and whole-value decode. Add Python differential fixtures matching json.loads(payload, parse_float=Decimal, parse_int=int) per the ballot's Python comparison.
6. Prove parity across comptime, interpreter, JIT, and AOT per I9 -- the typed visitor is Prelude-only logic (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/**), so AOT emit, jet-jit, and jet-comptime must call the same Prelude decode symbol, not re-implement number parsing.
7. docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md and docs/reference/core-library.md: document the exact-number model and its error kinds, naming Int (not BigInt) as the exact-integer destination if #1436 has landed by then.
8. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md or docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md decision log: append the dated D-JSON-EXACTNUM1=A entry, and cross-reference D-TYPE2-NUM1=A if the exact-integer destination was retargeted to Int.
Proof (post-#1394 and post-#1436, targeted, not full suite):
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test encoding_corpus -- decimal bigint json
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test encoding_parity -- json
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- <new example name>
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/<new-example>.jet (I9 parity across AOT/JIT/interpreter)
Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/JSONDataTree.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingTraits.rs, tests/encoding_corpus.rs, tests/encoding_parity.rs, docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md, docs/reference/core-library.md, examples/features/**. Do not touch crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/JSONCodec.rs (edition-2026 frozen).

cards.title: Signature-preserving callable policies
cards.body: Jet has no proven typed replacement for decorators. Prototype complete choices, obtain an owner ruling, then ship the selected mechanism without violating ratified metaprogram limits.
cards.plan:
Scope: D-CALLPOLICY1=E is ratified (2026-08-04): a declaration marker sets the default policy chain (beginner path, zero ceremony at the call site); an explicit apply(...) at a call site replaces that default with exactly the chain it names (expert override); apply with no policies yields the bare function. Both spellings use one typed policy value and one signature-preservation law: no policy may widen effects, errors, access, or view provenance, and public labels/defaults/zones from #1393 must survive unchanged. Blocked on #1393 (shipped, see this audit's #1393 note -- do not wait for its board criteria to flip, the underlying param_contract machinery already exists).

CRITICAL PRE-IMPLEMENTATION GATE -- resolve before writing the parser rule (also raised in this report's top-level "gates"): the ratified ballot's example spelling, "#Policy(retry(3), trace(\"users.load\")) +fn load_user(...)", COLLIDES with an existing, already-shipped marker of the exact same name at the exact same grammar position. crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/math_layout.rs:412 already defines MARKER_POLICY = "Policy" for D-MEM1/S7/D-POLICY-WORD1: a scoped compiler-policy marker ("#Policy(no_alloc)") that is legal at Function scope (crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs:7 PolicyScope::{Organization,Package,Module,Function,Block}; PolicyKey::{NoAlloc,ZeroRc,ArenaBounded,Unsafe,ScopedGc,ExplicitUnits}, Policy.rs:14-19). Both "#Policy(no_alloc) +fn f() {...}" (existing, ships today) and "#Policy(retry(3)) +fn f() {...}" (newly ratified) parse at the identical position before a function declaration. The D-CALLPOLICY1 ballot's adversarial review never checked this existing marker. This needs an explicit owner call before the parser change lands -- see the gate entry for the three live options (disambiguate by argument shape: a closed bare-identifier set vs. call-expression arguments; rename the new marker, e.g. #Wrap/#Around; or fold the two mechanisms so scoped compiler policies and callable-value policies share one registry). Do not silently pick one in code.

Approach (once the gate above is resolved):
1. Model the complete checked callable signature reusing #1393's shipped param_contract: public labels, local names, defaults, access modes, types, effects, errors, result, views, generics, and source identity (crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs Type::Fn).
2. Add the typed policy value: a policy is a function from a callable value to a callable value of the identical checked signature. Define it in crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/ alongside Type::Fn; enforce signature-preservation as a directional assignability check (a policy-wrapped value must equal the input's full signature, including param_contract) at the same site #1443 fixes contract laundering (crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs PartialEq) -- reuse that fix, don't duplicate it.
3. Declaration marker (whichever name the gate settles on): crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/marker_groups.rs, following the existing marker-group dispatch pattern; expansion happens after signature checking (S26/D-METADEPTH1/2/D-METADERIVE1 -- compile time cannot create a type, this only wraps a value).
4. apply(...) builtin: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/helpers_call_values.rs (function-value call-site handling) plus a new builtin entry; apply(f) with no policies yields the bare function (identity), apply(p1, p2, f) builds exactly that chain and replaces, never stacks under, the declared default.
5. Lower identically at every tier per I9: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/ (AOT/JIT shared), crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/dispatch/eval_method.rs.
6. Diagnostics: hidden authority, changed errors/effects/access, label loss, view-lifetime widening, duplicate declared markers -- each registered with a UI snapshot.
7. Formatter, tree-sitter/tmGrammar/vscode/zed grammars (regenerate via jet self devtools grammars), Source/LSP/Features.rs completion.
8. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: append the dated D-CALLPOLICY1=E entry naming the implementing card and the resolved marker-name gate.
9. Examples/goldens: retry+trace over a fallible network-shaped function, proving the declared-default vs call-site-override replace rule and the bare-function apply(f) case; prove under interpreter/JIT/AOT.
Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/math_layout.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs, crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/marker_groups.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/helpers_call_values.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/**, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/dispatch/eval_method.rs, Source/LSP/Features.rs, editors/**, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, tests/ui/*, examples/features/**.

questions.text: The point of this ballot and functionality is not at a;; c;ear to me. Would these not be markers/meta tags/traits/policies? I dont get it, need discussion
questions.answer: You are right that these shapes overlap — that overlap is exactly what this ballot decides. The job: wrap a function with behavior around each call (retry, cache, trace) without changing how callers call it. Python spells this @retry(3) above the def. The ballot picks where Jet spells it. Option B is literally a marker: #Policy(retry(3), trace(...)) on the declaration — the marker-plane answer. Option C spells it where the wrapped value is made: load_user_traced :: apply(retry(3), load_user). Option A is no new mechanism: you hand-write a wrapper function that repeats the whole signature, and the copy drifts when the original changes. Option D is a registry far from the code. Traits do not cover this job: a trait says what a type can do; a policy is a runtime value that wraps one specific function. So the live choice is B vs C. B: policy named once on the declaration — concise, but it changes the function for every caller and is invisible at call sites. C: policy named where the value is formed — the command tool and the web worker can wrap the same function differently, and a reader sees the wrapping where it happens. The rec is C for that locality; if you prefer all meta to stay on the # plane, B is the coherent pick and the ballot supports it. If the whole feature feels unnecessary, A ships nothing new.

questions.text: What about suiting beginner magic expert control by having both b and c? B is the default when something is called but maybe c can be an intentional override so you can enforce a SPECIFIC policy at a callsite but otherwise have localized control of a policy at the definition?
questions.answer: Yes — that combination works, and it is now option E on the ballot with the recommendation moved to it. It stays one mechanism: the marker and the application attach the same typed policy values, just at two points. The declaration marker is the beginner default: a library author writes #Policy(retry(3), trace(...)) once, and every plain call gets safe behavior with zero ceremony. The application is the expert override: apply(retry(1), load_user) at a call site enforces exactly that chain — the declared default does not stack under it, so what you read at the override is the whole truth. One rule had to be pinned for 'enforce a SPECIFIC policy' to mean something: apply replaces the declared chain rather than wrapping around it, and apply with no policies yields the bare function. The accepted cost: a plain call's default is visible at the declaration, not the call site — the same tradeoff Python decorators make — and any call site that cares can override locally.

questions.text: I’m inclined to go with your recommendation but WHAT THE FUCK is the =[!Mem.Alloc]=> doing in a marker position. That ONLY is the effect syntax for functions and lambdas, potentially markers… it can never go elsewhere.
questions.answer: You are right, and that was a sample error, not a proposal. The denial row is part of the signature effect arrow, exactly as MEM1 ratified: fn render(frame: Frame) =[!Mem.Alloc]=> Pixels { ... }. It never stands above a function; only markers stand there. cards.title: Zip family: n-ary inputs, length policy, and padding
cards.body:
`jet_iter_zip` currently pairs one receiver with one other input and stops at the shortest. D-ZIPLEN1=D already defines the safe family: strict `zip`, intentional `zip_short`, and longest `zip_pad`.

This card now completes the Python-equivalent family. It covers free calls such as `zip(a, b, c)`, equivalent receiver methods, heterogeneous typed rows, optional `None` padding, and explicit per-column fills. The family must support arbitrary input count without a dynamic `Any` row or a silent arity cap.

Exit criteria: D-ZIPPAD1 ratified; authority docs updated; sema preserves every input type and row field; one Prelude family serves free and method calls; AOT, JIT, interpreter, and web parity proven where applicable; examples and golden tests cover two, three, and many inputs, strict, short, padded, optional, common-fill, per-column-fill, lazy, and mismatch cases.
cards.plan:
1. Ratify D-ZIPPAD1 as the complete family contract. Keep D-ZIPLEN1's strict `zip`, intentional `zip_short`, and longest `zip_pad`; add n-ary free functions, equivalent methods, typed heterogeneous rows, default `None`, and typed per-column fills.
2. Record the type-pack, arity, row-field, method, and free-function rules in `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, `docs/spec/spec.md`, `docs/reference/core-library.md`, and the decision log.
3. Extend the existing variadic inference and call model to preserve each input element type. Add sema checks for minimum arity, fill shape, fill types, length policy, and stable generated row fields.
4. Implement one lazy Prelude family for `zip`, `zip_short`, and `zip_pad`. Make free calls and receiver methods marshal into that family; do not put policy in AOT emit, JIT hosts, or interpreter ambient.
5. Migrate two-input code, examples, symbol indexes, snapshots, and tests. Add n-way heterogeneous examples plus optional `None`, common-fill, per-column-fill, strict mismatch, short intent, lazy unknown-length, and method/free equivalence cases.
6. Prove parser → sema → TIR → AOT → default `jet run` → JIT/dev → interpreter, with web proof when the surface reaches web. Run an independent review for type safety, API shape, arity limits, and I9 drift before closeout.

cards.title: Decide reversible call syntax for prelude free functions
cards.body:
Owner request: make `print(x.get())` and `x.get().print()` both legal. Today only the first works, because `core.io.print` is a free function and Jet declined uniform function call syntax (D-UFCS1, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:256) with no surviving rationale.

Jet already has half the mechanism: D-EXTMETH1 (syntax-decisions.md:185) lets `fn Type.method(self)` at top level be dot-called, under a same-source-module orphan rule. `Display` (D-DISPLAYDBG1) gives `print` a receiver bound. So the owner's example may be reachable as a Core library declaration rather than a language change.

The cost is not aesthetic. Symmetric call syntax makes method lookup search every free function whose first parameter accepts the receiver, needs return-type-directed inference that D-LAMBDAINFER1 explicitly refuses, and hides D-MEM1 capability sigils behind a call site that no longer shows which argument is the receiver.

cards.body:

cards.title: Close List and Map surface gaps and the remove naming trap
cards.body:
Two concrete gaps and one trap, from `list_method_return` and `map_method_return` (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs).

Gap one: `Map.keys()` and `Map.values()` return eager `[K]` and `[V]`. Python, Java, and C# all return lazy views. Every membership test or scan over a large map allocates a full copy.

Gap two: List has `count_by(pred)` but no `count(value)`, and no `extend`/concat verb. `Bag<T>` has `count(value)`; List does not.

The trap: `List.remove` takes an index in Jet and a value in Python. Same name, opposite meaning, no error — a migrant writes `xs.remove(3)` meaning the value three and silently deletes the fourth item. Rust splits these as `remove(i)` and `retain`; Python splits `pop(i)` and `remove(v)`. Owner-gated because it renames a public surface: ballot D-LISTREMOVE1.

Jet already wins here and must keep it: pop, get, first, last, min, max, and index_of all return optionals where Python raises.

Exit criteria: lazy key and value views; the missing List verbs; ratified remove naming implemented with a migration of every in-repo caller; examples plus golden output; I9 parity.

questions.text: What about swift style where an unlabeled value is the logical default and a labeled value can choose either
questions.answer:
Ballot updated: option E now carries this idea, and it is the recommendation.

Half of the idea works, and it is the half that matters. Under D-APILABEL1=A, ratified today, a label-only zone lets one name carry both meanings: fn remove(*, at: Int = ..., value: T = ...). So remove(at: 3) and remove(value: 3) both read right, with no new names and no overloading.

The other half reopens the bug. If an unlabeled value keeps a logical default, then scores.remove(3) still compiles and still means one of the two. That line is Maya's whole story. Position as the default leaves the Python author wrong. Value as the default leaves every current Jet reader wrong, which is why option C loses. An explicit default is still an invisible one.

Swift does not do it either. Array has no unlabeled remove. remove(at:) is the only spelling and the label is required, so Swift's real answer is mandatory label, no default.

Two methods named remove, told apart by their labels, would need overloading. The breadth review of D-APILABEL1 tested overloads and turned them down as a second mechanism, in the version you ratified.

So option E keeps your shape, drops the default, and stops a bare remove(3) with a report naming both spellings. Its one cost: the signature says two optional labels while the real rule is exactly one, so sema needs one written check for a bare call or a doubled call.

cards.title: Executable single-file programs: direct launch and shebang
cards.body: A lone Jet file needs no project file, but it cannot yet act as an executable script. Add one direct launch path without a second script language or metadata system. The owner must choose whether Jet accepts an operating-system shebang as source launch metadata.
cards.plan:
## Grounded plan (D-SCRIPT-ENTRY1=A: first-line shebang)

Canonical: `#!/usr/bin/env jet` as byte 0 of the file. Lexer skips it. No new
CLI flag, no new resolver, no project file. Owner ruling: this is OS syntax,
not Jet syntax (see card question qknub48i answer) — do not invent a marker.

Parser/lexer:
1. Entry point is `pub fn lex(src: &str)` in crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Terminators.rs:15
   (also crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Scan.rs::lex_raw). Before scanning, if
   `src.as_bytes()` starts with `#!`, skip bytes through the first `\n`
   (or EOF) and do not emit a token for that line.
2. Line/col spans for every later token must still report the real source
   line (line 2 onward), not shift left. Check how the lexer currently
   advances its line counter per newline and confirm the skipped line counts
   as line 1 exactly like a comment line would.
3. `#!` appearing anywhere except byte offset 0 (e.g. after leading
   whitespace, or on a later line) is rejected with a new diagnostic —
   reserve the next free E-code per docs/spec/diagnostics.md "Adding a
   diagnostic"; what: "a shebang line is only recognized at the very start
   of the file"; fix: "move `#!...` to line 1, or delete it".
4. Direct-file resolution already exists (Source/main.rs ~line 1761, "a
   `.jet` file can define..."); confirm a shebang-prefixed file still
   resolves through the exact same path as `jet <file>.jet` with zero branch
   added there — the shebang is invisible below the lexer.
5. No dependency header, no option grammar, no interpretation of anything
   after `#!` — the whole rest of the line is opaque OS text Jet never reads.

Docs/registry (I7):
6. crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs: add a comment-only line citing
   D-SCRIPT-ENTRY1=A next to the other "adds no token" comments (see
   D-SHAPE3a, D-ARROW-CONTROL1 block ~lines 56-110) — the shebang mints no
   Jet constant, so there is nothing to add beyond the decision-ID note.
7. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: one log entry for D-SCRIPT-ENTRY1=A next to
   the other 2026-08-04 entries.
8. Run `jet devtools grammars` (Source/CmdDevTools.rs "grammars" subcommand)
   and confirm the diff is empty (no new token was added).

Examples/tests (I5, I9 — this is lexer-only, no runtime semantics change, so
AOT/jet run/interpreter parity is automatic once the same token stream feeds
every tier):
9. Add examples/features/cli/direct_launch.jet starting with
   `#!/usr/bin/env jet`, printing one line. Golden at
   examples/features/expected/cli/direct_launch.out.
10. New test in tests/cli.rs, next to the existing `#!/bin/sh` executable
    fixtures (e.g. ~line 3940): chmod +x the example file, exec it directly
    on the current Unix host, assert stdout/exit code are byte-identical to
    running the same file via `jet <path>`. Name it e.g.
    `direct_launch_shebang_runs_executable_file`.
11. New tests/ui/*.jet + .stderr pair for a `#!` NOT at byte 0 (model on
    tests/ui/loop_header_semicolon_retired.jet/.stderr) — auto-discovered by
    tests/diagnostic_snapshots.rs::ui_snapshots via fs::read_dir, no manual
    registration needed.

Exact test commands:
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli direct_launch_shebang_runs_executable_file`
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots`
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden` (example compiles/runs, AOT tier)

questions.text: I dont entirely understand the point of this. We should reunify meta things vs markers. Markers are # and "comptime" stuff/macros use $ for slices and $[...]$ for expansion macros. Maybe we use something like that instead of a regular marker? Need discussion.
questions.answer: The #! line is not Jet syntax and not a marker, so there is nothing to unify with the # / $ planes. It is an operating-system handshake: when you type ./backup.jet, the kernel — not Jet — reads the first two bytes of the file. If they are '#!', the kernel starts the named program (/usr/bin/env jet) and hands it the file. Jet only skips that first line; it produces no token and has no meaning inside the language. No Jet-owned spelling can do this job: a marker or $[...]$ form would run only after Jet is already running, but the whole point of this line is to start Jet when it is not running yet. The kernel accepts exactly one spelling, '#!', fixed since 1980 — Python, Ruby, shell, and Deno all accept the same line unchanged for the same reason; the resemblance to Jet's # marker sigil is coincidence. So the ballot adds no meta mechanism. The choice is only: A) tolerate the OS's line at byte zero so chmod +x works; B) generate a separate launcher file instead; C) do nothing, always type 'jet file.jet'.

cards.title: Interactive scripting closeout: real REPL and notebook journey
cards.body: Card #442 proved the shared session engine and protocol. The Python conversion evidence still found no complete first-party journey that a new user can install, open, edit, inspect, save, and share. Close that product gap without another evaluator or notebook-only type system.
cards.plan:
## Outcome

Ship the real user journey promised by the ratified notebook decisions and the shared REPL session.

## Work

cards.title: Script-to-system continuity capstone: grow without a rewrite
cards.body: Jet promises one language from a lone script to a durable program. Prove that promise with one source-backed project that grows into a package, tested CLI, service, native executable, and embeddable library. Layout may change through ratified split and fold tools, but program meaning must not be rewritten.
cards.plan:
## Outcome

Prove that a useful one-file script can grow into production forms through the same language and semantic model.

## Work

1. Start with a useful manifest-free file and the ratified direct run path.
2. Add tests, dependencies, typed CLI input, configuration, service operation, and package outputs in measured steps.
3. Use the ratified source split and fold tools. Do not maintain two layouts or rewrite semantics by hand.
4. Export the final library through the canonical native guest path.
5. Record each user action, source change, generated artifact, failure, and reversal.

## Proof

Run every stage on clean hosts. Compare results across direct run, dev, test, AOT build, service run, installed command, and foreign host call. Prove rollback after each structural transition.

cards.title: Comprehension guard spelling in the loop head
cards.body: Absorbed #1419 (c0s0594k) 2026-08-19: its criterion cites the very fixture this card ships (tests/ui/loop_guard_comma_misspelling.jet/.stderr) and its plan says "same fixture likely closes both cards' proof obligations — do not duplicate the file." One parser patch.
cards.plan:
## Grounded plan (D-LOOP-GUARD1=A: comma-less guard stays canonical)

Canonical spelling is unchanged: `loop u, users if u.active -> u.name` (no
comma before `if`) already parses and runs today — verified live:
`scripts/agent/jet-env target/debug/jet run` on that snippet prints the
filtered list. No grammar change to the accepted form.

Bug to add (this is the whole card): `loop u, users, if u.active -> u.name`
(comma before `if`) must stop silently misparsing as a stride and instead
teach the comma-less form. Verified live repro: this exact input today
prints `Error [E0003]: an if used as a value needs an else branch` pointing
at the end of the arrow line — a confusing, unrelated message.

Root cause (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs):
1. `at_yielding_loop_stride` (line ~1428) returns true for `TokKind::Comma`
   whenever `at_yielding_loop_clause` (line ~1421) is false. It does not
   special-case `, if`.
2. The three stride call sites inside `yielding_loop_expr`'s clause loop
   (~lines 96-99, 112-117, 124-130) see `at_yielding_loop_stride() == true`,
   call `self.take_loop_comma()` then `self.expr_no_struct_lit()`, which
   parses `if u.active -> u.name` as a value-`if` expression missing its
   `else` — hence E0003.

Fix: add a lookahead for `TokKind::Comma` followed by `TokKind::KwIf` at each
of those three call sites (and the clause-loop-continue check at line
~137-140). When seen, do NOT take it as a stride. Instead push a new
diagnostic and recover by consuming the comma and falling through to the
existing comma-less guard parse at line ~144 (`let guard = if
matches!(self.peek().kind, TokKind::KwIf) { ... }`) so the rest of the loop
head still parses and later diagnostics keep flowing (M1 recovery). Model
this exactly on the existing E0373 semicolon-in-loop-header handling in
`take_loop_comma` (lines ~1406-1416): push to `self.diags`, don't hard-Err.

New diagnostic: reserve the next free E-code in docs/spec/diagnostics.md's
registry table (grep the table for the current max/gaps immediately before
reserving — do not hardcode a number, other cards may reserve concurrently).
What: "a guard follows its source with no comma". Why: "the guard
self-announces with `if`, so the loop head only uses commas between
positional clauses" (per D-LOOP-GUARD1's ratified rec). Fix: "remove the
comma before `if`".

CONFLICT FOUND — bridged, not ballotable: D-LOOP-SUBJECT1's own ratified
option-A code sample shows a bindingless guard WITH a comma
(`loop users, if .active -> .name`), which contradicts this decision's title
ruling that guards are always comma-less. D-LOOP-GUARD1 is the decision that
specifically owns "guard spelling in the loop head" and its final
adversarial pass explicitly moved the outcome to comma-less; D-LOOP-SUBJECT1's
sample text predates that pivot and was not updated. Resolution used here:
apply the comma-less guard rule uniformly, bound or bindingless. Canonical
bindingless form is `loop users if .active -> .name`, NOT
`loop users, if .active -> .name`. #1417's plan carries this same note and
uses the corrected spelling throughout. Logged on both cards; flagged in the
prep-loops report for the owner to confirm if it matters beyond this bridge.

Formatter (I7/round-trip):
- Confirm the formatter's existing yielding-loop-guard emission (search
  crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Statements.rs and Expressions.rs for the
  guard/arrow emission path) already emits the comma-less canonical form
  byte-for-byte stable. Add one fmt STABILITY case (pattern in tests/fmt.rs,
  search "STABILITY" comments) for a guarded yielding loop if none exists.
  The old comma form is a parse error, not valid input, so there is no
  "rewrite the rejected spelling" fmt behavior to add — only confirm the
  accepted spelling round-trips.

Syntax.rs / decisions log (I7):
- Add a comment-only line in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs citing
  D-LOOP-GUARD1=A ("adds no token") next to the D-LOOP-COMMA1 note
  (~line 83).
- docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: one log entry for D-LOOP-GUARD1=A.
- `jet devtools grammars`: run and confirm empty diff (no new token).

Examples/tests (I5, I9 — parser-only change, no new runtime semantics; the
guard already lowers to the existing Switch-wrapped Yield AST at line
~201-212, so AOT/jet run/interpreter parity is automatic once one example
proves the SAME desugared program end to end):
- Add a guard-form example: examples/features/basics/loop_values.jet
  currently has zero `if`-guard usage — add one guarded yielding loop there
  (e.g. `active_doubled :: loop value, values if value > 1 -> value * 2`),
  update examples/features/expected/basics/loop_values.out to match.
- New tests/ui/loop_guard_comma_misspelling.jet + .stderr pair (model
  exactly on tests/ui/loop_header_semicolon_retired.jet/.stderr) —
  auto-discovered by tests/diagnostic_snapshots.rs::ui_snapshots, no manual
  registration.
- New forced-interpreter test modeled on
  tests/tir_collections_and_methods.rs::list_surface_forced_interpreter
  (uses `dev_iteration(path, false, true)`): run the updated
  loop_values.jet example through the interpreter tier and assert stdout
  matches the golden exactly.

Exact test commands:
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden` (AOT tier, updated example)
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots`
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test fmt`
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_collections_and_methods` (or
  wherever the new forced-interpreter test lands)

cards.title: Bindingless loops with an implicit subject
cards.plan:
## Grounded plan (D-LOOP-SUBJECT1=A: bare-member subject)

Depends on #1416's comma-less guard fix for its canonical spelling. NOTE the
bridged conflict logged on #1416: this card's canonical bindingless form is
`loop users if .active -> .name` (NO comma before `if`), not the comma form
shown in D-LOOP-SUBJECT1's own ballot code sample — that sample predates
D-LOOP-GUARD1's final comma-less pivot. Use the corrected spelling
everywhere in this card's examples, diagnostics, and tests.

Canonical forms (post-fix):
```
names :: loop users if .active -> .name
totals :: loop orders if .paid -> .total
upper :: loop words -> .to_upper()

doubled :: loop n, nums -> n * 2   // scalar source still names its binding
```

Current state (verified live): a bindingless head does not parse at all
today. `loop users if users > 1 -> users` produces
`Error [E0072]: this loop cannot yield a List because it has no finite
exhaustion edge` — the `finite_header` gate in
crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs (lines ~35-40) requires
the head to start with `Ident(_)` followed specifically by
`ColonEq | Semi | Comma`, or `LParen`; a bare source with no trailing comma
(bindingless) never satisfies that and falls through to the "no finite
exhaustion edge" branch meant for truly-infinite loops.

Grammar change (parser):
1. Extend `finite_header` (line ~35-40) to also accept `Ident(_)` followed by
   `TokKind::Arrow` or `TokKind::KwIf` — the two tokens that can legally
   follow a bindingless single source expression. D-LOOP-SUBJECT1's own
   technical text already resolves the ambiguity worry: "the comma-less
   source position is unambiguous because a condition loop cannot yield
   (E0072)" — this function only ever runs in yield position, so a bare
   source here can never be confused with a non-yielding `loop cond { }`.
2. Inside the non-counted clause-parsing branch (`else { loop { ... } }`,
   starting line ~84), add a path that detects "no binding, no comma" (i.e.
   the current `loop_source_binding` + `expect_loop_comma` pair does not
   apply) and instead parses the bare expression directly as the source,
   recording that this clause has no binding name (e.g. `var: None` in
   whatever shape clauses use — check the `clauses` tuple shape at line 53
   and adjust, or thread an `Option<String>` through `ForKind`/`Stmt::For`
   consistently with how `var2` already handles the optional second name).
3. `(key, value)` sources always keep their two names — no bindingless path
   for the two-name form (per the ratified option's carve-out); confirm
   `loop_source_binding`'s `LParen` branch (line ~1369) is left untouched.
4. Guard parse at line ~144 is unchanged — it already fires whenever the
   token after the source (or after clause continuation) is `KwIf`; once
   step 1 lets a bindingless source reach that point, the guard parses for
   free.

Bare-member subject resolution (parser or sema — pick the layer that already
owns dispatch-arm subject binding and reuse it, do not invent a second
mechanism, I8):
5. Precedent: D-IFDIST1's dispatch-arm subject binding lives in
   crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/conditionals.rs. It synthesizes
   `Syntax::KW_IT` (line ~426) as the pattern-scrutinee name when the subject
   is not a simple `Ident`, and bare arm-head atoms desugar against the
   subject via `parse_arm_and_cond`/`parse_arm_alternates_cond` (~line 677+).
   That mechanism handles bare atoms in a *comparison* position (arm heads),
   not bare `.member` as a plain value expression — this card needs the
   latter: `.member` used directly in the loop body/arm as a value (e.g.
   `-> .name`), which is a different grammar slot.
6. Currently NO grammar accepts a leading lowercase `.member` as a primary
   expression at all. The only existing leading-dot expression handling is
   `leading_dot_variant` in
   crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/binary_unary.rs:34-42, and it
   only matches an uppercase `Ident` or `null` (D-SHAPE3a expected-type
   static/variant shorthand) — verified live: `nums.map(.to_string())` today
   errors `Error [E0003]: expected a value, found '.'`.
7. Design choice for the implementer: either (a) desugar structurally at
   parse time — when parsing a bindingless loop's body/arm, thread the
   synthesized subject name (reuse `Syntax::KW_IT`, matching the existing
   dispatch-arm precedent) as an implicit receiver bound in that inner
   scope, so the body is parsed as ordinary code against a real binding
   (cheapest, reuses sema's existing name resolution, no new expression
   grammar); or (b) add a genuine primary-expression case for a leading
   lowercase-initial `.member` that resolves against an ambient "current
   subject" the parser/sema tracks. Prefer (a): it is a strict superset of
   the scalar case (`doubled :: loop n, nums -> n * 2` already binds `n`),
   costs no new AST node, and keeps `?`, `next`, `break` working unchanged
   because the body stays ordinary statements, not a lambda.
8. Nested loops: an inner bindingless loop under a bindingless outer loop is
   rejected with a diagnostic teaching named bindings — reserve a new E-code
   (see docs/spec/diagnostics.md "Adding a diagnostic"; grep the registry
   table for the current max/gaps first).
9. Precedence: bare `.member` in a bindingless loop body resolves against the
   loop subject before the D-SHAPE3a expected-type static shorthand can
   apply — state this as one ordered rule in sema's resolution comments, do
   not implement two independent lookups that could race.

Syntax.rs / decisions log (I7):
- Syntax.rs comment-only line citing D-LOOP-SUBJECT1=A ("adds no token",
  reuses `Syntax::KW_IT`) near the D-IFDIST1 note (~line 89).
- docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: one log entry for D-LOOP-SUBJECT1=A —
  correct the guard spelling in any transcribed example to the comma-less
  form (see conflict note above).
- `jet devtools grammars`: run, confirm empty diff.

Examples/tests (I5, I9 — the subject desugar happens in the parser and
produces the same AST as hand-written `subject.member`, so no Prelude/engine
change is needed; parity is proved by running the SAME desugared example
through all tiers):
- Add examples/features/basics/loop_bindingless.jet covering: plain map
  (`loop stops -> .city`), guarded map (`loop users if .active -> .name`),
  and the scalar carve-out (`loop n, nums -> n * 2`, binding still named).
  Golden at examples/features/expected/basics/loop_bindingless.out.
- tests/ui pair for nested-bindingless rejection (model on any existing
  loop_* ui fixture, e.g. tests/ui/loop_label_namespace_collision.jet/.stderr
  for the file-pair shape).
- Forced-interpreter test modeled on
  tests/tir_collections_and_methods.rs::list_surface_forced_interpreter
  against the new example.

cards.title: Bare-member shorthand for one-parameter callable arguments
cards.plan:
## Grounded plan (D-SUBJECT-CALL1=A: member chains as call-argument shorthand)

Independent of #1416/#1417's loop-head work — this owns the call-site half
only (`users.filter(.active).map(.name)`), per the decision's own scope note
("this ballot owns the call-site half on its own"). Not blocked, but shares
the same underlying "leading lowercase `.member`" grammar gap documented in
#1417 step 6 — implement whichever card lands first, then have the other
reuse the same primary-expression/desugar path (I8: one mechanism).

Canonical forms:
```
names :: users.filter(.active).map(.name)
shouting :: users.map(.name.to_upper())
oldest :: users.max_by(.age)

total :: orders.fold(0, fn (sum: Int, o: Order) => Int = sum + o.total)
// two-parameter callable: shorthand never applies, full lambda required
```

Current state (verified live): `nums.map(.to_string())` today errors
`Error [E0003]: expected a value, found '.'` — no grammar accepts a leading
lowercase `.member` anywhere, confirming zero prior art beyond
`leading_dot_variant` (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/binary_unary.rs:34-42),
which only matches uppercase idents/`null` (D-SHAPE3a).

Where the rule must fire: at a call argument position where the callee's
expected parameter type is a known one-parameter callable (`fn (T) => R`).
This is expected-type-driven, not purely syntactic — the same class of
inference D-SHAPE3a's `.new(...)` and `.Variant` already use. Ground this in
real code:
1. Find where D-SHAPE3a's expected-type dot-shorthand is resolved (search
   crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs and
   crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore*.rs for "expected_type" /
   "leading_dot_variant" call sites) — this is the existing precedent for
   "the parser accepts a bare-dot token stream, sema resolves it once the
   expected type is known." Reuse that same expected-type threading for
   call arguments, do not invent a second inference pass.
2. Grammar: allow a bare `.member[.method(args)]*` chain to parse as an
   expression at any argument position (same primary-expression extension
   #1417 step 6/7 needs) — reuse whichever implementation lands first.
3. Sema: when the parameter's declared/inferred type is a one-parameter
   callable (`fn (T) => R`) and the argument parsed as a bare member chain,
   desugar to `fn (__subject: T) => R = __subject<chain>` — literally
   synthesize the same lambda a user would have written by hand, so TIR,
   AOT, JIT, and interpreter all see an ordinary lambda AST and need zero
   new runtime support (I9 auto-satisfied by construction).
4. Exclusions (write the lambda instead, per the ratified option): operators
   (`!.active`), literals, and any callable with more than one parameter.
   Sema rejects a bare chain against a non-callable or multi-parameter
   expected type with a diagnostic teaching the full lambda — reuse or
   extend the diagnostic already covering unresolved bare-dot expected types
   if one exists (search for D-SHAPE3a's "unknown expected type" error),
   otherwise reserve a new E-code (grep docs/spec/diagnostics.md for the
   current max/gaps first).
5. Precedence: bare `.member` under a non-callable expected type still means
   D-SHAPE3a static/variant shorthand; under a one-parameter-callable
   expected type it means this lambda shorthand. The two contexts cannot
   overlap per the ratified rec ("function types have no static members") —
   state this as one ordered rule in sema, not two competing lookups.
6. Generic/inference edge case flagged by the ballot's adversarial pass: a
   generic adapter mid-inference may not yet know the parameter type: fire
   the shorthand only once the expected type is concretely known; otherwise
   emit the "write the lambda" diagnostic rather than guessing.

Syntax.rs / decisions log (I7):
- Syntax.rs comment-only line citing D-SUBJECT-CALL1=A ("adds no token,
  reuses the existing bare-member atom and dot punctuation") near the
  D-SHAPE3a note (~line 56).
- docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: one log entry for D-SUBJECT-CALL1=A.
- `jet devtools grammars`: run, confirm empty diff.

Examples/tests (I5, I9 — pure desugar to an ordinary lambda AST, so parity
across tiers is proved, not re-implemented, by running one example through
all of them):
- Add examples/features/basics/method_chain.jet (existing file) a
  bare-member-shorthand section, or add a new
  examples/features/basics/member_shorthand.jet — check which fits the
  file's existing scope before choosing; golden updated/added to match.
- tests/ui pair for a bare chain against a non-callable or multi-parameter
  expected type, teaching the full lambda.
- Forced-interpreter test modeled on
  tests/tir_collections_and_methods.rs::list_surface_forced_interpreter
  against the new/updated example.

Exact test commands:
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden`
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots`
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_collections_and_methods` (or
  wherever the new forced-interpreter test lands)

Jet already has the machinery: E4-JP2 action IR with complete cache identity, E4-JP5 binary caches, ratified D-JPK-CACHEAUTH1/CACHECONFIG1/REPROCACHE1/STOREBACKEND1. cards.title: hangar compat root: ABI isolation proof — no cross-universe library leakage
cards.plan:
## Why

Bedrock Linux deliberately refuses cross-stratum library sharing: ABI mixing is "theoretically possible but unsupported due to complexity/messiness" (bedrocklinux.org feature-compatibility). D-JOS-STORE1=A keeps imported Nix closures in a hangar-managed compat root, separate from native packages. That isolation is implied but not test-gated today.

Evidence: video mine 2026-08-04, claim ledger /tmp/ENejkGhMTww.claims.json (topic: no-cross-universe-library-sharing).

## Work

Add a targeted test proving compat-root libraries never enter native package link or build paths: native builds and native runtime closures must reference only hangar-native artifacts; compat-root closures stay self-contained. Failure mode to catch: a native package resolving a shared library out of an imported Nix closure. Test must fail when the isolation boundary is removed or bypassed.

criteria.text: A test proves native link/runtime closures reference only hangar-native artifacts and compat-root closures stay self-contained; the test fails when the D-JOS-STORE1 isolation boundary is removed or bypassed.
criteria.evidence: ABI-universe closure validation added in crates/jetpack/src/Store/Closure.rs (cause: unchecked cross-provider references), enforced before native output publication in Store.rs, with a native/compat isolation proof in Store/Tests.rs covering both leakage directions. Test: 1 passed, 0 failed.

cards.title: Syntax: call a returned function value with .call
cards.body: Pick and implement one clear spelling for calling a function value that another call just returned. Raised from the owner review of D-AUTODIFF1, where compute.grad(loss)(w, x) read as foreign. Scope: parser rule, diagnostic with fix-it, sema member lookup, formatter, tree-sitter and tmGrammar highlighting, LSP completion, docs, examples, goldens. Gated on D-CALLVALUE1.
cards.plan:
Scope: D-CALLVALUE1=B. Any call result requires a chained .call(...) to invoke again; ')(' directly after a call is a parse error with a fix-it inserting '.call'. Function-typed values gain a builtin .call(...) member; a struct member literally named 'call' shadows it. Direct calls on plain names/fields/index/lambdas are unchanged. Out of scope: D-CALLVALUE1 options A/C/D, autodiff (#1428-1436).
Approach:
1. crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/postfix.rs: in the postfix call loop, when '(' follows an already-built Call node, stop building a second Call directly; emit the new E0xxx diagnostic (docs/spec/diagnostics.md 'Adding a diagnostic', next free code near the E09xx call family) with a fix-it that inserts '.call' before the parens, mirroring the retired_callable_arrow teaching pattern in crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/conditionals.rs:104-128.
2. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs: give every function-typed receiver a builtin 'call' member whose signature mirrors the callee's parameter/return contract; resolve struct member lookup first so a user field/method named 'call' wins (same precedence pattern already used for builtin collection methods).
3. Lower '.call' identically at every tier per I9: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs (AOT/JIT shared TIR lower), crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs if JIT has a separate lowering path, and crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/dispatch/eval_method.rs (interpreter/comptime). '.call(args)' lowers to the same underlying call-of-value the parser used to accept directly -- no new runtime semantics, so verify all three tiers already share one lowering before adding tier-specific code.
4. crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Items.rs (or Expressions formatter): print the retained '.call' node; add a fmt STABILITY case in tests/fmt.rs using assert_fmt_stable.
5. Register the diagnostic in docs/spec/diagnostics.md and add tests/ui/<code>_call_result_not_called.jet + .stderr snapshot (pattern: tests/ui/E0927_unknown_marker_function.jet).
6. editors/tree-sitter/grammar.js, editors/jet.tmGrammar, editors/vscode/syntaxes/jet.tmLanguage.json, editors/zed/grammars: regenerate via 'jet self devtools grammars' (Source/CmdDevTools.rs) so '.call' highlights as a builtin member; do not hand-edit generated output.
7. Source/LSP/Features.rs: add 'call' to member-completion for function-typed receivers.
8. Add/extend an example under examples/features/ (a function returning a function, invoked via .call) with golden output in examples/features/expected/; prove it under both jet build and jet run per I9.
9. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: append a dated D-CALLVALUE1=B decision-log entry following the existing '**YYYY-MM-DD -- D-ID=Outcome**: ...' format at the end of the Decision log section, naming the implementing card.
Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots -- call_result (new E-code fixture)
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test fmt -- call_value (new stability case)
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test grammar

- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/<new-or-updated-example>.jet (I9: AOT + jet run agree; interpreter path exercised if deopt reachable)
Owned paths: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/postfix.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/dispatch/eval_method.rs, crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Items.rs, Source/LSP/Features.rs, editors/**, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, tests/ui/*, tests/fmt.rs, examples/features/**.

cards.title: Exponent semantics: precedence, associativity, Int typing
cards.body: Ratified D-EXPSEM1=A: power is right-associative (2^3^2 == 512); power binds tighter than unary minus (-3^2 == -9); Int ^ non-negative Int returns exact Int; Int ^ negative Int returns Float; any Float operand makes the result Float. Builds on the ^ operator from #1428.
cards.plan: 1) Parser associativity + precedence. 2) Sema result-type rules. 3) Prelude int_pow/float pow paths per I9. 4) Example + golden with the four canonical values. 5) Targeted parser and sema tests.

log.text: audit 2026-08-06: cleared blockedBy refs to retired done cards (dependency satisfied)
Closed. Exponent grouping, associativity and Int typing hold on every tier, and the overflow trap reads the same sentence everywhere.

Held again. The JavaScript preamble re-encodes the power rule instead of carrying it: Number.isSafeInteger caps exactness at 2^53 while the Prelude is exact to 2^63, so 2 ^ 60 answers correctly on AOT and JIT but throws in JavaScript. Floor division has the same shape and no overflow trap.

All review blockers are closed. The fixed-width branch now runs before the power early return, so small := U8.{2}; small ^= U8.{3} prints 8 on both tiers. The JavaScript target no longer emits **; it calls a jet_pow preamble that carries the Prelude rule, and the emitted helper traps with the same wording as every other tier. The trap wording is now one shared constant, and a test proves the Prelude text still matches so it cannot drift.

Review held this card. Criteria 1-5 and 7 are verified independently. Criterion 6 is not verified. Three blockers remain: fixed-width power assignment diverges between tiers, the JavaScript target emits a raw ** operator that never traps, and the trap wording is written in four places and has already drifted. The remaining sema question is now ballot D-EXPNEG1.

Review hold. Three tier-parity blockers. One: a fixed-width compound power diverges. A probe with w := U8.{3} then w ^= 6 prints 729 under jet run and traps under jet build. apply_binop_to_var in crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs line 7250 returns lower_pow before the IntN branch, so the fixed-width path never reaches INTN_OP_POW. The same statement with *= traps on both tiers. Two: the JS web tier emits plain JavaScript **. binop in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Web.rs line 4789 feeds tir_js_expr at line 4410, and jet build --target=web wrote return (2 ** n) into build/app.js. JavaScript ** never traps on a negative exponent and is not exact. Three: the trap wording is written four times, in Prelude/Core/Power.rs, MathLayout.rs, Builtins.rs and runtime_host.rs, and it already differs. A U8 power overflow says this operation overflows under jet run and this power overflows under AOT. Separate concern for the owner: sema turns only a written negative exponent into a Float, so 2 ^ e with a computed negative e traps instead of giving a fraction. D-EXPSEM1=A says an Int raised to a negative Int is a Float. That narrowing is a new user-facing rule and needs a ballot. It was written into docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md as if it were ratified. cards.title: Three-way comparison: <=> or compare method
cards.body: Ratified D-CMP3WAY1=B (owner overrode rec A): ship the spaceship operator <=> AND the Ordering story. cards.title: Default Int overflow model: arbitrary precision
cards.body: Ratified D-INTBIG1=A (amends D-NUMOPS1 for default Int): default Int becomes arbitrary precision with a machine-word small-int fast path, spilling past ~63 bits. Overflow stops existing for default Int. Fixed-width I8..I128 / U8..U128 keep trap-on-overflow plus explicit wrapping_*/saturating_* methods. Crossing to fixed-width or FFI range-checks with a real diagnostic. I9: identical semantics on AOT, JIT, interpreter, web — representation lives in Prelude, engines marshal only. This is the largest slice of the slate; sequence it last.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Finish D-INTBIG1=A (exact default Int with a machine-word fast path) by proving criteria 2 and 4. The former overflow repro must return the exact value, and small-int arithmetic must not heap-allocate while spill-boundary values round-trip exactly.

## Current state
- The carrier exists: `crates/jet-foundation/src/Numeric.rs:2988` (`inline_max`), `:2993` (`is_inline`), `:2998` (`from_i64`) and `:3160` (`JetInt::add` with an inline fast path). It is mirrored at `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:3972-3973` (`JET_INT_SMALL_MIN/MAX`).
- The golden `Examples/features/text/int_exact.jet` expects `15511210043330985984000000`, `9223372036854775808` and `1999999999999999999999999999998` (`Examples/features/expected/text/int_exact.out`).
- Criterion 4 fails today. Every Prelude op routes through the heap: `jet_int_add` (CommonTypes.rs:4317) calls `jet_int_add_hot!` (:4170), which calls `jet_int_exact_add` (:5085). That builds `CtBigInt` from both operands via `jet_std_raw_to_exact` (:5311) and `jet_int_value` → `JetBigInt::from_int` (:4013), so even inline values allocate limbs. The Jet emitter routes exact Int ops to `jet_int_owned_*` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Operations.jet:33-45, 347-363`), which wrap the same raw ops (CommonTypes.rs:4735-4794).
- Criteria 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are met.

## Changes
1. Depend on #2872. It rewrites the hot macros so inline operands take the `JetInt` inline path and only spill or trap on the cold rail. Do not duplicate that work here.
2. `crates/jet-foundation/src/Numeric.rs` tests module (`:85`): add `jet_int_inline_arithmetic_does_not_allocate`. A counting global allocator asserts zero allocations for add/sub/mul/div/mod within the inline range. Values at `inline_max()`, `inline_max()+1`, `inline_min()` and `inline_min()-1` must round-trip exactly through spill and back.
3. `tests/int_division.rs`: add `exact_int_inline_loop_allocations_do_not_scale`. Run `jet perf run` on the same add/mul loop at 1e3 and 1e6 iterations. The allocation count in the `.jettrace` must be equal (iteration-independent) on AOT and default run.
4. Criterion 2: the int_exact golden (i64::MAX+1 line) is the former overflow repro. Keep it and delete any residual default-Int overflow panic path found by grepping `overflow` in the exact-Int Prelude code.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/int_exact Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` prints exactly the three lines above on every golden tier.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-foundation --lib -- jet_int_inline_arithmetic_does_not_allocate` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test int_division -- exact_int_inline_loop_allocations_do_not_scale` passes.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: the Prelude Int carrier and tier parity.

## Dependencies
#2872 (the Prelude hot macros must stop materialising CtBigInt for inline operands).

cards.body: Full design pass for operator-level matrix and linear algebra (owner directive: design fully before any code). Deliverable is a proposal doc plus a ballot slate — no implementation on this card. Today core.compute is function-only (matrix, det, inv, solve, fft); no Matrix type, literals, or operator arithmetic. Design must cover: Matrix/Vector types, literal syntax, matmul vs elementwise operators, broadcasting, indexing/slicing, beginner surface vs expert control (views, in-place, layout), and interaction with the ratified operator slate (^ power, /% floor div, floored %, Float division, bigint Int).

questions.text: I like the idea of a leading . for elementwise, but consider all of jet syntax (current and planned changes), then repropose a new perfect system that incorporates the current recommendation with the .* and * syntaxes
questions.answer:
Reproposed as option F, now on the ballot, and it is my new recommendation.

F = the type says which, and the dot asks for cells where the plain operator would compose. Matrix composes under *. Grid and lane vectors multiply cells under *. A leading dot is legal only on a Matrix, where it means cells: pose .* spin. Where * is already cell by cell, the dot is refused — so no meaning ever gets two spellings.

Three findings from the syntax sweep that shaped it:

1. The dot is already Jet's word for distribute across members. D-SPREAD1=A gives prefix.[a, b, c] as member spread, and D-ENUMDOT1 gives .Variant. Applying an operator across cells is the same idea one level down, so .* costs no new concept.

2. Do not take option E whole. Its call half, f.(x), reintroduces call fan-out, which your own ratified D-VERDICT-1324-1 removed. F takes E's operator dot and leaves the call dot retired.

3. Cell-by-cell * is already law. D-VECARITH1 ratified element-wise + - * / for lane vectors. So Grid multiplying cells under plain * is not a new rule to learn — it is the rule the language already has, and Matrix is the one type that composes instead.

What F fixes about D, your current recommendation: under D a person porting a formula writes .cells() at the crossing point, so a line that reads the same in every other language does not read the same here. Under F they write .* on the value they already hold.

Honest costs: five new infix tokens (.*, ./, .^, .+, .-) plus compound forms. A porter who writes .* on a Grid gets an error rather than a result — that error is the teaching moment and needs registered what/why/fix text under I4. One lexing risk to check: ^ is take in prefix position under D-MEM1=A and power in infix position, so .^ must be lexed against both.

cards.title: Variadic methods: sema accepts the declaration but no tier can run one
cards.body:
A rest parameter on a method parses and registers, but no call to it can succeed. check_method_args rejects every arity with E0104, and loosening that check reaches an internal compiler error in Codegen/Items.rs — codegen has no lowering for a variadic method. Free-function variadics work on every tier.

Found while implementing D-APILABEL1 (#1393). Predates that card: master rejects 'l.write(1)' and 'l.write(1, 2, 3)' identically on a 'fn write(self, level: Int, parts: ...Int)'. The strict arity check stays in place so the failure remains a diagnostic rather than an ICE.

Done when a variadic method call lowers and runs with the same meaning on AOT, the Cranelift JIT and the interpreter, with an example and golden output, or when the language decides methods do not take rest parameters and says so with a registered diagnostic.
cards.plan:
Scope: make variadic method calls work end to end, with the same meaning as free-function variadics. Free functions already lower rest parameters on every tier, so methods reuse that one mechanism (I8). Out of scope: any new syntax; rest-parameter semantics changes.
Repro: type with 'fn write(self, level: Int, parts: ...Int)'. Both 'l.write(1)' and 'l.write(1, 2, 3)' fail with E0104 today. Loosening the arity check alone reaches an ICE in codegen.
Approach: 1) Add the failing example first: examples/features/functions (variadic method with zero, one, and three rest args) plus expected output. 2) Sema: extend check_method_args in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs (and the arity path in Sema/CheckerItems.rs) to accept rest-parameter arity exactly like the free-function path. Reuse the free-function logic; do not fork it. 3) Codegen: add method variadic lowering in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs mirroring the free-function lowering so the same TIR reaches AOT, JIT, and interpreter. No per-engine code. 4) Keep E0104 for genuinely wrong calls; existing snapshots unchanged.
Proof: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden with the new example filter; jet build + jet run + interpreter on the example give identical output; free-function variadic example still green.
Owned paths: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerItems.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs, examples/features/functions/, matching expected outputs.

cards.title: Rename the named Core container types to plain short words
cards.body:
Pick one plain short name for each named Core container. Jargon names (Deque, Bag, BitSet, ByteBuffer) block beginners. Slate chosen in chat with the owner; ballot D-COLLNAME1 records the pick.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The zero-hit greps in the criteria are the right shape for a ratchet. Land them through the retirement mechanism ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656) ratifies so the retired container names get the same error text, mechanical rewrite, and standing zero-count guard as every other retired spelling.
cards.plan:
