cards.title: Exhaustive enum value dispatch still demands else (E0003 fires before sema E0307)
cards.body: Repro: examples/features/types/enum_dot.jet label() — a fn returning `if d == { .North -> … .West -> … }` with every Direction variant covered still errors E0003 (a value dispatch needs a final else arm). Ratified spec says otherwise: docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:442 (D-IFDIST1) 'Exhaustive pattern arms may omit else'; docs/spec/spec.md:749 makes enum dispatch exhaustiveness a sema check (E0307). Root cause: parse_dispatch_expr (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/conditionals.rs:966-985) desugars expression-position dispatch into a nested Expr::If chain at parse time and hard-requires else, so sema's E0307 coverage machinery (CheckerCore/switches.rs statement form) never sees the table. AST Expr::If has a mandatory else_value, so an else-less exhaustive table has no representation today. Fix direction: carry the arm-table shape into sema for expression position, run the same missing_pattern_coverage/E0307 proof, lower with the dead unreachable arm codegen already anticipates (TIR/lower/patterns.rs:376, jit/lower_ctx.rs:4434). Full I9 parity: parser, sema, TIR, AOT, JIT, interpreter, formatter round-trip, E0003 Why-text update, snapshots; drop the commented-out else in enum_dot.jet. Same gap exists for subjectless guard tables used as values (conditionals.rs:1057) — cover or explicitly exclude.

log.text: Implemented at HEAD: parser NoElse marker for all-pattern else-less tables; sema coverage proof shared with the statement form (extracted note_pattern_coverage / check_pattern_coverage_complete — one policy, two entry shapes); diverging TExprKind::Unreachable across AOT/JIT/eval; fmt table rendering for pattern-headed value tables. Separate defects carded: #1444 union-subject expression dispatch ICE (predates this card, with-else spelling equally affected), #1445 stale snapshots from the epoch5 consolidation.

cards.title: Inferred .{…} literal rejected in single-expression fn body (= expr)
cards.body: Repro: fn mirror(p: Point) => Point = .{x: -p.x, y: p.y} fails with E0003 'expected a value, found .' while the block form return .{…} works. Root cause: the = expr body parses with expr_no_struct_lit() (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/functions_params.rs:105), and the D-DOTCTOR1 inferred-literal arm is gated on allow_struct_lit (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/binary_unary.rs:520). The gate contradicts its own comment — a leading dot immediately followed by { is unambiguous, so the no-struct-lit restriction (which exists for the dotless 'Type {' ambiguity) does not apply. Inconsistent with the adjacent ungated leading-dot enum arm: fn f() => Direction = .North parses, = .{…} does not. Same gate presumably blocks .{…} in other no-struct-lit positions (if/for heads, S61 param defaults at functions_params.rs:610) — audit those too. Fix direction: drop allow_struct_lit from the .{ arm; add UI snapshot + formatter round-trip proof; keep examples/features/types/dot_construction.jet's expression-bodied spelling as the executable spec once green.

log.text: Fixed in b9dfb3515 + follow-up: dropped allow_struct_lit from both leading-dot dot-brace arms (bare .{…} and .Variant.{…}). cards.title: Core surface ledger against every competitor language
cards.body:
Card #1398 gates release on Jet beating Python per workflow, but nothing enumerates the surface at method level, so gaps are found by accident. Owner ruling 2026-08-03: the bar is not Python — it is every language Jet competes with, and no missing feature or functionality is acceptable.

Build the ledger from the real tables, not from docs: crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs (list, map, set, sorted set, deque, priority queue, cache, bitset method returns), crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs and fixed_sigs.rs (core module items and signatures).

For every Core type and module, record each competitor's operation, the Jet spelling, and one verdict: Jet wins, equal, Jet loses, or deliberately declined with its decision id. Compare against Python, Rust, Go, Swift, Kotlin, C#, TypeScript, Ruby, and Elixir at minimum; add Julia and R for the data and math surface. Deliberate declines are answers, not gaps — record the id so they stop resurfacing.

Every 'Jet loses' row leaves the ledger with a card. Known open rows already carded: #1404 Set algebra, #1409 String surface, #1410 List and Map, #1402 progress, #1403 plotting, #1400 zip. Card #288 already audits core.files against pathlib and should be folded in rather than duplicated.

Exit criteria: a durable ledger under docs covering every Core type and module; every 'Jet loses' row carrying a card or a decision id; #1398 able to read its gate from this document.
cards.plan:
1. Generate a closed inventory from Collections.rs, module_items.rs, and fixed_sigs.rs. Do not trust prose as the source of shipped Jet methods.
2. Select every Python builtin type and stdlib module Jet claims to cover. Use official Python docs to enumerate the matching public surface.
3. Give every row a stable ID, Python member, Jet spelling, matched workflow, and one verdict: Jet wins, equal, Jet loses, or out of scope.
4. Link every Jet-loses row to one live Tower card or open decision. Out-of-scope requires a ratified product-scope decision that explicitly says Jet does not compete for that workflow. A design decline does not remove a scored loss.
5. Add deterministic checks for an unmapped shipped method, missing Python member, duplicate row, hidden exclusion, stale owner, source-table drift, or unratified scope exclusion.
6. Store the durable ledger under docs and make #1398 consume it as its only workflow inventory. Do not create a second benchmark framework.
7. A fresh reviewer checks closure against both source tables and official Python docs.

cards.title: D-APILABEL1 remainder: extern and Core call ordering, and contract laundering
cards.body:
Follow-ups from the second review of #1393. The label contract itself is shipped; these are the edges it does not yet cover.

Extern and Core calls ignore the source evaluation order. TExprKind::ExternCall holds TExternArg and the Core call node holds TExpr, so call_args_mut in Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs cannot reach either and preserve_source_arg_order silently does nothing. extern_to_sig publishes param_call, so an extern call does bind by label and then runs in declaration order.

Type::Fn PartialEq in crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs returns true whenever either side has no contract, so passing a contract-bearing function through an unannotated fn type and back drops the contract with no diagnostic. Symmetric equality cannot express this; it needs a directional assignability check where a contract-bearing type satisfies a contract-less parameter but not the reverse. expand_type_aliases in Codegen/Context.rs also hard-codes param_contract to None, so a type alias loses the contract.

Labels on builtin methods are unchecked: the subset gate's label guards were removed and the only remaining check is the zip family, so [1, 2].map(bogus: f) compiles with the label ignored. The ratified rule says sema rejects an unknown label.

effect_free treats Binary and Unary as pure, so a panicking division reorders against a real effect and is also excluded from the observable count.

Type::name() ignores param_contract, so a contract mismatch prints the same type on both sides and no snapshot covers that message.

Done when each is fixed or carved out, with a UI snapshot per new diagnostic and AOT/JIT/interpreter parity proved for the ordering cases.
cards.plan:
Scope: close the five D-APILABEL1 edges the second review of #1393 found. The label contract itself is shipped and stays as is.
Approach, one slice per defect: 1) Extern and Core call ordering: TExprKind::ExternCall holds TExternArg and the Core call node holds TExpr, so call_args_mut in Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs never reaches them and preserve_source_arg_order does nothing. Extend call_args_mut (or add sibling accessors) to cover both node kinds so source evaluation order is preserved. Prove with an example whose argument expressions have observable effects. 2) Contract laundering: Type::Fn PartialEq in crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs returns true when either side lacks a contract. Replace the symmetric check with directional assignability: a contract-bearing type satisfies a contract-less parameter, never the reverse. Register a diagnostic with a UI snapshot for the rejected direction. Also fix expand_type_aliases in Codegen/Context.rs which hard-codes param_contract to None. 3) Unchecked labels on builtin methods: sema must reject an unknown label such as [1, 2].map(bogus: f) with a registered diagnostic and UI snapshot; restore the label guard for the builtin-method path, not only the zip family. 4) effect_free treats Binary and Unary as pure: make potentially panicking arithmetic count as observable so it cannot reorder against a real effect. Cover with an ordering test where a panicking division sits beside an effect. 5) Diagnostic text: Type::name() ignores param_contract, so mismatches print the same type on both sides. Include the contract in the rendered type and snapshot the message.
Proof: targeted diagnostic_snapshots filters for each new snapshot; example plus golden for the ordering slices; ordering example agrees under AOT, jet run, and interpreter.
Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Context.rs, crates/jet-sema/src (label + effect checks), tests/ui/ new snapshots, examples/features/ new ordering example.

Plan is file/line-specific and does not overlap #1393's or #1396's owned paths.

cards.title: Expression-position dispatch over a union subject ICEs (I2): union if-let conds not in TIR subset
cards.body: Repro: fn describe(value: Int | String) => String { return if value == { .Int(n) -> "n={n}" .String(s) -> "s={s}" else -> "" } } — jet build ICEs (exit 101) at Codegen/Items.rs:2270 'codegen reached a construct the typed IR does not cover', and quick-run reports E0956. Statement-position dispatch over the same union works (Stmt::Switch lowers via TExprKind::EnumMatch with union repr, subset/structs_enums.rs handles Type::Union). Root cause: the expression form desugars to an Expr::If chain whose conds are payload-binding PatternTests; if_cond_in_subset (subset/statements.rs:471-560) admits user-enum variants only via cx.variant_owner, which has no entry for structural union members, so the whole function leaves the TIR subset and R7 has no AST fallback — an ICE instead of a diagnostic (I2). The lowering side (lower_if_cond_atom, lower/control_flow.rs:428-460) already falls back to variant_binding_types for non-Named subjects; the gate and the pattern render for JetUnion reprs are the open work. Affects with-else and else-less spellings equally — predates card #1440 (an else-carrying repro has no NoElse node by construction). examples/features/types/anonymous_unions.jet (owner's expression-form edit, uncommitted) is the executable spec: it must run identically on AOT, default jet run, and interpreter deopt once fixed.
cards.plan:
Repro: fn describe(value: Int | String) => String { return if value == { .Int(n) -> "n={n}" .String(s) -> "s={s}" } } (examples/features/types/anonymous_unions.jet, already committed). jet build ICEs (exit 101) at Codegen/Items.rs:2270 ("codegen reached a construct the typed IR does not cover"); jet run reports E0956. Expected: compiles and runs identically on every tier, or a registered diagnostic rejects it -- never an ICE.

Root cause hypothesis: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/statements.rs:505-522, the if_cond_in_subset gate for a user-enum variant if-let atom requires cx.variant_owner.get(variant) (line 516) to resolve the payload's owning enum. Anonymous-union member tags are never registered in cx.variant_owner -- only user-declared enum variants are. The statement-position sibling, switch_in_subset (same file, line 573+), already has a union_shaped fallback (~line 618-624, comment "D-UNIONTYPE1=A: union matches use member-type arm heads ... not in variant_owner ... resolved later from the subject's Jet type in lower_enum_match") that accepts a single-bind variant-pattern arm set even when variant_owner has no entry. if_cond_in_subset has no equivalent, so the desugared expression-position if/else chain falls off the TIR subset with no AST fallback (R7), hitting jet_foundation::ice! at Codegen/Items.rs:2270. Lowering already has the matching fallback (lower_if_cond_atom, control_flow.rs:431-453, "_ => variant_binding_types(cx, variant)" at line 442) for a non-Named subject, so lowering is likely ready once the gate admits the construct.

Approach:
1. Add a union_shaped fallback to if_cond_in_subset's user-enum-variant-if-let branch (statements.rs ~512-521): when variant is not JSON/Key and not in cx.variant_owner, but the subject's resolved type is Type::Union(members) whose member tags include variant, accept the single-bind case the same way switch_in_subset's union_shaped branch does.
2. Extend the same fallback to the wildcard/no-binding branches (statements.rs ~522-545) so else-less and wildcard-payload forms match statement-position parity.
3. examples/features/types/anonymous_unions.jet already exercises this exact expression form and is wired into tests/dev.rs's 3-way interpreter/JIT/AOT parity test and tests/golden.rs -- no new example needed, just make it pass.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev language_callables_and_types_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- anonymous_unions
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet build examples/features/types/anonymous_unions.jet -- no ICE, exit 0.

Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/statements.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/control_flow.rs.

cards.body: cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots fails: tests/ui/E1130_kernel_proof.jet now produces Error E0101 'this program has no run function' before the expected E1130 kernel-proof block. The fixture (4 lines, a #Kernel fn with no run) is untouched; the behavior change came from a recent runtime/entry commit (likely 12fc9ae76 'feat: complete epoch5 runtime paths' or the branch consolidation around it) making entry detection fire in this compile mode. Decide whether E0101-on-check is intended (then re-bless the snapshot after reading it against docs/spec/diagnostics.md) or a regression (then fix entry detection). Unrelated to cards #1440/#1441 — the fixture has no dispatch table and my diff doesn't touch entry detection.

cards.title: Entry model: run returns the program value
cards.plan:
Scope: D-ENTRY-VALUE1 outcome B, now also aligned with D-FAIL-EXIT1 and D-FAIL-EDGE1 (ratified 2026-08-06, one day after this card's own decision). One entry, fn run. No return means a script that runs and exits. A return type that is the App-family program value (today spelled WebApp; #1447 renames it to App) means the runtime serves that value, and jet dev serves the same value with watch/reload. fn <command>() stays the one override hook (today only fn dev()). Delete the hidden fn app() name sniff, the source-text overlay that synthesizes fn run(){ app().serve() }, and the run/app/dev precedence table.

D-FAIL-EXIT1/D-FAIL-EDGE1 alignment (new, cross-cutting): fn run is fallible by nature regardless of its return type. The "no return" (script) case needs no => () ? annotation ever — ? works inside with zero ceremony, and the old E0122 refusal of typed error families at the entry is deleted. An unhandled error escaping the entry reports a full frame and exits 1. Exit 101 is reserved for compiler-internal defects only (#Todo, raw Prelude panics) — never for a reported program error. The CryptoError exit-70/101 special case is deleted from the entry gate. On the App-return (serve) case, if building the App value fails before .serve() runs, the same report is delivered in the target's native shape per D-FAIL-EDGE1 — for the native/CLI build this card and #1447 exercise, that means the same full-frame-and-exit-1 behavior as the script case; web/wasm edge adapters are a separate concern (see newCards proposal / #1507) and out of scope here.

Out of scope: renaming WebApp to App (#1447), CLI args into an App entry (#1450), job naming (#1448/#1449), test/bench overrides (#1451/#1452), the web/wasm/service edge adapters D-FAIL-EDGE1 also requires (owned by whatever card implements the FAIL slate generally — none exists on the board today, see newCards).

Approach:
1. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/WebApp.rs: find_app_fn (:67-79) currently matches a function literally named "app". Change it to extract the builder graph from fn run's body when fn run's declared return type is the App-family type. Delete the "app" name convention.
2. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle.rs (:2279-2328, the CompileMode::Run/Eval entry gate) already requires a literal fn run; confirm it accepts fn run() => WebApp with no extra special-casing beyond the return type, AND remove any E0122-style refusal of a declared error family at this same gate per D-FAIL-EXIT1 (do this in the same pass since it is the same function).
3. Source/Interpreter.rs checked_bundle (:352-378): delete the has_app/has_run overlay synthesis entirely. jet run no longer injects a hidden fn run(){ app().serve() }; the file must declare fn run() => WebApp { ... } directly.
4. Source/main.rs: delete has_web_app_entry_fn (:2379-2403) and the app-name sniff in dev dispatch (:1775-1794). fn dev() stays checked first as the override hook; otherwise jet dev inspects fn run's return type the same way jet run does. Delete has_dev_entry_fn's role in a three-way precedence table — only two cases remain: dev() override present, or not.
5. AOT/JIT parity gap this closes (found during investigation, real I9 violation today): crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs emit_cli_entry_if_needed (:680-724) and crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs lower_jit_program (:924-964) already require a literal fn run, so no structural change, but the synthesized main must now call .serve() via crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/WebApp.rs when fn run's return type is App-family — this is what makes jet build/jet emit --rust work on a file that only has fn run() => WebApp (today those fail E0101 because there is no literal fn run and AOT never ran the JIT-only overlay).
6. Source/CmdCompile.rs run_web_app_dev_entry (:770-793) / run_dev_entry (:696-766): keep the watch/reload re-exec mechanism, but trigger it off "fn run returns an App-family type" instead of "fn app() exists".
7. Rewrite examples/features/web/web_app.jet to declare fn run() => WebApp { ... } directly (today it has no fn run() and relies on the overlay). Rewrite examples/features/web/app_hello.jet to delete its fn app() and keep only fn run() => WebApp.
8. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: add a "D-ENTRY-VALUE1=B — the entry returns the program" entry in the same format as the existing D-WEBAPP1/D-WEBAUTHOR1 log entries (around :4831-4843). Syntax.rs gets a matching "adds no token" prose comment (same pattern as the D-CLIFLAG1-family comments already there) since this is a semantic rule change, not a new keyword or sigil.
9. Sequencing: #1447 (App/WebApp unification) is blocked on this card — it renames the App-family type this card's return-type check looks for.
10. New (D-FAIL-EXIT1): in the same Bundle.rs entry-gate pass from step 2, delete the requirement that a fallible script entry declare => () ? before ? is legal inside fn run's body. The entry is unconditionally fallible; no annotation ever gates it for the default (untyped) case. An expert may still pin the family explicitly: fn run() ? StoreErr { ... }.
11. New (D-FAIL-EXIT1): in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs, delete the CryptoError exit-70/101 special-case arm in the entry's error-reporting emission (same function step 5 touches for the App-serve wiring). An unhandled entry error of any type reports a full frame and exits 1. Confirm #Todo and raw Prelude panics still route to exit 101 and nothing else does.
12. New (D-FAIL-EDGE1): if the App-family builder chain itself raises before .serve() is reached (App-return case), the error must go through the same one-report path as the script case, delivered as a native CLI exit (frame + exit 1) for this card's target. Do not build a separate ad hoc error path for the App-return case — it reuses the exact mechanism from step 11.
13. What NOT to build: do not keep the E0122 typed-error-family refusal at the entry; do not require fn run() => App ? or fn run() => () ? annotations to enable ? inside an entry body — fallibility is unconditional per D-FAIL-EXIT1, independent of the return-type dimension (script vs App) this card owns; do not invent a new exit code for entry errors — reuse 1 (reported), 70 (stop), 101 (compiler-only, unchanged meaning).

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_app
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_app_graph
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/web/web_app.jet (manual smoke: serves with no hidden overlay)
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet build examples/features/web/web_app.jet
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet emit --rust examples/features/web/web_app.jet (both must now succeed; today both fail E0101 on this file)
- scripts/agent/jet-env rg "fn app\(\)" examples/ crates/ Source/ docs/ (zero hits)
- scripts/agent/jet-env rg "has_web_app_entry_fn|has_app\b" Source/ crates/ (zero hits)
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet self devtools grammars (confirm no unexpected grammar diff, since no new token)
- new: scripts/agent/jet-env jet run <a script fn run() with an unannotated ? call>.jet on an unhandled error; confirm full report printed and exit code is 1 via echo $?
- new: scripts/agent/jet-env rg "CryptoError" crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs (zero hits in the entry-gate error-emission arm)

Owned paths: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/WebApp.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle.rs, Source/Interpreter.rs, Source/main.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs, examples/features/web/web_app.jet, examples/features/web/app_hello.jet, tests/web_app.rs, tests/web_app_graph.rs, tests/dev.rs, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs.

cards.title: One App type across targets
cards.plan:
Scope: D-APP-UNIFY1 outcome B. One App type for every target, replacing WebApp. Platform comes from the existing #Target marker or the manifest target: field, never from the type name. Using a capability the resolved target cannot honor is a compile-time diagnostic naming the target. Delete WebApp and migrate every in-repo consumer in this change. Out of scope: the entry-detection redesign itself (#1446, this card builds on it), CLI args into the entry (#1450), job naming/subcommands (#1448/#1449), test/bench overrides (#1451/#1452).

Depends on: #1446 (entry returns the program value). This card lands after #1446 so the rename targets the new single-fn-run, return-type-driven entry model instead of the old fn app() sniff.

Approach:
1. Rename the type: crates/jet-foundation/src/WebApp.rs (WebAppGraph and friends) and crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/WebApp.rs (JetWebApp builder impl, methods .route .page .layout .action .form .data .mount .routes .csr .ssr .ssg .stream/.streaming .island .hydration_dev .hydration_release .security .assets .split .code_split .cache .a11y .adapter .facts_json .serve .serve_on) from WebApp to App. Delete the old name; do not alias.
2. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/WebApp.rs (extract_web_app_graph, apply_method): update the return-type check from Named("WebApp") to Named("App") — this is the one line #1446 built the return-type check around.
3. crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/webapp.rs (eval_web_core_call, eval_web_app_method, run_web_app_server): rename types/calls to match; this stays the single I9 Prelude-backed marshalling adapter for JIT/interpreter, unchanged in structure.
4. crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/methods.rs and subset/types.rs: rename the recognized type/method table entries from WebApp to App.
5. Target capability check (the new diagnostic this option requires): crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/OSTarget.rs check_os_target (:304) and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerMarkers.rs (:118, #Target handling) — add a check that a capability method used on the App value (e.g. .csr()) is compatible with the resolved #Target (crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs :268,730 for the ratified Target values Native/Web/Wasm/JS/Freestanding/OS). Register a new diagnostic code under docs/spec/diagnostics.md naming the capability, the target, and the fix (I4: needs code + what/why/fix + UI snapshot).
6. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/{process_ui.rs,fixed_sigs.rs,core_types.rs} and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs: rename WebApp references to App in the type-checking tables.
7. crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Context.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs, eval/mod.rs, eval/exprs.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/builtin_methods.rs: rename WebApp references.
8. Migrate examples: grep -rl WebApp examples/ (currently examples/features/web/web_app.jet, examples/features/web/app_hello.jet, plus any others the grep finds) — rewrite each fn run() => WebApp to fn run() => App.
9. Migrate tests: tests/web_app.rs, tests/web_app_graph.rs, tests/web_build.rs — rename fixture text and assertions from WebApp to App.
10. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: add "D-APP-UNIFY1=B — one App type, target by marker" next to the D-ENTRY-VALUE1 entry. docs/spec/diagnostics.md: register the new target-capability-mismatch diagnostic with its UI snapshot under tests/ui/.
11. Do not converge this with the separate jetpack "package output" mechanism (Item::Const / OutputKind Executable/Service/Environment/Image/System/Fleet in crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/patterns.rs :330-399, checked in Bundle.rs :2283,2334,2459) — that is an unrelated, already-ratified mechanism for package-level output kind, not the App value type. Leave it untouched.

cards.title: Built binaries expose jobs as subcommands
cards.plan:
Scope: D-JOB-SUBCMD1 outcome C. Jobs become subcommands of the program itself on every tier: jet run app.jet -- migrate on plain source, and ./myapp migrate on a built binary, same argv contract, retiring the separate --job flag from #1448. The marker argument is a typed scope enum: .Ship, .Dev, or .Internal. A bare #Job means .Dev — a subcommand while developing (jet run/jet dev/debug builds dispatch every job), stripped from release builds unless marked #Job(.Ship). .Internal jobs are callable from code/scheduler only, never from argv. Release builds print what they stripped and name the fix (mark #Job(.Ship) to include). Out of scope: renaming the word job itself (#1448, must land first).

Depends on: #1448 (unify job vs task naming). This card's dispatcher and marker vocabulary are spelled in terms of "job", so #1448 must land first.

Approach:
1. New Prelude-owned scope enum (I9: semantics live only in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude): add a JobScope enum (Ship/Dev/Internal) to crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/ alongside the existing WebApp/App Prelude file, so AOT emit, Cranelift JIT, and interpreter ambient all read the same enum rather than re-encoding the default.
2. Marker AST field: crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/items.rs (:957-1016, Func.task_metadata / TaskMetadata) — add a scope: JobScope field, default JobScope::Dev when the marker carries no argument. Model the parsing exactly on the existing TaskCachePolicy enum pattern (:1058-1064, written today as #Job(cache: .Shared, ...)) and TaskSkip (:1013-1030) — enum-literal marker arguments (.Ship) already parse through the ordinary expression grammar via task_word (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/external_tests_ffi.rs :425-430); no new marker-argument machinery is needed, only a new field + enum + parse/match arms in the same shape as cache.
3. crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/external_tests_ffi.rs (task_metadata_from_marker, :236-260): parse the new scope argument.
4. crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs: register the #Job marker's new argument shape (scope enum) alongside its existing rule! entry, same pattern as the #Target rule at :730 with its allowed-values list at :268.
5. Dispatcher unification (this replaces the --job flag from #1448 entirely): retire Source/CmdCompile.rs run_task_entry's flag-driven invocation; instead route argv[1] against the discovered job table the same way on every tier — jet run app.jet -- <job> <args...> for plain source (dev-tier: dispatches every #Job regardless of scope), and the AOT-emitted main (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs emit_cli_entry_if_needed, :680-724) for built binaries (release-tier: dispatches only .Ship jobs, reserves other job names as "unknown command"). Both call into the same Prelude job-dispatch table so behavior matches per I9.
6. Release build summary: crates/jet-driver or Source/CmdCompile.rs build path — print "stripped N dev job(s): <names> (mark #Job(.Ship) to include)" when a release build drops non-Ship jobs.
7. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerSchedule.rs (:16,65-69, E0928): extend the reserved-lifecycle-name check so a job name can never collide with a real CLI flag or another job's name at the same scope; the dispatcher must reserve job names before flag parsing (adversarial-pass finding from the ratified ballot).
8. jet jobs listing (Source/CmdCompile.rs run_tasks/list_task_names, renamed to run_jobs/list_job_names by #1448): show each job's resolved scope.
9. Migrate examples/tests: examples/features/devloop/task_runner.jet, examples/features/devloop/schedule_every.jet — add explicit scopes where the story needs a non-default one; delete any remaining --job flag usage.
10. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: add "D-JOB-SUBCMD1=C — jobs as subcommands, typed scope" entry. docs/spec/diagnostics.md: if a new diagnostic is needed for a job/flag name collision, register it with a UI snapshot.

cards.title: Typed CLI args flow into the app entry
cards.plan:
Scope: D-APP-ARGS1 outcome A. One rule for every entry: parameters on an App-returning fn run become typed CLI flags exactly the way they already do on a script fn run, using the existing ratified #[CLI] field-marker mechanism (D-CLIFLAG1). An incompatible argument is a launch-time diagnostic naming the flag, the expected type, and the fix. No new mechanism — this card is "make the App entry participate in the exact pipeline scripts already use," not a new argument system. Out of scope: the entry-return-value model itself (#1446), the App type rename (#1447) — both are prerequisites.

Depends on: #1446 (entry returns the program value) and #1447 (one App type). This card only makes sense once fn run can return App.

Approach:
1. Confirm/generalize crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Outputs.rs cli_entry_param_shape (:27-56) and CLIEntryShape (:14-23): today this gate runs regardless of fn run's return type (it classifies the single parameter's shape into Struct/Enum/EnumBadVariants/Invalid via #[CLI] struct or enum-of-#[CLI]-structs). Verify no existing code path special-cases "Unit-returning fn run only" — if the entry gate in Bundle.rs (:2279-2328) currently only calls cli_entry_param_shape for the Unit-return branch, extend it to run identically when fn run returns App, so both branches share the exact same E1307/E1308 diagnostics.
2. crates/jet-foundation/src/CLISchema.rs (entry_schema / entry_schema_for_bundle): confirm schema extraction does not assume a Unit return type; if it does, remove the assumption so an App-returning entry's #[CLI] parameter produces the same CLIInputSchema.
3. AOT: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs emit_cli_entry_if_needed (:680-724) already synthesizes the __jet_cli_main wrapper from entry_schema; confirm/extend it to call the App-returning fn run and then .serve() the returned value (the #1446 change), instead of assuming the entry always just executes and exits.
4. JIT: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs lower_jit_program (:924-964, entry_name resolution via CLISchema::entry_schema) and crates/jet-jit/src/jit/functions_compile.rs (:807-946, cli_entry / __jet_cli_main handling): same extension — the CLI-args-to-struct marshalling is identical, only what happens with the returned value differs (serve vs. discard), and that difference is already owned by #1446's Prelude .serve() call, not by this card.
5. Interpreter/dev tier: Source/CmdDossier.rs (:152,242, CLIInputSchema JSON encode used by `jet explain`/dossier tooling) — confirm it already treats the schema uniformly; no App-specific branch should be needed since the schema doesn't encode the return type.

cards.title: Command metaprograms are expert-overridable
cards.plan:
Scope: D-CMD-OVERRIDE1 outcome C. The override rule generalizes from dev-only to every command: fn test(suite: TestSuite) and fn bench(suite: BenchSuite) may replace jet test's/jet bench's default harness, receiving the compiler-discovered suite (after --filter) as an ordinary value with run()/iteration/result access. A no-parameter override fully replaces the default (same shape as today's fn dev()). jet test --default and jet bench --default force the stock harness and ignore any override; verification contexts (CI, this repo's own test/bench closeout) must pin --default so an override can never mint false green. Out of scope: bench's target/filter parity itself (#1452, recommended to land first since this card's suite discovery reuses whatever #1452 builds); the entry-value model (#1446) and job subcommands (#1448/#1449) are unrelated.

Sequencing note (soft, not a hard block): implement #1452 (bench target/filter parity) before wiring fn bench(suite: BenchSuite) here, so the BenchSuite discovery/filter pass in Source/CmdDevTools.rs is written once against the parity-complete run_bench rather than twice.

Approach:
1. New types (I9: semantics live only in the Prelude): add TestSuite and BenchSuite to crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/ — neither exists anywhere in the codebase today (confirmed by grep). Each type wraps the discovered blocks after --filter with run(), iteration, and result access per the ratified technical note. AOT emit, Cranelift JIT, and interpreter ambient must all construct the identical suite value from the identical Prelude constructor — no re-encoding discovery/filtering in an engine.

cards.title: Bench runner reaches parity with test runner
cards.body: — Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Bench parity is affected by two open questions on card #1641: D-CLAIM-BENCH1 decides the bench marker and claim model, and card #1647 corrects the build profile `jet bench` actually runs. Build the shared runner and its test coverage now; take the marker spelling and the profile from those outcomes rather than recording a pairing rule that may be amended.
cards.plan:
Scope: D-BENCH-PARITY1 outcome B. jet bench accepts the same targets jet test already does: a file, a directory (walked recursively), or a project, plus --filter for region names by name. Benches still always run one at a time, serially, for timing integrity. Assertion-only test flags (--shuffle, --coverage, --update-snapshots) stay test-only. Multi-file output is one line per region plus a per-file heading; --json emits one record per region. A standing rule pins the two commands together going forward: future runner-surface changes apply to both or name an explicit carve-out. Out of scope: the fn bench(suite) override itself (#1451, recommended to land after this card so it reuses this card's discovery/filter pass instead of duplicating it).

Approach:
1. Port the existing TestRunOpts shape (Source/CmdCompile.rs :1207-1218: update_snapshots, coverage, filter: Option<String>, shuffle_seed: Option<u64>, serial: bool) into a bench-only options struct in Source/CmdDevTools.rs — only filter and an implicit always-serial flag apply to bench; coverage/update_snapshots/shuffle_seed are test-only per the ratified carve-out and must not appear on the bench struct.
2. Port collect_test_files_recursive (Source/CmdCompile.rs :1273-1289, skips build/ and dot-dirs) into Source/CmdDevTools.rs (or a shared helper both files call, if that's the smaller diff — prefer a shared helper under Source/ so #1452's standing "future changes apply to both" rule has one place to change) and reuse it for bench's directory walk.
3. Source/CmdDevTools.rs run_bench (:2447-2530): replace the single-file-only fn run_bench(file: &str, mode: OutputMode) with a directory/project-aware entry point mirroring Source/CmdCompile.rs run_test_opts's dir branch (:1242-1268) — p.is_dir() walks recursively via the shared helper, sorts paths, benches every file, aggregates a summary.
4. Add --filter to Source/main.rs's bench argument parsing (today minimal, no flag-parsing block comparable to test's at :2069-2110) — thread it to jet::has_bench_blocks / run_bench_regions (Source/CmdDevTools.rs :2532-2551) the same way JET_TEST_FILTER threads to the generated test harness (Source/CmdCompile.rs :1367-1369), matching region names post-discovery.
5. Bare-entry / project-root resolution: Source/main.rs (:1996-2010, resolve_bare_entry("test",...) vs the partial bare_bench_entry) — extend bench's bare-entry path to the same directory/project walk as test's, not just a single resolved file.
6. Multi-file output: one line per region plus a per-file heading (per the ratified technical note, to avoid filter-name collisions across files) — path-qualify region names in both human and --json output.
7. --json: one record per region (mirror whatever shape jet test --json already emits per test, adjusted for bench's timing fields).
8. Explicitly do NOT add --shuffle, --coverage, --update-snapshots to bench — these are named test-only in the ratified text; if the CLI flag parser is shared code, gate them behind the command (test vs bench) rather than deleting the parser.
9. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: add "D-BENCH-PARITY1=B — bench runner parity with test" log entry documenting the standing pairing rule for future runner changes, so the next agent who touches jet test's target resolution knows to check bench too (and vice versa).

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test jet_test (must stay green — this card must not regress test's own behavior while sharing helpers)
- new scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test jet_bench (add this test file mirroring tests/jet_test.rs's directory/filter coverage, since none exists today)
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet bench examples/features/ (manual smoke: directory target, was previously an error)
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet bench examples/features/ --filter=<a-real-region-name> (manual smoke: name selection, was previously unsupported)
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet bench . --json (manual smoke: one record per region across the project)
- scripts/agent/jet-env rg "\-\-shuffle|\-\-coverage|\-\-update-snapshots" Source/CmdDevTools.rs (zero hits — confirms the test-only carve-out held)

Owned paths: Source/CmdDevTools.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs (shared helper extraction only), Source/main.rs, tests/jet_bench.rs (new), docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md.

cards.title: Arrow loop bodies in statement position
cards.plan:
Scope: D-LOOP-STMT-ARROW1=C. In statement position every loop header (finite-source, condition-only, bare infinite, state loop) accepts an arrow body '-> statement' and the yielded value is discarded; a non-unit discarded value gets a lint naming ':: collection' and the '&' write-handle form ('loop v, &values -> v *= 2'). Value position (loop producing a collected list, D-LOOPEVAL1) is unchanged: still finite source + non-unit yield only. The body picks arrow-vs-block by line width per the shared rule with D-BODY-ARROW1 (companion card #1454) -- implement together where practical since both touch the same formatter width rule. Out of scope: value-position restrictions, the write-handle '&' mechanism itself if not already implemented (check crates/jet-foundation memory-model status first; if the '&' write handle does not exist yet, the lint text still names it but the mechanism is a separate card -- do not invent it here).
Approach:
1. crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs: 'effect_loop_body' (~line 1330) currently hard-errors on TokKind::Arrow with 'this effect-only loop uses a result arrow' and requires a brace block (~line 1330-1364). Replace: when the body is a single statement that fits one line, accept '-> stmt' and wrap it as a one-statement Vec<Stmt>; when it does not fit one line or the next token is '{', keep the existing brace-block path. This applies uniformly across all three call sites of effect_loop_body: the infinite loop (line ~1207 uses block_stmts directly, needs the same arrow branch added), the state/counted loop (~1247), the iteration loop (~1307), and the conditional loop (~1320).
2. Add the non-unit-discard lint: when the parsed arrow body's expression statement has a non-unit type (sema-checked, not parser-checked -- flag the node and let crates/jet-sema surface the lint) reading '::' for collection and '&' for write-in-place, matching the exact wording in D-LOOP-STMT-ARROW1's code sample.
3. crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Items.rs: emit '-> stmt' for a loop body that is one statement and fits the configured line width; otherwise widen to a brace block with one statement per line (S6). Add a fmt STABILITY case per form in tests/fmt.rs (assert_fmt_stable), covering all four loop header kinds.
4. Delete the retired-arrow diagnostic path for loops once the new rule lands (the 'this effect-only loop uses a result arrow' error text and its teach_control_braces call become dead for loops specifically; conditionals.rs's analogous if-statement path is card #1454's responsibility, do not touch it here unless sharing a helper forces a joint edit -- coordinate via the shared helper, do not duplicate it).
5. editors/tree-sitter/grammar.js, editors/jet.tmGrammar, editors/vscode/syntaxes/jet.tmLanguage.json: regenerate via 'jet self devtools grammars' if the loop-arrow shape needs a new grammar rule (loops already accept '->' in value position, so this may only need highlighting/precedence confirmation, not a new token).
6. Source/LSP/Features.rs: confirm completion/hover for loop bodies is not spelling-specific; update only if it hardcodes brace-only loop bodies.
7. Add/extend an example under examples/features/ demonstrating a one-line arrow-bodied loop in statement position (e.g. 'loop job, jobs -> print(job)'), golden output in examples/features/expected/, proven under jet build (AOT) and jet run (JIT) per I9; exercise the interpreter path if the example can reach deopt.
8. crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs: confirm the Arrow token's decision-id comment is updated/cross-referenced to D-LOOP-STMT-ARROW1 alongside its existing D-ARROW-CONTROL1/D-LOOPEVAL1 references (no new sigil, so no new constant).
9. docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: append the dated D-LOOP-STMT-ARROW1=C decision-log entry naming the implementing card.
Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test fmt -- loop_arrow (new stability cases per header kind)
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots -- loop (confirm the retired-arrow loop error/teaching text is gone and the discard lint fixture is added)
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test grammar
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- <new example name>
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/<new-example>.jet (I9 parity)
Owned paths: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs, crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Items.rs, crates/jet-sema/** (lint), docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, tests/fmt.rs, tests/ui/*, examples/features/**, editors/** (only if grammar changes).

cards.title: Marker uniform attachment: one parse path, markers retained on AST
cards.plan:
Implement D-VERDICT-1455-1 (D-MARK-REG1) structurally. One shared marker reader runs at every node start, accepts any name including keyword-lexed ones, and attaches Marker nodes to the owning AST node for every use site. Delete every hand-bumped marker token, both function-marker applicators, the marker_sequence_leads_to_function heuristic, the three shadow site tables, and all lexer marker-name knowledge. Sema receives markers; parse-time desugaring into flags ends. (This half of the card is unchanged from the original scope and is already in progress per its own criteria evidence.)

Added scope, ratified 2026-08-06 (D-META-ONE1=A, D-META-FORM1=A, D-META-NAME1=A): parse the declaration side too, since D-META-ONE1 explicitly "fulfills D-VERDICT-1455-1" by moving rule rows from Rust into Jet. A rule row is now written as an ordinary Jet declaration in Prelude source:

  marker Inline(mode: InlineMode = .Hint, $sites: [.Function, .Method, .Constant])
  marker Pre(condition: Any, message: String, $sites: [.Function, .Method], $repeatable: true)

The introducing keyword is "marker" (D-META-NAME1=A -- already the project's word everywhere else, no rename). Facts about the rule ($sites, $repeatable) are ordinary named parameters carrying the compile-time sigil "$", the same mark used by "$limit" and "T.$layout" -- there is no "on" keyword, no "repeatable" trailing word, no second parameter list, and no scope-block form (D-META-FORM1=A rejected all three of those spellings by name). This needs no new grammar beyond an ordinary named-parameter declaration list plus the existing "$" sigil applied to a parameter.

Not in scope for this card: lowering the parsed "marker" declarations into whatever runtime structure sema/formatter/tree-sitter consume as "registry rows" -- that is #1457's and #1458's job; do not duplicate that work here. Also not in scope: implementing D-META-STAGE1's retirement of "#Known" (a separate ballot, tracked on its own new card) -- do not special-case "#Known" here beyond whatever the existing keyword-lexed-marker-name handling already covers generically.

cards.title: jet run drops recoverable diagnostics that jet build reports
cards.body: jet run silently accepts a program that jet build rejects. Reproduced on a retired marker: 'jet build' reports E0927 for a retired rule, while 'jet run' prints the program output and exits 0. jet run drops every recoverable parse diagnostic. This is general, not marker specific, and it breaks execution-tier parity for diagnostics: the same source must have one meaning on every tier. It also hides real errors from the default developer loop, which is the tier most people use.
cards.plan:
Scope: jet run must report the same diagnostic set as jet build for the same source. Today jet run drops every recoverable parse diagnostic: a retired marker gets E0927 under jet build while jet run prints program output and exits 0. This is a tier-parity break for diagnostics and hides errors from the default developer loop.
Approach: 1) Failing test first: a driver-level test that compiles one source with a recoverable parse diagnostic through both the build path and the run path and asserts the identical diagnostic set (start from the E0927 retired-marker repro). 2) Find the divergence in crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs: the build and run entry points return Result with Vec of Diagnostic, but the run path proceeds when the parser recovered instead of surfacing the collected diagnostics. Route both paths through one shared diagnostic gate. Report what parser and sema already produced; do not re-check anything in the driver (I3). 3) Expect the gate to reveal pre-existing broken examples under jet run. Run the examples corpus under jet run once; card each newly failing example that is not a regression of this change, and list them in the log. Do not allowlist. 4) Parity: jet dev and the interpreter deopt path go through the same gate.
Proof: the new driver test passes; the retired-marker repro reports E0927 with identical text and a non-zero exit under both jet build and default jet run; targeted run of the examples the change touches.
Owned paths: crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs and the run/dev entry points, the new driver test, plus card-log entries for any newly revealed example breakage (fixes to those examples belong to their own cards).

cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 45 gaps in core.os against eleven languages. Read the cluster row in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json for the current list. Some rows are container-attribution artifacts where a competitor puts an operation on a primitive type; confirm each against Jet's real member tables before building.
cards.plan:
Scope: close the core.os loss cluster in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json (47 rows). Verified against crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs: core.os today has name, family, arch, cpu_count, temp_dir, executable, pid, hostname, username, set_current_dir, on_interrupt; core.env has get/set/unset/vars/current_dir/home_dir; core.process has exit/run/cmd/pipeline. Exclude container-attribution duplicates already shipped elsewhere: gap.filesystem.exit (already core.process.exit), gap.filesystem.getenv/setenv/unsetenv/putenv (already core.env.get/set/unset -- env access deliberately lives in core.env per the D-OSFACTS1 note in examples/features/io/os_facts.jet), gap.filesystem.now (already core.time.now), gap.filesystem.gc (Jet is ownership-based with no GC -- not applicable), gap.filesystem.parse and gap.filesystem.endianness (belong to core.path #288 and core.binary #1481 respectively -- do not build here, flag in the card log so the ledger's own container mapping can be revisited). That leaves roughly 38 real capabilities.

Real gap families: process identity accessors (getppid, getuid, geteuid, getgid, getegid, getgroups, getpgid, getpgrp, getsid); process/session control, POSIX-only, needs #Unsafe (I1) plus #Target(OS.*) gating per the pattern in examples/features/lowlevel/os_target_gating.jet and ratified D-OSTARGET1/2 (fork, setuid, setgid, setpgid, setpgrp, setsid, initgroups, kill, wait, waitpid, pipe, mkfifo); OS identity alongside existing name/family/arch (release, version); misc (exitcode, success, stop, sync, umask, utime, getpriority, setpriority, loadavg, uptime, atexit, repeat/times); verify-before-building (stacktrace -- check core.reflect #1481 first, likely belongs there instead).

Approach: 1) Re-check each excluded row's actual container field in the live ledger JSON (ids carry a stale filesystem. prefix that is not the real container) before skipping it. 2) Implement identity accessors and OS-identity additions first (no #Unsafe needed) in crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs and fixed_sigs.rs. 3) Implement POSIX-only control functions behind #Unsafe(reason) and #Target(OS.*); do not fake POSIX semantics on Windows. 4) Add new identity/OS-info calls to examples/features/io/os_facts.jet; put #Unsafe/#Target-gated process-control calls in a new sibling file examples/features/io/os_process_control.jet so the beginner-facing os_facts.jet stays simple. 5) Rebuild jet; regenerate the ledger.

cards.title: Close the core.time gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 43 gaps in core.time against eleven languages, including date parts, leap-year tests and rounding. The month accessor carries four witnesses.
cards.plan:
Scope: close the core.time loss cluster in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json (43 rows). Verified against crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/net_text_time.rs, which carries the real method tables for Date, LocalTime, DateTime, Instant, Period, Zone, ZonedDateTime. 12 of the 43 rows are already shipped and are extractor false positives -- exclude: date (DateTime.date), day (Date.day), hour (DateTime/LocalTime.hour), minute (.minute), month (Date.month), second (.second), weekday (Date.weekday), dayofyear (Date.day_of_year), todate/totime (DateTime.date()/.time()), clear (Date/DateTime.truncate), round (DateTime.round). That leaves roughly 31 real gaps.

Real gap families: sub-second accessors (microsecond, millisecond, nanosecond, microseconds, nanoseconds -- split across DateTime-side vs Duration-side per the witness language, check each before implementing); rounding (floor, ceil -- DateTime already has round and truncate, add floor/ceil alongside); calendar facts (daysinmonth, isleapyear, dayofweek -- check against existing Date.weekday/iso_weekday first, may be a duplicate spelling; quarterofyear); duration (duration, fromhours, iszero, totalseconds, difference -- a DateTime/Instant minus that returns a Duration, distinct from Date.diff_days which returns Int); component mutation (replace); DST/zone (isdst, dst); construction (datetime, time -- explicit component constructors, mirroring Date.new already used in examples/features/text/dates.jet); verify-before-building, likely already covered, do not add a second spelling per I8 (after, before, compare -- check the ratified spaceship operator and plain comparison operators on Date/DateTime/Instant first; utcoffset -- check ZonedDateTime.offset_seconds, may be just a naming gap; push/add -- check DateTime.plus_duration and Date.add_period; strftime/asctime/ctime/gmtime -- check the existing to_string/format/format_rfc3339/parse_time/parse_rfc3339 mechanism first, Jet has one formatting spelling).

Approach: 1) Resolve every verify-before-building item against net_text_time.rs and the ratified math-operator slate first; shrink the real-gap list accordingly. 2) Implement confirmed-real accessors/methods: add to the per-type match arms in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/net_text_time.rs, and I9 semantics in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomTime.rs (rebuild jet after every Prelude edit). 3) Extend examples/features/text/dates.jet with the new coverage; add a Duration-focused sibling example if the Duration family doesn't fit naturally alongside the calendar-focused dates.jet. 4) Regenerate the ledger.

Proof: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_surface_ledger; scripts/agent/jet-env jet build examples/features/text/dates.jet && scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/text/dates.jet; node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --check.

cards.title: Close the ByteBuffer gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 42 gaps in ByteBuffer against eleven languages. This cluster grew from 20 to 42 once container attribution was corrected, so it is larger than it first appeared.
cards.plan:
Scope: close the ByteBuffer loss cluster in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json (45 rows, all confirmed container=ByteBuffer with no cross-container leakage from core.io/core.binary). Verified against crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs byte_buffer_method_return: ByteBuffer today is write-only -- len, is_empty, clear, to_bytes, write_u8, write_u16_le, write_u16_be, write_u32_le, write_u32_be, write_u64_le, write_u64_be, write_bytes. Zero read, cursor, or string-like methods, so all 45 rows are real; this is the largest true gap in the batch and the one genuine design slice (a read cursor), not just API surface.

Real gap families: constructor (new -- build from existing bytes or a capacity); read cursor (read, readbyte, readbytes, readstring, seek, rewind, position, eof -- needs one cursor-index field, keep it the smallest complete mechanism); string-like ops, decode-then-delegate to the existing String type where possible instead of reimplementing byte-level logic (contains, startswith, endswith, trim, trimstart, trimend, tolower, toupper, title, replace, split, join, lines, map, next, first, isascii, lastindexof); I/O lifecycle (flush, close, shutdown, copy, copyto, getbuffer, parse/decode); verify-before-building, likely covered by an existing type, do not duplicate a mechanism per I8 (reader, writer, bufferedreader, bufferedwriter -- check core.io's existing Reader/Writer types in module_items.rs core.io list first; open -- check whether this means constructing from a file path, likely belongs to core.files not ByteBuffer).

Approach: 1) Design the cursor first: one position field on ByteBuffer, EOF defined as position == len; this underlies read/seek/rewind/eof/position. 2) Resolve the verify-before-building rows against core.io's Reader/Writer and core.files before writing new types; reuse if the shape fits. 3) Implement confirmed methods in crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs (byte_buffer_method_return) and the matching I9 semantics in the Prelude -- locate the exact bytes/IO Prelude file under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/ before writing (FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs is the closest existing IO-adjacent module; confirm it is the right home or find/create the bytes-specific one) -- plus signatures in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs. 4) Add examples/features/io/byte_buffer.jet (new file, no dedicated ByteBuffer example exists today) exercising every new method, golden output in examples/features/expected/io/byte_buffer.out. 5) Rebuild jet; regenerate the ledger.

cards.title: Close the core.tasks gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 32 gaps in core.tasks against eleven languages. Check each row against Jet's Sender and Receiver containers, which hold some operations a competitor puts on the task type.
cards.plan:
Scope: close the core.tasks loss cluster in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json (18 rows in the corrected ledger -- the earlier 32-row figure in the card body predates the fix logged 2026-08-06). Verified against crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs: Task has join/wait, detach, pause, resume, cancel, trace (task_method_return); Sender has send (sender_method_return); Receiver has receive (receiver_method_return); core.tasks module items are spawn, spawn_group, join_all, channel, after, interval. Exclude container-attribution duplicates already shipped under a different container: send (Sender.send already exists), get/set/clear (Julia/Python Queue put/get/clear map to Jet's Sender.send/Receiver.receive -- Jet has no separate Queue type, the channel is the queue). Exclude as a design decision, not this card's job: lock, acquire, release, notify -- OS mutex/condvar primitives; Jet's concurrency model is task-plus-channel (D-COROUTINE1) with no Mutex/Semaphore type today, and adding one is a second concurrency mechanism needing an I8 roadmap slot or owner approval, not a ledger-closure card. Also exclude shutdown, stop -- thread-pool/executor lifecycle; spawn has no persistent pool to shut down. That leaves 8 real gaps, 2 of which need a quick check first.

Real gap families: yield (let a running task voluntarily yield control); exception (read the failure of a completed task -- today only join/wait, pause/resume/cancel/trace exist, no error accessor); waitany (wait for the first of several tasks to finish -- join_all already waits for all); currenttask (a handle to the currently running task, for self-cancel/self-trace); close (explicit close on Sender/Receiver beyond drop); verify-before-building (run, start -- check against spawn's existing signature first, likely already covered by spawn's synchronous vs detached forms, only add if a genuinely distinct workflow remains).

Approach: 1) Confirm run/start against spawn/spawn_group; drop from scope if already covered, log the reconciliation either way. 2) Implement yield, exception, waitany, currenttask, close: extend crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs (task_method_return / sender_method_return / receiver_method_return) and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs, with I9 semantics in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs. 3) Extend examples/features/concurrency/task_controls.jet and examples/features/concurrency/tasks.jet with the new capabilities, golden-test the output. 4) Rebuild jet; regenerate the ledger.

cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 15 gaps in core.net against eleven languages. This cluster fell from 23 after the prefix-naming fix taught the matcher Jet's protocol-and-verb naming, so the remaining rows are the ones that survived that correction.
cards.plan:
Scope. Add to core.net: nodelay/set_nodelay (TCP_NODELAY toggle), ttl/set_ttl, a socket_type accessor, sendfile(conn, path), reverse DNS lookup (dns_ptr), and service-name/port lookup (getservbyname, getservbyport). Out of scope, already covered: AddressFamily (derivable from the existing ip_is_ipv4); create_connection/create_server (covered by tcp_connect(_addr)/tcp_listen(_addr)); gethostbyname (covered by dns_a, forward lookup); gethostname (already shipped as core.os.hostname — a different container; the ledger mis-attributed it to core.net). Out of scope, no coherent capability: TLS Send/Length/Unwrap/options — four 2-witness rows with no shared meaning across the witnessing languages; Send is already covered by core.tls.write/write_all. Do not add speculative TLS surface for these.

Approach.
1. Read crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs core.net list (~line 645) and core.os list (~line 36) before editing.

cards.title: Close the core.archive gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 14 gaps in core.archive against eleven languages. The open operation carries four witnesses.
cards.plan:
Scope. Add to core.archive: crc32 (already implemented as a private fn in the ABI kernel, just needs exposing), adler32 (new, small, well-known algorithm), a deflate write-path compressor complementing the existing inflate decoder (zip_compress today only stores data uncompressed), zip_names_json (list zip entry names, matching the existing tar_names_json), and a streaming multi-entry zip reader/writer (open/next/read/write/close) — the current zip_compress/zip_decompress are single-entry only, and the card body names the open operation as a four-witness capability. Out of scope, already covered: gzip/gunzip (already shipped as core.compress.gzip.compress/decompress under a different container name than the ledger attributed); create (already covered by zip_compress/tar_add). Small convenience once the streaming reader exists: extract/unzip-to-directory, cheap to add alongside item 3 below rather than a separate primitive.

Approach.
1. Read corelib/core.archive/pkgs/archive/src/lib.rs (the dependency-free ABI kernel, D-CORE-COMPRESS1=A/D-DEP-ARCHIVE1=A) — crc32() and inflate() already exist there as private fns; zip_compress currently stores raw bytes only (method byte, no real deflate).
2. Expose crc32 as a public jet_archive_crc32(data) fn; add adler32(data) as a new public fn (std-only, no dependency).
3. Add a deflate(data) fn mirroring the structure of the existing inflate() (Huffman encode, reverse of the existing decode path); wire jet_archive_zip_compress to use it instead of raw storage.
4. Extend zip handling to support multiple named entries (today single-entry only): add open/next/read/write/close over a JetZipReader/JetZipWriter-style value, plus zip_names_json for listing, following the read-modify-write pattern tar_add/tar_get/tar_names_json already use in the same file.
5. Register the new module_items.rs "core.archive" entries (~line 748) and fixed_sigs.rs signatures; wire crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/core_calls.rs (~line 3019) with new "core.archive" match arms via the existing FFI bridge mechanism (D-DEP-ARCHIVE1=A), same pattern as tar_add.
6. Extend examples/features/io/archive.jet and examples/features/collections/zip_family.jet with crc32/adler32/deflate and the streaming open/next/read/close + zip_names_json calls; bless expected outputs.
7. Update docs/reference/core-library.md core.archive section.
8. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh.

Proof.
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_surface_ledger
- JET_GOLDEN_FILTER='io/archive' scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- examples_compile_and_run
- JET_GOLDEN_FILTER='collections/zip_family' scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- examples_compile_and_run
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/io/archive.jet, comparing output to the expected file, to prove I9 parity between AOT (golden) and default jet run.

Owned paths: corelib/core.archive/pkgs/archive/src/lib.rs; crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs, fixed_sigs.rs; crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/core_calls.rs; examples/features/io/archive.jet, collections/zip_family.jet + expected outs; docs/reference/core-library.md.

Note: this stays inside the existing D-DEP-ARCHIVE1/D-CORE-COMPRESS1 dependency-free FFI-bridge package (no jet Cargo.toml entry) — I6-compliant, no new owner dependency gate.

No ratified decision contradicts this plan.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the core.regex ledger card. The accessors ship, so only the integrated-tree golden (c4) and default-run parity (c5) remain. Add interpreter parity under I9.

## Current state

Neither commit is an ancestor of the current HEAD.

Interpreter `count`/data-limit evaluation goes in the comptime and MIR evaluators. Do not cherry-pick stale commits blindly.

cards.title: Close the core.url gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 12 gaps in core.url against eleven languages, including the fragment accessor.
cards.plan:
Scope. Add username()/password()/userinfo()/authority() accessors (requires parsing user:pass@ from the URL authority, which JetURL::parse currently drops entirely) and default_port() (scheme -> well-known port table). Out of scope, already covered — extractor blind spot: host(), the fragment accessor, scheme(), and port() already exist as Url instance methods in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/UrlMime.rs and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/net_text_time.rs url_mime_method_return (~line 863); "Hostname" is the same capability as the existing host(). The ledger extractor only reads module_items.rs/fixed_sigs.rs/Collections.rs and never sees this file, so five already-shipped accessors score as losses. Out of scope, already covered by a different mechanism (I8, one mechanism): merge is RFC 3986 relative-URL resolution, already served by the existing join() method under a different name.

Approach.
1. Read crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/UrlMime.rs JetURL struct and parse()/jet_url_parse_authority (~lines 8-140) — confirm there is no username/password field today.
2. Add username/password fields to JetURL; extend jet_url_parse_authority to split a leading `user:pass@` (or `user@`) off the authority before host:port; percent-decode each part per RFC 3986.
3. Add username()/password()/userinfo()/authority() accessor methods on JetURL in UrlMime.rs and register them in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/net_text_time.rs url_mime_method_return (~line 863); add default_port() as a small scheme->port lookup table (http=80, https=443, ftp=21, ssh=22, ws=80, wss=443, etc.), std-only, no dependency.
4. Teach scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs to also read net_text_time.rs's url_mime_method_return method-name table for the Url/Mime containers. Card #1471 (core.regex) needs the same net_text_time.rs extractor fix for a different function (regex_method_return) in the same script — coordinate so the two edits compose instead of colliding.
5. Extend examples/features/net/url_mime.jet with username/password/userinfo/authority/default_port calls; bless expected/net/url_mime.out.
6. Update docs/reference/core-library.md core.url section.
7. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh.

cards.title: Close the core.crypto gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 11 gaps in core.crypto against eleven languages. This cluster only became measurable once hashlib and hmac were added to the Python surface, so it has never been audited before.
cards.plan:
Scope. Add sha1, sha224, sha384, sha3_224, sha3_256, sha3_384, sha3_512 (all std-only, hand-rolled pure Rust, same pattern as the existing crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/SHA256Raw.rs), pbkdf2_hmac (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 key derivation, reusing the HMAC primitive that already backs hkdf_sha256), and an incremental digest/update Hasher (new() -> update(chunk) repeatedly -> digest(), for streaming large inputs instead of one full-buffer call).

Owner gate — do not implement, report instead: New/generate_key/private_encrypt/private_decrypt/public_encrypt/public_decrypt name Elixir/TypeScript's RSA-style public/private-key encrypt-decrypt API. Jet's asymmetric mechanism is X25519 sealed-box (seal/open in jet.crypto), which already performs the same "encrypt to a recipient's public key, decrypt with the matching private key" workflow under I8's one-mechanism rule. A literal RSA-compatible primitive needs a bignum dependency (I6 owner gate) and would duplicate the sealed-box mechanism (I8) without a stated reason. Leave these four rows out of the implementation; the card cannot close them without an owner ballot approving either the new dependency or the duplicate mechanism.

Approach.
1. Read crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/SHA256Raw.rs (the existing hand-rolled SHA-256, 73 lines, std-only) as the implementation pattern. Locate the HMAC primitive backing hkdf_sha256 under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/ before writing PBKDF2.
2. Add sha1 and a SHA3 (Keccak) implementation as new files beside SHA256Raw.rs, each pure std Rust with no dependency; add sha224/sha384 as the existing SHA-256/512 compression function with the standard alternate IV and truncation.
3. Add pbkdf2_hmac(password, salt, iterations, key_len) reusing the existing HMAC primitive in an iteration loop.
4. Add a streaming Hasher type (new(), update(bytes), digest()) that feeds the existing one-shot sha256/sha512/blake3/sha1/sha3 implementations incrementally, or exposes their block-level compression step directly if it is already incremental internally.
5. Register sha1, sha224, sha384, sha3_224, sha3_256, sha3_384, sha3_512, pbkdf2_hmac, and the Hasher type/methods in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs jet.crypto list (~line 582) and fixed_sigs.rs (~line 1662 area).
6. Extend examples/features/crypto/hash.jet and crypto_suite.jet with the new hash functions, pbkdf2_hmac, and the streaming Hasher; bless expected outputs.
7. Update docs/reference/core-library.md core.crypto section; record the four declined rows with a one-line rationale rather than silently dropping them.
8. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh.

Proof.
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_surface_ledger
- JET_GOLDEN_FILTER='crypto/hash' scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- examples_compile_and_run
- JET_GOLDEN_FILTER='crypto/crypto_suite' scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- examples_compile_and_run
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/crypto/hash.jet, comparing output to the expected file, to prove I9 parity between AOT (golden) and default jet run. Cross-check each new hash's output against a known NIST test vector inline in the example, since golden diffing alone does not prove cryptographic correctness.

Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/ (new sha1/sha3 files, sha224/sha384 additions); crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs, fixed_sigs.rs; examples/features/crypto/hash.jet, crypto_suite.jet + expected outs; docs/reference/core-library.md.

The owner-gate paragraph declining RSA-style New/generate_key/private_encrypt/public_encrypt in favor of the existing X25519 sealed-box mechanism is sound and needs no new ballot.

plan + criteria written; ready to implement. sha1/sha224/sha384/sha3_224..512, pbkdf2_hmac, and a streaming Hasher are in scope, all std-only. The New/generate_key/private_encrypt/private_decrypt/public_encrypt/public_decrypt rows are out of scope: Jet's X25519 sealed-box (seal/open) already covers that workflow under I8's one-mechanism rule, and a literal RSA primitive would need a bignum dependency (I6). Killed rather than balloted, per owner design kill criteria (duplicate mechanism); not blocking the rest of the card.

cards.title: Close the core.log gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 11 gaps in core.log against eleven languages, including severity levels such as emergency.
cards.plan:
Scope. Add critical and fatal severities (fatal logs then exits the process, matching Go's log.Fatal), disable()/flush() controls, and enabled?(level) (query whether a level is active given the existing set_level). All are thin wrappers around the existing crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/RingCsvLogTimeCrypto.rs jet_log_emit(level, msg, fields) dispatcher. Out of scope, already covered by a different mechanism (I8, one mechanism): warning (alias of the existing warn); the generic log(level, msg) verb (Jet deliberately ships named severity verbs instead, D-LOGTRACE1=A); Group (already served by the existing span/enter/close nesting); Time (composable today from core.time + log.field, no new primitive needed); Add/Handle/Handler/Formatter (Jet's pluggable-sink model — set_sink/otlp_file — already serves the same "route and format log output" workflow as Python's Handler/Formatter classes; a competing OOP handler hierarchy would duplicate that mechanism).

Approach.
1. Read crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/RingCsvLogTimeCrypto.rs jet_log_emit/jet_log_format_active (~lines 276-460) and the severity-ordering/filter table backing set_level.
2. Add "critical" and "fatal" emission paths; fatal calls std::process::exit(1) after emitting. Insert both into the existing severity ordering used by set_level's filter.
3. Add disable() (suppress all emission until re-enabled) and flush() (force the active sink to flush buffered output) beside the existing set_sink/otlp_file plumbing; add enabled?(level) as a query against the current set_level threshold.
4. Register critical, fatal, disable, flush, enabled? in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs "jet.log" list (~line 560) and fixed_sigs.rs (~line 1604 area).
5. Extend examples/features/io/log.jet and log_structured.jet with critical/fatal/disable/flush/enabled? calls; bless expected outputs. fatal's process exit needs a subprocess-checked example — check tests/golden.rs for an existing exit-code-sensitive precedent before adding a new pattern.
6. Update docs/reference/core-library.md core.log section.
7. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh.

cards.title: Close the Deque gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 10 gaps in Deque against eleven languages.
cards.plan:
Scope. Deque<T> today ships only len/is_empty/push_front/push_back/pop_front/pop_back/peek_front/peek_back/clear/new (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs deque_method_return, ~line 1670), backed directly by std::collections::VecDeque (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Context.rs ~line 2084). Add capacity(), contains(value), get(index), delete(value) (remove-by-value, matching List.remove's convention), init(list)/from_list (construct from an initial List<T>), to_list() (ToArray), join(sep) (for Deque<String>, matching List.join), reverse(), and split(index) (split into two deques at a position, via VecDeque::split_off). All are thin wrappers over existing std::collections::VecDeque methods or the List equivalents Jet already ships — no new engine work, and "new" is already shipped (method_calls.rs already has a Deque.new() arm; the ledger extractor does not see it because it is wired outside module_items.rs/fixed_sigs.rs — no action needed there).

Approach.
1. Read crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs deque_method_return (~line 1670) and the Deque arm of builtin_method_mutates (~line 1737) — confirm the current method set and the mutate-tracking convention.
2. Add capacity, contains, get, delete, init, to_list, join, reverse, split to deque_method_return; mark delete/reverse (and push_front/push_back/clear, already marked) as mutating in builtin_method_mutates, the rest as non-mutating.
3. Wire codegen in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs (the existing ~line 4558 Deque.new() arm is the precedent to follow) to emit the matching std::collections::VecDeque call (capacity(), contains(), get(i), split_off(i), etc.). VecDeque has no remove-by-value, so delete needs a short linear-scan-then-remove(index) helper, matching how List.remove(value) already works.
4. Register the new method names wherever Deque method-name validation happens alongside deque_method_return (check for a name-list parallel to the return-type function near the D-COLLBREADTH1=A markers).
5. Extend examples/features/collections/deque.jet with capacity/contains/get/delete/init/to_list/join/reverse/split calls; bless expected/collections/deque.out.
6. Update docs/reference/core-library.md Deque section.
7. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh.
