cards.title: Close the remaining String gaps after card #1409
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 61 gaps in String against eleven languages. Card #1409 is done and delivered what it named. These are gaps the ledger found afterwards, so this is follow-on work, not a reopening.
cards.plan:
Scope: String ships 30 methods in string_method_return (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs:1082). Card #1409 closed the earlier gap batch. The ledger now scores 61 remaining jet_loses rows for container String. Verified 2026-08-06 by reading string_method_return directly: none of the 61 names are present under any spelling, so all 61 are real gaps, not extractor drift.

Approach:
1. Group the 61 names (docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, rows where container=String and verdict=jet_loses) into families and add each as a case arm in string_method_return (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs) plus the matching Prelude implementation in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/UnicodeString.rs:
   - Predicates: isdigit, islowercase, isuppercase, isletter, isprint, isspace, isvalid -> is_digit, is_lower, is_upper, is_alpha (already close to is_alphabetic), is_printable, is_space (folds into existing is_whitespace unless distinct), is_valid_utf8-style check. Reconcile naming against existing is_alphabetic/is_numeric/is_whitespace/is_ascii so Jet keeps one predicate family, not a duplicate is_x/isx pair.
   - Search/index: find, lastindexof, indexofany, lastindexofany, matches, match -> extend the existing index_of/count/split_once family rather than adding a second one.
   - Splitting/joining: rsplit, replacerange, join, concat, partition, rpartition, byteslice, chop -> extend split/replace/slice family.
   - Case/format: titlecase, swapcase, capitalize, ljust, rjust, tochararray, codepointat, normalize -> extend to_upper/to_lower/to_title family; ljust/rjust likely fold into existing pad_start/pad_end (D-textunicode) rather than new names.
   - Mutation-style verbs that don't fit an immutable String (clear, push, pop, remove, write): confirm String is immutable-value semantics in Jet (bytes()/chars() are the escape hatch); if so these are legitimate declines, record with a decision id rather than implementing mutation methods on String.
   - Comparison/equality/misc: compare, compareto, equals, clone, intern, isnullorempty, tofloat, parse -> parse/tofloat likely already answered by destination-owned Int.parse/Float.parse (E0311, noted won in #1409); record as declines pointing at that mechanism, do not add a second parse path.
   - Sequence-style ops borrowed from Iter/List vocabulary (all, skip, droplast, indexed, first, flatmap, each, last, max, min, fold, reverse, chunk, findlast, scan): confirm whether these should exist on String directly or only after .chars()/.bytes() converts to a List/Iter; if Jet's answer is "convert first," record that as the decline mechanism instead of duplicating Iter's whole surface onto String.
2. Update crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/UnicodeString.rs with the corresponding jet_string_* Rust implementations; keep Unicode-table-driven predicates consistent with the existing D-TEXTUNICODE1 approach.
3. Rebuild jet (prelude is include_str-embedded) after Prelude edits: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build.
4. Extend examples/features/text/strings.jet (and/or string_parse.jet) with cases for every shipped addition; regenerate examples/features/expected/text/strings.out (golden).
5. For every name recorded as a decline instead of an addition, log a decision id (new D-STR-* ballot only if it is a genuine owner-facing naming/scope call; otherwise a plain implementer note is enough since #1409 already established the "Jet already wins with a different mechanism" pattern for parse/partition).
6. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh to regenerate docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json and .md from the updated source, then --check to confirm it is self-consistent.
7. Update docs/reference/core-library.md String section to list the new methods.

- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_collections_and_methods (or the string-specific test module, confirm exact name before running) string

cards.title: Close the remaining List and Map gaps after card #1410
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 27 gaps in List and 25 in Map against eleven languages. Card #1410 is done and delivered what it named. List.contains is notable: Jet's List has no membership test at all, and that row carries five witnesses.
cards.plan:
Scope: List ships in list_method_return and Map ships in map_method_return (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs). Card #1410 closed the eager-view/count/extend/remove batch. The ledger now scores 27 remaining jet_loses rows for List and 25 for Map. Verified 2026-08-06 directly against both match tables: all 52 names are genuinely absent, none are extractor drift. One correction to the card body: "List.contains is notable ... no membership test at all" is stale — List.contains already ships (list_method_return line ~818) and scores verdict "equal" in the current ledger; it is not part of this remainder and needs no work.

Approach:
1. List gap families (docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, container=List, verdict=jet_loses), add to list_method_return + crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:
   - Search: binarysearch, binarysearchby, findlastindex -> extend existing index_of/find family (List already has find, index_of).
   - Slicing/splicing: slice, splice, copywithin, copyto -> extend the existing view()/split_write family; keep List value-copy semantics distinct from the View-based mutation family already shipped.
   - Prefix/suffix: startswith, endswith -> mirror String's starts_with/ends_with naming exactly.
   - Set-like ops on List: union, intersection, difference -> only add if this does not duplicate Set's algebra (#1404); if these exist elsewhere on List already as list-preserving-duplicates ops, keep the distinction explicit in naming/docs.
   - Growth/capacity: capacity -> expose the existing Vec capacity if Jet's List is backed by one; otherwise decline with a reason (Jet's List may not expose capacity as a concept).
   - Copy/replace: copy, replace -> extend copy semantics already used by Map.copy work below; check this does not collide with existing clone conventions.
   - Random/order: random, minmax, minmaxby -> extend min/max family already shipped.
   - Ends removal: removefirst, deleteat, shift, unshift -> extend existing remove/pop family; keep the D-LISTREMOVE1/F value-vs-position distinction (.Val/.Slot) consistent rather than adding a third removal spelling.
   - Iteration helpers: eachindex, eachslice, values, keys, reduceright -> keep list_method_return returning Iter<T> per the existing D-ITERTOOLS1=A pattern (take/skip/chunks etc already return iter_ty); do not add an eager-copy variant that fights the lazy-view precedent from #1410.
2. Map gap families (container=Map, verdict=jet_loses), add to map_method_return + Prelude:
   - Constructors/factories: new, fromkeys -> these may already be answered by dot-construction syntax `[K:V].{}` (see examples/features/collections/map_merge.jet); if so, record as a decline pointing at that mechanism instead of adding a `.new()` method, matching how #1409 declined a second parse path.
   - Ends removal: popfirst, pop -> Map is presently unordered/hash-based per has_key/get; confirm ordering semantics before promising a meaningful "first"/"last" pop, or decline with a reason.
   - Aggregates/predicates: all, any, filter, map, fold, max, min, collect, first, firstindex, flatmap -> mirror the existing Iter surface: Map.keys()/values() already return Iter, so route these through .keys()/.values()/.to_list() plus the existing Iter methods rather than duplicating the whole Iter surface directly on Map, unless the ledger's competitor evidence specifically wants key+value pairs (entries-style iteration) that .keys()/.values() cannot express — in that case add one Map.entries()-equivalent lazy view, reusing the D-LISTREMOVE1/F lazy-view pattern.
   - Copy/equality: copy, equal, containsvalue -> straightforward additions mirroring Set.has/List.contains naming.
   - Mutation: set, replace, update -> reconcile with the existing add/add_new pair (map_method_return already has add/add_new); do not add a fourth insert spelling without a clear distinct contract (set = upsert without the Option return, update = transform-in-place).
   - key, tolist, intersection -> tolist likely folds into to_list() already used elsewhere (keys/values already return Iter with .to_list()); intersection is a Map-keyed-by-Set operation, scope it narrowly (key-set intersection) or decline if it duplicates Set algebra.
3. Rebuild jet after Prelude edits: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build.
4. Extend examples/features/collections/list_surface.jet with every shipped List addition; extend examples/features/collections/map_merge.jet (or add examples/features/collections/map_surface.jet if the file grows unwieldy) with every shipped Map addition. Regenerate the matching .out goldens under examples/features/expected/collections/.
5. Record a decision id for every declined name (constructor sugar, capacity, ordering-dependent pop, redundant Iter duplication) rather than silently skipping it.
6. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh then --check.
7. Update docs/reference/core-library.md List and Map sections.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_surface_ledger
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_collections_and_methods
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/collections/list_surface.jet, diff against examples/features/expected/collections/list_surface.out
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/collections/map_merge.jet (or new map_surface.jet), diff against its golden
- AOT build of the same examples, diff against the same goldens, to prove I9 parity between AOT and default jet run
- node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --check

cards.title: Close the remaining Set gaps after card #1404
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 20 gaps in Set against eleven languages. Card #1404 delivered correctly: is_subset, is_superset and is_disjoint ship at Collections.rs:1571 and :1593. An earlier ledger run scored them as missing because its extractor dropped match arms. These 20 are the genuine remainder.
cards.plan:
Scope: Set ships in set_method_return and SortedSet in sorted_set_method_return (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs:1534, :1552). Card #1404 correctly shipped union/intersection/difference/symmetric_difference/is_subset/is_superset/is_disjoint; an earlier ledger extractor bug had wrongly scored those as missing, which is already corrected in the current ledger and in #1404's log. The ledger now scores 20 genuine remaining jet_loses rows for Set plus 1 for SortedSet ("new"). Verified 2026-08-06 directly against both match tables: all 21 names are absent, none are the extractor bug pattern from #1404.

Approach:
1. SortedSet "new": Set.from([...]) / SortedSet.from([...]) already exist as the constructor (examples/features/collections/set.jet). Record this as a decline — Jet answers construction through .from() and dot-construction literals, not a bare .new(); no code change needed here, just note it in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.md's decline list if the checker supports one, or as a log entry.
2. Set gap families (container=Set, verdict=jet_loses), add to set_method_return + crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:
   - Algebra-adjacent: replace, take, update -> extend the existing add/remove/clear family; update's contract needs to be distinct from the existing add (which already returns bool for "was new").
   - Predicates/iteration: all, filter, first, each, indexof, max, min, fold, indexed -> Set is unordered by definition (hash-backed per the file header comment), so "first"/"indexof"/"indexed" need either a documented arbitrary-order contract or a decline; route the rest (all, filter, each, max, min, fold) through the same to_list()-then-Iter-methods path already used for union/intersection results, unless the ledger's competitor evidence specifically wants set-native laziness.
   - Transform: flatmap, map, flatten -> map/flatmap on a Set risk producing duplicate or unhashable output; scope narrowly (e.g. map requiring Hash+Eq output type) or decline with a reason if it collides with I8 (one canonical mechanism, already served by .to_list().map(...)).
   - capacity, new -> same disposition as SortedSet.new above (decline, answered by .from()); capacity may be a genuine decline (Jet's Set may not expose backing capacity).
   - shuffle, sort, toset -> shuffle/sort do not make sense on an unordered Set without first converting; toset already exists implicitly as the identity, and .to_list() plus List.sort/shuffle (once #1477 ships shuffle) covers it — decline these on Set itself and document the .to_list() route.
3. Rebuild jet after Prelude edits: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build.
4. Extend examples/features/collections/set.jet with every shipped addition; regenerate examples/features/expected/collections/set.out.
5. Record a decision id or a plain implementer log entry for every declined name (construction, capacity, order-dependent ops on an unordered container).
6. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh then --check.
7. Update docs/reference/core-library.md Set/SortedSet section.

questions.text: This misses the philosophies of jet. Minimizes friction proportionally to frequency of use (most common things should be easiest/fastest) and beginner friendliness with magic and ergonomics out of the box but allow full expert control
questions.answer: Agreed, and the ballot is revised. New recommended option C ships Set.sort() and Set.shuffle(), each returning a List. Sorting is a top-tier operation in the usage-frequency report, and dedupe-then-sort is an everyday idiom, so the most common Set step becomes one call. Both are spellings of the existing List mechanism, so no second engine appears. indexof and indexed stay declined for meaning, not purity: a hash Set has no positions, and the number they return silently changes after any add or remove — a beginner trap, not a friction cut. Positions stay on List, where they are real.

cards.title: Close the remaining Iter gaps after card #1400
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 19 gaps in Iter against eleven languages. Card #1400 is done and delivered what it named. Iter.fill carries six witnesses.
cards.plan:
Scope: Iter ships in iter_method_return (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs:970), backed by jet_iter_* in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs. Card #1400 closed the zip family. The ledger now scores 19 remaining jet_loses rows for Iter. Verified 2026-08-06 directly against iter_method_return: all 19 names are absent, none exist under another spelling.

Approach:
1. Group the 19 names (docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, container=Iter, verdict=jet_loses) into families and add to iter_method_return + jet_iter_* in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:
   - Constructors (not adapters on an existing Iter, but ways to produce one): fill, cycle, repeat -> these are static/free constructors like the existing Iter.range() family (jet_iter_indexes/jet_iter_from_vec pattern), not methods taking `self`; scope as Iter.fill(value, n), Iter.repeat(value), receiver.cycle() (cycle is a genuine adapter, wraps an existing finite iterator to loop it — needs an explicit terminal guard so `.cycle().to_list()` on an infinite iterator does not hang; require `.take(n)` before `.to_list()` or make `.to_list()` on an unbounded cycle a diagnosed error).
   - Predicates: issorted, issortedby -> extend the existing all/any family.
   - Terminal/consumption: next, split, compact -> `next` implies a stateful pull-one-item API; confirm this doesn't collide with Jet's for-loop-based consumption model (D-ITER1) before adding a public `.next()` — if Iter is currently pull-only internally and not exposed as a manual-step API, this may need a decision id since it changes what "iterator" means to the user, or decline in favor of the existing for-loop/each().
   - Comparison/output: compare, tostring -> extend existing eq/format conventions; tostring likely folds into the existing "{x}" interpolation path already used elsewhere (String.to_string, per #1409) rather than adding a bespoke Iter.to_string().
   - List-shaped adapters ported from List (List already has or is gaining droplast, lastindexof, findlast, shuffle, average, toset per #1477/#1478's own gap lists): mirror the same names/signatures once those land, so Iter and List stay consistent (I8 one mechanism) rather than diverging.
   - dedupby -> extend the existing dedup adapter with a key-function overload, same pattern as min_by/max_by.
   - chunkwhile -> extend chunks/windows family with a predicate-driven variant.
   - clip -> Go's slices.Clip trims backing capacity; Iter is lazy and has no backing capacity to trim, likely a genuine decline (no analog in a lazy pull model).
2. Rebuild jet after Prelude edits: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build.
3. Extend examples/features/collections/iter_adapters.jet (or iter_tools_audit.jet, whichever already covers the adjacent adapter) with every shipped addition; regenerate the matching .out golden.
4. Record a decision id for any name that changes Iter's consumption model (next) or is declined (clip); everything else is an ordinary additive method needing no owner gate.
5. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh then --check.
6. Update docs/reference/core-library.md Iter section.

questions.text: This misses the philosophies of jet. Minimizes friction proportionally to frequency of use (most common things should be easiest/fastest) and beginner friendliness with magic and ergonomics out of the box but allow full expert control
questions.answer: Applied the frequency lens; the decline survives it, so the ballot now argues from friction, not rule-citing. Five of the six names (fill, cycle_n, duplicate, tostring, clip/iterator, compact) are synonyms of repeat, join, to_list, and filter. The canonical call is already the same length, so shipping them cuts zero friction and only grows what a beginner must learn. next would add a second, stateful consumption model beside loops and adapters, and its workflows already have one-call routes: chunk for pairwise reads, take and skip for bounded steps. If a real stepping workflow ever appears without a route, the answer is a new adapter, not a cursor.

cards.title: Close the remaining core.io gaps after card #1402
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 9 gaps in core.io against eleven languages. Card #1402 is done and delivered what it named.
cards.plan:
Scope: core.io ships jet_std_io_* in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs (stdin/stdout/stderr, style, progress). Card #1402 closed the progress-reporter batch. The ledger now scores 9 remaining jet_loses rows for core.io. Verified 2026-08-06 directly against every jet_std_io_* function in that file: all 9 names are absent, none exist under another spelling.

Approach:
1. Group the 9 names (docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, container=core.io, verdict=jet_loses) and add to crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:
   - readline -> jet_std_io_stdin already has stdin_read_line as a method on a reader handle; readline's competitor evidence (C#/Go/Julia/Rust) is a free-function/short-form read-one-line. Decide whether this needs a second free-function spelling or whether the existing io.stdin().read_line() already answers it (likely decline, pointing at the existing mechanism, unless the ergonomics gap is real — a bare top-level `readline()` next to the already-ambient `input()`).
   - readuntil -> extend the reader with a delimiter-bounded read, mirrors Rust's read_until; needs a Vec<u8>/String delimiter contract.
   - take -> a reader adapter that caps how many bytes/lines are pulled (Rust's Read::take, Julia's take!); scope narrowly to the stream/reader handles already in this file, do not duplicate Iter's own take.
   - buffered -> expose a buffered-reader wrapper; check if the existing stdin/file handles are already buffered internally (if so this is a decline: Jet already buffers by default and does not expose the distinction).
   - println, sprint -> println is Go/Julia/Kotlin's print-plus-newline; Jet's print() (D-PRELUDE1) may already add a newline, making this a decline pointing at the existing print(). sprint (format-to-string without printing) may already be covered by string interpolation "{x}"; check before adding a duplicate formatting path (I8).
   - binread, binwrite -> raw-bytes read/write on core.io, parallel to the existing stdout_write_bytes/stderr_write_bytes methods already shipped; add the missing symmetric stdin-side binread and a general binwrite if one isn't already covered by write_bytes.
   - repr -> Julia/Python's debug representation of a value; check whether this belongs in core.io at all or is a core.reflect concern (the ledger container attribution may be wrong here — verify against the actual competitor evidence before committing to core.io).
2. Rebuild jet after Prelude edits: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build.
3. Add examples/features/io/io_surface.jet (new file, following the list_surface.jet naming precedent) covering every shipped addition, plus examples/features/expected/io/io_surface.out golden.
4. Record a decision id or plain implementer log entry for every name declined because it duplicates print()/interpolation/buffering already ratified elsewhere.
5. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh then --check.
6. Update docs/reference/core-library.md core.io section.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_surface_ledger
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test corelib (confirm exact IO test module name before running; io_input_reads_a_line_from_stdin already lives there per io_prelude.jet's own comment)

- AOT build of the same example, diff against the same golden, to prove I9 parity between AOT and default jet run
- node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --check

Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs, examples/features/io/io_surface.jet, examples/features/expected/io/io_surface.out, docs/reference/core-library.md, docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.md.

cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 75 gaps across seventeen small containers that do not each justify a card: core.sync 11, core.encoding.xml 8, core.process 8, core.db 7, core.testing 7, core.reflect 6, core.http 5, core.tls 5, core.uuid 4, core.binary 3, core.encoding.csv 3, core.random 2, PriorityQueue 2, core.args 1, core.encoding.json 1, core.mem 1, core.mime 1. Six of these containers are new, created when the ledger began measuring domains it had previously skipped. Work them from the cluster rows in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json.
cards.plan:
Scope: 17 small containers, each too small for its own card. Verified 2026-08-06 directly against docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json lossClusters: the live counts are core.sync 11, core.encoding.xml 8, core.process 9, core.db 7, core.testing 7, core.reflect 6, core.http 5, core.tls 5, core.uuid 4, core.binary 3, core.encoding.csv 3, core.random 2, PriorityQueue 2, core.args 2, core.encoding.json 1, core.mem 1, core.mime 1 = 77 rows, not the 75 the card body states. The delta is core.process (9 now vs 8 in the body) and core.args (2 now vs 1) — the ledger moved since the body was written; work the live 77, not the stale 75. All 17 modules already exist in source (located below); this is real gap-filling, not new-module bootstrap.

Real source per container (module_items.rs entry for module-level containers, Collections.rs for the one collection-method container):
- core.sync -> crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Sync.rs; module_items.rs "core.sync" entry
- core.encoding.xml -> crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingCodecs.rs + EncodingStream.rs (jet_xml_*); module_items.rs "core.encoding.xml" entry

Verified gap names per container (docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, verdict jet_loses):

- core.encoding.xml (8): close, end, flush, indent, name, nodetype, push, write
- core.process (9): id, kill, output, spawn, success, wait, exitcode, exited, start
- core.db (7): close, commit, len, name, raw, rollback, merge

For each container, confirm each name against real Jet source before adding (some rows are container-attribution artifacts per the card's own warning — e.g. core.reflect's "get"/"set"/"tostring" might already be answered by generic reflect.of(x) plus String interpolation, and core.testing's "run"/"main" might collide with Jet's own program entrypoint conventions; check before adding a second mechanism per I8).
2. Ship real gaps as functions/methods in the file listed above for that container, following each file's existing naming and error-handling conventions (Result<T, IOError> for fallible IO, plain return for pure functions).
3. For any row that is a container-attribution artifact, a duplicate of an existing mechanism, or out of scope for this pillar (e.g. a name that only makes sense inside a different container Jet already owns under another name), record a named decline with a reason instead of adding code.
4. Rebuild jet after Prelude edits: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build.
5. Extend the nearest existing example per container (only add a new file where none exists close enough): core.sync -> examples/features/tooling/sync_crdt.jet; core.encoding.xml -> find or add under examples/features/serde/ (no xml example currently exists — verify before assuming); core.process -> examples/features/io/process_builder.jet; core.db -> examples/features/io/db.jet; core.testing -> examples/features/tooling/testing_helpers.jet; core.reflect -> examples/features/comptime/reflect.jet or examples/features/reflection/reflect-value.jet; core.http -> examples/features/net/http_client.jet; core.tls -> examples/features/net/http_client.jet (no dedicated tls example exists; add one under examples/features/net/ if the surface warrants it); core.uuid -> examples/features/text/uuid.jet; core.binary -> examples/features/parsing/binary-reader.jet; core.encoding.csv -> examples/features/serde/csv.jet or encoding_csv_stream.jet; core.random -> find the existing random example under examples/features/math/ (verify exact name before editing); PriorityQueue -> examples/features/collections/iter_tools_audit.jet; core.args -> examples/features/io/args_audit.jet; core.encoding.json -> find the existing json example under examples/features/serde/ (verify exact name before editing); core.mem -> examples/features/memory/ (pick the nearest arena/pool example, verify exact name); core.mime -> examples/features/net/url_mime.jet. Regenerate every touched golden.
6. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh then --check.
7. Update docs/reference/core-library.md for every touched container.

questions.text: This misses the philosophies of jet. Minimizes friction proportionally to frequency of use (most common things should be easiest/fastest) and beginner friendliness with magic and ergonomics out of the box but allow full expert control. We want the BEST APIs/surfaces/methods/etc of any language. If we can improve our APIs, then we should do so even if it means updating the existing one
questions.answer: Applied both lenses; ballot revised. Frequency: every one of the 75 already reaches its result in equal or fewer keystrokes under Jet's canonical name, so declining taxes no frequent path — the cost is one docs lookup, and the reference names the route beside each declined name. Best-API: the ballot now commits to your rule — when a competitor's spelling beats ours, we replace ours outright (greenfield), never alias. This sweep's head-to-heads all came out win-or-tie for the current names (v4 vs uuid4, query_one vs first, next vs read, float_range vs uniform). The four real gaps found ship with the card, and the two real TLS gaps have a follow-up card. Locks and reflect writes stay out by the safety design: concurrency routes through core.tasks, and reflection stays read-only.

cards.title: Separate repeated capabilities from same-named distinct operations in the surface ledger
cards.body: The Core surface ledger parks 8172 rows in a single-witness bucket on the rule that one language alone is not evidence of a gap. A probe finds 1316 of those rows have two or more witnesses once container is ignored, and 686 carry a member that is already a scored loss elsewhere. The probe conflates two different things: one capability counted once per container, such as iter across ten containers, and distinct operations that merely share a name, such as close on ByteBuffer versus close on core.db. No mechanical separator was found; it needs judgement per name. Until it is separated, the single-witness bucket is the ledger's weakest number.
cards.plan:
Scope: ledger methodology only, not Core code. The witness count that decides jet_loses vs single_witness (scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs, verdict rule at line ~1460: languages.length >= 2 ? jet_loses : single_witness) is computed per container in isolation. A capability whose name recurs across many containers (e.g. "close") never pools its witnesses across containers, so every occurrence can get stuck at single_witness even when, pooled, 2+ languages clearly ship it — while other same-named rows (e.g. "close" on ByteBuffer vs "close" on core.db) are genuinely distinct operations that should stay separately scored. SYNONYM_GROUPS (same file, line ~187) already handles spelling variance within one workflow; it does not handle this cross-container name-reuse question. No mechanical separator exists (confirmed by the card body); this needs a per-name human classification. Re-derive the exact repeated-name count at start of work rather than trusting the card body's 465/1316/686 figures, since the ledger has moved since those were computed (the same drift pattern hit #1476-#1481).

Approach:
1. Re-run the probe: for every row currently verdict single_witness, pool by source.member across all containers (ignore container), and list every member name whose pooled distinct-language-witness count is >= 2. That is the current "distinct repeated member names" list; get its live count before doing anything else.
2. For each name, read every row's competitors block (the actual language + operation + container triple) and classify:
   - Same real capability, Jet lacks it wherever it applies -> this is a genuine pooled gap. Promote by having the scoring rule pool witnesses across containers for this name specifically (do not just hand-flip verdict strings in the generated JSON — docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json is generated and --check rejects hand edits per the script's own header).
   - Same real capability, but Jet already ships it somewhere under a different spelling that the matcher is not credited for -> this is a SYNONYM_GROUPS gap, fix there instead of in the witness-pooling logic.
   - Coincidental name reuse across genuinely distinct operations (the card's own worked example: ByteBuffer.close vs core.db.close) -> leave single_witness, per container, and mark it as reviewed so a re-run does not re-flag it as unclassified.
3. Implement the classification as data plus code in scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs, not as hand-edited JSON: add a table (e.g. CROSS_CONTAINER_CAPABILITIES, parallel in spirit to SYNONYM_GROUPS) naming every classified repeated name and its verdict (pool | distinct), and change the verdict rule so a name in the "pool" set counts witnesses across containers before applying the >=2 threshold, while a name in the "distinct" set (or any name not yet classified) keeps today's per-container behavior.
4. Extend repeatedCapabilities() (same file, line ~1615) so pooled-and-promoted names show up there with their full cross-container evidence, matching the existing 35-entry report's shape.
5. Add a hostile fixture to hostileFixtures() (same file, line ~2135) and its matching case in tests/core_surface_ledger.rs: introduce an unclassified repeated name and assert --check rejects it, so a future ledger refresh cannot silently reintroduce an unreviewed repeat.
6. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh to regenerate docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json and .md with the corrected pooled verdicts, then --check to confirm self-consistency.
7. Document the pooling rule and the classification table's location in docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.md's methodology section.
8. Flag, do not fix here: pooling may promote some single_witness rows to jet_loses for containers that currently have zero recorded losses, which would need a new or reopened lossCluster/owner card. That follow-on triage is separate work, not part of this card's scope.

Proof:
- node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --check exits 0 against the refreshed ledger
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_surface_ledger passes, including the new hostile fixture for an unclassified repeated name
- A completeness check: every name in the live repeated-name list from step 1 appears in the classification table (pool or distinct) with zero unclassified names remaining

Owned paths: scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs, docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.md, tests/core_surface_ledger.rs.

cards.title: Comptime folding evaluates runtime input and takes fallbacks as constants
cards.body: The comptime evaluator folds expressions that can only be known at run time. Reproduced on jet run: io.args().len(), env.get(NAME) and files.read on a path that does not exist are all evaluated during the build, and the ?? fallback is then taken as a constant. A program that divides by a value read from the environment stops the build with E0953 instead of running. Two consequences. First, the compiler's own environment is baked into the program, so the answer depends on the machine that built it rather than the machine that runs it. Second, no Jet source can reach the Cranelift host's zero-divisor or overflow branches, because folding always wins first, which leaves those branches untestable from source.
cards.plan:
Repro: fn main() { n :: io.args().len(); print(n) } -- and: fn main() { zero :: env.get("DIVISOR") ?? "0"; n :: 10 / zero.to_int() }. scripts/agent/jet-env jet run on the second stops with E0953 "your comptime code stopped the build" instead of running and trapping at runtime with the Prelude's division wording. Expected: io.args/env.get/files.read(missing path) are unknown at build time; the ?? fallback is not taken as a constant; the divide reaches the real runtime trap.

Root cause hypothesis: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/deopt.rs:293-296 run_whole_interp runs Comptime::TirBridge::run_bundle for the WHOLE PROGRAM under jet run's deopt tier through the same evaluator and error voice as pure compile-time comptime folding. crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:2050-2053 sets impure_depth: if allow_impure {1} else {0} for the entire program run, so ambient calls execute for real (correct for genuine execution) but any downstream failure (div-by-zero at eval/mod.rs:217-227 or eval/exprs.rs:5913+, "your comptime code stopped the build") surfaces through E0953's comptime-voiced diagnostic and returns via Err(d) => RunOutcome::Problems(...) in deopt.rs (a build failure), never a runtime panic + exit code. deopt.rs:188-207 rewrite_runtime_tier_diag already gives E0956/E0951 "quick run" voice but has no case for E0953, and more importantly the RunOutcome category itself stays Problems for ANY Diagnostic-shaped failure from deopt-interpreted code -- this is why "no Jet source can reach the Cranelift host's zero-divisor or overflow branches, because folding always wins first."

Approach:
1. The explicit #Const/comptime-binding evaluator (crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/dispatch/eval_method.rs:630-731) already gates Tier-2 ambient calls correctly behind #Impure (E3410/E3411) -- that path is fine and out of scope.
2. Distinguish "the deopt interpreter genuinely executing the program at runtime" (should read real args/env/files) from "the compiler deciding at build time whether a value is constant" (must never see ambient I/O results). Make crates/jet-jit/src/jit/deopt.rs run_whole_interp report a downstream panic as a real RunOutcome::Ran (panic on stderr, Prelude exit code), not RunOutcome::Problems.
3. Give E0953 (and any diagnostic reachable only via ambient runtime input under deopt) the runtime-tier voice rewrite, or better -- change the underlying panic path so a genuine runtime trap under deopt never uses "your comptime code stopped the build" wording; reserve that wording for an actual #Const/comptime-binding failure.
4. Re-point tests/floor_division.rs's "compiler folds the divisor" note at the now-reachable Cranelift-host branch (per commit db869244e's note on all_failfast.jet).
5. Coordinate with card #1488 (epoch e2, same concern per this card's 2026-08-06 log) before closing either -- do not implement twice.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test floor_division (re-pointed zero-divisor-under-jet-run case proves the Cranelift/deopt trap instead of being skipped).
- New golden example: jet run on a program dividing by an env-derived value exits with the Prelude's exit code/wording, not E0953.
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run <repro>.jet manual smoke matching jet build && ./<bin> byte-for-byte (I9).

Owned paths: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/deopt.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs, tests/floor_division.rs. Coordinate with card #1488.

cards.title: Fixed-width divide by zero panics with raw Rust text at exit 101
cards.body: U8 divided by a zero U8 stops the AOT binary with the raw Rust message 'attempt to divide by zero' and exit code 101. Invariant I2 says a rustc-level failure is an internal compiler error, never a user diagnostic, and every other divide-by-zero path reports the Prelude wording and exit 70. The fixed-width division path was left alone by the division-family work and still lowers to a bare Rust operator.
cards.plan:
Repro: fn main() { a: U8 = 10; zero: U8 = 0; print(a / zero) }. jet build && ./<bin> (AOT) exits 101 printing the raw Rust "thread 'main' panicked at ...: attempt to divide by zero" instead of exit 70 with the Prelude's "this division can't be done (dividing by zero, or overflow)" wording every other tier/type gives.

Root cause hypothesis: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs:1701-1721 emits BinOp::Div/Rem through the trapping .jet_div/.jet_rem helpers (Prelude/Core.rs:1387-1397, JetArith impl, already covers u8/i8/... with a branded panic) ONLY when the node's overflow flag is true; otherwise it falls to the bare Rust operator (line ~1719: format!("(({}) {} ({}))", ls, op.spell(), rs)). That flag is computed at lowering (TIR/lower/expressions.rs:872-879) as arith_overflow = ... && (ast_operand_is_integer(l, env) == Some(true) || ...), replaying ast_operand_is_integer (TIR/lower/fields.rs:28-42) on the AST operands. Type::is_integer() (jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs:850-855) does include Type::IntN, so a bare U8 IDENTIFIER operand should already trap correctly -- the gap is most likely in an operand shape ast_operand_is_integer resolves to None for (struct field, call result, a parameter path env.ty_of doesn't resolve for some fixed-width case), matching the card's framing that this is a pre-existing gap the recent division-family work (tests/floor_division.rs, tests/int_division.rs, which added a separate BigInt/Prelude/Core/Division.rs path for Int's /, /%, %, %%) never touched, since it left the old generic JetArith/overflow-flag mechanism alone for fixed-width /.

Approach:
1. Reproduce with a bare-identifier U8 divisor (confirm it already traps correctly) AND a non-Ident operand shape (struct field, function-call result, function parameter) to isolate exactly which ast_operand_is_integer case silently returns None/false for a fixed-width type.
2. Fix at the shared root: make ast_operand_is_integer (or the arith_overflow computation) correctly recognize every fixed-width-integer-typed operand shape the checker can resolve -- not a per-caller patch, and not limited to / or to U8; +,-,*,/,% on any fixed-width type must route through JetArith.
3. Only if jet_div's existing checked_div+branded-panic proves insufficient for some fixed-width-specific case (e.g. a width-specific overflow), route fixed-width division through the newer Prelude/Core/Division.rs machinery instead -- prefer the smaller fix (route through the existing trap) first.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test int_division (add a fixed-width U8/I8 divide-by-zero case asserting the Prelude wording + exit 70, not exit 101, if not already covered).
- New example + golden (.out/.err.out) for a fixed-width divide-by-zero, proving AOT wording matches Int's.
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet build <repro>.jet && ./<bin>; echo $? manual smoke -- exit 70, Jet-branded message, no raw Rust panic text.

Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/fields.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs, tests/int_division.rs.

cards.title: The JavaScript tier caps whole numbers at the double range
cards.body: On the web target a whole number is emitted as a JavaScript number, so it is exact only to 2 to the 53 while every other tier is exact to 2 to the 63. Measured: 2 to the power 60 answers 1152921504606846976 on AOT and 1152921504606847000 in JavaScript, and 3 to the power 39 answers 4052555153018976267 against 4052555153018976000. The arithmetic helpers compute in BigInt and then return a number, so the rounding is in the tier's representation, not in the helpers. This is a silent wrong answer rather than a trap.
cards.plan:
Repro: print(2 ^ 60) and print(3 ^ 39) built for the web target. AOT/native answers 1152921504606846976 and 4052555153018976267; the web/JS tier answers 1152921504606847000 and 4052555153018976000 -- silently wrong, not a trap.

Root cause hypothesis: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Web.rs:4863-4869, the jet_i64 JS helper (inside JS_POWER_PRELUDE) computes its range check precisely in BigInt (value < JET_I64_MIN || value > JET_I64_MAX) but then does "return Number(value);" at line 4868 -- converting the exact BigInt back to a JS double, exact only to 2^53. Every whole-number JS helper (jet_pow, jet_floordiv, jet_bitnot, the remainder helpers ~4917/4923) routes its result through jet_i64, so this one coercion is the shared point where every JS-tier whole-number op loses precision above 2^53, even though commit db869244e already made the intermediate computation and overflow-trap boundary exact. The broader cause is architectural: Int is plain JS number throughout the non-ABI JS emission path (Web.rs:4431, tir_js_expr's E::IntLit(n, _) => n.to_string() emits a plain numeric literal) while the wasm-ABI boundary emitter already uses BigInt literals (tir_js_abi_int_expr, same file ~4392: E::IntLit(n, _) => Ok(format!("{n}n"))) -- BigInt is only carried at the wasm-to-JS marshalling seam, not through general JS-side arithmetic/variables/comparisons.

Approach:
1. No new owner gate: D-BIGINT1 (2026-08-05 math-operator slate, ratified) already makes default Int arbitrary-precision -- the web tier carrying BigInt is I9 parity implementation of an existing ruling, not a new design choice. Run the tower CLI decision list command to confirm no narrower carve-out already covers the web tier before proceeding.
2. Represent whole numbers as JS BigInt throughout the plain-JS emission path, not just the wasm-ABI boundary: literals (tir_js_expr's IntLit, Web.rs:4431), the jet_i64/jet_pow/jet_floordiv/remainder helpers' return values, comparisons, and any print/JSON/foreign-boundary conversion currently assuming number.
3. Audit every other whole-number JS helper for the same Number-at-the-end pattern and convert each boundary to stay in BigInt until the value legitimately needs a JS number (Float ops, DOM APIs) -- a narrow, explicit conversion, not the default representation.
4. Prove tier parity above 2^53 using the tier_support assert_tiers_agree-style harness db869244e already added.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test power_and_exclusive_or (extend with a case above 2^53, e.g. 2^60, 3^39, asserting web/JS output matches AOT).
- scripts/agent/jet-env full cargo test --test web_build (or the specific web-example test covering arithmetic) for the built web bundle.
- Tower CLI decision list -- confirm no open/competing decision before treating this as pure implementation.

Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Web.rs, tests/power_and_exclusive_or.rs.

No owner gate: Int-as-bigint is already ratified (D-BIGINT1); this is I9 parity implementation, not a new design choice.

cards.title: A panicking task renders an empty panic block under jet run
cards.body: When a task inside a task group panics, the AOT binary prints the full six-line panic block and the trailing 'panic: a task panicked' line, while default jet run prints an empty block with no message, no function name and a blank source line, and omits the trailing line. A plain top-level panic renders correctly under jet run, so the fault is in the task-group panic path rather than the panic renderer itself. Reproduced twice on examples/features/concurrency/all_failfast.jet with stdout and stderr captured separately.
cards.plan:
Repro: examples/features/concurrency/all_failfast.jet (existing example) -- a taskgroup where boom() calls panic("task failed") while a sibling task is still running; g.all([slow, bad]) fails fast. AOT: stderr shows the full six-line block (panic: task failed / --> .../all_failfast.jet:17 in boom / source line + caret) then the trailing "panic: a task panicked" line, matching examples/features/expected/concurrency/all_failfast.err.out. Default jet run: the block's fields render empty (no message, no function name, blank source line) and the trailing line is also missing per the card.

Root cause hypothesis: panic("...") lowers to jet_panic_rich(file, line, fn_name, src_line, col, caret, msg, locals) (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs:1422-1461), the shared Prelude function AOT calls directly, which eprintln!s the six-line block itself before unwinding. Under jet run's Cranelift JIT tier, JIT-compiled code cannot call that Rust function directly -- it calls a separate reimplementation, jet_jit_rich_panic (crates/jet-jit/src/jit/runtime_host.rs:848-883), an extern "C" JIT-host bridge that resolves its string arguments via rt.heap.clone_string(...).unwrap_or_default() (~858-862) against Concurrency::with_runtime_mut's state, which is thread_local! (crates/jet-jit/src/Concurrency.rs:22). A taskgroup task body runs on a scheduler worker thread spawned via std::thread::spawn (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, worker loop ~2470-2510), which gets its own fresh JitRuntime/heap on that new OS thread. If the panic's string data was allocated on the MAIN thread's heap (heap handles are per-thread), clone_string on the worker thread finds nothing and silently returns None for every field via unwrap_or_default() -- producing exactly "no message, no function name, blank source line" while the block's fixed structure (labels/arrows/pipes) still prints. This also reads as an I9 concern: jet_jit_rich_panic re-implements the same rendering jet_panic_rich already owns in the shared Prelude, instead of the JIT calling through to that one Prelude function.

Approach:
1. Confirm by tracing whether jet_jit_rich_panic's rt.heap.clone_string(...) calls return None specifically when invoked from a taskgroup worker thread vs the main thread for a top-level panic (which the card says renders correctly).
2. Fix at the shared root, not the taskgroup caller specifically: either (a) make the scheduler worker thread share or correctly re-resolve heap handles across the std::thread::spawn boundary, or (b) per I9, stop re-implementing the six-line renderer in jet_jit_rich_panic and have JIT-compiled task code marshal through to the same Prelude rendering AOT uses.
3. Investigate the missing trailing "panic: a task panicked" line under jet run too -- likely the same cross-thread state issue (jet_scheduler_fatal, Scheduler.rs:101).
4. Prove AOT and default jet run produce byte-identical stderr for the example (I9); interpreter deopt too if taskgroups reach it.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- all_failfast (AOT vs examples/features/expected/concurrency/all_failfast.err.out).
- New/extended targeted test asserting jet run's stderr on all_failfast.jet matches the same golden byte-for-byte (I9) -- likely alongside tests/dev.rs's existing 3-way parity harness.
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/concurrency/all_failfast.jet manual smoke, comparing stderr to the AOT run.

Owned paths: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/runtime_host.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/Concurrency.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, tests/dev.rs.

cards.title: Value dispatch rejects a range arm head
cards.body: A value dispatch arm whose head is a range fails to parse. examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet:37 writes 'return if n == { 0..9 -> 1 }' and the parser reports E0003 'expected -> after a value dispatch arm head, found ..', then cascades. The example stopped parsing at commit c3cbdc85b. It is the only failure in the fmt lossless corpus, so it has been masking that suite all session.
cards.plan:
Repro: examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet:37 -- "return if n == { 0..9 -> 1 ... }". jet build/jet fmt on it reports E0003 "expected -> after a value dispatch arm head, found .." and cascades; it's the only failure in the fmt lossless corpus.

Root cause hypothesis: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/conditionals.rs. The range-arm-head grammar (Int .. Int -> ..., with the E0318/..= and E0319/step recovery diagnostics) is implemented ONLY inline inside if_arms (the STATEMENT-position when/switch parser, function starting at line 413, range detection ~452-536) -- it is never extracted into the shared if_arm_head helper (line 575+). parse_dispatch_expr (line ~943, the EXPRESSION-position, value-producing "return if n == { ... }" form per D-IFDIST1) calls if_arm_head directly (line 999) for each arm head with no range detection, so it parses "0" as a bare value head, then self.expect(TokKind::Arrow, "after a value dispatch arm head") (line 1000) fails on the next token ".." -- exactly the reported E0003.

Approach:
1. Extract the range-arm-head detection block (conditionals.rs ~452-536: the Int .. Int ->, ..= -> E0318, step -> E0319 recovery logic) out of if_arms into a shared helper (or fold it into if_arm_head itself) so BOTH statement-position when/switch and expression-position value dispatch (parse_dispatch_expr) call the same range-arm-head path -- fix at the shared root, not by duplicating the block into parse_dispatch_expr.
2. Verify the formatter (crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Expressions.rs / Statements.rs) round-trips the expression-position range arm the same way it already does for the statement form.
3. Confirm sema/TIR treat a range arm in the value-dispatch (expression) form the same as the statement form (TIR/lower/patterns.rs lower_range_switch or equivalent) -- this likely already works once parsing succeeds, since the desugared AST shape should be the same regardless of arm-head spelling.
4. Coordinate with card #1489 (epoch e2, duplicate per this card's 2026-08-06 log, "the later number but sits in the epoch that owns the example") -- keep one, close the other, do not implement twice.

Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test syntax_reconciliation (add a UI/example case for "return if n == { 0..9 -> 1 else -> 0 }" if none exists).
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet build examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet -- parses and runs; matches its golden.
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test fmt -- the fmt lossless corpus no longer fails on this example (currently the ONLY failure per the card).

Owned paths: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/conditionals.rs, examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet, tests/fmt.rs. Coordinate with card #1489.

cards.title: Implicit const-fold evaluates nondeterministic Core calls (random, time)
cards.body:
An immutable binding is an implicit folding opportunity (D-VERDICT-1308-1, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs:687). The comptime evaluator accepts core.random and core.time calls, so those fold to compile-time literals while the runtime seed call stays a statement.

Repro A: random.seed(11); a :: random.normal(0.0, 1.0); random.seed(11); b :: random.normal(0.0, 1.0) -> a == b prints false. examples/features/math/random_audit.jet already shows this; examples/features/expected/math/random_audit.out is correct and the compiler is wrong.

Repro B: a :: time.now(); b :: time.now() -> a == b prints true.

Emitted Rust proves the fold: `let user_x: f64 = 0.7399976204803688f64;` beside a live `jet_std_random_seed(11i64);`. Mutable `:=` bindings are unaffected.

Root cause: the fold gate is Comptime::is_tier2_core_call (crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/dispatch.rs:93). It only treats core.random as Tier-2 under repl_mode, and never treats core.time as Tier-2. Sema already knows the full set as Purity::is_nondeterministic_core (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Purity.rs:99); the two lists must agree.

Keep random.rng(seed) foldable: an explicitly seeded generator is injected deterministic data. Implicit folds fail silently, so blocked calls fall back to the ordinary runtime path; explicit comptime bindings get a real diagnostic instead of a wrong literal.
cards.plan: 1) Extend the Tier-2 fold gate to every nondeterministic Core call (core.random except rng, core.time now/sleep/start, core.crypto.random.bytes), unconditional on repl_mode. 2) Keep the comptime list and Sema::Purity::is_nondeterministic_core in one shared place so they cannot drift. 3) Prove the reseed identity on AOT, jet run, and interpreter deopt (I9). 4) Audit examples and goldens that silently depended on a folded clock or RNG.

cards.title: Value dispatch rejects range arm heads (0..9 -> 1)
cards.body:
Statement dispatch accepts a range arm head; value dispatch does not.

Works: if n == { 0..9 -> { return 1 } else -> { return 3 } }
Fails: return if n == { 0..9 -> 1  10..99 -> 2  else -> 3 }
  Error [E0003]: expected `->` after a value dispatch arm head, found `..`

examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet has carried this hard parse error since c3cbdc85b, so the fmt-lossless corpus cannot format it.

Root cause: the range-head parser (including the E0318 `..=` and E0319 `step` porting hazards) is inlined twice in crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/conditionals.rs, at :457 and :1278. The shared head parser if_arm_head (:575) has no range case, and parse_dispatch_expr (:999) calls only if_arm_head.

The fix is a net deletion: move range-head parsing into if_arm_head and delete both inline copies, so every dispatch form gets ranges from one place. A range arm desugars to the same PatternTest node the statement form already produces, so sema, TIR, AOT, JIT, and interpreter need no new semantics.
cards.plan: 1) Move range-head parsing (lo..hi, E0318 ..=, E0319 step) into if_arm_head. 2) Delete the two inline copies. 3) Formatter emission plus fmt STABILITY round-trip for a value-form range arm. 4) Restore branch_dispatch_bench.jet with golden output and prove it on every tier (I9).

E0318/E0319 fire byte-identical in value-dispatch position. branch_dispatch_bench golden passes on jet run + AOT release; fmt --check clean. Note: fmt-lossless-corpus test currently fails on an unrelated pre-existing UI-manifest gap (tests/ui/E0927_retired_pure_callable.jet, from unrelated commit e122019c7) — not caused by this card and not blocking; branch_dispatch_bench itself formats losslessly.

cards.title: fmt-lossless corpus red on master: UI config fixtures pinned as parse-invalid
cards.body:
tests/fmt fmt-lossless-corpus currently PASSES on master (fab1faba3) — commit 70eb0086d ("test(fmt): true-up UI parse-validity pins after Pure retirement") fixed a different red-corpus cause (retired-pure fixtures plus serde_rename_not_string) after this card was filed. The category error below is still real and unfixed; it just is not red right now, so criterion #1 is a regression guard, not new work.

tests/ui/build_entry_conflict/pkg.jet does not parse as program source (E0003 on the `payload:` header) and IS already listed in UI_PARSE_INVALID (fmt_lossless.rs:6, sorted list, line 20). It is not absent — that original claim is stale. It is the 22nd of 22 tests/ui/**/pkg.jet files; the other 21 sit in that manifest only because a package manifest is config, never program source. That is a category error: a new manifest fixture still breaks the corpus the moment its parse-invalidity does not match by luck.

The examples loop (tests/support/fmt_lossless.rs, run_supported_source_corpus, lines 1275-1283) classifies PAYLOAD_FILE/WORKSPACE_FILE as config and skips them. The UI loop (lines 1311 onward) does not; every tests/ui/**/pkg.jet must be hand-pinned in UI_PARSE_INVALID instead.

Second defect: the corpus asserts inside the scan loop (line 1321, assert_eq!(actual_is_invalid, expected_invalid, ...)), so the first mismatch aborts the run and every later fixture goes unchecked.

examples/jetpack/epoch5/config/dev.jet needs no fix. It is ordinary Jet syntax (a top-level `dev :: Config.{ ... }` binding), not a `payload:`/`workspace:` header, so it already parses and formats through the normal example_programs path — confirmed with `jet fmt --check --diff`, which reports only a whitespace reformat, not a parse error. Out of scope for this card.
cards.plan: 1) Classify PAYLOAD_FILE and WORKSPACE_FILE under tests/ui as config, matching the examples loop (run_supported_source_corpus, lines 1275-1283). 2) Delete the 22 pkg.jet lines from UI_PARSE_INVALID — all 22 tests/ui/**/pkg.jet files are currently pinned there (`find tests/ui -name pkg.jet` finds 22; `find tests/ui -name workspace.jet` finds none, so only pkg.jet needs the reclassification today). 3) Collect mismatches in the UI loop (currently lines 1311-1348) into a Vec and assert once at the end so a single bad fixture stops masking the rest. 4) No fix needed for examples/jetpack/epoch5/config/dev.jet — confirmed out of scope, see body.

cards.title: Close the Bits copy gap the ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger's pooled-witness pass scored one real gap: BitSet (renamed Bits by #1439) is missing a copy/clone method, matched against C#'s BitSet.Clone. core.fmt and core.text.unicode show zero scored gaps as of the 2026-08-06 ledger snapshot; re-check the live ledger before assuming the card body's original three-container framing still holds.
cards.plan:
Scope: re-verified 2026-08-06 directly against docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json (generatedOn 2026-08-06, same day as this audit). The card body's claim of three containers gaining scored gaps (core.fmt, BitSet, core.text.unicode) is stale: the live ledger rows show ZERO jet_loses rows for core.fmt (131 rows: jet_wins/single_witness only) and ZERO for core.text.unicode (59 rows: jet_wins/equal/single_witness only). Only BitSet has a real scored gap, and only one: gap.BitSet.copy, a pooled witness from C# BitSet.Clone (pooledWitnessCount 2, witnessCount 1). Work the live ledger, not the stale body: the only real work item right now is a copy/clone method.

Dependency: BitSet is renamed to Bits by ratified D-COLLNAME1=A (card #1439, phase ready). This card is blocked on #1439 landing first, and the plan below is written directly against the post-rename name (Bits) so no further edit is needed once #1439 ships.

Approach:
1. Confirm #1439 has landed (Bits.* exists in crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs bit_set_method_return, Syntax::TYPE_BIT_SET string value is 'Bits').
2. Re-run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh immediately before building, since the ledger has moved twice already in one day (per this card and #1481's own notes) -- do not trust the card body's row counts.
3. Add a copy method to bit_set_method_return (crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs:1800) returning Some(Some(Type::Named(Syntax::TYPE_BIT_SET.to_string()))) (post-rename: Bits), following the exact pattern byte_buffer_method_return already uses for its own 'clone' | 'copy' row (same file, ~line 1819) -- a value copy, not a reference alias.
4. Add the matching jet_bits_copy (or equivalent) Prelude implementation beside the existing Bits add/remove/has/to_list implementations, and register it wherever those are dispatched (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs and the codegen TIR match arms that already handle Bits per #1439's sweep).
5. Extend the Bits example (examples/features/collections/, whichever file #1439 renames the former bitset example to) with a .copy() call proving the copy is independent of the original (mutate one, assert the other is unchanged); regenerate its golden.
6. Run node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs --refresh then --check to confirm BitSet/Bits shows 0 jet_loses.
7. Update docs/reference/core-library.md Bits section with the new method.
8. Re-check core.fmt and core.text.unicode against the freshly refreshed ledger before closing the card; if a later pooling pass reintroduces gaps there (the mechanism the card body describes), work those rows using the same real-source-first method #1481 and #1470 use: locate the real Prelude file, ship or decline with a reason, do not invent a new module.

cards.title: Synonym groups cross domains and invent losses
cards.body: SYNONYM_GROUPS in scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs is one global table, so a collection verb folds a maths or time operation into itself. Proven rows: core.math.clear is scored from C# Math.Truncate and Kotlin truncate, because truncate sits in the clear group; core.time.push is scored from C# DateTime.Add, Elixir add and Go Add, because add sits in the push group; core.time.clear is scored from Elixir truncate and Go Reset. Rounding toward zero is not emptying a container, and date arithmetic is not appending. The table needs to be scoped by container kind, the same way witness pooling now is.
cards.plan:

2. Give canonicalKey and synonymsFor the container, and skip a type-only group in a module container.
3. Refresh and report how far the loss count moves.
4. Add a hostile fixture that fails if a collection verb matches in a module container.

questions.text:
1) What is the / separator in the examples? That doesnt look like syntax we have already and I dont think i like it. I might be ok with like a plus operator to concat strings together easily then a more advanced concat function to enable delimiters and stuff. I dont know the details of how a - operator would work or any others though. 
2) What if we need to ensure we have an ACTUAL path type, not just a string, for safety or other compatibility issues? Is that a legitimate concern or not? If it is, then how can experts enable path only input mode?
questions.answer:
1) The / in the ballot examples is not Jet syntax today. It was copied from Python pathlib as a sketch. / in Jet is still division. You are right to reject it here.

Path joining should use methods we already lean on (and that D-PATHFS1 started): path.join("logs"), path.parent(), and so on. No new operator is required for this ballot.

About +:
- String + String stays ordinary text glue. Writing base + "/" + name is still the bug Path exists to stop.
- Path + String (or Path + Path) can later mean “join as a path,” with the right OS separator. That is a separate, small syntax choice. It is not required to pick Path as a type.
- A richer join helper (custom delimiters, many parts) belongs on Path or strings as a named function, not as -, /, or other arithmetic operators. Those names fight math.

I will change the ballot examples to .join, not /.

2) Yes, wanting a real Path sometimes is a fair concern. A Path means “this value was built or checked as a filesystem path,” not “any text.” That matters for untrusted input, FFI, and APIs where a random String would be the wrong kind of value.

It is not a good default for every call. fs.read("notes.txt") is clear. Forcing Path.from on every literal is beginner tax (ballot option C).

Default Core stays String | Path (option A): beginners pass strings; experts pass Path when they have one.

Experts who need Path-only can use:
- APIs or overloads that take only Path (expert surfaces, FFI bridges, validators that return Path)
- A boundary convert once: raw text -> Path (check/normalize), then pass Path downstream
- Optional later: a project lint or policy that forbids bare String at filesystem calls

So: Path type yes; String still welcome at Core doors; Path-only where the API truly needs it, not everywhere.

cards.title: Type system v2: carriers and knowledge — first-principles proposal + ballot slate
cards.body: Proposal at docs/proposals/type-system-v2-carriers-and-knowledge.md. One foundation for types, numbers, units, refinements, measures, and fact planes: a type is a carrier plus knowledge. All eleven D-TYPE2-* ballots are ratified, every one option A. What is left on this card is the record work: write the outcomes into the spec, update the owner-controlled surface file, regenerate the grammars, re-bless the snapshots, and confirm the implementation cards exist. The build lives on those cards.
cards.plan:
All eleven D-TYPE2-* ballots are ratified, every one option A, on 2026-08-06:
FOUND1 carrier plus knowledge, NUM1 the number grid with BigInt folded into Int,
REFINE1 one range spelling, TIME1 time on the unit plane, MEASURE1 one measure
substrate, EXACT1 the precision conservation law, UNCERT1 the measured grade,
PLANE1 the plane law, SPELL1 inline ranges in type position, IMAG1 the 4i literal,
DEFAULT1 exact by default.

This card builds nothing further. Its remaining job is to write the law down and
hand the build to eleven implementation cards, one per decision.

Step 1 — Record the outcomes. Add one entry per ratified decision to
docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md. Each entry names the option, the surface it fixed,
and every decision it amends:
  - NUM1 retires the BigInt name and the four errors that police mixing Int with
    BigInt; sized widths such as U8 become Int plus a proven range and a one-byte
    layout, spelling unchanged.
  - REFINE1 makes distinct Int(1..6) the one spelling and retires the #Invariant
    marker under law zero, with a replacement note.
  - SPELL1 allows Int(0..100) in any type position and keeps the literal-only
    bounds rule from D-RANGE-VALUE1.
  - TIME1 makes Duration the delta quantity and Instant the point quantity of one
    canonical Time family, and deletes both hidden duration suffix tables.
  - MEASURE1 amends the stored encoding chosen by D-COMPUTE-TYPE1 for vector and
    matrix sizes while keeping its semantics unchanged.
  - DEFAULT1 amends D-INTDIV1, D-EXPSEM1, D-EXPNEG1 and D-NUMTYPE1 by name.
  - PLANE1 extends the marker registration law to dimensions, measures, exactness
    and classifications.
  - EXACT1 enters as a written law: knowledge grows silently, is lost only at a
    spelled step, and erases at runtime.
  - IMAG1 makes the i suffix an imaginary literal on the shipped unit-literal path.
  - UNCERT1 adds the measured grade with first-order propagation and states in the
    docs that correlated errors are out of scope.
  - FOUND1 states the foundation: a type is a carrier plus knowledge, and all
    knowledge erases before the typed IR.

Step 2 — Tombstone the retired forms in the same edit: BigInt, the #Invariant
marker, and the two hidden duration suffix tables. Each tombstone names its
replacement.

Step 3 — Update crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, the owner-controlled surface
file. Three ratified changes touch a user-typable name: the imaginary literal
suffix i (IMAG1), the inline range form in type position (SPELL1), and the
deletion of the #Invariant marker constant (REFINE1). Follow the file's rule and
give each entry its decision-ID comment.

Step 4 — Regenerate the devtools grammars so the tree-sitter and highlight files
match Syntax.rs after the marker deletion and the new literal suffix.

Step 5 — Re-bless the snapshots the surface change touches.

Step 6 — Confirm one implementation card exists per ratified decision, and link
all eleven from this card's refs.

Do not build here. No checker work, no number-tower work, no unit-plane work, no
reflection work. All of that lives on the implementation cards. Do not close this
card until the eleven cards exist and the spec, Syntax.rs, grammars and snapshots
are done.

cards.title: Phantom fact names are refused at the signature with a fix-it
cards.body: core_type_known (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs:154-157) returns true for any rule_arg_declaration name, so fn f(x: Capability) compiles to a dead end: E0112 at every call, no constructor exists. Same for PolicySetting, TaintKind, ObligationMode, State, InlineMode. Before D-RULEARG-TYPES1 shipped these were honest E0119. Marker-argument enums must be known only in marker-argument position. D-FACT-HOME1=A makes this the ratified shape: a phantom fact-menu name is refused at the signature, and the diagnostic names the real path rather than a bare unknown-type error. The census is about eighteen names, not seven.
cards.plan:
Remove the `crate::Policy::rule_arg_declaration(name).is_some()` early-return from `core_type_known` (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs:154-157). This function backs `check_declared_type_rules` (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/type_assign.rs:169), which validates every user-written type annotation (fn params, struct fields, let types) — a general position these marker-argument enums were never meant to reach. Confirmed by repro: `fn f(x: Capability) {}` compiles today, but `Capability.FS.read` used as an ordinary expression fails E0107 'nothing named `Capability` exists here' — the type is nameable but never constructible outside marker position, an unconstructable dead end.

Marker-argument position does not depend on `core_type_known` at all: `CheckerMarkers.rs`'s `validate_rule_arguments` (~line 90) calls `crate::Policy::rule_arg_declaration` directly to validate `#Grant(...)`/`#Caps(...)`-style payloads, bypassing `check_declared_type_rules` entirely. So removing the blanket accept does not touch marker-argument parsing/validation.

After the removal, `fn f(x: Capability)` falls through type_assign.rs's existing chain (type-param scope, trait names, type-alias, registry.contains, imported-module registries) to the pre-existing fallback at type_assign.rs:225-237: E0119 'there's no type called `Capability`'. No new diagnostic code needed — E0119 is already registered (docs/spec/diagnostics.md:202) and already fires this way; add a UI snapshot fixture exercising this specific case.

Swept examples/ and tests/ for any current general-position use of the seven rule-arg names (Capability, Target, PolicySetting, TaintKind, ObligationMode, State, InlineMode) as a `: Name` annotation — none found. The one incidental hit, tests/ui_lint/subjectless_guard_field_enum_dispatch.jet's `state: State`, is a locally user-declared `enum State`, unaffected: `self.registry.contains("State")` (type_assign.rs:201) already resolves it once the blanket core_type_known accept for the core-registry name is gone — this also quietly fixes a latent shadowing bug where the core reflection name currently wins over a same-named user type even outside marker position.

cards.title: Concurrency: work is a value — first-principles proposal + ballot slate
cards.body: Proposal at docs/proposals/concurrency-work-is-a-value.md. A unit of concurrent work is an ordinary value carrying three facts the compiler already tracks: state, duty, and reach. Ten D-CONC-* ballots are ratified, every one option A. Two ballots the final proposal depends on, D-CONC-SPAWN1 for spawning and fan-out and D-CONC-FAIL1 for task failure, were never raised on the board, while the two they replaced, GROUP1 and OUTCOME1, were ratified. The spawn surface and the failure rail are therefore still undecided. What is left here is that gate plus the record work.
cards.plan:
## State

Thirteen D-CONC-* decisions are ratified: UNIT1, JOIN1, GROUP1, OUTCOME1, CROSS1, STM1, SCHED1, STREAM1, CHAN1, SHARE1, SPAWN1 (D), FAIL1 (A), CHAN2 (D). Every gate is closed. All work below may start now.

## Record work

1. Record every ratified D-CONC-* outcome in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md. One entry per decision, naming the option, the surface, and the decision IDs it amends (the amendment map is in each ballot).
2. SPAWN1=D: the spawn surface is the task keyword family - task f(), task.all { }, task.race { }, task.any { }, task.group g(limit: n). Only task is reserved.
3. FAIL1=A: join() returns T ? TaskFailure. TaskFailure is a normal enum (.Cancelled, .DeadlineBlown, .Panicked). trace(), exception(), TaskOutcome, and TaskStatus are deleted.
4. CHAN2=D: no new keyword. The readiness wait is a subjectless if table whose arm heads are binding, source pairs; an after arm takes a Time delta; an optional else arm makes the wait non-blocking; the whole table is one atomic wait; mixing readiness heads and Bool heads in one table is a registered diagnostic. select stays a free identifier everywhere. This amends the subjectless table law (D-IFGUARD1); record that amendment.
5. Correct the stale S53 tombstone: concurrency is live law, not deferred past v1.0. Point it at the recorded entries.

## Surface work

6. crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs: register the task keyword family (SPAWN1=D) with decision-ID comments; register builtin channel<T>() and the drain loop source form (CHAN1/CHAN2); delete the select builder chain, the .read arm, the dead Channel entry, the shared closure forms (SHARE1), and the trace()/exception() surface (FAIL1). select is not reserved.
7. Regenerate devtools grammars. Re-bless touched snapshots. Formatter round-trip for any changed form.

## Card work

8. Map all thirteen ratified decisions to implementation cards. Known impl cards are #1557-#1565; mint homed, criteria-carrying cards for any decision without one (SPAWN1, FAIL1, CHAN2 are the likely gaps). Link the map from this card and log it.

## Proof

rg shows one syntax-decisions.md entry per ratified D-CONC-* ID and no deferred-concurrency S53 text. Grammars regenerated, snapshots re-blessed, one targeted fmt stability run. This card ships records and surface registration only; runtime work lives on the impl cards.

questions.text:
What about all task keywords but nested so you have task, task.group, task.race, task.all, task.any

Any issue with this?
questions.answer: No blocking issue — nesting is strictly better. Bare all, race, any, and group would reserve four common identifier names; nested, only task is reserved, and typing task. autocompletes the whole concurrency surface. The parser gains one head form instead of four. The only cost is a short task. prefix at each fan-out site. The ballot now carries this as option D, and the recommendation moved to D. All ratified laws (scope-end joins, fail-fast, cancel-losers, first-Ok) carry over unchanged.

questions.text: I want to use if but have a nicer native  syntax like option a’s select.
questions.answer: Done: the ballot now has option D, and it is the recommendation. The wait is a subjectless if table with option A's exact arms: if { job, jobs -> handle(job)  msg, control -> obey(msg)  after 100ms -> retry() }. No new keyword and no S68 amendment. A comma head can never be a Bool expression, so the parser knows the table waits, and the whole table compiles to one atomic wait. select stays a free name everywhere.
