cards.title: Two tier ledgers disagree: jit_gaps marks comptime/embed and comptime/find covered, parity audit shows them failing at run
cards.body: tests/jet_gaps.txt lists comptime/embed and comptime/find as covered, and the tier-parity audit records both failing at the default run tier with E0956. jit_gaps tracks compile coverage, not run coverage, and nothing cross-checks the two ledgers, so a real I9 parity failure is invisible to CI. Found during the metaprogramming first-principles audit.
cards.plan:
Root cause: neither ledger is lying on its own terms; the word `covered` is. tests/jet_gaps.txt says at the top that covered means `TIR lowered and Cranelift compiled end-to-end`, which is compile coverage. The tier-parity audit measures run coverage. Nothing cross-checks the two, so comptime/embed, comptime/embed_bytes, comptime/find and comptime/find_empty sit in jit_gaps.txt `covered:` and in tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt `frontend_rejected:` at the same time, while passing under `jet run --release`. Under I9 that is a real parity failure that is invisible to CI.

What D-META-EFFECT1 and D-META-ONE1 change about the word: today `can this run at compile time` is membership in a closed Rust allow-list, which is what raises E0956. D-META-EFFECT1=A retires that allow-list and makes the effect set the answer, and it merges the two purity checkers. So `covered` must be keyed on tier and effect, not on a table, and E0956's compile-time wording must never surface from the run tier. That is why the four comptime rows are owed to the D-META-EFFECT1 card and not fixed here.

Build:
1. In tests/jet_gaps.txt and in tests/dev.rs (jit_coverage_audit_inner, the JET_DUMP_JIT_GAPS writer, and parse_jit_gap_manifest), rename the `covered:` section to `compile_covered:` and update the header lines to say plainly that this file tracks compile coverage only. One word, and both ledgers stop claiming run coverage.
2. Add one cross-check to the same test: a stem in `compile_covered:` may not appear in tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt under `frontend_rejected:`, nor under `deopt_interp:` carrying an error diagnostic, unless the stem is listed in a new `run_gaps:` section. The failure message quotes both ledger lines and the stem.
3. Add the `run_gaps:` section to tests/jet_gaps.txt with the same shrink-only ratchet semantics the file already uses (D-LENS-RUN2), seeded with exactly the E0956 rows recorded in docs/audits/jit-run-tier-vs-aot-parity-audit-2026-07-28.md, each with its audit line as the reason. Growth fails CI.
4. Comment the four comptime rows with the card that owes them: the D-META-EFFECT1 implementation card. Do not change the examples, the interpreter, or E0956 here.

Proof: one targeted check that a stem present in both ledgers fails the gate; `cargo test --test dev jit_coverage_audit` green; the four comptime rows visible in `run_gaps:` with the audit cited.

Do not build: no new gate binary and no second manifest (I8), no per-example allow-list beyond the one shrink-only section, no silent removal of the four rows.

log.text: Follow-up from review: the three inert run_gaps rows (collections/dynamic-array-view, io/db, io/args_audit — stems not in compile_covered, so the cross-check can never reach them) are dropped and the ceiling is lowered from 15 to 12. Proof: ledger_cross_check 2/2 and both jit audit tests green in one run on master.

[handoff] All five criteria met. Branch bd3/ledger, head d3c9fa1ce, worktree .claude/worktrees/ledger, cut fresh from master 7b127acab. Not merged; ready for review and integration. Two files changed: tests/dev.rs and tests/jit_gaps.txt.

WHAT LANDED
The word covered was the bug. jit_gaps.txt measures compile coverage, the corpus gate measures run coverage, and nothing compared them, so four comptime stems sat in both covered: and the gate's frontend_rejected: at once. The section is now compile_covered: with a header that says what the file measures and names the gate as the other ledger. ledger_cross_check_holds fails when a compile_covered stem is one the gate records as failing at the run tier, quoting both ledger lines, unless run_gaps: names it. run_gaps: holds the fifteen E0956 rows from the 2026-07-28 parity audit with their reasons, shrink-only behind a ceiling of 15. The four comptime rows name card #1543 (D-META-EFFECT1) as the owner of their fix.

The cross-check reads manifest against manifest, so it compiles and runs nothing. It reuses the existing parse_corpus_gate_manifest; no second reader and no new gate binary (I8).

TESTS
- cargo test --test dev ledger_cross_check: 2 of 2 pass.
- Negative control end to end: deleting the comptime/embed row from run_gaps: turned ledger_cross_check_holds red with the full quoted pair; restoring it turned it green.
- cargo test --test dev example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate: the manifest still parses and classifies; its only two failures are concurrency/shield_commit and io/terminal_parity, unrelated and pre-existing (the same two failed on master during card #1527).
- cargo test --test dev --no-run: clean.

PRE-EXISTING RED FOUND, NOT THIS CARD
- jit_coverage_audit fails on master today: the measured compile-covered set has moved to 401 stems while the file records 399 (8 stems left, 10 arrived, among them collections/iter_adapters, effects/taint, io/args_audit leaving and errors/u8_divide_zero, net/dns_lookup, types/anonymous_unions arriving). cards.body:
Six comptime decisions exist only as prose in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md and have no Tower record: D-CTCORE1, D-CTEFFECT1, D-CTIO1, D-CTFIND1, D-CTCODEGEN1, D-METADEPTH1. Five ratified D-META decisions now amend them by name, and lint cannot link an amendment to a record that does not exist. Record-keeping only.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Ballot D-ONCE-LEDGER1 (card #1656) decides the one home for ratified decisions — Tower with the spec rendered, or the spec with Tower rows linking to spans. Record these six decisions so the outcome holds either way: the record must cite its spec source line, and it must carry the supersession or amendment link, which is mandatory under every option. Do not extend this to a bulk import of the other spec-only IDs before the ballot answers.
cards.plan:
Checked against the ratified D-META slate. The card is not overtaken; it gets smaller and more urgent, because five ratified decisions now amend records that do not exist.

What the slate did to each of the six:
- D-CTCORE1: the curated allow-list of pure Core calls is retired by D-META-EFFECT1=A, which makes the effect set carry the fact. Record it as ratified, then record the amendment.
- D-CTEFFECT1: survives unchanged. D-META-EFFECT1 states the three tiers keep their meaning; only the vocabulary merges. Record as ratified, no amendment.
- D-CTIO1: the embed_file and embed_bytes escapes and the no-escaping-the-project-root rule survive. Only the allow-list clause it shares with D-CTCORE1 moves. Record as ratified with that note.
- D-CTFIND1: untouched by the slate. Record as ratified.
- D-CTCODEGEN1: amended by D-META-CODE1=A. A derive body is now an item template parsed at definition time, not emitted text, and the ratified law that no pre-parsed AST is ever injected explicitly still holds. Record both halves.
- D-METADEPTH1: the ceiling rises. D-META-USER1=A lets a user rule add code and D-META-DSL1=A lets a library declare a checked text block. The laws that survive are no mutation, no shadowing of what the user wrote, and no library changing the grammar. Record as ratified with the raised ceiling named.

Build: mint six Tower decision records, status ratified, each carrying the outcome quoted from docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md with its source line cited (the comptime block near lines 2021-2050 and the derive line near 2068), then add the amendment cross-links so `tower lint` can resolve every D-META amendment reference.

Do not build: no re-ballot and no reopening. These are records of law the owner already ratified. No spec text changes; the spec is the source being cited.

cards.title: Ship the standard dimension set: Mass and the SI base dimensions
cards.body:
Correction to the original premise (verified live against the current tree, 2026-08-06): the claim "Jet ships five dimensions: Length, Time, Speed, Area, Temperature. There is no Mass" is stale. All seven SI base dimensions (Length, Mass, Time, Current, Temperature, AmountOfSubstance, LuminousIntensity) plus a large set of derived dimensions (Area, Volume, Speed, Acceleration, Force, Pressure, Energy, Power, Charge, ElectricPotential, Capacitance, Resistance, Conductance, MagneticFlux, MagneticFluxDensity, Inductance, LuminousFlux, Illuminance, Radioactivity, AbsorbedDose, EquivalentDose, CatalyticActivity) already exist in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Units.jet (928 lines, commit cada551c "feat: open dimension algebra", 2026-07-29) and are already wired into every module by crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle.rs::inject_units_prelude, which injects any standard #UnitFamily whose name or unit member is textually mentioned in the module, plus its dimension dependencies transitively.

Live proof (this audit, against target/debug/jet built 2026-08-06):
  fn run() { m :: 2kilogram; a :: 3meter_per_second_squared; f :: m * a; print(f) }
  => "6 meter*kilogram/second^2"   (correct force, computed from Mass with zero new code)
  p :: f / 1square_meter; print(p)
  => "6 kilogram/meter*second^2"   (correct pressure, computed from Mass with zero new code)

So the seven SI base dimensions, Mass included, are already standard, already in the Prelude, and already produce correct force/pressure values through ordinary * and / on unit-literal values -- this card's criterion 1 is already met by existing code. Rides D-TYPE2-MEASURE1=A, which ratified one measure substrate for exactly this kind of compile-time-number-in-type work and explicitly called out that the coming matrix surface (#1437) would otherwise have added a fifth encoding.

What is genuinely missing (found live, same probe session): named derived-unit values do not print and do not compose across dimensions. Force.{ m * a } fails print with "E0112: print doesn't know how to show Force" (no Display on the #UnitFamily-minted named struct), and dividing a named Force by a named Area fails with "E0109: / can't compare or combine Force and SquareMeter" (no cross-family operator on named types; only the bare/generic composite-dimension route above works). This card's real remaining scope is proof (an example) plus, if the owner wants the named-type ergonomics rather than the already-working generic route, closing those two gaps.
cards.plan:
Scope: D-TYPE2-MEASURE1=A (ratified). Mass and the full SI base set already ship in the Prelude (see corrected body above) -- this plan is proof-first, not addition-first.
1. Minimal path to close both criteria as written (no engine changes needed): add examples/features/types/dimensional_quantities_mass.jet computing a force (mass * acceleration) and a pressure (force / area) using the already-working generic/anonymous composite-dimension route demonstrated live in this audit (2kilogram * 3meter_per_second_squared, then dividing by an area value) -- mirror the style of the existing examples/features/types/dimensional_quantities.jet (Length/Time/Speed/Area). Add golden output in examples/features/expected/types/dimensional_quantities_mass.out. Prove under jet build (AOT) and jet run (JIT); exercise interpreter path if reachable via deopt (I9).
2. Optional/follow-on, only if the owner wants named-type ergonomics (Force.{...}, Pressure.{...}) rather than the generic route: (a) give #UnitFamily-minted named structs the same auto-derived Printable that ordinary structs get under D-META-AUTO1 (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Units.jet + wherever unit-family members expand to structs -- check crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/distinct_units_structs.rs and crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/ for the expansion site); (b) wire cross-family operators (Force / Area -> Pressure) on named types through the same dimension-composition resolution that already works for the bare/generic route in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema (look for the composite-dimension unifier the working probe above already exercises). Do not scope this into criterion 2's golden proof unless the owner asks for the named-type spelling specifically -- the generic route already satisfies the literal wording of both criteria.
3. Update this card's body (see newBody) so a future reader does not re-attempt "add Mass to the Prelude" -- that work already shipped in commit cada551c.
4. docs/reference/core-library.md or docs/spec/spec.md: if the dimension catalog isn't already documented as complete (seven base + derived), add a short reference note; check first, this may already be covered by the existing Units.jet doc comments.
Proof:
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- dimensional_quantities_mass
- scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/types/dimensional_quantities_mass.jet (I9 parity)
Owned paths: examples/features/types/dimensional_quantities_mass.jet, examples/features/expected/types/dimensional_quantities_mass.out, and (only for the optional step 2) crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Units.jet, crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/distinct_units_structs.rs.

cards.title: fmt simplify mode: AST-driven simplest-spelling rewriter
cards.body: Goal: a jet fmt mode that rewrites code to the simplest canonical spelling that expresses the same program - the formatter reads the AST and emits the most concise ratified surface form (drop redundant parens, braced return bodies to = expr, verbose literals to shorthand). Card #1512 is the first concrete slice. The rewrite catalog, the flag surface, and whether any rewrite becomes default fmt behavior are owner decisions raised at plan time.
cards.plan:
## Gate

Ballot D-FMT-SIMPLIFY1 on this card picks the catalog, the surface, and the default. No implementation before it is ratified. Card #1512 is the first concrete slice and lands under whatever surface the owner picks.

## Starter catalog (each cites its law; all proven by AST equality: emit, re-parse, compare)

- R1 — braced single-return body becomes a one-liner (card #1512).
  Before: `fn mirror(p: Point) => Point { return .{x: -p.x, y: p.y} }`
  After:  `fn mirror(p: Point) => Point = .{x: -p.x, y: p.y}`
- R2 — else-if chain becomes one ordered arm table (S68, D-BRANCH-PREF1, the shape L0507 teaches).
  Before: `if code == 200 { ok() } else if code == 301 { redirect() } else { log(code) }`
  After:  `if code == { 200 -> ok()  301 -> redirect()  else -> log(code) }`
- R3 — struct literal drops a type name the context already knows (dot-construction law).
  Before: `p :: Point.{x: 1, y: 2}` where the binding or parameter already fixes Point... only when the context types it.
  After:  `p: Point :: .{x: 1, y: 2}` / argument position `draw(.{x: 1, y: 2})`
- R4 — listed run of integers in an expression fence becomes a range (D-FENCE-RANGE1=A, card #1516; gated on #1516 shipping).
  Before: `$[0, 1, 2, 3]$`   After: `$[0..3]$`

## After ratification

1. Implement per the chosen surface. Reuse the fmt engine and emitters. One catalog module, one rewrite per entry, each tagged with its decision ID.
2. Every rewrite gets the AST-equality check and a fmt stability test case.
3. Run the chosen mode over the in-repo corpus once and re-bless goldens/snapshots in the same change if the owner picked a batch surface.
4. Targeted proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test fmt` once at the end.

log.text: Criterion 5: corpus simplify check is green. R2/R3 remain disabled (AST identity). Card still building until orchestrator close; R2/R3 are not remaining open criteria.

Criterion 5 corpus pass: `jet fmt --simplify examples` rewrote 157 teaching files; a second `jet fmt --simplify --check examples` exits 0. cards.title: Map type spacing: [K:V] or [K: V]
cards.body: Update Map syntax to be [K:V] rather than [K: V]
cards.plan:
Scope: type-position map colon only. `[K:V]` (no space). Value-position map literal entries (`["ana": 31]`) and record fields (`.{x: 1}`, `age: Int`) keep their space -- unchanged.

Parser: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Types.rs:435-446 -- map-type parsing checks TokKind::Colon and the lexer discards inter-token whitespace generically, so both `[K:V]` and `[K: V]` already parse today. No parser change needed.

Formatter: crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Expressions.rs:348-354, the Type::Map branch -- change `self.write(": ")` to `self.write(":")`. Also check crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs:651 and :745 (Display-style `"[{}: {}]"` helpers used for type-name strings in diagnostic/error text) and update those to `"[{}:{}]"` too, for I4 consistency between formatter output and diagnostic type-name rendering -- confirm both are type-position only (not literal-position) before touching them.

Syntax.rs: the map-type decision lives in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/math_layout.rs:139-143 (TYPE_MAP comment references D-LISTMAP-CANON1=A and spells `[K: V]` in the comment; no literal string constant exists to edit). Update the comment to `[K:V]` and add 'amended by D-MAPSPACE1=A (2026-08-06)'.

syntax-decisions.md: two spots reference the canonical map-type spelling -- :906-907 (D-TYPE-ALIAS-CANON1 + D-LISTMAP-CANON1=A summary line) and :952-954 (S64, 'Map shorthand & entry iteration', the primary decision text). Update both to `[K:V]`; append a new dated log entry recording D-MAPSPACE1=A amending D-LISTMAP-CANON1/S64.

Migration (greenfield, one change): after the formatter lands, run the repo's fmt-write path over every in-repo .jet file so type-position map colons collapse to `[K:V]`. This does NOT touch docs/**/*.md (formatter doesn't reformat markdown) or value-position literals -- hand-fix those. Migration surface (ballpark rg, needs manual triage to exclude value-position `["key": value]` and field-declaration false positives): ~33 occurrences across ~20 .jet files (examples/features/collections/{wordcount,map_merge,map_surface,map_key}.jet, examples/features/basics/{loop_values,loop_forms}.jet, docs/reference/syntax-surface.jet, tests/ui/bad_map_key.jet, tests/fixtures/jetpack-project/functional-env.jet, others) and ~43 occurrences across docs/**/*.md.

Grammar: editors/tree-sitter/grammar.js:564-566 `map_type: ($) => seq("[", $._type, ":", $._type, "]")` is whitespace-agnostic already -- only its comment (`[K: V]` -> `[K:V]`) needs updating, mirrored in editors/zed/grammar-repo/grammar.js and editors/zed/grammars/jet/grammar.js. Tests: fmt stability home is tests/fmt.rs -- existing map-type fixtures at :556 (`typed_lookup :: [String: Int].{`) and :822/830 (`counts: [String: Int]`) need their expected output updated to `[String:Int]`; extend/add a case asserting the formatter emits no space and output is idempotent on a second pass.

cards.title: Expression fences: expand integer-literal ranges $[0..3]$
cards.body: Allow following syntax change: ```    print(pick_str($[0, 1, 2, 3]$))``` to ```    print(pick_str($[0..3]$))```
cards.plan:
CORRECTION to this card's prep brief: D-FENCE-RANGE1's ratified option-A technical text says 'Expansion applies only when both endpoints are integer literals and the range ascends... Any other range entry is a normal expression entry.' No diagnostic is specified for descending or non-literal ranges -- they silently stay a single Range-value entry, matching how the existing Ident..Ident range branch already behaves for expression fences today (parse_entries, FencedNames.rs:300-327: `Err(diagnostic) if binding_fence => return Err(diagnostic), Err(_) => {}` -- for expression fences, a malformed range silently falls through to a normal entry, no error). The brief's suggested criterion ('reversed/non-literal bounds report E<code> with blessed snapshot') is unratified scope -- do not add a new diagnostic under this card. If the owner wants one later, that needs its own ballot.

Parser: crates/jet-parser/src/FencedNames.rs, parse_entries() (~279-334). Add a branch alongside the existing `content.len() == 3 && matches!(content[1].kind, TokKind::DotDot)` check (line 300): also match TokKind::DotDotLt (the `..<` token), and check `(TokKind::Int(lo, _), TokKind::Int(hi, _))` endpoints instead of Ident. Gate on `!binding_fence` (binding fences already reject non-Ident entries via the 'needs plain names' check at ~372-381, so this is belt-and-suspenders, not load-bearing). Accept DotDot with lo<=hi, or DotDotLt with lo<hi. On success: emit one `Token { kind: TokKind::Int(n, n.to_string()), span }` entry per step -- NOT TokKind::Ident; these are expression entries substituted into pick_str(...)-style calls, unlike the existing name-range branch which produces identifiers for bindings. Also set `FencedNames.range = Some((lo.to_string(), hi.to_string()))` so the formatter's EXISTING range-collapse path (see below) reconstructs `$[lo..hi]$` automatically -- no formatter code change needed. On any non-qualifying shape (descending, non-literal endpoints, or anything else): fall through unchanged to the existing generic per-entry path below it (no diagnostic -- matches the existing Ident-range fallthrough).

Formatter -- confirmed no code change needed. crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Statements.rs, fmt_fenced_names() (:74-122): when `fence.range` is Some, it already re-emits `$[ start..end ]$` (lines 75-83) -- reused automatically once the parser sets `range` for the new int case. When `fence.range` is None (the general entry-list case, e.g. `$[0, 1, 2, 3]$` spelled out by hand, or a parenthesized `$[ (0..3) ]$` escape), it already falls back to each entry's ORIGINAL SOURCE SLICE (lines 88-97, `self.src.get(span.start..span.end)`) -- this is what already preserves entry-level parentheses verbatim; the ratified 'formatter keeps entry-level parentheses' obligation is satisfied by existing code, not new code. Do NOT add auto-collapsing of a hand-spelled `0, 1, 2, 3` list into `0..3` -- that's a different, unratified formatter feature; only literal `..`/`..<` source gets expanded/collapsed.

Syntax.rs: crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs:96-98, the SIGIL_FENCE_OPEN/CLOSE doc comment currently cites 'D-EACH1=C / D-VERDICT-1320-1'. Append: 'D-FENCE-RANGE1=A: an ascending integer-literal range in an expression-fence entry expands one entry per number; parenthesize to keep a Range value.'

syntax-decisions.md: docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:5477-5488 holds the current D-VERDICT-1320-1 fence entry. Append a new dated entry '2026-08-06 -- D-FENCE-RANGE1=A (amends D-VERDICT-1320-1)' recording the ascending-integer-literal-range expansion rule (`lo..hi` with lo<=hi, `lo..<hi` with lo<hi; any other range entry stays a normal expression entry) and the parenthesized escape.

Grammar: fence content is a generic bracketed entry list at the grammar level -- expansion is a parser-side token rewrite, not a grammar-level distinction. Confirm with `rg fence editors/tree-sitter/grammar.js` before assuming no-op, then run the regen commands per criterion #3: `nix develop -c cargo run --bin jet -- devtools grammars` then `nix develop -c cargo test --test grammar`.

I9 parity -- trivially satisfied and needs zero per-tier work: fence expansion runs once, pre-parse, in FencedNames.rs (invoked from crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/mod.rs:43 and :83, before sema/TIR/any codegen). AOT, resident JIT, interpreter, and web all consume the identical already-expanded token stream/AST.

Golden test (the concrete I9 proof): tests/fenced_names.rs already has `fenced_names_match_on_aot_jit_and_interpreter` (build_and_run for AOT + resident JIT + forced-interpreter dev_iteration, asserting identical stdout across all three). Add a sibling test/const there, e.g. `SOURCE = "fn run() { print($[0..3]$) }"`, `expected = "0\n1\n2\n3\n"`, reusing the same tri-tier harness -- this is the direct proof for criterion #5 below.

Example: examples/features/basics/fenced_names.jet is the general (non-web-locked) fence showcase -- add a line such as `print($[0..3]$)` and extend its golden/expected output (check tests/golden.rs coverage for this stem). The card's own worked example, examples/features/web/web_wasm_string.jet:15 `print(pick_str($[0, 1, 2, 3]$))`, is optional to touch -- it's #Target(JS)-only, golden-tested via tests/web_build.rs (web_wasm_string_export_hostile_roundtrip against examples/features/expected/web/web_wasm_string.out). If edited to `$[0..3]$`, output shouldn't change (same 4 calls); re-run that golden to confirm.

Unit tests: FencedNames.rs already has inline tests numbered_range_expands_in_binding_and_receiver_expression (:633) and expression_entries_expand_an_expression_statement (:651) -- add integer_literal_range_expands_in_expression_fence, integer_literal_range_parenthesized_stays_single_value, integer_literal_range_descending_or_non_literal_stays_single_value alongside them.

Test commands: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test fenced_names`; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-parser FencedNames`; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden` if fenced_names.jet/web_wasm_string.jet output changes; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_build web_wasm_string` if that example is edited.

log.text: Timeline audit 2026-08-10: sequenced behind #1729. This card adds range expansion inside the $[ ... ]$ expression fence. D-ONCE-AT1=D moves the prefix compile-time mark from $ to @ and its technical text names "comptime splices" as part of the mechanical respell; D-ONCE-DOLLAR1=B then gives $ a different job (environment reads in config surfaces) and states that ordinary program code does not use $. Building fence expansion first means writing $[0..3]$ and respelling it immediately. #1729 must state the fence spelling; this card then lands once, at the final glyph.

Prep: dropped the brief's unratified 'reversed/non-literal bounds -> E<code>' ask; D-FENCE-RANGE1's ratified text specifies no diagnostic for that case (falls through as a normal expression entry, matching existing Ident-range behavior). Criteria adjusted to test the actual ratified rule instead.

cards.title: One manifest parser and the ratified manifest vocabulary
cards.body: package.jet is read by two parsers today. The compile path uses the legacy flat parser at crates/jet-pkg-model/src/PackageManifest/ (wired at crates/jet-driver/src/Loader.rs:349), which knows payload:, packages:, effects: and build: and has no vocabulary for outputs:. Tooling and Canvas read the same file with the role-typed parser at crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package.rs. This card makes the role-typed parser the only one and lands the ratified field list: bare name: and version: at the top level, the identity: wrapper deleted, and deps:, outputs:, settings:, build:, policy:, members: as the block nouns.
cards.plan: Implements D-CONF-PLANE1, D-CONF-NAME1 — ratified 2026-08-06. Read each decision verbatim (tower brief on this card's parent proposal, or tower decision show) before building; the ratified outcome text is the law, this plan is the route. Every requirement is a discrete exit criterion below: meet each with targeted proof (tests, snapshots, examples with golden output), and keep I9 tier parity inside this card — AOT, default jet run (JIT), and the interpreter must agree on every surface this card ships before it closes. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/build-config-one-plane.md.

log.text: Closed: single role-typed manifest parser merged to master; outputs proof 4/4 and hello smoke green after integration. Reviewer bd2-rev3 verified all nine criteria.

Fixed both reviewer blockers on bd2/manifest (commit 15f6bec8d, worktree .claude/worktrees/manifest).

BLOCKER 1: remote.rs's #[cfg(test)] callers now build DepSource::Provider{provider:Source::Path,..}/DepSource::Version values instead of string literals. cargo test -p jetpack --lib now compiles. But fixing compile surfaced 12 further failures the broken build had hidden: MemberSelect, Provider/fetch, Provider::tests, Trust::tests fixtures all still wrote payload:-wrapped pkg.jet (pre-rewrite syntax the new strict parser rejects) and Transition::legacy_plan re-read the Package root from disk (re-parsing the untranslated legacy payload: text) instead of composing from the already-translated in-memory root_facts. Migrated every stale fixture to bare name:/version: and fixed the disk re-read. Final: 556 passed, 5 failed (script_registry needs-php/needs-ruby, Shell fish pty, Store::Broker peer-creds, Store::Tests module-boundary — all env-flaky, exact same 5 that fail on master).

BLOCKER 2: outputs_build fixture rewritten. entry: run (single segment) can never prove outputs: drives anything: entry_path and legacy_run_entry run the literally identical root-file scan for that case (confirmed by testing — renaming the fn to a non-run name just fails compile with E0101, since sema independently requires a literal fn run regardless of the manifest). Used the dotted form instead: entry: service.run, where entry.jet's use service import leads entry_path into service/module.jet, a directory module the legacy fallback structurally cannot reach (it only scans root-level files). Verified manually both tiers (jet run + jet build/AOT) resolve and produce the expected output, and that deleting outputs: fails closed (can't find the file run.jet). Added entry_resolution_requires_the_outputs_block as the negative proof. All 4 tests in tests/package_outputs.rs pass.

Non-blockers taken: (1) Blocks.rs MANIFEST_SCALAR_FIELDS now also masks members:/configs: (defaults/environments/services were already in MANIFEST_BLOCKS, contra the review note; only members/configs were genuinely missing). (4) docs/spec/architecture.md:184 and tests/workspace_crates.rs:217,273 PackageManifest -> PackageFacts.
Skipped: (2) Transition.rs:1672 nameless-pkg.jet already fails closed downstream via PackageFacts::MissingName (not silent success, just a less specific message); real fix isn't a one-liner, left for follow-up. (3) auto_derive_policy_invalid stderr saying package.jet for a pkg.jet fixture: other diagnostics in the same file hardcode package.jet in fix text the same way, may be an intentional canonical-name nudge rather than a bug; skipped rather than guess.

Verified: cargo build --workspace clean; cargo test -p jetpack --lib 556/5 (matches master shape); cargo test --test package_outputs 4/4; cargo test -p jet-pkg-model --lib unaffected by Blocks.rs change (diffed with/without the edit, same failure set as master aside from one flaky FFI test). Not merged; branch left at bd2/manifest for integration.

REVIEW non-blocking notes (do not need to hold the merge): (1) MANIFEST_SCALAR_FIELDS (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/Blocks.rs:979) omits members, configs, defaults, environments and services, so a package.jet with a co-located fn build plus e.g. members: find("./packages") still leaks unmasked manifest text into the build-entry parse — same shape as the bug 0a2a86863 fixed, left half closed. (2) crates/jetpack/src/Transition.rs:1672 render_legacy_package_root now hand-rolls a payload:/identity: reader; it is a one-way migration splice guarded by a following canonical parse, but a pkg.jet with no name now emits name: "" and fails downstream with MissingName instead of master's explicit migration error. (3) tests/ui/auto_derive_policy_invalid/stderr now tells the user to fix package.jet while the fixture file is literally pkg.jet. (4) docs/spec/architecture.md:184 and tests/workspace_crates.rs:217,273 still name PackageManifest as a live seam touch point (comments only).

REVIEW BLOCKER 2 (criterion 4) — tests/package_outputs.rs is false-green: it cannot distinguish outputs:-driven entry resolution from the pre-existing legacy_run_entry fallback. Proof: copy examples/features/packages/outputs_build/service.jet next to a package.jet holding only name:/version: (outputs: block deleted) and jet run prints the same 'outputs: demo drives the build', while jet build emits the same build/service.rs. Cause: for a single-segment entry (entry: run), PackageFacts::entry_path (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs:648-668) runs the identical algorithm as legacy_run_entry (mod.rs:633-641) — root-level files with a unique top-level fn of that name. The two asserts the test does make (no main.jet/run.jet; manifest contains outputs:) are satisfied by the fallback too. To prove the criterion the fixture must be unresolvable by legacy_run_entry: use the dotted entry: module.function form, or an entry function not named run, or two root files with fn run.

REVIEW BLOCKER 1 (criterion 1) — missed consumer of the parser swap: crates/jetpack/src/Provider/remote.rs:569,573,577. classify_canonical_dep changed from source: &str to source: &Package::DepSource (remote.rs:322-330, commit fb77a8a3c) but its three #[cfg(test)] callers still pass string literals. cargo test -p jetpack --lib fails to compile with 3x E0308 (expected &DepSource, found &'static str), hiding all 561 jetpack unit tests. On master the same command builds and runs (556 passed, 5 pre-existing failures). cargo build --workspace cannot see this because cfg(test) code is not compiled — which is exactly the evidence criterion 1 rests on.

cards.title: The build fact plane: registered facts read with @build
cards.body: Every build fact becomes a typed value on one registered plane: identity, machine, profile, settings, policy and stamps. build.os becomes the plane's first row instead of a special case in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/OSTarget.rs. Facts are read with the compile-time mark, as $build.package.version, $build.os, $build.profile and $build.settings.tls, and every read folds to a constant before codegen, so the word build stays an ordinary identifier and a user module named build keeps working. Bare scripts read fallback identity: the file name and 0.0.0.

cards.title: One contribution law for every fact, and jet explain
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571. One rule decides which written value wins. In source scopes the nearest scope wins, on the full six-rung ladder: item, block, function, module, file, package. Across contribution layers the most explicit writer wins: declaration, profile, workspace, environment, system, fleet, command line. Two writers at the same layer with different values stay a hard error naming both sources. At system and fleet layers a .Force pin outranks the command line. jet explain prints the whole chain with every writer named.

cards.title: Facts in text, actions in fn build: recorded contributions
cards.body: Manifest text is the complete index of what is configurable: every fact is declared there with its type and default. fn build performs actions and may contribute a value to an already declared fact with b.contribute(fact, value). It can never mint an undeclared fact. Every computed contribution is recorded in .jet/lock and named by jet explain, so a probed toolchain or a find() member list stays honest without a knob that exists nowhere in text.

cards.title: Generic modules spell like functions, and their members are reached through the instance
cards.body: Modules spell exactly like functions: types in angle brackets, value parameters in parens with name and type, and :: to bind the instance. module cache<K>(capacity: Int) declares, module int_cache :: cache<Int>(64) instantiates, and a module with no value parameters needs no parens. The instance's types are its members, so a user writes three_ints.Buffer the way they already write three_ints.echo, and the mangled symbol becomes an internal detail that never appears in a diagnostic.

cards.title: A build fact may be a generic-module value argument
cards.body: Settings and module value parameters share one evaluator, one fuel budget and one diagnostic family. The visible gain is that a fact becomes a legal value argument: module tuned :: cache<Int>($build.settings.cache_slots) works, each profile produces its own cached specialization, and jet explain traces the value into the instantiation. The fact-fed value may also size a fixed array, exactly as a different literal instantiation does today.

cards.title: Provenance facts: a binary names its own build
cards.body: Stamp facts join the plane so a binary can name the exact source and toolchain that built it: $build.stamp.* reads source and toolchain identity, plus $build.stamp.at, a timestamp captured once when the lock is written and replayed from the lock afterwards. Rebuilds stay reproducible because the value comes from the lock and never from the clock. The docs must say plainly that stamp.at describes the lock file's history, not the moment this binary was built.

cards.title: One meaning for the word profile: rename the other three
cards.body:
Profile keeps one meaning, the optimize bundle selected by --profile and its ratified --release sugar. The other three uses are renamed before any user meets them. TargetProfile is a machine description and moves into the machine vocabulary, selected beside triples with --target. Environment profiles: becomes presets: and --env-profile becomes --preset. Package and user profiles adopt the word generation in prose. No behaviour changes; this is a rename that must land before the surfaces that build on these words.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): For the record, not a scope change to this verify-phase card: the per-spelling teaching diagnostics landed here are one instance of a mechanism ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656) generalizes. When that ballot lands, the retired `profile` spellings should also carry the shared rewrite and the zero-count ratchet.

cards.title: One outcome carrier under T? and T ? E
cards.body: An outcome has three independent facts: a payload (a value, part of one, or none), a verdict (clean, succeeded with notes, or failed) and attached reports. T? is the view where absence is clean and T ? E is the view where the report matters, so the two surface spellings stay exactly as ratified while the thing underneath becomes one carrier. Success-with-notes and failure-with-partial-results are the same carrier's middle states, reached without a third type, and conversions between the views stop being ceremonies because there is nothing to convert.
cards.plan: Implements D-FAIL-CARRIER1, D-FAIL-MODEL1 — ratified 2026-08-06. Read each decision verbatim (tower brief on this card's parent proposal, or tower decision show) before building; the ratified outcome text is the law, this plan is the route. Every requirement is a discrete exit criterion below: meet each with targeted proof (tests, snapshots, examples with golden output), and keep I9 tier parity inside this card — AOT, default jet run (JIT), and the interpreter must agree on every surface this card ships before it closes. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/failure-one-report-three-routes.md.

log.text: Log correction: .noting() was removed in review round 1. It was an invented write spelling that duplicated the ratified ? "note" hop (D-FAIL-CTX1, card #1532). Notes are read-only on this card: they live on the outcome value, opt-in per error type like partial. Review passed after the fix. The carrier home deviation from I9's named folder is balloted as D-I9-HOME1 on card #1604.

[review-fixes] Fresh-context review raised four blocking findings on bd2/carrier; all four are fixed on commit 4e898cd4f.

B1 notes bag. jet_noting pushed into a thread-local and jet_notes drained it, so two outcomes shared one set of notes, a second read came back empty, and notes did not cross a thread. Notes now live on the outcome value, opted into per error type exactly as partial results already were: an error type carries them under the field name notes. The thread-local is deleted. .noting is deleted with it — writing a note is the ? hop D-FAIL-CTX1 ratifies, which is card #1532's; criterion 4 asks for the read, and the read is what shipped.

B2 false green. The example now holds three outcomes at once with distinct notes, reads one of them twice, and its golden output shows people, ports, then people again. The targeted test does the same and also asserts the program's actual output on the interpreter tier, so a shared bag cannot pass it.

B3 engine drift. One TIR node, CarrierFact, now carries both middle states. AOT emit spells the projection onto the report; both interpreters call one marshaller, Comptime::Builtins::carrier_fact, which hands that projection to the prelude's jet_partial or jet_notes. What a success and a failure each answer is stated once, in the prelude. The hardcoded field name in the comptime arm is gone; every path takes the name from the same Syntax constant.

B4 tautology. The erasure test imports jet::Outcome::{JetAbsent, JetOutcome} instead of declaring local copies, so it fails if either type grows a field. Source/lib.rs re-exports the module for it.

Proof after the fixes: cargo build clean. cargo test --test outcome_carrier 5 of 5. Golden 61 failures, unchanged from before the fixes, neither example among them, and the re-blessed partial_and_notes.out matches AOT and default jet run line for line. Corpus parity gate: both examples pass; its only two failures remain concurrency/shield_commit and io/terminal_parity, unrelated and pre-existing. jet fmt --check clean on all three new files. The carrier_partial_not_kept UI snapshot still matches.

[deviation] The one carrier lives in crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs, not under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/** as criterion 1 and the I9 text say. Reason: the comptime interpreter must name the same Rust type, and jet-comptime cannot depend on jet-codegen, so jet-foundation is the only crate both sides already share. The file is still prelude part one — Codegen/mod.rs includes it verbatim, ahead of every other part, for native builds, and Codegen/Web.rs includes the same file for the wasm module. It is also a real module in jet-foundation, which is what lets the compiler's own interpreters call the very same jet_partial and jet_notes the generated program calls; that is the mechanism that keeps the tiers from drifting rather than a way around I9. Flagging it for the owner: either the invariant text should say Prelude parts may live in jet-foundation when a seam crate must share them, or the carrier needs a different home.

[handoff] All ten criteria met. Branch bd2/carrier, head e580c8064, worktree .claude/worktrees/carrier. Not merged; ready for review and integration.

COMMITS THIS SESSION
- af487b194 wip: .or_err lifts a clean absence into a failure (checkpoint of the prior session's uncommitted work)
- 3d57f72da merge: master fixture repairs into bd2/carrier. Three conflicts, each master adding a feature beside a line the carrier had rewritten; every resolution keeps master's feature and states it in the carrier's vocabulary. Rebase was not cheap: master moved 178 files with 20 overlapping this branch.
- 19e0718a5 feat(carrier): the outcome's middle states are readable from Jet
- e580c8064 feat(carrier): the web tier and the priority queue join the one carrier

WHAT LANDED
- .or_err("why"), .partial(), .noting("...") and .notes(). Semantics live only in crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs, which is prelude part one. AOT emit, the TIR interpreter and the comptime interpreter marshal onto them, and both interpreters call the very same jet_noting and jet_notes symbols.
- A failure keeps part of its work by carrying it on its report under the field name partial, at the same type the outcome carries. That is the ratified opt-in-per-error-type shape. An error type that declined gets the ordinary E0302.
- The web tier stopped spelling T? as Rust's own Option. Its wasm module now includes the same Outcome.rs file the native prelude puts first.
- PriorityQueue.remove arrived from master answering a plain Option; it now answers the carrier.

TESTS
- cargo test --test outcome_carrier: 5 of 5 pass, including the two new middle-state and web-tier proofs.
- cargo test --test golden: 61 failures, down from the 63 the branch inherited. Neither new example is among them and no example was edited to pass.
- cargo test --test dev example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate: both examples pass in the deopt_interp AOT-oracle class, so pure interpreter, default tiered run and AOT agree on each. The gate's only two failures, concurrency/shield_commit and io/terminal_parity, are unrelated and pre-existing.
- cargo test --test grammar: 18 of 18 pass. jet fmt --check clean on all three new files. cargo build clean throughout.

KNOWN UNRELATED RED, NOT THIS CARD
- tests/fmt.rs fmt_is_lossless_on_supported_source_corpus fails on examples/features/packages/outputs_build/package.jet, which the fmt corpus cannot parse. That file arrived with master's manifest work (card #1517).
- 28 ui_snapshots mismatches are master's diagnostic-text drift. A scan of the full run shows none mentions the carrier, or_err, partial or notes, so blessing them here would accept another card's change.
- 20 web test failures in web_build, web_partition and web_tir_contract. Measured with and without this card's web change: the failure sets are identical, so they are pre-existing fixture drift.

NOTE FOR LATER CARDS
The web tier's TIR support does not lower an optional inside a wasm function at all today (E-WEB-TIR-UNSUPPORTED). That is a pre-existing web gap, not one this card opened. The carrier is in place for when web lowers one.

[handoff] Branch bd2/carrier, head 78ebd8810, worktree .claude/worktrees/carrier. Build green; tests/outcome_carrier.rs passes (2/2); golden is back at the base 63-failure line with no new failure and no example edited.

DONE this session
- The carrier moved to crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs and is still the first PRELUDE_PART, so AOT, the Cranelift hosts and the comptime interpreter all name one Rust type. jet-comptime does not depend on jet-codegen, so jet-foundation is the only shared home. Every module that include!s a prelude file now imports it.
- Converted the prelude surfaces that still answered a plain Option: byte buffers, paths, parsed CLI arguments and typed entry decoding, regex matches, URL and MIME parts, weak shared handles, loadable values, local cells, HTTP request and response headers, random picks, DKIM configuration, encoding stream readers, left joins, plot reference lines, IO report resource/os code/cause, process terminal sessions, encoding limits, and the line/column/row/cause of encoding, XML and data reports.
- Host adapters in jet-jit and jet-comptime convert at their own boundary; they re-encode no meaning.

REMAINING
- c1: the comptime interpreter still has four constructors, CtValue::Some / None / ResOk / ResErr, which is the second representation the decision retires. About 890 call sites across jet-comptime, jet-codegen TIR eval, jet-jit ambient and Source/Compiler.rs. The shape to land: Present(payload) plus Failed(report), with a clean report for the optional view.
- c4: a failure that carries a partial payload and an outcome that carries notes, both readable from Jet, with a golden example under examples/features/errors/. No surface exists yet.
- c5: .or_err("why"). The carrier already has the method in Rust; Jet has no spelling for it. Needs sema method inference, TIR lowering, AOT emit, the Cranelift path and interpreter ambient.
- c6: parity ledger entry for the c4/c5 examples.
- c7 to c10: Syntax.rs entries, the syntax-decisions.md log, regenerated grammars and re-blessed snapshots, all owed by c4 and c5.
- tests/corelib.rs: 134 pass, 52 fail. The remaining failures are DB JetMap/BTreeMap and a &String mismatch, neither of which involves the carrier; io/db was already failing at the base. The corelib base count was not measured, so the next owner should measure it before reading those 52 as clean.

cards.title: Contracts run on every tier and erase under proof
cards.body:
Contracts get a real node in TIR and the check itself lives in the Prelude, so AOT, the JIT and the interpreter all run the same one instead of two tiers silently skipping them. A #Pre breach points at the call site because the caller broke the promise; a #Post or require breach points at the body because the callee broke its own. When a range fact already proves the condition, for example an argument typed Int(1..), no runtime check is emitted at all.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Putting the contract check in the Prelude with engines marshalling only is right under every option and is the substance here. The strength of the interpreter-tier requirement in the criteria is what ballot D-ONCE-TIER1 (card #1656) settles; the AOT and default-run parity requirement holds either way.

The .context method is deleted, along with the __Fallible__ lowering sentinel it used.

cards.title: Unit-fallible signatures lose the unit
cards.body: A function that returns nothing but can fail writes its ? clause straight after the parameters: fn save(path: String) ? IOError reads as save, can fail with IOError. Bare fn sync() ? means the default error. The arrow introduces a returned value, so where there is no value there is nothing to arrow. Value-returning signatures keep the arrow exactly as today. The old => () ? form is deleted, not aliased.

cards.title: The fallback can see the error: ambient err
cards.body: Inside a fallback expression, err simply names the failure. No lambda, no binder, no parentheses, so the upgrade from swallowing a failure to handling it costs one word. The name is in scope only inside the fallback, the way result is in scope only inside #Post. On an optional's fallback there is no failure to name, so writing err there is a compile error.

cards.title: The compile-time mark is $ and it is written at every mention
cards.body: Compile time is spelled four ways today. This card makes $ the one mark, and the mark belongs to the name, so it is written at every mention: $limit :: 1000 then print("{$limit}"). #Known, #Known if and the #Known block retire in favour of $name, $if and a bare $ block, and #Known leaves the marker plane because a stage is not a rule about a target. The rule for carrying a value out of a compile-time block disappears, because the name is the same name inside and outside, so D-CTMARKER1 retires outright.
cards.plan: Implements D-META-STAGE1 — ratified 2026-08-06. Read each decision verbatim (tower brief on this card's parent proposal, or tower decision show) before building; the ratified outcome text is the law, this plan is the route. Every requirement is a discrete exit criterion below: meet each with targeted proof (tests, snapshots, examples with golden output), and keep I9 tier parity inside this card — AOT, default jet run (JIT), and the interpreter must agree on every surface this card ships before it closes. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/metaprogramming-one-compile-time-program.md.

[handoff-correction] The previous note in this log was mangled by shell expansion; this replaces it. c1+c6 still open. Head stays d22b848d1. I reverted my working tree rather than commit an unproven change, per instruction. Both halves plus the key check are done and measured, and the failure moved twice. The chain below rules out three hypotheses and leaves one concrete blocker.

KEY CHECK, answered: the comptime scope keys the mark. A binding takes its name from expect_ident, which consumes the merged token, so ct_scopes holds the marked name; Expr::ComptimeName carries the marked name too (jet-parser Parser/Expressions/primary.rs, the is_comptime_name arm). No key mismatch anywhere. The userct_ mangling is codegen-only and never reaches the scope map.

HALF 1 IS NOT NEEDED, and this corrects the recipe. jet-comptime has no expression evaluator of its own to add a read arm to. Comptime::Interpreter::eval at crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Interpreter.rs:461 merges scope into globals, builds a TirBridge ExprEvalRequest, delegates to TirBridge::eval_expr, then copies the mutated map back into scope. The only Expr matches left in jet-comptime are Purity's no-op, the write_back I already fixed in d22b848d1, and two integer-width helpers. There is exactly one evaluator, the TIR one, so the whole fix lives there.

HALF 2 AS PRESCRIBED, and why the fold survived without a read arm. In crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs the arm matching ComptimeName with a stamped value lowers to CtLit, and it sits BEFORE the is_eval_fragment arm, so it shadowed it. Inside a fold fragment a marked mention lowered to a baked value and never a place, which is exactly why write-back had nothing to reach. Reordering so the fragment arm wins makes the mention a Local place.

WHAT THAT EXPOSED, measured in order:

1. With the reorder alone: three E0107, "nothing named $ct exists here", whose fix line suggests the identical spelling. That is the same self-suggesting message dollar3 measured. Cause: the lexer merges the mark into one Ident token, so take_mark never fires for a marked binding in a function body, and the binding parses through the ORDINARY path with is_comptime false. See the construction near line 117 of jet-parser Parser/Statements/bindings.rs; the is_comptime true construction near line 543 is unreachable for this spelling. A marked binding was therefore getting implicit-fold semantics, and the implicit path calls forget_ct_bindings when a fold advances a receiver. That is what deleted the marked reader from the scope between line 5 and line 6 of the reproducer.

2. Setting is_comptime from the name, with is_comptime set to Syntax::is_comptime_name of the binding name at that construction, cleared all three E0107. The mark is the demand. That single line reads correct against D-META-STAGE1=B on its own and is worth keeping when someone lands the whole fix.

3. That left four E0956, "method read_u8 can't run at compile time yet", on both marked read lines. Binding the fragment local with the folded value's type instead of None did not move it.

THE ONE REMAINING BLOCKER: as a baked CtLit the receiver was a concrete value and the TIR evaluator's handle path accepted read_u8; as a Local place it does not. The gate is in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/handles.rs, the only place read_u8 is named outside jet-sema's signature table and jet-foundation's StreamCursor. Someone needs to make that handle path admit a marked Local receiver the same way it admits whatever the CtLit form presented. That is the whole remaining distance: the E0107 and the forget-the-binding behaviour are solved, and only the handle gate stands between this and the reproducer printing 7 then 9.

Nothing was committed from this attempt. d22b848d1 is unchanged and still builds clean.

[bd3-dollar3] Criteria 1 and 6 stay open. I tried the prescribed fix, measured it twice, and it is not sufficient — the branch is back at d22b848d1 with no net change from me, because a half-fix here is worse than none. Recording what I proved so the next worker does not spend the same two build cycles.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
The reproducer prints 7|7|7|9 on d22b848d1, as logged.

The TIR side is not missing a marked-name concept. crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs has three ComptimeName arms; the first, guarded on value: Some(..), lowers every mention to TExprKind::CtLit. A CtLit is a value, not a place, so no write-back can reach it — that is why the marked reader never advances while the plain one does. The plain one advances because Expr::Ident lowers a seeded comptime binding to TExprKind::ConstRef, and ConstRef both reads (eval/exprs.rs:2157) and writes back (eval/exprs.rs:5476, added for card #1602). So the shape of the fix looked obvious: give ComptimeName the same treatment Ident gets.

WHY THAT ALONE FAILS
I tried it two ways: reordering so the eval-fragment arm wins, and mirroring the Ident const branch exactly (lower_comptime_scalar, else ConstRef(name)). Both build clean and both produce the identical result — three E0107 'a name must be declared before it's used' on the marked names, instead of 7|9|7|9.

The reason is in jet-comptime, not jet-codegen. A repository search for ComptimeName across crates/jet-comptime returns exactly two hits: Purity.rs:244, which ignores it, and Methods/dispatch.rs:1601, the write_back arm added in d22b848d1. There is no read arm anywhere in jet-comptime that resolves Expr::ComptimeName to a value. Today the fold only works because sema stamps value: Some(..) on each mention and the CtLit arm hands that stamp back. The moment a marked name resolves as a place instead of the stamp, nothing can read it, the fold of  :: .read_u8() fails,  never gets a value, and its later mentions report E0107.

THE FIX NEEDS BOTH HALVES IN ONE CHANGE
First, jet-comptime needs a read arm for Expr::ComptimeName that resolves from the comptime scope by the marked name, mirroring its Expr::Ident arm — the mark is part of the identifier, so the scope key carries it. Second, once a marked name can be read as a binding, TIR lowering can resolve it as a place the way Ident does, and the write_back arm already in place closes the loop. Landing the second without the first is what I measured, twice.

Worth checking while doing it: whether the comptime scope stores the binding under the marked key or the bare one, because ConstRef lookup goes through self.globals and a key mismatch would look exactly like this failure too.

[handoff] Head d22b848d1 on bd3/dollar. Criteria 1 and 6 still open. I prescribed the fix last session and it was only half right, so here is the sharpened diagnosis with the evidence, because the next worker should not re-derive it.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
A marked name is resolved and written back on TWO independent evaluator paths, not one, and my earlier note named only the first.

1. jet-comptime's dispatcher. Its write_back matched Expr::Ident and Expr::Field but not Expr::ComptimeName, so a marked receiver never advanced. Fixed in d22b848d1: the arm now reads Expr::Ident(name, _) | Expr::ComptimeName { name, .. }, which is what D-META-STAGE1=B means by the mark being part of the identifier.

2. The TIR evaluator in jet-codegen, reached through Comptime::TirBridge. This is the one that actually folds the failing fixture: read_u8 is implemented in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs and nowhere in jet-comptime (a repository search for "read_u8" returns jet-sema's signature table, the TIR subset gate, and jet-foundation's StreamCursor — no comptime arm). A search for ComptimeName under crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/ returns nothing, so that evaluator has no marked-name concept at all and resolves marked names by some other route without write-back.

So the remaining work is to give the TIR evaluator the same treatment: a marked name resolves and writes back as an ordinary name whose identifier includes the mark. Until both paths agree, criterion 1's second clause and criterion 6 cannot be claimed.

REPRODUCER, small and self-contained
fn run() {
    $ct :: Reader.over([U8].{7, 9, 11})
    $ct_a :: $ct.read_u8() ?? panic("ct a")
    $ct_b :: $ct.read_u8() ?? panic("ct b")
    rt :: Reader.over([U8].{7, 9, 11})
    rt_a :: rt.read_u8() ?? panic("rt a")
    rt_b :: rt.read_u8() ?? panic("rt b")
    print("{$ct_a}|{$ct_b}|{rt_a}|{rt_b}")
}
Prints 7|7|7|9. It must print 7|9|7|9. The marked reader does not advance; the plain one does.

The other two failures are the same root cause seen from different sides: comptime_loadable_matches_runtime types a module-level marked name from the folded value rather than its binding, so Loadable.Idle loses its methods; reusable_regex reports E0956 on replace_all_with. Both fixtures are faithful migrations of master's text, verified with git show master:tests/comptime_diff.rs.

- comptime_diff 23 of 26, the three above.
- fmt 163 of 163. grammar 18 of 18. diagnostic_snapshots 4 of 4.
- golden 63 failures, exactly the branch baseline, and zero comptime examples among them.
Eight of ten criteria stay met and are unaffected by the open two.

THE I2 VIOLATION IS FIXED. A folded value whose Rust spelling pins none of its type parameters reached rustc as E0282, which surfaces as an internal compiler error. TWO MORE DEFECTS OF THE SAME SLICE, ALSO FIXED
- The mark leaked into generated Rust identifiers, emitting , which rustc cannot parse. mangle() now spells a marked name userct_<name>. That keeps the mapping injective, which is exactly what the ratified text needs: a plain name and a marked name can never denote the same binding, so they must never mangle to the same Rust place.
- T.$layout had regressed to E0302. Sema, TIR lowering and the interpreter now read the one COMPILER_FACTS table, so $layout, $name and $fields are one spelling.

WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY IT IS ONE THING
Criterion 1's second clause and criterion 6 are the same defect. A marked name resolves through current_ct_globals(), a snapshot, instead of through the ordinary binding path an unmarked name used before this card. Three consequences, all visible as the three remaining comptime_diff failures:
- sequential_comptime_reads_advance_the_shared_reader: a real divergence, comptime gives 7|7|3 where runtime gives 7|9|1. Reading $ct twice does not advance the shared reader because each mention reads the snapshot; apply_ct_mutations writes back to ct_scopes but the marked name does not route through it.
- comptime_loadable_matches_runtime: the type comes from the folded CtValue rather than the binding, so Loadable.Idle comes back as a bare Loadable and loses its methods. I fixed the local case by looking the name up in the ordinary environment first, but a module-level marked binding is not in that environment.
- reusable_regex_matches_across_comptime_tir_and_runtime: E0956 on replace_all_with.
All three fixtures are faithful migrations of master's text, verified with git show master:tests/comptime_diff.rs, so the cause is the branch's resolution path, not the migration. The fix is to make a marked name resolve as an ordinary name whose identifier text includes the mark, which is what D-META-STAGE1=B means by 'sema treats the sigil as part of the identifier'. That is a focused pass on sema's binding registration and is the honest remainder of this card.

PRE-EXISTING RED, NOT THIS CARD

TRAP WORTH KNOWING, cost me a wrong diagnosis
With CARGO_TARGET_DIR shared across worktrees, another worktree's build replaces target/debug/jet and the shared dep artifacts underneath you. I read a stale binary and concluded my sema fix had not worked when it had, and a lib-test compile failed with 'no variant named ComptimeName in jet_lexer::AST::Expr' because it linked another worktree's artifacts. Build and run in the same command, or verify the binary is yours before trusting a probe.

cards.title: One registration table: marker, plane, right and fact
cards.body: Four registries were proposed in one week for one job. This card builds one declaration kind in the Prelude with a target kind, so a marker rule, a knowledge plane, a right and a build fact are rows of the same table separated only by what they attach to. The declaring word is marker for rules, and a rule carries its own facts as named parameters marked with $, so $sites: [.Function, .Method] describes the rule while ordinary parameters are what a user writes. Reflection, jet inspect and the drift guards are written once and serve all four. D-FACT-LAW1=B adds the law to the table itself: every row states which way is safe and which written words move it the other way, and a drift guard fails a row that states neither. D-FACT-OWN1=A adds one row kind for facts a prover publishes, such as sendability and view provenance, which register without any plane algebra.

Marker names resolve through ordinary name resolution, so there is exactly one parse path, and the four checks of D-MARK-FORM1 read a declaration instead of a Rust row. Nothing a beginner types changes. This makes marker law zero structurally true rather than enforced by a CI scan, and it is the substrate the five open marker cards should build on.

cards.title: Users may declare rules that record facts or add code
cards.body: A user declares a rule with a signature and legal sites, exactly like a compiler rule. A rule with no body records a fact. A rule with a body adds code. This is the same power the compiler has, so #Codable and #Inline stop being special cases. Law 1 still holds: a rule adds items and facts and can never change or shadow what the user wrote, and that is checked rather than trusted.

cards.title: Derive bodies are real code with holes
cards.body:
A derive body contains Jet members, not a string. The header already names the trait and the type, so no inner impl is written, and the parser checks the body when it is written rather than after re-lexing emitted text. Splices are typed holes filled at expansion, and compile-time control flow inside the body generates one member per field when a derive needs that. b.generate takes the same block of items, so the build entry needs no separate form.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): This card builds the provider-definition meaning of `derive`, which every option on ballot D-ONCE-DERIVE1 (card #1656) preserves — proceed. Keep the definition meaning strictly separate from the request meaning in the parser, examples, and spec text, so the ballot's outcome on the request spelling lands without touching this work.

cards.title: A library may declare a checked text block
cards.body: A library may declare a block rule, the way the standard library adds SQL. Jet reads the block boundary with its own grammar and hands the inside to the library as text; the library checks it and adds code. Jet's grammar never moves, because the braces are always Jet's braces, so no library can change how anything outside the block parses.

cards.title: One effect model at both stages
cards.body:
Compile-time code declares what it touches with the same syntax as run-time code. The three comptime tiers keep their meaning exactly, but they stop being a separate vocabulary and become what the effect set already says: tier 0 is an empty effect set, tier 1 is a recorded effect, tier 2 needs #Impure plus permission. The curated allow-list of pure Core calls retires because the effect set already carries the fact, and the two purity checkers merge into one, retiring one diagnostic family.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Criteria are frozen for this building card, so this is a note only. The fourth criterion preserves `--allow-impure`; ballot D-ONCE-GATE1 (card #1656) asks whether that flag retires in favour of one shared org-policy ladder for every audited escape. Keep the ratified tier meanings as written, and treat the flag's spelling as provisional — do not add new consumers or new documentation promises for it inside this change.

cards.title: A compile-time value is legal anywhere a constant is legal
cards.body: An array length or an enum number may be any expression the compiler can compute, not just a literal or a bare name. Both sites call the evaluator that already exists. The rules that follow are unchanged: the value must be known and it must be an integer. Only the shape of what a person may type changes, and S26 is untouched because the value stays a value and never selects a type.

cards.title: Everything derivable is derived unless refused
cards.body:
If the compiler can derive a trait from a type's shape, it does. The default set widens from four traits to every structurally derivable trait, Codable included, so json.encode(u) works with nothing asked for. A type refuses one trait with the exclamation mark it already uses and a project refuses one everywhere through a declared setting. Traits that cannot be derived structurally stay opt-in because there is nothing to derive, and the existing eligibility gates still apply silently.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The refusal spelling in the criteria is settled and unaffected. The spelling a type uses to *request* a derived capability is on ballot D-ONCE-DERIVE1 (card #1656) — marker form versus the body line. Nothing in this card should introduce or document a request spelling; the opt-in traits it leaves behind adopt whichever the ballot ratifies.

cards.title: Type foundation: one knowledge vector on Type
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1538. Ten kinds of compile-time fact live in ten private mechanisms in the checker. Give Type one knowledge vector and one registry instead. Identity becomes the carrier plus the facts a plane declares identity-bearing. Function obligations compare by subsumption, which repairs the live defect where two function types each equal a third but not each other. All knowledge erases before the typed IR, so codegen and every execution tier are untouched. Nothing a user writes changes and every existing test stays green. This is the first card of the type-system-v2 slate; every other D-TYPE2 card lands on top of it.

cards.title: Fact planes: one registry, nameable facts, complete typed reflection
cards.body: Every fact plane must live in one registry and obey the law markers already obey: a plane exists exactly when it is registered, its facts are nameable, reflection reports them as typed values, and the compiler's own planes ship as readable prelude source. Extend the marker registration law to dimensions, measures, exactness and classifications. Remove the last string fallbacks from reflection, so Type.reflect() answers facts and dimensions as real values and marker arguments arrive as typed records on fields, methods and variants, matching what the type level already gives. Add drift guards that walk every registered plane end to end, the same pattern the marker rebuild uses on cards #1457, #1458 and #1460. Under D-FACT-READ1=A the per-fact read is the $ mark, built on card #1623; reflect() stays as the aggregate view over the same typed facts, and the two never diverge.

cards.title: Inline value ranges in any type position
cards.body: A value range should not require minting a named type first. Make Int(0..100) legal wherever a type is written: parameters, returns, fields and bindings. Literals check at compile time and unproven values convert fallibly, exactly as U8 works today. The inline form is structural, so two inline types with the same base and the same range are the same type, while distinct stays the nominal wrapper for when identity matters. This only removes the requirement to pre-declare a name; the checking rules are the ones already ratified.

cards.title: The number grid: sized widths become Int plus a range, and BigInt retires
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1547. Every number type becomes one cell of a two-axis grid: the value world (whole, ratio, real, complex) and the knowledge grade (exact unbounded, exact bounded, approximate, measured). A sized width such as U8 becomes Int plus a proven range and a one-byte layout, with its spelling and behavior unchanged. BigInt retires, because the arbitrary-precision Int holds every value it held, and the four errors that police mixing Int with BigInt retire with it. The ratified widening law, value-set containment, becomes the theorem that a subset needs no conversion, and one interval prover replaces the width table, the range checks and the fixed-list index proof. This reshapes a name other open cards use, so it runs before them.

cards.title: Exact by default: decimal literals, exact division, approximation opted in
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571. Ordinary numbers become exact. A decimal literal is an exact Decimal, so price * 3 gives 59.97 exactly and 0.1 + 0.2 equals 0.3. Division of exact values lands in exact rational territory: a result with a finite decimal prints as a decimal, otherwise it prints as a fraction and stays exact, so 1 / 3 prints 1/3 and third * 3 equals 1. Functions that truly leave the rationals, such as square root and sine, answer approximate and say so. Experts opt into Float or F32 at the declaration and hot code keeps today's machine arithmetic. Exact values use machine-word fast paths with spill, the same playbook as the bigint Int.

cards.title: Time joins the unit plane: one Time family, one literal system
cards.body: Durations and instants become ordinary unit-plane quantities. Duration is the delta quantity of a canonical Time unit family stored as a 64-bit nanosecond count, per the ratified resolution decision, and Instant is the matching point quantity, reusing the affine machinery temperatures already use. Every 500ms resolves through the one unit plane, in user code, timeouts and schedules alike, and both hidden suffix tables are deleted. Because time is on the plane, it joins unit algebra: 12meter / 2s is a speed.

cards.title: One measure substrate for list lengths, matrix shapes, lanes and exponents
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1547. Four private encodings hold compile-time numbers in types today: list lengths, matrix shapes, vector lanes and dimension exponents. Make them one thing. A measure is a compile-time number attached to a type through the plane registry, and each use declares its own combination rule: joining two lists adds lengths, matrix multiply matches inner sides and composes outer sides, multiplying quantities adds exponents. Surfaces do not change; the encodings underneath become one. Measures are declared literals or module value parameters and are never computed by user code, so the ratified wall that compile-time evaluation cannot create types still stands. Symbolic lengths from generic modules resolve at specialization exactly as today, without the placeholder-zero sentinel.

cards.title: The one law on the knowledge planes, and its sema gate
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571 and #1624. Write the conservation law into the spec and give it teeth: knowledge grows silently, is lost only at a spelled step, and erases at runtime. The two existing spellings stay, because each names its own operation well. approx marks accepting a representation's precision, and rounded conversions name a mode because rounding direction matters there. Add the sema check the law needs, so any operation that discards range, exactness, unit, state or classification must require a spelled step. The law then binds every future surface without a new ballot.

cards.title: Measured values: the uncertainty knowledge grade
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1547. Measurement becomes the measured grade of numeric knowledge. Arithmetic and the math functions propagate uncertainty by the standard first-order rules, and exact values are zero-uncertainty, so mixing them needs no ceremony. Nothing changes for any program until a measurement enters it. Printing shows the value with its uncertainty. Propagation uses first-order linear approximation with uncorrelated inputs, and the docs must say so plainly; correlated errors are out of scope. Measured unit scales produce measured conversion results, which connects the two places uncertainty already lives.

cards.title: The 4i imaginary literal on the unit-literal path
cards.body: A numeric literal with the suffix i is an imaginary number, so real plus imaginary reads like the textbook: 0.5 + 0.8i. The suffix resolves through the shipped, table-free unit-literal machinery, so there is no new grammar. It mints the imaginary component of the ratified Complex type. Only the suffix form is special: the identifier i on its own stays an ordinary variable name, and shadowing behaves like any unit suffix in scope.

cards.title: Dropping a bound task handle is a compile error
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571 and #1624. The join duty becomes the same rule every single-use value follows. Binding a task handle and then never using it fails to compile, and the fix text names the three exits: join it, use its result, or call detach for fire-and-forget. Work is then never lost silently and the choice is always visible on the page. This extends D-LIN1 to Task<T> and to the list forms from D-VERDICT-1323-1, and handles are discharged by all, race and any at those calls. It amends the L1101 behavior in the task section of the spec.

cards.title: Shared values read and write like values, and the transaction law matches the runtime
cards.body: Shared state drops its closure ceremony. shared expr builds the cell, reads and writes are plain field access, and each statement is one atomic step. Several statements commit together under #Transact, whose name becomes optional and is kept for on_commit and on_rollback. The read and edit closure forms are deleted; expert guards and Condition stay for manual control. In the same change, correct the transaction law to match what ships: the block body runs exactly once and the commit takes locks in a fixed order, so log lines never duplicate and heavy contention waits on locks instead of retrying. Both halves are the same commit engine, so they land together. Race freedom does not move: the compiler still checks every crossing and orders every lock.

cards.title: A stream is a task: one cancellation and cleanup law
cards.body:
Streams and tasks have two separately written shutdown laws, and the copies drifted. Delete the second one. A stream producer is a scheduler child: dropping the iterator cancels it, and it unwinds at its next wait point running its cleanups, exactly as any cancelled task does. yield is a wait point and drop-close is a cancel. The generator decision's separate shutdown wording is replaced by a reference to the task law, so the drift class dies by construction. Tier parity follows because all tiers already share the task cancel path.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The cancellation and cleanup unification is the substance of this card and stands under every option. The word `stream` itself is on ballot D-ONCE-WORD1 (card #1656) — one option keeps `Stream<T>`, another renames the type. Write the spec text so the law is stated once about the generator type, and adopt whichever name that ballot ratifies rather than fixing the word in new prose.

cards.title: Typed schedules and one word for a unit of work
cards.body: The schedule behind the marker is a string parsed by a private suffix table in the schedule checker. Make it a typed value every consumer reads: jet dev, services and jetos timers. Delete the private suffix table and give the marker's value type Duration or a wall-clock time on the one time rail, which is why hours and days start working. In the same change finish the vocabulary cleanup card #1448: a job is a task the runtime starts, one word, not two. This amends the value grammar of D-SCHEDULE1, not its placement rules, and aligns D-TAG-SURFACE1 and D-TASK-META1. The service plane is not built here: D-SERVICE1 and its siblings build on the group substrate with no new mechanism, and those cards keep their own homes.
