cards.title: A taskgroup may be named in any borrow position
cards.body: A taskgroup is a borrow of its scope, so it should work as a parameter anywhere a borrow works: free functions and methods alike. Lift the named-free-function restriction of D-TASKGROUP-PARAM1 to all direct parameter positions, including the parameter lists of methods. Storage, return, capture and fields stay banned with the existing teaching error, so no child ever outlives its scope. Spawns through a parameter group still own their captures. Helpers can then live where the code lives.

log.text: c5 root cause confirmed and a second defect found underneath it. looks_like_item at crates/jet-repl/src/lib.rs:1374-1386 only inspects the trimmed start, so a source opening with comments (the shared SOURCE constant does) is classified as statements and fails E0003/E0102. I tried teaching the classifier to skip leading line and block comments; the classification became correct and the test then died with a stack overflow (SIGABRT) inside the item path. So there are two bugs stacked: the classifier misreads commented item sources, and the item path recurses without bound on this input. I reverted the classifier change because a clean E0003 is better for a user than a crash. Fixing c5 means fixing the recursion first, then the classifier.

c5 has one precise blocker. tests/taskgroup_parameter_tiers.rs is registered at tests/suites.txt:256 and runs 18 tests, 17 passing. The one failure is repl_runs_group_parameter_example at :107-110: jet::REPL::run_transcript rejects the shared SOURCE constant with E0003 on the struct and fn, then E0102 for a missing run, because SOURCE opens with leading comments. Every other tier accepts the identical text, so this is a REPL front-end intake defect rather than anything about Group parameters. Fix the REPL intake and c5 closes.

Criteria 1-7 implemented 2026-08-19 (commit pending integration): the two owner_type.is_none() gates in Registration.rs::check_params_and_body were the whole defect, so a taskgroup parameter now works on methods exactly as on free functions, with every storage/return/capture/field refusal preserved and admit_scoped_borrow still refusing a Parameter-origin scoped borrow. cards.title: Typed task outcome and status replace the trace strings
cards.body: Two small enums replace the formatted strings a program reads today. outcome() consumes the handle, like join, and says how the task ended while carrying the value: Finished, Panicked with a reason, Cancelled, DeadlineBlown, mirroring what the runtime already knows. status() borrows the handle and answers live questions: running, paused, cancel requested. Select results and event dispatch states adopt the same words, so there is one outcome vocabulary. trace() and exception() are deleted, not aliased. Hold this card until the spawn-and-failure gate on #1505 closes: the proposal's unraised D-CONC-FAIL1 would put task failure on the ? rail with no separate outcome type, which would delete this work.

cards.title: Authority substrate: one rights tree, one holds relation, one gate record
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571. Nine mechanisms answer authority questions today and they can disagree. Build one substrate in jet-foundation that owns the root table, the subsumption lattice behind effect_covers, the scope ladder from D-MARK-SCOPE1, and the gate ledger. Effects.rs, Policy.rs, EffectBudget.rs, BuildEffects.rs, both purity checkers and the REPL authorizer become consumers of it. Nothing a user types changes. The compiler, the budget, the sandbox, the REPL and the trust store then give the same answer with the same names. Semantics stay in the substrate per I3 and the generated Rust stays byte-identical. This card runs before the other authority cards.
cards.plan: Implements D-AUTHORITY-MODEL1 — ratified 2026-08-06. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/authority-one-model.md.

cards.title: Effect roots: one FFI root with languages as leaves
cards.body:
The closed root table drifted: the docs claim ten roots, the code has twenty-eight, and two promised roots were never added. Heal it. The table becomes thirteen roots, the ratified ten plus FFI, Browser and Secret, and the sixteen language roots become leaves under FFI: FFI.Go, FFI.Java, FFI.Lua, plus the promised FFI.Py and FFI.Octave. Ancestor subsumption already gives FFI covering FFI.Go, so a bound written as no-FFI forbids every foreign call at once. Existing rows migrate in one pass and the old flat spellings are deleted. This card absorbs the three open drift cards #1502, #1503 and #1504.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): This is the reference case for one table rendered everywhere: after the merge, EFFECT_ROOTS is the only home and the enums, CLI deny flags, E3503 menu copy, and spec table must be rendered or guarded against it, not re-listed. Delete the flat language spellings through the retirement mechanism on ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656) so the retired roots carry a ratchet.

Read each decision verbatim (tower brief on this card's parent proposal, or tower decision show) before building; the ratified outcome text is the law, this plan is the route. Every requirement is a discrete exit criterion below: meet each with targeted proof (tests, snapshots, examples with golden output), and keep I9 tier parity inside this card — AOT, default jet run (JIT), and the interpreter must agree on every surface this card ships before it closes. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/authority-one-model.md.

log.text: c17 is blocked on an I9 question the owner must answer, not on missing work. examples/features/lowlevel/polyglot_fortran/main.jet checks clean but default jet run fails E0956: the evaluator hard-refuses TExprKind::ExternCall at Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs:9580, while AOT emits the FFI wrapper at TIR/emit/expressions.rs:6266-6285. The call crosses a native Fortran ABI, so the interpreter genuinely cannot evaluate it. I9 allows exactly one escape here: an owner-ratified carve-out naming a tier that cannot apply to a surface. Native FFI under the interpreter is that shape. The alternative, deopting ExternCall to a compiled path instead of refusing, is real work and a different card. Local AOT additionally stops E3201 because gfortran is absent; tests/golden.rs:746-769 already capability-gates that, so it is environment, not defect.

Reconciled against the one-crossing slate (#1655) on 2026-08-19: no pre-law conflict. D-BOUND-UNDO1 does NOT depend on this table - crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Effects.rs:179-197 fires E0746 on is_extern plus a missing #Undo, not on the effect root - so UNDO1 was never blocked on this card. The 16 flat language effect roots (Prelude/Effects.jet:22-38) remain this card's scope.

D-PANICROOT1 IS RATIFIED, outcome A (deny-only), created and ratified 2026-08-15, ballotMode full, all five review passes recorded, whyNot covering B/C/D. It is NOT awaiting the owner -- I twice reported it as owner-gated and both claims were wrong. All 572 board decisions are ratified; there are no open ballots anywhere.

The live gap is IMPLEMENTATION, and outcome A is unimplemented at da0d189b1. Under A the CODE moves, not the corpus. Three sites still contradict the ratified outcome:
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerItems.rs:3427 -- inside check_panic_call (declared :3423), `self.record_effect(Effect::Panic.name(), call.name_span)` still records Panic as an ORDINARY effect.
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Effects.jet:18 -- `effect Panic` is still declared a root alongside GPU and FFI.
- E0751, the positive-mention diagnostic option A specifies, exists nowhere in crates/ (grep returns no matches).

Single seam for the fix: `effects_uncovered` at crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Effects.rs:148. Its own doc comment states it is reached by every E0740/E0741/E0712/E0747/E0742 subset check, so dropping the Panic root there implements A everywhere at once rather than per call site.

Two shipped failures this must clear, both currently red:
- examples/features/effects/effect_grant.jet -- `#Grant(caps: FS, IO)` at :16 omits Panic while the body panics at :17 and :18, so E0712.
- examples/features/lowlevel/polyglot_fortran/main.jet:4 -- `fn run() =[Fortran, IO]=>` omits Panic and the reach is cross-file, so E0740.

Care needed: deny-only is ASYMMETRIC. A deny surface must still refuse Panic (=[!Panic]=>, effects:{deny:[Panic]}, E0749, and the #Pre/refinement discharge from D-NOPANIC1=D all stay), while #Grant/#Caps must neither require nor accept it. Simply deleting Panic from the table would lose the deny side too. Under A the 21 gate sites across 12 example files plus 8 in tests that a grantable-Panic world would need become unnecessary; if any still needs a declaration afterwards, the gate is asymmetric the wrong way.

Orchestrator finding at master 6cfe66872: the Panic effect root is already breaking the shipped corpus, which raises the priority of this card's root-count question. examples/features/effects/effect_grant.jet fails the front end with E0712 'this #Grant region uses the effect Panic, which it has no capability for' at effect_grant.jet:16 on '#Grant(caps: FS, IO) {', and examples/features/lowlevel/polyglot_fortran/main.jet fails with E0740 'run uses the effect Panic, which its signature doesn't allow'. Panic ships as a root in Prelude/Effects.jet alongside the 30 others this card records, so every #Grant region and every signature that can panic must now declare it. That is a large new declaration burden on the beginner surface and it is an owner call, not an implementation detail: decide whether Panic is an effect root at all before migrating the examples. If it stays a root, the examples need Panic in their caps lists and the beginner story needs review; if it does not, the root table shrinks toward the 13 this card specifies.

Timeline audit 2026-08-10: two open adapter cards add flat per-language effect roots that this card deletes. #504 (COBOL, phase building, workOrder 990) and #1154 (Octave, workOrder 1000) both land ahead of this card at workOrder 1120, and D-AUTHORITY-ROOTS1=A names FFI.Octave by name as an arriving leaf under the one FFI root. Whatever flat root those two add, criteria 2 and 5 here delete and make unparseable. Both cards now carry a note pointing here. If either has already landed a flat root when this card starts, fold its migration into criterion 5 rather than minting a new card.

ABSORBED cards 1502, 1503 and 1504 (anti-inflation fold). This card's own criterion 6 already stated it closes them: 'The E1221 explain text and the stale Effects.rs comments are corrected, closing 1502, 1503 and 1504.' Verified live: EFFECT_ROOTS in crates/jet-foundation/src/Facts.rs has 28 entries with no Py or Octave roots. One worker fixes all three doc/table drifts plus the missing FFI leaves in a single pass. The three folded cards are deleted; their content is this log plus criterion 6.

cards.title: The Authority value: one named type that crosses boundaries
cards.body: The carried rights set has no real type today, so a phantom sits at a dead end. Give it one: a type named Authority in the prelude that carries a rights set across every boundary. The grant handle has this type, the workspace call returns it, plugins receive it and sessions hold it. It narrows and never widens, and it never takes part in dispatch, so it stays ordinary data under the fact model. Construction keeps the ratified PascalCase convention. cards.title: One authority block in the package manifest
cards.body:
Grants are spread across several manifest keys, so no reviewer can see what a package may do in one place. Collapse them into a single authority block that holds the package's own bound, its per-dependency grants, its trust defaults and its provider bounds. Old keys migrate in one pass and are deleted. The policy key keeps only floors and unsafe mode. One parser reads the block and one diagnostic family reports a malformed one, and the lockfile and the ledger mirror its shape.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The first criterion says `pkg.jet` accepts the authority block. The ratified manifest root is `package.jet` (D-ECO-FILEROOT1); `pkg.jet` is a retired spelling. Build the authority block on the current-form manifest, and leave the retired name to the retirement mechanism on ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656).

cards.title: One gate ledger for every step off the safe path
cards.body:
Every written word that moves a fact away from safety is a gate: #Unsafe, #Impure, a dependency grant, a trust grant, .Force, a taint scrub, detach or .drop with a reason, approx and wrapping. Today each family is recorded somewhere different, so nobody can read the whole picture. Give every gate kind one ledger and one reader, jet inspect gates. Sources stay where they are: source markers, the lockfile and the trust store. The ledger is the merged read model that keeps provenance, so this adds no new write surface, and no gate gains new ceremony. The existing per-kind views keep working as filters.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The ledger half of this card is ratified law (D-FACT-GATE1) and should be built. The ladder half is not: ballot D-ONCE-GATE1 (card #1656) decides whether `#Unsafe`, `#Impure`, and `#Nondeterministic` share one org-policy ladder and whether `--allow-impure` retires. Build the one ledger and its reader now; add the policy ladder in whatever shape that ballot ratifies, and do not mint a second impure-policy surface in the meantime.

cards.title: Retire the word capability from every user-facing surface
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1501. The word capability means four different things across Jet's surfaces, so it means nothing. Take it off every surface a user reads. Borrow diagnostics say write access instead. The carried rights value takes the name Authority. The product claim manifest becomes feature claims. Docs may still say capability-based when describing the design tradition, but no user-facing message, name or identifier uses the bare word. No grammar changes; the diagnostic copy is snapshot-tested product text, so those snapshots are re-blessed in the same change. This reshapes wording that other open cards quote, including #1499 and #1501, so it runs before them.

cards.title: Adopt the Core namespace tree
cards.body:
Core has short-door one-offs, duplicate homes and namespaces that answer the same question twice. Move to the final tree in Part B of docs/proposals/corelib-overhaul.md, which is the authoritative map for this card, together with its disposition table. Keep core.files. Nest random under math, fmt under text, and the net and crypto leaves under their parents. Merge env and os into sys. Split core.io and delete it. Do not add core.json. Rename science.measurement to units. The get and post doors stay on the http parent. People learn nested paths once, then alias. This moves module paths that many other open cards touch, so it runs before them.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): This namespace migration deletes many old paths in one change. Perform the deletions through the retirement mechanism ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656) ratifies, so each retired path gets the same error, mechanical rewrite, and zero-count ratchet rather than a card-local resolution error. Separately, any Core method name this move touches must follow the verb table on ballot D-ONCE-VERB1 — do not settle a verb here.

cards.title: Prelude policy and the ratified prelude additions
cards.body: Write down what needs no import and then add exactly what the policy allows. The seven criteria become law: measured frequency, total and safe, names that never carry semantics, no better home, first-hour coverage, one fixed set, and collision-conscious names. Shadowing lets the user win with a compiler warning, and new names land only at epoch boundaries with a migration lint. Then ship the ratified additions: eprint, input, assert, assert_eq with a structural diff, the type names Clock, Instant, Date, Duration and Path, the blessed doors Clock.now() and Date.today(), and the file trio read_file, write_file and file_exists as re-exports of the file-system functions carrying the file-system effect. Random stays behind one import in core.math.random. Every entry is total or returns a result, and no implicit conversion ever enters the prelude. This reshapes the ambient name set every other card writes against, so it runs early.

cards.title: The Path type, with strings accepted everywhere
cards.body:
A file path becomes a real type with methods, so joining is correct on every system and a reviewer can see what is a path. Path lives in the prelude and carries join, parent and the other path methods. Every Core function that takes a path accepts a plain string or a Path, so a beginner never constructs anything. The core.path free functions are deleted because the methods replace them. Expert Path-only APIs may take Path alone, but the default Core doors accept both. No path-join operator is added.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Two ballots touch this card. The tombstone for the deleted `core.path` free functions should use the retirement mechanism from ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656), not a card-local tombstone. The constructor spelling for building a Path from a string is on ballot D-ONCE-VERB1 (bare `.from` versus `Type.from_x`) — implement whichever it ratifies.

cards.title: Eager collection helpers with a .lazy opt-in
cards.body:
Helpers on a real list, map or set run at once and return a plain collection, so nothing re-runs invisibly and results are inspectable in a debugger. Writing .lazy first gives the same vocabulary as a deferred view, for large or infinite work. Sources that are already streams, such as file lines, streams and channels, keep returning the deferred view because they arrive over time. The optimizer may fuse adjacent eager adapters when the intermediate is unobservable. This amends the lazy default of D-ITERTOOLS1 and touches the open Iter work on #1479.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The eager/lazy split is independent of naming and can proceed. The verbs on the collection surface this card touches are on ballot D-ONCE-VERB1 (card #1656), which adopts one verb per job across List, Map, and Set. Do not settle a collection verb spelling inside this change; migrate any renamed verb through the retirement mechanism when the ballot lands.

cards.title: Adopt the extended Core API doctrine
cards.body:
The Core API rules stop at L8 today. Extend them with the Part A rules from docs/proposals/corelib-overhaul.md, which is the authoritative list for this card, and make them law in docs/spec/stdlib-api-laws.md: call site C1 to C3, defaults and options D1 to D4, failure F1 to F3, types T1 to T3, naming N1 to N2, layering L-A to L-D, evolution E1 to E2. Every new or changed Core API passes them in review, the same way L1 to L8 work today, and call sites are judged by reading them aloud. Options are enums, not booleans. Every magic default is listed in one docs table with its override. Existing drift is carded, not grandfathered.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Ballot D-ONCE-VERB1 (card #1656) amends the constructor rule in this doctrine (the `Type.from_x()` versus bare `.from` question) and the one-verb-per-job rule for collections. Write every other rule now; leave the constructor and collection-verb rows to be recorded from the ballot's ratified outcome, and do not mint drift cards against those two rows before it answers.

questions.text: This misses the philosophies of jet. Minimizes friction proportionally to frequency of use (most common things should be easiest/fastest) and beginner friendliness with magic and ergonomics out of the box but allow full expert control
questions.answer: Agreed, and the ballot is revised. Every name is now weighed by the usage-frequency report (docs/research/corelib-api-usage-frequency-2026-08-06.md), not by a flat rule. New recommended option C ships the high-traffic names directly on String: to_int and to_float (parse-to-number is a dominant string operation, and they chain: line.trim().to_int()) plus match and matches for regex. Each is a spelling of the one existing mechanism (Int.parse, Float.parse, core.regex), so beginners get the zero-ceremony call and experts keep one engine. The rest stay routed: mutation verbs clash with immutable String, and char-level sequence work sits below the frequency line, where one chars() call is proportional friction.

cards.title: JIT native coverage: closure methods deopt to interpreter for List
cards.body:
List closure methods such as all() run through interpreter deopt rather than native JIT code, and Set inherited the same coverage gap. Semantics are correct (same Prelude path), so this is a dev-loop performance gap, not an I9 violation. Extend the JIT-native coverage allowlist and lowering for the closure-method family.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The body's claim that a deopt to the interpreter is a performance gap and not an I9 violation rests on the tier question ballot D-ONCE-TIER1 (card #1656) resolves. Treat the performance work as valid under every option, but do not cite this card as precedent for the interpreter's parity status until the ballot answers.
cards.plan: Extend JIT-native coverage so List and Set closure methods such as all() lower to native code instead of deopting to the interpreter. The gap lives in crates/jet-jit/src/jit/safety.rs (resident_safe_closure_method, around line 1673) and crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs (lower_closure_method, around line 19418): both currently reject part of the closure-method family and fall back to interpreter deopt. Add native lowering for the missing methods, following the pattern the already-covered methods use in the same two functions. The known gap is recorded in tests/jit_gaps.txt line 435 ('collections/set: run: jit closure method unsupported'); delete that line once the method lowers natively. Semantics do not change: this only moves work from interpreter deopt to native JIT code, so no sema, TIR, or Prelude file changes, and I9 stays satisfied by construction. Prove it with cargo test --test dev jit_coverage_audit, which reads tests/jit_gaps.txt and fails if a listed gap still deopts, and confirm examples/collections/set gives identical output under jet run and jet run --release.

log.text: audit #1869: set stem (jit_gaps row 435, 'jit closure method unsupported') re-homed here from #1758 — it is exactly this card's closure-method family (safety.rs resident_safe_closure_method, lower_ctx.rs lower_closure_method ~20417). Current fallback confirmed at lower_ctx.rs:20417.

criteria.text: resident_safe_closure_method and lower_closure_method in crates/jet-jit/src/jit/{safety.rs,lower_ctx.rs} natively lower the List/Set closure-method family, including all(), instead of deopting
criteria.evidence: Measured at the re-derived ledger. collections/set records resident_jit, which in this gate is an observed parity proof rather than a label: classify_corpus_stem diverts a stem to TierDivergent unless the JIT and AOT outputs are identical, separately asserts interpreter equals AOT, and requires both that no deopt occurred and that Cranelift actually executed - so criterion 4's byte-identical output under jet run and jet run --release is what that row means. The gap line this card asked to remove is gone: jit_gaps.txt gaps: and run_gaps: are both empty. Set's all, filter, each, fold, map and flat_map were already admitted through the Set arm of jit_closure_elem_type_for plus lower_closure_source. What landed extends the family with each admitted method's lowering arm changed in the same slice: TakeWhile and SkipWhile, and Position, through lower_iter_take_skip_while and lower_iter_position, which now bind the element type instead of hardcoding Int; MinBy and MaxBy through lower_iter_min_max_by, where the element travels only as the packed-Option payload; and CountBy through lower_iter_count_by. Two polarity corrections went the OTHER way and are recorded because a wrong refusal and a wrong admission are both bugs: TakeWhile, SkipWhile and Position now REQUIRE a Bool callback body in both tables, because the lowerings compare the result with an I8 icmp and a non-Bool body handed Cranelift mismatched operand types - an I2 internal compiler error rather than a deopt - and sema types both predicates Bool so no live case is lost; and CountBy's predicate had checked the element while its lowering demanded both element and key, so a receiver the predicate admitted was refused one step later and the function deopted anyway. Set receivers are deliberately excluded from all four positional walks, because a hash Set publishes no position per D-SET-DECLINE1=C and max_by keeps the last tie over an AOT Set order that is unspecified. Criterion 5 holds: only crates/jet-jit/src/jit/safety.rs and lower_ctx.rs changed, no sema, TIR or Prelude file. One I8 deletion came with it - six copies of the args.first() to lambda to body-type ladder collapsed into one resident_safe_expr_callback, and resident_safe_binary_lambda lost its last caller and was deleted.

cards.title: Evaluate one canonical UI architecture (TEA-style) for Jet's user-facing UI framework
cards.body: Video-mining evidence (Elm retrospective, 2026-08-06): a single prescribed model-update-view architecture with one mutation site is Elm's most-exported asset (Bubble Tea, iced, Redux, Lustre), and Gleam's lack of one pushes an extra architecture decision onto every user. Jet has no ratified user-facing UI framework; Canopy/blueprint (#182) is a projection editor, not a stdlib UI architecture. When the UI framework surface is designed, evaluate a TEA-style single canonical architecture (fits I8 one-mechanism) including micro details: the minimal init/update/view function triad and lazy view-render caching (skip re-render when inputs are unchanged). Owner-gated surface; ballot rides the design, not this card. Re-home if a dedicated UI-framework epoch appears.
cards.plan:
Deliverable is a design-doc section, not a ballot yet (owner-gated surface; ballot rides the future UI-framework design doc).
1. Write a worked TEA-style option: minimal init/update/view function triad in Jet syntax, one mutation site, with a before/after example (naive re-render loop vs the triad).
2. Evaluate lazy view-render caching as a default: skip re-render when inputs are unchanged. Show the mechanism and its cost in Jet syntax.
3. Run a beginner pass (safe default, no ceremony) and an expert pass (explicit control over caching, effects, and update scheduling) over the triad.
4. Do not open a ballot on this card. When a dedicated UI-framework epoch or design doc lands, the ballot slate for the architecture choice rides that doc; re-home this card there if it appears.

log.text: Criterion reconciliation (2026-08-19): read criterion 3 as "ballot DEFERRAL is recorded — the slate rides the future UI-framework design doc; no ballot opened on this card; no implementation before that ratification." Plan step 4 ("do not open a ballot on this card") governs.

video-mine design input (2026-08-19, SwiftUI 'Flow data through SwiftUI', Qxv4Tf4-AdU): (1) AVOID SwiftUI's mechanism fragmentation — six decorated mechanisms (@State/@Binding/@Observable/@Environment/@AppStorage/@Model) chosen per data-flow tier; the talk exists because users cannot pick. Jet's signal surface should cover view state, model, preferences, and persistence as ONE mechanism with scope/lifetime parameters (I8). (2) @State's real model — framework-owned storage keyed by view identity, view structs transient — is the subtle part; Jet signals are explicitly owned values (owner Drop detaches the graph), a simpler story worth keeping. (3) Jet already BEATS the @Observable model: JetDerived.get() auto-subscribes the active observer — fine-grained signal graph vs SwiftUI re-running whole view bodies; record as beat vector. (4) Worth designing: type-keyed environment/context injection for rarely-changing shared objects (prop-drilling relief) and an @AppStorage-class persistent-preference scope (#505 live queries and #765 #Persist cover the model/persistence tiers; preferences tier is uncovered). (5) SwiftData micro surface worth stealing: relationship delete-rule cascade + inverse declared on the model.

video-mine design input (2026-08-12): HAM ships long-press inspect-element inside production apps — runtime introspection as a first-class UI-framework feature. Worth weighing in the canonical UI architecture evaluation.

Timeline audit 2026-08-10: given a work order ahead of the Canvas RAD family, because six cards build on the answer this card owes. #757 and #1053 to #1057 (work order 5360 to 5410) build a component tree, palette, property inspector, source-backed layout editing and callback generation over today ui.* constructors. D-ONCE-UITREE1=C defers the UI-tree spelling to this card, and card #1736 marks that spelling unbuilt and points here. If this card later ratifies a different canonical architecture, every one of those six is rewritten. This card had no work order at all, so nothing scheduled it. Raise its ballot before the RAD family starts.

cards.title: Benchmark agent codegen quality on Jet (strict-typing hypothesis)
cards.body: Video-mining evidence (Elm retrospective, 2026-08-06): untested hypothesis that rigid typed languages yield better AI-generated code; an experienced commenter counters that typed declarative architectures mostly reduce how much codegen is needed. Jet bets on typed diagnostics helping agents but has no measurement. Run an internal benchmark: agent codegen success rate on Jet example tasks vs a control language, measuring compile-first-try, diagnostic-guided repair rounds, and semantic correctness. Internal instrumentation only; no product claim before data.
cards.plan:
1. Define the harness: a task set drawn from examples/features (representative feature slices, not synthetic toy problems), a control language (a mainstream dynamically-typed or weakly-diagnostic language for comparison), and metrics: compile-first-try rate, diagnostic-guided repair rounds needed to reach a green build, and semantic correctness against each task's expected output.
2. Run the harness with an agent generating code for each task in Jet and in the control language, capturing raw pass/fail, repair-round counts, and diagnostic text seen.
3. Write results to docs/research/agent-codegen-benchmark-<date>.md with the raw data table alongside the summary. Internal instrumentation only: no product or marketing claim is adopted without citing this measurement.

log.text: Timeline audit 2026-08-10: sequenced behind #1165 so this measurement rides the corpus harness instead of building a second one. Step 1 of this plan defines its own harness: a task set drawn from examples/features, a control language, and metrics. Cards #1165 to #1172 already build a frozen corpus from real agent work with Bash, Python and Node baselines, and #1165 plan states the corpus is not another test runner or benchmark framework when existing harnesses suffice. Siblings #1874, #1876 and #1880 each repeat that rule. The research question here is different and worth answering: codegen success rate, repair rounds, semantic correctness. Answer it with the corpus task set, the corpus runner and the corpus baselines, and write the result beside the corpus report rather than to a private harness. This card had no work order and no milestone, so it could be picked before the corpus existed.

cards.title: scope.guard is dropped: the cleanup closure never runs
cards.body: A scope.guard binding lowers to a bare unit, so its cleanup never runs. Generated Rust for examples/features/errors/must_use.jet shows 'let user__g: _ = ();' where the jet_scope_guard call should be. Reproduces at 9f2f9f2a1, before any carrier work, so it is not a regression from card #1527. Two golden examples fail on it: errors/must_use and io/scope_guard.
cards.plan:
Root cause confirmed by instrumenting and dumping generated Rust for examples/features/errors/must_use.jet (reverted after diagnosis — no debug code left in tree): the D-VERDICT-1308-1 implicit immutable-binding const-fold (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs:687, `evaluate_owned_with_imports_opts_collecting`) tries to comptime-evaluate every `::` binding's initializer, including `scope.guard(() => {...})`. That call routes through `Comptime::TirBridge::eval_expr` (crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/TirBridge.rs:99) into jet-codegen's TIR-eval interpreter (installed by `install_comptime_bridge`, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:2169), which lowers the AST call to TIR and evaluates `TExprKind::CoreClosureCall { kind: TCoreClosureKind::Guard { executable, .. } }` at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs:5094-5099. That handler pushes the guard's executable lambda onto `self.scope_guards` — correct for real program execution, where a block's guard_mark/drain machinery (eval/mod.rs:1488-1508) runs cleanup LIFO at scope exit — and returns `Ok(CtValue::Unit)` as a placeholder, since ScopeGuard has no literal CtValue form.

That placeholder is harmless during real execution (the guard is tracked procedurally). It is wrong when the same evaluator is reused, one-shot, purely to PROBE whether a binding can fold: there is no owning scope to drain `self.scope_guards` from, so the registered executable is discarded and the caller only sees `Ok(CtValue::Unit)`.

The actual defect is in the fold-acceptance gate: `ct_value_fits_binding` (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs:169-189) has no arm rejecting a `CtValue::Unit` result against a non-Unit declared type; its catch-all `_ => true` (line 187) wrongly accepts the placeholder as 'fits' a ScopeGuard-typed binding. So `b.ct = Some(CtValue::Unit)` gets recorded, and codegen serializes the folded literal `()` instead of emitting the real `jet_scope_guard(closure)` call (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs ~4959-4961 — confirmed correct in isolation, never reached because the fold wins first). The guard is never constructed, so its Drop (JetScopeGuard in Prelude/Core/RuntimeControl.rs) never runs, so cleanup never fires. Confirmed empirically: generated Rust for must_use.jet is exactly `let user__g: _ = ();` (the `_` type annotation is intentional/correct per D-DEFER1 — ScopeGuard is generic over its closure type; only the RHS is wrong).

Because this is a shared sema fact (I3: all checking lives in sema), the wrong fold propagates to every downstream tier that consumes `b.ct`/TIR alike — AOT rustc emit, the Cranelift JIT (`jet run`/`jet dev`), and interpreter deopt all inherit the same wrong literal. Fix once at the shared gate, then prove the guard fires on all three (I9).

Fix location (root cause, one shared gate, not a per-call-site patch): add a match arm in `ct_value_fits_binding` (bindings.rs, before the `_ => true` catch-all at line 187) rejecting `(CtValue::Unit, ty)` unless `ty` is itself `Type::Named("Unit")` — a folded Unit only fits a Unit-typed binding. This leaves the interpreter's real-execution semantics untouched (they are already correct) and needs no parallel 'closure-taking core call' exclusion list in bindings.rs.

Related discovery, not required for this card but worth a grep before closing: `TCoreClosureKind::OnCommit`/`OnRollback` (eval/exprs.rs:5100-5117) have the identical push-then-`Ok(CtValue::Unit)` shape. If any live example binds a transaction hook with `::` (immutable) instead of `:=`, it would have the same latent bug — confirm none does, or file a follow-up card.

cards.title: core.tls ciphersuites/tlsversion: native TLS-bridge extension
cards.body: D-CORESURF-SMALL1 (ratified) explicitly defers 2 of core.tls's ledger rows — ciphersuites and tlsversion (the negotiated values, not the with_version_bounds request) — as real gaps needing a native TLS-bridge change, out of scope for that ballot. Extend the JetTLSPeerSnapshot handoff to expose the negotiated cipher suite and protocol version on TLSPeerIdentity, with full AOT/JIT/interpreter parity (I9), example + golden. Then mark docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json's gap.network.ciphersuites / gap.network.tlsversion rows resolved and update docs/reference/core-library.md's core.tls note.
cards.plan:
Extend the native TLS bridge so TLSPeerIdentity exposes the negotiated cipher suite and protocol version. D-CORESURF-SMALL1 (ratified) names both as real gaps deferred to this card. No new syntax, no new dependency, no ballot needed.

Surface: stream.peer_identity().cipher_suite -> String (for example TLS13_AES_128_GCM_SHA256); stream.peer_identity().tls_version -> TLSVersion (the existing enum: .Tls12 / .Tls13).

Steps:
1. crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/NetTls.rs: widen JetTLSPeerSnapshot from 8 to 10 elements, appending the cipher suite name (String) and the negotiated version (i64, the same coding with_version_bounds already uses). In jet_net_tls_peer_identity_impl read conn.negotiated_cipher_suite() and conn.protocol_version(); both are present after a finished handshake; map an absent value to an Err exactly like the existing missing-chain case.
2. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/NetHTTP.rs: update the mirrored JetTLSPeerSnapshot alias and jet_net_tls_peer_identity_from_snapshot so JetTLSPeerIdentity carries the two new fields. The tuple widening makes the compiler flag every remaining construction and destructuring site; fix each one. All tiers share this one Prelude path (I9); no engine re-encodes anything.
3. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs: in core_struct_field add cipher_suite -> String and tls_version -> Named TLSVersion to the TLSPeerIdentity arm.
4. Docs: extend the stream.peer_identity() row in docs/reference/core-library.md and rewrite the ledger-declined note in the core.tls section so ciphersuites and tlsversion are shipped, not gaps. In docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json give gap.network.ciphersuites and gap.network.tlsversion the shipped jetSpelling and a winning verdict, copying the shape of an already-resolved gap row.
5. Proof: extend core_tls_expert_config_peer_identity_and_directional_close_are_real in tests/corelib.rs. Pin .Tls13 version bounds in the fixture, print both new fields, assert tls_version is Tls13 and cipher_suite starts with TLS13_ (the exact suite can vary with rustls defaults, so assert the prefix). Add the same two prints to the localhost TLS harness in tests/dev.rs to prove the default jet run tier returns the same values through the same Prelude symbol.

cards.title: release_gates.rs pre-existing failures: canon.jet E0999 marker brackets, E0328 explain gap
cards.body:
Found while proving CI test-shard coverage for #211 (2026-08-06, commit
b0ad4e932): tests/release_gates.rs has 2 pre-existing failures unrelated to
CI sharding, on unmodified master HEAD (cargo test -p jet --test
release_gates):

1) canon_compiles_and_runs: examples/canon.jet:121 uses `#[Doc("port to
   listen on")] port: Int = 3000` — bracketed single-marker form, rejected by
   the ratified E0999 single-marker-bracket rule ("one marker stays bare,
   brackets group two or more"). Card #1331 (done) fixed this same pattern
   for semindex dossier fixtures; examples/canon.jet was apparently missed,
   or regressed after #1331 closed. Fix: `#Doc("port to listen on") port:
   Int = 3000`.

2) ga_every_diagnostic_has_explain: the M17 GA gate scans docs/spec/
   diagnostics.md for codes lacking a `jet explain` entry and flags E0328.
   diagnostics.md:301 marks E0328 `~~retired by D-IFDIST1=A~~` (strikethrough)
   — either the scan should skip retired codes and doesn't, or a retired
   code legitimately needs to stay explainable for old error logs and its
   explain entry was dropped. Needs a decision, not a blind fix.

Repro: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet --test release_gates
cards.plan:
Two independent fixes. No owner decision is needed; both follow existing law and precedent.

Fix 1 - canon.jet marker brackets. examples/canon.jet:121 spells #[Doc("port to listen on")] around one marker. The ratified E0999 rule says one marker stays bare; brackets group two or more. Change it to #Doc("port to listen on"). This is the same fix #1331 applied to the semindex fixtures.

Fix 2 - the E0328 explain-gate failure is a Markdown escaping bug, not a policy question. Explain::index() in crates/jet-cli/src/Explain.rs keeps only registry rows that split into exactly 3 cells, and split_cells already honors \| escapes. The E0328 row (docs/spec/diagnostics.md:301) contains raw pipes inside backticks, so it splits into more than 3 cells, the row is dropped, and E0328 never enters the explain index. Every other retired code stays in the index and passes the gate, so retired codes staying explainable is the established behavior (I4, old error logs). Fix: escape the in-cell pipes in that one row as \|. Do not change the gate scan or Explain.rs.

Proof: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet --test release_gates goes green; jet explain E0328 prints the retired notice; a grep shows no other registry row with an unescaped in-cell pipe.

log.text: The blocker chain under criterion 5 is finished on branch bd3/reader (worktree .claude/worktrees/reader), HEAD 54fef177c, still unmerged. cargo test -p jet --test release_gates is now 16 of 16, canon_compiles_and_runs included. Two gaps had to be closed to get there: Reader/Cursor handle ops in the canonical TIR evaluator (#1602) and typed codec decode in the same evaluator (#1605). examples/canon.jet prints byte-identical output under default jet run, under jet run --release, and against tests/fixtures/canon/expected.out. One stale fixture line, 'fanout: 3 6 9', left behind when dffe457b8 removed the S75 fan-out operator, was deleted on the same branch. A separate pre-existing divergence found on the way is card #1607: json/toml/yaml parse errors word differently on the two tiers because each tier runs its own parser.

The Reader/Cursor blocker on #1602 is implemented on branch bd3/reader (worktree .claude/worktrees/reader), commit 382de4645, and left unmerged. release_gates now runs 15 of 16 green; canon_compiles_and_runs still fails, but only on a third pre-existing gap that the Reader/Cursor fix uncovered: 'jet run' rejects json.decode_traced at examples/canon.jet:161 with E0956. That is card #1605. Under 'jet run --release' examples/canon.jet now matches tests/fixtures/canon/expected.out byte for byte, after one stale fixture line ('fanout: 3 6 9', left behind when dffe457b8 removed the S75 fan-out operator) was deleted on the same branch.

Fixed both diagnosed defects: examples/canon.jet's bracketed #[Doc(...)] moved to bare #Doc(...) per E0999 (criterion #1's marker-fix half); docs/spec/diagnostics.md:301 E0328 row's in-cell pipes escaped as \| so ga_every_diagnostic_has_explain passes (criteria #2-4 met). Fixing the marker bracket let canon_compiles_and_runs proceed further and hit a THIRD, previously-masked pre-existing failure: examples/canon.jet:130 Reader.over(packet) fails E0956 under quick-run (default jet run) — the shared ambient evaluator has ALL Reader/Cursor handle ops stubbed unsupported (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs:856-874), not a narrow gap. Also found and fixed 3 more masked failures in the same file: edition_too_new, no_edition_field_is_accepted, supported_edition_is_accepted all built their test manifests with the retired payload:{...} wrapper (D-CONF-NAME1 retired it) — moved to bare name:/version:/edition:, all 3 now pass. Remaining blocker: canon_compiles_and_runs (criterion #1) and full release_gates green (criterion #5) are blocked on the Reader/Cursor quick-run gap, which is substantial implementation work (10 handle ops, stateful byte-cursor value, endian decoding, D-PARSESTR1 pattern-match integration) — logged as new card #1602, out of scope for this test-health closeout. Leaving criteria #1 and #5 open pending #1602.

cards.title: canon.jet: Reader/Cursor handle ops unsupported in quick-run (jet run)
cards.body: Found while closing #1597 (release_gates.rs test-health). Fixing that card's original 2 bugs (E0999 marker brackets in canon.jet, E0328 explain-gate escaping) let canon_compiles_and_runs proceed further and hit a THIRD, previously-masked pre-existing failure: 'jet run examples/canon.jet' (the default quick-run/JIT tier) fails with E0956 'handle ReaderOver isn't supported in Jet's quick-run mode yet' at examples/canon.jet:130, Reader.over(packet). This is not a narrow gap: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs stubs ALL Reader/Cursor handle ops as unsupported() in the shared deopt/interpreter ambient evaluator — ReaderOver, ReaderReadU8, ReaderReadU16Le/Be, ReaderReadU32Le/Be, ReaderReadU64Le/Be, ReaderTake, ReaderRemaining, ReaderAtEnd, CursorOver, CursorTakeUntil, CursorSkipWs, CursorTakePattern, ReaderTakePattern (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs:856-874). canon.jet is the flagship canonical example (I5: every feature ships an example proving the same meaning on every applicable execution tier) and its stream-parsing section (D-SHIFT1, 'the shift kernel for linear stream parsing') currently only works under AOT/full build, not the default jet run tier — an I9 gap. This is substantial implementation work (wiring a stateful byte-cursor value into the shared CtValue-based ambient evaluator, endian-aware decoding, D-PARSESTR1 pattern-match integration for CursorTakePattern/ReaderTakePattern), not a test-fixture fix, so it was left out of #1597's scope. Repro: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet --test release_gates canon_compiles_and_runs (after #1597's other 2 fixes land).

log.text: Review fixes, commits 3f830eb89 and 29a752219 on bd3/reader. R1: take_pattern's advance and miss text were written three times (AOT emit, Cranelift host, evaluator). They now live in jet-foundation/src/StreamCursor.rs beside the rest of the D-SHIFT1 kernel, with MatchScan::bin_match_consumed owning the mid-byte rule; every tier calls them and keeps only its own match engine and binding projection. The evidence gap the reviewer named is covered: tests/comptime_diff.rs::sequential_comptime_reads_advance_the_shared_reader runs two #Known reads off one reader and compares against the same code at run time. Neutering apply_ct_mutations makes it fail with comptime '7|7|3' against runtime '7|9|1', so it is not green by accident. Re-run after the refactor: release_gates 16 passed 0 failed; comptime_diff 26 passed 0 failed; corelib typed_codec_decode_matches_between_full_build_and_quick_run passed; jet-foundation 138 passed; jet-codegen prelude 2 passed. One unrelated harness bug surfaced and is fixed in the same commit: comptime_diff numbered its rustc artifacts by per-test case index, so two tests both at index 0 raced for one output path and failed as a fake I2 miscompile on '2 + 3 * 4'. [handoff] Branch bd3/reader is unmerged in worktree .claude/worktrees/reader, on top of bd3/tests. It needs an independent review and then #1605 before criterion 2 can close.

Implemented on branch bd3/reader (worktree .claude/worktrees/reader), commit 382de4645. The D-SHIFT1 kernel moved from the emitted prelude into crates/jet-foundation/src/StreamCursor.rs, which Codegen/mod.rs splices back into generated Rust verbatim. AOT, the Cranelift host, and the new interpreter adapter (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/stream.rs) now call the same functions, so no tier owns reader semantics. The pattern scans moved the same way into crates/jet-foundation/src/MatchScan.rs, replacing the JIT's private copy. Two supporting bugs surfaced and are fixed: implicit binding folding baked a stale receiver (canon.jet's stream section was wrong under AOT as well), and an expression fragment discarded the bindings it mutated. cards.title: json.decode_traced / typed codec decode unsupported in quick-run (jet run)
cards.body: Found while closing #1602 (Reader/Cursor in quick-run). With the Reader/Cursor gap fixed, 'jet run examples/canon.jet' now reaches line 161 and fails with E0956: core.encoding.json.decode_traced() is not supported in the canonical TIR evaluator. The same gap covers typed decode<T> and decode_traced<T> for json/toml/yaml/csv: the AST comptime interpreter supports them (Comptime/Methods/dispatch/eval_method.rs routes to TypedDecode::eval_typed_decode using the call's type arguments), but TExprKind::CoreCall in the TIR evaluator carries no type arguments, so apply_core_call falls through to the 'not whitelisted' arm. The evaluator already owns the pieces: eval_datatree_decode walks a DataTree into a typed value, and apply_codec_migration replays the D-MIGRATE3 plan. What is missing is the CoreCall arm that recovers the target type from the call's resolved return type (Result<T, [FieldError]> for decode, Result<DecodeResult<T>, [FieldError]> for decode_traced), plus the DecodeResult { value, migration } shape and its migrated flag. AOT is correct today. This is the last blocker for release_gates::canon_compiles_and_runs and therefore for #1597.

log.text: Review fix, commit 3f830eb89 on bd3/reader. R2: the D-MIGRATE4 version vocabulary was written twice — Codegen/Items.rs baked 'v{i}->v{i+1}' into the generated chain-walker while the evaluator rebuilt the same strings. Both now call Codegen/TIR/mod.rs::migration_shape_name and ::migration_step_name. Re-run after the refactor: release_gates 16 passed 0 failed with canon_compiles_and_runs green; comptime_diff 26 passed 0 failed; corelib typed_codec_decode_matches_between_full_build_and_quick_run passed; examples/canon.jet still byte-identical under jet run, jet run --release, and tests/fixtures/canon/expected.out. [handoff] Branch bd3/reader is unmerged and awaits the reviewer's recheck.

Targeted proof, branch bd3/reader HEAD be05f1f8f. cargo test -p jet --test release_gates: 16 passed, 0 failed (canon_compiles_and_runs green). cargo test --test comptime_diff: 25 passed, 0 failed, so the binding-folding change from #1602 still holds. cargo test --test corelib typed_codec_decode_matches_between_full_build_and_quick_run: 1 passed. examples/canon.jet is byte-identical under jet run, jet run --release, and tests/fixtures/canon/expected.out, with ~/.cache/jet cleared first. Not run: the full suite, per the scoped-proof rule.

Implemented on branch bd3/reader (worktree .claude/worktrees/reader), commit 54fef177c, on top of the Reader/Cursor work for #1602. Approach: the CoreCall arm recovers the target type from the call's resolved return type, parses with the codec's own parser through apply_core_call's existing parse arm, and decodes by running the type's generated Decode TIR — the same body AOT compiles — so the evaluator adds marshalling only. apply_codec_migration now reports the MigrationStatus of the walk, and that status is an out-param only the top-level call reads, so nested fields cannot leak into a parent's status. Parse-failure wording routes through Comptime::codec_parse_error_for_tir, the helper comptime already used. Targeted proof: new tests/corelib.rs::typed_codec_decode_matches_between_full_build_and_quick_run passes; release_gates is 16 of 16 with canon_compiles_and_runs green; examples/canon.jet is byte-identical under jet run, jet run --release, and tests/fixtures/canon/expected.out. examples/features/serde/decode_traced.jet, previously stopped at the E0956 boundary under quick-run, now runs and prints its full output. [handoff] Branch bd3/reader is unmerged and needs an independent review.

Blocking #1602 criterion 2 and #1597. Branch bd3/reader (worktree .claude/worktrees/reader, HEAD 19ea9b34e) fixes the Reader/Cursor half; build on top of it, since examples/canon.jet only reaches line 161 with that branch applied. cards.title: Marker retention for block-construct statements and expressions, and the last lexer marker names
cards.body:
Card #1456 finished the parse-path unification and the flag-shaped retention: one shared reader reads every hash-name marker, Binding keeps markers: Vec<Marker> with no derived booleans, and the two statement switch attributes share one Stmt::Switched node that carries its marker. What that pass deliberately did not change, and what this card carries:

1. Block-construct statements (#Unsafe, #Impure, #Context, #Caps, #Grant, #Transact, #Region, #Policy, #Live, #Nondeterministic, #Reactive, #Shield) keep dedicated Stmt variants. Their fields are the marker's own arguments, so the node is the construct rather than a flag derived from a marker. The same holds for #Todo, #Tainted and the open tag-prefix operator in expression position. Whether D-VERDICT-1455-1 also wants a retained Marker node on these is a design question for the owner, not a mechanical change: adding one beside the parsed arguments duplicates the same fact in two places.
2. Two marker-name references remain in the lexer, both automatic-semicolon rules rather than marker parsing: jet-lexer Scan.rs (FFI) and Terminators.rs (UnitFamily). The #1456 plan's sweep asks for all lexer marker-name knowledge to go.
3. The same plan's other sweep items are also open: the marker_sequence_leads_to_function lookahead heuristic and the function_marker_has_applicator name list, which is a shadow site table beside the registry.
cards.plan: Ballot D-MARK-BLOCK1 is ratified as option A: block-construct nodes keep their typed fields and no second marker record is stored, so nothing about the tree shape changes. The one build item from A is a registry-derived accessor that maps any block-construct node to its Policy::APPLIED_RULES row plus argument values; put it beside the existing row helper in crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs (marker_row, line 133) and make the formatter and any reflection walk call it instead of matching each Stmt variant. The rest of the card is the mechanical sweep D-MARK-REG1 already demands. Remove the marker names from the lexer at crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Scan.rs:59 (MARKER_FFI) and crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Terminators.rs:42 (MARKER_UNIT_FAMILY) by driving both automatic-semicolon rules from the registry row instead of a name literal. Make marker_sequence_leads_to_function read the registry (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/marker_groups.rs:733, called from imports_policy.rs:436, :666, :777), and delete function_marker_has_applicator (same file, line 1271) so applicator knowledge lives only on the row that crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/mod.rs:948 already reads. Delete each replaced name list in the same change; no shadow table survives. Prove it red-then-green with scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-parser --lib plus the targeted parser, formatter and snapshot tests, and run the D-MARK-REG1 name-literal scan over crates/jet-lexer and crates/jet-parser. No Core semantics change here, so I9 is unaffected: the parse tree is the same for every tier.

cards.title: json.parse reports different parse-error wording in quick-run than AOT
cards.body:
Found while closing #1605 (typed decode in quick-run). The two tiers run different JSON parsers, so a malformed document produces different text. Repro: a file with 'if json.parse("{oops") == { .Ok(v) -> print("ok") .Err(e) -> print("parse err: {e.message}") }'. Under 'jet run' it prints 'expected object key'; under 'jet run --release' it prints 'expected quoted text'. AOT parses with jet_std::parse_json in the emitted prelude; quick-run parses with Comptime/JSONInterp.rs::parse_json, reached through apply_core_call. Both walk their own error vocabulary. The same divergence reaches typed decode: json.decode of a malformed document reports the parse failure through the same message. Error text is snapshot-tested product copy, so one parser has to own it. Independent of #1605, whose targeted test avoids the parse-failure path for exactly this reason and covers decode-body errors instead, which do agree.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The third criterion pins shared wording across two JSON parsers, which keeps the second copy alive and only tests that it agrees today — the same shape as the four hand-written statistics kernels and the two schedulers. The corpus law's one-source rule says delete the second parser: one implementation in the Prelude, engines marshalling onto it, and a guard that fails if a second parser appears. Restate the fix that way before implementing.
cards.plan: I9 says one home for this behavior: the parse-error wording is product copy, and today two parsers own it per format. AOT parses JSON with jet_std parse_json in the emitted prelude; quick-run parses with crates/jet-comptime Comptime/JSONInterp.rs parse_json via apply_core_call. TOML and YAML have the same split (jet_std toml/yaml parse_to_tree versus Comptime/EncodingLite.rs). Fix the family together. Approach: move each text parser (or at minimum its complete error-message vocabulary) into a shared embedded-Prelude part that jet-comptime may reach — that means jet-foundation, since comptime may depend only on jet-foundation (I6). Codegen keeps embedding the same part; comptime calls the same function. Do NOT hand-copy strings between the two parsers: a synced copy is the drift I9 forbids. Order: (1) repro both wordings with the brief fixture under jet run and jet run --release; (2) relocate the JSON parser first, prove criteria 1-3; (3) repeat for TOML and YAML; (4) add one targeted test that feeds the same malformed document to both tiers per format and asserts identical text, including the json.decode FieldError path. Rebuild jet before smoke tests (embedded prelude). blockedBy: none.

The same two-parser split exists for TOML and YAML: AOT parses with jet_std::toml::parse_to_tree and jet_std::yaml::parse_to_tree, quick-run with Comptime/EncodingLite.rs. Fix the family together, not just JSON.

cards.title: Interpreter tier silently skips view-range bounds check (I9 gap)
cards.body:
Found while closing #1601 (diagnostic_snapshots drift). tests/ui/view_mut_bounds_interpreter.jet ('// @dev_interpreter', values := [1]; outside :: [&values[0..0], &values[2..2]]) expects E0953 ('can't view 1 items from 2 to 2 (inclusive)') under the forced interpreter tier (dev_iteration(path, false, true)) — this is a genuine out-of-bounds view (values has 1 element, index 2 is out of range). Confirmed default jet run (AOT/JIT) still correctly panics with this exact message (verified via probe). The forced interpreter path now returns RunOutcome::Ran with no error at all — it silently accepts the out-of-bounds view instead of rejecting it. Checked crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/{mod.rs,builtins.rs}: both view_bounds_diagnostic (mod.rs:211) and TBuiltinOp::ViewNew (builtins.rs:451-472) appear to implement the same bounds check the AOT Prelude uses (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs jet_view_new) — the exact interpreter code path that's skipping the check for THIS expression shape (a list literal of two view sub-expressions) wasn't pinned down; did not chase further given time budget. This is a safety-relevant I9 tier-parity gap (I1: memory-safe by default — an unchecked view bound is a wild read), not a text drift, so #1601 did NOT re-bless this fixture to '(no errors)' — it stays red pending this investigation.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Fix the skipped bounds check regardless of the ballot: silently omitting a safety check is a defect under every option. What ballot D-ONCE-TIER1 (card #1656) settles is how much of AOT's behavior the interpreter tier must match in general — I9's blanket parity versus D-VERDICT-1254-1's lower-concern carve-out. Frame the fix as restoring the safety check, not as a general parity claim for the tier.
cards.plan: Safety-relevant tier-parity gap: the forced interpreter accepts an out-of-bounds view that AOT correctly rejects with E0953. The bounds check exists in both crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs (view_bounds_diagnostic, line ~211) and eval/builtins.rs (TBuiltinOp::ViewNew, ~451-472), so the bug is a routing gap: the failing shape is a list literal whose elements are view sub-expressions (&values[0..0], &values[2..2]). Steps: (1) rebuild jet, repro with dev_iteration(path, false, true) on tests/ui/view_mut_bounds_interpreter.jet; (2) trace how the interpreter evaluates view sub-expressions inside a list literal — find the code path that constructs the view without going through ViewNew or view_bounds_diagnostic (likely an aggregate or alias evaluation path); (3) fix by routing that path through the same bounds semantics the Prelude jet_view_new (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs) defines — do not add a second check with its own wording; (4) restore tests/ui/view_mut_bounds_interpreter.stderr to its original E0953 expectation and prove cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots green. Criteria already carry the acceptance; the reviewer must confirm the fix is in the shared path, not a shape-special-case.

cards.title: tir_unsafe_and_runtime: 3 remaining failures (qualified-name cascade, Clone bound, D-FLOWTYPE1 else-branch narrowing)
cards.body: Found while closing #1600. Two separate remaining tir_unsafe_and_runtime.rs failures, deeper than originally scoped: (1) foreign_struct_construction (E0113: fn make() => Note declared but note.Note.{...} construction infers Type::Named("note.Note") — check_struct_lit's import_ns qualification (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs check_struct_lit, nominal_name = import_ns.map(|alias| format!("{alias}.{type_name}"))) disambiguates same-named structs across modules but breaks THREE downstream consumers that expect bare registry-keyed names: field_type (fixed in #1600, splits qualified names back apart before struct_owner_module lookup), return-type assignability (E0113, still broken — check_type_assignable doesn't know alias.Type equals Type), and TIR subset coverage (is_covered_struct_ty/tir_covers in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/entry.rs also expects bare names — using note.Note as a DECLARED return type annotation to dodge E0113 makes tir_covers wrongly return false, producing an ICE 'codegen reached a construct the typed IR does not cover (make)' since the AST-fallback path is retired). Root cause needs one fix, not three patches: either make check_type_assignable/is_covered_struct_ty also split-and-compare qualified names (matching the field_type fix's approach), or reconsider whether check_struct_lit should qualify the nominal name at all for the common case. Left the fixture at its ORIGINAL bare  return type (still red, E0113) to avoid shipping the ICE regression. (2) generic_struct_fns (E0277 rustc rejection): after fixing the real ownership-sigil bug (D-MEM1 struct-literal field fill/rebind from a read-only param needs ~a/~b/~s, not bare — this part IS fixed and committed), a new codegen gap surfaced: struct Stack<T> { items: [T] } derives a Rust  bound on the struct, but fn empty_stack<T>() => Stack<T> doesn't get that same bound propagated to its own generic parameter, so rustc rejects the generated  (I2). Needs the same bound-propagation fix generic struct-returning functions elsewhere presumably already have — or doesn't, if this is the first generic-struct-with-list-field-returning-function case exercised end to end.
cards.plan: Five criteria, four independent root causes, each already diagnosed in the body and logs — implement, do not re-investigate from scratch. (1) Qualified-name cascade: pick ONE mechanism and apply it at every consumer. Do not ship three local patches. Keep the fixture at its original bare return type; it must pass without dodging E0113. cards.title: corelib.rs: 49 pre-existing test failures across email/TLS/DB/codec/CBOR/XML/CSV/os fixtures
cards.body: Found while closing the bd3-tests2 batch's combined proof run (cargo test --test corelib, --no-fail-fast). Confirmed unrelated to any of this batch's 5 cards: the only corelib.rs edit this batch touched was 2 lines in decode_traced_migration_chain (card #1612, itself passing) — none of these 49 failing tests call that function or share its fixture. This is large-scale, pre-existing drift across many DIFFERENT root causes, not one bug: sampling the front-end-rejection messages shows at least value-if-without-arrow (D-SG2, 5+ occurrences: 'expected -> after the condition of a value-producing if'), retired loop-header semicolon (D-LOOP-COMMA1-family, 3+: 'this loop header uses a semicolon'), D-ENUMDOT1 bare variant patterns needing a leading dot (E0367, 5+), bare None ambiguity (E0308, 3+), plus rustc-rejection (I2) and assertion-mismatch failures in the codec/CBOR/XML/CSV/email/TLS/DB/os-interrupt families. 49 distinct #[test] functions fail; full list attached as refs. Given the scale (comparable to or larger than this whole batch's combined 5 cards) this needs its own dedicated pass, likely split into several cards by root-cause family (value-if arrow, loop-semicolon, enum-dot, and the rustc/assertion-mismatch group needing individual triage).

Every test in the captured list is assigned to exactly one child; the partition is by test-name family. This parent closes only when all four children are done and one combined run proves the suite: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test corelib green with no --no-fail-fast. If that combined run finds a new red that no child fixed (an interaction), it belongs here, not on a child.

cards.title: The environment-module selector flag still spells the retired word profile
cards.body:
Card #1526 renamed every profile meaning per the ratified one-word ruling, but the ruling's fold list assumed --env-profile and the env --profile select the same thing. They do not: --profile selected a declared composition (now --preset), while --env-profile selects one env.<name> module. One name cannot answer both, so --env-profile kept its spelling and only its prose moved off the retired word. The flag a user types still says profile. Ballot D-ENVFLAG1 attached.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): `--env-profile` is a surviving use of a retired word. Fold this rename into the retirement sweep rather than shipping a private teaching diagnostic for it: ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656) decides whether a retired spelling errors, auto-rewrites, or both, and every retirement carries the same three parts (error, rewrite, ratchet).
cards.plan: D-ENVFLAG1=A is ratified: the flag becomes --env <name>, spelling the env.<name> axis it selects, uniform on every command; --env-profile retires and teaches the replacement. Mechanical rename plus one new retirement diagnostic. Steps: (1) rename EnvProfileFlag and its parse row to Env across the six known sites (criterion 1 lists them); (2) add the retirement diagnostic row copying the E1300 --profile pattern, with snapshot; (3) sweep help text, docs, and examples for the old spelling; (4) prove with the usage tests and the new snapshot. Greenfield: delete the old spelling outright — no alias, no fallback parse. blockedBy: none.

cards.title: One flow-fact store with one join rule
cards.body: Six stores track facts that change along control flow: moved bindings, uninit fields, typestate, optional narrowing, taint and view windows. Each hand-writes its own branch merge, and two of those merges are dead code, so typestate and partial init keep whatever branch the walker saw last. Build one store keyed by binding and plane. Each plane supplies only its join rule, and the shared walker applies joins at every merge point. Sema only; nothing a user types changes. This is substrate: it lands before any per-plane card builds on it.

log.text: bd-fix-heavy: fixed 3 review findings — L0152 false positive on exhaustive else-less switches (criterion 5), CountedLoop dropping the zero-iteration path in State.rs/Taint.rs (criterion 7), and reverted a stray copy-paste that had corrupted two unrelated uninit_fixed.rs test fixtures. Combined proof: cargo test --test typestate --test taint --test uninit_fixed --test flow_facts_tiers, all green (14/23/13/9).

One flow-fact store is in: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/FlowFacts.rs holds the Plane trait, the Facts store keyed by binding and scope depth, one branch-merge rule and one loop rule. Moved, uninit, narrowing, view, binding, typestate and taint facts all live on it. The two dead joins are gone as a class: State.rs join_after is deleted and its rule is now the typestate plane's join, and UninitState::merge_paths is live. New warning L0152 reports a branch that leaves a value in two different states. Green: typestate 12, uninit_fixed 13, flow_facts_tiers 9, taint 22, pin 21, arena 10, diagnostics_coverage 11. Criterion 9 is still open: the corpus run cannot give a clean signal while the shared tree carries other sessions' unfinished codegen and runtime work, so the byte-identical check is owed once the tree is quiet. Failures in ownership, single_use and sema_soundness were each reproduced on a clean HEAD build of the same tree, so they are not from this change.

cards.title: Home the orphan facts on the one registry
cards.body: Some facts the compiler holds live outside every registry. Send-safety is a stray flag on the checker. #Track origin, view provenance and unit-scale provenance are recorded but unreadable. Failure attribution and maturity are unregistered. Each fact a user can meet becomes a typed row on the one registration table and is readable like every other fact. Prover internals stay engine-side, per the ownership wall.

Delete the stray sendable flag on LocalInfo in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema (grep sendable under crates/jet-sema/src) once send-safety reads from the registry instead. Make failure attribution readable as report.$attribution, and wire every new row through the $ read surface and reflect() (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Reflect.rs). Leave uninit tracking and exhaustiveness engine-side with no row, matching the same ownership wall, and state in docs/spec which facts are user-facing versus prover-internal. Prove tier parity (I9) with one test per tier — parser, sema, TIR, AOT, JIT/dev, comptime, REPL, web — showing the same fact value, plus one targeted test per homed row exercising $ and reflect().

cards.title: The @ fact read: one act for every registered plane
cards.body:
Reading what the compiler knows becomes one act with one mark. Severity.$range, send_report.$effects, Order.$states and Meters.$dimension answer typed values from the one registry, and $build.profile is the same act with the build as its subject. The string fallback in reflection dies, and reflect() stays as the aggregate view over the same typed facts. Comptime only: a fact is a value, it never mints a type and it never dispatches.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): the read spelling ($ vs @) is now on open ballot D-ONCE-AT1 (option D would respell $range/$build reads as @range/@build) with D-ONCE-DOLLAR1 as the companion. Implement per the ratified outcome; the mechanism is glyph-neutral.

— Ratified (2026-08-07): D-ONCE-AT1 = D — prefix @ is the compile-time mark and fact-read glyph; infix @ unchanged; $ is freed. The pending-input clause above is resolved; implement this outcome.
cards.plan: Implement the fact-read act so Severity.$range, send_report.$effects, Order.$states, Meters.$dimension, and $build.* all resolve typed values from the one registry in crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs, using the prefix glyph ratified by D-ONCE-AT1=D (prefix @, not $). Delete the "\0state:" string encoding and the reflection string fallback in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Reflect.rs, keeping reflect() as the aggregate view over the same typed facts. Reject a fact read outside comptime, a fact used in type position (S26), and any fact-driven runtime dispatch (D-FACTMODEL1) with registered diagnostics and targeted tests. Fold every fact read before codegen so AOT, jet run, and the interpreter see one already-folded program. Add a golden example under examples/features/reflection/ reading a fact from four different planes, add the Syntax.rs entry, and regenerate grammars and snapshots.

cards.title: One law voice: facts tighten, gates loosen
cards.body: Five words name the same one-way rule today: tighten, attenuate, narrow, conserve and erase. Diagnostics and docs adopt one pair. A fact tighten silently; a gate loosens it, and loosening is always written. Operation names are untouched: flow narrowing keeps its name, widening conversions keep theirs, and no user-typed spelling changes.

cards.title: Names, modules, and visibility: one tree — capstone proposal and ballot slate
cards.body:
First-principles audit of names, modules, imports, and visibility. Finding: five doors to a name, six visibility spellings, six compiler-side binding stores. Proposal: one tree — a declaration attaches, an alias points, pub fences, $ grades, and the underscores are one ladder. Proposal doc and nine D-NAME-* ballots carry the owner choices. Backend consolidation (one sema name ledger, one mangle path) rides the adopt ballot and lands as impl cards after ratification. Reworked 2026-08-07 after owner review: full surface pass, expert audit exits for zero-import, lexical-space rethink, viewer-safe formatting.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The `@` sigil's unfulfilled reservation is owned by ballot D-ONCE-AT1 (card #1656), which decides whether the promised location feature is designed, the reservation is narrowed to its ratified packaging meaning, or the reservation is published with a minting condition. Keep D-NAME-SIGIL1 clear of `@` so the two slates do not decide the same sigil.
cards.plan: All eight D-NAME ballots are ratified, so this card holds no open owner choice; it is now the recording and hand-off step, and criterion 5 is the only real work left. Seven landed as A. D-NAME-FILES1 landed as C, which keeps manual named imports and drops the auto-import half of the proposal, so no minted card may plan against ambient project files. Write one new section at the end of docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, `## The one-tree name slate (D-NAME-*, ratified 2026-08-07, card #1625)`, with one bullet per outcome, in the same shape as the say-it-once slate section already at line 5964; fold the existing 2026-08-07 FILES1 decision-log entry into that section so the outcome has one home. Then mint one implementation card per adopted ballot (TREE1, ALIAS1, FENCE1, WALK1, ROLEMOD1, REFLECT1, SIGIL1) plus one for the backend consolidation D-NAME-TREE1's technical note names: fold reference_anchors and import_targets into one sema-owned name ledger read by codegen, JIT, interpreter, LSP, REPL and devserver, one mangle function, and fix the pub(package) divergence at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Imports.rs:83. FENCE1, WALK1 and SIGIL1 change user-typeable spellings, so their cards carry the Syntax.rs entry, grammar regeneration, formatter round-trip and snapshot chores. Each minted card must state the I9 requirement: name resolution and visibility mean one thing across AOT, jet run and the interpreter, because all of them read the one ledger. This card writes no compiler code, so its own criteria 9, 11 and 12 close by naming in a log note which minted card owns each chore. FILES1=C removes work rather than adding it: record it and mint nothing for it.

cards.title: Script mode + fn run: bare statements are the entry body
cards.body: Owner-approved direction 2026-08-07: a .jet file of bare statements is a script; jet run executes them. Defined as sugar — bare statements are the body of an implicit fn run() (I8 one mechanism, I9 tier parity; substrate for notebooks and the REPL). Owner rulings baked in: imported scripts never run; bare code + explicit fn run is an error with a jet fix auto-wrap; diagnostics nudge promotion, never punish the script rung. Proposal at docs/proposals/script-mode-fn-run.md (branch worktree-agent-adaa2f8233e718056, pending integration). Two ballots carry the owner choices. Parallel D-NAME-* slate on #1625 owns the file-import spelling; not touched here.
cards.plan: Both ballots are ratified: D-ENTRY-SCRIPT1=B and D-ENTRY-ORDER1=B, so criterion 5 is the remaining work. SCRIPT1=B means the whole verb table lands now: a file of bare statements is the body of an implicit fn run, jet run runs it, jet dev hot-reloads it with the fn dev override per U19, and jet test file.jet runs the file's #Test blocks while package-level jet test keeps D-ECO-OUTPUT-DEFAULT1's plural rule. A script may hold any ordinary declaration beside its loose code; only an explicit fn run conflicts. ORDER1=B means declarations keep the existing file-wide law and loose statements run in written order as the run body, so the desugar is exactly the composition of two rules Jet already has and sema needs no new scope rule. Record both in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md as `## The script-mode slate (D-ENTRY-*, ratified 2026-08-07, card #1627)`, in the shape of the say-it-once slate section at line 5964, naming the S12 and E0003 copy amendments and the three owner rulings: imported scripts never run, bare code beside an explicit fn run is an error with a jet fix auto-wrap, and diagnostics nudge promotion rather than punish the script rung. SCRIPT1's technical note ties the import-error rule to D-NAME-FILES1, which ratified as C (manual named imports), so the minted cards write that rule against explicit use lines and never against ambient project files. Mint implementation cards covering: parser (bare statements at file level), sema (implicit entry plus the two new diagnostics, each with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot), TIR and every tier so a script means the same under AOT, jet run and the interpreter as I9 demands, an example with golden output, formatter round-trip, the jet fix wrap, and jet dev and jet test on a single file. This card writes no compiler code, so its criteria 6, 8 and 9 close by naming in a log note which minted card owns each chore.

cards.title: CoreHost stops re-implementing the core.os facts

A host_fns! declaration keeps one listing and generates the other three, about 2,300 lines less, and turns the silent mismatch into a build error.
