cards.title: core.random normal() non-deterministic on reseed -- breaks Rng reproducibility contract
cards.body:
Minimal repro (AOT jet build, no JIT involved):
use core.random as random
fn run() {
    random.seed(11)
    a :: random.normal(0.0, 1.0)
    random.seed(11)
    b :: random.normal(0.0, 1.0)
    print(a); print(b); print(a == b)
}
prints two DIFFERENT floats and false. Code inspection (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomFns.rs: jet_std_random_seed/jet_rng_next/jet_std_random_normal) shows no Box-Muller cache -- each is a pure function of the thread_local JET_RNG cell, so two identical seed()+normal() pairs SHOULD produce identical draws. The divergence means either the second random.seed(11) isn't taking effect before the second normal() runs (evaluation-order/let-binding-timing bug), or something else perturbs JET_RNG between reseed and draw. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to the #1755 JIT ?? fix -- reproduces on a clean AOT build (jet build, not jet run) with #1755's edits git-stashed out. tests/golden.rs's examples_compile_and_run already fails math/random_audit on this exact line. Needs a root-cause dive into TIR/AOT evaluation order for back-to-back core.random ambient calls, not the normal() formula itself.

log.text: Fixed by the #1788 merge (same patch, repro verified by bd19-rev on both jet run and AOT). Closing.

[review bd19-rev] Repro proven fixed by the #1788 patch on bd18/randomfold 1a6ab9988. One root cause shared with #1788: a D-VERDICT-1308-1 implicit fold of the :: initializer evaluated the call against the comptime interpreter's ambient PRNG instead of leaving it to the runtime Prelude RNG. Evidence: the same shape on master 0356941ff prints false under jet run and under the jet build binary; on the branch it prints true on jet run, jet run --release and AOT. This card carries no criteria to mark; it closes with #1788 after merge-to-master proof.

cards.title: modules/generic_modules: jet run fails E0956/E0107, computed-module $base can't run at compile time
cards.body:
Discovered while verifying JIT-parity cards #1756/#1759/#1760/#1761 (worker bd12-jitb). Pre-existing, unrelated to that JIT work — reproduces on a clean target/debug/jet build with zero code changes near modules/.

jet run examples/features/modules/generic_modules.jet fails outright:
  E0956: unbound $base can't run at compile time yet (generic_modules.jet:8, $computed_size :: $base + 1)
  E0107: nothing named $computed_size exists here (generic_modules.jet:30)

tests/jit_gaps.txt's compile_covered: section still lists modules/generic_modules, but tests/dev.rs::jit_coverage_audit's live collect_jit_coverage() no longer includes it in the actual covered set — the ledger and reality have drifted. This is the only drift found; every other stem in the committed manifest matched actual compile behavior across 6 full-corpus jit_coverage_audit runs this session.

Likely related to computed-module / pure-eval work in flight (see MEMORY note computed-modules-pure-eval-shifted-up: 'extend comptime.rs; pack.jet -> env.jet clean break'). $base looks like a computed-module reference the TIR evaluator doesn't resolve.

Repro: rm -rf ~/.cache/jet/{build,run} && target/debug/jet run examples/features/modules/generic_modules.jet
cards.plan: Fix the comptime-binding lifetime defect that kills computed generic modules. The fixture (examples/features/modules/generic_modules.jet:7) chains @base into @computed_size (spelled $ today; build in @ per D-ONCE-AT1=D — the mechanism is glyph-neutral); the ledger row is tests/jit_gaps.txt:254 and the dedicated test tolerates frontend rejection instead of proving parity (tests/dev.rs:6661; current failure is E0857 per its comment, not the filed E0956/E0107 — retarget the card text to the live failure). Fix: preserve earlier comptime bindings while registering module items at crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration/Items.rs:238, carry them through generic-module expansion (Sema/Bundle/GenericModules.rs), and resolve fragment comptime bindings during TIR lowering at Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs:653 (fallback comptime evaluation adjacent at :668).

log.text: ORCHESTRATOR CALL on the structural question, technical not owner-gated: the topic-level manifest STAYS and example module names stay unique, which is what the fix does. Moving package.jet into its own subdirectory would remove modules/fact_value_arguments from the top-level stem set, and that forces EXAMPLE_CORPUS_FLOOR and CORPUS_GATE_ROW_FLOOR down. Those two ratchets are shrink-resistant on purpose - they exist because a stem that lost its row was previously indistinguishable from a stem that changed class, and the cheapest way to green a failing check was to delete the row. Lowering a floor to accommodate a cosmetic relocation spends a real safety property for no behavioural gain, so the answer is no. Recorded here rather than raised as a ballot because it decides nothing user-visible.
Implementation is already integrated on master; corrected stale building phase to ready while orchestrator completes the remaining targeted exit-criteria proof.

criteria.text: jet run examples/features/modules/generic_modules.jet succeeds with no E0956 or E0107
criteria.evidence:
Root cause found and fixed, and the card's stated premise was refuted first. The gate ledger classified the stem frontend_rejected with E0606 'project module project.math is declared more than once' - NOT the E0956/E0107 the card names, which commit a5d9bc9cf had already fixed. That E0606 was shared VERBATIM by seven sibling stems, so it was never a generic-module defect at all: examples/features/modules/package.jet is the only topic-level manifest under examples/features, making the whole topic one package, and five files declared module math while two declared module text. Renaming them to arith, numeric, scale, doubling and banner freed the topic. Measured effect: frontend_rejected fell 46 -> 39 and compile coverage rose 444 -> 451, the seven new rows being lowlevel/layout_columnar plus modules/generic_modules, inline_module, library, module_inline_sibling, pub_file and selective_imports. The polarity is recorded because it matters: E0606 here is a TRUE refusal enforcing a ratified one-declaration law, pinned by its own duplicate_declarations_are_conflicts_even_when_skipped test, so no predicate was widened - the fixtures were violating the law.

The underlying E0956 defect that the earlier commit fixed is also recorded for the next reader: eval_comptime_items buffered folded values and stamped them only after its loop, so generic-module expansion re-entering registration with an already-folded predecessor lost @base, and @computed_size :: @base + 1 then saw it unbound. E0107 was a pure cascade of that. Values are now re-seeded and stamped immediately.

One structural question was raised and answered by the orchestrator rather than escalated, because it decides nothing user-visible: the topic-level manifest STAYS and example module names stay unique. Moving package.jet into its own subdirectory would drop modules/fact_value_arguments from the top-level stem set and force EXAMPLE_CORPUS_FLOOR and CORPUS_GATE_ROW_FLOOR down, spending two deliberately shrink-resistant safety properties for a cosmetic relocation.

cards.title: sccache: branch-safe shared compile cache for cold worktrees
cards.body: Shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR across diverged worktrees is banned (papercut pc08xq6wo: artifact clobbering, phantom errors). Persistent per-worktree caches solve warm rebuilds but every NEW worktree still pays a 15-20 min cold build. sccache caches rustc invocations keyed by inputs — safe across branches and concurrency. Add to the dev shell (env.jet) and wire jet-env to use it for fresh worktrees (RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 there), keeping plain incremental in persistent worktrees.

log.text: Owner directive: suites must be massively faster. Sol analysis at docs/research/test-suite-performance-2026-08-08.md — golden ~476 rustc calls, each rebuilding ~445KB embedded runtime optimized+ThinLTO; corelib ~153; dev batteries up to ~958 duplicate optimized builds. This card now owns fix #1: canonical cached runtime rlib. Implementation dispatched.

[settle round 2] bd15-rev's cwd bug fixed: probe uses the checkout root (baked into the nix-develop transplant as an argument); reviewer's warm-subdir repro now yields wrapper=none. Cold-build wall-clock measurement still rides the next fresh worktree.

[review bd15-rev] BLOCKED, c1 not met on two of its three clauses. 'No shared target dir anywhere' holds -- sccache is input-keyed and the CARGO_TARGET_DIR ban in jet-env is untouched; flake.nix and env.jet both gain sccache. But: (1) 'jet-env chooses the right cache mode per tree' is wrong. cache_mode_env probes tgt=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$PWD/target} (scripts/agent/jet-env:49) using the CALLER's cwd, not the repo root, while cargo resolves the target dir from the workspace root regardless of cwd. Any jet-env invocation from a subdirectory misreads a warm tree as cold. Reproduced on the warm main tree: cd crates/jet-sema; jet-env sh -c 'echo $RUSTC_WRAPPER $CARGO_INCREMENTAL' prints 'sccache 0' -- exactly the mode the card says warm trees must not get, so warm subdir builds silently lose incremental. One-word fix: $repo/target. (2) 'fresh worktree cold build measured before/after' is unmet by the evidence's own admission ('wall-clock cold-build delta accrues from the second cold worktree -- measured at next fresh worktree creation'). The recorded probe shows mode selection, not a before/after measurement. Either take the measurement or amend the criterion.

cards.title: golden RED: an immutable :: binding of a core.random call ignores random.seed (math/random_audit)
cards.body:
tests/golden.rs::examples_compile_and_run is RED on master today. Scoped repro: JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=math/random_audit cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run fails, output line 3 is false where examples/features/expected/math/random_audit.out says true. That line is print(a == b) after two identical random.seed(11) calls (examples/features/math/random_audit.jet:8-12).

Root cause is narrower than the example. An immutable :: binding whose initializer is a core.random call does not read the runtime PRNG that random.seed writes; a mutable := binding does.

Probe, same file, one run:
  random.seed(11); a := random.normal(0.0, 1.0); random.seed(11); b := random.normal(0.0, 1.0)  -> a and b both 0.14096253901337438, correct
  random.seed(11); c :: random.float();          random.seed(11); d :: random.float()            -> c=0.7399976204803688, d=0.13464645403170952, wrong, and neither value is on the seeded stream

Tier-independent: identical wrong values under default jet run, under jet run --release, and from the real AOT binary produced by jet build. So this is not an I9 parity break, it is one broken meaning in the shared path, most likely the comptime fold of a :: initializer taking the pure random dispatcher instead of the seeded runtime RNG (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomFns.rs:70-104 holds the seeded thread-local, which is correct in isolation).

Not caused by the 81be2a12e..HEAD stack: nothing in that range touches random or comptime folding, and examples/features/math/random_audit.{jet,out} last changed at 87be3d865. Filed by bd17-rev during the composed-stack review so the standing full-suite red has an owner.

Decline falls back to runtime codegen on every tier, proved above. cards.title: generic-module substitution overwrites a locally rebound name inside a template function body
cards.body:
substitute_expr (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/GenericModules/Substitution.rs:48-68) rewrites every Expr::Ident and, since #1780, every Expr::ComptimeName whose name is a key in the instantiation values map, with no regard for a binding that shadows that name inside the walked body. The template local silently loses.

Probe A, marked name:
  module box<capacity: Int> { $base :: capacity   pub fn shadowed() => Int { $base :: 5   return $base } }
  module b32 = box<32>
  run() prints 32. Expected 5.

Probe B, plain name, same shape with an unmarked local named capacity: also prints 32.

Probe B proves the hole predates #1780, so the new ComptimeName arm inherits it rather than introducing it; both are wrong the same way and should be fixed once, in substitute_expr, not per arm. The lazy fix is to shadow the key out of a locally cloned values map for the rest of the block when substitute_stmts walks a binding that rebinds that name.

No example hits this today, which is why it is silent. Found by bd17-rev while verifying #1780.

cards.title: Generic-module substitution rewrites T.{…} to a builtin head and emits a false E0119
cards.body:
Substitution.rs:198-210 (commit 0356941ff, #1787) rewrites a struct-literal head naming a type param to the substituted type's canonical name even when that type is a builtin. For T=Int the head becomes Int, and sema then reports E0119 "there's no type called `Int`" — a false statement.

Hand-written `Int.{ value }` is legal and runs: it parses as Expr::TypedLit, not Expr::StructLit. Probe: `fn run() { value :: 3   local :: Int.{ value }   print(local) }` prints 3. Inside a template, `T.{ value }` parses as a StructLit (T is a bare identifier), so substitution produces a StructLit with head `Int`, which can never be valid.

Two consequences. First, a substituted `T.{ … }` for a builtin T never means what the same text means when written by hand — a uniformity break. Second, the diagnostic lies: Int exists, it just isn't a struct. Before 0356941ff the same shape failed as "no type called T", so this is not a regression, but the new arm buys no working case and launders one wrong message into another.

tests/generics.rs::generic_modules_complete_instantiation was rewritten in the same commit to drop `local := T.{ value }` on the stated ground that the shape is law-invalid for T=Int. That ground is false. Found by bd19-rev reviewing #1787.

log.text: implemented: builtin generic T.{…} now becomes parser-equivalent Expr::TypedLit with preserved span and scalar Empty/Value body; restored complete-instantiation local := T.{ value } with ^#Marked T. Targeted proof for orchestrator: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test generics. Static proof here: git diff --check; no cargo/jet run per instruction.

cards.title: #Pre/#Post contracts trap under AOT but are silently skipped under jet run (I9)
cards.body:
Probe, no generics involved:
  #Post(result == 99, "must equal 99")
  fn get() => Int { return 1 }
  fn run() { print(get()) }

`jet build` + run the binary: `#Post contract failed: must equal 99`, exit 70. Correct.
`jet run` (default): prints 1, exit 0. The contract never runs.

Same for a contract on a module function. docs/spec says #Pre/#Post are checked in every build by default — not a debug/release split — so the JIT/interpreter tier silently dropping them is an I9 parity break: one program has two meanings.

examples/features/contracts/pre_post.jet only exercises the passing case, so the golden suite cannot see this. A failing-contract example (or a corelib test asserting the trap on both tiers) is the missing proof.

cards.title: core.time.date.today() folds the build machine's wall clock into a :: binding — same class as #1788
cards.body:
crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/CorePureParity.rs:63 answers ("core.time.date", "today") with Date::today_utc(), which reads std::time::SystemTime::now() (line 1432-1433). core.time is not in is_tier2_core_call's ambient list, so the D-VERDICT-1308-1 implicit fold of an immutable binding bakes the build date into the artifact:

  d :: date.today()   // frozen at build time, never the run date
  d := date.today()   // read at runtime

#1788 fixed exactly this shape for core.random with a guard in the TIR eval CoreCall dispatch (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs). Wall-clock reads need the same treatment, but at a different (module, method) pair, so it is not covered by that one-line guard.

Sweep the rest of the ambient surface while fixing: any CorePureParity/apply_core_call arm that reads process, machine, or clock state rather than its arguments has the same hole.

Found by bd19-rev reviewing #1788.

cards.title: Reflectable canonical name paths
cards.body: Ratified D-NAME-REFLECT1=A. Make canonical type paths available to reflection, diagnostics, hover, project output, and JSON.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-NAME-REFLECT1=A in the self-hosted compiler. Static `T.reflect().path` and runtime `value.path` show the canonical typeable path from the one name ledger, while `.name` stays the leaf. Diagnostics, hover, project output and JSON use the same spelling.

## Current state
- Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet builds the path by string concatenation, `"{registered_module.module_path}.{definition.name}"`, for structs (:1369), enums (:1431) and distinct types (:1472). Methods receive `module_path` directly (:790, :817, :1098). None of this reads the ledger.
- The ledger exists: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet:1438 `sema_name_scoped_path`, :1449 `sema_name_add_item` and :1603 `sema_name_build_facts` (MirNameFacts: modules, declarations, aliases, references).
- Runtime path: Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:1248 `.ReflectValuePath` routes to the host `jet_jit_reflect_path`, and Emit/Operations.jet builds the reflect payload. The host `jet_reflect_*` in the Prelude remains the retained boundary.
- Existing golden Examples/features/comptime/reflect_paths (run.jet plus shapes.jet) expects `Point` and `shapes.Point` (expected/comptime/reflect_paths.out). Criterion 2 is met (diagnostics, hover and JSON).
- Rust history: the Rust implementation landed in 31b0c79ec and was reopened on 2026-09-15 for source-path leakage. The 2026-09-22 review found crates/jet-sema Pipeline/CheckInner.rs:169-183 still built the path from `m.display`. That path is archived.

## Changes
1. CheckProgram.jet: expose a lookup, `sema_name_declaration_path(facts, module_index, name)`, that returns the ledger's canonical path.
2. Reflection.jet: thread MirNameFacts, or a path lookup built from it, into `sema_comptime_reflection_type_info_fields` and the method, trait-contract and variant builders. Replace the concatenations at :1369, :1431 and :1472 and the `module` field values with ledger paths, and keep `.name` as the leaf.
3. JetCodegen Emit/Operations.jet: emit the same ledger path into the reflect payload so `jet_jit_reflect_path` returns it. There is no host change unless the payload field is missing.
4. Extend reflect_paths/run.jet: print `value.path` at runtime next to the static path, and add one aliased import so the path is the ledger's canonical path, not the alias spelling.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=comptime/reflect_paths cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes (AOT).
- `~/.cache/jet-luna/safe-jet.sh run Examples/features/comptime/reflect_paths/run.jet` and the same command with `run --interpret` print output identical to expected/comptime/reflect_paths.out (I9).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0. The golden runs through the self-hosted route once #218 lands.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: this is the reflection producer in JetSema plus one codegen payload field, proved by a golden and a tier run.

## Dependencies
None. #1929 is done.

cards.title: URL Path DateTime typed heads

cards.plan:
## Goal
Ratified D-BOUND-HEAD1=A: checked `URL{"…"}`, `Path{"…"}` and `DateTime{"…"}` literal heads share one hole law, are validated at compile time, and produce the same typed value on every tier. I9: the Prelude owns the crossing; AOT emit, the Cranelift JIT host and the interpreter call the same `jet_*` symbol instead of re-encoding the rule.

## Current state
- Self-hosted checker is done: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/Constructors.jet:349-351` classifies the heads, `:698-731` validates the literal text at compile time (E0155; DateTime rejects holes at `:672-673` and `:717-718`), and `:744-745` lowers to `THostCall.TypedTextInterp` (URL results type as `Url`). The Rust bootstrap mirrors it (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:1804-1824`).
- Criteria 2-3 are met. Criterion 1's dotted spelling `URL.{"…"}` is stale; E0320 requires the no-dot form (Tower log 2026-09-22). The live spelling is `URL{"…"}`.
- Witness: `Examples/features/types/typed_literal_forms.jet:27-34` (URL, Path and DateTime lines) with golden `Examples/features/expected/types/typed_literal_forms.out`; UI fixtures `tests/ui/typed_literal_datetime_hole.jet`, `typed_literal_url_port_hole.jet` and `typed_literal_url_scheme_hole.jet`.
- The tier run is still red. `tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt:109` lists `types/typed_literal_forms: AOT compile or run failed` under `aot_broken`. The interpreter previously failed with E0956 "MIR typed boundary type ID has no type row" (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs:18575`).

## Changes
1. Reproduce the AOT failure with the shipped binary: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet build Examples/features/types/typed_literal_forms.jet`. Fix it at the Rust emission leaf (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs`, the `TypedTextInterp` route) so all three heads call the Prelude `jet_*` typed-boundary constructors. Do not re-encode the rule in generated Rust.
2. Interpreter: make `MIREval.rs` resolve the `Url`/`Path`/`DateTime` type rows for the typed boundary (the path near `:18575`) through the same Prelude symbol.
3. If the Jet emitter (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit`) prints the same route differently, align it in the same patch so both emitters agree.
4. Move the stem out of `aot_broken` in `tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt` into its observed run section. Change criterion 1's text to the `URL{"…"}` spelling.

## Proof

- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/typed_literal_datetime_hole.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: E0155 is unchanged.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: the remaining work is tier parity in the retained Prelude/emission/interpreter host, proven by a three-tier golden run.

None.

cards.body: Owner ask 2026-08-10: Jet needs the equivalent of Rust's global allocator — a way to make every allocation in a program go through an allocator you name, such as a counting or capping wrapper. Jet already has scoped allocators (arenas, fixed) and freestanding profiles already declare an allocator as a typed fact (D-TARGET-ALLOC1). This card carries the ballot for how hosted programs name theirs.

Code does not change; beginners never see it; the hidden system heap stays the default; the build dossier shows which allocator shipped. Surfaces: extend the typed target/program allocator facts (crates/jet-foundation/src/TargetMachine.rs:585) and package parsing (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/Blocks.rs); install the selected or wrapped allocator through the one semantic home (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Mem.rs:572 scoped machinery is the prior art; whole-program install sits beside it, Mem.rs:64/:587); sema availability rules beside CheckerCoreLib/alloc_ptrs.rs:10; engines marshal only (crates/jet-jit/src/Memory.rs) — no engine-side allocator policy (I9). Wrapping composes with #Policy(gc), arenas (examples/features/memory/arena.jet), and the D-MEM-SENTRY1 sentries.

Root-caused + fixed both card-log items: (1) E0433 jet_std::JetTask unresolved on AOT -- collect_used_core (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Validation/CoreUsage.rs) never marked any used_core usage for the task/task.group keyword surface (no 'use core.X' import touches it, unlike every other CORELIB_KERNEL_PARTS consumer), so core_needs_embedded_runtime() stayed false and the whole jet_std module (which carries TaskGroup.rs) never got embedded. Added note_core_usage('core.concurrency::task', ...) for Stmt::TaskGroup and for MethodCall{receiver: INTERNAL_TASK_RECEIVER} in CoreUsage.rs, mirroring the existing #Shield/Live/Reactive pattern. (2) Once E0433 was gone, task.all/task.race/task.any leaked a raw Rust Result as 'Ok([1, 2])' etc: jet_std::jet_task_all/race/any (Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs) return JetOutcome<T,TaskFailure> but sema types task.all/race/any as plain [T]/T (no Result) -- a real type/codegen mismatch, present since these combinators were first implemented (same TIR node for old g.all/new task.all, not something the respell introduced). Added jet_task_outcome_unwrap() (success unwraps, failure panics fail-fast, mirrors JetTaskGroupRuntime::close_with + the interpreter's already-correct jet_task_select handling) and wired it into the 3 AOT emission sites in Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs. task_control_tiers::task_control_plane_matches_under_aot now compiles and the Ok()-wrapping is gone. Remaining red in that test is unrelated pre-existing scheduler non-determinism, tracked as new card #1860 -- not part of this card's scope.

Migration scope bigger than card body: retired 'taskgroup NAME { }' / 'NAME.task =>' / 'NAME.all|race|any([...])' spellings hit ~30 in-repo files (tests/concurrency_boundaries.rs, shared_guards.rs, tir_unsafe_and_runtime.rs, dev.rs, canvas.rs, corelib.rs, observe.rs, path_durability.rs, taskgroup_params.rs, tests/ui/*.jet, tests/fuzz/sema/**/*.jet, ~14 examples/features/concurrency/*.jet + memory/shared_guard_queue.jet, docs/spec/spec.md concurrency section, 2 docs/research files). Also found: bare 'task' keyword binds to taskgroup_stack.last() -- a function with TWO simultaneous TaskGroup params (old spawn_both test) cannot target the non-last param; ratified text is silent on multi-group-per-fn, so restructuring that one test instead of guessing new syntax.

cards.title: dev suite aborts on stack overflow in TIR lowering
cards.body: With the parser OOM fixed, tests/dev.rs no longer allocates (peak RSS under 5 MB) but aborts the whole binary on stack overflow, first in array_of_structs_field_mutation_three_way and, after skipping that one, in body_only_edit_is_type_stable. Suspect: checkpoint fef006684 added prepare_interrupt_callback_locals at the top of lower_stmts (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs:445), so every nested statement list re-walks its whole subtree while lowering is already deep. That roughly doubles peak lowering stack, which the default 2 MiB test thread cannot absorb. Hoist the interrupt-callback scan to one pass per function instead of one per statement list.
cards.plan: The root cause is named: checkpoint fef006684 added prepare_interrupt_callback_locals at the top of lower_stmts in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs:445, so every nested statement list re-walks its whole subtree during lowering, roughly doubling peak stack depth. Move that interrupt-callback scan out of lower_stmts so it runs once per function instead of once per statement list — likely hoisted to the function-lowering entry point that calls lower_stmts. Do not raise the test thread's stack size or skip/shrink the failing tests; fix the lowering algorithm itself. cards.title: Generated mailer AOT code rustc-rejected: .send() on non-mut local (E0596)
cards.body: corelib test core_email_mailer_surface_constructs_with_real_secret fails: generated email_mailer_surface.rs calls .send() on a jet_email::Mailer local not declared mut; rustc E0596 at generated line ~43789. rustc rejecting generated code is an I2 violation. log.text: Root cause: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs's is_file_handle allowlist (the set of types whose local binding forces Rust 'let mut' even when the Jet binding is immutable, because their methods take &mut self) never included Mailer. jet_email::Mailer::send (Prelude/CoreLib/Email.rs:987) takes &mut self, so 'mailer :: email.smtp(config)' emitted a bare 'let mailer = ...;' and rustc rejected '.send()' with E0596 (I2 violation). Fix: added "Mailer" to the allowlist (one line). This is the single shared TIR lowering both AOT emission and JIT read from, so no separate JIT-side fix needed (I9). scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test corelib core_email_mailer_surface_constructs_with_real_secret now passes (1 passed).

cards.title: TIR interpreter ICEs on a panic inside a task combinator branch (SOFT_EXIT unregistered diagnostic code)
cards.body: examples/features/concurrency/all_failfast.jet (task.all with a panicking branch) ICEs under default 'jet run' (tier0 interpreter, forced by task-combinator deopt): 'internal compiler error: diagnostic SOFT_EXIT has no typed row' at crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs:213, then 'a scoped thread panicked' / 'evaluator worker panicked: Any' at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:1256/2637. AOT (jet build) is CORRECT (verified byte-identical to examples/features/expected/concurrency/all_failfast.err.out, exit 70) -- this is interpreter-only, an I9 tier-parity gap plus a real I2 ICE. Root cause: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs (~line 5032, the TRequireKind::Panic/Require handler) constructs Diagnostic::error("SOFT_EXIT", ...) as a deliberate internal control-flow sentinel (caught later by 'Err(error) if error.code == "SOFT_EXIT"' at eval/mod.rs:2064 and by Source/Interpreter.rs:149 / jet-jit/src/jit/deopt.rs:310). But Diagnostic::error() (crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs:204) unconditionally looks up the code in the central Registry (crate::Registry::diagnostic, backed by Prelude/Diagnostics.jet) and panics via unwrap_or_else if not found -- and "SOFT_EXIT" is deliberately NOT a registered user-facing diagnostic code, so constructing it always panics. This path is apparently only reached when TIR-eval interprets a panic AND self.sink is set (which normal non-task panics under jet run don't hit, since simple programs run natively via the JIT and never touch this interpreter code at all) -- task combinators force an interp deopt (confirmed via '[tier0 interp (whole-program deopt)]' trace), so 'task.all{...}/task.race{...}/task.any{...} with a panicking branch under a forced interp deopt' was never reachable before the D-CONC-SPAWN1=D respell (retired taskgroup syntax didn't even parse, card #1854). Fix needs a raw/internal Diagnostic constructor that skips the registry lookup for this one deliberately-unregistered sentinel code (or register a real internal-only row), not a broad Registry change. NOT part of #1854/#1859 scope -- found while proving the migrated all_failfast.jet example; investigate whether native_cancellation/native_deadline/native_panicked_wait taskgroup_params.rs tests hit the same or a related failure (currently investigating, will follow up).

log.text: Found + fixed a sibling of the same bug: 'TASK_CANCELLED' (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs + eval/exprs.rs, 3 sites) is a second deliberately-unregistered internal sentinel diagnostic code (task-wait-point-observed-cancel), hit by tests/shared_guards.rs::cancelling_condition_wait_unregisters_and_releases_guard (task.race with a Condition.wait() loser) -- construction itself panicked via the same Diagnostic::error() registry-lookup path, but since this one isn't caught by run_checked's SOFT_EXIT special case, the panic surfaced as a genuine HANG (a scoped worker thread panicked inside std::thread::scope, and the outer .join().expect(...) then blocked/aborted rather than returning promptly) instead of a clean ICE message. Generalized the fix: Diagnostics.rs now has a shared internal_sentinel(code, what, why, span) fn skipping the registry lookup, with soft_exit() and a new task_cancelled() both built on it. Verified: examples run clean (no ICE, no hang), tests/shared_guards.rs::cancelling_condition_wait_unregisters_and_releases_guard passes in 3.94s (was hanging past 120s before).

Fixed. Root cause confirmed: Diagnostic::error() (crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs) always looked up the code in the Registry and panicked on a miss; 'SOFT_EXIT' is a deliberately unregistered internal control-flow sentinel used by the TIR interpreter (4 sites in eval/mod.rs + eval/exprs.rs) and jet-comptime (1 site in Methods/core_calls.rs) to unwind cleanly after already writing to the shared DevSink. Added Diagnostic::soft_exit(what, why, span) -- a raw constructor that skips the registry lookup -- and switched all 5 construction sites to it. Also fixed a related I9 gap: AOT's task.all/race/any print two lines on a failing branch (the branch's own rendered panic, then a combinator-level 'panic: a task panicked' from card #1854's jet_task_outcome_unwrap), but the interpreter only printed the first line. Added task_select_failure() (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs, task_select) to append the same trailing line when a branch failure already wrote to sink, leaving unrelated task_select errors (cancel/deadline propagation with no sink write yet) untouched. Verified: examples/features/concurrency/all_failfast.jet now produces byte-identical stderr on both AOT (jet build) and default jet run (tier0 interpreter, forced by the task.all deopt) matching examples/features/expected/concurrency/all_failfast.err.out exactly, exit 70 on both tiers. Previously-hanging/crashing tests unblocked: taskgroup_params::early_return_closes_group_before_caller_continues, native_cancellation/native_deadline/native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues (verifying in the combined proof run now).

cards.title: Task surface residual defects: tie-break, name collision, panic propagation
cards.body:
3 tests newly reachable after card #1854's syntax migration (previously blocked by E0003 parse errors on the retired taskgroup spelling) expose runtime gaps in how a child task's panic surfaces through task.group's auto-join and Drop-based close:

1. tests/taskgroup_params.rs::early_return_closes_group_before_caller_continues -- 'bad :: task panic("child")' inside a task.group, never explicitly joined (relies on append_taskgroup_auto_joins' compiler-inserted cancel()+join() at group-scope-exit). Expected exit code 70 (panic), got 0 -- the auto-inserted plain '.join()' returns T ? TaskFailure and its Result is silently discarded (not checked, not re-raised), so the panic never surfaces as a process exit.

2. tests/taskgroup_params.rs::native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues -- 'slow :: task slow_value(gate)' (tight 2M-iteration compute loop, no wait point) + 'ignored :: task.any { fail_after_start(gate) }' (panics almost immediately) + trailing 'slow.join()'. Expected stdout '' (process exits via panic before slow's loop finishes, ~instant). Got stdout 'settled\n' after ~6.5s -- slow's loop actually completes. Hypothesis (not fully confirmed): jet_task_outcome_unwrap (card #1854/#1862, Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs) takes the 'jet_scheduler_panic_should_unwind()' raw-panic branch instead of the immediate-process::exit(70) branch at this call site, so the panic unwinds through task.group's Drop (JetTaskGroupRuntime::close_with), which cancels+joins slow -- but slow has no wait point (D-CANCELMODEL1=C cancellation is only preemptive AT wait points), so join() blocks for the full 6.5s before the panic continues propagating. Needs verifying whether jet_scheduler_in_task()/jet_runtime_should_unwind() is misreporting 'in a task' for code running in the task.group's own (non-task) scope, or whether the real issue is that Drop-based close_with blocking on an uncancellable sibling is simply the correct-but-untested behavior and the test's EXPECTED stdout is now wrong given a tight-loop task can never be interrupted.

3. tests/taskgroup_params.rs::native_cancellation_closes_group_before_caller_continues -- also fails (assert_native_wait_exit checks exit code + stderr contains 'cancel' + a native-tier trace line); root cause not yet isolated, same family (task.group + task cancellation via external tasks.spawn().cancel() on a function containing a task.group).

None of these are the SOFT_EXIT/TASK_CANCELLED/STM-mut bugs already fixed under #1854/#1862 (verified via direct repro: 'settled' prints identically on BOTH AOT and interp tiers, so it isn't a tier-specific interpreter gap either). This is deep task-cancellation/auto-join runtime semantics, out of scope for the #1854 syntax migration itself -- flagging for dedicated investigation rather than guessing a fix under time pressure. Repro scripts used: /tmp/claude-*/scratchpad/any_cancel_repro.jet (recreate from tests/taskgroup_params.rs::native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues source if needed).
cards.plan: Three residual defects in tests/taskgroup_params.rs, all newly reachable after #1854's syntax migration unblocked them from an E0003 parse error, and all in task.group's compiler-inserted auto-join/Drop-based close (append_taskgroup_auto_joins and JetTaskGroupRuntime::close_with, referenced from Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs): (1) early_return_closes_group_before_caller_continues — the auto-inserted join()'s Result<T, TaskFailure> is discarded instead of re-raised, so a child panic never reaches process exit 70; (2) native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues — Drop-based close blocks on a sibling task with no wait point instead of the panic propagating immediately, because D-CANCELMODEL1=C cancellation only preempts at wait points; verify whether jet_scheduler_in_task()/jet_runtime_should_unwind() misclassifies this scope, or whether the test's expected stdout needs updating to match correct-but-untested Drop-blocking behavior; (3) native_cancellation_closes_group_before_caller_continues — same family, root cause not yet isolated. Fix the auto-join Result handling to always propagate a child panic, and resolve the Drop-based blocking question with a decision, not a guess. Confirmed non-tier-specific (same failure on AOT and interpreter), so fix in the shared Prelude task/scheduler code, not per-engine. Proof: all three named tests pass on every tier (I9).

Absorbed content — 1860: task.race/task.any tie-break is nondeterministic on near-simultaneous branches. 1861: the 'task' reserved keyword collides with pre-existing local variables named task. Nothing is hidden; each defect is now a discrete exit criterion below. Cards 1860 and 1861 deleted to keep the board count honest.

cards.title: Tower CLI enforces honest card counts: duplicate probe, symptom lint, open-count trend
cards.body: Owner mandate 2026-08-10: card counts must be honest and must fall. Prose law now lives in docs/agents/orchestration.md and the tower skill; this card makes the CLI enforce it so the rule does not depend on an agent remembering. Three mechanisms: a duplicate probe at mint time, a lint rule for symptom-shaped duplicates, and a visible open-count trend so inflation cannot hide.
cards.plan: Add three mechanisms to the Tower CLI (plugins/tower/tower.mjs and its test suite under node plugins/tower): (1) tower card add probes open cards for a near-duplicate title or a shared failing-test/fixture-name substring in the body, prints candidates, and requires --force to proceed anyway; (2) tower lint gains a rule flagging two or more open cards that name the same test/fixture/example path as duplicate-suspects; (3) tower status prints an open-count trend (delta over a configurable window). Also add tower card criteria <ref> --reopen with an audit-logged reason, and a lint rule flagging any criterion marked met/verified whose own evidence text disputes it, or any card whose phase is behind its criteria rows. Proof: the node plugins/tower test suite covers all three mechanisms plus the reopen command and the new lint rule, with no false-positive block on legitimately separate open cards.

cards.title: Memoize a pure function with one marker
cards.body: Jet ships the bounded Cache<K,V> collection but no way to cache a function's own results. A user who wants that today writes the store, the lookup and the save by hand inside every function, and copies it again for the next one. Jet already has the two checks this needs: the empty effect row proves a function is pure, and key types are checked for hashing at compile time. The surface itself is an owner call under I7. Ballot D-MEMO1 carries the choice; the criteria below carry the requirements.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-MEMO1=A: #Memo on a pure function — one store per function, repeat calls answered from it, default bound 128 with LRU eviction, #Memo(bound: none) unbounded, lazy Iter<T> arguments refused, name.cache() statistics. Register the marker (Syntax.rs + Prelude/Markers.jet), parse/attach beside function markers (Parser/Items/functions_params.rs:124), enforce purity via the existing is_pure fact (Sema/Purity.rs:120), hashable argument tuples via the existing checker (jet-foundation Collections.rs:73), and Iter<T> refusal; the store reuses the bounded Cache substrate (Collections.rs:1865, Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:3) — one Prelude implementation, engines marshal only (TIR/lower/builtins.rs:315 seam). Diagnostics: impure, unhashable-key, and lazy-iterator refusals each get a registered code with what/why/fix + UI snapshot (I4). Record D-MEMO1=A in syntax-decisions.md.

cards.title: An expensive computed field runs again on every read
cards.body: D-FIELDPOL1 says a computed field 'name: T => expr' is never stored, so every read runs the expression again. A field whose expression is slow therefore pays that cost on each access, and the only fix today is to store the value in a second data field by hand. Caching one is harder than caching a function: the expression reads sibling fields that can change, so a stored value can go stale. The surface is an owner call and waits on the D-MEMO1 outcome so both spellings agree.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-FIELDMEMO1=A: a marked computed field keeps its answer after the first read and drops it when any sibling the formula reads is written (nothing can go stale). Amends D-FIELDPOL1's every-read-recomputes default for marked fields only. Reuse the sibling dependency set and cycle machinery (Sema/CheckerFieldPolicy.rs:66/:147) and getter synthesis (:339); keep/invalidate policy lives in one Prelude part (beside Prelude/Core/Collections.rs cache substrate), engines adapt only (TIR/eval/exprs.rs:393 seam). Spelling: reuse the #Memo marker family from #1871 on fields (one mechanism, I8) — if sema needs a distinct row, it is the same registry family. Blocked by #1871 (shares the cache substrate and marker). Record D-FIELDMEMO1=A in syntax-decisions.md.

log.text: audit #1869: plan authored; D-FIELDMEMO1=A is ratified (packet claim of unratified was stale — board record is authoritative). Blocked by #1871 (shared cache substrate + marker family).
audit #1869: plan authored from the 2026-08-12 evidence packet (target-audit-e3/packets-infra.md); criteria hardened to the exit-criteria quality bar.

Minted from mining https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jW3PChEAWWQ. The video's stdlib module also memoizes a computed attribute (cached_property); Jet's ratified D-FIELDPOL1 recomputes a computed field on every read, so the same cost exists here. Blocked on #1871 so both spellings agree.

cards.title: Prove the agent fix loop converges: check, apply fix_edits, repeat
cards.body:
Jet ships every part of an unattended repair loop: jet check --json emits jet.report/v1, each report can carry fix_edits, and the command exits 1 while errors remain. Nothing proves the loop terminates.

The property to gate: an agent that applies every fix_edit and rechecks reaches a clean file in a bounded number of rounds, and never oscillates between two states. Bun's port relied on exactly this loop over cargo check to clear about 16,000 errors without a human.

Reuse the existing corpus harness. Do not add a benchmark framework.

cards.title: Measure agent success and context economy on Jet vs a known language
cards.body:
Baselines #1170-#1172 compare Jet against Bash, Python, and Node. All three are heavily represented in model training data, so a Jet loss cannot be separated from Jet simply being unfamiliar to the model.

The open question: does compiler strictness and diagnostic quality carry an agent through a language it has never seen? If it does, Jet's unfamiliarity is not a permanent tax and the diagnostics are the lever. If it does not, that is a product finding that belongs on the record.

Measure it on the frozen corpus tasks already defined. Do not add a runner or a scoring model.

Absorbed #1880 (c03g2e1j, "Context economy: measure tokens per unit of progress") 2026-08-19: same frozen corpus tasks, one fixed model and settings, adds-no-runner constraint — the identical runs that yield success/repair-round metrics yield the token counts; separate cards pay for expensive agent runs twice.

cards.title: Machine fixes are scraped from English prose instead of built at construction
cards.body:
Diagnostic::error() attaches a machine fix by regexing its own human fix sentence for two templates: "replace `x` with `y`" and "remove `x`". Any other phrasing yields no fix_edits and no jet fix action, however mechanical the repair.

Proved live. E0037 says "replace `println` with `print`" and jet fix applies it. E0102 says "did you mean `print`?" for a single-candidate typo the compiler already resolved, and jet fix reports no changes made. E0111 says "declare it with `var x = ...` instead" and emits nothing.

Coverage is therefore decided by copywriting, not by whether a fix is mechanical. The comment at Diagnostics.rs:164 states that human prose is never parsed back into protocol data; attach_teaching_edit does exactly that.

The edit belongs at the construction site as a typed field, next to the span the checker already holds.

Moving the edit to the raise site fixes the scrape; it does not by itself reach these two emitters. Both need to carry the typed edit through.

cards.title: The report cause chain is a hardcoded empty array
cards.body:
docs/spec/diagnostics.md documents cause as the causal report chain of jet.report/v1. Diagnostics.rs emits the literal ",\"cause\":[]" for every report, and the Diagnostic struct has no cause field at all. The chain has never carried a value.

This is the field that decides whether a large error count is workable. Bun's Zig-to-Rust port faced about 16,000 compiler errors and cleared them with agents looping on the compiler. An agent facing a cascade needs to know which reports are roots and which follow from a root; without that it fixes leaves, or fixes in an order that invalidates its own work.

Either populate it or delete it from the schema and the spec. A documented field that is always empty teaches every consumer to ignore it.

Same class as #1649 (L2901 registered with no implementation): a registered surface that cannot fire.

log.text:
Scope correction from the cannot-fire sweep (2026-08-10): three emitters hardcode the empty chain, not one.

crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/TestReport.rs, and Source/LSP/Server.rs each write "cause":[] as a string literal. Fixing only the first leaves test reports and the LSP path emitting a permanently empty chain under the same schema name.

Criterion 5's delete-instead option has the same reach: removing the field means removing it from all three.

cards.title: Unsafe ratchet: the audited-region count cannot grow unnoticed
cards.body:
Bun's Rust codebase carries about 4,000 permanent unsafe blocks. Nobody chose that number; it accumulated one justified call at a time, and Rust offered no signal while it happened.

Jet's #Unsafe("reason") is already better than Rust's bare unsafe: it carries a reason and obligations, and jet inspect unsafe reviews it. What is missing is the derivative. Nothing today notices that the count went up.

A ratchet makes accumulation a visible event rather than a discovered condition. It is cheap now and impossible to retrofit once the number is large.

Related: D-FFI-UNIFY1 keeps generated bindings safe by construction, so FFI growth must not move this number at all.

cards.title: Record the agent-optimality frame in philosophy.md
cards.body:
Jet's goal is the language any agent would choose for any task. The repository states the safety and beginner philosophy that serves human readers, and states nothing about what makes a language good to be driven by a machine.

Five quantities decide that, and Jet's existing invariants already serve four of them without saying so. Verdict fidelity is I3. Verdict latency is per-file checkability. Verdict actionability is I4. Repair determinism is I8 — one mechanism means one obvious repair, which is why agents do not thrash between four valid fixes the way they do in languages with several. Context economy has no owner yet.

Writing this down changes how future designs get argued. I8 currently reads as an aesthetic preference; it is also the property that makes Jet cheap to drive.

cards.title: The diagnostics coverage guard only ratchets one way
cards.body:
tests/diagnostics_coverage.rs blocks a newly registered code that nothing emits, with a clear failure naming it. That half works.

The other half is computed and thrown away. now_emitted collects every allowlist entry that is now emitted, and the next line reads: let _ = now_emitted. The comment beside it says to remove such codes from the list when a feature lands, and nothing checks that anyone did.

So EXPECTED_SPEC_AHEAD_OF_IMPL can only grow. An entry that was honest when written stays after the code starts firing, and the list slowly stops describing reality. Whether it is stale today cannot be answered from outside, because the guard discards the one value that would say.

cards.title: Map.add returns a wrong value on the default jet run tier (I9 silent data corruption)
cards.body:
Found by binary probing during video mining (youtu.be/7H--tn8RLSc). Map.add(k, v) must return the previous value as V? (AOT comment: 'previous value if any, then overwrite'). On the default tier the caller receives a result-arena Option HANDLE as if it were the unwrapped value, so the program computes with wrong data and no error.

Live two-case contrast (probe /tmp/jet-probe/addsem2.jet):
  m := [String: Int].{ "k": 41 }; old := m.add("k", 5); fresh := m.add("new", 9)
  jet run:            old=0   fresh=1     (arena slot ids leaking as values)
  jet run --release:  old=41  fresh=-99   (correct: old value, then None)

Root cause: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs:15396-15415 TBuiltinOp::InsertMap returns the raw map_get_opt handle ('Ok(prev)') without unwrapping through the result arena. The sibling TBuiltinOp::AddNewMap at :15417-15455 converts correctly via host.result_is_ok — InsertMap needs the same representation discipline.

Not covered by card #1755/c0casx3j collections residue: that card verified example outputs, and examples/features/collections/map_surface.jet never reads add's return value. This is silent wrong data, not a compile-coverage gap.
cards.plan: One representation conversion. Resident Map.add returns the raw result-arena handle from map_get_opt (crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs:15396, return at :15415) instead of the language-level Option<V>; AOT converts correctly with jet_outcome_of (Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs:1204). The adjacent Map.add_new lowering (:15431) already treats map_get_opt as a result-arena handle via result_is_ok — do the same conversion for Map.add: occupied key yields the previous value, vacant yields None. This is P0 silent data corruption on the default tier (probe: jet run old=0 fresh=1 vs correct old=41 fresh=None).

cards.title: Runtime panic reports ship below ratified E3001 and diverge between tiers
cards.body:
Found by binary probing during video mining (youtu.be/7H--tn8RLSc). Ratified E3001 (docs/spec/diagnostics.md:501, :1365, D-OBS1/D-OBS2) promises: 'panic: {msg}' with Jet file, line, FUNCTION NAME, SOURCE-LINE CONTEXT BOX, and (debug builds) safe local values — and explicitly names 'a bounds/key check triggered at runtime' as an E3001 case.

Live contrast (probe /tmp/jet-probe/missing.jet — m := [String: Int].{ "a": 1 }; print(m["zzz"])):
  jet run:            panic: the map has no entry for this key            (nothing else — no location at all)
  jet run --release:  panic: the map has no entry for this key
                        --> /tmp/jet-probe/missing.jet:3                  (file:line only — no function, no context box, no locals)

Three defects in one shape: (1) default tier prints no source location at all; (2) neither tier meets the ratified E3001 report shape; (3) the message omits the offending key — Python's KeyError: 'zzz' beats us on actionability for the most common runtime error a beginner hits. Related closed card #1486 fixed task-panic blocks only; the scalar/key panic path was never covered. Distinct from #1878 (compile-report cause chain).

Per I9 the report shape must render from one Prelude source, not per-engine strings.

cards.title: E0003/E0163 fix text for indexed compound assignment teaches a runtime panic
cards.body:
Found by binary probing during video mining (youtu.be/7H--tn8RLSc). The counter idiom counts[w] += 1 is rejected per ratified S17 (LHS must be a mutable binding or & parameter) — the rejection is law and stays. But the diagnostic's suggested fix is a trap:

  crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:474-477 (compound assign, emitted as E0003)
  crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/names_incdec.rs:107-111 (E0163 ++/--)
  both say: write the full update: map[key] = map[key] + 1

For the use case that triggers this error (counting/accumulating into a map), map[key] on the RHS panics at runtime when the key is absent (probe: exit 70, 'the map has no entry for this key'). The compiler's own fix text walks a beginner from a compile error into a runtime panic. The safe total spelling today is map[key] = (map.get(key) ?? 0) + 1.

Scope: correct both fix texts (and the statements.rs code choice — a compound-assign shape error reusing generic E0003 'expected X, found Y' deserves its own registered code or at least distinct what/why), update the UI snapshots. Do not relitigate S17. The missing one-lookup upsert API is the sibling feature card.

cards.title: One-lookup map upsert: the counter idiom needs a canonical surface
cards.body:
Found by binary probing during video mining (youtu.be/7H--tn8RLSc — Rust's entry API exists precisely because get-then-insert double-lookup plus NLL rejection made the common case miserable). Jet's Tier-1 value semantics dodge the borrow problem entirely, but the most common map operation in real code — count/accumulate under a key — currently has NO good spelling:

  counts[w] += 1                          -> E0003 (S17, ratified rejection; fix text is a trap, card #1885)
  counts[w] = counts[w] + 1               -> runtime panic on missing key (exit 70)
  counts[w] = (counts.get(w) ?? 0) + 1    -> works; two hash lookups; nobody's first guess
  counts.get_or_insert / upsert / update  -> E0311, method does not exist
  counts.add_new(k, v)                    -> returns Bool, not the value; still needs a second lookup

Peer field (all one-lookup, one spelling): Rust map.entry(k).or_insert(0) += 1; Zig getOrPut; Swift d[k, default: 0] += 1; Python defaultdict/setdefault; Go m[k]++. Jet is currently worst-in-class here on both ergonomics and hash-count for the #1 beginner-and-agent map idiom.

This card carries the ballot: one canonical one-lookup get-or-insert surface honoring I8 (one mechanism) and D-ONCE. Candidate shapes to work in the ballot (grounded, not exhaustive): (a) m.get_or_insert(k, default) -> value view/copy; (b) closure form m.update(k, default, v => v + 1); (c) indexing default m[k, default: 0] usable as an lvalue (would also re-open the S17 interaction deliberately). Runtime already has the primitive (JIT host jet_jit_map_increment exists at crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs:987 — currently engine-private, which is itself an I9 smell worth folding into the chosen design).

Owner gate: API name/shape (and syntax if option (c) wins). Implementation must land on all tiers with one Prelude semantic (I9).
cards.plan: Give the counter idiom one canonical one-lookup surface. Map has get/add/add_new but no upsert (Collections.rs:1203/:1973). Surface choice is API naming (not syntax): follow the ratified D-ONCE-VERB1 verb law and the D-CORE-DOCTRINE1 rubric to pick the one method shape (e.g. m.update(key, default, fn) or m.upsert(key, fn) — decide in-plan against the doctrine table, cite the rubric row in the implementation log; no owner ballot needed since no new glyph/keyword and I8 is satisfied by exactly one new method). Semantics live beside jet_map_insert in Prelude/Core.rs:981 (one home); TIR/eval/comptime/JIT marshal only (TIR/lower/builtins.rs:315, TIR/eval/builtins.rs:183, Comptime dispatch eval_method.rs:1672, jet-jit Collections.rs:988). Document in core-library.md. Coordinate: #1883's Map.add fix lands first (same JIT file).

cards.title: Foreign loop keywords get a false E0003; method-not-found lies and offers no candidates
cards.body:
Found by binary probing during video mining (youtu.be/7H--tn8RLSc). Two truthfulness defects in the errors an outsider (human or agent) hits in their first minute. D-S14-PAUSE (teaching layer paused until post-Epoch 6) promises retired/foreign forms get ORDINARY syntax errors — what ships instead is a false statement about the program:

1. 'for w in words { ... }' and 'while i < 3 { ... }' -> E0003 'this line computes a value but doesn't do anything with it / Why: only calls, bindings, assignments, and return are allowed here'. The line does not compute an unused value; for/while lex as plain identifiers since #1669 deleted KwWhile/KwFor. The two most common loop spellings on Earth produce a lie with no path to 'loop'. Fix within the pause: a truthful generic statement-start error ('expected a statement, found for ...'), NOT a teaching alias.

2. E0311 on a Map receiver: m.gett("a") -> 'gett isn't a method on this value / Why: only struct and enum values have instance methods / Fix: check the spelling of gett'. The why-text is false (a Map is neither a struct nor an enum, and it HAS ~30 methods); the fix offers no candidates although 'get' is edit-distance 1. Repair determinism for agents: one error should admit one obvious fix; today it admits a shrug.

Scope: truthful E0003 statement-start text for identifier-headed garbage; truthful E0311 why-text per receiver kind; did-you-mean candidate list (edit-distance over the receiver's real method set) in E0311's fix. UI snapshots updated. Does not unpause D-S14 teaching.

cards.title: Hardened profile: runtime-verify the #Unsafe islands and FFI edges
cards.body:
From video mining youtu.be/7H--tn8RLSc (Zig's Fil-C-inspired 'actually memory safe' compilation mode proposal) plus its strongest practitioner comment ('compile with fil-c, run your fuzzing tests in CI with it, find issues, fix, ship raw').

The lesson, reframed: Rust's static guarantee is undermined by trusted unsafe blocks and C/C++ deps; Zig's answer is whole-program runtime checks + GC at 1-6x slowdown with an ABI break, because Zig has no static safe/unsafe partition. Jet has the partition both lack: safe Jet is proven at compile time, and every trust boundary is already lexically named — #Unsafe("reason") regions (E3101-E3112), FFI edges (E0702 boundary checks, extern rust/c/cpp), with policy floors (unsafe: .Forbid), typed obligations (D-UNSAFE-OBLIG1 — currently compile-time audit records only), a GeneratedUnsafe budget metric, and jet inspect unsafe.

The gap: nothing VERIFIES the islands at runtime. A wrong #Unsafe region or a misbehaving C dep corrupts memory exactly as in Rust, and Jet offers no first-class detection profile — practitioners would have to leave the toolchain (ASAN/valgrind on the generated artifact).

The greenfield opportunity, first-class and island-scoped: a named build/test profile (e.g. jet test --profile hardened) that instruments ONLY the audited islands — raw-pointer ops inside #Unsafe get bounds/liveness/alignment checks (discharging D-UNSAFE-OBLIG1 obligations dynamically instead of trusting the assertion), FFI-visible allocations go through a quarantining allocator, foreign-call boundary contracts (E0702 type/access modes) get runtime assertions. Cost proportional to the unsafe surface — near zero for typical Jet programs — never a whole-program 1-6x tax, no GC, no ABI break for the normal profile. Neither competitor can match this cheaply: Rust lacks first-class per-region instrumentation culture; Zig lacks the static partition entirely.

Beginner pass: invisible (beginners cannot write #Unsafe). Expert pass: one profile flag; report lands in the existing audit/observability rails (jet inspect unsafe, dossier).

Owner gates, explicit: new mechanism (I8), possible profile surface addition, and the D-UNSAFE-OBLIG1 amendment (obligations checkable at runtime in the hardened profile). Ballot before any implementation. Related but distinct: c053e5jw (program allocator ballot), c0gso01s (unsafe count ratchet), c0fzojeh (specific vuln triage).
cards.plan: Implement D-HARDENED1=A and D-MEM-HARDEN1=A through the existing named profile and sentry mechanisms. Extend `jet test` to accept the same `--profile=hardened` selector as build and run. In that profile only, instrument every `#Unsafe` raw pointer operation with bounds, liveness, and alignment checks; assert every recorded static obligation at runtime; and apply the existing all-foreign-dependency fence. cards.title: View-store copy semantics: D-MEM-COPYSEM1
cards.body: Implement D-MEM-COPYSEM1=A: storing a read-only view stores a copy (same lowering as explicit ~; ViewMut stores keep the error). Retire E2307 for read views. Add: jet audit copies (per-copy site+size ledger), jet fmt --explicit-copies (invited materializer), package.jet policy key copies: .Explicit restoring the error. D-SHAPE-COPY1 untouched: ~ stays the one copy spelling. Proposal: docs/proposals/memory-one-question.md element 1. I9: all tiers, examples + goldens updated in the same change.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-MEM-COPYSEM1=A (operative wording: the memory-audit slate section at the end of syntax-decisions.md, :6683): a read-only view flowing into a non-view slot means a semantic copy, lowered exactly like explicit ~ on every tier; ViewMut stays an error; ~x remains the one explicit spelling; the audit/format/policy ladder ships with it (jet audit copies, ghost hints, jet fmt --explicit-copies, source #Policy(copies: .Explicit) and package copies: .Explicit restore refusal). Surfaces: the view-to-owned coercion + explicit-copy lowering (Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:1348/:1707), routed through bindings/fields/collections/captures (CheckerCore/bindings.rs:825, CheckerInfer/expr.rs:2580/:2817/:2879); copies policy key (Policy.rs:15, Parser imports_policy.rs:51, pkg Package/Blocks.rs:806). Reuse the ~ lowering (one Prelude copy path; engines marshal). Executable spec: examples/features/memory/copy_verb.jet extends.

log.text: audit #1869: plan authored from the 2026-08-12 evidence packet (target-audit-e3/packets-infra.md); criteria hardened to the exit-criteria quality bar.

criteria.text: Copy semantic scoped to non-view flows only; declared View<T>/ViewMut<T> boundaries unchanged; E2305/E2307 split preserved with snapshots; #Policy(copies: .Explicit) + package mirror per D-PACKAGE-POLICY-SCOPE1; I7 Syntax.rs rows; I9 proof on all tiers
criteria.evidence:
The semantics this card names had already landed in b2caf787e; verified present rather than assumed: the policy key and its package mirror, the I7 syntax row carrying D-MEM-COPYSEM1, the sema materializer with implicit_copy_target / infer_owning_value / insert_implicit_copy and owned_type_for_read_view, the MaterializeView TIR node, the full audit / ghost-hint / fmt --explicit-copies ladder, and three refusal fixtures FLIPPED to '(no errors)' with _explicit variants that restore E2307. What ratified D-MEM-COPYSEM1 requires is that a read-only view stored into a non-view slot becomes an owned copy with the same lowering as an explicit ~ on every tier, that ViewMut stays an error, that ~ remains the one spelling with nothing injected into source, and that copies: .Explicit at either scope restores the refusal.

The real remaining defect was I8 and I9 drift, and it is now closed: three engines each re-encoded the same four-arm window-type-to-Prelude-symbol ladder - AOT emit, the wasm path and the JS path - plus a fourth partial copy in lambda lowering. One table now owns the mapping, with view_copy_symbol and view_copy_owned_type, and all four sites marshal only. The mapping was transcribed arm for arm, so there is no behaviour change; the only remaining literals are the table itself and the Prelude kernels. AOT, wasm and JS all reach jet_view_copy / jet_string_view_copy in Prelude/Core/ViewCopy; the JIT path is documented identity because ViewNew already returns an owning handle; and the interpreter marshals through clone_structural_value on the owned result type.

Proof is a run, not a reading: tests/memory_semantics.rs passes 11 of 11, and it now asserts examples/features/memory/string_view.jet against its golden byte-identically across release AOT, default jet run and --interpret - previously only memory/copy_verb was covered that way. A drift guard was added asserting both Prelude kernels declare the two symbols and that no engine names one itself, so this particular duplication cannot silently return.

cards.body: Implement D-CONC-FREEZE1=A: freeze(x) prefix verb returns a deeply immutable value; bare task captures of frozen values are legal; writing to frozen is a compile error naming the freeze site. ^x in a group-child capture consumes (existing E0121 applies after). Rewrite E1101 fix menu: give it (^), freeze it (freeze), or lock it (Shared). Shared/Cell untouched. Proposal element 5. I9 parity across tiers; examples for both verbs with goldens.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-CONC-FREEZE1=A (slate wording at syntax-decisions.md:6685): freeze(x) is a prefix verb returning a deeply immutable value; bare task capture of frozen values is legal; writes through a frozen value name the freeze site; freezing twice is identity; ^x consumes into the child task (E0121 applies after); E1101's fix menu becomes give (^) / freeze / share. Surfaces: register freeze + ^ capture (Syntax.rs; parser functions_params.rs:124; capture collector Sema/Captures.rs:566); capture legality + fix menus (CheckerTaskGroup.rs:186/:252, lambdas.rs:294); moved-value enforcement reuse (CheckerOwnership.rs:4005); deep-immutability fact carried through TIR with one Prelude representation, engines marshal only. cards.title: Fault injection over effect roots: SQLite-grade failure loops as a test feature
cards.body: SQLite's reliability engine is mechanical: fail the first allocation and run, fail the second and run, until a clean pass proves every out-of-memory path; the same loop covers IO faults and out-of-order power-loss writes. It works because every syscall and allocation sits behind a swappable pointer table. Jet's typed effect roots are better seams than pointer tables and sit unused — no test-double or fault-injection surface exists (board search found zero cards). Design effect substitution in #Test: fail the nth allocation, fail the nth IO operation, deterministic schedules. The public surface is an owner call raised from this card's plan.
cards.plan: Owner ballot D-TESTFAULT1 (rev 4, 2026-08-12): recommendation A — the #Test marker gains one typed argument: #Test(faults: [Fs.Write]) names the effect roots the harness must fail. Harness owns the SQLite loop (fail each reachable call site once, re-run until no new site); the body handles injected failures on the ordinary error rail; an iteration passes when the body returns without panic and with cleanup intact (defer/sentry integration). No new glyph, no grammar change: signature stays pure contract, marker stays harness configuration. Rejected on review: nested .faults member (rev 1), effect-row question-mark suffix (rev 3 — rows never carry failure information; owner found it unreadable), test keyword (parked as a future option). Implementation after ratification: faults parameter on the #Test registry row, unknown-root teaching diagnostic + UI snapshot (I4), one Prelude harness part with engine marshalling (I9), golden example (I5).

cards.title: Panic law enforcement: Panic as a deniable effect-tree row
cards.body: Ratified D-NOPANIC1=D (owner, board UI, 2026-08-12): panic becomes a row in the effect tree that callers and manifests can deny, riding the shipped prohibition arrow (D-PROP1, E0749) and the manifest-deny precedent (D-AUTHORITY-MEM1=B). A denied function that could stop fails to compile. The proof is discharged by #1549 refinement proofs and #Pre facts. The escape exits stay honest: return a fallible result, add facts, or stay undenied. One mechanism, function-to-dependency-graph scope, zero runtime cost.

Denied scopes must prove they cannot stop: expected failure becomes T ? E; programmer-error stops move behind #Pre or refinement proof (discharge path). Surfaces: add Panic to the effect tree/names/parsing (jet-foundation Effects.rs:12/:65); project the existing reaches_panic bit (Sema/Effects.rs:600/:631 __jet_panic__ seeding) into normal transitive denial; manifest acceptance (pkg Blocks.rs:623); compiler facts exposing reaches_panic (jet-driver Driver/mod.rs:2551, Source/Compiler.rs:263); E0749 row + snapshots. cards.title: io/terminal_parity diverges between tiers: secret-read error and stream ordering differ
cards.body: From the #1648 divergence-table triage (probe 2026-08-12, target-audit-e3/divergence-triage.md). examples/features/io/terminal_parity.jet: non-PTY, default jet run prints 'secret: other error' and emits the stderr stream before the stdout result lines; release prints 'secret: non-tty' (matching the expected golden) with stderr after progress. Under a PTY both read the secret but still differ in prompt/progress ordering (release uses carriage-return progress, run uses newline-separated lines). Genuine I9 divergence: the run tier's terminal handling does not call the same Prelude terminal path AOT embeds. Expected golden says 'secret: non-tty', so the default tier is the wrong side.
cards.plan: Make io/terminal_parity byte-identical across tiers by routing the run tier onto the Prelude terminal path. Non-PTY: run prints 'secret: other error' and emits stderr before stdout result lines; release matches the golden 'secret: non-tty'. PTY: prompt/progress ordering differs (release uses carriage-return progress; run newline-separates). Locate the JIT/interpreter host's terminal/secret-read implementation (crates/jet-jit host fns for core.io terminal + Comptime ambient) and replace any re-implemented logic with marshalling into the same Prelude terminal functions AOT embeds (Prelude/CoreLib IO terminal part) — the non-tty detection and stream interleaving are Prelude policy, not host policy (I9). Re-verify on a post-#1929 binary first.

cards.title: Diagnostics: cross-language method-name suggestions
cards.body: E0311's did-you-mean covers close typos only. Live contrast (2026-08-14, playlist mining run): nums.psh(4) gets 'did you mean `push`?' but nums.append(4) — the Python habit — gets only 'check the spelling of `append`'. Python 3.15 hard-codes cross-language suggestions (array.push suggests append) because newcomers and coding agents arrive with another language's method vocabulary. Jet should map the common foreign names on known receiver types to the one Jet name: append/add/push_back/extend -> push on List, size/length/count -> len, contains_key -> has, etc. One suggestion table in the sema method-not-found path; no new mechanism. Evidence probes: /tmp/jet-probes/p2_typo.jet, p2b_close.jet. Source: Python 3.15 tour (youtube khIUGLwK-9U at 46:07) crossed with live E0311 output.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
E0311's method-not-found fix names the real Jet method when the caller used a common foreign-language name on a known Core receiver (nums.append(4)/items.add(x)/v.push_back(x) → push on List; s.length() → len on String; contains_key → has on Map), while true-typo suggestions (nums.psh(4) → push) and plain spelling fixes stay byte-identical. E1004 module-item misses additionally suggest a qualified submodule path (crypto.uuid → core.crypto.uuid.v4). All four criteria proven by UI snapshots.

## Law
- No decision dependencies — diagnostic fix-text/suggestion improvement; adds no user-typeable syntax (I7 untouched). I4 binds: E0311/E1004 keep registered what/why/fix and every changed rendering gets a blessed snapshot.

## Work
1. Trace the one suggestion path first: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs — `method_candidate` (~:45-69, builds candidate list from Collections::builtin_method_names + user methods, calls `suggest_field`) and `missing_instance_method_diagnostic` (~:90-117, builds the E0311 fix + TextEdit). `suggest_field` (edit-distance) lives in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Diagnostics.rs:867.
2. Add ONE static alias table next to `suggest_field` in Sema/Diagnostics.rs: rows of (foreign_name, receiver_family, jet_method) — at minimum: append/add/push_back/extend→push (List); size/length/count→len (List, Map, String); contains_key/has_key→has (Map); insert→push or set per receiver; get→at only where at exists. Receiver family comes from the existing `receiver_method_label` (method_calls.rs:71-81). Do NOT re-encode the table anywhere else (no engine copy, no parser copy).
3. Wire it as a fallback inside `method_candidate`/`missing_instance_method_diagnostic`: consult the alias table only when `suggest_field` returns None (preserves criterion 2 — close typos keep edit-distance behavior), and only emit an alias suggestion when the mapped Jet method is actually in the receiver's candidate list. Fix text names the real method ("did you mean `push`? `append` is the Python spelling") and keeps the `with_edit` TextEdit so agents can apply it.
4. Criterion 4 (E1004 submodule path): crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs `unknown_core_item` fallback (~:96-117). The core module item registry is CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs (one `module → &[items]` table). When `{module}.{name}` misses, scan registry keys prefixed `{module}.` (and their items) for `name`; if found, the fix names the full path, e.g. "use `core.crypto.uuid.v4`". Keep the existing plain fix when nothing matches.
5. Fixtures + snapshots: add tests/ui fixtures covering each criterion-1 receiver (nums.append(4), items.add(x), v.push_back(x), s.length()), a criterion-2 pair (nums.psh(4) unchanged; an unrelated name gets the plain spelling fix), and a criterion-4 case (crypto.uuid). Bless scoped: JET_UI_FILTER=<fixture> UPDATE_EXPECT=<fixture> (never blanket; card #2026's shrink/reason gates are live).
6. If the E0311/E1004 registered row text (Prelude/Diagnostics.jet rows) needs no change (the fix string is per-site), leave the registry alone; otherwise update the row and its explain snapshot together.

## Not building
- No new Jet syntax, keywords, or Syntax.rs entries (FOREIGN_* S14 parse-level teaching words are a sibling mechanism; this card is sema method lookup only).
- No changes to method resolution itself — only the miss diagnostic.
- No expanded-output work (#1966), no lint work (#2033), no runtime report work (#2044).

## Proof
- `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` filtered to the new fixtures (JET_UI_FILTER) — criteria 1, 2, 4 each shown by a blessed snapshot.
- Live probe: `./target/debug/jet check /tmp/jet-probes/p2_typo.jet` and a probe with nums.append(4) — before/after fix text in card evidence (criterion 1, 2).
- Criterion 3: point at the single table location in the diff (one file), and grep shows no second copy in jit/interpreter/parser (`grep -rn push_back crates/jet-jit crates/jet-comptime` stays empty for the alias table).
- Compile-time-only change: no `jet run`/`--release` parity run required (no runtime behavior changes).

## blockedBy
none — all seams live in-tree; no decision or sibling card gates this.
