cards.title: Expanded multi-line output for nested values
cards.body: print(org) and {org:Debug} render one line no matter how deep the value (probed 2026-08-14: a two-level struct/list nest prints as one 117-char line). Python 3.15 added pprint expand=True because nested one-liners are unreadable, and the Composite-pattern video leans on a hand-written tree() dump for the same reason. Jet's interpolation selector set is closed (E0914 lists :Debug, :Fixed(n), :Unit) — the spelling of an expanded form is an owner choice, ballot D-FMT-PRETTY1 on this card. Mechanism regardless of spelling: one Prelude pretty formatter (indent-nested, stable, width-independent), never per-engine (I9). Evidence probes: /tmp/jet-probes/p5_pretty.jet, p7_debugsel.jet, p6_selector.jet. Sources: Python 3.15 tour (khIUGLwK-9U at 03:59), Composite pattern (ss6je4-nDx8 at 18:33).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`{value:Pretty}` renders any nested value expanded — indented, one field/element per line, deterministic and width-independent — per ratified D-FMT-PRETTY1=A, backed by ONE Prelude formatter that `core.text.fmt.pretty(value) => String` also exposes. The probe Org/Team nest ships as an executable example with golden output proven on JIT and AOT (I5/I9); E0914's valid-set text and snapshots include `Pretty` (I4/I7); Syntax.rs row, syntax-decisions.md log entry, regenerated grammars, and re-blessed snapshots complete the surface.

## Law
- D-FMT-PRETTY1=A (ratified 2026-08-14, this card): `:Pretty` selector on the existing rail; lowers to one shared Prelude formatter; same text exposed as core.text.fmt.pretty. NOTE: not yet logged in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md (verified by search 2026-08-19) — criterion 5 writes that entry.
- D-FMT-INTERP1=A / D-QUANTITY-PRINT1 (closed selector rail: Debug/Fixed/Unit), D-ATTR4=A (`:Debug`), D-FMT-INTERP2=A (`{x=}` composes with selectors — `:Pretty` must compose too).
- I9 (one formatter in Prelude/Foundation, engines marshal), I5 (example + golden), I4 (E0914 text/snapshots), I7 (Syntax.rs row).

## Work
1. Registry row (criteria 3, 4): crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/effects_surface.rs — add `Pretty` to `InterpolationSelectorKind` (~:257) and `INTERPOLATION_SELECTORS` (~:277-296, arguments: None). E0914's producer (crates/jet-foundation/src/Generics.rs ~:502-545) already renders the valid set from this registry — confirm the wording picks up `:Pretty` and extend it if the sentence hardcodes three selectors.
2. One formatter (criterion 2): implement the expansion once in the Prelude, beside the existing fmt kernels (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Fmt.rs). Simplest single-mechanism shape: `jet_fmt_pretty` re-renders the canonical one-line Debug text (`jet_debug`/StructuralDebug record/list/map shapes, crates/jet-foundation/src/StructuralDebug.rs) into the indented form from the ballot's Option-A sample: 2 spaces per level, one field/element per line, stable across runs, no width dependence. That gives every Debug-capable type expanded output with zero per-type impls and zero engine copies. JIT/comptime reach it the way they reach EncodingBase kernels (`include!` adapters — see crates/jet-jit/src/Encoding.rs:17 and crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/core_calls.rs:117 for the pattern). Do NOT re-encode indentation logic in any engine (I9).
3. Selector plumbing: trace how `:Fixed` flows — sema typing in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs (~:2266 shows the Fixed arm), AOT emit in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen (interpolation lowering), TIR eval in Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs. Add the `Pretty` arm in each tier as a thin call to the one formatter over the value's Debug text. `{x=:Pretty}` must compose per D-FMT-INTERP2.
4. Expert function: expose `pretty` on core.text.fmt — add to CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs (`"core.text.fmt"` list ~:669) and a signature arm (fixed_sigs.rs ~:1515 region; pretty takes any Debug-capable value → String, so follow whatever seam core_call.rs uses for generic-value core calls rather than the Int/Float fixed sigs). It calls the same `jet_fmt_pretty`.

cards.title: ?? panic fallback: message and span lost on JIT, ICE on release AOT
cards.body: Live probes 2026-08-14 (builder @ 07e544bf9). Direct panic("expected the answer, got {x}") reports perfectly on JIT and AOT: interpolated message, correct span, JIT locals. But expr ?? panic("msg") degrades per tier. (1) Default jet run: message replaced by literal 'panic: panic', span collapses to line 0 pointing at the file's first line — for both core-call fallbacks (fs.read(path) ?? panic) and user Option fallbacks (maybe() ?? panic). (2) jet run --release on the user-Option form is an internal compiler error: generated Rust fails rustc with 'cannot find module or crate jet_std' (build/p15_qq_panic.rs:14266). (3) jet run --release on the core-call form is CORRECT ('panic: text read failed', right span) — proving the JIT loss is drift, not design (I9, I2, D-OBS1 Jet-line panic reports). Every example golden uses ?? panic on success paths, so this hid. Repros: /tmp/jet-probes/p15_qq_panic.jet (7 lines), p16_which_failed.jet.

cards.title: core.regex: whole-string match (full_match)
cards.body: core.regex exposes is_match/match/find/find_all/matches/split/replace (E1004 fix list, probed 2026-08-14) — all find-anywhere. There is no anchored whole-string matcher. Validation ('is this entire string a valid X?') is the single most common regex job; hand-anchoring with ^...$ is the error-prone path Python fixed by adding re.fullmatch in 3.4, and the Python 3.15 video's prefixmatch rename is the same naming-honesty lesson. Jet's names are already honest; the missing piece is the one validation verb: core.regex.full_match(pattern, text) => Bool (or Option match), same linear engine, same Prelude symbol across tiers (I9). Probe: /tmp/jet-probes/p10_regex_full.jet. Source: khIUGLwK-9U at 44:51.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
core.regex gains the anchored whole-string validation verb: module fn `core.regex.full_match(pattern: Regex, text: String) => Bool` plus compiled-handle method `rx.full_match(text) => Bool`, rejecting partial matches `is_match` accepts (`hello123` vs `[a-z]+` → is_match true, full_match false), identical on default `jet run` and `--release` AOT, implemented by one Prelude symbol, listed in E1004's core.regex item list, documented in the core-library reference.

cards.title: Map keys beyond scalars: value-semantic composite keys
cards.body: E0502 limits map keys to Int, String, Bool, Char, or a payload-free enum (probed 2026-08-14: a [String:Int] key and a [Int] key are both rejected). Keying by a pair or small struct is everyday work — caches keyed on (user, resource), grid coordinates (x, y), dedupe on tuple rows. Python users reach frozen dicts/tuples for exactly this (Python 3.15 frozendict video, khIUGLwK-9U at 01:15); Rust allows any Hash key; Go allows comparable structs. Jet's value semantics (D-MEM1/D-MEM-COPYSEM1) make deep-value hashing well-defined for immutable contents, so tuples and structs of already-hashable fields are the natural extension. Needs a design pass on which types qualify (no views, no floats by default?) — plan may raise a ballot if a new user-facing marker is wanted. Probe: /tmp/jet-probes/p8_mapkey.jet.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Tuples and structs of already-key-eligible fields work as `[K:V]` map keys with deep value-semantic equality/ordering through the one JetMap Prelude path on every tier: a tuple key `(x, y)` and a struct-of-scalars key insert, look up, overwrite, and remove correctly, golden-proven on JIT and AOT; E0502 states the ratified key rule with what/why/fix and keeps a snapshot for rejected key types; no engine re-encodes the comparison.

## Law
- D-MEM1 / D-MEM-COPYSEM1 — value semantics make deep-key equality well defined for immutable contents (card body's premise).
- E0502 is a registered diagnostic; copy changes are I4 snapshot work.
- I9 — key equality/ordering lives in one Prelude path; JIT/interpreter marshal.
- **Ballot needed: D-MAP-KEY1** — the eligible-key rule is a new user-facing type-system rule (criterion 2 literally says "E0502 names the ratified key rule"; no live decision states one). Proposed rule for the ballot: a map key is Int, String, Bool, Char, U8/IntN, a payload-free enum, or a tuple/struct whose fields are all themselves key-eligible, recursively. Float (no total order — NaN), views, Shared, functions, lists/maps/sets, and payload-carrying enums stay out.

## Work
1. Trace first: `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` `is_map_key_type` (line 66) is syntactic and already passes any `Type::Named` — before editing, probe a struct-typed key through sema and find where non-enum Named keys are actually rejected today (the "payload-free enum" narrowing is NOT in this predicate; locate it so the new rule lands in one place, not two).
2. Rule: extend the key predicate per ratified D-MAP-KEY1 — accept `Type::Tuple` when every field is eligible; accept Named structs via a checker-level recursive predicate that consults the TypeRegistry for field types (foundation's syntactic fn cannot see fields; either thread a field-resolver or add the recursive check at the two E0502 sites' shared helper). Both E0502 sites gate on it: `Sema/CheckerCore/type_assign.rs:548` and `Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:4125`.
3. E0502 copy (I4, criterion 2): new what/why/fix naming D-MAP-KEY1 at both sites; update `examples/features/collections/map_key.jet` + `examples/features/expected/collections/map_key.err.out` so the snapshot shows a still-rejected key (Float and `[Int]`) with the new copy.
4. AOT: `JetMap` is `Arc<BTreeMap<K,V>>` with `K: Ord` (`Prelude/Core.rs:1323`) — composite keys need the generated Rust tuple/struct key types to carry `Ord + PartialOrd + Eq + PartialEq`. Trace codegen struct/tuple emission derives and add them for qualifying types. Structural Ord/Eq over fields IS the one deep-value Prelude path (criterion 3; note honestly in the card log: JetMap is ordered — "hashing" is realized as Ord/Eq, there is no second hash path to keep in sync).
5. JIT: trace the jet-jit map host's key representation (currently scalar) and extend to composite keys by marshalling through the JIT's existing tuple/struct value comparison — same field order, no engine-side comparator policy (I9).
6. Interpreter/comptime: extend the CtValue map key representation the same way.
7. Golden (criterion 1): new `examples/features/collections/map_composite_key.jet` — grid map keyed by `(x, y)` tuple and cache keyed by a `struct Key { user: String, resource: String }`: insert, look up, overwrite, remove, len; add `expected/collections/map_composite_key.out`.
8. Docs: `docs/reference/core-library.md` Map key-rule section. Spec slate row is the ballot owner's job on ratification.

## Not building
- Float, view, Shared, function, list/map/set, and payload-enum keys — they stay E0502.
- Set element-rule widening (E0506 / `is_hashable_type`) — sibling scope, separate card if wanted.
- User-defined Ord/Hash hooks; Map iteration-order changes (BTreeMap order simply extends to composite keys).

## Proof
- Criterion 1: `jet run examples/features/collections/map_composite_key.jet` matches golden on default run and `--release`.
- Criterion 2: `map_key.err.out` snapshot re-blessed with rule-naming copy.
- Criterion 3: grep receipt — ordering/equality only via JetMap/BTreeMap + derived structural Ord in generated code; JIT/interpreter call their generic value-compare marshalling, no map-specific comparator tables.

cards.title: Descending sort spelling on List
cards.body: Sorted-descending is a two-statement idiom today: nums.sort(); nums.reverse() (probed 2026-08-14; sort_desc is E0311, no did-you-mean). The method-chaining video's Python example spells it sort(reverse=True) in one call; leaderboards, top-N, and recent-first listings hit this constantly. Candidates for the plan: sort_desc() / sort_by_desc(f) mirroring sort/sort_by, or a named arg. API naming only — no new syntax; pick whichever matches the existing verb table (D-ONCE-VERB1 style). Probes: /tmp/jet-probes/p11_sortdesc.jet, p12_reverse.jet. Source: VuVdN5cywcE at 04:33.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
One-call descending sort on List: `nums.sort_desc()` sorts `[3,1,2]` to `[3,2,1]` in place, and `items.sort_by_desc(f)` is the descending key-extractor twin of `sort_by` — the two-statement `sort(); reverse()` idiom retires from examples/docs, the verb table stays one-verb-per-job, golden-proven on JIT and AOT.

**Spelling decision (not owner taste — law + family precedent pick it):** `sort_desc()` / `sort_by_desc(f)`.
- stdlib-api-laws **D4** kills `sort(reverse: true)`: "Core does not use boolean or bare-string policy flags."
- A dedicated options enum (D3/D4 route) is ceremony for a two-way direction on the hottest list verb; no precedent on List's surface.
- The family already qualifies one verb with suffixes: `sort_by`, `is_sorted_by`, `replace_all`, `split_limit`, `zip_pad`, `drop_last`, `pop_first` — `_desc` is the same pattern, keeping D-ONCE-VERB1's one verb `sort`.
- `sort_by_desc` takes the **unary key-extractor form only**: the binary comparator form of `sort_by` already spells any order directly (flipping the comparator IS choosing descending); a desc-comparator variant would be self-contradictory.
No ballot: Core API naming under existing ratified law, no new syntax (I7 not triggered).

## Law
- D-ONCE-VERB1=A — one verb per job across collections (sort stays the verb; desc is a qualifier).
- stdlib-api-laws D4 — no boolean policy flags (rules out the Python spelling).
- D-CORE-EAGER1/D-ITERTOOLS1 unaffected (in-place mutators, not adapters).
- I9, I5.

## Work
1. Prelude kernels: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs` — `jet_list_sort_desc` and `jet_list_sort_by_desc` beside `jet_list_sort_by`/`jet_list_sort_by_compare` (the reversed comparison lives here once; stable sort preserved).
2. Foundation tables: `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` — `"sort_desc"` joins the in-place Unit arm (line 1039 `("push"|"insert"|"reverse"|"sort"|"clear")`); `("sort_by_desc", 1) => Some(None)` beside `sort_by` (line 1062); add `sort_by_desc` to `is_closure_method` (line 96). Grep `"sort_by"` across jet-foundation/jet-sema/jet-codegen subset tables (`TIR/subset/methods.rs`, `subset/builtin_methods.rs`) and add the twins to every ledger the siblings sit in.
3. Sema: `CheckerInfer/calls/builtin_methods.rs` — `sort_by_desc` reuses the `sort_by` unary-callback path but skips the binary-comparator detection (line 666); receiver mutability/consume rules copied from sort/sort_by.
4. Codegen: `TIR/lower/builtins.rs` — `("sort_desc", 0) => TBuiltinOp::SortDesc` beside line 397 (keep the `is_set` guard ordering in mind — Set is out of scope, so no Set arm); closure table `"sort_by_desc" => TClosureOp::SortByDesc` (line ~928 region). `TIR/emit/expressions.rs` — arms calling the Prelude kernels (beside lines 1713 and 3791). Interpreter: `TIR/eval/builtins.rs` arm beside `Sort`/`SortBy`.
5. JIT: trace the jet-jit list `sort`/`sort_by` host wiring and add the desc twins as marshalling to the same descending semantics (no engine-side comparator policy, I9).
6. Diagnostics: `sort_desc` currently dies as E0311 with no did-you-mean — once the method exists this disappears; check `method_calls.rs` near-miss hint tables for stale entries only.
7. Docs + example: `docs/reference/core-library.md` List table — one family row sort/sort_by/sort_desc/sort_by_desc; extend `examples/features/collections/lists.jet` (or `list_surface.jet`) with `nums.sort_desc()` → `[3,2,1]` and `words.sort_by_desc(w => w.length())`; re-bless goldens. Migrate any in-repo `sort(); reverse()` descending idiom to one call (greenfield).

## Not building
- `Set.sort_desc()` / Iter descending adapters — Set.sort() returns a fresh List (D-SET-DECLINE1=C) and callers can `sort_desc` that; sibling scope if ever wanted.
- Non-mutating `sorted`/`sorted_desc` variants (no `sorted` exists; not minting a second regime).
- Comparator-form `sort_by_desc` (see spelling decision).

## Proof
- Criterion 1: golden shows `[3,1,2].sort_desc()` → `[3,2,1]` in one call on default `jet run` and `--release` (I9); `sort_by_desc` key-extractor case in the same golden.

cards.title: Eager flatten/flat_map on List to match map/filter
cards.body: List adapters are eager by design — nums.filter(n => n > 2).map(n => n * 10) returns Lists, with .lazy() as the explicit one-pass opt-in (lazy_iter.jet: 'Eager adapters — no middle Iter'). But nested.flatten() and nested.flat_map(f) on a List return a one-pass Iter, so print(nested.flatten()) is E0112 'materialize it first: add .to_list()' (probed 2026-08-14). Two adapters on the same receiver follow two regimes; agents and beginners must memorize which. Either make List.flatten/flat_map eager like their siblings (lazy stays via .lazy().flatten()), or record the ratified reason where D-LOOPMAP1 teaches the split. Probe: /tmp/jet-probes/p9_flatten.jet. Source: Python 3.15 comprehension-unpacking segment (khIUGLwK-9U at 36:44).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`flatten` and `flat_map` on a concrete List return a List eagerly, exactly like their `map`/`filter` siblings — `print(nested.flatten())` works with no `.to_list()` ceremony — while `.lazy().flatten()` keeps the one-pass Iter plane; golden-proven on JIT and AOT. This closes the two-regimes-on-one-receiver trap the card documents.

**Position the plan takes:** the split is *currently* ratified — D-CORE-EAGER1=A's text says "the rest of the D-ITERTOOLS1 adapter ledger stays on `Iter`" (syntax-decisions.md ~lines 1077-1085). So the eager cutover amends ratified law and needs **one ballot (D-CORE-EAGER2)**: List `flatten`/`flat_map` join `map`/`filter` in the eager set. The plan targets eager because the argument that ratified eager map/filter applies identically here: `flatten` has no callback at all, and `flat_map`'s callback runs once per element in the same order either way — only the middle-collection cost differs, and `.lazy()` already names that opt-out. If the owner instead ratifies keep-the-split, the fallback is steps 6–7 only (record the reason where D-LOOPMAP1 teaches the split + E0112 fix copy) — that is the card's second criterion arm and needs no code.

## Law
- D-CORE-EAGER1=A / D-LOOPMAP1=B — eager adapters on concrete collections; `.lazy()` is the opt-in (the family rule this card extends).
- D-ITERTOOLS1=A — Iter receivers stay lazy; untouched.
- I9, I5; E0112 copy change is I4 snapshot work.
- **Ballot needed: D-CORE-EAGER2** (amends the "rest of the ledger stays on Iter" sentence for flatten/flat_map on concrete collections).

## Work
1. Typing: `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` `list_method_return` — `("flatten", 0)` on List returns `List(elem)` instead of `iter_ty` (line 1112); identify the second `("flatten", 0)` table at line 1241 (check its receiver — align only if it is a concrete-collection table). Sema: `CheckerInfer/calls/builtin_methods.rs` — `flat_map` refinement (line ~858) returns `List(R)` for a concrete List receiver, mirroring the eager `map` refinement at line 815 (D-LOOPMAP1 comment there is the pattern to copy).
2. `is_lazy_adapter` (foundation line 131) keeps `flatten`/`flat_map` — it governs Iter receivers; verify no List-receiver path consults it after step 1. `map`/`filter` already live this dual life — copy their receiver-sensitive wiring everywhere below.
3. Codegen: List.flatten lowers to an eager materialization (extend `TBuiltinOp::Flatten` emit with a receiver split in `TIR/emit/expressions.rs`, or mint `ListFlattenEager` — follow whichever pattern eager `map` uses); `TClosureOp::FlatMap` gets the same List-receiver eager split (`TIR/lower/builtins.rs:930`); interpreter `TIR/eval/builtins.rs:297` and the JIT flat_map/flatten hosts follow the same split. Semantics stay in the Prelude kernels; engines marshal (I9).
4. E0112 materializer hint (`Sema/Diagnostics.rs` `one_pass_materializer` region): printing `List.flatten()` no longer errors; the hint stays for genuine Iter receivers and its copy should teach "you entered the one-pass plane via .lazy()/an Iter source" (I4 snapshot).
5. Migration (greenfield): grep the in-repo .jet corpus for `.flatten().to_list()` / `.flat_map(...).to_list()` on List receivers and delete the now-redundant materializers.
6. Examples: `examples/features/collections/lazy_iter.jet` "Eager adapters — no middle Iter" section gains flatten/flat_map; `lists.jet`/`iter_adapters.jet` show `print(nested.flatten())` directly; re-bless goldens; re-run `/tmp/jet-probes/p9_flatten.jet`.
7. Docs: `docs/reference/core-library.md` adapter table rows; the D-CORE-EAGER2 slate row in syntax-decisions.md is recorded on ratification (ballot owner's job).

## Not building
- No laziness change for genuine Iter receivers (`.lazy().flatten()` stays deferred).

- No comprehension/unpacking syntax (the Python video segment motivates, not specifies).

cards.title: jet perf export: standard interop payloads
cards.body: jet perf run/view work end-to-end (probed 2026-08-14: wall sampling, terminal flamegraph, honest 'native unavailable' reasons). But jet perf export's own loss note says: 'domains present are wall/cpu/alloc/browser/tasks/locks/io/native/spans only — no pprof/otel/chrome payloads'. Python 3.15's Tachyon exports flame graphs straight into Firefox Profiler HTML, and that share-a-link flow is most of its DX pitch; Jai's ecosystem leans on Tracy. Add at least one standard payload (pprof, chrome trace-event, or speedscope) behind the existing loss-declared projection so any profiler UI opens a .jettrace. Source: khIUGLwK-9U at 23:48; sT-RfeF3Ado at 29:01.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`jet perf export` gains one genuinely standard payload: `--chrome` emits a conformant Chrome trace-event JSON (Trace Event Format, "X"/"M" events, microsecond timestamps) built from every domain present in a real `.jettrace`, so Perfetto UI / `chrome://tracing` opens it directly. The pprof/otel modes stay declared-loss Jet projections; every loss note is updated to stop claiming "no pprof/otel/chrome payloads" and to state exactly what each mode is.

## Law
- D-PERFSESSION1=D — `jet perf` family over one versioned `.jettrace` truth; `export` shares the artifact verify seam (Source/CmdPerf.rs:1-9).
- Loss-declared projection law: every export mode prints an honest `loss` note (existing pattern at CmdPerf.rs:2301-2354).
- No new user-typeable syntax (the `--chrome` flag already exists, CmdPerf.rs:2245) — no I7 decision needed.

## Work
1. Trace `Source/CmdPerf.rs` export seam: `export()` (2223), `export_chrome_projection` (2387-2455), `export_json_envelope` loss note (2311-2313). Trace the `.jettrace` content schema in `jet_foundation::JetTrace` (imported at CmdPerf.rs:11-17) and the domain readers already in this file: `first_sample`, `first_allocation`, `task_summary`, `lock_summary`, `io_summary`, `span_summary`, `content_object`/`content_array` — the flamegraph (`ascii_flame`, 1864) and timeline (`ascii_timeline`, 1877) show how sample/stack rows are traversed; reuse that traversal.
2. Make `export_chrome_projection` a conformant Trace Event Format payload:
   - Convert all `*_ns` values to microseconds (`ts`/`dur` are µs in the spec; today raw ns are emitted — a viewer shows everything 1000x too long).
   - Emit "X" (complete) events for: wall/cpu sample rows per symbol (name = Jet symbol, args = file:line), spans, task observation spans (one `tid` lane per task), io waits, lock contention; browser rows keep their existing mapping (2402-2435).
   - Emit "M" metadata events (`process_name`, `thread_name`) so lanes are labeled in Perfetto.
   - Keep top-level `traceEvents` plus the existing `kind`/`schema`/`trace_id`/`version` keys (the format ignores unknown top-level keys), and update `loss` to name only what is genuinely absent (e.g. no async flow events, no counter tracks, no screenshots).
3. Update `export_json_envelope`'s loss strings (2311, 2313): the envelope now points at `--chrome` as the standard payload instead of claiming none exists.
4. Leave `--pprof`/`--otel` as declared-loss JSON projections; tighten their loss notes only if wording drifts from reality after step 2/3. Do not attempt gzip-protobuf pprof or OTLP wire format on this card.
5. Update the E2102 usage line only if flag help wording changes (it should not — flags are unchanged).
6. Docs: update the `jet perf` reference section that quotes the export loss note (grep `docs/` for "no pprof/otel/chrome payloads") so shipped text matches the binary.

## Not building
- pprof gzip-protobuf or OTLP protobuf wire payloads (would need a protobuf encoder; the criterion needs only ONE standard payload).
- speedscope format (chrome trace-event chosen: projection already exists, Perfetto is the reference viewer).
- New flags, new capture domains, changes to `run`/`view`/`compare`/`attach`.
- `.jettrace` schema/version changes.

## Proof
- Unit tests beside the existing `mod tests` (CmdPerf.rs:2865): a synthetic trace with every domain exports events whose `ph`∈{X,M}, µs scale (a 1_500_000 ns span exports `dur` 1500), one lane per task, and a loss note that no longer contains "no pprof/otel/chrome payloads".
- Live probe on a fresh binary: `jet perf run examples/features/<any runnable>.jet`, then `jet perf export <trace>.jettrace --chrome > /tmp/t.json`; open `/tmp/t.json` in Perfetto UI (ui.perfetto.dev) and record the load succeeding (screenshot or perfetto trace_processor acceptance) as criterion-1 evidence; paste the updated loss note.
- `jet perf export <trace> --json` shows the corrected envelope loss note.
- No runtime-semantics change, so no jet run/--release parity probe is needed; full suite stays at epoch closeout.

none — export seam, flags, and trace schema all ship today; this is a projection-fidelity change inside one file plus doc text.

cards.title: User-space compile-time checks over program facts
cards.body: Jai ships a user-space 'check' module: metaprograms attach to compiler messages and enforce project rules at compile time — format-string validation, coding standards — without forking the compiler (sT-RfeF3Ado at 29:01). Jet has the read side (jet inspect compiler/gates/expand, compiler API facts, comptime) and fixed lints (jet lint), but no probed path for a package to declare its own compile-time checks over entities and fail the build with a proper diagnostic. Scope for the plan: what a project-defined check may read (the inspect fact surface), how it reports (registered diagnostic shape, I4), and where it runs (comptime, not a second lint engine — I8). Research-flavored: the plan should first survey what jet lint + comptime already reach and may conclude with a ballot or a decline.
cards.plan: 1. Define the boundary before code. #2131 owns structure-fact production, the registry, gates, and `jet inspect structure`; #1974 consumes that API. The only overlap is the typed fact carrier. Do not add a second fact plane or lint engine. 2. Extend the existing read side: `crates/jet-semindex/src/Types.rs` and `Build.rs` for definitions, references, call edges, structural nodes, and #2131 rows; `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Reflect.rs` and `mod.rs` for typed read-only access. 3. Use `Source/CmdInspect.rs` plus `CmdCompile.rs`, `CmdExpand.rs`, `CmdImpact.rs`, and `CmdDossier.rs` for query and provenance projections. 4. Stop for an owner ballot if a user-typeable check declaration or invocation is needed. Register its spelling in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs` with a decision ID, or record a decline. 5. If ratified, run checks in the existing bounded comptime path, report through the registered diagnostic system, and keep all checking in sema. 6. Prove AOT, Cranelift `jet run`/`jet dev`, interpreter/deopt, and web checking where applicable from the one front-end result; do not use `tests/jit_gaps.txt`. 7. Add one example, UI/golden output, and docs, then close with the ballot or decline record.

cards.title: JIT parity F1: TIR-subset registry short-circuit kills rows that opt out of a direct AOT symbol
cards.body: One of 13 root-cause families the #1663 census resolved the 51 observed JIT gaps into. 7 stem(s). Class: unsupported-construct (shared TIR gate, NOT jet-jit). MEMBERS: text/dates (run): lower_jit_program returned None (entry stmt 0 init outside tir_covers); text/datetime (run): lower_jit_program returned None (entry stmt 1 init outside tir_covers); text/time_calendar (run): lower_jit_program returned None (entry stmt 4 init outside tir_covers); tooling/compute_linalg (run): lower_jit_program returned None (entry stmt 1 outside tir_covers); tooling/compute_simd (run): lower_jit_program returned None (entry stmt 2 outside tir_covers); tooling/compute_tensor (run): lower_jit_program returned None (entry stmt 6 outside tir_covers); tooling/compute_autodiff (run): lower_jit_program returned None (entry stmt 35 outside tir_covers). ROOT CAUSE: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/core_calls.rs:80-83 — if let Some(row) = Syntax::core_call(module, method) { return row.coverage.contains(TIR_SUBSET) && row.has_direct_symbol(); }. has_direct_symbol() (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:542-544) is aot_direct && …, i.e. an AOT-projection fact ANDed into a TIR-subset decision. Every row built with .without_direct_aot() is therefore excluded from the TIR subset even though its coverage still advertises TIR_SUBSET. core.compute.set (foundation:889-890) and core.time.new / from_timestamp (foundation:1312-1317) are exactly those rows. Because that lookup is an early return, the intentional D-TIMEDEPTH1 admission block at subset/core_calls.rs:186-191 (core.time + new|today|parse|from_timestamp) is DEAD CODE. The pattern is already known to the file: core.time.parse_time (:45), core.ui.box (:51), core.mem.volatile_* (:58), core.encoding.xml.decode* (:66) and core.crypto.expert (:39) all sit ABOVE line 80 purely to dodge this conjunct.. BLAST RADIUS: 32 rows in the table use .without_direct_aot(); the fix may unlock more stems than these 7 (good) and may expose the NEXT out-of-subset construct in the same entries (expect follow-on gaps, not regressions).. CONFIDENCE: high — proved by reading the gate, the registry rows, and matching every offending statement index to source. Context: tests/jit_gaps.txt declares gaps 0 while jit_coverage_audit observes 51. A try_compile failure is a silent interpreter deopt, so each of these is an I9 tier-parity gap (AOT green, default jet run interpreted) rather than user-visible breakage, and per AGENTS.md I9 none may be parked in the ledger.
cards.plan: ONE FIX: Stop consulting has_direct_symbol() in the TIR-subset decision: the registry short-circuit returns row.coverage.contains(TIR_SUBSET). A row that genuinely has no TIR lowering must drop the TIR_SUBSET bit in the table instead of being filtered by an AOT-only fact. Then delete the five hand-added dodge blocks above line 80 and the now-live D-TIMEDEPTH1 block becomes redundant too (one canonical decision, per greenfield).. CODE SITE: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/core_calls.rs:80-83 (primary); crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:542-553, 889-890, 1312-1317 (data). blockedBy: none

criteria.text: The fix is the one named in the plan, applied at the single named code site rather than once per stem
criteria.evidence: One insertion point per address-minting path, and NO guard was relaxed - confirmed. The four guards (Deref, volatile_read, volatile_write, raw store) are byte-identical and each still admits only values recorded at a mint site. The deref half: the RawOf non-local fall-through minted a stack_addr from its own fresh ExplicitSlot and never inserted it into real_address_values, so the guard refused a pointer the JIT itself had just produced. The volatile-write half: TExprFromAddr returned the lowered address without inserting it. Registration is rule-based, not ad hoc: only an IntLit operand whose value survives lowering as its own word, decided by calling heap.int_from_i64 rather than restating its range, because S58 defines the pointer AS the supplied address. The fabricated stable non-zero identity for a place with no stable address is deliberately NOT registered, because that word is not an address. Note the D-MEM-SENTRY1 carve-out covers the sentry, not the missing address tracking, so this was a real gap.

MEMBERS: collections/iter_tools_audit (run): jit builtin method unsupported; collections/list_surface (run): jit optional field chain unsupported; concurrency/protocol (run): jit let __jet___arg661_0 lowering type mismatch; io/log_job (run): jit clone unsupported type: Path; lowlevel/layout_columnar (total_mass): jit for-in columnar unsupported; memory/memoize (run): jit call to unknown function \0jet.memo.stats.square; types/multi_head_functions (run): jit enum named payload field unsupported: Float; types/traits (run): jit closure method unsupported. ROOT CAUSE: see census. OVERLAP: some member stems are already named by existing M13 cards #1754, #1761. Those cards describe the stem; THIS card describes the shared root cause. Fix once here; close the overlapping card on the same evidence. BLAST RADIUS: not assessed. CONFIDENCE: high on sites, except the two undifferentiated messages noted. A try_compile failure is a silent interpreter deopt, so each of these is an I9 tier-parity gap (AOT green, default jet run interpreted); per AGENTS.md I9 none may be parked in the ledger.
cards.plan: ONE FIX: No shared fix — 8 separate cards (or 7 if io/log_job is merged into the Path card with io/path). Two of them (iter_tools_audit, types/traits) must FIRST get a discriminating message; that is a real criterion, not busywork.. CODE SITE: see census. blockedBy: none

criteria.text: Every member stem compiles on the resident JIT: cargo test --test dev jit_coverage_audit no longer lists collections/iter_tools_audit, collections/list_surface, concurrency/protocol, io/log_job, lowlevel/layout_columnar, memory/memoize, types/multi_head_functions, types/traits under jit gaps
criteria.evidence:
Measured at the re-derived corpus gate ledger: 496 stems classified as frontend_rejected 39, gate_excluded 12, expected_exit 18, aot_broken 7, resident_jit 387, deopt_interp 33, and tier_divergent EMPTY. cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate passes 6 of 6. JIT compile coverage was re-derived from observed runs to 451 of 496 with ZERO compile gaps, and COMPILE_COVERED_FLOOR was raised 442 -> 444 -> 451 in the same diffs as the gains.

This card's own gap is closed. lowlevel/layout_columnar was the last compile gap in the epoch and it now lowers. Criterion 2 is satisfied exactly as written - the fix is at ONE site, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_columnar_gather, with the host bridge both columnar reads pass through, rather than once per stem. The for-in refusal needed no lowering arm at all: that tier holds a columnar list as its logical rows exactly as the interpreter ambient does, so iteration IS the plain list walk and the refusal was simply wrong - the polarity is that columnar is no longer consulted for the walk. Three expression gates were added, each admitting exactly what its arm compiles, with ColumnarColumnRead gated strictly narrower than the record_slot accessor it reuses, so the predicate is never wider than the lowering and no Cranelift rejection of generated code is possible (I2). The shared symbol is jet_columns_gather in Prelude/Core/Columns.rs reached through JetColumns<C>::gather, so the host marshals and the Prelude owns the meaning (I9); store width is taken from row 0 so record slot count cannot drift from column count. Criterion 3 holds: nothing is parked in tests/jit_gaps.txt - its gaps: section is empty because there is nothing to record - and no skip guard was added.

The AOT half was separately implicated, as that work predicted, and is also fixed: the emitter wrote JetColumnList<S>::from_aos, which is not Rust, and rustc answered 'comparison operators cannot be chained' - an I2 internal compiler error. The constructor path is now turbofished. That was the single site calling an associated function on the type string; gather_at and iter_aos are method calls on a value.

cards.title: JIT emits invalid CLIF L1: Call argument f64 passed where the callee signature says i64
cards.body: Cranelift's verifier rejected CLIF that JET ITSELF EMITTED. These 9 are NOT unsupported constructs. Cranelift's verifier rejected CLIF that Jet itself emitted — a lowering bug of the same class as I2's "rustc rejecting GENERATED code is a compiler bug". They must be filed as compiler bugs with a severity above the unsupported families, and they must never be recorded as unsupported in the ledger. 3 stem(s). MEMBERS: ui/ui_null_backend (run): verifier: inst107 v82 = call fn47(v81) arg 0 (v81) has type f64, expected i64; inst112 v86 = call fn50(v85) same; web/web_hello (run): identical instructions/values (inst107/inst112, fn47/fn50) — same construct, same bug; comptime/computed_constants (Frame::decode): verifier: inst166 call fn72(v130, v129) arg 1 (v129) has type f64, expected i64. ROOT CAUSE: see #1663 census. This is NOT an unsupported construct and must never be recorded as one in tests/jit_gaps.txt: it is a lowering bug of the same class as I2's rule that rustc rejecting generated code is a compiler bug, and it sits at a severity above the unsupported families.
cards.plan: Give host-handle field reads ONE total type source (the same table AOT uses) instead of per-receiver special cases, so Print and call-argument marshalling select hosts from the same fact. A defensive assert/convert at call_host (reject a Value whose CLIF type disagrees with the declared AbiParam) turns any future instance into a loud internal error instead of a verifier crash — cheap and worth its own criterion. CODE SITE: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs:23912-23944 (type recovery), :25105-25126 (print host), :16748-16793 (host-handle field reads). blockedBy: none

cards.body: Cranelift's verifier rejected CLIF that JET ITSELF EMITTED. These 9 are NOT unsupported constructs. cards.title: Scheduler panic hook hides the message for every task body
cards.body: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs:68-80 suppresses the panic message whenever JET_SCHEDULER_CATCHING_PANIC is set, and that flag is set for the entire duration of every spawned task body. So any failure inside a task body -- including a nounwind abort -- prints nothing. This cost a burndown lane most of its budget: .claude/burndown-logs/dev3.txt records an abort with zero diagnostic text, and the lane had to reconstruct the cause statically because the message was swallowed.
cards.plan: Suppression exists so an expected caught panic does not spam the user. That is legitimate for a panic the scheduler is about to catch and convert. It is not legitimate for one that is escaping. Print unconditionally when the panic will not be caught -- in particular on the nounwind/abort path, where the message is the only evidence anyone will ever get. Keep the quiet path for genuinely caught-and-converted panics. blockedBy: none

criteria.text: A panic escaping a task body prints its message and location even with JET_SCHEDULER_CATCHING_PANIC set
criteria.evidence: Fixed in f7fee5d51. Suppression now keys on the payload, so only the control-transfer types the scheduler actually swallows stay quiet. cards.title: JIT unwind safety: mechanism decision + no Rust unwind through FDE-less JIT frames
cards.body:
cranelift-jit 0.112.3 registers NO unwind information for the code it emits, and there is no API to ask it to. Verified mechanically: grep for eh_frame|__register_frame|unwind|UnwindInfo|register_frame across the whole crate source returns zero matches, while a control grep for 'fn |struct |impl ' on the same path returns 60+, so the zero is real. define_function_with_control_plane compiles, copies the code buffer into RWX memory, collects relocs, records for perf and updates the GOT -- it never calls compiled_code.create_unwind_info(isa) and never registers an FDE.

Consequence: when JIT-compiled frames are on the stack, the unwinder cannot walk past them. _Unwind_Find_FDE misses, libgcc phase 1 returns _URC_END_OF_STACK, and std's rust_panic rtaborts with 'fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 5'. A clobbered or absent return address in a JIT frame is equally consistent with the bare SIGSEGV the dev suite still ends on.

This is why error 5 is NOT a stack-space condition and why bumping COMPILER_STACK_SIZE cannot help: real exhaustion prints 'has overflowed its stack' plus 'fatal runtime error: stack overflow', a textually distinct pair. Evidence trail: .claude/burndown-logs/dev.txt:4005-4006 has the exhaustion pair; dev2.txt and dev6.txt have the error-5 pair instead; dev2.txt predates the sized-stack boundary by 4.5 hours, so the boundary is not implicated.

Absorbed #1995 (c0oks05m, "extern "C" JIT frames abort the process instead of reporting") 2026-08-19: same defect class (Rust unwind reaching FDE-less JIT frames aborts the process), same crate; the mechanism decision here determines the entire fix shape, and #1995's site inventory (deopt.rs:451 jet_deopt_call, Concurrency.rs bare panic! + ~14 .expect) is exactly the call-site inventory this card's plan names as prerequisite.
cards.plan:
The invariant to establish and then enforce: a Rust panic must never be raised while JIT frames are on the stack. Two candidate mechanisms, and the choice is an architecture call worth making explicitly rather than per-site.

(1) Emit and register unwind info for JIT'd code. cranelift's compiled_code.create_unwind_info(isa) exists at the codegen layer even though cranelift-jit does not call it; registering FDEs would make JIT frames walkable and let a panic cross them. Cost: platform-specific frame registration, and it makes unwinding a supported path through generated code, which is a larger semantic commitment than it looks.

(2) Guarantee conversion at the boundary: every host seam that can panic converts to a status BEFORE returning into JIT'd code, so no unwind ever starts with JIT frames below. This matches how the tiers already talk -- #Shield delivers deferred cancel as a status, and 9623985d0 put the same conversion at jet_deopt_call. Cost: the guarantee must hold across all 1679 host_fns entries, so it needs a mechanical check, not review discipline.

Prerequisite for either: the call-site inventory of places that can raise while JIT frames are live. Note that host_fns being extern "C" does NOT save us -- rustc gives an extern "C" body an empty-filter landing pad, so those panics are found in phase 1 and die in phase 2 as 'thread caused non-unwinding panic', a different abort. Error 5 is specifically the case where phase 1 finds nothing at all. blockedBy: none

log.text: Absorbed #1995. Combined criteria added.

ARCHITECTURE CALL (orchestrator, technical/internal - not an owner gate). Mechanism (2) boundary conversion is chosen over (1) FDE registration. Reason: (1) makes unwinding a SUPPORTED path through generated code - a far larger semantic commitment than it looks, platform-specific frame registration, and it writes Rust panic propagation into the contract of Jet-generated machine code. (2) matches how the tiers already talk: Shield already delivers deferred cancel as a status rather than an unwind, and 9623985d0 already placed exactly this conversion at jet_deopt_call. COST, which is the design centre and not an afterthought: the guarantee must hold across ~1679 host_fns entries, so it needs a mechanical check rather than review discipline. Lever already exists - card 1633 made host_fns declare each JIT host symbol once, so the boundary conversion is GENERATED from that macro and a test scans for any extern C fn jet_ in crates/jet-jit not routed through it. A guarantee that depends on someone remembering is not a guarantee. No ballot raised: this is an internal mechanism choice, not user-facing syntax, no invariant carve-out, no new dependency.

REPRODUCER FOUND (2026-08-15, at f7f21742c). The error-5 abort no longer needs the whole suite: it fires in ~3 seconds from one child case.

  cargo test --no-fail-fast --test dev -- --test-threads=1 --exact --nocapture jit_1216_adversarial_regressions

Output:
  generator: stdout:
    running 1 test
  stderr:
    fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 5, aborting

So the `generator` adversarial case of jit_1216_adversarial_regressions spawns a child test process that dies with the exact _URC_END_OF_STACK abort this card describes. That child is a single Cranelift-compiled generator program, which is a far smaller surface than a 168-test binary.

Why this matters for the fix: it confirms the diagnosis independently. Error 5 means phase 1 walked off the top of the stack without finding a handler, and a generator is precisely where JIT frames sit under a resumption/unwind edge -- consistent with cranelift-jit registering no eh_frame for emitted code. It also explains why no full-suite log in this campaign ever contained libtest's `---- <test> stdout ----` failure section: the abort kills the process before libtest prints it, which is why every lane in this session had to reconstruct failure bodies from serial reruns.

Use this reproducer rather than the suite. It is deterministic, isolated, and fast.

cards.title: 43 example stems are invisible to the JIT coverage audit
cards.body:
collect_jit_coverage skips a stem entirely when it fails Loader or Sema in-process, so the stem enters neither compile_covered nor gaps -- it simply vanishes from the audit's universe. 43 stems are currently in that state: net/*, serde/*, modules/*, crypto/vault_*, memory/pin, io/watcher and others. Found while reconciling the ledger for #1663 (391 -> 414 rows).

Why this matters more than the count: every coverage claim the audit makes is silently scoped to the stems it could load, so 'gaps: 0' has never meant 'no gaps'. It means 'no gaps among the stems that loaded'. That is the same class of false confidence #1663 exists to correct, one level further out -- the ledger was falsified by hand three times, and this hole means even an honest ledger overstates coverage.

This is a frontend/universe hole, not a JIT regression: the stems fail before the JIT is consulted.
cards.plan: Establish why each of the 43 fails Loader/Sema in-process when the same examples are expected to build in the corpus. Two candidates, and the split matters: (a) they genuinely need a package/manifest context the in-process harness does not construct, in which case the harness must construct it or the audit must declare them out of universe EXPLICITLY rather than by silent omission; (b) they fail for a real frontend defect, in which case each is a bug and the audit was hiding it. Do not close this by adding a skip list -- an explicit out-of-universe declaration must name the reason per stem and be counted, so the number can only shrink. Then pin the universe size the same way COMPILE_COVERED_FLOOR pins coverage, so a stem cannot fall out of the universe silently. blockedBy: none

log.text:
SHARPENED COUNT and a consequence I must own, 2026-08-15.

Two independent lanes counted the universe hole larger than this card's 43: one measured 81 stems absent from observe_jit_coverage's universe, the other measured the corpus at 496-498 top-level stems against 415 compile_covered rows and 374 corpus-gate rows -- 122 stems classified in NO gate section, and 83 absent from compile_covered of which 64 are classified resident_jit or deopt_interp by the gate, i.e. they demonstrably DO compile.

Consequence I own: commit 12648cdcc reconciled tests/jit_gaps.txt to the audit's OBSERVED set, deleting ~63 rows. Verified at f148867d1 that the audit's red arm is `gaps:` (29 unrecorded gaps), NOT the `unrecorded`/GREW arm -- so the deleted stems are not observed covered either, and the ledger is self-consistent with the audit. But that is the weaker property than it sounds: absence from the observed set means EITHER genuinely not covered OR not in the universe, and for at least six named stems (concurrency/parallel_scan, crypto/vault_keys, crypto/vault_secret, memory/expiring_secret, tooling/debug_native and others) the corpus gate classifies them resident_jit. So the reconciliation made the ledger agree with an INCOMPLETE oracle, and the ledger now understates real coverage by roughly the size of this hole.

No product behaviour changed and nothing was falsified in the 100e24b93 sense -- the rows were removed because the oracle could not see them, not to green a test. But the correct order of work is now clear: CLOSE THIS HOLE FIRST, then re-derive compile_covered against a complete universe and raise COMPILE_COVERED_FLOOR once. Re-adding rows by hand against the gate's classification would be a third hand-edit of a file that has already been falsified three times.

Also found: examples/features/tooling/data_plot.jet appears in NO corpus-gate section, violating that file's own stated invariant that every top-level example appears in exactly one. It is the surviving half of the same line-plot lineage that produced the data_line orphan deleted in f148867d1.

Ledger reconcile for #1663 surfaced a false pin here: serde_jit_parity_manifest_pins asserts 'serde/encoding_breadth must remain compile-covered', but that stem is NOT observed covered. It never enters the JIT coverage audit's universe at all, because it fails Loader/Sema in-process (root cause carded as #1998, 43 stems in that state). It was already like this at the start of the 2026-08-15 session, so the pin has been asserting something untrue. The stale compile_covered row was REMOVED rather than kept, so the purpose-built alarm now fires instead of being absorbed -- keeping it would have been exactly the falsification #1663 documents. Resolve by deciding which side is wrong: either the stem should be covered (find why it is not; it may be the universe hole rather than a lowering gap), or the pin asserts a capability the product never had and the pin is the defect. Do NOT re-add a compile_covered row to make it pass.

criteria.text: Each of the 43 stems is classified as genuinely out-of-universe with a named reason, or as a frontend defect with a card
criteria.evidence: Both silent-drop sites are gone. tests/dev.rs:665-673 replaces Err(_) => continue on Loader failure and :680-686 replaces the Sema-error continue; each now returns JitCompileVerdict::OutOfUniverse with a named reason string of the form loader|sema: CODE: message. The loop body is a match on an exhaustive three-variant enum, so totality is structural rather than a convention - no continue remains in the walk. observe_jit_coverage asserts covered + gaps + out_of_universe == corpus. Measured at c2eb365be: 53 stems classified out-of-universe, each carrying its real diagnostic (28x E2402 no declared NetError->Err conversion, 7x loader E0606 project module declared more than once, 5x E0405, 3x E0113, and 10 singletons). Follow-up card minted for that population so the number can only shrink.

cards.title: Interpreter ambient reads host env, not the Jet-owned env table
cards.body:
crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs:2563-2566 reads NO_COLOR and TERM with std::env::var_os / std::env::var -- the HOST process environment. AOT (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:657) and the JIT host (crates/jet-jit/src/IO.rs:158-168) both read the Jet-owned LOGICAL env table, per D-ENV-MUTATE1.

Observable consequence: a program that calls env.set("NO_COLOR", ...) at runtime disables colour on two tiers and not the third. One program, two meanings -- an I9 break.

Found while diagnosing the io_style presence-semantics test. Presence semantics themselves are correct on every tier and need no change; the defect is purely which env table the interpreter ambient consults.

Related, same area, worth fixing together: tests/dev.rs:6248 probes jet_style_env_enabled(), a symbol DELETED on 2026-08-13 by 97469e2f9 / 6ed8d4a95 when the terminal runtime was unified and its body was inlined into jet_style_enabled. The probe compiled and passed from 2026-07-28 until then and has been a hard rustc error since. Renaming it to jet_style_enabled() would go green while proving NOTHING: under libtest, stdout is piped, so jet_term_stdout_is_terminal() is false and jet_term_style_enabled returns false regardless of NO_COLOR. That is a false green an earlier Tower review already flagged. The correct fix restores an env-only seam.
cards.plan: Route ambient_interp.rs to read the same Jet-owned logical env table AOT and the JIT host read, so env.set is visible identically on all three tiers. Do not duplicate the lookup: per I9 the engines are marshalling adapters and the table is the single owner, so the interpreter should call the same accessor rather than growing its own. Then restore an env-only seam for the style probe so the test can assert presence semantics WITHOUT depending on whether stdout is a terminal, and state plainly in the test what it does and does not prove. blockedBy: none

cards.title: each loses its capture write on both dev tiers
cards.body:
A closure passed to `each` runs, but a write it makes to a captured local never reaches the caller's frame -- on BOTH the interpreter and the resident JIT. Only AOT is correct, which is why the goldens are right and the failure looked like an interpreter-only golden mismatch.

Minimal reproduction, verified at 54e7ca662:

  fn run() {
      xs := [1, 2, 3]
      seen := [Int].{}
      xs.each((n: Int) => { seen.push(n) })
      print("list each: {seen}")
      s := Set.from([1, 2, 3])
      t := [Int].{}
      s.each((n: Int) => { t.push(n) })
      print("set each: {t}")
      print("fold: {s.fold(0, (a: Int, n: Int) => a + n)}")
  }

  jet run           -> list each: []   set each: []   fold: 6
  jet run --interpret -> list each: []   set each: []   fold: 6

`fold: 6` on the same receiver proves the collection is populated and the callback IS invoked; only the capture write is dropped. Not Set-specific -- a plain List each fails identically.

Why it hid: every other closure form (filter, map, all, fold, flat_map) consumes the callback's RETURN value, so a dropped capture write is invisible. `each` returns Unit, so the capture write is its ONLY observable effect. Diagnosed via examples/features/collections/set.jet, where one line of ~40 differs: 'each visited sorted: []' against the golden's '[1, 3, 4]'.

Probable mechanism (from the diagnosing lane, unconfirmed): eval/mod.rs sync_callable_captures published write-back by iterating TLambda::captures only, but that vector is filled exclusively from the AOT clone pack (lower/lambdas.rs). For a non-escaping FnMut lambda `is_move` is false and AOT deliberately relies on Rust's native &mut lexical capture, so nothing is packed and `captures` is EMPTY. The write completes inside the callable slot and is then dropped at the scope boundary. A first attempt to seed and republish lexical captures did not fix it.
cards.plan:
Model a non-packed capture as what it is on every other tier: a reference to the enclosing local, seeded before the call and published after. Fix it at the shared seam, not per engine -- the JIT shows the identical symptom, so an interpreter-only patch would leave the I9 break half-closed.

Hard constraint on the predicate: names in frozen_captures (D-CONC-FREEZE1) and materialized_captures (D-MEM-COPYSEM1) are ratified SNAPSHOTS and must NOT track the outer local. Publishing through them would trade a missing write for a corrupted one, which is worse. Lambda source_params are likewise excluded.

Severity note for scheduling: `jet dev` currently reports success for a program whose loop body does nothing observable, so this is a beginner-facing correctness trap on the most ordinary imperative idiom in the language. blockedBy: none

cards.title: E2201 blames a missing run function when lowering failed
cards.body:
A whole-program TIR lowering failure is reported to the user as E2201 "`jet dev` needs a `run` function to run", why: "a library with no `run` has nothing to execute" -- on a program that HAS a `run` function. The diagnostic names a cause that is provably not the cause.

Found in the `range_unboxed` fixture of `range_values_run_in_resident_jit_without_fallback`: the fixture does define `fn run()`, and the lane confirmed on a second tier that the real failure is an internal lowering error. So this is an I2 case surfacing as a user diagnostic instead of exit 101, and simultaneously an I4 case: the message teaches the reader a false rule about their own program and sends them to add a function that already exists.

Severity is higher than the one fixture suggests. Any program whose whole-program lowering fails on this path gets told its `run` is missing, so the misattribution hides every defect that reaches it -- including, until this session, the coverage gap the fixture was written to detect. It also means the test's claim ("range values run in the resident JIT without fallback") has never actually been verified.
cards.plan:
Separate the two failures the path currently conflates. A genuinely absent `run` is a real user error and keeps E2201. A lowering failure is a compiler defect and must take the branded internal-error rail: render the actual lowering reason and exit 101 (I2), never blame the user's program. Find where the lowering Err is discarded and replaced by the entry-point check, and carry the real reason through instead.

Then check the same shape elsewhere: an entry-point precondition tested AFTER a fallible lowering step, so that any lowering failure is reported as the precondition failing. Report every instance found, not only this one.

Related: the sibling test was strengthened to report the real reason rather than the misattributed E2201, so once this is fixed the test should name the genuine gap. blockedBy: none

cards.title: E1004 rejects json.decode and then suggests json.decode
cards.body:
The untyped D-JSON3 form `json.decode(text)` is rejected by sema with a self-contradicting diagnostic:

  E1004 "`core.encoding.json` has no item `decode`"
  why:  "standard library modules expose a fixed set of public items"
  fix:  "did you mean `decode`?"

The fix suggests the exact name the message just said does not exist. Any user who hits this is told to write what they already wrote.

Two defects sit on top of each other and both need naming. The DIAGNOSTIC is an I4 failure: a suggestion identical to the rejected name is not product-quality copy, and it also implies the suggester is comparing against a candidate set that contains `decode`, which contradicts the message. Separately, whether `core.encoding.json.decode` should resolve at all in the untyped form is a real surface question -- if D-JSON3 ratifies the untyped spelling, the module surface is the defect, not the fixture.

Found while diagnosing json_coerce_audit_reports_jit_gap_on_default_dev, whose fixture uses this form and therefore never reaches the coercion-audit boundary it exists to test. That test is CORRECT and stays red until this is resolved.
cards.plan:
First settle the surface question by reading D-JSON3: does the untyped `json.decode(text)` form resolve, and to what? If yes, the module surface is missing an item and the fixture is right. If no, the fixture must use the ratified spelling -- and the diagnostic must then say what to write instead of echoing the rejected name.

Either way fix the suggester: a candidate suggestion that equals the rejected identifier must never be emitted. Find where the edit-distance candidate list is built and exclude the exact input, then check whether other E1004/E0107 paths can produce the same echo -- this is a generic suggester bug, not a json one. Note the sibling precedent already found this session: `iter_missing_method_hint` had a related echo problem, so a shared suggester is likely.

A UI snapshot must pin whichever final wording lands (I4: no diagnostic without a snapshot). blockedBy: none

log.text: E1004 no longer echoes the rejected name; untyped json.decode is D-JSON3; json_coerce_audit reaches E2201; UI snapshot json_unknown_item; suggester paths skip distance 0.

Unit test suggest_field_never_echoes_the_rejected_identifier: identical-only candidate set yields None. UI json_unknown_item.stderr suggests decode for decod, never the rejected spelling.

cards.title: Four copies of the raw env lookup want one owner
cards.body:
The raw-by-name environment lookup over the Jet-owned logical env table is implemented four times: the Prelude's jet_env_value_raw (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:841), CoreHost::jet_std_env_get (crates/jet-jit/src/CoreHost.rs:75-81), IO.rs::env_value (crates/jet-jit/src/IO.rs:158-164), and ambient_env_value_raw added in bbdc5015d.

This is the shape that produced the I9 divergence that commit just fixed: the interpreter ambient read the HOST process environment with std::env while AOT and the JIT host read the Jet-owned table, so env.set("NO_COLOR", ..) took effect on two tiers and not the third. With four copies, the next engine to need an env read has four precedents to choose from and no single owner to be wrong about.

Recorded rather than done because the consolidation crosses files that were outside the fixing lane's writable paths.
cards.plan:
Add one pub(crate) CoreHost accessor for the raw-by-name read over the env snapshot, and have IO.rs and the interpreter ambient call it. Per I9 the table is the single owner and engines are marshalling adapters, so there should be one lookup and N call sites, not N lookups. Estimated at three lines added plus two deletions by the lane that found it.

While there, confirm the Prelude copy is genuinely separate rather than a fifth caller: the Prelude fragment is embedded into generated programs, so it may legitimately need its own definition -- say which, so the count is honest. blockedBy: none

criteria.text: One accessor performs the raw-by-name env read; IO.rs and the interpreter ambient call it rather than reimplementing
criteria.evidence: One accessor performs the raw-by-name read: crates/jet-jit/src/CoreHost.rs:1233 jit_env_value_raw, with jit_env_value at :1243 and jit_env_set at :1250. Converted call sites: CoreHost.rs:75-77, IO.rs (local fn env_value DELETED; callers at 160/161/392/396/520/577), ambient_interp.rs (ambient_env_value_raw and ambient_env_value DELETED, now CoreHost at 2570-2608). A FIFTH copy the card did not list was folded in too: the extern-C heap shims at CoreHost.rs:1768-1777, which duplicated both the lookup and a validate+remove+push write.

criteria.text: The Prelude copy is either the same accessor or documented as necessarily separate with the reason
criteria.evidence: The Prelude copy is documented as necessarily separate at crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:863-878. Reason recorded at the definition: the fragment is embedded verbatim into a generated program, a standalone Rust crate linking no Jet crate, so it cannot call CoreHost; and it cannot be include!d into jet-jit either because it reaches its table through jet_env_read(), which only the generated crate defines. The comment states the honest count - exactly two definitions, one per linkage world, and a third in any engine is an I9 violation.

criteria.text: A test pins that env.set is visible identically on AOT, resident JIT and interpreter
criteria.evidence: Verified by orchestrator at 7599f9dcc in .claude/worktrees/builder. tests/env_overlay.rs env_set_is_visible_identically_on_aot_jit_and_interpreter PASSES (suite 6 passed at baseline to 8 passed; this test absent from the failure list). It reads through BOTH the decoding surface and the raw-lookup consumer (env.get plus io.terminal_width/height), because an env.set/env.get pair alone is a false green - two owners agreeing with themselves. AOT is a rustc-built binary; the JIT tier asserts jit_executed_for_test() with deopt/fallback absent; the interpreter tier asserts !jit_executed_for_test() so a silent deopt cannot supply the answer. Getting it green also required fixing a divergence the card did not know about: core.sys.get/set under the interpreter were answered by Comptime impure.rs with std::env - the COMPILER's host environment - while io.terminal_width() in the same tier read Jet's logical table.

cards.title: Five Prelude fragments declare a colliding bare `mod tests`
cards.body:
Prelude fragments are emitted into one flat generated crate, so a crate-root `mod tests` in two fragments collides. Five declare the bare name: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/NumericWiden.rs:45, Prelude/TaskGroup.rs:491, Prelude/TestReport.rs:146, Prelude/Ui.rs:919, Prelude/Core/Progress.rs:71.

The convention to avoid this already exists and four siblings follow it: SharedProtocol.rs:684 `shared_protocol_tests`, TypedText.rs:147 `typed_boundary_tests`, Auth.rs:657 `auth_tests`, Scheduler.rs:2900 `interrupt_boundary_tests`. So this is five fragments violating an established convention, not a missing one.

Two of the five are UNCONDITIONAL in PRELUDE_PARTS (NumericWiden since 2026-07-29 in e61c31131, Core/Progress since 2026-08-04 in d0098d284), so every generated program carries two colliding declarations before any conditional fragment is added. TestReport's landed 2026-08-13 in 07ba4870c; TaskGroup's and Ui's wait on conditional fragments.

Not a shipped defect, which is why this is hygiene: nothing ships a cfg(test) build of generated Rust, and `jet test` builds its own harness through TEST_PRELUDE. The collision only surfaces under a raw `rustc --test` of generated code, documented in tests/common/mod.rs:189-191 as an uncommon inspection mode. But it cost one test nine days of latent breakage -- io_style's probe hit E0428 from 2026-08-04 and had it masked by a second, unrelated break -- and it will cost the next person who inspects generated Rust the same way.
cards.plan:
Rename the five bare declarations to fragment-unique names following the existing convention. Purely mechanical: these are unit tests inside embedded fragments and nothing outside a fragment names its own test module.

Then make the convention enforceable rather than aspirational: a test that scans PRELUDE_PARTS for a crate-root `mod tests` and fails, so a sixth cannot appear. Without that this recurs -- two of the five arrived AFTER the convention was already established by the four that follow it.

While there, decide whether a raw `rustc --test` build of generated Rust should be supported at all. If it is genuinely unsupported, the harness should fail fast with a clear message rather than surfacing as E0428 from the middle of a 10,000-line generated file. blockedBy: none

criteria.text: No two Prelude fragments declare the same crate-root module name
criteria.evidence: Six bare `mod tests` declarations renamed to fragment-unique names following the four existing exemplars (SharedProtocol shared_protocol_tests, TypedText typed_boundary_tests, Auth auth_tests, Scheduler interrupt_boundary_tests): NumericWiden.rs:45 -> numeric_widen_tests, Core/Progress.rs:71 -> progress_render_tests, TaskGroup.rs:491 -> task_group_tests, TestReport.rs:146 -> test_report_tests, Ui.rs:919 -> ui_backend_tests, and a SIXTH the card did not know about, crates/jet-foundation/src/StructuralDebug.rs:199 -> structural_debug_tests. StructuralDebug is UNCONDITIONAL in PRELUDE_PARTS (Codegen/mod.rs:205), so every generated program carried THREE colliding declarations, not the two the card estimated. Scope note for honesty: the guard added below enforces the `mod tests` collision that was actually occurring, not general uniqueness of every crate-root module name.

cards.title: check_latency_under_budget is load-dependent inside the parallel suite
cards.body:
The test asserts a wall-clock compile-latency budget while running inside the parallel `dev` suite, so its verdict depends on how much else the suite is doing.

Demonstrated at 04c910a45: it FAILS in the full parallel run and PASSES in isolation (`--test-threads=1 --exact check_latency_under_budget`, 0.43s). It passed in the full run at 1c18fd006 and started failing at 04c910a45 -- not from any change to the compiler, but because the suite began running 32 MORE tests once the generator unwind abort was fixed (e074041ce). Reached-test count went 107 to 139 and wall time 454s to 941s in the same window.

So the budget was being measured against a quieter machine than the suite now is, and it will drift again every time the suite gets faster or slower. As a latency regression detector it currently reports scheduler contention, not compiler latency.
cards.plan:
Make the measurement independent of suite load. Options in preference order, and the choice is worth stating rather than defaulting: (1) measure work rather than time -- count the compiler-owned steps or bytes the existing budget machinery already tracks, which is what `jet check` budgets do elsewhere in this repo, so a busy machine cannot move the verdict; (2) if wall-clock is genuinely the property under test, run it serialized or outside the parallel suite, and say so in the test name; (3) keep wall-clock but calibrate against a same-run baseline measured on the same machine under the same load, so the ratio is the assertion rather than an absolute.

Do NOT simply widen the budget. That trades a flaky failure for a detector that no longer detects anything, and the number would need widening again on the next machine.

Related context: #677 covers typed project compile-latency budgets, so this may fold into that card's mechanism rather than needing its own. Check before duplicating. blockedBy: none

criteria.text: The latency verdict is independent of how many other tests are running
criteria.evidence: Approach recorded with its reason: option 2, keep the basis and move the place. D-DEV3 is a wall-clock promise to the user (docs/spec/diagnostics.md, roadmap.md:67), so the basis stays wall clock and the budget stays 200ms; only the location changed. tests/dev_latency.rs is its own cargo test target holding exactly one test, and both cargo test and tools/ci/test-shards.sh run one target per process, so nothing else executes while the number is taken. Work counts were rejected because they need a machine-specific steps-to-ms constant and stay green through a blocking regression; a same-run baseline ratio was rejected because it cancels the fixed per-save cost that D-DEV3 exists to bound.

criteria.text: The test passes in the full parallel suite and in isolation, on the same commit
criteria.evidence: Verified at 47225c565: cargo test --test dev_latency = ok, 1 passed / 0 failed in 0.43s, and the old in-suite copy is deleted from tests/dev_parts/routine.rs so the fact has one owner.

criteria.text: The budget is not merely widened; the measurement basis is stated in the test
criteria.evidence: It still catches the regression it guards. The timed round is the same jet::check_with_path the watch loop runs per save, so a slower parse, a per-check stdlib re-read or a quadratic sema walk still trips it. Two teeth were added rather than removed: the example must check CLEAN, so a load failure can no longer hold the budget green while measuring nothing, and the test asserts its own source holds exactly one test, so the load dependence cannot be reintroduced by adding a second test to this target.

cards.title: A return inside a task body erases later declarations
cards.body:
One `return` inside a `task { ... }` body makes sema discard every declaration that follows it in the ENCLOSING block, producing a page of phantom "nothing named X exists here" errors for bindings that are plainly declared.

Observed: a fixture with `child :: task { return "child" }` produced ONE real error (E0113, the return handing a String back from a fallible `run`) followed by ELEVEN phantom ones -- nine E0107 for all_result / cancelled / cancelled_result / failed / failed_result / error, plus two E0003. Removing the single `return` removed all eleven.

Mechanism, traced by the diagnosing lane: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:370-371 sets `self.flow.reachable = false` after a `Stmt::Return`, and lines 366-369 restore `self.flow = before` for each FOLLOWING statement, discarding its declaration. Nothing saves or restores that flag around a lambda body -- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/lambdas.rs:608-609, `Checker::check_lambda`, the `LambdaBody::Block` arm, calls `check_block(stmts, false)` -- so the task body's `return` leaks into the enclosing block. `child` survived because it was declared before the leak took effect; every later binding did not.

Why this is wrong on the semantics and not only the ergonomics: a `task { }` body is a closure that may run later or not at all, so statements after the task ARE reachable. Treating the task body's return as an unconditional return of the enclosing function is a category error. Note the enclosing-function targeting itself is correct and the corpus depends on it (examples/features/net/http_get.jet uses `?? return` inside `task { }` to leave `run`) -- what is wrong is the REACHABILITY consequence, not the target.

Severity is a diagnostic-quality problem as much as a correctness one: one mistake inside a task body buries its own real error under a page of unrelated ones, which is exactly the experience I4 exists to prevent.
cards.plan:
Save and restore the reachability flag around a lambda/task body so a `return` inside it cannot mark the enclosing block unreachable. The narrow fix is at the `LambdaBody::Block` arm of `check_lambda`; confirm whether the expression-bodied arm needs it too, and whether any other construct checks a nested body through `check_block` without isolating flow (loop bodies, `#Unsafe` blocks, comptime blocks).

Then decide what SHOULD happen to the enclosing flow. A `return` inside a task body still returns the enclosing function when that task body runs, so it is not a no-op for flow analysis -- but it is conditional, not unconditional. Say explicitly which model you implement: conditional-return (enclosing stays reachable, which is what fixes this) or something stricter.

Add a regression test that a binding declared AFTER a task containing a `return` resolves. Without it this recurs invisibly, because the phantom errors look like ordinary user mistakes. blockedBy: none

log.text: Conditional-return for task/lambda bodies; regression green.

criteria.evidence: check_conditional_block in CheckerCore/blocks.rs saves and restores flow.reachable. check_lambda LambdaBody::Block uses it (lambdas.rs). Model: conditional return.

criteria.evidence: blocks.rs documents inline bodies keep check_block; loop/switch joins unchanged (FlowFacts::after_loop, merge_states).

criteria.evidence: tests/task_state.rs a_return_inside_a_task_body_keeps_later_declarations: later::7 after task { return } has no E0107/E0102; mistaken return "child" still errors without phantom cascade. cargo test --test task_state passed.

cards.title: Cancel raised while already unwinding aborts the process
cards.body:
examples/features/streams/generators.jet aborts deterministically on AOT after 'consumer: 1' with 'panic in a destructor during cleanup / thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting.', exit 1.

Chain, confirmed by two independent lanes: JetStreamSender::drop (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Stream.rs:299) sends completion; JetSchedulerSender::send opens with a cancel wait point (Prelude/Scheduler.rs:2170-2171); that reaches jet_task_deliver_cancel and panic_any(JetCancelUnwind) at Scheduler.rs:334 -- raised while the thread is ALREADY unwinding from the same payload (jet_stream_task resume_unwind, Stream.rs:55). Raising during unwind is a double-panic and aborts.

The guard already exists one function away: jet_scheduler_shield_leave_status at Scheduler.rs:307 checks std::thread::panicking(). jet_task_deliver_cancel does not.

Affects streams/generators on AOT, so it also fails stream_pull_hostile_matrix_matches_interpreter_jit_and_aot and collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot. The JIT half of that first test was fixed separately; this is the second, independent defect behind it.
cards.plan:
Two candidate fixes, and the choice is a semantics call rather than a mechanical one.

(a) Guard jet_task_deliver_cancel on !std::thread::panicking(), matching jet_scheduler_shield_leave_status. Minimal and consistent with existing practice, but it silently drops the cancel delivery when it collides with an unwind.

(b) Send the completion inside a shield, so a dropped consumer still observes Completed or Failed rather than losing the notification. Semantically better -- the consumer learns the real outcome -- but it changes when cancellation is deliverable, which is a D-CANCELMODEL1 call and may need ratification.

Whichever lands, no host seam may panic: under an FDE-less JIT frame a raise aborts (#1997). Prefer a status. blockedBy: none

log.text: c4 now has one real blocker, isolated. The battery was drowning in false timeouts: eight stems compile AOT concurrently against a fixed 30s budget measured on a warm cache, and the new runtime-cache prune leaves it cold. With JET_TIER_PARITY_TIMEOUT_SECS=300 the timeouts vanish and one true failure remains: JIT vs AOT divergence for memory/pool_stale_id. JIT reports the E3001 stale-id stop; AOT does not match. The old JetId ordering blocker is genuinely gone (MathTaskMem.rs:1146-1160).

Criterion 4 is not met and now has a named blocker. Ran both named tests at HEAD: stream_pull_hostile_matrix_matches_interpreter_jit_and_aot passes; collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot FAILS with a JIT versus interpreter divergence for memory/shared_transact. Probed it directly: --interpret prints from=200/to=800/total=1000 matching the golden, while default jet run prints from=500/to=500 and then repeats Stop [E3012] stack overflow in transfer for 24 lines. So the default tier both loses the write and then blows the stack. Filed as #2123 (P0, i9). The battery also reported memory/arena_regions timing out after 30s, but that example runs clean standalone on both tiers in under a second, so that one looks like harness contention rather than a program defect.

Criteria 1/2/3 met 2026-08-19. Criterion 4 is half proven: cargo test --test dev_tier_parity stream_pull_hostile_matrix_matches_interpreter_jit_and_aot ok (20.40s). The other half, collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot, fails on an UNRELATED stem for an unrelated cause: collections/iter_tools_audit is refused by the Cranelift residency gate on BuiltinMethod:Unzip with a tuple-struct carrier while compile=Ok(()), i.e. the fourth gate-versus-lowering drift found today. It is not a cancellation or stream defect and it is owned by #2091 (lift the gate/lowering tables so the class cannot recur). This card's own assertions are reached; criterion 4 closes when that stem is resident again.
