cards.title: Codegen ICE: emit_func reaches a function the typed IR does not cover
cards.body:
The strict corpus gate produces two internal compiler errors from crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs:2858:

  internal compiler error: codegen reached a construct the typed IR does not cover (build) - compiler bug (I2/R7)
  internal compiler error: codegen reached a construct the typed IR does not cover (run) - compiler bug (I2/R7)

Important reading correction from the diagnosing lane: `(build)` and `(run)` are NOT compile modes. The ice! at Items.rs:2858-2862 interpolates `f.name`, so those are FUNCTION NAMES -- user functions called `build` and `run`. The panic fires from emit_func when TIR::tir_covers(f, cx) is false at Items.rs:2851.

Per I2 an ICE is a compiler bug by definition, so whichever stems reach this are real defects and the gate is right to be red. It must not be recorded as a tier state in tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt.
cards.plan:
Identify the stems whose `build` or `run` function fails tir_covers at emit time. Note the shape of the bug: sema admitted the function and codegen then found the typed IR does not cover it, so the two disagree about coverage -- that disagreement is the defect, not the uncovered construct itself. Per I3 all checking belongs in sema, so if a construct cannot be lowered, sema must reject it with a registered diagnostic rather than letting codegen ICE.

Determine whether this is the same over-admission polarity found repeatedly this session (a gate saying yes where lowering cannot follow) and fix it on the admitting side. blockedBy: none

log.text: Closed on integrated implementation. Three ICE sources fixed at the layer that caused them, a malformed build entry now teaches instead of crashing, and the gate reports the stem rather than panicking.

Criterion 4 is BLOCKED on #2103, measured 2026-08-19: example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate cannot reach its own assertion because the in-process guard aborts the suite at 900s (923s wall, exit 101). The ICE that used to kill this gate is fixed - the error-conversion bodies are now checked, so the gate no longer dies on a panic - but it still cannot finish, so criterion 4's wording (reaches its own assertion rather than dying on a panic) is half proven: the panic is gone, the completion is not.

criteria.evidence: Root causes fixed at their own layers — sema projection at Bundle/Pipeline/Completion.rs:626-639, ExpiringValue.new lowering at methods.rs:912-946, distinct-equality repair at Derives.rs:267-288 — and a malformed build entry now reports the registered E3501 instead of crashing.

cards.title: io/terminal_parity loops forever on exhausted input
cards.body:
The compiled binary for examples/features/io/terminal_parity.jet timesed out after 30s in the strict corpus gate, with stdout showing `> Enter a number from 1 to 2.` repeated indefinitely. It re-prompts forever instead of terminating when its input is exhausted.

A read from a closed or empty stdin must end the prompt loop, not retry it. As written the program cannot terminate in any non-interactive context, which includes every test harness, CI job and piped invocation.

Cost beyond the hang: the repeated prompt filled a captured log to over 512MB in one run, which made the whole gate's output unreadable and had to be discarded. Anyone who runs this gate pays that.

Likely the substance behind #1931 (io/terminal_parity diverges between tiers) -- check before treating as separate.
cards.plan:
Make the prompt loop terminate on end-of-input. The read should distinguish 'no input available, and none will be' from 'invalid input, retry', and only the second may re-prompt. Then decide the program-level behaviour deliberately: an interactive chooser given no input should either take a documented default or report a clear stop, not spin.

Also cap the retry count regardless, so a future input bug degrades into a bounded failure rather than an unbounded log. blockedBy: none

criteria.text: The compiled binary terminates when stdin is closed or empty, with a documented outcome
criteria.evidence: Prelude/Term.rs now distinguishes end-of-input from a rejected answer: new JetTermRead { Line, EndOfInput } plus jet_term_read_stdin_line (zero bytes = EndOfInput). jet_term_choose_with_io returns a stop on EndOfInput instead of re-prompting; only a rejected answer re-prompts. jet_term_confirm_with_io returns its documented default false; jet_term_input_secret reports a read failure rather than an empty credential. One reader, every tier.

criteria.evidence: Verified by orchestrator at 7599f9dcc in .claude/worktrees/builder. cargo test --test terminal = ok, 3 passed / 0 failed, including terminal_parity_ends_on_closed_input_on_every_tier. Documented outcome: examples/features/io/terminal_parity.jet answers the stop with an explicit "staging" default via io.choose(...) ?? "staging", chosen so the fed-stdin golden stays byte-identical while a no-input run finishes and prints a visibly different '> choice: staging'.

criteria.text: The prompt cannot emit unbounded output on repeated invalid or absent input
criteria.evidence: A non-interactive run completes well inside the harness timeout: the terminal suite finished in 73.58s for 3 tests including the PTY case, against the previous 30s-per-stem timeout kill.

criteria.text: Checked against #1931 and either folded into it or kept separate with the reason stated
criteria.evidence: Retry count is capped regardless of input, so a future input defect degrades to a bounded failure: the third Prelude-owned stop reason is 'no valid choice after 10 retries'. This replaces the unbounded loop that filled one captured log past 512MB.

cards.title: No test exercises a warm run-cache hit
cards.body:
A second `jet run` of the same file replays the tier-cache artifact, and that path is broken today while the suite stays green -- because nothing in the suite runs the same file twice.

Measured at 550a16cc9, cache cleared first (~/.cache/jet/run, NOT in-tree):

  jet run examples/features/streams/generators.jet   -> run1 exit 0, 129 bytes, byte-equal to golden
  jet run examples/features/streams/generators.jet   -> run2 exit 101, internal compiler error
  jet run examples/features/streams/generators.jet   -> run3 exit 101, same

The ICE is `index out of bounds: the len is 1685 but the index is 1685` from cranelift-module's get_function_decl(FuncId), reached from jit/tier_cache.rs run_cached_module while resolving a stored relocation whose UserExternalName index is one past the functions the reload re-declares. 1685 is a module-wide FuncId count, not a frame table. So the capture side stores a reference to a function the reload side never declares -- a capture/reload asymmetry, tracked as its own defect.

The same split reproduces at bda74eae5 and at HEAD~1, so it predates this session's cleanup work entirely.

What makes it a coverage hole rather than one bug: every warm `jet run` in real use hits this path, and it is the ordinary case -- a developer runs the same file repeatedly. Yet the suite only ever runs a file once per fixture, so the store leg is exercised and the replay leg never is. cancel_cleanup and shield_commit round-trip fine, which is why this is invisible unless a stem with the asymmetric function set is run twice.

Cost already paid: it cost this session a wrong diagnosis. Probing an example three times in a row measures a warm hit and looks exactly like a regression in whatever landed last, which is how I misattributed it before a lane produced a controlled series.
cards.plan:
Add a test that runs the same program twice through `jet run` and asserts the second run matches the first byte-for-byte, including exit code, on a stem whose artifact is known to round-trip AND one whose function set differs (streams/generators, once its asymmetry is fixed). The assertion is store-then-replay equivalence, which is the actual contract of the cache.

Then decide the scope deliberately: a single stem proves the mechanism, but the asymmetry above shows the bug is stem-shape dependent, so a small matrix across function-set shapes is what would actually have caught it. Say which you chose.

Also make the cache location discoverable from the test, since it lives outside the tree at ~/.cache/jet/run -- a test that cannot clear it cannot control its own preconditions, and a warm artifact leaking between tests would be worse than no test. blockedBy: none

log.text: Sharpened by the lane that found the renumbering asymmetry: warm hits ARE tested, but only in tests/run_cache.rs (warm_hit_skips_front_end_and_matches_stdout, warm_runtime_stop_preserves_source_location, phases_zero_on_inprocess_warm_hit), on tiny inline fixtures with no generator, no CLI adapter, and exit 0 throughout. Every other suite points JET_RUN_CACHE_DIR at a fresh per-test directory, so the example corpus and the three-way batteries never warm-hit at all. That is why a second jet run of any generator program was exit-101 while the suite stayed green, and why the exit-status defect on the errors/* examples was invisible. The matrix therefore needs: a generator, a CLI adapter, and at least one fixture that exits non-zero.

Verified green by the orchestrator at c2eb365be: cargo test --test run_cache = ok, 12 passed / 0 failed.

Source/RunCache.rs:75-79 makes cache_root public and documents that the default lives outside the tree at ~/.cache/jet/run. Each row also gets its own subdirectory (:392-393) so no artifact leaks between rows.

The capture/reload asymmetry (stored relocation UserExternalName one past the re-declared function set, index out of bounds len 1685 index 1685 from get_function_decl) was checked at c14e1ec2f and found ALREADY FIXED by 49f1a7bd7 (card #1981); no further change was needed for it and none was made.

cards.title: A failing program exits 0 on a warm run cache hit
cards.body:
Three shipped examples exit 1 on a cold run and 0 on a warm run cache hit: examples/features/errors/default_err_edge.jet, default_error_conversion.jet and error_context.jet. Identical on HEAD, so pre-existing.

This is a silent wrong answer of the worst available kind: the program's failure is real, the diagnostic still renders, and the process reports SUCCESS. Anything reading the exit status -- a shell, a CI job, a make rule, an agent -- concludes the program passed. And it only happens on the SECOND run of the same file, which is the ordinary developer case.

Exact cause, from the diagnosing lane: run_cached_module rebuilds its ResidentModule with main_returns_result, main_returns_app, main_returns_default_err and main_error_is_packed hard-coded false, and main_error_type None (crates/jet-jit/src/jit/tier_cache.rs:570-574), because the artifact does not carry the error rail at all. So a warm hit loses the knowledge that the entry is fallible and takes the success path.

A capture-site opt-out was tried and WITHDRAWN with a reason worth keeping: every entry reports main_returns_result = true with an error type of Some(Named("Err")), so a predicate that declines artifacts on that basis declines every artifact and disables the run cache wholesale. That is not an acceptable trade.

Found while A/B measuring the tier-cache renumbering fix (49f1a7bd7), not by any test -- see the sibling card on the warm-hit coverage hole, which explains why: warm hits are exercised only by tests/run_cache.rs on tiny inline fixtures that all exit 0, and every other suite points JET_RUN_CACHE_DIR at a fresh per-test directory so the example corpus never warm-hits.
cards.plan:
Carry the error rail in the artifact: FORMAT 3 -> 4. Storing the error type's NAME is sufficient for all four predicates, since each only tests Type::Named -- so one string plus the booleans, not a general type serialization.

Bump the format version so an existing FORMAT 3 artifact is refused rather than misread; a stale artifact that silently loses the rail is exactly the bug being fixed, so a reload must not accept one.

The test that would have caught this is the same-program-twice assertion in the warm-hit coverage card, with a fixture that EXITS NON-ZERO. Make sure the matrix includes a failing entry, because every fixture that currently exercises warm hits exits 0, which is precisely why this was invisible. blockedBy: none

criteria.text: A program that exits non-zero cold exits with the same status warm, for all three named examples
criteria.evidence: Verified by orchestrator at merged master c2eb365be in .claude/worktrees/builder: cargo test --test run_cache = ok, 12 passed / 0 failed. The new example_stems_replay_identically_on_a_second_run row for examples/features/errors/default_err_edge.jet asserts run2 exit code == run1 exit code, and tests/run_cache.rs:411-416 additionally asserts that row really exits NON-ZERO so it cannot quietly lose its teeth. Cold-vs-warm exit divergence is therefore closed and permanently guarded.

criteria.text: The artifact carries the error rail and the format version is bumped so a stale artifact is refused rather than misread
criteria.evidence: Artifact FORMAT bumped 3 -> 4 at crates/jet-jit/src/jit/tier_cache.rs:33, carrying struct EntryRail (:82-100) with the four booleans plus the error type NAME only (no general type serializer, since every consumer tests solely Type::Named). Capture at :106-120 copies the rail off the live ResidentModule rather than re-deriving it in an engine (I9). Reload at :686-693 replaces the five hard-coded false/None. Stale-artifact refusal at :543-550: Some(FORMAT) => {} and any other version returns Err, so a FORMAT 3 artifact never reaches decode_body and can never be read as if it had a rail. Source/RunCache.rs:207-214 turns that Err into a miss, removes the directory, and recomputes cold.

criteria.text: The run cache is not disabled wholesale; warm hits still occur for programs that legitimately cache
criteria.evidence: Not disabled wholesale: cargo test --test run_cache shows the pre-existing warm-hit tests still green (warm_hit_skips_front_end_and_matches_stdout, phases_zero_on_inprocess_warm_hit, default_run_stays_jit_module_cache_not_aot all ok). The withdrawn capture-site opt-out was NOT reintroduced. tests/run_cache.rs:418-430 runs a traced third run on the failing row and requires a literal [run-cache] hit, proving the row passes from the warm path rather than from a refused artifact recompiling cold - identical output alone would not have distinguished those.

criteria.text: A warm-hit test covers a fixture that exits non-zero, not only exit-0 fixtures
criteria.evidence: The matrix includes a non-zero-exit fixture: examples/features/errors/default_err_edge.jet, must_exit_nonzero = true. Previously every warm-hit fixture exited 0, which is exactly why this defect was invisible.

cards.title: jit_covered_example_stems drops stems silently, the same hole as the coverage audit
cards.body:
Sibling of #1998, found while fixing it. `observe_jit_coverage` silently dropped any stem whose in-process Loader or Sema failed, so 81 of 496 stems never entered the audit's universe; #1998 replaced that with a total three-way classification.

`jit_covered_example_stems` still has the SAME silent-drop defect, and it feeds `cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`. So the three-way differential battery is scoped to an unstated denominator in exactly the way the coverage audit was: stems it cannot load are not reported as uncovered, they simply are not tested, and the battery still reports success.

That is the same false-confidence class #1998 and #1663 exist to correct, one battery further out.
cards.plan:
Give jit_covered_example_stems the same totality #1998 gave observe_jit_coverage: every stem lands in a named bucket, an out-of-universe stem carries a counted reason, and the battery states the universe it is scoped to rather than implying the corpus.

Prefer sharing the classification helper #1998 introduced over writing a second one — two oracles that can disagree is the defect being removed, not a smaller version of it (I8).

criteria.text: jit_covered_example_stems classifies every stem it walks; no code path drops a stem without a counted reason
criteria.evidence: jit_covered_example_stems no longer exists. It had a single caller, so rather than wrapping it the function was DELETED and cranelift_three_way_differential_battery now reads the shared memoised observation directly. Its three silent drops are therefore gone by construction: the Err(_) => continue on Loader failure, the bare continue on any Sema error, and a third implicit drop where a stem failing either resident_jit_safe_bundle or try_compile_bundle was pushed nowhere and counted nowhere.

criteria.text: It shares the classification helper introduced for observe_jit_coverage rather than reimplementing it
criteria.evidence: There is one oracle, not two. classify_jit_compile feeds observe_jit_coverage, memoised once per test binary by collect_jit_coverage, and both jit_coverage_audit_inner and cranelift_three_way_differential_battery_inner destructure that same value. The generalization was made to the existing helper rather than beside it: JitCompileVerdict::Covered became a struct variant carrying resident_refusal, and the second question is asked only in the try_compile Ok arm, so the audit's covered, gaps and out_of_universe sets are byte-for-byte unchanged. A source audit confirmed no second corpus walk remains in tests/: all 21 other try_compile_bundle callers are single fixtures.

criteria.text: cranelift_three_way_differential_battery states the universe it is scoped to, and cannot report success while that universe is incomplete
criteria.evidence: The battery states the universe it is scoped to, before and after the walk, and cannot report success while that universe is incomplete. It prints the scope line before the loop so a differential failure inside cannot suppress it, then buckets every universe stem into ran / no_golden / held_back and asserts ran + no_golden + held_back == resident_safe.len(), so no code path leaves a stem uncounted. The previously anonymous web/app_hello skip became a counted row with its reason, and is now held back by a DERIVED service predicate rather than by name.

criteria.text: The universe size is pinned so a stem cannot silently leave it
criteria.evidence: The universe size is pinned outside the files it guards: EXAMPLE_CORPUS_FLOOR = 496 and OUT_OF_UNIVERSE_CEILING moved from function-local to module scope so both readers assert them, plus RESIDENT_SAFE_FLOOR and THREE_WAY_RAN_FLOOR for the battery's own denominator. Recorded honestly for the next agent: an audit found the resident-safe and ran floors are slack by roughly 90 stems because they were set on a smaller corpus, so they hold but weakly until raised to observed counts; and a FOURTH silent-drop site was found in print_jit_op_report, which is report-only and cannot false-green but still re-derives coverage from its own walk.

cards.title: tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt is 122 rows stale, so its classifications cannot be cited
cards.body:
Measured while fixing #1998: the corpus holds 496 top-level stems and tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt records 374, so 122 stems have NO row in any gate section. The file's own stated invariant is that every top-level example appears in exactly one section.

Consequence, and the reason this is P1 rather than hygiene: several open cards cite this file's resident_jit and deopt_interp classifications as current evidence about which tier runs a stem. With 122 stems unclassified and the file not reconciled since the corpus grew, those citations are not trustworthy, and example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate cannot be green while the file disagrees with the corpus.

examples/features/tooling/data_plot.jet is one confirmed instance: it appears in no section at all.

This is a sibling of #1998 (the coverage audit's universe hole) and #1663 (the jit_gaps ledger's three hand-falsifications), and it must not be fixed the way those were broken: by hand-editing rows to match whatever an incomplete oracle currently observes.
cards.plan:
Re-derive the gate file from an observed run once, after #1998's total classification has landed, and pin its row count against the corpus stem count so a stem cannot fall out of a section unnoticed.

Do not hand-add rows. The reconciliation that produced the current state of tests/jit_gaps.txt (12648cdcc) made the ledger self-consistent with an INCOMPLETE oracle and thereby understated real coverage; repeating that here would be the fourth hand-edit of a file class that has already been falsified three times.

Sequencing: depends on #1998 being integrated first, since a re-derivation against a blind oracle reproduces the bug.

log.text: MECHANISM AND RE-DERIVATION BOTH LANDED at f7aab7bf8. The ledger is regenerated from an OBSERVED run, not hand-edited: JET_DUMP_CORPUS_GATE=1 JET_WRITE_CORPUS_GATE=1 cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate -- --exact --nocapture, 374 -> 496 rows, so every one of the 496 corpus stems now carries a section and the 122-stem hole is closed. tooling/data_plot specifically has a row. Hand-editing was refused on purpose: the sibling ledger tests/jit_gaps.txt has been falsified three times and a classification typed by hand is the same mistake. The ratchet closed in the same diff: CORPUS_GATE_ROW_FLOOR 374 -> 496 (may only grow), CORPUS_GATE_UNCLASSIFIED_CEILING 122 -> 0 (may only shrink), resting on an asserted classified + unclassified == corpus identity plus corpus >= EXAMPLE_CORPUS_FLOOR. Enforcement is cheap and host-independent: corpus_gate_manifest_accounts_for_every_example parses the ledger and walks examples/features/<topic>/ with no Cranelift host, no rustc and no run, and a negative-control test proves the audit actually names a missing row, a duplicate, a ghost and a reasonless exclusion. The strict gate's own duplicate ghost/unlisted check was deleted and now calls that one law (I8). Root cause of the staleness is recorded: the file last changed 2026-08-13, one day before d1aaf936e rewrote error handling across 39 net and serde examples, so those resident_jit rows were never re-observed. Two caveats worth carrying: dump mode returns BEFORE every ratchet so a regeneration cannot self-check, and stems file as expected_exit when rustc is absent, so regenerate only on a Cranelift-supported host with rustc.

criteria.text: Every top-level corpus stem appears in exactly one section of tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt, and the file's row count is pinned against the corpus stem count
criteria.evidence: Every one of the 496 corpus stems now appears in exactly one section, and the row count is pinned against the corpus stem count. Verified at 404bfb6fc by reading the committed ledger: 496 rows across frontend_rejected 46, gate_excluded 12, non_runnable 0, expected_exit 27, resident_jit 368, deopt_interp 34, run_tier_broken 9. CORPUS_GATE_ROW_FLOOR is 496 and may only grow; CORPUS_GATE_UNCLASSIFIED_CEILING is 0 and may only shrink; both rest on an asserted classified + unclassified == corpus identity plus corpus >= EXAMPLE_CORPUS_FLOOR, so a stem cannot leave the accounting.

criteria.text: The rows are re-derived from an observed run, not hand-added to match a classification
criteria.evidence: The rows were re-derived from an observed run, never hand-added. Command: JET_DUMP_CORPUS_GATE=1 JET_WRITE_CORPUS_GATE=1 cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate -- --exact --nocapture, run twice (374 -> 496, then again after serde/json_coerce started type-checking). Hand-editing was refused deliberately: the sibling ledger tests/jit_gaps.txt has been falsified three times and a classification typed by hand is the same mistake. Two caveats are recorded for future regenerations: dump mode returns BEFORE every ratchet so a regeneration cannot self-check, and stems file as expected_exit when rustc is absent, so regenerate only on a Cranelift-supported host with rustc.

criteria.text: A stem that leaves a section fails a test rather than disappearing
criteria.evidence: A stem that leaves a section fails a test rather than disappearing. corpus_gate_manifest_accounts_for_every_example parses the ledger and walks examples/features/<topic>/ with no Cranelift host, no rustc and no run, so the check is cheap and host-independent; corpus_gate_ledger_audit_fires_on_a_missing_row is a negative control proving the audit names a missing row, a duplicate, a ghost and a reasonless exclusion. The strict gate's own duplicate ghost/unlisted check was deleted and now calls that one law (I8).

criteria.text: tooling/data_plot specifically has a section and a reason
criteria.evidence: tooling/data_plot specifically has a row and a section: it is recorded under resident_jit, so the stem the card named as appearing in NO section is now classified and running on the resident tier.

criteria.text: No card's evidence still cites a classification this file no longer supports
criteria.evidence: No card's evidence still cites a classification this file no longer supports. Two consumers were corrected in the same work: serde_jit_parity_manifest_pins had asserted serde/encoding_breadth must remain compile-covered while the coverage oracle could not see the stem at all, and the ledger cross-check flagged types/no_any_alternatives as compile-covered while the gate recorded it frontend_rejected - that stem's example was repaired (a panic-to-error conversion had hoisted a DataTree literal out of one expression and broken sema) and it now runs, printing 3 / typed / present / jet. The re-derivation also exposed a NEW and sharper finding the stale ledger had hidden: 9 AOT-green stems sit in run_tier_broken, and the gate's own law asserts that section must stay empty. That is recorded and assigned rather than absorbed.

cards.title: concurrency/scoped_borrow_bands: the interpreter fails a task.all that AOT completes
cards.body:
Found by the strict corpus gate at c2eb365be (tests/dev.rs:9194, thread corpus-gate-5). The pure interpreter and AOT disagree on examples/features/concurrency/scoped_borrow_bands.jet.

AOT: stdout "[12, 34]\n12\n20\n34\n23\n23\n", empty stderr, exit 0.
Pure interpreter: empty stdout, and a Stop [E3001] `panic: task.all failed` raised at scoped_borrow_bands.jet:23 in run, from the `} ?? panic("task.all failed"))` arm.

So task.all succeeds on AOT and fails on the interpreter for the same program. This is an I9 tier-parity violation and a member of the silent-wrong-answer class: the interpreter produced a confident, well-rendered failure for a program that is correct.

The panic( arm is the example reporting the failure, not the cause. The cause is whatever makes task.all fail under the interpreter.
cards.plan:
Find why task.all resolves to a failure under the pure interpreter when AOT completes it. Per I9 the join/outcome semantics belong to the Prelude and the interpreter ambient is a marshalling adapter: if the ambient re-derives any part of task.all's completion or outcome, that is the defect. Do not weaken the example, do not replace the ?? panic( arm, and do not record this as a tier classification.

Related context: this epoch already found time.sleep not being a wait point (which made #Shield a semantic no-op) and a task's panic discarding the program's own message. Check whether either mechanism is implicated before looking wider.

criteria.text: The root cause of the interpreter-side task.all failure is named at file:line, and it is a single mechanism rather than a per-stem patch
criteria.evidence: Root cause named and it is one mechanism, not a per-stem patch. `left :: &particles[0]` is claimed by the split-view planner (TIR/lower/statements.rs:1473-1526 split_view_candidate, unioned at :1593-1637) so it lowers as TStmt::SplitViews and binds a __JetViewMut place region keyed by the OWNER LOCAL NAME (eval/stmts.rs:1936). eval_spawn clones captures into a fresh map for a child on its own thread, so the child scope holds `left` but never `particles`, and view_mut_owner_value / load_view_mut_owner_list did scope.get("particles") == None and returned unsupported("view-mut owner"). That Err became EvalTaskSelectError::Child, task_failure_value, CtValue::failed, and the example's own reporting arm. The representation was the defect: a write window keyed by a scope-local NAME cannot cross a thread.

criteria.text: concurrency/scoped_borrow_bands produces byte-identical stdout, stderr and exit code on AOT, default jet run, and the pure interpreter
criteria.evidence: Verified by orchestrator at 9164f7e13+bd-w3 merge in .claude/worktrees/builder: cargo test --test run_interpret = ok, 7 passed / 0 failed. scoped_borrow_bands_agrees_on_every_tier passes, asserting byte-identical stdout, stderr and exit code on AOT, default jet run and the pure interpreter.

criteria.text: Any task.all completion or outcome logic re-encoded in the interpreter ambient is deleted and replaced by a call to the same Prelude symbol AOT uses (I9)
criteria.evidence: Nothing was re-encoded: task.all already routed through the shared selector crate::task_group::jet_task_select (eval/mod.rs:1347), the same selector behind AOT's jet_std::jet_task_all, so no ambient copy existed to delete. The fix EXTENDED the one existing place-loan mechanism (I8) to __JetViewMut regions rather than adding a second: a shared Arc<Mutex<CtValue>> slot in place_loan_slots, a loaned handle carrying no owner local, and close_place_loans flushing into the owner place when the group joins. D-TASKBORROW1's "owner sees every write once the block ends" holds on BOTH paths - close_taskgroup (eval/mod.rs:2663-2671) computes the flush eagerly and returns joined.and(closed), so the cancelled path flushes too because its children are already drained.

criteria.text: A cross-tier differential test covers the case and asserts the tier actually compiled the function, so a silent deopt cannot supply a passing answer
criteria.evidence: The differential asserts the tier, and that assertion earned its keep twice. First it rejected the initial fix: output matched but the test reported 'default jet run reported no tier for run'. That was traced to a genuine second defect - a warm run-cache hit replayed captured tier-1 machine code and never called record_trace (tier_cache.rs:696), while every COLD route does record a `run` row (api_debug.rs:78/98, deopt.rs:373 with gap.rs:22-39 naming it), so an empty trace was only ever possible on a warm replay. Fixed by carrying the tier roster in the artifact (FORMAT 4->5, published at resident.rs:519-524, recorded at tier_cache.rs:744-762) - the same argument that already makes the artifact carry the entry error rail, since a warm run has no TIR program to ask. An output-only check would have called this stem fixed and shipped a silent reporting hole.

criteria.text: No stem is parked in a gap ledger and no skip guard is added
criteria.evidence: No stem was parked in a gap ledger and no skip guard was added.

cards.title: tooling/data_json: the interpreter fails a data.json decode that AOT completes
cards.body:
Found by the strict corpus gate at c2eb365be (tests/dev.rs:9194, thread corpus-gate-5). The pure interpreter and AOT disagree on examples/features/tooling/data_json.jet.

AOT: stdout "team:String
minutes:Float
selected:2
Tools:5.0
Core:8.0
empty_struct:0
generic:value:Int
core.data.json:native
", empty stderr, exit 0.
Pure interpreter: empty stdout, and a Stop [E3001] `panic: bad json` raised at data_json.jet:20 in run, from `rows :: data.json<Ticket>(raw) ?? panic("bad json")`.

So a typed generic JSON decode succeeds on AOT and fails on the interpreter for the same input. This is an I9 tier-parity violation of the silent-wrong-answer class.

Note the last line of the AOT output, `core.data.json:native`: the example itself asserts which implementation answered, so the interpreter is not merely slower, it is taking a different path.
cards.plan:
Find why data.json<Ticket> decode fails under the pure interpreter while AOT decodes the same text. Per I9 the decode is Prelude/CoreLib semantics and the interpreter ambient marshals only; a re-implemented or partially-implemented decode in the ambient is the defect. Generic type argument handling is the first suspect, since the failing call is data.json<Ticket> with a user struct and the sibling generic surface prints generic:value:Int.

Do not weaken the example and do not change the golden.

criteria.text: The root cause of the interpreter-side decode failure is named at file:line
criteria.evidence: Root cause named: TIR/eval/data_calls.rs:553-558 decode_json_rows was a STUB that discarded every argument and unconditionally returned err(decode_error("data.json on the JIT interpreter path is not wired yet")). The generic type argument was never lost - list_elem already recovered Ticket; the interpreter simply had no decoder. Its csv sibling at :506-551 was the second half of the same defect: a full re-implementation with a hand-written cell-type ladder (parse_cell, :71-108) parallel to the shared decode.

criteria.text: tooling/data_json produces byte-identical stdout, stderr and exit code on AOT, default jet run, and the pure interpreter
criteria.evidence: Verified by orchestrator at 9164f7e13+bd-w3 merge in .claude/worktrees/builder: cargo test --test run_interpret = ok, 7 passed / 0 failed. data_json_agrees_on_every_tier passes, asserting byte-identical stdout, stderr and exit code on AOT, default jet run and the pure interpreter.

criteria.text: The interpreter reaches the same Prelude decode symbol AOT embeds; any re-implemented decode path in the ambient is deleted (I9)
criteria.evidence: The interpreter now reaches the shared symbols and the duplicates are deleted. Getting there took removing three separate blockers found in sequence, each surfaced only by re-running: (1) the decode stub and the duplicate csv ladder; (2) a spurious L0502 float-comparison warning that made AOT alone write to stderr - it fired on the COMPILER-GENERATED auto-derive Equatable.equal body, which Sema/Registration/Derives.rs:93-102 builds at the struct's name_span, so any struct with a Float field warned at its own declaration (the enum arm at :436-442 had the same defect, and a committed snapshot tests/ui_lint/float_money.warn had BLESSED the wrong behaviour); (3) core.data.table/rows/schema sat in a blanket unsupported arm at eval/data_calls.rs:407 while the kernel answering them existed only as a private method on the AST comptime interpreter. That kernel was extracted to Comptime/DataPipeline.rs (table_value:145, rows_value:166, schema_columns_for_type:175, schema_value:210) and both interpreters now delegate to it - the AST interpreter's own copy was deleted, so this closed by removing a duplicate rather than adding a third path.

criteria.text: A cross-tier differential test covers a typed generic decode and asserts the tier actually compiled the function
criteria.evidence: A cross-tier differential covers a typed generic decode: the example's golden requires the type-driven schema path specifically, since [Empty].{} must yield 0 columns and [Box<Int>].{} must yield value:Int after substituting T->Int, which is why the schema lookup reads sema's registered field/type tables rather than sampling a row.

criteria.text: No stem is parked in a gap ledger and no skip guard is added
criteria.evidence: No stem was parked in a gap ledger and no skip guard was added. Boundary admission was checked and proven NOT required rather than assumed: the failure was a runtime E2201 at data_json.jet:21, which proves dispatch already reached eval_core_data_call, the registry row core.data.table -> jet_data_table is CoreCallCoverage::ALL, and the JIT boundary already admitted table|rows|schema at safety.rs:1449.

cards.title: The strict corpus gate hangs 30s on web/app_hello because a server example has no bounded stop
cards.body:
Found by the strict corpus gate at c2eb365be (tests/dev.rs:418). The compiled binary for examples/features/web/app_hello.jet prints `serving http://127.0.0.1:8080` and then never exits, so the gate kills it after 30s and records a classification failure.

This is not a tier divergence. It is a harness/corpus contract gap: the gate compiles and RUNS every top-level stem, and a server example's correct behaviour is to serve until stopped. Under the current contract a correct program is indistinguishable from a hung one.

Cost: 30 seconds of every gate run, plus a classification failure that masks whether anything else about this stem is wrong. Card #1796 covered a DIFFERENT app_hello failure (Rc<dyn Fn> not Send) and is closed; this is new.
cards.plan:
Decide the contract deliberately, then implement it once for the whole family rather than special-casing one stem. Either a server-shaped example declares a bounded stop the harness can drive (serve-then-exit on a signal, a request budget, or a documented run mode), or the gate declares such stems out of its RUN universe with a counted, named reason while still requiring them to COMPILE.

The second option must follow the rule established for the coverage audit's universe on card #1998: an excluded stem carries a named reason and is counted, so the number can only shrink. A bare skip list is not acceptable.

Audit for siblings: any other stem that serves or waits indefinitely has the same problem and must be handled by the same mechanism.

criteria.text: The chosen contract is recorded, and it is one mechanism applied to every indefinitely-running stem rather than a per-stem exception
criteria.evidence: The contract is recorded and it is one mechanism, not a per-stem exception. A service entry leaves the gate's RUN universe and stays in its COMPILE universe. The reason is DERIVED from the program by jet_foundation::AST::bundle_serves_until_stopped, never a stem list, and the four private returns_app copies that previously encoded the same fact with no shared predicate were deleted. That absence of a shared predicate is precisely why nothing forced the gate to notice when commit 36e558986 turned three examples into services.

criteria.text: The strict corpus gate no longer spends its timeout on web/app_hello, and a genuinely hung program is still distinguishable from a correct server
criteria.evidence: Verified at 16345204a: cargo test --test dev -- example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate --exact no longer reports web/app_hello at all, and the gate no longer spends a 30-second timeout on it. A genuinely hung program stays detectable because exclusion is a compiler fact rather than a timeout waiver: DEV_DIFF_TIMEOUT still applies to every non-service stem, and a service that stops compiling now fails an explicit assertion, since try_compiled_binary_build was split out of try_compiled_binary_output so a service can be compiled without being run.

criteria.text: Every server-shaped or indefinitely-waiting stem is enumerated and handled by that mechanism
criteria.evidence: The whole family was enumerated rather than left to the next timeout. Three stems return App and were all in the run universe: web/app_hello, web/web_app and web/app_typed_args. Only app_hello ever reported, because all three race a fixed port 8080 and the losers die E3001 instead of hanging. Already-excluded siblings with their own named reasons: net/http_server plus five http_server_* and socket_echo (network service), game/raylib_window, ui/ui_native_linux, lowlevel/cross. Confirmed genuinely bounded and correctly left in the run universe: net/http_readiness, http_rest_service, http_routes, http_server_limits, http_web_defaults, ws_echo, http_client, http_get. Flagged as a latent host-dependent hang, bounded only by stdin EOF rather than by the program: io/stdin_filter and io/io_surface.

criteria.text: If any stem is excluded from the run universe, the exclusion is counted and carries a named reason, and the stem is still required to compile
criteria.evidence: The exclusion is counted and shrink-only, following the rule card #1998 established: CORPUS_GATE_EXCLUDED_CEILING = 12 in tests/dev.rs asserts that GateExcluded records may only decrease, with the message telling a future reader to drive the stem instead of excluding it. A bare skip list is what let stems leave a universe unnoticed, so a ceiling makes leaving cost a reviewed edit. The stem is still required to compile.

criteria.text: example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate reaches its own assertion without a timeout kill
criteria.evidence: example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate reaches its own assertion with no timeout kill. The three-way differential battery holds services back by the same derived predicate rather than by a hardcoded stem name, so a fourth service example is classified instead of being discovered by a timeout.

cards.title: One stdin fixture source for the three harnesses that feed terminal examples
cards.body:
Found while closing #2009. examples/features/io/terminal_parity.jet needs stdin, and the answer bytes are hardcoded in three places today: tests/golden.rs:469 (b"\nnot-a-number\n3\n2\n"), tests/corelib_parts/http_data.rs:1362, and tests/terminal.rs (four call sites, the PTY one appending a trailing "secret\n").

Two dev.rs batteries feed NO stdin at all and compare a no-input run against the fed-stdin golden: interpreter_matches_expected_golden (via dev_iteration_with_timeout) and assert_io_cli_terminal_time_three_way (via dev_iteration plus compiled_binary_output). Before #2009 that mismatch presented as a 30s hang; after #2009 it is a fast, readable golden mismatch, which is why this is now tractable.

The hard half: dev_iteration_with_timeout runs IN-PROCESS on a worker thread (tests/dev.rs:463-471), so there is no child stdin to pipe. That half needs either a real subprocess or an injected reader. dev.rs:228 compiled_binary_output_with_stdin takes Option<&Path> while golden.rs hardcodes bytes, so the signatures disagree too.

That combination is why this is a design task and not plumbing, and why it is its own card rather than folded into a terminal lane.
cards.plan:
Introduce one stem-to-stdin-answers source, read by golden.rs, both dev.rs batteries, and terminal.rs. One fixture, N readers (I8) — a fourth hardcoded copy of the same byte string is the defect, not the fix.

Resolve the in-process half explicitly: either dev_iteration_with_timeout gains an injected reader, or the battery moves to a real subprocess. Say which and why, since the choice decides whether the interpreter path is exercised in-process or out.

Unify the signature disagreement between compiled_binary_output_with_stdin (Option<&Path>) and golden.rs (inline bytes) rather than adding a converter at each call site.

log.text: Dedupe note: shares tests/golden.rs with #2025 and tests/dev.rs with #2076 but scopes are disjoint — this card unifies the stdin fixture source; #2025 owns red-target/routine-set enforcement; #2076 owns oracle build caching.

leftover criterion 5: fixture wiring is in; runtime proof blocked by a repo-wide generated-Rust ICE. cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run (JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/terminal_parity) fails I1 unsafe then rustc E0433 crate::ice! missing diagnostic template hole. cargo test --test terminal fails the same E0433 on all three terminal_parity tests. Same ice! on basics/hello. Not a stdin-fixture defect; log and leave #5 open.

cards.title: 53 shipped examples fail in-process Loader or Sema and were invisible to every coverage claim
cards.body:
Exposed by #1998, which replaced the JIT coverage oracle's two silent `continue`s with a total three-way classification. Measured at c2eb365be by `cargo test --test dev -- jit_coverage_audit --exact --nocapture`:

  jit compile-coverage universe: 496 example stem(s) = 415 compile-covered + 28 compile gap(s) + 53 outside this oracle

Those 53 shipped examples FAIL in-process Loader or Sema. They were invisible for as long as the oracle existed, so no coverage or parity claim has ever included them. Breakdown by diagnostic, with a representative stem and the real message:

- 28x sema E2402 - `?` can't convert `NetError` into `Err` - no declared conversion exists (net/dns_lookup, net/email_dkim, net/email_message, net/http_rest_service, net/http_routes, net/http_server_lifecycle, and 22 more; the net/* and serde/* families)
- 7x loader E0606 - project module `project.math` is declared more than once (modules/fact_value_arguments, modules/generic_modules, modules/inline_module, modules/library, modules/module_inline_sibling, modules/pub_file, +1)
- 5x sema E0405 - `?? return` here needs a value (net/http_client, net/http_get, net/http_readiness, tooling/debug_native, web/ui_showcase)
- 3x sema E0113 - `run` promises to return Unit ? Err, but this `return` is empty (concurrency/parallel_scan, concurrency/parallel_scan_expert, io/watcher)
- 2x sema E0740 - `run` uses the effect `Panic`, which its signature doesn't allow (crypto/vault_keys, io/db_read_footprint)
- 1x each: E0510 core.crypto.vault.get requires an audited #Unsafe region (crypto/vault_secret); E0712 #Grant region uses Panic without capability (effects/effect_grant); E0106 the name `Queue` is built in and can't be redefined (memory/pin); E1101 `changed` cannot cross the `task capture` boundary (memory/shared_guard_queue); loader E0003 expected `::` or `:=` (modules/package); E1004 core.encoding.json has no item `decode` (serde/json_coerce); E0107 nothing named `time` exists here (text/duration_facts); E0956 core.compiler.lex is compile-time only (tooling/compiler_api)

The split that matters is whether each is (a) an in-process HARNESS gap - the stem needs a package/manifest context the oracle does not construct, and compiles fine in the corpus - or (b) a real frontend defect on a shipped example. The uniformity of the 28x E2402 and 7x E0606 suggests (a) for those two families, and the singletons look more like (b), but NEITHER has been established. Do not assume.

Known related cards, check before duplicating: #1782 owns modules/generic_modules E0956/E0107; #2002 owns E1004 rejecting json.decode then suggesting json.decode; tooling/compiler_api's E0956 is the same family as #1782.
cards.plan:
Establish the (a)/(b) split with evidence, one family at a time, largest first.

For an (a) family, the fix is to make the oracle construct the context the corpus gate already constructs, so the stems enter the universe and are actually judged. Declaring them permanently out-of-universe is the weaker outcome and must be justified per family, not per stem.

For a (b) stem, the example or the front end is genuinely broken and the audit was hiding it; fix the defect. E2402 in particular is a real language question: 28 shipped net/* examples using `?` on NetError with no declared conversion is either a missing Prelude conversion or 28 examples written against a surface that no longer exists.

Whatever the outcome, OUT_OF_UNIVERSE_CEILING in tests/dev.rs must be lowered by exactly the number of stems this card recovers, in the same diff. The ceiling is the ratchet: the population may only shrink.

Do not add a skip list, and do not raise the ceiling to accommodate a new failure.

log.text: Closed on integrated evidence: every family is either recovered or justified, the NetError conversion is fixed at the mechanism, the ceiling moved with the recovered stems, diagnostic_snapshots is green and the last stem (compiler_api) now runs in-process.

Criterion 2 and criteria 6-9 remain open, and the blocker is named: they need the corpus ledger regenerated from an observed run, which cannot happen until #2103 lands, because the differential gate is aborted by the 900s in-process guard at 923s wall and so never reaches its write phase. Specifically: criterion 2 needs the harness-context families re-derived into the oracle's universe from a real run; criteria 6-9 are the syntax chores (Syntax.rs entry, syntax-decisions log, regenerated grammars, reblessed snapshots) which this card only owes if its work introduced surface, and it did not - the recovery was a Prelude conversion rail plus ceiling corrections, no new user-typeable syntax. Recommend closing 6-9 as not-applicable once an owner or reviewer confirms that reading; I have not marked them met because I did not want to silently reinterpret a criterion.

Criteria note: the trailing syntax-chore rows (Syntax.rs entry, grammars regenerated, snapshots re-blessed) are inapplicable — this card changes no syntax surface. Meet them with evidence "n/a: no syntax change" unless a (b)-stem fix touches diagnostics snapshots, in which case re-bless those and name the causing compiler change.

D-FAIL-CONV2=A IMPLEMENTED AND REVERTED THREE TIMES; the ruling is right, the injection STRATEGY is wrong. Work preserved on branch bd-conv and tag e3-conv-rail at fc523963f, three commits, buildable. What landed and is correct: one Prelude/Errors.jet declaring 13 impl <CoreError> => Err on the existing D-ERR-CONV rail; inject_error_conversions in Sema/Prelude.rs mirroring the Prelude/Units.jet shape, called from Bundle/Pipeline.rs before registration, skipping NoPrelude and no_alloc modules and yielding to any user-declared pair; a derived family with a stated 3-part criterion (BrowserError DBError DataError EncodingError EnvError HTTPError IOError JSONError NetError RangeError TextError UTF8Error WsError) recorded as is_core_error_family_type; CryptoError excluded by law because a secret-bearing type must not flatten into a message (E0915) and TaskFailure excluded because D-FAIL-CARRIER1 owns it; a new example plus golden for I5; the JIT interpolation fall-through routed to lower_jet_show_value (the same route print takes) with a CoreErrorCarrier table; core_alias_leaf taught the family so the dotted import-alias spelling resolves; and the display seam spelled crate::JetDisplay so it resolves both in a generated program, where the fragment is the crate root, and in jet-jit, where it is included at depth 0. THE DEFECT IS BLAST RADIUS, measured three times: attempt 1 took dev from 138 passed / 8 failed to 68 / 78 because the JIT could not interpolate a Named error type; attempt 2 failed to compile jet-jit on the display seam; attempt 3 built clean and still gave 87 / 59. Cause: every module receives all 13 conversion functions whether it needs them or not, so any defect in any one of them breaks every program. DIRECTION FOR THE NEXT ATTEMPT: make the injection DEMAND-DRIVEN - inject only the conversions a module actually exercises, determined from the error types its own ? operators can produce, so blast radius scales with use instead of being total. That also removes the 13-dead-functions-per-module cost the first lane flagged. This needs a worker with build access to iterate compile-test-fix; three source-only rounds could not converge because each defect was only visible after a 6-minute build.

CORROBORATED from a second direction at b3c8235cc. A lane working the json_coerce failure independently reached the same root cause and quantified the family: the re-derived corpus gate ledger shows E2402 rows for roughly 20 more corpus stems on the identical unmigrated D-FAIL-CONV1 pattern (serde/json, serde/encoding, net/dns_lookup and siblings). It also proved the decode surface itself is NOT at fault: the ledger row for serde/json_coerce reads E2402 rather than E1004, and that row was re-derived AFTER the untyped-decode arm landed, so json.decode(raw) does type as DataTree ? JSONError and the failure is purely the missing conversion from JSONError into the default Err. One example was migrated as the ratified explicit form to prove the shape works: examples/features/serde/json_coerce.jet now declares fn run() ? JSONError and the ledger records it as 'parity', i.e. agreeing across all three tiers. That is option B of ballot D-FAIL-CONV2 demonstrated on one stem. The remaining ~20 stay unmigrated pending the owner's choice, because doing them per-example is what this card's criterion 4 forbids.

Root cause established by lane audit, verdict (b) real frontend defect and NOT a harness gap. The oracle (tests/dev.rs:772+781) and the corpus gate (tests/dev.rs:9274+9288) call the identical Loader::load_entry then Sema::check_bundle(CompileMode::Run) pair, so no package or manifest context differs and there is nothing for the harness to reconstruct. Commit d1aaf936e (2026-08-14) mechanically rewrote x ?? panic(...) into x? and fn run() into fn run() ? across 39 net and serde files. That surface had been deleted 8 days earlier by D-FAIL-CONV1=A, which removed the implicit trait rail so sema now accepts only a declared impl X => Err plus the single Prelude String => Err arm. That is exactly why net/url_mime (errors are ? String) is covered while net/dns_lookup (? NetError) is not. It landed invisible because typechecked_example_stems() at tests/dev.rs:565-575 silently drops every sema-failing stem and feeds the filtered list to the dev default battery - the same hole #1998 closed in observe_jit_coverage and #2012 closed in jit_covered_example_stems, in a third oracle. That third hole is routed to the tests/dev.rs owner this wave. Also recorded: tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt last changed 2026-08-13, the day BEFORE the migration, so its resident_jit rows for these stems were never re-observed and are stale (card #2013). BLOCKED on ballot D-FAIL-CONV2: both remaining fixes are owner-gated. Option A ships one Prelude conversion, which is an unratified user-facing policy; option B corrects 28 examples, which this card's own criterion 4 forbids as a per-example fix. OUT_OF_UNIVERSE_CEILING deliberately left at 81 - on outcome A it drops by exactly the recovered count, and only an oracle run after the fix is an honest source for that number.

criteria.text: Each of the 53 stems is established as (a) an in-process harness/context gap or (b) a real frontend defect, with per-family evidence rather than an assumption
criteria.evidence: All 53 established, and the count itself was stale twice over. Re-derived at HEAD with a HEAD-matched binary over all 500 top-level stems: only FOUR stems actually failed in-process Loader/Sema - crypto/vault_secret, memory/shared_guard_queue, modules/package, tooling/compiler_api. The other 49 were already recovered before the work began: 36 by the ratified D-FAIL-CONV2=A core-error rail, 7 by the modules rename, 10 by sibling example fixes, and 4 singletons. Each class is recorded with its diagnostic and its recovering commit.

criteria.text: Every (a) family either enters the oracle's universe because the harness now constructs the context, or carries a per-family justification for remaining outside it
criteria.evidence: The last family is recovered: examples/features/tooling/compiler_api.jet now runs in-process (card #2094 closed) because its generated artifact is gitignored instead of committed. No skip list was introduced and no per-family justification remains outstanding.

criteria.text: Every (b) stem is fixed, or has its own card with the diagnostic recorded
criteria.evidence: Three of the four remaining stems were fixed at root and the fourth was carded: tooling/compiler_api is #2094, whose cause is that the example's OWN generated output was committed so the build API correctly refused to shadow it - and that is now fixed too, by deleting the committed artifacts per D-BUILDGEN1's 'never committed' rule. The lock digest is a hash of formatter output, so a committed generated file is stale by construction.

criteria.text: The 28x E2402 NetError conversion family is resolved at the mechanism level, not by editing 28 examples one at a time
criteria.evidence: Resolved at the mechanism level, exactly as the criterion requires and NOT by editing examples: one impl <CoreError> => Err on the existing conversion rail in Prelude/Errors.jet, with is_core_error_family_type consumed by the fallible checker. Worth recording that this rail was only half-true when the card was written: the conversions were injected AFTER body checking, so all 13 of them reached codegen un-normalized and ICEd - meaning the 36 stems were clean through sema and would have died in codegen. That is fixed (see #2008), so the mechanism-level claim now holds end to end.

criteria.text: OUT_OF_UNIVERSE_CEILING is lowered by exactly the number of stems recovered, in the same diff, and no skip list is introduced
criteria.evidence: The ceilings were wrong in BOTH directions and are now the values a measurement supports, with the provenance written into the doc comments: OUT_OF_UNIVERSE_CEILING 11 -> 1, SEMA_REJECTED_CEILING 11 -> 1, EXAMPLE_CORPUS_FLOOR 498 -> 497. The 53->11 drop in the snapshot commit had no measurement behind it and was ALSO wrong the other way: jit_gaps.txt compile_covered held 481 rows against a 500-stem corpus with gaps:0, so out_of_universe was arithmetically 19 against a ceiling of 11, which means jit_coverage_audit could not have been green at that HEAD.

criteria.text: Syntax.rs entry updated
criteria.evidence: No new syntax in this card: it fixes in-process loader/sema context gaps and the NetError conversion mechanism. Nothing to register in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs; no new keyword or sigil appears in the diff.

criteria.text: syntax-decisions.md log entry
criteria.evidence: Same reason as c6: no syntax decision to log. The mechanism fix (one Prelude conversion source for Net/serde ? consumers) implements existing ratified law.

criteria.text: jet devtools grammars regenerated
criteria.evidence: No grammar change: no new keyword or sigil, so jet self devtools grammars produces identical output.

criteria.text: snapshots re-blessed
criteria.evidence: cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots is green at HEAD: 11 passed, 0 failed (ui_snapshots and lint_snapshots both ok).

cards.title: The jet-codegen lib test target never ran, hiding a TIR coverage failure and a stack overflow
cards.body:
The `jet-codegen` lib test target has never been runnable, so 217 unit tests including the whole `Codegen::TIR::tests` coverage suite have never guarded anything. Found while verifying #2004, whose enforcement test lives in this target.

Two compile errors, both present at c14e1ec2f and fixed by the orchestrator in 3360a6bb0 so the target builds:
- `Codegen/mod.rs` tests module called `install_comptime_bridge` without importing it (E0425)
- `time_monotonic_pos` was bound twice, so the first binding was unused and `#![deny(warnings)]` rejected the crate

With the target compiling, two REAL defects are now visible (`cargo test -p jet-codegen --lib -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` at 3360a6bb0):

1. `Codegen::TIR::tests::covers_generic_optional_return` FAILS: `assertion failed: covers(src, "opt_id")` at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/tests.rs:2068. A generic function with an optional return is not TIR-covered. This is the same predicate family as #1976/#1986/#1987 and the same "sema admits, TIR does not cover" polarity as #2008.

2. `Codegen::TIR::tests::covers_labeled_loops` ABORTS the process with a genuine STACK OVERFLOW:
```
thread 'Codegen::TIR::tests::covers_labeled_loops' has overflowed its stack
fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
```
Note the discriminator that card #1997 documents: this is the textually distinct exhaustion pair (`has overflowed its stack` + `fatal runtime error: stack overflow`), NOT the `failed to initiate panic, error 5` case. So this IS real recursion depth, and raising a stack constant would be treating the symptom - something is recursing without bound on labeled loops.

Because the abort kills the process partway through the suite, every test ordered after `covers_labeled_loops` is still unmeasured. The pass/fail counts above are a floor, not the full picture.
cards.plan:
Fix both defects, then run the whole target once to find what the abort has been hiding - the two known failures are only the tests reached before the process died.

For `covers_generic_optional_return`: establish whether the correct outcome is that lowering learns the construct (preferred, real capability) or that sema rejects it with a registered diagnostic (I3/I4). Do NOT make `covers` return true without proving lowering handles it; a wrong true in a coverage predicate already admitted an unsafe function to the JIT this epoch.

For `covers_labeled_loops`: find the unbounded recursion. Treat a stack-size increase as a non-fix.

Then decide how this target stays runnable, because it silently rotted: it is not in the dev suite's build set, which is why two compile errors and two live defects sat undetected. Either it joins a routine target set or something asserts it compiles.

log.text: All criteria met by builder; orchestrator close.

DONE builder: full jet-codegen lib target 217/217 (+1 ignored) with --test-threads=1, no abort. Remaining hidden failures accounted: GetMap pins use Let list not body index; covers_after_sema installs TIR bridge and uses CompileMode::Check; prelude split test tracks Columns/ColumnList and real include! macros; stream cancel no longer resume_unwind. Compile ratchet in tests/workspace_crates.rs.
started: remaining jet-codegen lib failures after labeled-loop stack fix; account hidden tests and keep target runnable

PROGRESS at 1a4f7b0 (merged): the target now runs 186 tests, up from about 87 before, and both original defects are closed at their true causes. covers_labeled_loops was NOT unbounded recursion: the coverage walk is provably bounded (every stmt_in_subset and if_cond_in_subset arm recurses into a strictly smaller node, and the test nests only 4 levels). It was frame size against libtest's 2 MiB test thread - the test called Parser::parse and tir_covers directly, below all four funnels where CompilerStack installs the boundary for exactly this abort, whose doc names this exhaustion pair. Seven helpers now hop through CompilerStack::run_on_compiler_stack and COMPILER_STACK_SIZE was untouched. covers_generic_optional_return was the TEST using the wrong helper: bare Val(x) parses to Expr::EnumLit with an empty carrier and only sema rewrites it to Expr::Present, so the gate's rejection was correct; the assertion now runs through covers_after_sema and no gate was widened. STILL OPEN, criterion 3 not met. The abort moved rather than vanished, and it is now a DIFFERENT class: scheduler_host_tests::stream_drop_uses_the_shared_task_cancel_cleanup_path aborts with 'panic in a destructor during cleanup' then 'thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting.' That is the third distinct abort shape this epoch has met, alongside error-5 (missing unwind info, cards 1995/1997) and genuine stack exhaustion. A panic in a Drop during unwinding is the mechanism card 2007 owns (cancel raised while already unwinding), so that stem is routed there rather than duplicated here. Seven newly-measured failures in the previously hidden 97: Codegen::TIR::tests::concurrency_method_names, covers_optional_return_and_chaining, covers_recursive_struct_construction, refined_collection_results_have_exact_tir_types, rejects_range_switch_over_non_ident_subject, and Codegen::tests::aot_ffi_host_installs_bridge_reporter, core_prelude_stays_split_by_runtime_ownership. These are pre-existing defects the abort had been hiding, not regressions.

criteria.text: Codegen::TIR::tests::covers_generic_optional_return passes because lowering handles the construct, or sema rejects it with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot - not because the coverage predicate was loosened
criteria.evidence: covers_generic_optional_return uses covers_after_sema after install_comptime_bridge; cargo test -p jet-codegen --lib covers_generic_optional_return passed. Gate not loosened.

criteria.text: Codegen::TIR::tests::covers_labeled_loops completes without aborting, and the fix is the unbounded recursion rather than a larger stack
criteria.evidence: covers_labeled_loops already hops CompilerStack (no stack-size bump). cargo test -p jet-codegen --lib covers_labeled_loops passed.

criteria.text: The full jet-codegen lib test target runs to libtest's own summary with no SIGABRT, and every test the abort previously hid is accounted for
criteria.evidence: cargo test -p jet-codegen --lib -- --test-threads=1: 217 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (scale_100k), finished in 3.51s, no SIGABRT. stream_drop no longer abort: jet_stream_task swallows JetCancelUnwind so sender Drop is not a destructor-during-cleanup.

criteria.text: The target is kept runnable by a stated mechanism, so two compile errors cannot sit in it undetected again
criteria.evidence: Default-members still skip crate libs; tests/workspace_crates.rs::jet_codegen_lib_tests_compile runs cargo test -p jet-codegen --lib --no-run from the root suite. verify-full already shards every lib via tools/ci/test-shards.sh.

cards.title: The dev suite exceeds its own 900s budget, so ~30 tests never run and no summary prints
cards.body:
Measured at c89ccb688 by `JET_NIX_TMP_CLEANED=1 timeout 3500 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --no-fail-fast --test dev`. The run ends:

  jet test guard: exceeded the 900s suite budget - aborting; this suite must be split or sped up, not given a longer deadline
  error: test failed ... (signal: 6, SIGABRT: process abort signal)

Consequences, all measured in that one run:

- 169 tests are declared; only 139 ever START. About 30 never run at all, so they guard nothing.
- libtest never prints `test result:` and never prints its `failures:` section, because the guard aborts the process first. The only failure record is the inline `... FAILED` markers, which is why a full-suite log does NOT contain the failure bodies (re-run a single test with --test-threads=1 --nocapture to get one).
- Inline tally at abort: 123 ok, 16 FAILED.
- 43 individual tests each report `has been running for over 60 seconds`.

This makes every dev-suite pass/fail number a PARTIAL measurement rather than a result. The 2026-08-15 handoff recorded "121 passing / 18 failing", which is within noise of this run's 123/16 - strong evidence that figure was also truncated by the same guard and was never a whole-suite count.

The guard's own message states the resolution and forbids the easy way out: split or speed up, never extend the deadline. AGENTS.md agrees - a guard trip is a defect to report, never a limit to raise.

Separately worth recording because it is the good news in the same run: this abort is the BUDGET guard, not an unwind failure. No `failed to initiate panic, error 5`, no SIGSEGV, and no `overflowed its stack` appeared anywhere in the log. The 2026-08-15 handoff described the suite ending on a bare SIGSEGV; that specific failure mode is absent here.

The 16 inline failures at abort, for reference (several are expected-red pending the M13 tier-parity families and must not be assumed independent): cranelift_matches_variadic_fixed_writeback, cranelift_matches_plain_parameter_read_write_and_take_modes, jit_1216_adversarial_regressions, json_coerce_audit_reports_jit_gap_on_default_dev, interpreter_matches_expected_golden, range_values_run_in_resident_jit_without_fallback, jit_coverage_audit, jit_try_compile_manifest_matches, cranelift_three_way_differential_battery, stream_pull_hostile_matrix_matches_interpreter_jit_and_aot, concurrency_and_game_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot, example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate, collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot, unsafe_blocks_reach_the_canonical_tir_interpreter_boundary, crypto_auth_and_vault_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot, data_pipelines_and_parsing_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot.
cards.plan:
Split the suite so every declared test actually runs and libtest reaches its own summary. Do not raise the budget.

Where the time goes, from the same run: the 43 slow tests are dominated by whole-corpus three-way differentials (the `*_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` family, example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate, cranelift_three_way_differential_battery, jit_coverage_audit, jit_try_compile_manifest_matches). Each compiles a large slice of the example corpus, and several compile overlapping slices, so the same stems are compiled repeatedly across tests.

Two directions, and the choice should be stated rather than assumed:
1. Split by cost into separate targets, so a routine target stays fast and the expensive corpus batteries run as their own target with their own budget.
2. Share the compile work. collect_jit_coverage already memoises one corpus observation per test binary via LazyLock; the differential batteries could read one shared observation instead of each walking the corpus. That attacks the cause rather than the symptom.

Prefer 2 where the batteries genuinely want the same observation, and 1 for the rest. Note that a split must not quietly drop a test from the routine set: the reason five jit_run failures went unrecorded for a whole session is that jit_run was not in the routine set.

Whatever the shape, the acceptance is that the summary prints and the declared count equals the run count.

criteria.text: cargo test --no-fail-fast --test dev reaches libtest's own summary and prints test result plus a failures section, with no budget-guard abort
criteria.evidence: Verified at 47225c565: every target reaches libtest's own summary and prints test result plus a failures section, with no budget-guard abort and no SIGABRT anywhere. cargo test --no-fail-fast --test dev --test dev_latency --test dev_interp_parity --test dev_default_parity gives dev 131 passed / 15 failed in 109.72s, dev_latency 1 passed, dev_interp_parity 3 passed / 2 failed, dev_default_parity 3 passed / 1 failed. The second run of --test dev_tier_parity --test dev_corpus --test dev_corpus_gate likewise reaches every summary: dev_tier_parity 8 passed / 11 failed in 370.08s, dev_corpus 3 passed / 3 failed in 405.22s, dev_corpus_gate 3 passed / 1 failed in 382.60s. Before this change the single dev binary aborted at the 900s guard having started only 139 of 169 declared tests, so no summary and no failures section ever printed.

criteria.text: Every declared test runs: the started count equals the declared count, and no test is silently skipped
criteria.evidence: Every declared test runs. All 166 #[test] functions were accounted for across the split (143 routine plus 2, 1, 16, 3, 1), verified programmatically rather than by eye: brace and paren balance zero per file, every non-blank original line surviving, and no duplicate or missing fn definition. A new test, every_dev_slice_is_wired_into_a_test_target, fails if any slice is included by nothing, so a slice cannot be orphaned. The measured totals above sum to the declared counts per target.

criteria.text: The 900s budget is met by splitting or speeding up, and the budget constant is NOT raised
criteria.evidence: The 900s budget was met by attacking the cause, and the budget constant was NOT raised anywhere. Measured root cause: ten curated tier batteries each carried a PRIVATE copy of one child-spawn loop and ran children strictly in series, roughly 160 optimized rustc builds nose to tail, and the three-way battery walked about 350 stems the same way. Every battery also held dev_diff_lock, so the whole binary was one serial chain. One shared run_child_stem_battery replaces all ten copies (I8) with test_worker_count(8) children and a cross-process FfiBridgeLock for bridge stems, and run_three_way_battery_parallel reuses the worker-queue mechanism the corpus gate already used for the identical three legs.
