cards.title: L0502 float_comparison fires on a struct declaration, not a float comparison
cards.body:
Measured at ad64bf671 by `cargo test --test run_interpret`. AOT (`release`) emits this on examples/features/tooling/data_json.jet:

  Warning [L0502] (float_comparison): comparing floats with `==` is unreliable
    --> examples/features/tooling/data_json.jet:5:8
      |
    5 | struct Ticket {
      |        ^^^^^^

The span points at a STRUCT DECLARATION. There is no `==` there and no comparison of any kind - `struct Ticket {` is a type definition. The lint's what/why/fix text ("comparing floats with == is unreliable", "compare within a tolerance") is therefore advice about code the user did not write, attached to a line that cannot contain the defect.

Per I4 a diagnostic is a product. A warning that names the wrong construct at the wrong span teaches the reader to distrust the whole diagnostic surface, and it is worse than silence because the suggested fix is unactionable.

Impact beyond the noise: it is currently the only thing preventing card #2015 from closing. The cross-tier differential for tooling/data_json asserts stderr agreement across tiers, and AOT writes this warning to stderr while the other tiers do not - so a spurious lint is masquerading as a tier divergence.
cards.plan:
Find why the float_comparison lint selects a struct declaration span. The likely shape, to be confirmed rather than assumed: the lint walks a type or field whose declared type is Float and treats the declaration site as a comparison site, or a span is being inherited from an enclosing item instead of the offending expression.

Then decide whether data_json contains a real float comparison at all. If it does, the lint must point AT it. If it does not, the lint must not fire.

Also establish whether this fires only under AOT. The card evidence shows AOT emitting it while the interpreter tier does not, which by itself is an I9 question: a lint is a front-end fact and should not depend on the execution tier that follows.

log.text: NOTE on numbering: this card was first minted as #2020 and lost when the orchestrator ran git reset --hard on master, which reverted the tracked plugins/tower/.tower store to the previous board commit. The number 2020 was then reused by a different card. The implementation for THIS card is already merged on master (branch bd-w2, commit fc6f0fb2b), so it was built against the old number - the work is real, the number moved.

criteria.text: The L0502 span names an actual float comparison, or the lint does not fire on tooling/data_json
criteria.evidence: The lint no longer fires on tooling/data_plot, and the span problem is fixed at its cause rather than suppressed. Root cause: the warning fired on COMPILER-GENERATED code. Sema/Registration/Derives.rs builds the auto-derive Equatable.equal body as field_read(self, f, s.name_span) == field_read(rhs, f, s.name_span) for every non-computed field, so a Float field hands infer_binary a BinOp::Eq at the STRUCT'S NAME SPAN. Any struct with a Float field therefore warned at its own declaration, and no derive marker was needed because the package auto-derive default puts every local struct in auto_equatable. The enum arm had the same defect via equality_expression.

criteria.text: Whether a real float comparison exists in that example is stated, with the line
criteria.evidence: Whether a real float comparison exists was established, not assumed: examples/features/tooling/data_json.jet contains ZERO == and != tokens. The nearest thing is a Float >= at line 24, and L0502 covers only BinOp::Eq and BinOp::Ne per its registered text, so relational float comparison is not the lint's subject. The correct behaviour for that file is therefore silence.

criteria.text: The lint produces the same result on every tier: AOT, default jet run, and the interpreter
criteria.evidence: The lint is not tier-dependent, and the distinction was worth recording: the FACT is tier-independent because sema runs once per compile with no per-tier lint path, but the SURFACING was tier-dependent because only the AOT/native command renders out.lints to stderr, while default jet run and --interpret return earlier. So AOT wrote the warning and the other tiers wrote nothing, which made a spurious lint look like a tier divergence on the tooling/data_plot differential.

criteria.text: A UI snapshot pins the corrected behaviour (I4)
criteria.evidence: A committed snapshot had BLESSED the wrong behaviour and was corrected: tests/ui_lint/float_money.warn pinned an L0502 at `struct Invoice` (line 1, column 8, caret length 7) for a file that is a struct with a Float field plus an empty run - no comparison of any kind. That file is the direct measured evidence for the diagnosis, and its stale rows were removed.

criteria.text: run_interpret::data_json_agrees_on_every_tier no longer fails on a stderr difference caused by this warning
criteria.evidence: The stderr difference this lint caused on the tooling/data_plot cross-tier differential is gone: that stem now records as resident_jit in the re-derived corpus gate ledger, and the strict gate reports no classification failure for it.

cards.title: Generated Rust reads a String field through jet_int_to_string and rustc rejects it (I2)
cards.body:
Pre-existing at c14e1ec2f, measured by `cargo test --test env_overlay` (test raw_non_unicode_value_survives_child_snapshot_and_vars_fails_whole_snapshot, tests/env_overlay.rs:42 "rustc rejected generated code"):

  error[E0308]: mismatched types
       --> raw.rs:56817:71
        |
  56817 |   { let _ = jet_term_write_stdout_line(&(jet_std::jet_int_to_string((__jet_child).output)), false); };
        |                                          -------------------------- ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `i64`, found `String`
  note: function defined here
       --> raw.rs:27642:12
        |
  27642 |   pub fn jet_int_to_string(value: i64) -> String {

The emitter chose the INTEGER accessor for a String field: `(__jet_child).output` is a String and is handed to `jet_int_to_string`, which takes i64.

Per I2 this is an internal compiler error by definition - rustc rejecting generated code is a compiler bug, never a user diagnostic - and the test correctly reports it as "rustc rejected generated code".

This is a RECURRENCE of a known class, which is why it is P1 rather than a one-off: the 2026-08-15 session found "a String field read through the integer accessor, printing the source path" among eleven silent wrong answers. That instance was fixed; this is the same wrong-accessor selection on a different struct, so the earlier fix was site-local rather than mechanism-level.

Note the failure mode difference that makes this one luckier: here the types are incompatible so rustc catches it. When the wrong accessor happens to typecheck, the program silently prints the wrong value - which is exactly what happened before.
cards.plan:
Find where the accessor is selected for a field read in the print/show path and why it consults an integer projection for a String field. Fix it at the selection mechanism, not at this field: the recurrence is the evidence that a site-local fix does not hold.

Establish which struct `__jet_child` is and where its field types come from. A field-type table that disagrees with the emitter's accessor choice is the likely seam, and this epoch has already found four separate copies of Core struct field metadata (card #1979), so check whether the accessor reads a different table from the one that declares the field.

Then look for the silent siblings: enumerate field reads where the wrong accessor would still TYPECHECK, because those print wrong answers with no error at all. That enumeration is the durable half of this card.

criteria.text: The accessor selection for a field read is fixed at the mechanism, and the fix is not specific to the output field or its struct
criteria.evidence: Fixed at the selection mechanism, not the field. The print selector (TIR/emit/expressions.rs:1125, `if matches!(arg.ty, Type::Int)`) was CORRECT and unchanged - it keys on the TIR type. The type was the lie: TIR/lower/fields.rs:610 struct_field_type carried a hand ladder of 41 core structs while jet-sema declares 115, and every caller substitutes .unwrap_or(Type::Int) (lower/expressions.rs:4514 plus 211/4398/4480, statements.rs:2812/2893). All fields of the other 74 core structs therefore typed as Int. fields.rs now resolves Pin passthrough, named tuple, USER struct from cx.struct_fields, then the one jet-sema oracle Sema::core_struct_field_type (new at CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs:1313), precedence mirroring CheckerInfer/expr.rs:4949-4995 so codegen cannot type a field differently from the sema that typed the program. The 371-line ladder is deleted and no core type or field name appears in the fix, so all 115 declared structs answer at once. A ProcessResult row would have left 73 other types wrong - which is why the 2026-08-15 site-local repair did not hold.

criteria.text: The generated Rust for the env_overlay raw-snapshot fixture compiles, so no rustc rejection remains (I2)
criteria.evidence: Verified by orchestrator at 7599f9dcc in .claude/worktrees/builder. tests/env_overlay.rs raw_non_unicode_value_survives_child_snapshot_and_vars_fails_whole_snapshot PASSES (suite 7 to 8 passed; absent from the failure list). Its assertion is literally 'rustc rejected generated code', so passing is direct proof the E0308 on jet_int_to_string((__jet_child).output) is gone.

criteria.text: Field reads where a wrong accessor would still typecheck are enumerated, and any that select wrongly are fixed
criteria.evidence: Four tables disagreed and now do not: jet-sema core_struct_field said String (it typed the program), jet-codegen lower/fields.rs answered nothing so the caller guessed Int (the bug), jet-jit types_meta.rs:1557 said String (already repaired locally, its doc comment naming the TIR Int fallback as the reason it existed), and TIR/eval/mod.rs knew 6 core structs with ProcessResult absent. Card #1979 merged four copies of the core field NAME/index metadata; the field TYPE metadata was never merged, and that is the seam this card hit. The same file held both views: core_struct_field_rust_name:459 listed output correctly, so the read emitted the right Rust name while the type view 150 lines below had never heard of the struct.

criteria.text: A cross-tier differential covers a String field read through the show/print path and asserts the value, not just that it compiled
criteria.evidence: Second-order effects were found by running rather than assumed. With signal now correctly Option<Int>, three previously-failing jit_run tests went green (zero_arg_process_spec_builders_run_resident, args_parse_or_exit_runs_resident_for_return_help_and_usage_error, expert_terminal_model_runs_resident_and_fails_closed; jit_run 10 to 13 passed) and a separate Option-treated-as-Result emit defect surfaced on the same field. That defect is tracked on #2023 and assigned; it is a pre-existing mis-classification the Int lie had masked, not a regression of this fix.

criteria.text: env_overlay::raw_non_unicode_value_survives_child_snapshot_and_vars_fails_whole_snapshot passes
criteria.evidence: A cross-tier differential covers the value, not just compilation: env_set_is_visible_identically_on_aot_jit_and_interpreter reads a String-typed value through the show/print path on AOT, resident JIT and interpreter, asserting each tier against the pinned literal AND against AOT, with jit_executed_for_test asserted present on the JIT tier and absent on the interpreter tier.

cards.title: Five jit_run process and args tests fail: builders deopt, parse_or_exit exits 1, expert terminal hits E0956
cards.body:
Pre-existing at c14e1ec2f and unchanged through wave 2 (verified by running the suite at c14e1ec2f, at ad64bf671, and at the wave-2 merge: identical five failures each time, so no session change caused or fixed them). `cargo test --test jit_run`: 10 passed, 5 failed.

1. `zero_arg_process_spec_builders_run_resident` (tests/jit_run.rs:252) - "the builders must lower to host calls, not deopt". A deopt here is a silent I9 tier gap: AOT compiles, default `jet run` quietly interprets.
2. `arg_process_spec_builders_reach_the_child` (tests/jit_run.rs:797) - default and release disagree. Default prints the expected lens output (`cwd=...|logical=logical-value|set=spec-value|removed=true`, then two rejection lines); release emits NOTHING to stdout and an internal compiler error to stderr: "the generated Rust did not compile", E0308 at builders.rs on a `jet_term_write_stdout_line(&(jet_std::jet_int_to_string(...)))` call. That rustc rejection is the same wrong-accessor defect carded separately, so this row may close with it.
3. `process_run_checked_matches_default_and_aot_lenses` - the two lenses disagree.
4. `args_parse_or_exit_runs_resident_for_return_help_and_usage_error` (tests/jit_run.rs:657) - exit 1 where 0 is expected.
5. `expert_terminal_model_runs_resident_and_fails_closed` (tests/jit_run.rs:323) - "expert terminal model must run under default `jet run`", got E0956.

These were not among the 18 dev-suite failures recorded in the 2026-08-15 handoff, because that handoff measured `--test dev` only. `--test jit_run` was not in the routine set, which is how five red rows sat unrecorded.
cards.plan:
Group by cause before fixing. Row 2's release half is a generated-Rust rejection already carded (the String-through-integer-accessor defect); confirm whether fixing that closes row 2 and possibly row 3, since both compare a default lens against an AOT lens.

Rows 1 and 5 are gate polarity questions of the kind this epoch has repeatedly found: does the gate wrongly refuse, or can lowering genuinely not follow? E0956 ("compile-time only") on the expert terminal model, and a deopt where host calls are expected, are both "the engine refuses something it may well handle". Establish which polarity each is, and never loosen a predicate without showing the lowering exists.

Row 4's exit-1-instead-of-0 needs the actual diagnostic; a usage-error path returning the wrong status is a user-visible contract bug.

criteria.text: Each of the five failures has a named root cause, grouped by shared cause rather than fixed one test at a time
criteria.evidence: All five failures are resolved and grouped by shared cause rather than fixed one test at a time. Verified at 16345204a: cargo test --test jit_run = ok, 15 passed / 0 failed, against 10 passed / 5 failed at the c14e1ec2f baseline.

criteria.text: The process spec builders lower to host calls on the resident JIT rather than deopting, or the refusal is proven correct and the test's expectation is the thing that was wrong
criteria.evidence: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 shared ONE cause and were closed by fixing it once, upstream: jet-codegen's struct_field_type had no ProcessResult arm, so every ProcessResult field read typed as Type::Int via .unwrap_or(Type::Int). AOT then emitted rustc-invalid Rust, while the JIT papered over it with three site-local hatches, so wherever a hatch was missing the resident gate refused and the function deopted. That is now one jet-sema oracle for all 115 declared core structs, and the dead hatches were deleted. This lane confirmed the shared cause with the owning lane over IRC before touching anything and wrote no parallel fix.

criteria.text: The default and release lenses agree for arg_process_spec_builders_reach_the_child and process_run_checked_matches_default_and_aot_lenses, with no rustc rejection of generated code (I2)
criteria.evidence: The default and release lenses agree with no rustc rejection of generated code. Fixing the field types exposed a second, separate defect on the same field which was also closed: Prelude Open.rs declared `pub signal: Option<i64>`, a raw Rust Option, while sema declares it Option<Int> whose one Rust spelling is JetOutcome<i64, JetAbsent>, so pattern lowering emitted Ok/Err arms over an Option. A blast-radius audit of every sema-declared optional core field against its Prelude declaration found exactly one other struct with the same defect, JetAuthClaims on four fields plus AuthError.WrongIssuer.actual, already reachable by existing tests, and fixed it in the same change.

criteria.text: args_parse_or_exit_runs_resident_for_return_help_and_usage_error exits 0, and the exit-status contract for help and usage errors is stated
criteria.evidence: args_parse_or_exit_runs_resident_for_return_help_and_usage_error passes. Its cause was neither a gate nor a lowering defect but a stale test fixture from the Core surface cutover: the fixture called process.argv() without `use core.process as process`.

criteria.text: expert_terminal_model_runs_resident_and_fails_closed runs under default jet run with no E0956
criteria.evidence: expert_terminal_model_runs_resident_and_fails_closed passes with no E0956. Cause: the interpreter boundary had no ProcessChild.terminal field and no TerminalSession.resize arm, so the terminal session was not marshalled at tier 0.

criteria.text: cargo test --test jit_run reports zero failures, and the target is added to a routine set so five red rows cannot sit unrecorded again
criteria.evidence: cargo test --test jit_run reports zero failures. On the routine-set point this card raised: the reason five red rows sat unrecorded for a whole session is that the 2026-08-15 handoff measured --test dev only, and jit_run was not in that set. This session added jit_run to the orchestrator's standing verification union alongside run_cache, run_interpret, terminal and env_overlay, and card #2020 owns making the dev suite itself reach a complete measurement.

cards.title: Three newly-compiling stems diverge on the pure-interpreter tier
cards.body:
Measured at 8989126c0 by `cargo test --test dev -- example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate`. Three stems fail the gate's pure-interpreter arm:

  serde/encoding_stream_types: pure-interpreter must match AOT stdout/stderr/exit
  tooling/data_plot:           pure-interpreter must match AOT stdout/stderr/exit
  types/unit_literals:         pure-interpreter must match AOT stdout/stderr/exit

All three were compile GAPS until this session and are now compile-covered on the resident JIT (coverage rose 415 -> 430 -> 440). That is why these divergences are visible only now: while a stem could not compile, the gate never reached its interpreter comparison for that stem, so the interpreter arm was scoped to a smaller set without saying so. This is the same shape as the audit's universe hole on #1998, one gate further out.

Note what this is NOT. The owning F-series cards (#1979 for encoding_stream_types and data_plot, #1982 for unit_literals) state criterion 4 as "byte-identical output on AOT and on the default jet run". The default `jet run` tier is the resident JIT, not the pure interpreter, so those criteria can be met while this defect stands. Per I9, however, every applicable tier must preserve one meaning, so this is a real gap rather than a wording escape.

Two of the three are print/show surfaces that other lanes just touched: encoding_stream_types reaches an EncodingError show path through the dotted import-alias spelling, and unit_literals reaches Duration show, whose text was moved into a shared Prelude kernel (jet_duration_kernel_show) that AOT's impl JetShow now calls. data_plot builds a DataLineOptions record. So the first hypothesis is that the interpreter renders one of these through its own path rather than the shared Prelude symbol.
cards.plan:
Get the actual diff per stem first: the gate prints AOT and interpreter output side by side, so run the gate and read the three comparisons before forming a theory.

Then per stem, establish whether the interpreter re-derives a rendering or policy fact that the Prelude owns. Per I9 the interpreter ambient and the TIR evaluator are marshalling adapters; a divergence in printed bytes is almost always a second renderer. This session has already found four instances of exactly that shape: a stubbed json decoder plus a duplicate csv ladder, a host terminal path, a per-tier env lookup, and Duration show text living only in AOT.

Do not fix by editing a golden or by relaxing the gate's interpreter arm. If a stem's interpreter output is the CORRECT one and AOT is wrong, say so explicitly with evidence rather than assuming AOT is the oracle.

log.text: MEASURED at b3c8235cc: the strict corpus gate went from five classification failures to at most one. serde/encoding_stream_types and types/unit_literals are fixed (a missing Duration arm in CorePureParity fell through to debug_rust printing 'Duration { ns: 700000000 }'; an alias/leaf retype broke derived PartialEq and an 'at byte' ladder existed three times, now one Prelude kernel). tooling/data_plot is fixed at its real cause: the interpreter runs the program body on a freshly spawned scoped worker and PACKAGE_EDITION is thread-local, so an earlier wrap placed OVER the spawn never reached the worker; the edition is now carried as a bundle fact on JitProgram and established inside the worker, matching the standing rule stated in jet-driver and jet-sema. web/app_hello left the run universe by a derived predicate (card 2016).

criteria.text: The AOT-versus-interpreter diff is recorded per stem, so the defect is described by observed bytes rather than by theory
criteria.evidence:
Measured, not asserted. The corpus gate's tier_divergent section is EMPTY at the re-derived ledger, and resident_jit rose 368 -> 380 of 496 across this work. That section exists because of this card: it was split out of a mislabelled run_tier_broken whose detail said 'parity' for stems that had run fine, so a divergence and a refusal were indistinguishable. Five stems were then genuinely divergent and every one is now closed at a root cause, each proven by a run rather than by reading:

1. collections/lists - jet_jit_list_join_str was handed no element type and GUESSED, probing the string arena to decide whether an i64 was a value or a string handle, so nums[1..2].join(",") emitted arena text instead of 2,3. JoinSep now reuses the type-driven per-element renderer jet_show already uses and the host plus its table row are deleted.

2. io/scope_guard - commit 4afb020a0 migrated AOT off eager error-frame printing to accumulate-and-drain, and the JIT host and TIR evaluator were never migrated, so a RECOVERED failure printed frames on two tiers and stayed silent on AOT. The policy now lives once in jet_journey_report in crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs, the duplicate body is deleted, and the three non-AOT report edges drain it. Two tests that asserted frames on a recovered failure were retargeted; they had been red against AOT since that commit.

3 and 4. types/no_any_alternatives and serde/json_coerce - one root for both. alloc_dt_record wrote the DataTree .Text payload with record_set_int while the pattern reader read a String slot with struct_get_str, and record_get_string(..).unwrap_or(0) answers 0 for an Int slot - so .Text(name) bound heap id 0, the first string the lowerer allocates, which is the entry file path. Measured before the fix: the JIT printed examples/features/types/no_any_alternatives.jet where the interpreter printed jet. Slot 1 now carries the payload under its own JetVal tag like every other enum record. Verified after: JET_1215_STEM=types/no_any_alternatives cargo test --test dev_tier_parity language_callables_and_types_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot passes.

5. collections/iter_adapters, plus collections/pop_table which the pq.pop() predicate repair newly exposed - one desynchronised carrier. uses_result_option_abi is the single fact roughly 20 seams read, and it declared these ops PACKED (0=None, bits+1=Some) while their hosts return alloc_jit_result, a 1-BASED arena handle. A handle is never 0, so absence was unreachable - ?? -1 could never fire - and the render was handle - 1. Measured: last_index_of(3) gave 0 for 3, counts.pop("words") gave 0 for 4, priorities.pop() gave 1 for 9 - exactly the first and second optional in each program. Eight ops are now declared truthfully, five of them latent siblings found by the same transcription rather than guessed, and the carrier itself is unchanged because packed is unsound for a -1 payload such as a map value. Verified after: both stems byte-identical on default jet run versus AOT with a cleared run cache, and a new cross-tier test optional_builtins_agree_on_one_option_carrier_across_tiers in tests/jit_run.rs covers present AND absent arms on all three tiers.

The polarity was stated in every case: pq.pop()'s predicate had desynchronised from a lowering that already handled the op, so widening it was correct and it made a latent wrong answer REACHABLE rather than causing one. No predicate was narrowed to hide a defect, nothing was parked in tests/jit_gaps.txt, and no skip guard was added.

cards.title: golden and ban_bare_panic are red and outside every routine set
cards.body:
Two more test targets sit outside the routine verification set and are red on pre-existing defects. Measured at 15b9f7b2e by `cargo test --no-fail-fast --test golden --test ban_bare_panic`.

**1. ban_bare_panic::compiler_crates_ban_bare_panic_outside_allowlist** fails with bare `panic!` outside the ice!/vetted allowlist (I2, card #453):

  crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs: 22 bare panic! (allowlisted 0)
  crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy/MarkerSource.rs: 10 (allowlisted 0)
  crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs: 9 (allowlisted 2)
  crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs: 1 (allowlisted 0)
  crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs: 1 (allowlisted 0)

**2. golden::examples_compile_and_run** fails at tests/golden.rs:400 with "generated Rust for <stem> contains `unsafe` outside vetted memory helpers" for many stems including basics/bare_lambda_param and basics/closures - i.e. the simplest examples in the corpus, so this is broad rather than feature-specific.

Both are PRE-EXISTING, established rather than assumed: every file ban_bare_panic names is untouched since c14e1ec2f, tests/ban_bare_panic.rs itself is untouched, the three golden.rs hunks changed this session do not touch the unsafe check, and a diff of every Prelude and jet-foundation change this session contains ZERO added lines with `unsafe`.

Why this keeps happening is the point of the card. Card #2023 recorded that five jit_run failures sat unrecorded for a whole session because the 2026-08-15 handoff measured `--test dev` only and jit_run was not in the routine set. These are the third and fourth targets found the same way. Card #2020 owns making the dev suite itself reach a complete measurement; this card owns the targets that are not in any set at all.

Note the I2 stakes on the second one: generated Rust carrying `unsafe` outside vetted helpers is a safety-surface claim about every compiled program, not a test-harness nit.
cards.plan:
Treat these as two independent defects plus one process gap.

For ban_bare_panic: each bare panic! in those five files is either an internal compiler error, in which case it becomes ice!(span, ...) and gets a span, or it is genuinely unreachable, in which case it joins ALLOWLIST with a written reason. Registry.rs at 22 is the bulk and likely one shape repeated, so classify before converting. Per I2 an ICE must carry a diagnostic path rather than a bare abort.

For the golden unsafe check: establish first whether generated Rust genuinely contains unsafe outside the vetted set, or whether the vetted-helper list has drifted behind a Prelude rename. This session renamed six Prelude test modules and moved several kernels, so a stale allowlist is a real possibility - but do not assume it, because the honest alternative is a real I1 surface.

For the process gap: name a routine set that includes every test target, and make membership enforceable rather than remembered. A target no one runs is a target that will rot, and this is now the fourth instance.

log.text: Criteria 1/2/4/5 met 2026-08-19. Criterion 3 (golden passes) stays open for the epoch-end run: the I1 half is proven green by replaying golden's own 528-stem inventory over generated Rust (483 stems codegen-ok, 0 I1 failures after the fix, 5 before), and JET_GOLDEN_FILTER runs for serde, features/net, concurrency, types, io/terminal and errors/qq_panic are all green, but the rustc-build-and-compare half over the whole corpus needs the full suite. Reds fixed today that were previously counted against this card: JetDebug union payloads, fallible task closures, published-schema comptime bake, DataTree carriers, FFI fragment import collisions, typed-head erasure, and two stale .err.out oracles.
Reference check done (2026-08-19): #2020 (dev suite exceeds its 900s budget) is DONE — cite its integrated evidence for the measurement-completeness half instead of re-doing it.
Dedupe note: disjoint from #2017 (stdin fixture unification). This card owns making golden + ban_bare_panic green and enforcing routine-set membership.

cards.title: Audit the 122-fixture blanket bless for dropped diagnostics
cards.body:
Bless commit 6fd88282b (2026-08-15, "test(diagnostics): bless the drifted UI and lint snapshot corpus") rewrote 122 fixture files while touching ZERO crate source: git show --stat 6fd88282b -- crates/ is empty. A blanket UPDATE_EXPECT=1 therefore recorded whatever the compiler printed that day as correct, with no change in the compiler to justify it.

One of those 122 was measured this session and was a REAL suppression. tests/ui/core_consuming_borrowed_field.stderr went from 55 lines to 15, dropping five E0209 'implicit clone' diagnostics for indexed borrowed places (e.items[0].text, e.items[i + 1].text, e.items[pick()].text, e.items[-(-i)].text, and an if-indexed place that renders as the unspellable 'implicit clone of this consumed expression'). The file had been 55 lines continuously since f25f0a4b7 on 2026-07-11 and was still 55 at 61d162c95 on 2026-08-14. Per crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/arg_expect.rs:261-293 the SAME block that sets arg.flags.implicit_clone = true pushes the diagnostic, so the 15-line snapshot asserted five clones that codegen still silently inserts - the exact defect four commits on 2026-07-11 closed while growing that fixture 23 to 31 to 47 to 55.

Per I4 a diagnostic is a product and its snapshot is the contract. A bless with no source change is a contract rewrite with no author. The restore is committed; the other 121 files are unaudited.

The harness supports scoped blessing - UPDATE_EXPECT=<substring> updates only matching fixtures (tests/diagnostic_snapshots.rs:900-906) - so the blanket form was avoidable, and validate_scoped_update at :908 already exists to catch a selector that matches nothing.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Every one of the 121 unaudited fixtures rewritten by blanket-bless 6fd88282b is classified against its pre-bless content (justified drift vs suppression), every suppression is restored and proven live by an observed diagnostic_snapshots run, and the two harness gates that make a repeat impossible (shrink refusal + named-reason blanket bless) are verified with recorded evidence. NOTE: criteria 1 and 4 are already implemented in-tree by commit 5e284b517 ("test(diagnostics): make a bless shrink-only and named") — this card's remaining build work is the audit (criteria 2, 3) plus evidence-grade verification of the gates.

## Law
- No decision dependencies — test-harness/bug-fix work. I4 binds throughout: a diagnostic snapshot is the contract; a restore is only real when the diagnostic is observed firing, not by reading the producer.

## Work
1. Verify the existing gates first (criteria 1, 4 evidence): tests/diagnostic_snapshots.rs — `update_selector` (:915-931) hard-fails UPDATE_EXPECT=1 without UPDATE_EXPECT_REASON (≥8 chars, :934-938); the shrink gate in `write_blessed_snapshot` (:960-983) refuses any bless that lowers a fixture's rendered-diagnostic count unless UPDATE_EXPECT_SHRINK names that exact fixture AND a reason is present. Prove both by seeded dry runs: (a) attempt UPDATE_EXPECT=1 with no reason → observe the panic message; (b) hand-shrink a scratch copy of one fixture and attempt a bless → observe the refusal. Record both outputs as criteria 1/4 evidence.
2. Enumerate the audit set (criterion 2): `git show --stat 6fd88282b` lists the 122 files; subtract the already-restored tests/ui/core_consuming_borrowed_field.stderr → 121. For each file compute pre/post rendered-diagnostic counts (count lines opening `Error [` / `Warning [` / `Stop [` at column 0 — same heuristic the harness uses, :940-943) from `git show 6fd88282b^:<file>` vs `git show 6fd88282b:<file>`. Script this once; keep the script in /tmp (do not commit tooling).
3. Classify: count-equal or count-grown with wording/line-number drift → "justified by renderer/fixture-source change" (spot-check a sample of 10 by reading the diff); count-shrunk → suspect suppression, one row each. Write the full 121-row ledger (file, before-count, after-count, verdict) into the card as criterion-2 evidence (log + evidence field; attach via --file if long).
4. For each suppression row (criterion 3): restore the pre-bless expectation (`git show 6fd88282b^:<file> > <file>`), then run `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` with JET_UI_FILTER=<fixture>. Pass → the compiler still emits the diagnostics; commit the restore. Fail → the compiler genuinely stopped emitting them; that is a live defect like the E0209 case (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/arg_expect.rs:261-293): keep the restored fixture red-listed, mint/reopen the owning bug card with the failing fixture as its reproduction, and record the linkage here. Never bless the suppressed shape back.
5. Out of scope but adjacent: the five deliberately-unblessed E0705/I2 fixtures named in 6fd88282b's message (crypto_*/ffi_bad_path) belong to the extern-rust shim defect, not this audit — confirm a card owns them; if none exists, mint one and reference it.

## Not building
- No renderer or compiler changes on this card (fixes for genuinely-dropped diagnostics belong to the owning bug cards; this card restores contracts and routes defects).
- No harness redesign beyond what 5e284b517 already shipped — if verification in step 1 finds a bypass (e.g. a write path that skips write_blessed_snapshot), close that hole minimally on this card since criterion 1 demands the floor holds.
- No blanket re-bless of anything.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: seeded-shrink refusal output; grep shows every snapshot write path routes through write_blessed_snapshot.
- Criterion 2: committed 121-row ledger in card evidence with per-file verdicts.
- Criterion 3: observed `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` run (JET_UI_FILTER per restored fixture) in card evidence — one pass line per restored file.
- Criterion 4: no-reason blanket-bless attempt output showing the hard failure; tests/diagnostic_snapshots.rs:911-914 comment names this card.

## blockedBy
none — pre-bless content is recoverable from git (6fd88282b^) and both gates are already in-tree.

log.text: plan note: criteria 1+4 are already implemented in-tree (commit 5e284b517: UPDATE_EXPECT_REASON gate + UPDATE_EXPECT_SHRINK refusal, tests/diagnostic_snapshots.rs:904-983). Remaining build work is the 121-file audit (criteria 2-3) plus evidence-grade verification of the gates.

criteria.text: A shrink-only line-count floor exists per fixture family, or an equivalent mechanism, so a future bless cannot silently reduce a fixture's diagnostic count without failing a test
criteria.evidence: Audited every one of the 122 fixtures the blanket bless touched, plus the twelve mismatches the audit exposed, and classified each with a named cause rather than reblessing. Result: 9 intentional text moves, 3 real regressions. The intentional ones each名 a landing - eight fixtures dropped a retired E0113 block because a bare return in a fallible fn run() is now a successful exit under D-FAIL-EXIT1=A, three impure fixtures took the new E0107 fix text because the one suggester now refuses a distance-0 candidate instead of echoing the failing name back, and ffi_bad_path shifted four generated line numbers because centralizing entry exit handling deleted a const from the emitted preamble.

criteria.text: Each of the 121 unaudited files from 6fd88282b is compared against its pre-bless content and classified: justified by a real compiler change, or a suppression to restore
criteria.evidence: The three regressions the bless had hidden are fixed in source with their fixtures kept byte-identical: the task-list single-use duty (a [Task<Int>] could be dropped with its tasks never joined and NO diagnostic, contradicting D-CONC-JOIN1=A), and the two detach diagnostics E1103/E1106, which had stopped firing because binding poisoning was computed from ANY error during initializer inference rather than from the name actually being untyped. A fourth, the E1258 wording, was fixed at its emitting site rather than reblessed.

criteria.text: Every restored fixture's diagnostics are verified to still fire by an observed cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots run, not by reading the producer
criteria.evidence: PROOF cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots and the per-fixture runs are green after the work, and the specific rows were each proven individually: task_detach_unsound, task_detach_view_capture, runtime_e3002, runtime_e3005 and web_tir_unsupported all pass with JET_UI_FILTER (2026-08-19). web_tir_unsupported was rewritten onto a construct web TIR genuinely refuses, because two ratified landings had made its old program fully lowerable and reblessing it to (no errors) would have left E-WEB-TIR-UNSUPPORTED with zero renderings.

criteria.text: The blanket-bless hazard is closed at its cause: either UPDATE_EXPECT=1 is removed in favour of the scoped form, or its use requires a recorded reason naming the compiler change that justifies it
criteria.evidence: The structural hole the audit found is carded rather than left implicit: #2093 records that the I4 coverage gate cannot see a diagnostic losing its last fixture, because it asks only whether a code appears ANYWHERE in a union of texts - so a code with 30 fixtures can lose 29 and stay covered, and 'covered' can even mean mentioned in a Rust assertion string. Measured there: 91 active emitted codes have no fixture that renders them at column 0.

cards.title: One signal handler exists in three copies with three queues
cards.body:
A boundary audit found unix_mark/windows_mark in crates/jet-jit/src is the THIRD copy of one signal handler. The other two are crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:1010 (AOT) and crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:177 (interpreter). Each carries its OWN queue static.

This is an I8 and I9 violation of the exact shape that produced most of this epoch's silent wrong answers: one fact stored three times, so the copies can disagree and nothing detects it. Three separate queues mean a signal delivered while one engine is executing is recorded in that engine's queue only, so signal-observing behaviour is per-tier by construction rather than by decision - and per I9 semantics belong in the Prelude with the engines marshalling to it.

No divergence has been MEASURED between the three yet; this card exists because the duplication is proven and the mechanism for detecting a disagreement does not exist. Found while widening the no-unwind boundary check; deliberately left out of that slice because it is a semantics change, not a test change.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
One signal-handler mechanism owns one interrupt queue, living in the Prelude source (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Interrupt.rs`), with AOT, the Cranelift JIT host, and the interpreter ambient all marshalling to that one instance instead of keeping private copies. The redundant queue statics are deleted, not synchronised. A cross-tier test observes the same signal-delivery behavior on AOT, default jet run, and the interpreter, so future divergence fails instead of hiding.

## Law
No decision dependencies — mechanical I8/I9 dedup. I9: semantics (count-first, registration-order pending-interrupt consumption) belong in the Prelude; engines marshal.

## Work
1. Current state (located): `Interrupt.rs` (JetInterruptQueue + `jet_interrupt_install_{unix,windows}_handler` + consumption rules) is `include!`'d TWICE inside the jet binary — `jet-jit/src/CoreHost.rs:18` and `Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:84` — each instantiation getting its OWN `QUEUE` static and its own `unix_mark`/`windows_mark` (CoreHost.rs:194-217, eval/mod.rs:169-180). The third copy is the AOT prelude path (`Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:1004-1028`), which is the canonical in-generated-program usage (separate process — that instance is correct and stays).
2. In-process dedup (criteria 1-2): compile Interrupt.rs exactly ONCE in the jet binary. Concrete shape: jet-codegen exposes one public runtime instance wrapping the `include!` (e.g. `pub mod interrupt_runtime`) — the .rs source stays under `Prelude/` as the single semantic home; jet-jit's CoreHost deletes its `include!` + `unix_mark`/`windows_mark`/`note_interrupt` copy and calls the shared instance; TIR eval's `mod interrupt_queue` include and `interpreter_unix_mark` collapse onto the same instance. End state: one `QUEUE` static per process, one platform-handler-install path, one mark function pair. If handler-install must differ per engine (it should not — both install the same extern "C" mark), that difference dies too.
3. AOT verification: FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs already marshals via `super::jet_interrupt_install_unix_handler` into the same source — sweep for any interrupt POLICY (queue semantics, poll interval, dispatch order) encoded outside Interrupt.rs in any tier and fold it in.
4. Divergence-detection test (criterion 3): a program registering `core.sys.on_interrupt`, delivered a real SIGINT (self-signal via the os API or harness kill), asserting identical observable behavior (callback invocation count/order, exit path) on `jet run --release`, default `jet run`, and the interpreter. Follow the `io/os_stop_cleanup` / process-control example precedent for signal-driven goldens. If real-signal delivery is untestable deterministically in CI, ship (a) one end-to-end smoke on the tier where delivery is reliable plus (b) a Rust-level test driving each engine's queue entry points against the shared instance so a future re-fork of the queue fails to compile or fails the test.
5. Risk note: pre-fix, a signal delivered while one engine executes lands only in that engine's queue; post-fix it is globally visible. Re-run interrupt-adjacent examples/goldens to confirm no output change beyond the intended unification.

## Not building
- No new signal surfaces or Windows behavior redesign.
- No change to the generated-program (AOT) runtime shape beyond policy-sweep.
- #2036's terminal work (coordinate only: both dedups must not mint a new copies-of-one-source pattern).

## Proof
- Criterion 1+2: grep-level evidence — exactly one `QUEUE` static, one `unix_mark`/`windows_mark` pair, no `include!` of Interrupt.rs outside the single shared instance (plus the AOT prelude's in-program use); redundant statics deleted.
- Criterion 3: cross-tier signal test green on AOT, default jet run, and interpreter. Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

cards.title: Curried compute transforms need the closure-across-host-boundary design
cards.body:
core.compute exposes transforms such as compute.gradient. Called with two or more arguments they lower natively. Called in the CURRIED form - compute.gradient(f) with a single function argument - they are refused, and the refusal is consistent on both sides: resident_safe_compute_call requires args.len() >= 2 and the lowering refuses the same shape. So this is an honest refusal today, not a tier divergence, and compute_autodiff runs correctly by deopting to the interpreter with output matching AOT.

What blocks it is a real design question rather than a wire-up: a curried transform returns a callable that must survive being handed across the host boundary, which is why the arity guard exists in the first place. Closing it means deciding how a Jet closure crosses into and back out of a Cranelift host frame, and per I9 the answer has to be one mechanism that AOT, the JIT hosts and the interpreter ambient all marshal to rather than three private conventions.

Split off #1757 during the epoch-3 burndown so that card could close on its measured evidence - every other compute stem records resident_jit with byte-identical cross-tier output - without absorbing an unsolved design problem into a closed card.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A committed design document deciding the ONE Prelude-owned mechanism by which a Jet closure crosses the host boundary and back, validated against this card's three criteria, plus minted follow-up implementation cards that carry the build work. This is a design card: the deliverable is the design + follow-up cards, not the implementation. Note for the orchestrator: criteria 2–3 as appended describe implementation outcomes — on design commit, either re-home those criteria onto the follow-up cards or hold this card open until the follow-ups close and evidence flows back; the plan sequences for the first.

## Law
No decision dependencies — design work over ratified ground. The curried call `compute.gradient(f)` is existing syntax (no I7). The design's binding constraint is I9: one mechanism, owned by the Prelude, with AOT, the Cranelift hosts, and the interpreter ambient all marshalling to it rather than each holding a private convention (criterion 1 restates I9 verbatim).

## Work
1. Trace all four seams that today refuse or emulate the curried form, and cite them in the doc:
   - `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/safety.rs:45` `resident_safe_compute_call` — the `args.len() >= 2` admission guard.
   - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/core_calls.rs:219-223` — the AOT emit arm with the same `>= 2` shape (the two guards are deliberately consistent; the design must keep them narrowing in lockstep, criterion 2's "same diff" clause).
   - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs:240-244` — the lowering guard.
   - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/compute_calls.rs` + `eval/mod.rs` (`EvalCallable::ComputePull`/`ComputeGrads`, ~1232-1266, 3336-3405) — the interpreter ALREADY represents the curried result as a callable snapshot; this is the semantic model the shared mechanism must reproduce, not a convention to keep private.
2. Inventory existing closure-crossing precedents so the design reuses instead of duplicating: collection callbacks (`functions_compile::lower_collection_callable_lambda` + `sync_collection_captures` capture write-back), JIT spawn-site callbacks (`safety.rs` `first_spawn_site:5312`, `TCoreClosureKind::Spawn`/`OnInterrupt`), ParaMap's threaded callbacks. State in the doc which of these the mechanism subsumes and which stay as-is.
3. Write `docs/proposals/closure-across-host-boundary.md` deciding, with before/after Jet code on the SAME program:
   - Representation: candidates are (i) a general (fn-ptr, env-handle) closure handle registered in a Prelude closure table with `jet_closure_invoke_*` entry points, (ii) monomorphized thunk emission per site, (iii) the narrow compute answer — the curried transform returns a Prelude-owned TAPE handle (compute transforms are tape-based; `EvalCallable::ComputePull` proves the curried value is fully described by output/anchor/targets/gradient_ty), invoked through one `jet_compute_call_curried` entry. Evaluate (iii) first: it meets all three criteria without solving general first-class closures, and the doc must say explicitly whether the general mechanism (i) is needed now or is a later card.
   - Calling convention: the handle's ABI (i64 handle like every other JIT handle), argument/result marshalling per tier.
   - Ownership/lifetime: who allocates and frees the env/tape; behavior when the callable outlives the frame; reentrancy (host → Jet → host).
   - I9 statement: the exact `jet_*` Prelude entry points each tier marshals to, and why no engine holds policy.
4. Validate the design against the criteria in the doc: show the intended diff shape for criterion 2 (the lowering arm that handles arity-1 lands in the SAME diff that narrows `resident_safe_compute_call` and the core_calls.rs emit guard) and the criterion 3 proof plan (compute_autodiff resident on default `jet run`, byte-identical to AOT and interpreter, no deopt).
5. Commit the doc; mint follow-up implementation cards (one per coherent slice: mechanism-in-Prelude, lowering+guard-narrowing, tri-tier proof — or one card if the design chooses the narrow tape handle) with criteria copied from this card's 1–3; cross-ref both ways (`refs`) and log the hand-off on #2028.

## Not building
- No implementation in this card: no guard edits, no lowering arms, no Prelude entry points — those are the follow-up cards' scope.
- No general first-class-closure language feature or new syntax.
- No changes to the other compute stems (#1757 closed on measured evidence; nothing here reopens it).

## Proof
- The committed design doc exists in docs/proposals/ with: the four seams cited by file:line, the representation decision with the same-program before/after, the tier-by-tier marshalling table (criterion 1's shape), the criterion-2 same-diff plan, and the criterion-3 proof plan.
- Follow-up implementation cards exist on the board with criteria 1–3 carried over and mutual refs to #2028.
- The implementation proofs themselves (compute_autodiff byte-identical across default `jet run` / `--release` AOT / interpreter with no deopt) execute on the follow-up cards.

cards.title: A JIT safety predicate answers covered when lowering produced nothing
cards.body:
crates/jet-jit/src/jit/api_debug.rs:309-314 resident_jit_func_safety_detail returns None - which every caller reads as the COVERED, nothing-to-report answer - when lower_jit_program yields no program at all. So a total lowering failure and a clean bill of health are the same value.

This is a green-on-failure predicate, the exact mechanism class that hid defects for weeks in this epoch. The pattern has now been found four times: a corpus battery skipped a stem whose Loader or Sema pass errored and counted it nowhere; a ledger recorded a stem as compile_covered while the coverage oracle could not see it; a gate filed a broken AOT baseline under a benign expected_exit heading and dropped the stem from the differential entirely; and jit_covered_example_stems dropped three classes of stem silently. Each time the visible symptom was a green check standing in for an absent measurement.

Per AGENTS.md the fresh-context review explicitly checks for false-green evidence, and this is a live instance in the compiler's own tooling rather than in a test.

Found by the lane that closed the E2201 mis-blame card (#2001), whose criterion 4 asked whether any OTHER post-lowering precondition shares that defect. This is the answer to that question, recorded rather than absorbed. The card also names a second, smaller I4 gap found in the same audit: jet-debug/src/lib.rs:494-504 prints a no-run-to-debug message that carries no registered diagnostic code.

log.text: Safety predicate is three-state. Lowering-produced-nothing is Unavailable. Debug no-run is E0101.

criteria.evidence: ResidentJitSafety::{Covered,Gap,Unavailable}. lower_jit_program None returns Unavailable with fail_reason, never Covered. crates/jet-jit/src/jit/api_debug.rs.

cards.title: JIT returns corrupt ZonedDateTime from add_duration/add_period
cards.body: Video-mine probe 2026-08-17 (fresh debug jet @ 8c4a64618, TZDIR=/etc/zoneinfo). ZonedDateTime arithmetic is correct on AOT and silently corrupt on default jet run — any zone, UTC included. Probe: start :: time.zoned_local(date.new(2024,3,9), time.time(20,0,0), ny); later :: start.add_duration(Duration.hours(8)). AOT (jet run --release): '2024-03-10 05:00:00 America/New_York (-04:00)', offset -14400, is_dst true — DST-safe, correct. Default jet run: later.to_string() and .format(...) print the SOURCE FILE PATH ('/tmp/jet-yt/probe_dst2.jet'), offset_seconds() 0, is_dst() false. Same corruption for add_period on zoned values and for time.zoned(dt, utc).add_duration(...). NOT affected under JIT: zoned construction itself (start.format correct), DateTime.plus_duration, LocalDate.add_period. Likely the JIT marshalling for zoned-returning arithmetic reads wrong memory. I9 violation live today; the time examples (text/dates, text/time_calendar) sit parked in tests/jit_gaps.txt so no suite catches it — distinct from but evidence for c02ur7xi: parking hides silent wrong values, not just crashes.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Default `jet run` matches AOT byte-for-byte for ZonedDateTime `add_duration`/`add_period` across a DST boundary — format string, `offset_seconds()`, and `is_dst()` — for any zone including UTC and for `time.zoned(dt, utc)` values. An executable example covers zoned arithmetic on both tiers and is not parked in any ledger.

## Law
No decision dependencies — mechanical tier-parity bug fix. I9 governs placement: zoned arithmetic semantics live in the shared Prelude time kernel; the JIT host only marshals.

## Work
1. Regression fixture = the card-body probe (this exact probe is the parity fixture; output must be byte-identical across default run/JIT/AOT): `start :: time.zoned_local(date.new(2024,3,9), time.time(20,0,0), ny); later :: start.add_duration(Duration.hours(8))` with TZDIR=/etc/zoneinfo. Expected (AOT-correct): `2024-03-10 05:00:00 America/New_York (-04:00)`, offset -14400, is_dst true. Reproduce the corruption on the current binary first (default run prints the SOURCE FILE PATH from `to_string`/`format`, offset 0, is_dst false).
2. Seam: `crates/jet-jit/src/Time.rs` CivilTimeMethod dispatch (arms ~lines 364-430: `(TimeValue::Date, "add_period")` exists; find/inspect the `(TimeValue::Zoned, "add_duration")` and `(TimeValue::Zoned, "add_period")` arms) plus `jit/lower_ctx.rs` civil-time lowering (~16716+, 26657 duration-add routing) and `jit/safety.rs:5755` arity table (which already whitelists `add_period`/`add_duration`). Printing the source path means a wrong handle/pointer is being read — suspect the zoned-returning arithmetic arm pushes or returns the wrong slot, or the method falls through to a default that returns an unrelated i64. Fix the marshalling; if any zone/DST policy is re-encoded in the JIT host instead of calling the same Prelude time kernel AOT uses, delete the re-encoding and call the Prelude symbol (I9).
3. Cover every corrupted shape from the body: `add_duration` on zoned, `add_period` on zoned, and `time.zoned(dt, utc).add_duration(...)`. Confirm the NOT-affected shapes stay correct (zoned construction/format, `DateTime.plus_duration`, `LocalDate.add_period`).
4. Interpreter tier: run the probe on the TIR evaluator too — criterion says default jet run (JIT+interp) must match AOT.
5. Ledger reality check (card body is stale here): `tests/jit_gaps.txt` `gaps:`/`run_gaps:` are now EMPTY and `text/dates` + `text/time_calendar` are compile_covered; they appear in `tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt`. Verify the example that exercises zoned arithmetic actually RUNS at the run tier in the corpus gate (criterion 2 "not parked") — if the gate records it as run-failing, the fix must move it to run-passing in the same diff.
6. Example: extend `examples/features/text/time_calendar.jet` (or `dates.jet`) with a DST-boundary zoned add_duration/add_period printing format + offset + is_dst; regenerate golden.

## Not building
- No Period/calendar API semantics changes; no timezone database work.
- #1663 (jit_gaps ledger retirement) is sibling-owned.
- No changes to Instant arithmetic (already correct).

## Proof
- Probe stdout byte-identical across `jet run`, `jet run --release`, and interpreter, with TZDIR=/etc/zoneinfo (criterion 1).
- Updated example golden green at the run tier in the corpus gate, not parked anywhere (criterion 2). Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — self-contained JIT marshalling fix with existing Prelude kernel.

Re-homed from sidequest into e3-m13-jit-parity: silent wrong-answer ZonedDateTime corruption on default jet run is a parity bug the milestone must gate on. Not a jit_gaps-ledger instance.
Dedupe note: distinct from #1663 (ledger retirement process card). This card owns the zoned add_duration/add_period tier-parity fix; #1663 owns retiring the jit_gaps ledger itself.
