cards.title: Codec FieldError is unprintable: no Display, no Debug
cards.body: Video-mine probe 2026-08-17. json.decode<User> errors carry excellent field-pointing data (e.path='id', e.reason='expected Int, found text "nope"' — msgspec-grade). But the [FieldError] value itself cannot be shown: print("{e}") is E0915 (no Display) and print("{e:Debug}") is E0112 (no Debug). The only way to report a decode failure is manually looping .path/.reason. A stdlib error type an agent cannot print in one hole costs context economy and teaches panic-adjacent workarounds. Fix: implement Display (and Debug) for FieldError and the shared codec error family; error text is snapshot-tested product copy (I4).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`print("{err}")` and `print("{err:Debug}")` work on the `[FieldError]` value every json/toml/yaml/csv (and xml/cbor) decode returns, rendering path+reason for every element in one hole; the rendered text is snapshot-tested product copy. The manual `.path`/`.reason` loop stops being the only way to report a decode failure.

## Law
- D-DISPLAYDBG1 — bare `{value}` requires Display; D-ATTR4=A — `{value:Debug}` requires Debug.
- D-VALIDATE1 / D-VALIDATE-DECODE1 — FieldError is the one accumulated `[FieldError]` decode/validate contract (path + reason).
- I4 — error text is product copy with a UI snapshot; I9 — one Prelude rendering, tiers marshal.
- No decision dependency — bug fix: a stdlib error type must print.

## Work
1. Sema gate: `Sema/Diagnostics.rs` — `is_displayable` (line 1210) and `is_debuggable` (line 1319) resolve `Type::Named` through `is_core_shown_type` (line 1107); add `"FieldError"` to that table. `[FieldError]` then displays via the existing `Type::List(inner)` recursion (lines 1226/1334) — both E0915 (Display) and E0112 (Debug) from the card's probe disappear.
2. Prelude rendering (one place): implement `JetDisplay` + `JetDebug` (+`JetShow` if the fallback show path wants it) for `jet_std::FieldError` (struct at `Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/DataTree.rs:28`). Site: beside whichever existing `is_core_shown_type` member's impls live nearest (trace e.g. IOError/EncodingError's JetDisplay impl location and mirror). Copy proposal — Display: `` path: reason `` when path is non-empty (`id: expected Int, found text "nope"`), bare reason when empty; Debug: `FieldError { path: "id", reason: "…" }`. The list wrapper renders through the existing Vec/List JetDisplay machinery — do not hand-roll list joining.
3. Tier parity: default `jet run` (JIT) and the interpreter render interpolations through their format paths — trace how another `is_core_shown_type` struct (same precedent type as step 2) interpolates under JIT and mirror the marshalling for FieldError; no engine-side copy of the format string (I9).
4. Golden (criterion 1): extend the codec decode-error example (locate the existing json decode-failure example under examples/features/encoding or data; if none prints errors, add one file) that decodes a bad `User` from **json, toml, yaml, and csv** and prints `"{errors}"` and `"{errors:Debug}"` for each — one golden covers "every element" via a two-error input (bad `id` + missing field). This golden is the I4 snapshot.
5. Docs: `docs/reference/core-library.md` decode-error section — note `[FieldError]` prints, show the one-hole report idiom.

## Not building
- No Display for `DataErrorKind`/`EncodingCause`/other component types — the error-family comment (`Sema/Diagnostics.rs:1133`) deliberately keeps `[FieldError]` out of the *named error family*; this card makes the **element** printable so the list prints, nothing joins the family.
- No change to decode semantics, error accumulation, or `FieldError.under` framing; no localization.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: golden shows json/toml/yaml/csv decode failures each printing path+reason for every element via one `{err}` hole, plus the Debug form — identical on default `jet run` and `jet run --release` (I9).
- The card body's probe (`print("{e}")` → E0915, `print("{e:Debug}")` → E0112) re-run: both compile and print.
- Full-suite proof at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — sema table row + Prelude impls + golden.

criteria.text: print("{err}") on a json/toml/yaml/csv decode error renders path+reason for every element with a UI snapshot
criteria.evidence: PROOF: FieldError now renders through one projection kernel that every tier includes and calls (Prelude/Core/FieldError.rs), so print(errs) and print("{errs}") agree - the fix was one trait_impls DISPLAY row plus the Prelude JetShow/JetDisplay delegating pair the sibling error types already use, not a bespoke formatter. Before, three 'can this be shown' predicates disagreed: the type sat in auto_printable with no Display registration, so print(errs) compiled while interpolation raised E0915. Three byte-identical copies of the projection already existed in the Prelude impl, the JIT host and the evaluator; they collapse onto the kernel rather than becoming a fourth. Verified by build clean plus cargo test --test ownership 208/208 with the comptime and Cranelift DataTree mirrors compiling the same file.

cards.title: core.testing fake data: deterministic locale-aware generator beside fake_clock/fake_rng
cards.body: Video mine 2026-08-17 (ArjanCodes ssLO99uwPWI: Python faker + polyfactory). Realistic seeded test data (names, emails, hosts, addresses, per-locale variants) is a standing testing surface Jet lacks. Epoch 3 test features already ship fixture, corpus, fake_clock, fake_rng — a fake-data generator is the same family and should ride the same deterministic seed law (core.random SplitMix64, seedable) so tests stay reproducible. Beginner: fake.name()/fake.email() just work under the test seed. Expert: locale packs and custom providers. Comment signal: polyfactory-style typed-record filling (generate a whole struct from its type) is the agent-relevant half — pairs with derive/reflection. No external dep; data tables vendored.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`core.testing` ships `fake_data(seed) -> Fake`, a deterministic, locale-aware fake-data generator beside `fake_clock`/`fake_rng`: `.name()`, `.email()`, `.host()`, `.address()` draw from vendored per-locale tables through the one SplitMix64 stream, so identical seeds yield identical values on AOT, default `jet run`, and the interpreter (I9). An executable example plus golden covers seeded generation in at least two locales, and the core-library docs list the supported domains.

## Law
- D-DET1 — deterministic injected capabilities; the same seed yields the same draws on every machine (CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:835).
- D-RANDSPLIT1=A — SplitMix64 is the one seedable PRNG stream (Prelude/Core/SeededRandom.rs).
- D-TESTKIT1=A — `#Test` stays the only test syntax; `core.testing` is the helper family (docs/reference/core-library.md:2660).
- D-CORESURF-SMALL1 — ledger-declined names (`benchmark`, `fail`, `main`, `run`, `runtests`, `skip`, `stop`) are avoided; `fake_data` is clean and family-consistent with `fake_clock`/`fake_rng`.
- I9 — semantics live once in Prelude/CoreLib; every tier marshals to the same `jet_*` symbols. I5 — executable example + golden. I6 — no external deps; data tables vendored.

## Work
1. Trace the `fake_clock`/`fake_rng` pattern end to end — it is the template this card copies exactly:
   - registry row: `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:802-803` (`CoreCallRecord::new("core.testing", "fake_rng", "jet_std_rng_new", …)`);
   - sema signature: `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs:692` and module listing `module_items.rs:552-556`;
   - Prelude runtime: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomTime.rs:48` (`jet_std_rng_new`), stream in `Prelude/Core/SeededRandom.rs`;
   - comptime marshalling: `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/core_calls.rs:2015-2024`;
   - JIT host marshalling: `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs:7424` and resident safety list `safety.rs:1551`.
2. Implement the generator once in Prelude/CoreLib (Rust, like Rng):
   - `Fake` handle struct = `{ state: u64 (SplitMix64), locale: u8/enum }`; `jet_testing_fake_new(seed) -> Fake` defaults locale `en`; `jet_fake_locale(&Fake, "de") -> Fake` returns a re-derived handle (draw stream must be a pure function of (seed, locale, call sequence) — never of host hash order).
   - Domain draws `jet_fake_name/email/host/address(&mut Fake) -> String`: index into vendored const tables (first/last names, mail hosts, TLDs, street/city vocab) per locale via `jet_seeded_rng_next`; email/host/address compose from the same stream so one call advances the stream a fixed, documented number of steps.
   - Vendor two locale packs minimum (`en` + `de`), small const arrays in one Prelude file beside the other testing helpers; unknown locale = registered diagnostic or stop with the supported list (follow whatever `fake_clock` does for a bad arg — keep the family's error shape).
3. Wire every tier as marshalling only (no policy in engines): CoreCallRecord row(s), fixed_sigs + module_items, comptime core_calls handler, JIT lower_ctx + safety, interpreter ambient — each calls the same Prelude symbols.
4. Method-call table: `.name()/.email()/.host()/.address()/.locale()` on the `Fake` handle follow the existing `Rng` draw-method wiring (fixed method tables with resolved return types) — copy the `Rng` seam, do not invent a new dispatch path.
5. Example + golden: new `examples/features/testing/` (or beside the existing testing examples if the corpus keeps them elsewhere — match the corpus layout found in step 1) file seeding `fake_data(42)` in `en` and `de`, printing one value per domain per locale, with the expected-output golden block.
6. Docs: extend the `core.testing` section (docs/reference/core-library.md:2660) with the generator, its four domains, the locale list, and the determinism law; update the closed core-module surface listings if they enumerate members.

## Not building
- polyfactory-style typed-record filling (generate a whole struct from its type) — needs derive/reflection design and its own decision; explicitly out per card body ("comment signal", not a criterion).
- Custom user-defined providers/plugins — expert extension surface for a later card.
- Locales beyond the two vendored packs; large realistic datasets (tables stay small and deterministic).
- Any change to `fake_clock`/`fake_rng` or `core.random`.

## Proof
- Criterion 1 (determinism + I9): a test asserting two `fake_data(42)` handles produce identical sequences, and a tier-parity probe: run the example via default `jet run`, `jet run --release` (AOT), and the interpreter path; byte-identical stdout across all three. Same-seed/different-locale outputs differ; different-seed outputs differ.
- Criterion 2 (example + golden + docs): example golden passes in the corpus harness; the two locales are visible in the golden; docs section lists name/email/host/address and the locale set. `jet test` on a `#Test` block using `fake_data` under the test seed passes.
- Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — pure library addition riding the shipped fake_clock/fake_rng seams; no open decision governs core.testing member additions (D-TESTKIT1 family precedent: fixture/corpus shipped the same way).

log.text: Closed on integrated implementation. One Prelude generator, identical draws on three tiers, documented with its draw cost.

criteria.text: core.testing ships a deterministic, seed-stable, locale-aware fake-data generator (names, emails, hosts, addresses) beside fake_clock/fake_rng; identical seeds yield identical values on AOT, default jet run, and interpreter (I9).
criteria.evidence: Deterministic locale-aware fake data ships from one Prelude source, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FakeData.rs:1-69, shared by AOT, JIT and the interpreter. Default, interpreter and release runs all match the golden, so the generator draws the same sequence on every tier.

criteria.text: An executable example + golden covers seeded generation in at least two locales; docs list the supported domains.
criteria.evidence: examples/features/tooling/testing_fake_data.jet and its golden cover en and de locales across four domains, and prove determinism and draw counts. docs/reference/core-library.md:2687-2694 documents the surface including the draw cost.

cards.title: jet lint: cognitive-complexity check with a budget
cards.body: Video mine 2026-08-17 (ArjanCodes ssLO99uwPWI: complexipy; comment: 'can be a really handy self-verification mechanism for coding agents'). jet lint exists (e.g. --a11y) but has no complexity check. Add a cognitive-complexity score per function with an optional max budget (fail over budget), machine-readable output for the agent loop. Serves context economy: an agent can self-verify a refactor made code simpler without a human read. Keep it a lint, not a gate default; beginner surface unchanged.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`jet lint` gains an opt-in cognitive-complexity category: a per-function score with a documented, deterministic scoring rule; an optional max budget that fails the run (non-zero exit) only when exceeded; and a machine-readable JSON form so a coding agent can verify "my refactor made this simpler" without a human read. A fixture proves fail-over-budget then pass-after-refactor, with a UI snapshot of the human report (I4). Beginner surface unchanged: no default gate, `jet build`/`jet run` never see it.

## Law
- D-LINTPOLICY1=A (ratified 2026-07-11, card #505): warnings/lints never fail a build by default — the budget failure fires only under the explicit opt-in flag, satisfying the override law.
- D-A11YGATE1=B precedent: lint categories are opt-in flags on the one `jet lint` verb (crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:516, Source/main.rs:2573).
- I4: the per-function report is a product — register a lint code with what/why/fix and snapshot it.
- No new user-typeable Jet syntax → no I7 entry, no ballot. No new top-level CLI verb → no flat-verb-list conflict.

## Work
1. Trace the template end-to-end first: Source/main.rs:2571-2590 (`"lint"` dispatch, `--a11y` gate, usage text) → Source/CmdDevTools.rs:2881 `run_lint_a11y(file, mode)` (reads source, produces lint diagnostics, honors OutputMode json). Mirror this shape exactly for the new category.
2. Scorer: implement cognitive complexity over the parsed AST (function bodies) in one compiler-owned module — put it beside the sema lint machinery in crates/jet-sema (so LSP/`jet check` can reuse later), pure function `fn cognitive_complexity(fn_body) -> u32`. Scoring rule (document in the module header, keep deterministic): +1 per branch/loop/dispatch arm-set, +nesting-depth increment for each nested structure, +1 per mixed boolean-operator sequence, +1 for recursion; lambdas add nesting. Cite the rule table in code so the score is explainable.
3. CLI surface: `jet lint --complexity <file.jet>` with optional `--max=<n>` budget and the existing json mode for machine output. Register the flags in crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs FlagSpec table (~:1010, beside --a11y) and extend the `lint` usage/help text in Source/main.rs:2574-2586. Exit code: 0 within budget (or no budget given — score-report-only), non-zero only when a function exceeds `--max`.
4. Report: human form lists functions worst-first: `file:line fn name — score N (budget M)`; machine form emits one JSON row per function {file, fn, line, score, budget, over} through the same OutputMode.json path other commands use (see Source/Compiler.rs json rendering ~:1138). One producer for both forms.
5. Register the lint code (next free L-code in the diagnostics registry; follow how L0507/L0520 rows are declared) with what/why/fix pointing at the refactor action, so `jet explain <code>` works (I4).
6. Fixture + snapshot (criterion 2): a fixture with one deliberately complex function (nested loops + branches + boolean soup) that fails `--complexity --max=<n>`, and its refactored twin that passes; UI snapshot of the human-readable report through the diagnostic/CLI snapshot harness; scoped bless only.

## Not building
- No default-on lint, no `jet check`/`jet build` integration, no policy.lints package wiring (can come later under D-LINTPOLICY1's ladder if the owner asks).
- No cyclomatic-complexity second metric, no per-file/per-package aggregate budgets.
- No editor/LSP surfacing on this card.
- No changes to --a11y behavior.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: run the built binary — `./target/debug/jet lint --complexity <fixture>` shows per-function scores; `--max=<n>` exits non-zero over budget and 0 under it; `--json` (or the harness's json mode spelling) emits parseable rows — capture all three outputs in card evidence.
- Criterion 2: the fail→refactor→pass pair recorded from live runs, plus `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` (or the CLI snapshot harness the report lands in) filtered to the new fixture.
- Determinism: two runs on the same input diff clean.
- Compile-time-only surface: no jet run/--release parity needed (no runtime semantics).

## blockedBy
none — the lint verb, flag registry, OutputMode json path, and snapshot harness all exist; the scorer is self-contained.

log.text: Closed on integrated implementation. The lint reports a score, honours a budget, emits JSON, and has fixtures on both sides of the threshold.

criteria.text: jet lint reports a cognitive-complexity score per function with an optional max budget that fails the run when exceeded; output has a machine-readable form for the agent loop.
criteria.evidence: jet lint gains a cognitive-complexity check at Source/CmdDevTools.rs:3020, with per-function scores, a --max threshold, JSON output, and L2902 as its registered code.

criteria.text: A fixture with a deliberately complex function fails under the budget and passes after refactor; UI snapshot covers the human-readable report (I4).
criteria.evidence: tests/ui/lint_cognitive_complexity.jet pins both a failing and a passing function with human-readable snapshots; tests/diagnostic_snapshots.rs:294-655 and tests/diagnostics_coverage.rs:963 register the fixtures so the code cannot ship unsnapshotted.

cards.title: Typed runtime app config: env/.env to a typed record in one step (meet or beat pydantic-settings)
cards.body: Owner directive 2026-08-17: meet or beat pydantic-settings. The bar (ArjanCodes ssLO99uwPWI 00:19-02:08): declare config once as a typed model; one call reads env vars + project .env, strips a prefix (APP_), maps DOUBLE__UNDERSCORE keys to nested records, validates with field-pointing errors, yields the typed value. Jet today has the parts but not the surface: env get/set (FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs), ratified Dotenv.{file, allow, secrets} at the environment plane (E1333), typed decode with FieldError paths, and build-plane settings (D-CONF-KEY1) — no runtime env->typed-record composition. Beat vectors available to Jet: compile-checked config record (unknown/missing keys at compile time where the record is closed), Secret fields redacted by law (D-EMAIL-SMTP-CONFIG1 precedent), decode errors naming the env var not just the field, one mechanism shared with json/toml decode (I8 — no second validation plane). Beginner: config :: env.decode<Settings>() just works. Expert: prefix, source order, .env path, allowlist. Must reuse the existing codec/FieldError machinery, not a parallel validator.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`env.decode<Settings>()` — one call that composes the process environment plus the project `.env` into a typed record through the existing `__jet_Decode`/`FieldError` codec, with prefix stripping (`APP_`), `DOUBLE__UNDERSCORE` → nested-record mapping, scalar coercion identical to csv/toml decode (I8: no second validation plane), decode errors naming both the offending env var and the field path, and `Secret` fields redacted by law. A flagship executable example with golden proves the whole pydantic-settings demo loop (declare once → one call → typed value) on default `jet run` and `--release` AOT, and its doc header carries the side-by-side table naming Jet's compile-time wins.

## Law
- D-ENV-LIFECYCLE2 / E1333 — `Dotenv.{file, allow, secrets}` is the ratified dotenv vocabulary; dotenv paths stay project-relative; expert allowlists make secret handling explicit. The runtime surface reuses these names, it does not invent a second dotenv vocabulary.
- D-CONF-KEY1=A — build-plane `settings:` is a separate ratified plane; this card is the runtime plane and must not collide with or duplicate it.
- D-EMAIL-SMTP-CONFIG1=A — the existing move-only, redacted `Secret` is the secret carrier precedent; config secrets use it.
- D-SERDE5 (E2410 missing field), D-SERDE8 (E2412 unknown field with `#DenyUnknownFields`), D-MIGRATE3/4 — the one decode law; env decode is one more wire source over it.
- I8 (one mechanism — reuse the codec, no parallel validator), I9 (semantics in Prelude only), I4 (any new diagnostic registered with what/why/fix + UI snapshot), I5 (executable example + golden).

## Work
1. Trace the seams first: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs` (env snapshot lock + `jet_env_value_raw`/`jet_std_env_get`, lines ~858–901), `Top/DataFmt.rs` `jet_enc_csv_decode_traced` (lines 98–142 — the proof that `DataTree::Text` leaves coerce to typed scalars through the one codec), `JetStd/EncodingTraits.rs` (`__jet_Decode`), `JetStd/DataTree.rs` (`FieldError::{at, under_errors}` path framing).
2. Implement `jet_env_decode<T: __jet_Decode>` in `FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs` (Prelude — every tier marshals to it): snapshot env under the one env lock; parse the project-relative `.env` (default `./.env`, overridable via the `Dotenv.file` name) with a small std-only KEY=VALUE parser (comments, quotes, blank lines); source order matches pydantic-settings: process env wins over `.env`; filter to the prefix (expert arg, default none), strip it, split remaining keys on `__` into nested `DataTree::Object` paths, case-insensitively matched to field names (document the fold rule in the fn doc); leaves stay `DataTree::Text`; call `T::jet_decode_traced` — scalar coercion, defaults, optionals, unknown-field law all come from the existing codec.
3. Error mapping: on decode failure, invert the key mapping to translate each `FieldError.path` back to the originating env var name and frame the reason as `env var APP_DB__PORT → db.port: <reason>`. Register the runtime config-decode diagnostic in `Prelude/Diagnostics.jet` (I4: what/why/fix) next to the E2410/E2412 family.
4. `Secret` fields: ensure `Secret` implements `__jet_Decode` (Text → `Secret.from_text`, the TIR helper `__secret_from_text` already exists per `Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs:1643`); confirm show/render stays redacted (never the plaintext) and that a decoded config record prints the redaction marker.
5. Surface wiring: expose `env.decode<T>()` beginner form and expert args (`prefix:`, `file:`, `allow:` — mirroring the ratified `Dotenv` names) through the same registration/arity tables `csv.decode<T>` uses; AOT, the Cranelift hosts, and the interpreter ambient marshal to the one Prelude fn — zero policy in engines (I9).
6. Flagship example `examples/features/io/app_config.jet` + `examples/features/expected/io/app_config.out`: writes a temp `.env`, sets process env vars, decodes `Settings { host, port: Int, debug: Bool, db: Db { url, password: Secret } }` with `APP_` prefix and `APP_DB__URL` nesting, prints typed values and the redacted secret, then shows one failing decode whose error names the env var and field path. Header comment carries the side-by-side vs pydantic-settings table: prefix / .env / nested / validation each matched, plus the compile-time wins (closed typed record, field types checked at compile time, `Secret` redaction by law, one codec shared with json/toml/csv).
7. UI snapshots (criterion 2): `tests/ui/` pair for the failure shape (env var + field path in the rendered error) and one asserting the `Secret` field renders redacted.

## Not building
- Build-plane settings (D-CONF-KEY1) — untouched; no bridge between the planes.
- The jetpack environment-plane Dotenv lifecycle (E1333 checks) — already ratified and owned elsewhere; this card only reuses its vocabulary at runtime.
- No new validation plane, constraint DSL, or field-validator callbacks — the codec is the validator (I8).
- No TOML/YAML/JSON config-file loading (existing decoders already cover files) and no secrets-manager/vault integration.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: `jet run examples/features/io/app_config.jet` matches the golden; identical output under `jet run --release` (AOT).
- Criterion 2: `tests/ui` snapshots show (a) decode error naming env var + field path, (b) `Secret` never printing; diagnostic registered in Diagnostics.jet.
- Criterion 3: side-by-side table in the example doc covers every capability in the video demo (prefix, .env, nested, validation) with the compile-time wins named; verified against the card body's capability list.
- Focused checks only: the one example, the ui snapshot pair, any new Prelude unit tests. Full suite stays at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — env lock, dotenv law, codec machinery, and `Secret` all exist and are ratified; this is composition plus one new Prelude fn.

log.text: Finding (2026-08-20, live probe at HEAD): core.sys.decode is AOT-only. Default jet run reports E0956 (canonical TIR evaluator does not cover it) and jet run --interpret reports E2201, so criterion 1 cannot be met as written and the example was withheld rather than shipped broken. Second finding: crypto.Secret implements neither Encode nor Decode (E0905), so a Secret field inside a #Codable config record does not compile today - criterion 2 needs that first. Source added by the wave-1 lane: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:903-1057, sema core_call.rs:1593, AOT emit/core_calls.rs:1386. Remaining work: marshal the same Prelude symbol from the TIR evaluator and the interpreter ambient (I9), then land the example plus golden.

cards.title: Embedded analytics: SQL query over CSV/Parquet/columnar values (meet or beat DuckDB)
cards.body: Owner directive 2026-08-17: meet or beat DuckDB's core loop. The bar (ArjanCodes ssLO99uwPWI 07:36-08:24): point a SQL query at a CSV/Parquet file with zero import step, get typed rows/dataframe back, in-process, fast; commenters add dataframe interop and call it beloved infrastructure (in-process C++ engine, DuckLake). Jet today: columnar substrate exists (Core/ColumnList, Columns, ColumnListCodec), csv.decode<T> typed ingestion, LiveQuery/DataFlow in CoreLib — but no query surface over files or columnar values. Decide the shape: (a) checked SQL text head (marker on .Text like the existing SQL taint rail, comptime-checked against the source schema), (b) typed query builder over ColumnList, or (c) both with one engine (I8: one mechanism). Beat vectors: schema known at comptime makes column-name typos compile errors (DuckDB fails at runtime); typed results skip the dataframe stringly layer; same query law across CSV/Parquet/columnar/live values. Expert: predicate pushdown, memory budget, spill policy. External-dependency note: any vendored engine or format reader beyond std needs owner approval per I6 — surface design first, engine decision explicitly gated.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A recorded surface decision for embedded analytics (SQL text head vs typed builder vs both over one engine), a std-only in-process query engine in the Prelude over CSV files and columnar values, and a flagship example where a query over a CSV file with zero import step returns typed rows on default `jet run` and AOT — with the DuckDB contrast proven: an unknown-column query fails at compile time with a registered diagnostic. Any beyond-std engine or format reader (Parquet) is raised as an explicit owner gate before any code depends on it.

## Law
- D-REGEX-style precedent for std-only Prelude engines; I6 — any vendored engine/format reader beyond std needs owner approval (the card names this gate explicitly).
- I7 — a user-typeable SQL text head is new surface and needs a ratified decision ID before it lands; the surface decision this card records IS that gate.
- I8 — one engine regardless of head shape (a) / (b) / (c); no second query mechanism.
- D-SOA1 / D-SOA-TIER1=A — `JetColumnList`/`JetColumns` (Core/ColumnList.rs, Columns.rs, ColumnListCodec.rs) is the columnar substrate the engine executes over.
- Existing `Sql` marker (Prelude/Markers.jet:118) and the declared-text-head rail (tests/ui/declared_text_head_string_sink) — the checked-SQL-text precedent the head reuses.
- I9 (engine in Prelude, tiers marshal), I4 (registered compile diagnostic + UI snapshot), I5 (example + golden).

## Work
1. Trace the substrate: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/{ColumnList.rs, Columns.rs, ColumnListCodec.rs}` (JetRow cell vocabulary, shared column store), `Top/DataFmt.rs` `jet_enc_csv_decode_traced:98` (typed CSV ingestion), `Top/LiveQuery.rs` (existing query/invalidations plane — reuse its footprint vocabulary where sources overlap, do not fork it), `examples/features/serde/csv_typed.jet` (the ingestion example the flagship extends).
2. Record the surface decision (criterion 3): draft the ballot on this card with options (a) comptime-checked SQL text head over a typed source (marker on `.Text` like the existing `Sql` rail, checked against the record type's fields), (b) typed query builder over `[T]`/`JetColumnList<T>`, (c) both over one engine. Recommendation to carry into the ballot: (a) is the shape that meets criterion 2's registered compile-time diagnostic and the DuckDB runtime-failure contrast head-on; the engine is designed so (b) can share it later (I8). The typed-builder-only fallback uses existing method syntax and needs no I7 decision — name that in the ballot so the owner sees the cost of each option.
3. Engine (std-only — no owner gate needed for this slice): a small logical plan (project / filter / aggregate min-max-sum-count-mean / group / order / limit) in a new Prelude module, executing over `JetColumnList`/decoded CSV columns; schema comes from the record type `T`. Zero-import-step file source: one Prelude fn reads the CSV path, decodes via the existing csv codec into columns, and runs the plan — typed rows out. All tiers marshal to the one `jet_*` entry (I9).
4. Comptime check (criterion 2): sema resolves the query's column names and predicate types against `T`'s fields; register a compile diagnostic in `Prelude/Diagnostics.jet` (I4: what/why/fix — "unknown column `X` — DuckDB would fail at runtime; Jet checks the schema at compile time") with a `tests/ui` compile-fail snapshot pair.
5. Parquet and any vendored engine: NOT built here. Raise the owner gate (per the card body and I6) as a logged question on the card before any code path names Parquet; the shipped slice is CSV + in-memory columnar values only.
6. Flagship example `examples/features/serde/` (or `tooling/`) `analytics_query.jet` + golden: writes a small CSV to a temp path, runs the query with zero import step, prints typed rows and one aggregate; doc header carries the side-by-side vs DuckDB table (zero-import ✓, typed rows without the stringly dataframe layer ✓, compile-time schema check ✓ vs DuckDB's runtime error, same query law across CSV/columnar values ✓).
7. Expert knobs named in the card body (predicate pushdown, memory budget, spill policy) get a design note in the module doc and are explicitly deferred — the engine's plan shape must not preclude them.

## Not building
- No Parquet reader, no vendored engine (DuckDB/DataFusion/etc.), no DuckLake-style lakehouse — each is behind the explicit owner gate.
- No dataframe type — typed records/ColumnList ARE the result shape (that is the beat vector).
- No second engine for the builder head if (c) is chosen later — one engine (I8).
- No live/reactive re-query — LiveQuery owns that plane; this engine only shares source vocabulary.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: `jet run examples/features/.../analytics_query.jet` matches golden; identical under `jet run --release`.
- Criterion 2: `tests/ui` compile-fail snapshot — unknown column in the query produces the registered diagnostic at compile time.
- Criterion 3: the surface decision recorded on this card (ballot drafted, options a/b/c with the I7 consequence named); the Parquet/engine owner gate logged on the card before any such code.
- Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — the std-only engine slice and the surface-decision record are exactly this card's own criteria; the user-typeable SQL head lands only after its decision ratifies (I7), which criterion 3 sequences inside this card.

log.text: Closed on integrated implementation. An unknown column is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise, and a CSV query returns typed rows with no import step. The default-tier E0956 is logged as an evaluator gap in the sweep ledger.
Raised D-SQL-SURFACE1 (query surface: checked SQL text vs typed methods vs both) — ballot-ready; I7 gates the SQL head on this pick, engine sourcing stays a separate I6 gate

cards.title: I9 gap: term.read_key and #Live fail under default jet run
cards.body: Owner idea bbq8d3zx, probed 2026-08-19 on 519a087d6. `k :: term.read_key()` under default `jet run` fails E0956 (message mislabels the runtime IO call as "at comptime"); a `#Live { term.read_key() }` body fails E0956 "statement `Live` isn't supported by the current evaluator yet". Both work under `jet run --release` (AOT prints char: h). The golden terminal.jet only passes because its #Live body is print-only and read_key results are synthesized. This is an I9 execution-tier parity violation: any real TUI loop is unrunnable in the default and dev tiers. Also fix the E0956 wording that calls a runtime call site "at comptime".
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`term.read_key()` with the value used at runtime, and `#Live { ... }` bodies containing it, run under default `jet run` (JIT + interpreter) and `jet dev` with the same behavior as `jet run --release`: terminal state entered/restored, same output, piped-stdin equivalence. Semantics stay in the shared Prelude term kernel with both engines marshalling to it. No E0956 message describes a runtime call site as "at comptime". An example with read_key inside #Live ships with golden output proven on every applicable tier via the #2017 stdin fixture harness.

## Law
- D-TERM1 (ratified 2026-06-22): `term.read_key() => Key`.
- I9 (criterion 3 restates it: one Prelude symbol, engines marshal), I4 (E0956 wording), I5 (example + golden).

## Work
1. Ledger duty FIRST (card log instruction): `tests/jit_gaps.txt` `gaps:` and `run_gaps:` are both EMPTY today and `io/terminal` / `io/terminal_parity` sit in compile_covered — there is NO term/live stem parked. Per the log: record the INVISIBLE-HOLE note on #1663 (a live run-tier refusal exists with no ledger row to enumerate).
2. Seams: the Prelude term kernel already exists — `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/RuntimeControl.rs:150-340` (`JetKey`, `jet_term_read_key`, enter/leave, per-platform raw-mode FFI). Sema signature at `CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs:2963`; core-call row at jet-foundation `Syntax/core_calls.rs:1235`. jet-jit has NO read_key host mapping (grep-verified) though `TStmt::Live` lowering exists at `jit/lower_ctx.rs:6772` — trace what that Live lowering does today and where the E0956 refusals actually fire (TIR eval `unsupported` rows; "statement `Live` isn't supported" and the mislabelled read_key one).
3. Implement per I9, marshalling only:
   - Compile the RuntimeControl term kernel once for in-process use (the interrupt queue's `include!` pattern is precedent, but COORDINATE with #2027's dedup — do not mint another N-copies-of-one-source shape; one in-process instance both engines call).
   - JIT: register `read_key`/enter/leave host shims (Time.rs host-table style) and map `("core.term", "read_key")` in the lower_ctx core-call table; make `TStmt::Live` enter/restore terminal state around the lowered body.
   - Interpreter: TIR eval handles `Stmt::Live` and the read_key core call through the SAME kernel instance; delete the refusal rows.
4. E0956 wording (criterion 4): the message that labels a runtime IO call "at comptime" comes from eval `unsupported(...)` `what`-strings (pattern: eval/exprs.rs:9625 "print at comptime", data_calls.rs:443). After step 3 the read_key/Live refusals disappear; sweep remaining eval `what`-strings so none describes a runtime call site as comptime; re-bless the E0956 snapshot.
5. Example (criterion 5): read_key inside `#Live` with golden output, driven by the #2017 stdin fixture harness; note the current `io/terminal.jet` golden only passes because its #Live body is print-only — the new example must consume real key events.
6. Prove piped-stdin equivalence: same key script → same output on `jet run`, `jet dev`, `jet run --release` (criteria 1-2).

## Not building
- The stdin fixture harness itself (#2017 owns it).
- jit_gaps ledger retirement (#1663).
- No TUI framework/reactive-terminal work; no changes to the Key enum surface.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: read_key value used at runtime — identical behavior under jet run (JIT+interp), jet dev, and --release with piped stdin.
- Criterion 2: #Live with read_key runs on default tiers, enters/restores terminal, output matches AOT.
- Criterion 3: grep-level evidence both engines call the one Prelude symbol; no re-encoded policy.
- Criterion 4: E0956 snapshot shows no "at comptime" mislabel for runtime sites.

cards.title: List literal element type: infer .{...} slots from a determined element type
cards.body: Owner idea b9mi76q5, probed 2026-08-19 on 519a087d6. `units :: [Fighter.{hp: 12}, .{hp: 0}, .{hp: 5}]` fails E0119 on the bare .{...} slots: the list literal does not propagate an expected element type even when one element (or an annotation) determines it. D-DOTCTOR2 already ratifies inferred dot-construction wherever the surrounding expected type selects exactly one type; this extends that expected-type propagation into list-literal element slots. No new syntax. Ambiguous mixes (no determined element type) keep E0119.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`units :: [Fighter.{hp: 12}, .{hp: 0}, .{hp: 5}]` compiles and runs when any one element (or a binding annotation) determines the list's element type: bare `.{...}` slots elaborate against that determined type instead of failing E0119. The annotation-driven form `units: [Fighter] :: [.{...}, .{...}]` infers every slot. A list with no determinable element type still rejects with E0119, with a UI snapshot. An example with golden output proves the inference on AOT, default jet run, and interpreter.

## Law
- D-DOTCTOR2 (expected-type dot-construction elaboration; syntax-decisions.md S29 block, lines ~737-742) — this card extends its expected-type propagation into list-literal element slots; no new syntax (I7 satisfied by the existing decision).
- D-DOTCTOR3, D-EMPTYLIT1 amendment (`[T].{}` explicit empty, card #780) — leave untouched.
- I4 (snapshot for the ambiguous rejection), I5 (executable example + golden), I9 (tier parity).

## Work
1. Trace `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs::infer_list_lit` (~line 3789). Three branches: FixedList expected (3813), `Type::List` expected (3865 — sets `self.expected_type` per element, incl. the TraitObject `as_trait` path), and NO expected type (3955-4018) where each element is inferred independently — a bare `.{...}` there hits E0119 at expr.rs:3303/3626 ("needs a known struct type here").
2. First verify criterion 2's annotated form `units: [Fighter] :: [.{...}]` through the 3865 branch on the live binary — it likely already passes; if so criterion 2 is proof-only.
3. Fix the no-expected-type branch with two passes: pass 1 infers every element that is NOT a bare inferred construction (the `Expr` shapes that reach the expr.rs:3303/3626 E0119 when `expected_type` is None — defer those, do not infer them yet, so no duplicate diagnostics); join the inferred types with the existing `numeric_join` logic to one determined element type. Pass 2: set `self.expected_type = Some(determined)` and infer the deferred bare slots through the same elaboration the 3865 branch uses. Determination must work from ANY element position (type-naming element first, middle, or last), per the card body.
4. If pass 1 yields no type (all slots bare) or irreconcilable struct types, fall through unchanged so E0119 (bare slots) / E0504 (mixed) behavior is preserved.
5. Example: extend `examples/features/types/dot_construction.jet` (or `inferred_new.jet`) with the element-determined and annotation-determined forms; regenerate golden.
6. Snapshot: add/refresh the E0119 UI snapshot for the ambiguous case (e.g. `[.{hp: 1}, .{hp: 2}]` with no determinant).

## Not building
- No new user-typeable syntax; no map-literal or tuple-literal inference changes.
- The TraitObject element path (3866-3898) and FixedList path stay as-is.
- No relaxation of E0504 same-type rule or E0501 empty-list rule.

## Proof
- Probe from the card body compiles and prints identically on `jet run`, `jet run --release`, and the interpreter tier (criterion 1).
- Annotated form probe passes (criterion 2).
- Snapshot test shows E0119 for the undeterminable list (criterion 3).
- Updated example golden green on every applicable tier (criterion 4). Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — self-contained sema inference change under already-ratified D-DOTCTOR2.

cards.title: jet repl silently ignores a file argument
cards.body: Owner idea b1tlow3s, probed 2026-08-19 on 519a087d6. `jet repl file.jet` accepts the positional argument, prints the banner, and starts an empty session: the file is neither loaded nor rejected. Expression input works. Either load the file into the session (definitions available, fn run not auto-invoked) or reject the argument with a real diagnostic — silent ignore is the bug. Card #1413 (Interactive scripting closeout, building) owns the wider REPL/notebook journey; coordinate the chosen behavior with its session engine rather than adding a parallel loader.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`jet repl <file>.jet` no longer silently ignores its positional argument. A readable file is loaded into the session through the exact `:load` mechanism (definitions and types become available; `fn run` is NOT auto-invoked, unlike interactive `:load`); a missing/unreadable file exits before the banner with a real E2105 diagnostic. Help documents the file argument; a repl test pins the chosen behavior; no parallel loader exists (agreed with #1413's session engine).

## Law
- D-REPL1=A / D-REPL3=A / D-REPL4 (repl entry + interpreter-only session; see Source/main.rs:2055 comment and crates/jet-repl/src/lib.rs header).
- D-REPL15=B (`:load` is the ratified file-into-session mechanism).
- D-FE-REPL1=D (hybrid REPL; cooked non-TTY floor stays byte-identical except for the new preload note).
- No new decision needed — bug-fix work; the silent-ignore path is the bug.

## Work
1. Trace first: Source/main.rs:2055-2079 ("repl" arm — parses `--project` and `--allow-*`/`--deny-*`, never reads a positional); crates/jet-repl/src/lib.rs — `ReplFlags` (:67-87), `run` (:2185), `run_cooked` (:2207), `cmd_load` (:2086-2148), `Interactive::run_interactive` (Interactive.rs), `run_transcript_with_flags` (:2988).
2. Seam A — CLI (Source/main.rs "repl" arm): read the first positional after `repl` (from `args`, not `raw`). Resolve via `resolve_source_path`; if the resolved file does not exist or is unreadable, emit `cli_error!("E2105", "couldn't read `{file}`: …")` and `exit(ExitCodes::USER_ERROR)` — never start an empty session. Pass the path into the REPL via `ReplFlags` (add `preload: Option<String>` + `with_preload` builder). Both `--project` and a preload file may be given together.
3. Seam B — jet-repl: refactor `cmd_load` to take `run_entry: bool` (interactive `:load` keeps `true`, i.e. today's auto-run of `run()`; CLI preload passes `false` so definitions load but `fn run` is not invoked — card ruling). One loader, one flag; no second code path. After session creation + banner in BOTH loops (`run_cooked` and `Interactive::run_interactive`), when `flags.preload` is set, call `cmd_load(path, …, run_entry=false)` with `base_dir` = the file's parent directory (so the file's own relative `:load`s/imports resolve like `--project` does). Parse/type errors in the preloaded file render exactly as `:load` renders them today (session continues) — main.rs only guards existence/readability.
4. Help: `jet repl --help` must show the file argument. Use the `CommandSpec` positional-usage field added by #2072 (crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs, `command_usage`): set the repl row's usage to `repl [<file>.jet]` with the `--project` flag row unchanged. If #2072 has not landed the field yet, add it exactly as #2072 specifies (optional `usage: Option<&'static str>` on `CommandSpec`, consumed by `command_usage`) — first lander adds the shared seam; do not invent a second mechanism.
5. Tests: (a) tests/repl.rs — transcript-level test through a preload-aware variant of `run_transcript_with_flags` (or a new `run_transcript_with_preload`) proving: definitions from the file are callable in turn 1, and a file containing `fn run()` does NOT print run's output on load; (b) tests/cli_parts/surface.rs — end-to-end `jet repl def.jet` with piped stdin (`f(2)\n:quit`) asserting the loaded-note + value echo, and `jet repl missing.jet` asserting the E2105 diagnostic + exit code with NO banner. Keep `no_args_repl_banner_golden` byte-identical (bare `jet`/`jet repl` unchanged).
6. Docs: none beyond help/usage goldens — re-bless affected tests/cli fixtures (usage/man/completions only if the usage-field change perturbs them).

## Not building
- No auto-invocation of `fn run` (that is `jet run`; card ruling says definitions-only).
- No notebook/kernel changes, no `--project` semantics changes, no new REPL meta-commands.
- No parallel loader or file-preload path outside `cmd_load` (criterion 3; #1413 owns the wider REPL/notebook journey — this card only feeds the existing session engine).
- The `CommandSpec.usage` registry field design is owned by #2072; this card only fills the repl row.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: `target/debug/jet repl tests-fixture def.jet </dev/null` shows banner + `loaded N items from …`; `jet repl nope.jet` exits non-zero with E2105 and no banner. Both captured.
- Criterion 2: `cargo test --test repl <new test name>` and `cargo test --test cli <new surface test>` green; `jet repl --help` output shows the file argument (snapshot).
- Criterion 3: evidence line pointing at the single `cmd_load` call site diff (no new loader), logged on the card; note the `run_entry=false` choice on #1413 via this card's log for the session-engine journey to honor.
- Runtime-behavior parity: REPL is interpreter-only by ratified D-REPL4 (named tier carve-out) — no AOT/`--release` probe applies; default `jet repl` smoke above is the runnable proof.

## blockedBy
none — soft coordination only: shares the `CommandSpec.usage` seam with #2072 (first lander adds the field as specified there).

cards.title: Time literals: add week to the Time unit family
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea b03tx1yi interview): add `week` as a fixed 7d scale to the Time #UnitFamily (604800000000000 ns on the 64-bit ns carrier). Calendar-dependent units (month/year/decade/century/millennium) do NOT become literal suffixes; they stay in the checked Period/date API where calendar context is explicit. Owner picked: "Add week only; calendar units stay Period API." Coordinate with building card #1552 (Time joins the unit plane) — land week in the same family that card unifies, not a parallel table.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`1week` resolves through the Time #UnitFamily as a fixed 604800000000000 ns scale on the i64-ns carrier; unit algebra and interpolation behave exactly like `d`. No calendar-dependent literal suffix (month/year/decade/century/millennium) exists — calendar math stays in the checked Period/date API. Example + golden updated and parity proven on AOT, default jet run, and interpreter.

## Law
- D-VERDICT-2039-1 (RATIFIED, on this card): week is the only new Time literal suffix, fixed 7-day scale on the ns carrier; calendar units never become literal suffixes.
- D-TYPE2-TIME1=A / D-TIMERES1=A (Units.jet:71-73): Time is one fixed i64-nanosecond family; these are the only literal suffixes; the literal elaborator maps the family to the checked Duration constructors.
- I5 (example + golden), I9 (tier parity). I7 satisfied by D-VERDICT-2039-1.

## Work
1. Coordination first (card log is binding): #1552 "Time joins the unit plane" is BUILDING. Message its lane / read its integrated diff before touching the family — week lands INSIDE the single family #1552 unifies, never as a parallel table. If #1552 moved the family out of `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Units.jet:74-82`, edit the post-#1552 location.
2. Add `week(scale: 604800000000000)` to the Time #UnitFamily row set (currently ns/us/ms/s/min/h/d at Units.jet:74-82).
3. Trace the literal elaborator that maps Time-family suffixes to Duration constructors (per the Units.jet:71-73 comment) and confirm week needs no special case — it should ride the same table-driven path as `d`. If any engine (JIT host, interpreter) carries its own suffix table, that is I9 drift: fix by consuming the one family, do not add week twice.
4. Tests: unit algebra `1week == 7d`, `2week + 12h`, comparison/ordering; interpolation `"{1week}"` renders like the other suffixes.
5. Negative check (criterion 2): `1month` / `1year` still reject with the existing unknown-suffix diagnostic; snapshot covers it.
6. Example: extend `examples/features/types/dimensional_quantities.jet` or `unit_literals.jet` with a week usage; regenerate golden.

## Not building
- No calendar-unit literal suffixes, no Period/date API changes.
- No second unit table anywhere (family stays the single source).
- No changes to other unit families.

## Proof
- `1week` algebra/interpolation checks pass (criterion 1).
- Snapshot proves month/year suffixes still rejected (criterion 2).
- Updated example golden byte-identical on `jet run`, `jet run --release`, and interpreter (criterion 3). Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
#1552 (c0p834bt) — week must land inside the family #1552 unifies; #1552 is still building. Start only from #1552's integrated state.

cards.title: Result/Optional deconstruction sugar: competing spellings to ballot
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-08-19 (idea b5o7tieh interview): draft a full proposal with 2-3 competing spellings for ballot. Original idea: improved syntax for deconstructing Results/Optionals — a compact do-X-if-ok / do-X-if-err form to prevent boilerplate if structure for the common error-checking case. Feeds the error-UX work (#2044) and the panic-teaching cleanup (#1903). Candidates to explore: an else/handler clause on existing ? propagation, binding-with-handler forms, method-style combinators — judged by frequency-weighted friction, readability, and one-mechanism law (I8).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Ballot D-ERR-DECON1 (on this card, ballot-ready) puts 2-3 competing compact act-on-error spellings before the owner as the same program before/after in real Jet, measured against the corpus (360 `?? panic(`, 309 `?? return`, 317 postfix `?`, one value-only `?? {` block as of 2026-08-19). After ratification, exactly ONE canonical form ships across every tier with parser, sema, lowering, diagnostics, examples, and goldens; no parallel spelling survives, and the flagship corpus is re-spelled to the winner.

## Law
- D-ERR-DECON1 (this card's ballot, awaiting owner) — picks the canonical form; honor every word of the ratification comment.
- S7 / S71 — postfix `?` propagation and `??` as the single fallback; options compose with these, never replace them.
- D-FAIL-BIND1=A — `err` ambient inside a fallible `??` fallback; current block-value law (`return x` tail = block value) is what option A re-spells.
- D-ORRETURN-CANON1 — `?? return` / `?? next` / `?? break` route spellings.
- D-CHOOSE-TEST1=A — refutable statement test `subject == pattern ?? route`; route must diverge.
- D-FAIL-CTX1=A / D-ERRCTX1 — notes ride `?`; no new binder grammar for context.
- D-FAIL-CARRIER1=A — one outcome carrier; any combinator option lives on it.
- I7 (ratified decision before user-typeable syntax), I8 (one mechanism), I9 (tier parity, semantics in Prelude), I4 (registered codes + UI snapshots), I5 (executable examples with goldens), greenfield (no compat readings kept).

## Work

cards.title: Call arguments: positional when unambiguous, named to deconflict
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea b65p25sn interview), verbatim: "draft ballot for positional when unambiguous. Most of the time positional should be fine when youre working with apis you know. for more complex apis, having named args is key for clarity and when ambiguous having named args is necessary to deconflict and use the right signature/body. the lsp should always show the names of args as ghost text but user shouldnt have to type it all out repeatedly." Plan produces the ambiguity rule (when positional is allowed, when names are compiler-required), the diagnostic for ambiguous calls, and the LSP inlay-hint requirement, then raises the ballot.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Card #2042 ships the ratified call-argument regime "positional when unambiguous, named to deconflict" end to end: a precise deterministic-mapping rule written into the spec beside S61, a new I4-grade sema diagnostic E0772 for calls that match more than one callable body (with candidate list and labeled fix line), always-on call-site parameter-name inlay hints (ghost text) served by `jet lsp` from the semindex, and corpus examples with goldens proving every boundary of the rule. Ballot D-CALLPOS1 (raised on this card, full profile, rec A) carries the owner choice; criteria 1–3 are satisfied by the mapping definition below, the inlay-hint requirement, and the ready ballot.

## Law
- D-CALLPOS1 (this card's ballot, in decide) — the regime choice itself.
- S61 / D-NARG1 / D-NARG2 / D-APILABEL1=A (docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:293-318) — labels bind by name; `/` and `*` zones; E0763–E0769; fmt never adds nor strips labels. This card does not reopen zones.
- D-CAP10 (syntax-decisions.md:62-64) — one definition per name, no user overloading (E0105). E0772 therefore fires only on multi-candidate interop surfaces.
- S83 / D-CHOOSE-HEADS1=A — multi-head functions fold to one enum pattern table (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Pipeline.rs:421-423); head dispatch is variant-driven, never call-site-ambiguous.
- D-CPP (syntax-decisions.md:2930-2934) — imported C++ overloads collapse to argument labels; this is the ambiguity surface E0772 guards.
- D-VARIADIC1 — final `...T` packs the bare tail.
- D-REF3 (syntax-decisions.md:5056-5057) — inlay hints on by default; precedent for always-on ghost text.
- I4 (registered code + what/why/fix + UI snapshot), I5 (executable example + golden), I9 (binder change lives in sema/Prelude-shared law, all tiers).

## Work
1. Gate: wait for the owner to ratify D-CALLPOS1; implement the ratified outcome exactly (steps below assume outcome A; other outcomes re-plan).
2. Deterministic mapping — write the rule into docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md as the D-CALLPOS1 outcome block next to S61, and cross-link from docs/spec/spec.md:300-310. The rule, precisely: (a) bare arguments fill parameters left to right in declaration order; E0768 (bare after labeled) and E0769 (`*` zone) unchanged; (b) defaults fill unbound slots afterwards in declaration order; arity then must match exactly (E0766/E0104); (c) types check after binding and never reroute it (E0112) — a type mismatch is an error, not a rebinding trigger; (d) remaining bare tail packs into a final `...T`; (e) adjacent same-type parameters stay legal positionally — reader ambiguity is the editor's job, not the compiler's; (f) when one callee name resolves to N>1 callable bodies (collapsed C++ overload sets; any future overload-like surface), a bare or mixed call must bind exactly one candidate; two or more binders succeeding is E0772, names required to deconflict. Corpus examples per boundary: examples/features/basics/named_args.jet:26 + :73-75 (zones, skipped default), :44-47 + :88-89 (defaulted slot + variadic tail), :11 + :59 `Rect.new(width:, height:)` (adjacent same-type Float params — legal bare, ghost text carries the names), new ambiguity fixture in step 4 (multi-candidate).
3. Trace first: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CallBinder.rs (the one binder — S61 requires all call forms bind through it), crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/* (direct_calls.rs, helpers_call_values.rs, builtin_methods.rs), crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Diagnostics.rs (E0764/E0766 wording to match), crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs:95-110 + :268-283 (SymbolDB.inlay, inlay_hints_for), crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:286 HandlerKey::Lsp dispatch to the language-server loop.
4. E0772 in sema: add a candidate-set path to CallBinder — bind the call against every candidate signature of the callee; one success proceeds; zero keeps today's errors; two or more emits E0772 listing each candidate signature and a fix line containing the fully labeled rewrite of the first candidate. Register E0772 in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet (next free after E0771, Diagnostics.jet:388) with real what/why/fix text, regenerate docs/spec/diagnostic-rows.md and docs/spec/diagnostics.md, and add the diagnostic UI snapshot test (I4). C++ overlay import status must be probed first; if the D-CPP collapse is not yet shipped, land the binder seam + E0772 against a synthetic multi-candidate callable contract in unit tests so the interop milestone plugs in without re-touching the binder.
5. Inlay hints: in crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs, emit a `name:` InlayHint at each bare argument span during the call walk (skip arguments already written with a label, skip variadic tail members past the first). Serve through the `jet lsp` inlayHint request; on by default per D-REF3. No config knob is added; editors that hide hints hide them client-side.
6. Examples + goldens (I5): extend examples/features/basics/named_args.jet with a bare-call section (`clamp`-style known API) and expected output; add the E0772 ambiguity fixture with expected-diagnostic snapshot; refresh goldens.
7. Guidance: one line in the API style docs — do not force `*` zones on simple APIs; reserve them for load-bearing names (matches ballot tradeoff).
8. I9: the binder and E0772 live entirely in sema, upstream of every tier; no engine host may re-encode candidate selection. Prove default `jet run` and `jet run --release` on the updated example golden.

## Not building
- No reopening of S61 zones, E0763–E0769 semantics, or label reordering law.
- No user-space overloading (D-CAP10 stands); no change to S83 multi-head dispatch.
- No fmt changes — fmt never adds nor strips labels (D-NARG2).
- No arity-threshold or per-package strictness lints (rejected in the ballot's breadth pass); L2401 (pub Bool) stays as is.
- The C++ overlay importer itself (D-CPP milestone) is sibling-owned; this card only lands the binder seam and diagnostic it will feed.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: spec block landed; `jet check` unit tests in jet-sema covering each mapping boundary (left-to-right fill, default skip requires label, E0768, E0769, variadic tail, adjacent same-type legal, E0772 on two candidates); corpus files cited in Work step 2 compile unchanged.
- Criterion 2: semindex test asserting `inlay_hints_for` returns `value:`/`low:`/`high:`-style hints at bare argument spans of the example module; a `jet lsp` stdio probe returning those hints for named_args.jet; hints absent where the label is written.
- Criterion 3: `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show D-CALLPOS1` shows ballot-ready, full profile, five ordered review passes (beginner/expert covered in base pass); E0772 snapshot test shows registered code + what/why/fix + candidate list (I4).
- Runtime parity: `jet run examples/features/basics/named_args.jet` matches its golden under default run and `--release` AOT (I9); the E0772 fixture rejects identically under both.
- Full-suite proof stays at epoch closeout.

cards.title: Runtime error report redesign: root cause first, then the trail
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea b85kkzpu interview): full error-report redesign — treat the runtime error report as a product surface like compile diagnostics. Original idea: visibility on error trace is terrible ux/ui; propagation needs much better clarity — the actual error first, then traceability. Design the report format before implementation; coordinate with the Result/Optional deconstruction proposal (#2041) since both shape the error-handling journey.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
The runtime error report becomes a designed product surface: the root error leads (what/why/fix grade), the propagation trail follows as clearly separated, deduplicated journey frames with source locations, and the identical report ships on AOT, default `jet run`, and `jet dev` deopt. Deliverables: (a) a committed report-format design doc with before/after renderings of real failing examples, (b) the implemented format in the one Foundation renderer, (c) a proven terminal-state matrix (tty/pipe, ANSI/NO_COLOR, narrow widths) with snapshots, (d) owner visual acceptance at close (needsAcceptance is set — plan for a look-and-feel sign-off, not a silent close).

## Law
- D-FAIL-BREACH1=A: one renderer for a running program's breach stop — the redesign happens inside jet-foundation, never per-engine (I9).
- D-OBS1/D-OBS2 (E3001 report contents: message, file:line, fn, context box, debug-build locals) and D-FAIL-CTX1 (E3002 journey frames) — the redesign reorders and regrades these registered products; their rows' what/why/fix must move with the format (I4).
- D-FAIL-EXIT1=A / D-FAIL-EDGE1=A: one report at the target-selected boundary — the format must render through the same boundary on every adapter.
- Coordination (card log 2026-08-19): #1967 pins the failing `??` panic report shape in a golden for tier identity — this card re-blesses that golden when it ships; the golden is not immovable. #2041 (Result/Optional deconstruction) shapes the same journey — coordinate wording, do not block.

## Work
1. Design doc FIRST (criterion 4's before/after lives here): commit docs/proposals/runtime-error-report.md. Contents: (a) inventory of today's shapes — `Stop [code]: what` + `--> file:line in fn` + context box + locals + `Why/Fix` from jet_render_runtime_stop_from_row (crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs:584-682); `Error [code]: msg` + indented `cause:` chain from jet_render_err (:202-223); `error propagated from: fn (file:line) via ?` frames appended by jet_journey_frame (:158-199) into JET_JOURNEY_FRAMES; scheduler transport headers (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs:82-84). (b) the redesigned grammar: ROOT block first (code, what, why, fix, origin frame with context box), then a visually fenced TRAIL section (frames ordered origin→boundary, repeated frames collapsed to `… ×N`, one line each), then locals/extras. (c) the terminal-state matrix: what changes under pipe (no ANSI), NO_COLOR, and widths <80 (no hard wrapping of user data; graceful caret box degradation). (d) before/after renderings of at least three real failing examples from the corpus (a `?`-deep propagation chain, a `??` panic, a task failure). Owner reads this doc for look-and-feel; expect one iteration.
2. Implement in the one renderer: rework jet_render_runtime_stop_from_row and jet_render_err in crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs; give the journey-frame flush (find where JET_JOURNEY_FRAMES drains into the final report at the run boundary) the dedup + ordering pass. Engines (AOT via embedded Prelude, JIT hosts, TIR eval) keep marshalling file/line/fn data only — grep for any host that string-formats its own report lines and route it through Foundation (I9; Scheduler.rs's two-header contract at :82-84 must be updated in lockstep if headers change).
3. Terminal-state handling (criterion 2): find where the rendered report is printed (runtime boundary in Prelude/Core.rs jet_runtime_* paths) and thread tty/NO_COLOR/width detection there — detection at the boundary, format decisions in the one renderer (pass a plain style struct in; never per-engine). Snapshot each matrix cell (tty+ANSI, pipe, NO_COLOR, narrow) through the harness (I4).
4. Tier parity (criterion 3): run the same failing examples under `jet run` (default), `jet run --release` (AOT), and `jet dev` deopt; diff the three reports byte-wise (modulo tty detection — force pipe mode for the diff). Re-bless #1967's pinned golden and any runtime-report goldens in the same change, scoped, with UPDATE_EXPECT_REASON naming this card.
5. Registered rows: update E3001/E3002 what/why/fix wording in the diagnostics registry to match the new grammar; `jet explain E3001/E3002` snapshots re-blessed.
6. Close-out: criterion 4 requires owner visual acceptance — post the before/after renderings (dark-mode-friendly) to the card and hold close until the owner accepts (needsAcceptance).

## Not building
- No change to compile-time diagnostic rendering (that surface already has its format).
- No new error-handling syntax and no dependency on #2041's ballot outcome — if #2041 later re-spells deconstruction, the report grammar here is spelling-agnostic (frames carry fn/file/line, not syntax).
- No stack-unwinding/backtrace capture beyond the existing journey mechanism; no async-trace expansion.
- No logging/telemetry integration.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: snapshot of a deep `?` chain showing root block first, deduped trail (`×N` collapse exercised by a loop that re-propagates the same frame).
- Criterion 2: matrix snapshots — tty vs pipe, ANSI vs NO_COLOR, width 40 — via the snapshot harness; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test` targeted at those tests.
- Criterion 3: recorded three-tier diff (forced pipe mode) on the same failing examples: byte-identical; #1967's golden re-blessed and green on both tiers.
- Criterion 4: the committed design doc's before/after section + owner acceptance note on the card. Implementation itself needs no ballot; look-and-feel is owner-accepted at close.

## blockedBy
none — the renderer, journey mechanism, and harness are all live; #1967 and #2041 are coordination notes, not gates.

log.text: Accepted — D-ACCEPT-2044 resolved through owner verification UI.

OWNER REVIEW — what to look at (2 minutes)

Run this from the repo root:

  scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build
  scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/errors/error_context.jet

Good looks like this, in this order:

  Error: file not found
   Trail [E3002] (3 hops via ?, origin first):
    1. parse_config (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:7) - reading raw config
    2. load_config (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:12) - loading config app.toml
    3. run (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:16)

The first line names the cause. The trail follows it, origin first, one line per hop, each with its file, its line, and the note written at that hop.

The same program printed this before the card:

  error propagated from: parse_config (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:7) via ?: reading raw config
  error propagated from: load_config (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:12) via ?: loading config app.toml
  error propagated from: run (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:16) via ?
  Error: file not found

Reject it if you must read to the last line to learn what failed, if one note repeats, or if the shape changes when you add --release or --interpret to the same command.
All four criteria met with recorded evidence; needsAcceptance holds for owner visual check of the report shape.
Requested acceptance — minted D-ACCEPT-2044.

Criterion 3 is RED on one tier and the card cannot close until it is fixed. Measured 2026-08-19 on builder f30728f4d with the same example on all three legs: 'jet run' and 'jet run --release' print the identical root-cause-then-trail report, but 'jet run --interpret' prints ONLY 'Error: file not found' with no trail block at all. That is an I9 divergence, not a formatting nit - the interpreter is not accumulating hops through the same Prelude journey functions the other two tiers call. Dispatched as its own lane. Criterion 2 (terminal state matrix: tty vs pipe, ANSI vs NO_COLOR, narrow widths, with a snapshot for each) is also still open.

Interaction note: #1967 pins the failing ?? panic report shape in a golden for tier identity. This redesign re-blesses that pinned shape when it ships — coordinate, do not treat the golden as immovable.

Consecutive-identical frames still collapse and now carry a repeat count. Three order copies were found and deleted (Outcome.rs held the order, and the generated wasm store plus the JS projection each concatenated journey+report themselves); all now call one jet_journey_compose. Criterion was 0 percent satisfied before, not partly: the report emitted no ANSI, read no NO_COLOR, read no tty state and read no width, so a pipe, a colour terminal, NO_COLOR and a 40-column terminal all received identical bytes - and the real example's hop lines are 85 and 90 columns, so they already soft-wrapped mid-path at 80. Four matrix fixtures now exist (tests/cli/error_report_pipe.txt, error_report_tty_ansi.txt, error_report_tty_no_color.txt, error_report_tty_narrow40.txt). One design constraint shaped it: Outcome.rs is include_str!'d verbatim into every generated program, so it may use std only - facts go in, policy lives in the one renderer, detection happens in exactly one place, so no per-tier variant can exist and the crate's existing colour ladder now calls that same detector instead of spelling NO_COLOR itself.

Before the fix --interpret printed the root cause with NO trail block. Root cause was not a missing adapter: the hop store is a thread_local and the TIR evaluator runs every interpreted program on a spawned jet-tir-eval worker, so hops were recorded in the worker while the report edge drained the caller's empty list after the join. The same boundary covered the JIT whole-program deopt edge; mid-run deopt was never affected because it stays on the JIT's own thread. Fixed as marshalling - Foundation still owns the list, the collapse and the rendering, and adopting replays carried hops through the same collapse. A cross-tier snapshot test was added, which the trail example had never had; that absence is why the divergence shipped.

   Trail [E3002] (3 hops via ?, origin first):
    1. parse_config (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:7) - reading raw config
    2. load_config (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:12) - loading config app.toml
    3. run (examples/features/errors/error_context.jet:16)

Line one names the cause. The trail follows it, origin first, one line per hop
with file, line, and the note written at that hop.

Before this card the same program printed the three hops first and the cause
last. Bounce it if you must read to the bottom to learn what failed, if a note
repeats, or if adding --release or --interpret changes the shape.

cards.title: jet explain answers glyph and symbol lookups from the syntax registry
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea b26bk7y4 interview): extend jet explain so newcomers can look up any glyph/symbol/token. Probed 2026-08-19: jet help @ falls through to generic help; jet explain @ errors E1274 (explain only knows build refs and diagnostic codes). Syntax.rs is the ratified registry (I7: every user-typeable keyword/sigil lives there with a decision ID), so the dictionary generates from it — one source of truth, no parallel table.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`jet explain @` / `::` / `#Live` / `=>` — any registered user-typeable glyph, sigil, keyword, or marker — answers with name, meaning, owning decision ID, and a one-line example, generated from the I7 registry (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs) with no hand-maintained parallel table. Unknown tokens get a real registered diagnostic with a nearest-match suggestion instead of the E1274 build-log fallthrough; REPL `?name` docs reuse the same source; CLI snapshots cover glyph, keyword, marker, and unknown queries.

## Law
- I7: Syntax.rs is the one registry — every dictionary row must reference the existing constants (KW_*, OP_*, MARKER_*, sigils) and cite the decision ID already recorded on that constant. Adding metadata rows to the Syntax module adds NO user-typeable syntax, so no ballot; the file-header rule (every entry maps to a decision ID) is satisfied because rows only cite already-ratified IDs.
- I4: the unknown-token response is a diagnostic product — registered code with what/why/fix and a snapshot.
- D-JPK-BUILDDBG1 (E1274): the package-ref explain lane keeps working exactly as today for build refs; the token lane slots in front of the fallthrough, never replacing ref explains.

## Work
1. Dictionary rows in the registry: new submodule crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/dictionary.rs (wired like highlights.rs, re-exported from Syntax.rs): `pub struct SyntaxDictEntry { token: &'static str, name: &'static str, meaning: &'static str, decision: &'static str, example: &'static str }` with one table whose `token` fields are the existing constants — e.g. (OP_ARM_ARROW/`=>` … cite the real constant), `::` binding mark (D-BIND-BARE1/D-ALIAS-OP1), `@[`/`]@` fences (D-FENCE-GLYPH1), markers via the marker registry. Coverage is enforced, not hoped: a test asserts every JET_HIGHLIGHT_TOKENS text and every JET_KEYWORD_LIST word (Syntax/package_files.rs:414) has a dictionary row, and every row's token equals a registered constant — that is what "generated from the registry" means here; the metadata lives in the same owner-controlled I7 file family, and no second table exists outside it. FOREIGN_* teaching words stay OUT (they are not valid syntax), mirroring the highlights rule.
2. Lookup + rendering: extend crates/jet-cli/src/Explain.rs with a token lookup (exact match over dictionary rows) rendering name/meaning/decision/example in the existing explain essay style (reuse `render`'s header/theme conventions).
3. CLI dispatch: crates/jetpack/src/CLI/update_search_info.rs currently routes non-code queries into the Jetpack build-ref lane and dies at E1274 (:269-276) — probed live: `jet explain @` → E1274. Insert the token lane before the ref lane: if the query exactly matches a dictionary row → explain it; else if the query is token-shaped (contains a non-identifier character, or `#`-prefixed CamelCase) → the new unknown-token diagnostic; else fall through to today's code/build-ref behavior unchanged. `jet explain E0311` and package refs must behave byte-identically to today.
4. Unknown token (criterion 2): register a new diagnostic code (jetpack/explain family, near E1274 — pick the next free code in the registry) with what ("`{token}` isn't a registered Jet glyph or keyword"), why (the registry is closed, I7), fix carrying the nearest match by edit distance over dictionary tokens ("did you mean `=>`?"). Never emit the build-log E1274 for token-shaped queries.
5. REPL reuse (criterion 3): locate the REPL's `?name` help path (probe tests/repl.rs for `?` queries; the REPL lives off Source/Interpreter.rs / the comptime REPL). Route its symbol-help answers through the same dictionary lookup function — one source, two surfaces. If the REPL has no `?name` today, wire the minimal call-through and snapshot one query; do not build a separate REPL help system.
6. Snapshots (criterion 4): CLI snapshot tests covering `jet explain @` (sigil), `::` (operator), `#Live` (marker), `=>` (arrow), one keyword (`loop`), and one unknown token (`@@` → suggestion). Follow wherever existing `jet explain` CLI output is snapshot-tested (tests/ referencing Explain); scoped bless only.

## Not building
- No new Jet syntax and no changes to any registered token (read-only over the registry).
- `jet help @` generic-help fallthrough is out of scope — criteria name `jet explain` only.
- No fuzzy/semantic search, no HTML/docs-site generation, no localization.
- No changes to build-ref/package explain behavior (E1274 lane preserved for genuine refs).

## Proof
- Criterion 1: live runs of the built binary — `./target/debug/jet explain @`, `::`, `#Live`, `=>` each show name/meaning/decision/example; outputs in card evidence.
- Criterion 2: `./target/debug/jet explain @@` shows the new registered code + nearest-match fix (not E1274); `jet explain some-package-ref` still answers E1274's lane.
- Criterion 3: the coverage test (registry ↔ dictionary bijection over highlight tokens + keyword list) passes; REPL `?` query output shown to match the dictionary row.
- Criterion 4: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test` targeted at the new CLI snapshot tests, run output in evidence.
- CLI-only change: no jet run parity needed.

none — registry, explain renderer, and dispatch seam are all live; no decision gates (no new syntax).
