cards.title: Research: what structure do effect definitions actually need
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea b2z65gxf interview): research card. Original idea: Effects.jet roots are bare names (effect Net) — should they carry subeffects, prohibitions, requirements? Rule for this card: propose fields only with a real consumer attached; no speculative schema.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A committed research report (docs/research/, via `tower docs add --section research`) that (1) names every current consumer of the effect roots in Prelude/Effects.jet with file:line evidence and states what each would do with sub-scoping, implication, or prohibition data; (2) attaches a concrete consumer + use case to every proposed field and explicitly rejects every field without one (YAGNI); (3) recommends adopt/defer per field and raises draft ballots only for surface-visible changes. No schema change to Effects.jet ships from this card.

## Law
- D-META-ONE1=A: the effect roots are written in Prelude/Effects.jet and nowhere else; every consumer reads that list (Facts.rs:168-173). Any proposed field must keep this one-home law.
- D-EFFECT-DECL1=A (card #1299, Syntax.rs:174-175): `effect Root.Leaf` already adds one package-view leaf fact that erases before TIR — sub-scoping partially EXISTS as user-side declarations. The survey must reconcile any root-side subeffect field with this ratified surface instead of duplicating it (I8).
- D-EFFBUDGET1 (E1220/E1221): package effects:/grants: budgets validate against the closed vocabulary (jet-pkg-model Package/Blocks.rs:785).
- D-FACT-LAW1=B: any new effect metadata is a fact row — one home, safe direction, gate word.
- I7: any surface-visible field (new syntax after `effect Name`) needs a ratified decision before implementation — hence criterion 3's ballots.

## Work
1. Build the consumer table. Known entry points to trace and extend (grep `EFFECT_SOURCE|EffectRoots|BuildEffect|effect ` outward from each):
   - **Checker/sema**: jet-foundation/src/Facts.rs:168-173 (EFFECT_SOURCE parse → canonical roots; effect parsing, rule arguments, fact registration, diagnostics, reflection all consume it) and the sema effect-row checker reached from Sema/Effects.rs.
   - **#Caps / marker arguments**: jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs:926 (`RuleArgType::EffectRoots`, "[Effect]"), Policy/MarkerSource.rs:135-137, jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerMarkers.rs:172-217 (list-literal argument checking).
   - **Facts/reflection**: the fact registry rows effects register (Sema/Effects.rs fact_registry) and whatever `jet inspect`/facts JSON renders them.
   - **Package budgets**: jet-pkg-model/src/Package/Blocks.rs:785 (effects:/grants: names must be known roots; E1221) and the E1220 transitive-budget checker (find its call site).
   - **Diagnostics**: Prelude/Diagnostics.jet rows E1220/E1221/E1803 — note E1803 already speaks `{Root}.{Operation}` granularity, live evidence that operation-level sub-scoping demand exists in the REPL today.
   - **REPL/CLI deny flags**: jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:895-899 + 1842-1846 (`--allow-{root}`/`--deny-{root}` generated from BuildEffect::ALL — find where BuildEffect::ALL comes from and whether it re-reads Effects.jet or holds a copy; a copy is a D-META-ONE1 drift finding, file it), jet-repl/src/lib.rs:208-217 (deny > allow > prompt policy).
   - **audit**: locate `jet audit` / `jet inspect guarantees` effect consumers (grep audit + effect in jet-cli); record what they render per root.
   - **FFI runtime family**: Effects.jet:21-38 — the 17 foreign-runtime roots (Go, Java, … Py) are a family with an implicit relationship to `effect FFI`. Answer with evidence: does using `Py` imply `FFI` anywhere today? This is the strongest live implication candidate.
   For each consumer, write one row: what it reads today / what it would do with (a) sub-scoping (Net.Http vs Net), (b) implication (Py ⇒ FFI), (c) prohibition (a root a package may declare it never uses).
2. Evaluate candidate fields against the rule "a field exists only with a real consumer attached":
   - **subeffects/leaves on the root**: weigh against D-EFFECT-DECL1=A (leaves already declarable package-side) and E1803's operation granularity. Likely verdict: the root file needs no field; leaves stay declaration-side — but let the consumer table decide.
   - **implication (root ⇒ root)**: consumer = budget checker (grant Py without separately granting FFI?) and REPL deny flags (deny FFI should deny Py). If the code today special-cases this anywhere, that hardcoding is the consumer; propose the field. If nothing consumes it, reject.
   - **prohibition/requirements on the root**: find a real consumer or reject explicitly (the card body's own YAGNI rule).
   - Any field proposed must state its Effects.jet spelling (comment-level vs parsed syntax) — parsed syntax is surface-visible → ballot.
3. Write the report with the consumer table, per-field adopt/defer verdicts with reasons, and the explicit rejected-fields list. Commit via `tower docs add --section research --title "Effect root structure: consumers and fields" --file <report.md>`.
4. For each ADOPTED surface-visible field only: draft a ballot on this card (`decision add '#2047' --draft --file <payload> --by <You>`). Internal-only findings (e.g. BuildEffect::ALL drift) become bug cards, not ballots.
5. Meet criteria 1-3 with evidence (report path + section anchors; ballot IDs or "none — all fields rejected/internal"). Commit doc + board together.

## Not building
- No edit to crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Effects.jet — this card researches; implementation follows ratification on successor cards.
- No checker/budget/REPL implementation work; drift findings get filed as cards, not fixed here.
- No speculative schema: a field with no consumer row in the table is rejected in writing, not deferred silently.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: the report's consumer table has one row per consumer listed in the criterion (checker, #Caps, facts, diagnostics, audit, repl deny flags) with file:line for each — quote the table anchor in evidence.
- Criterion 2: every proposed field's row names its consumer; the rejected-fields section exists and is non-empty (at minimum, whichever of subeffects/prohibitions/requirements found no consumer).
- Criterion 3: adopt/defer verdict per field recorded; `card show '#2047' --json` lists draft ballots exactly for surface-visible adopted fields, none otherwise.
- Research card: no runtime behavior changes → no run/parity proof; no builds beyond greps and reads.

## blockedBy
none — read-only research over the live tree plus board writes; all referenced law is ratified.

cards.title: Research: cross-language library survey for Core absorption
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea b1trfpk1 interview): research card only — owner runs broader audits manually. Original idea: look at the best and most commonly used libraries across all major languages; what can Core absorb to make exceptional experiences and obviate external libs for as many users as possible.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
One committed survey document `docs/research/core-absorption-survey-2026-08.md` covering the top libraries **by real usage** across Python, JS/TS, Rust, Go, Java/Kotlin, C#, Swift, Ruby, and PHP; every candidate mapped to already-in-Core (with evidence), gap-worth-absorbing (with a proposed surface sketch), or explicitly-out (with a reason); absorption candidates ranked by user reach and cross-referenced against existing Core coverage and the #1161 framework-transplant lineage; follow-up Tower cards minted for accepted gaps. **No implementation, no ballots** — owner ruling 2026-08-19: research card only.

## Law
No decision dependencies — research-only task; the deliverable mints follow-up cards, not decisions. Owner ruling on idea b1trfpk1 bounds scope (owner runs broader audits manually).

## Work
1. Prior art first (extend, never redo): `docs/research/corelib-lauded-designs-2026-08-06.md`, `prelude-scope-across-languages-2026-08-06.md`, `corelib-api-usage-frequency-2026-08-06.md`, `docs/proposals/corelib-overhaul.md`. Coverage evidence base: `docs/reference/core-library.md` + `docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json` (machine-checkable Core surface) + `docs/reference/python-surface.json`.
2. Usage evidence per ecosystem (criterion 1 — "usage evidence, not vibes"): pull top ~20 libraries per ecosystem from primary download/usage sources — PyPI (pypistats/top-packages), npm download counts, crates.io downloads, Go module proxy import counts, Maven Central, NuGet, SwiftPM index + CocoaPods, RubyGems, Packagist. Record source + date + number for every row in the doc.
3. Dedupe the ~180 rows into capability clusters (HTTP client, serialization, CLI args, datetime, DB access, testing, logging, async/concurrency, crypto, validation, templating, compression, image, retry/resilience, i18n, …).
4. Verdict per cluster (criterion 2): check Jet Core coverage via the surface ledger + core-library.md, and settle ambiguity with live binary probes (`jet run` one-liners in /tmp — shipped behavior beats docs). Verdicts: **already-in-Core** (cite ledger id / doc section / probe output), **gap** (sketch the proposed `core.<ns>` surface at signature-header level only — no design pass), or **out** (reason: framework-scale, OS-specific, churns too fast, conflicts with a ratified decline like D-STR-DECLINE1/D-SET-DECLINE1).
5. Rank gaps by user reach (criterion 3): normalized download share of the libraries each gap obviates, summed across ecosystems; cross-reference `#1161` framework-transplant lineage so retired/decided transplants are not re-litigated (link verdict rows).
6. Commit the doc. Mint follow-up cards: one per accepted gap cluster (`kind: task` research→feature promotion left to the owner lane), each ref'ing the survey section; log the minted card ids on #2048 (`card update '#2048' --log`).

## Not building
- No Core code, no spec/decision edits, no ballots, no proposals beyond header-level surface sketches.
- No re-run of the 2026-08-06 research corpus (delta on top of it).
- No manual broader-audit scope — the owner runs those.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: doc contains all nine ecosystems, each row with a linked usage source + number + retrieval date.
- Criterion 2: every candidate row carries one of the three verdicts with its evidence cell (ledger id, probe transcript, or reason).
- Criterion 3: ranking table present; lineage cross-ref section links #1161 verdicts; the card log lists the minted follow-up card ids. Doc committed (git hash in the card log).

cards.title: TUI DX audit: every Jet-facing terminal surface vs omp-grade interaction
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea b1l7zqt1 interview): design-goal audit card. Original idea: Oh My Pi as inspiration for all user-facing TUI ux/dx/ui. Audit every Jet-facing TUI surface against omp-quality interaction patterns and produce a gap list plus follow-up cards.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A committed TUI DX audit (docs/audits/tui-dx-audit-2026-08-XX.md) that inventories every Jet-facing terminal surface with live current-state captures, scores each against named omp-grade interaction patterns, and lands a ranked follow-up card list on the Tower plus a durable principles reference (docs/reference/tui-interaction.md) that future TUI work cites. Audit card: NO implementation — the deliverable is the report, the principles doc, and the minted follow-up cards.

## Law
- No decision dependencies — audit/task work. Honor existing ratified TUI law as the scoring baseline, not as ballot targets: D-FE-REPL1=D (hybrid REPL), D-FE-HELP1=D (`jet ?` interactive help), D-REPL-COLOR=A + shared NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR policy (jet-foundation Terminal/Theme), D-FE-REPL-MULTILINE1=A, D-FE-REPL-HISTORY1=A, I4 (diagnostics registered + rendered via the one shared renderer), I6 (std-only; `stty` shell-out, no line-editing crates).
- Prior art to build on, not duplicate: docs/audits/cli-diagnostics-accessibility.md, docs/audits/persona-audit-2026-08-14.md.

## Work
1. Fix the surface inventory (criterion 1 names seven; capture all, add any found while tracing — candidates in parentheses are also user-facing and MUST be included):
   - REPL: crates/jet-repl/src/{Interactive.rs,Render.rs,Term.rs,History.rs} — raw-mode loop, turn gutter, pin rail, folds, ^B bindings pane, F3 history search.
   - Dev loop: `jet dev` — Source/CmdDevTools.rs (`run_dev`, `render_dev_iteration`), jet::DevServer (incl. `jet inspect live` polling loop, Source/main.rs:1509-1537 — hand-rolled `\x1b[2J\x1b[H` clear).
   - Test runner: `jet test` progress/result output — Source/CmdCompile.rs `run_test_opts` and the harness output contract.
   - Build/progress output: `jet build`/`jet run` compile progress, timing lines — CmdCompile `run_compile_cmd` and Driver progress rendering.
   - Diagnostics: the shared renderer (`jet::render_all_colored`, jet-diagnostics) — human frame, colors, spans, `jet explain` pointer line.
   - Explain: `jet explain <code>` and `jet inspect …` textual reports (CmdDevTools `run_explain`, CmdDossier).
   - Canvas CLI: the canvas/scene terminal surface (tests/canvas.rs entry points, docs/reference/canvas-protocol.md).
   - (Also: `jet ?` interactive help app — run_question_mark, Source/main.rs:1040-1076; `jet debug` interactive session — crates/jet-debug; `jet notebook` terminal client; bare-`jet` greeting + usage_page.)
2. Current-state capture per surface: drive the LIVE binary (fresh `cargo build` jet), record transcripts under both TTY (use `script -qec` or a pty helper) and non-TTY/piped, with and without NO_COLOR=1, plus a narrow-terminal (COLUMNS=60) run. Store raw captures in the audit doc as fenced blocks (trim to representative excerpts; note exact commands so they are reproducible).
3. Score each surface against the named interaction patterns (criterion 2, one row per surface x pattern, score + one-line evidence): responsiveness (first paint, perceived latency, streaming vs batch), keyboard model (consistent keys, discoverability, escape/cancel behavior), progressive disclosure (folds, summaries, drill-down like omp's), color/NO_COLOR discipline (Theme-only color, no raw escapes outside Term — grep for `\x1b[` outside jet-foundation Terminal/jet-repl Term as a mechanical check), resize behavior (SIGWINCH/redraw or graceful degradation).
4. Gap list: each concrete gap gets severity (P1-P3), affected surface, evidence pointer, and a one-line proposed fix direction. Rank the list.
5. Deliverables: (a) docs/audits/tui-dx-audit-<date>.md — inventory + captures + scorecard + ranked gaps; (b) docs/reference/tui-interaction.md — the durable principles (the five patterns above as requirements, the Theme/NO_COLOR rule, the raw-mode/I6 rule, the non-TTY floor rule), written so future cards cite sections; (c) mint one Tower follow-up card per ranked gap cluster (`node plugins/tower/tower.mjs card add … --by <name>`, kind bug/task, refs back to the audit doc + this card), then list the minted card numbers in this card's log and in the report; commit board JSON immediately after minting (tracked-store rule).
6. Close-out: update this card's criteria evidence with the doc paths + minted card ids.

## Not building
- No code changes to any surface — fixes belong to the minted follow-up cards.
- No re-audit of diagnostic wording/registration (I4 is covered by docs/audits/cli-diagnostics-accessibility.md; only its interaction/rendering gaps are in scope here).
- No LSP/editor/browser (non-terminal) surfaces; the notebook browser client is out — only its terminal client is in.
- No new ballots: scoring against ratified law, not proposing syntax.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: report section per named surface (repl, dev loop, test runner, build/progress, diagnostics, explain, canvas CLI) each with a reproducible capture block — verify by reading the committed doc.
- Criterion 2: scorecard table covers every surface x all five named patterns with evidence pointers — mechanical check: every row cites a capture or file:line.
- Criterion 3: `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs card show '#<new>'` for each minted follow-up card; docs/reference/tui-interaction.md exists and at least the minted cards' bodies cite it. `git log --oneline -1` showing report + reference + board committed together.
- No runtime-behavior change → no jet run/AOT parity probe; no test suite runs (audit-only).

cards.title: fmt simplify: owner demo plus IR unification so R2/R3 can enable
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-19 (idea bcyn0x8b interview): two-part card. #1514 shipped fmt --simplify with R1 (braced single-return to = expr) and R4 (integer fences to ranges); R2 (else-if chain to one ordered arm table) and R3 (drop redundant Type.{ head) are DISABLED because they change parsed AST identity (subjectless nested Switch vs dispatch; inferred vs named StructLit). Part (a): owner-facing demo of what --simplify does today. Part (b): unify the IR forms so R2/R3 rewrites prove AST equality and can enable. R2/R3 are the two most visible rewrites of the original goal.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Two-part deliverable per the owner ruling: (a) an owner-facing before/after demo of what `jet fmt --simplify` does today (R1 braced-single-return → `::` body, R4 integer fences → ranges) on real corpus files, presented for visual acceptance (card is needsAcceptance); (b) the parsed-AST forms behind R2 (else-if chain → one ordered arm table) and R3 (drop redundant `Type.{` head) are unified so both rewrites pass the span-free AST-identity check, and R2/R3 are enabled in the simplify catalog with fmt idempotence and corpus `--check` staying green.

## Law
- D-FMT-SIMPLIFY1=A (card #1514) — opt-in `--simplify`, only ratified simplest-spelling rewrites; identity check compares simplify output against plain-fmt output (crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/mod.rs:1671-1695; implementation log docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7323).
- D-IFGUARD1=A — subjectless guard tables reuse `if`/`else`/arm arrows; classic `if` and the guard table are intentionally ONE semantic node (`Stmt::Switch` with compiler-private `true` subject; crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/statements.rs:35-60).
- D-IFDIST1=A — comparison-marked dispatch; D-DOTCTOR1/D-DOTCTOR3 — `Type.{ … }` named vs `.{ … }` inferred struct/typed literals (crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/expressions.rs:556-583).
- No new user-typeable syntax (I7 untouched): both rewrites emit already-ratified spellings.

## Work
1. Demo first (criterion 1, independent of R2/R3): run `jet fmt --simplify` across `examples/**/*.jet` and `tests/ui/*.fixed.jet`, collect real diffs, and assemble a short owner demo (one before/after pair per rule R1/R4, same program both sides, real Jet syntax, dark-mode-friendly if rendered). Park it on the card log/refs for acceptance at close.
2. Ground R2. Today a classic chain `if a {…} else if b {…} else {…}` parses as NESTED subjectless `Stmt::Switch` (each `else if` = a one-arm Switch in `else_body`; formatter prints it back via `switch_was_classic_if` + the else-if pattern at Formatter/Statements.rs:1007-1011), while the guard table `if { a -> …; b -> …; else -> … }` parses FLAT (one Switch, N arms). Unify at the parser: extend the existing one-node precedent (statements.rs:35-60) so a classic else-if chain parses into the FLAT arm-list Switch — the parser appends each `else if` arm instead of nesting, and classic spelling stays recoverable from source spans via `uses_classic_if_spelling` (spelling is already span-derived, not AST-derived, so plain fmt round-trip is preserved).
3. Migrate every consumer of the nested shape found by grep `is_subjectless_guard` / nested-else-if patterns: TIR lowering `else_is_elseif` (jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs:3231, lower/control_flow.rs:826), subset statements.rs:660, sema CheckerCore/switches.rs (subjectless arms>1 paths already exist at 919), devserver edit_actions/graph_projection classic-if projections, formatter classic printer (fmt_classic_switch). Behavior must be provably unchanged: nested and flat lower identically (`} else if`), so this is shape migration, not semantics.
4. Implement R2 in the simplify catalog (Formatter/Statements.rs beside R4 at 157): a subjectless classic chain of >=2 arms emits the guard-table arm form. With step 2 done, simplify output reparses to the identical flat Switch → identity assert (mod.rs:1692) passes.
5. Ground R3. `Rect.{…}` vs `.{…}` differ in AST (`StructLit { type_name, inferred }` / `TypedLit { head: Option }`). Dropping a head can never canonicalize away blindly (it would equate `Rect.{…}` with `Point.{…}`). Unify via context elaboration in the identity check: teach `canonical_program` (Formatter/mod.rs:36) a normalization pass that, for struct/typed literals in syntactically-typed positions ONLY (binding with declared type `x: Rect = …`, field value whose field type is named in the same file's struct decl is NOT syntactic — exclude; typed-list element under a `[T].{` head; `return` of a function whose declared return type is in this AST), fills the inferred head from that context — mirroring exactly the elaboration sema performs (expressions.rs:574-577).
6. Implement R3 gated to exactly the positions step 5's normalizer proves: drop the head only where (i) the context names the same type syntactically and (ii) the resulting bare `.{` still parses there — respect the `expr_no_struct_lit` refusal (a `::` one-line body cannot open `{`; see tests/fmt.rs:1070 `fmt_simplify_keeps_a_struct_literal_return_braced` — that constraint stays).
7. Enable both rules only under `options.simplify`; plain `jet fmt` output must be byte-identical to today. Update the D-FMT-SIMPLIFY1 implementation log in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md (7323-7329) to record R2/R3 enabling.
8. If step 2's blast radius proves the parser unification unsafe (a consumer genuinely needs the nested shape), fall back to normalizing nested→flat inside `canonical_program` only (same place R3's normalizer lives) and record why in the card log — the identity check is the ratified arbiter either way.

## Not building
- New simplify rules beyond R2/R3; changes to plain (non-simplify) fmt output.
- Sema-powered simplification (R3 stays syntactic-context only; no type inference in the formatter).
- Changes to the guard-table or dispatch grammar itself.
- Auto-applying --simplify anywhere (stays opt-in per D-FMT-SIMPLIFY1=A).

## Proof
- Criterion 1: demo artifact linked on the card; owner visual acceptance at close (needsAcceptance).
- Criteria 2-3: new tests in tests/fmt.rs — an else-if chain simplifies to the arm table and round-trips the identity check; a typed-binding `Rect.{…}` drops to `.{…}`; a return-position struct literal stays braced; `.{` never emitted where `expr_no_struct_lit` refuses it; guard-table input is untouched (already simplest).
- Criterion 4: R2/R3 active under --simplify; `fmt(fmt(x)) == fmt(x)` on every corpus file (existing tests/fmt.rs idempotence law, spec.md:1131); `jet fmt --check` over examples/ stays green; second `--simplify` pass is a no-op on a file exercising R1-R4.
- Parser unification (step 2) is a compiler-shape change: run the focused switch/dispatch sema+TIR test set and one example golden through default `jet run` and `--release` AOT to prove lowering parity. Full suite at epoch closeout.

none — D-FMT-SIMPLIFY1=A is ratified with R2/R3 named in the original card #1514 scope; the owner ruling on this card (2026-08-19) authorizes the IR unification route.

cards.title: persist.jet teaches the real hot-reload journey
cards.body: From owner interview 2026-08-19 (retired ideas b02bgft8/b7jiiibo). #Persist hot-reload persistence is implemented (#765; test persist_binding_survives_hot_swap_and_resets_on_shape_change) but examples/features/devloop/persist.jet is an inert print of the initial value — it never shows the point: mutate state at runtime, hot-reload code, state survives (the game-dev on-the-fly-test loop). Rework the example (or add a devloop journey doc/example pair) so the teaching corpus shows real survival across a jet dev hot swap, within golden-test constraints. Equality teaching needs no new work: probed 2026-08-19, == works on all primitives and structs auto-derive it; examples/features/types/auto_derive_policy/main.jet covers the policy surface.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`examples/features/devloop/persist.jet` stops being an inert print of the initial value and teaches the real hot-reload journey — mutate state at runtime, hot-swap code, `#Persist` state survives, shape change resets — while its golden stays deterministic under plain `jet run`; the dev-tier survival claim is proven by a scripted `jet dev` test that drives this exact example file.

## Law
- D-PERSIST1 — `#Persist` module binding survives `jet dev` hot reload (identity = module path + binding name + compatible shape); release/run semantics identical with or without the marker (persist.jet:1-10; shipped by #765).
- I5 — features ship executable examples with goldens; golden output must stay deterministic.
- I9 — dev-tier carry-across lives in the shared `jet_foundation::Persist` store consulted by both interpreter and Cranelift tiers (persist.jet:8-10); this card must not add engine-side persist logic.
- No decision dependencies beyond the shipped D-PERSIST1 — mechanical example/teaching work.

## Work
1. Read the shipped proof first: `tests/dev.rs::persist_binding_survives_hot_swap_and_resets_on_shape_change` — copy its session-driving mechanics (how it starts `jet dev`, swaps source, reads output) rather than inventing new harness plumbing.
2. Rework `examples/features/devloop/persist.jet` into a journey program: `#Persist counter := 0`, and `run()` MUTATES the state before printing (e.g. `counter += 1; print("{counter}")`). Under plain `jet run` this prints exactly `1` every time — deterministic golden. Under `jet dev`, each hot swap re-runs `run()` against the SURVIVING counter, so the printed number climbs — the on-the-fly-test loop made visible.
3. Rewrite the example's comment narration to teach the journey explicitly: what you see on first run, what you see after editing an unrelated line and saving (counter keeps counting — survival), what you see after changing the binding's shape (reset), and why plain `jet run` always prints 1. Keep the `// --- expected output ---` golden block in the corpus's exact format.
4. Add (or extend beside) a dev test in tests/dev.rs that drives THIS example file: start a scripted `jet dev` session on `examples/features/devloop/persist.jet`, observe first output `1`, apply a hot swap that touches code but not the binding shape (e.g. edit the print label), observe the next output proves the counter survived (`2`), then a shape-change swap and observe reset to `1`. Reuse the existing test's swap/reset assertions; the new value is that the teaching corpus file itself is the fixture.
5. If the corpus harness or `jet dev` cannot target an examples/ path directly, have the test copy persist.jet into its tempdir verbatim (byte-identical fixture) so the example is still the thing proven; note which route was taken in the card log.
6. Sweep sibling teaching surfaces that quote persist.jet's old inert output (grep docs/ and examples index for the example) and update the quoted text.

## Not building
- Equality/auto-derive teaching — probed 2026-08-19: `==` and struct auto-derive are covered by examples/features/types/auto_derive_policy/main.jet; explicitly no new work (card body).
- Changes to the persist store, hot-swap machinery, or `#Persist` semantics (shipped by #765).
- A separate journey doc if the reworked example + comments carry the teaching alone; a paired doc is the fallback, not the default.
- Interactive/animated demos; goldens stay plain text.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: the reworked example shows runtime mutation + hot reload + survival — evidenced by the file diff plus the scripted dev-session test output (survival step asserts a value that can only exist if state crossed the swap).
- Criterion 2: corpus golden harness passes on persist.jet under default `jet run` AND `jet run --release` (identical `1` — I9/release-inertness of `#Persist` proven at both tiers); the new tests/dev.rs case passes (`cargo test --test dev persist` focused run in the builder worktree); existing persist test stays green.
- Full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — D-PERSIST1 machinery and the dev-test harness both ship today; this is example + test work on existing seams.

log.text: Finding (2026-08-20): criterion 1 as written is not buildable today. A module-level `#Persist counter := 0` cannot be mutated from a function - sema reports E0111 `counter` is a const and can never change (live probe at HEAD). So a journey example that increments the persisted value does not compile, and the wave-4 lane's rewrite broke the golden suite; the inert-print example was restored to keep the corpus green. Real work needed first: a mutable module-level persist binding (or a ratified spelling for one). Then the journey example plus a scripted jet dev session can land.

cards.title: Structure is a value: engineering-principles audit — proposal and ballot slate
cards.body: First-principles audit of Jet against the classic software-engineering principles (owner request 2026-08-19). Verdict: Jet already enforces more principles as law than any peer (visibility ladder, acyclic imports, contracts, effects, delegation). Five structure truths have no home: name liveness, API lifecycle, import-edge rules, cross-cutting policy home, and template reach into registries. Proposal frames all five as one fact plane under D-FACT-LAW1 and mints six direction-level ballots D-STRUCT-PLANE1/LIVE1/LIFE1/EDGE1/POLICY1/ONCE1. Probes also found drift bugs filed as separate cards (trait-value coercion E0112 vs spec.md:814; inline-module struct E0119; E0113 self-contradictory fix text).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Criteria 4-8 of this card are closed: all six ratified outcomes (D-STRUCT-PLANE1=A, LIVE1=A, LIFE1=A, EDGE1=A, POLICY1=A, ONCE1=A, ratified 2026-08-19) are recorded as an operative slate section in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md; one implementation card per outcome is minted with I4/I5/I7/I9 build gates; the Syntax.rs I7 registry carries the new-surface entries; the syntax-decisions log entry exists; jet devtools grammars are regenerated and snapshots re-blessed for the surface the recording itself changes. Criteria 1-3 are already met — do not re-litigate the ballots.

## Law
- The six ratified decisions on this card, verbatim from `card show '#2052'`: D-STRUCT-PLANE1=A (structure facts join the fact registry; rows: liveness/lifecycle/edge, each with safe direction + gate word; `jet inspect structure`), D-STRUCT-LIVE1=A (four verdicts: unused_import/unused_binding/unused_fn/unreachable_export; `_name` suppression; export tier scoped to pub(package) + application targets; library pub exempt), D-STRUCT-LIFE1=A (#Deprecated(since:, use:, removed_in:?) marker for every package; BOTH Core table copies deleted — jet-pkg-model Manifest.rs:110-141 canonical + Sema/Edition.rs:34 mirror; cbor.encode/decode become ordinary markers; warning rides the live L2001/E2002 path re-reading the marker registry; removed_in dormant until editions), D-STRUCT-EDGE1=A (boundaries: manifest key, effect-budget shape, deny rows {from,to} with one trailing-* subtree wildcard per side, resolution-time check, error names edge+rule index+two fixes, zero-match rule = liveness warning), D-STRUCT-POLICY1=A (user-declared policy settings via checked marker-body machinery D-META-USER1=A; `pub policy name(params) { wrap(call) { … } }`; preserved-contract invariant of D-CALLPOLICY2; nominal, package-scoped; #Policy/apply spelling untouched), D-STRUCT-ONCE1=A (@loop legal in marker bodies, top-level impl-item position, test/bench blocks; sources are written literal tables/comptime-pure values; TWO NAMED AMENDMENTS: closed-type-list comptime binding kind beyond D-GENMOD-VALUE1, and interpolated declaration names in marker bodies).
- Owner ratification comment on D-STRUCT-ONCE1 (binding): "With this decision, we need to reverse the decision made earlier today to erase @if and collapse to if." The reversal is part of criterion 4's recording work.
- Anchors the slate composes with: D-FACT-LAW1=B, D-LINTPOLICY1, D-NAME-SIGIL1, D-EFFBUDGET1, D-PACKAGE-POLICY-SCOPE1, D-CALLPOLICY1=E/D-CALLPOLICY2=C (shipped), D-META-USER1=A, D-META-CODE1=A, D-ONCE-LAW1, greenfield law, D-VERDICT-1455-1 (markers exist iff registered).
- House rule (memory://root, #1889 lesson): the spec slate section is the operative wording; ballot texts are historical.

## Work
1. Resolve the @if reversal FIRST, since the ONCE1 spec entry depends on it: the erase-@if/collapse-to-if decision is NOT in the Tower decision store as of this plan (searched: no decision, no verdict row mentions it). It is being drafted/recorded today on the isomorphic-ontology ballot cards (#2039-#2043 lineage — D-VERDICT-2039-1 is that slate's first ratified row). Locate it via `jq` over .tower/tower.json decisions + `card show` on #2040-#2043, and ask Main/Ballot204xb over hub if absent. Then record the reversal where the original lives (reopen/amend that decision per owner comment, quoting it) and make the D-STRUCT-ONCE1 spec entry state plainly: `@if` survives as the comptime conditional beside `@loop`. If the original truly was never recorded, log that finding on #2052 and record the owner comment itself as the operative ruling in the slate entry.
2. Criterion 4a + 6 — write the slate section at the END of docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md (match the existing end-of-file slate style, e.g. the D-MEM slate): one entry per decision carrying the operative wording distilled from the ratified option-A technical text (the Law section above is the checklist), each naming its amendments explicitly — LIFE1 opens the Core-only E2001/E2002/L2001 area to every package; ONCE1 carries its two template-law amendments and the @if reversal note. Cite docs/proposals/structure-program-is-a-value.md as the source proposal and card #2052.
3. Criterion 4b — mint six implementation cards (`card add`, epoch e3, refs = proposal + decision ID, `--by <You>`), each with observable exit criteria and gates:
   - **PLANE1 card** (substrate): structure fact rows (liveness/lifecycle/edge kinds) in the fact registry with stated safe direction + gate word; `jet inspect structure` lens; drift guard (a row with no direction/gate fails the compiler's own build); I3 runtime erasure. Natural host: the name ledger / D-NAME-TREE1 resolver work (proposal "Implementation shape A"). Other cards block on this one.
   - **LIVE1 card**: four registered diagnostics (I4: code + what/why/fix + UI snapshot each), `_name` suppression honored, policy names unused_import/unused_binding/unused_fn/unreachable_export deny/allow-able; the package-wide reference pass for the export tier (pub(package) + application targets only; library pub exempt); `jet fix` remove-or-underscore repair; I5 example + golden; I9 same verdicts on every tier (facts are compile-time — state the trivially-satisfied tier story in the card). Note the proposal's escape hatch: if the reference pass proves expensive, file-local ships and the export tier gets its own criterion evidence.
   - **LIFE1 card**: #Deprecated registered in Prelude/Markers.jet (D-VERDICT-1455-1: registry row or it does not exist); L2001/E2002 emission rewired from the hardcoded table (CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs) to the marker registry; BOTH table copies deleted in the same change (greenfield); cbor.encode/decode migrated to markers; `jet fix` applies plain-rename replacements; removed_in: optional + warn-only until editions; policy name deprecated_use.
   - **EDGE1 card**: `boundaries:` key parsed in jet-pkg-model (sibling of the effects: block, Package/Blocks.rs), registered diagnostic naming edge + rule index + both fixes (I4), check at import resolution, zero-runtime presence, zero-match rule surfaces as a liveness warning (ties to LIVE1), I5 example.
   - **POLICY1 card**: `pub policy name(params) { wrap(call) { … } }` declaration riding D-META-USER1 marker-body machinery; wrap body is ordinary checked Jet; effects join the wrapped row visibly; signature edits forbidden (D-CALLPOLICY2 preserved-contract invariant); unknown setting stays an error naming the declaring package; I7: new user-typeable syntax → Syntax.rs rows + grammar + snapshots on that card.
   - **ONCE1 card**: @loop reaches marker bodies / impl-item position / test+bench blocks; the two amendments implemented exactly as named; orphan rule at expansion site; `jet inspect expand` coverage; dogfood migration = acceptance test: Units.jet 24-row prefix blocks (~700 lines), Errors.jet 13 impls, the 4x3x2 bench matrix — deletions land with the feature per greenfield.
   Wire blockedBy: LIVE1/LIFE1/EDGE1 cards → PLANE1 card; POLICY1 and ONCE1 are independent. Commit the board immediately after minting (tracked-store lesson).
4. Criterion 5 — Syntax.rs (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs): add the I7 entries the slate creates: MARKER_DEPRECATED (LIFE1), the boundaries: manifest field constant (package_files module, EDGE1), the `policy` declaration word (POLICY1), and the @loop position extension note + @if reversal note (ONCE1); PLANE1/LIVE1 add no token — record them as "adds no token" doc lines, the file's established pattern. Constants without shipped parser support are legal there (see the D-CONC block precedent, Syntax.rs:230-232: rows land now, parsing lands on the implementation cards).
5. Criteria 7 + 8 — regenerate the editor grammars (the devtools grammar regen path named by D-VERDICT-1455-1's CI guards; find the command via `jet devtools --help` / the grammar-generation test) and re-bless the affected snapshots (`cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` bless flow) — scoped to what steps 2-4 actually change (doc + registry rows). If grammar output is byte-identical because no marker row shipped yet (rows may land with the POLICY1/ONCE1 impl cards instead — decide by whether step 4 adds registry rows or doc-only lines), record that as the criterion evidence rather than forcing a diff.
6. Meet criteria 4-8 with concrete evidence (spec section anchor + commit, six card numbers AND Tower ids — numbers are reusable, ids are not — Syntax.rs diff, grammar/snapshot command output). Commit source + board together.

## Not building
- No implementation of any element — verdicts, marker rewiring, boundaries parsing, policy declarations, template reach all belong to the six minted cards.
- No re-opening of ballot content; the six outcomes are ratified =A and the review passes stand.
- The drift-bug cards #2053/#2054/#2055 are separate and untouched.
- The @if reversal is recorded, not implemented: if the collapse shipped code today, reverting that code belongs to a card named in step 1's finding, not to this pass.

## Proof
- Criterion 4: spec slate section committed (quote heading + commit hash); `card list` shows the six impl cards with criteria and refs; blockedBy edges present.
- Criterion 5: Syntax.rs diff showing the entries; the file's own I7 header rule satisfied (every entry maps to a D-STRUCT id now in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md).
- Criterion 6: the syntax-decisions log entry (the file's changelog convention) in the same commit.
- Criteria 7/8: grammar-regen command output + re-blessed snapshot test run (`cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` green), or the recorded byte-identical no-op rationale.
- Recording changes no runtime behavior → no jet run/--release parity probe; full-suite proof stays at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy

cards.title: Trait value never forms at argument position: E0112 rejects what spec.md:814 promises
cards.body: Spec (spec.md:814, S48): 'A trait name in type position ([Shape], fn f(s: Shape)) means dynamic dispatch with invisible boxing.' Probe: trait Shape + struct Circle impl Shape + fn show(s: Shape); calling show(c) with c :: Circle.{radius: 1.0} fails E0112 'show wants Shape (a trait value) for argument 1, but this is Circle'. Same for direct literal argument. Only the [Shape] list-literal path coerces (examples/features/types/traits.jet golden only exercises that path). Fix text 'use Shape (a trait value) here' gives no way to make one — repair-determinism defect too. Repro: target-probes/sr/trait3.jet, jet run exits 1. DIP through trait params is unusable at call sites until this lands.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A trait value forms at argument position exactly as spec.md:814 (S48) promises: `fn show(s: Shape)` called with a concrete `Circle` value (binding or literal) compiles, boxes invisibly, and dispatches dynamically. The probe `target-probes/sr/trait3.jet` runs and prints the area on AOT, default jet run, and interpreter, byte-identical. E0112 fix text for trait-parameter mismatches becomes actionable (never prescribes an unmakeable "trait value"). Snapshots re-blessed.

## Law
- spec.md:814 S48 (ratified): a trait name in type position (`[Shape]`, `fn f(s: Shape)`) means dynamic dispatch with invisible boxing. Default resolution is IMPLEMENT the promise; the criterion's spec-correction alternative applies only if implementation uncovers a genuinely unratified surface question — log it on the card if so.
- D-ANY-JAI1 (single-trait `as_trait` coercion shape, already shipped for list literals).
- I4 (repair-determinism of the E0112 fix text), I9 (tier parity).

## Work
1. Root cause (located): `direct_calls.rs:1603-1669` — `check_type_assignable` (type_assign.rs:833) returns `false` for a SATISFIED TraitObject arm ("compatibility not handled"), then `compatible` (line 1641) demands exact type equality → generic E0112 with `Type::show()`'s "(a trait value)" rendering (jet-foundation AST/types.rs:2066). The list-literal path (CheckerInfer/expr.rs:3866-3898) instead sets `StructLit.as_trait` so codegen boxes.
2. Sema fix: in the argument-check paths (direct_calls.rs; audit the method-call/lambda/variadic equivalents in calls/method_calls.rs, helpers_call_values.rs, variadic.rs for the same equality gate), when `param_ty` is a single-trait `Type::TraitObject` and the arg's concrete type `implements_trait`, accept the argument and mark the coercion:
   - `Expr::StructLit` argument → set `as_trait`, mirroring the list path.
   - Non-literal argument (`show(c)`) → the existing `as_trait` mechanism only covers StructLit (TIR lower statements.rs:1772, emit expressions.rs:2918 `Box::new(lit) as Box<dyn Trait>`). Add one coercion seam in TIR lowering for a call argument whose concrete type meets a TraitObject parameter — box the value in AOT emit, and mirror the marshalling in TIR eval (eval/exprs.rs StructLit as_trait handling shows the value-shape) and the JIT lowering. One mechanism for literal and non-literal; check first how a `[Shape]` list built from IDENTS behaves today and reuse/extend whatever codegen path that exercises.
3. Verify sibling positions with quick probes (return position `=> Shape`, binding `s :: Shape :: c`): fix argument position on this card; if others fail, log them (new card) rather than widening scope.
4. E0112 fix text: after the fix, satisfied-trait cases no longer reach E0112. For remaining genuine mismatches (type does NOT implement the trait), the path already emits e0905 via type_assign.rs:837 — confirm no E0112 with "use Shape (a trait value) here" survives; adjust `type_fix_hint` if it can still render an unmakeable prescription (I4).
5. Example: extend `examples/features/types/traits.jet` with a function taking a trait parameter called with a concrete binding AND a direct literal; regenerate golden (the current golden only exercises the `[Shape]` list path).

## Not building
- Multi-trait objects (`TraitObject` len > 1) at argument position — unchanged.
- No generics/monomorphization redesign; no effect-bound changes for dynamic dispatch (D-EFF3 path untouched).
- Inline-module visibility (#2054) is sibling-owned.

## Proof
- `jet run target-probes/sr/trait3.jet` exits 0 and prints the area; byte-identical on `jet run`, `jet run --release`, interpreter (criteria 1+2).
- Direct-literal-argument variant also passes.
- Updated traits.jet golden green on all tiers; diagnostic snapshots re-blessed. Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

cards.title: Struct declared in an inline module is invisible to its own module (E0119); E0113 emits self-contradictory fix
cards.body: Probe: module bank { pub struct Account { balance: Int } pub fn open() { a :: Account.{balance: 100} } } fails E0119 'no type called Account' — the struct is unusable inside its own inline module, in type position and literal position, qualified or not. Generic modules (module cache<K>(...) { pub struct Buffer ... }) DO support member structs, so plain inline modules are inconsistent. Shipped evidence: examples/features/web/ui_showcase.jet:16-29 documents being unable to group functions into #Target(JS) module browser {} because of this bug plus an I2 codegen rejection, and ships 10 repeated per-function #Target(JS) tags as the workaround. Related message bug from same repro: E0113 says "promises to return bank.Account, but this returns vis2.bank.Account ... Fix: use bank.Account here" — the fix prescribes exactly what the user wrote (I4 violation). Repros: target-probes/sr/vis3.jet (E0119), target-probes/sr/vis2.jet (E0113).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A struct declared inside a plain inline module is visible to its own module: the card-body probe (`module bank { pub struct Account { balance: Int } pub fn open() { a :: Account.{balance: 100} } }`) compiles, in type position and literal position, qualified or not. E0113 never emits a self-contradictory fix (prescribing exactly the spelling the user wrote). Diagnostic snapshots re-blessed.

## Law
- D-MOD2 / D-MOD3 (inline module item mangling + qualified access), D-NAME-WALK1=A (inline module scoping maps) — this is a bug fix inside their shipped semantics; no new syntax.
- I4: the E0113 fix must never prescribe the rejected spelling.

## Work
1. Repros: `target-probes/sr/vis3.jet` (E0119 "no type called Account") and `target-probes/sr/vis2.jet` (E0113 "promises to return bank.Account, but this returns vis2.bank.Account ... Fix: use bank.Account here"). Reproduce both on the current binary first.
2. E0119 half: trace `Sema/Pipeline.rs:923-931` — `Item::CodeModule` registers inline-module FUNCTIONS under mangled names (`__jet_math__double`) for call-site checking, but struct/enum/type items in `cm.body` are not registered into the type registry that `CheckerItems.rs:1832/1856` and `CheckerCore/type_assign.rs:258` consult. Generic modules DO support member structs (`Bundle/GenericModules.rs` specializes them into ordinary items) — mirror that: register plain-CodeModule member types so they resolve (a) bare inside their own module's bodies, (b) qualified `bank.Account` inside and outside per `pub`, reusing the D-NAME-WALK1 inline-scope maps (Sema/mod.rs:1296-1319) so nothing leaks into sibling scopes.
3. E0113 half: the mismatch at `CheckerCore/statements.rs:1685` renders want/got with different qualification (file-qualified `vis2.bank.Account` vs `bank.Account`) for what is ONE declaration. Fix identity, not wording: `nominal_type_identity` / `same_declared_name_identity` (type_assign.rs:849+) must treat the two spellings of one declared type as identical, which makes the false E0113 disappear. For remaining genuine mismatches, render both sides under one display convention so the fix text can never prescribe the input spelling (I4).
4. Consistency check: generic-module member structs (`module cache<K>(...)`) must behave identically before/after — no regression in `modules/generic_modules`.
5. Shipped-evidence follow-up: `examples/features/web/ui_showcase.jet:16-29` documents this bug PLUS an I2 codegen rejection as the reason for 10 repeated `#Target(JS)` tags. After the sema fix, probe whether `#Target(JS) module browser {}` now works end-to-end; if the I2 codegen half still rejects, log that finding on this card (and let the milestone mint a codegen card) — do not half-migrate the example.
6. Re-bless E0119/E0113 snapshots; `modules/inline_module`, `modules/module_inline_sibling`, `modules/library` goldens stay green.

## Not building
- The `#Target(JS)` I2 codegen rejection (separate defect unless the trace proves one root).
- No visibility-rule redesign (`pub` semantics unchanged), no generic-module changes.

## Proof
- vis3.jet and vis2.jet compile and run byte-identical on `jet run`, `jet run --release`, interpreter (criterion 1: probe compiles, E0113 fix no longer self-contradictory).
- Snapshot suite for E0119/E0113 re-blessed; module example goldens green. Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

none — self-contained sema registration + type-identity fix.

cards.title: core.io watcher events are stringly typed: ev.domain/kind are Strings where enums exist
cards.body: examples/features/io/watcher.jet:31,68-76 matches on ev.domain == { "process" -> ... "port" -> ... } and threads string sentinels (first_kind := "none"). The watcher stdlib API hands back string domain/kind fields instead of enums, forcing stringly-typed consumer code while enum and distinct exist and stdlib-api-laws demand illegal-states-unrepresentable surfaces. Found by the engineering-principles corpus audit (card #2052).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`WatchEvent.domain` and `WatchEvent.kind` become typed payload-free Core enums — `WatchDomain { File, Process, Port }` and `WatchKind { Created, Modified, Removed, Error, Exited, Ready }` — the String fields are gone (greenfield cutover, all in-repo consumers migrated), exhaustive switches over both enums compile without a wildcard, and the watcher example + golden behave identically on AOT and default `jet run`.

## Law
- stdlib-api-laws **D4** — "Options use dedicated enums; Core does not use boolean or bare-string policy flags" + illegal-states-unrepresentable (the card's cited law).
- D-WATCH-SCOPE1 — `core.watcher` owns file/process/port watch handles with `WatchEvent` values.
- Greenfield invariant (no compat shims), I9, I5.
- No ballot — conformance fix to ratified D4; the enums are Core API types under the existing core-enum mechanism (precedent: `ProcessStreamMode`, `TextWidth`, `Key` via `resolve_enum_variants_cloned`).

## Work
1. Inventory producers first: `Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/ReactiveEventWatch.rs` — domains `file`/`process`/`port`; kinds `Created`/`Modified`/`Removed` (fs diff, lines 1956-1963), `Error` (1808), `Exited` (1821, 1830), `Ready` (1846). Grep `WatchEvent {` repo-wide (incl. jet-jit) to confirm the closed set and find every constructor; trace how core.watcher marshals under default `jet run` (JIT host vs Prelude) so the field-type change lands on every tier.
2. Prelude types: `Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs` — add `pub enum WatchDomain` / `pub enum WatchKind` (derive Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq) beside `struct WatchEvent` (line 488); switch the two fields; update `JetShow for WatchEvent` (line 2478) to render variant names (match how an existing core enum shows — trace `ProcessStreamMode`'s rendering and copy the convention). Update all constructors in ReactiveEventWatch.rs; `jet_watch_event` (line 1969) takes `WatchKind`, the `&str` parameter dies.
3. Sema: `CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs` — field table (line 1255) becomes `("WatchEvent", "domain") => Named("WatchDomain")`, `("WatchEvent", "kind") => Named("WatchKind")`; register both enums' variants through `resolve_enum_variants_cloned` (mirror `TextWidth` at ~line 2050 and `core_key_variants` at line 1782) so dot-literals (`.File`, `.Created`) resolve and the exhaustiveness checker sees the closed variant sets; add both names to the core type-name reservation list (line 244 region).
4. Exhaustiveness (criterion 1): verify `switch ev.domain { .File -> … .Process -> … .Port -> … }` (no wildcard) and the six-arm kind switch compile — the core-enum variant table drives the existing checker (Key precedent); fix the table registration if either demands a wildcard.
5. Migrate consumers (criterion 1, greenfield): `examples/features/io/watcher.jet` lines 31, 68-76 — `ev.domain == "process"` string matches become enum switches; the `first_kind := "none"` sentinel becomes `WatchKind?` (Option) or a switch-carried value; grep the whole in-repo .jet corpus + tests for `.domain ==` / `.kind ==` string comparisons and migrate every one. Confirm `ev.domain == "process"` now fails with the ordinary type-mismatch copy (adequate teaching; no new diagnostic).
6. Golden: re-bless `examples/features/expected/io/watcher.out` — the JetShow rendering change is the only expected output delta.
7. Docs: `docs/reference/core-library.md` watcher section field table shows the enum types and variant sets.

cards.title: core.regex runtime: naive Pike VM is quadratic in practice; grep-class engine needed
cards.body: Video-mine evidence (Why Its So Hard To Write A Fast grep, UJ_W0O3sFnY, 2026-08-19): a naive spec-shaped regex engine was 70x slower than grep; swapping to a SIMD-prefiltered engine (vectorscan) cut 170s to 7s on 4GB. Jet probe on today's binary (901bfe9b5): re.find_all(.{"struct"}, text) literal scan — 40KB=0.7s, 400KB=15.4s default jet run (superlinear), 4MB never finished in 300s; GNU grep does the full 4MB in 0.004s (31,476 hits). Causes in Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/Open.rs: find_from re-runs the Pike VM at every byte position; run_at/add_thread allocate Vec + BTreeSet + caps.clone() per position; JetRegexMatch clones the ENTIRE haystack String per match (3,087 matches x 400KB = about 1.2GB copied). The ratified semantics are right (D-REGEXENGINE1 linear time, no backreferences — DFA-able by construction; the std::regex trap is spec-level and Jet avoided it). Only the runtime is slow. Direction: byte-level lazy DFA or NFA simulation without per-position restart, memchr/Teddy-class literal prefilter (jet_compute already proves vetted-unsafe AVX2/SSE2 runtime dispatch is invariant-clean, Compute.rs jet_compute_simd_backend), span-based matches with lazy group extraction, zero allocation on the scan hot path. Engine lives in the Prelude so all tiers share it (I9 structural).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
The core.regex runtime in Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/Open.rs is replaced with a grep-class linear engine: one-pass byte-level Pike-VM/lazy-DFA simulation with no per-position restart, a memchr/Teddy-class literal prefilter with std-only SIMD runtime dispatch, span-based matches with lazy group extraction, and zero allocation on the scan hot path. The card's own 4MB-corpus probe (`re.find_all(.{"struct"}, text)`) completes under default `jet run` within a stated multiple of GNU grep with the same match count, and output is byte-identical across AOT, default JIT, and interpreter.

## Law
- D-REGEXENGINE1=A — core.regex is RE2-class and linear by default (captures, named groups, replace, split, flags, Unicode classes); std-only in the generated prelude; no backtracking/backreferences. The semantics are ratified and unchanged — this card fixes only the runtime.
- I9 structural — the engine lives in the Prelude; every tier marshals to the same `jet_regex_*` entries; byte-identical output.
- I5 — existing regex goldens must stay green; the probe recipe is recorded.
- No new user-typeable syntax → no I7 decision. No new diagnostics expected → I4 untouched unless an error message changes (then re-snapshot).

## Work
1. Trace the hot path in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/Open.rs`: `matches:399` → `find_from:483` → `regex_search_positions:1263` (iterates EVERY char index — the quadratic restart), `run_at:496` (fresh `Vec` + full `caps` vec per position), `add_thread:534` (`caps.clone()` per transition), `JetRegexMatch:149` (`text: String` — clones the whole haystack per match). Parser (`RegexParser:698`) and compiler (`RegexCompiler:987`) largely stay; the simulation and match carrier are the rewrite.
2. Byte-level program: recompile `RegexProgram` matchers to byte-oriented instructions (UTF-8 class lowering to byte ranges/alternations, or char-decode only inside class steps), preserving current match semantics exactly — leftmost start, greedy `last_match` extension as `run_at` implements today; the existing goldens are the semantic oracle.
3. One-pass simulation: replace per-position restart with the standard unanchored Pike VM — inject the start thread at each input byte while no match has begun; dedup threads with two preallocated sparse sets sized by instruction count (no `BTreeSet`, no per-position `Vec` growth); run capture slots ONLY when the program has groups and the caller asks for them.
4. Lazy captures + span matches: `find_all`/`matches`/`is_match` first run the capture-free VM for spans; `JetRegexMatch` stores a shared haystack (`Arc<str>`, one refcount bump per match, never a String clone) plus spans; `group(n)`/named groups re-run the full-capture VM over the matched window on demand. Public API (`group`, `named`, replace expansion `expand_regex_replacement:1281`) is unchanged in shape and output.
5. Literal prefilter: derive a required prefix/inner literal from the compiled program; scan with a std-only memchr-class routine — chunked u64 SWAR baseline plus vetted-unsafe AVX2/SSE2 with runtime feature dispatch, mirroring the invariant-clean precedent in `Top/Compute.rs` `jet_compute_simd_backend:4011`. The prefilter only proposes candidate positions; the VM remains the semantic authority (a prefilter bug can cost speed, never correctness).
6. Wire `matches`, `replace`/`replace_impl`, `split`, `is_match`, `match_value` through the new engine and DELETE the old `regex_search_positions`/per-position `run_at` path (greenfield — no dual engine, no fallback flag).
7. Keep the whole engine in Open.rs (Prelude) so AOT/JIT/interpreter share it structurally; no engine-host code changes should be needed — verify none exist.

## Not building
- No backreferences, lookaround, or PCRE compatibility (excluded by D-REGEXENGINE1).
- No external crates (regex/memchr/aho-corasick) — std-only is law.
- No full lazy-DFA cache if the one-pass NFA + prefilter already meets the stated multiple — simplest engine that clears criterion 4.
- No parallel file scanning — that is #2057 (which depends on this card).

## Proof
- Criterion 4 (the real exit bar; rows 1–3 are blank placeholder rows per the card log — close them with evidence "empty placeholder row — superseded by the appended criterion"):
  - Rebuild, regenerate the 4MB corpus exactly as the card probe did (concatenate repo sources to ~4MB), run `re.find_all(.{"struct"}, text)` under default `jet run`: completes, match count agrees with `grep -c` on the same corpus, wall time recorded on the card as a stated multiple of GNU grep.
  - Scale sanity: 40KB / 400KB / 4MB timings show linear growth (kills the 0.7s→15.4s→never curve).
  - Zero hot-path allocation: sparse sets and caps buffers preallocated at compile of the program; assert by code inspection in review + a debug counter in a unit test if cheap.
  - I9: byte-identical output for `examples/features/text/regex.jet` and the probe across default `jet run`, `jet run --release` (AOT), and the interpreter.
- Existing goldens green: `examples/features/text/regex.jet` vs its expected out; `tests/ui/regex_interpolation` snapshot unchanged.
- Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — semantics ratified, seam isolated to Open.rs, SIMD-dispatch precedent already in-tree.

cards.title: core.files parallel walk + grep-class file-scan flagship
cards.body: Video-mine evidence (UJ_W0O3sFnY): the winning architecture for scanning 200k files / 4GB was NOT io_uring (queue exhaustion, overflow buffers, free lists — complexity swallowed the gains and it was scrapped) but the simplest parallel shape: one shared queue of directories; every thread pops a directory, enumerates it, pushes discovered subdirectories, and processes that directory's files sequentially; plus write batching to cut lock contention and write syscalls. Final: 1.2s for 4GB, within 80ms of ripgrep. Jet today: fs.walk (FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs walk_dir) is single-threaded recursive with per-directory sort; no parallel traversal or high-throughput scan primitive exists. Deliverable: a parallel walk/scan path in core.files honoring the shared-queue architecture, and a grep-style flagship example proving Jet can be the fastest-grep substrate (depends on #2056 for the matcher). Expert notes for later, not this card: sink-aware zero-copy (splice) is what lets cat-class tools win; mmap loses to plain read for sequential scans once page faults are paid.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
core.files gains a parallel walk/scan path implementing the video-proven shared-queue-of-directories architecture (workers pop a directory, enumerate it, push subdirectories, process that directory's files sequentially, with batched result writes), plus a grep-style flagship example whose golden output equals the sequential walk result set, and a measured 200k-file-fixture throughput number recorded on the card.

## Law
No decision dependencies — mechanical/performance work extending the existing `fs.walk` contract; binding constraints are structural: I9 (traversal semantics in Prelude only; engines marshal), I5 (flagship example + golden), greenfield (no duplicate walk semantics — one traversal contract, two schedules).

## Work
1. Trace the baseline: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs` `walk_dir:161-195` — single-threaded recursion, per-directory sort, root-relative shown paths, its depth/symlink/error policy. That contract is the semantic oracle: the parallel path must produce the SAME result set (order normalized by one final sort).
2. Implement `jet_std_fs_walk_parallel` next to `walk_dir` (Prelude, std-only): a `Mutex<VecDeque<PathBuf>>` shared directory queue with an active-worker count + condvar for termination (queue empty AND no worker mid-directory ends the walk); `std::thread::available_parallelism()` workers; each worker pops one directory, reads its entries once, pushes discovered subdirectories, and handles that directory's files sequentially; per-directory result batches append to a locked sink in one lock take (the video's write-batching lesson); one final sort yields deterministic output identical to the sequential contract.
3. Explicitly NOT io_uring and NOT mmap — the card body records both as losing architectures (queue exhaustion/complexity; page-fault cost on sequential scans). Plain `read` + threads is the design.
4. Surface: keep beginner `fs.walk` untouched; expose the parallel path through the same registration/arity tables as the existing fs verbs (as the walk's parallel sibling — same row shape, same error type). AOT, Cranelift hosts, and interpreter ambient all marshal to the one Prelude fn; zero traversal logic in engines (I9).
5. Grep-style flagship: `examples/features/io/grep_scan.jet` + `examples/features/expected/io/grep_scan.out` — builds a small fixture tree under a temp dir, walks it with the parallel path, scans files with core.regex (the #2056 engine) for a pattern, prints a sorted match summary AND an in-example equality check against sequential `fs.walk`'s result set (prints `walks agree: true`), so the golden itself proves criterion 4's set-equality clause.
6. Throughput measurement: script-generated 200k-file fixture in a temp dir (recipe recorded in the card log, fixture not committed); measure parallel vs sequential walk wall time on it and record the numbers on the card via `card update --log` (criterion 4 requires the measurement ON the card).
7. Blank criterion rows 1–3: per the card log, close them with evidence "empty placeholder row — superseded by the appended criterion".

## Not building
- io_uring, mmap, or splice-based zero-copy sinks — the card body defers sink-aware zero-copy explicitly ("expert notes for later, not this card").
- No changes to `fs.glob` or the sequential `fs.walk` semantics (per-directory sort, shown paths, error policy stay).
- No general thread-pool/executor abstraction — one queue, one function; TaskGroup/scheduler planes untouched.
- No matcher work — the regex engine is #2056's scope.

## Proof
- Criterion 4: `jet run examples/features/io/grep_scan.jet` matches its golden (which embeds the parallel-vs-sequential set-equality check) on default `jet run` AND `jet run --release` (AOT); measured 200k-file fixture throughput (parallel vs sequential, wall seconds) logged on the card.
- Regression: `examples/features/io/files_depth.jet` golden unchanged (sequential walk untouched).
- Determinism: two consecutive parallel runs produce byte-identical output (the final sort is the determinism guarantee).
- Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

cards.title: Default jet run: hot numeric list loop runs ~1400x slower than AOT
cards.body: Probe on today's binary (901bfe9b5, 2026-08-19): fn sum_all(xs: [Int]) with loop x, xs { total += x } over a 2,000,000-element list — default jet run: 2815ms/2829ms per call; jet run --release: 2ms per call. Same source, same output (I9 semantics hold; this is a pure performance gap of about 1400x on the beginner-default tier). Compiler-opts video (BOrAVwwCXq8) context: this magnitude is not missing autovectorization (that costs about 8x) — it is the shape of a loop interpreting or crossing a boxed/deopt boundary per element. Also note (probe side-evidence, belongs to the compiler-speed family): rerunning jet run --release on an unchanged single-file probe recompiled for 35-41s each time — no cache reuse observed. Diagnose which tier actually executes this loop (Cranelift native vs TIR-eval deopt), record the cause, and close the gap to a defensible dev-lens multiple. The video's benchmark lesson applies directly: users WILL benchmark default jet run, and today it measures the interpreter, not Jet.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
The tier actually executing the 2M-element `sum_all` loop under default `jet run` is identified and the cause recorded on the card; default `jet run` closes to a stated, defended dev-lens multiple of AOT on the probe, proven by committed bench numbers. Semantics stay identical (they already are — this is pure performance).

## Law
- D-LENS-RUN2 (dev-lens: the default tier is what users measure; direction ratchet).
- I9 (any speedup must not fork semantics into an engine; hot paths still marshal to shared kernels for policy).
- Card log: the original three criterion rows were minted EMPTY — when closing, meet each blank row with evidence "empty placeholder row — superseded by the appended criterion".

## Work
1. Fixture = the card-body probe: `fn sum_all(xs: [Int])` with `loop x, xs { total += x }` over a 2,000,000-element list, timed per call (baseline on 901bfe9b5: 2815ms default vs 2ms release ≈ 1400x). Commit it as a bench (follow `tooling/branch_dispatch_bench` / `tooling/bench` precedent) so the numbers are reproducible.
2. DIAGNOSE BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING (criterion demands the cause on the card): `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/tiers.rs::plan_tiers` builds a `TierRow` per function with a named deopt reason and `whole_interp`; `api_debug.rs` + `trace.rs::note_jit_execution` are the observation surface. Extract the plan for the probe. Falsify in order:
   a. `sum_all` (or the entry) is deopted/whole_interp — the reason string names why (memo, canonical_deopt, resident-safety refusal in safety.rs);
   b. native, but the loop crosses a host boundary per element (list index/get shim + `emit_trap_check` per iteration);
   c. native, but Int arithmetic routes through boxed/checked `jet_std` helpers per element.
   The magnitude (~1.4µs/element) most resembles (a) interpreter execution — but record what the plan SAYS, not the smell.
3. Record the identified tier + cause on the card (log entry) before fixing.
4. Fix the named cause at its seam: (a) → lower the refused construct so the loop function goes native (fix the lowering gap, never park it — gaps may only shrink); (b) → lower `loop x, xs` over `[Int]` to direct bounds-checked memory access in Cranelift instead of per-element host calls; (c) → keep overflow SEMANTICS identical but inline the fast path. Policy (overflow behavior, bounds message) stays sourced from the shared kernel.
5. State and defend the target multiple in card evidence: pick the dev-lens defensible bound for a hot native-lowered numeric loop and defend it with before/after numbers on the same machine (default vs release, multiple runs). 1400x is indefensible; the number you commit to must name what remains (e.g. trap checks, no autovectorization ≈ single-digit x).
6. Side-evidence from the body (35-41s `--release` recompile of an unchanged file, no cache reuse) belongs to the compiler-speed family: add a log pointer to the warm-AOT cards (c09otnjg content-addressed rlibs) — do NOT fix here.
7. I9 guard: probe output (the sums printed) stays byte-identical across default run/JIT/AOT before and after.

## Not building
- Autovectorization or a general JIT optimizer.
- AOT compile-speed/cache-reuse work (c09otnjg family owns it).
- No new bench framework — reuse the existing bench example/harness shape.

## Proof
- Criterion 4: card log carries the identified tier + cause; committed bench numbers show default `jet run` within the stated, defended multiple of AOT on `sum_all`; probe output identical across tiers.
- Blank criterion rows 1-3 met with the superseded-placeholder evidence line per the card log. Focused checks only; full suite at epoch closeout.

cards.title: Self-hosted optimizer design: SSA backend fed by sema facts
cards.body: Owner directive (2026-08-19 video-mine run): the self-hosted compiler must eventually beat the underlying Rust compiler on generated-code quality, not only on build latency. Compiler-opts video (BOrAVwwCXq8) supplies the catalog and the leverage: SSA + explicit CFG make every classic pass a lookup instead of an analysis; aliasing is the most common vectorization blocker; purity is the universal optimization currency. Jet's categorical edge: sema already PROVES facts rustc must re-infer from scratch — D-MEM1 exclusivity (& is exclusive-for-the-call: noalias by construction), the one effect model (purity per function), value semantics + deep freeze (D-CONC-FREEZE1: immutability facts), typed bounds. Today those proofs are discarded at emit and LLVM re-derives approximations. The self-hosted optimizing backend must consume them directly. docs/plans/compiler-speed.md bets 1-6 cover build speed and monomorphization; no card owns optimizer design. This card is the design doc, not the implementation.
cards.plan:
Design-doc card: the exit artifact is a committed design (docs/plans/ or docs/adr/), not code. Lives in the DEFERRED self-hosting milestone; the doc can be written any time, implementation cards wait for the owner to reopen the chain.

Doc contents, mapping to criteria 5-6:
1. IR shape: SSA with explicit CFG for the self-hosted backend; where it sits relative to the frozen TIR contract.
2. The sema-fact seam: which proven facts flow in and how — D-MEM1 exclusivity (& is exclusive-for-the-call: noalias by construction), effect purity per function, value semantics + deep freeze (D-CONC-FREEZE1 immutability), typed bounds, contracts, view/ownership facts (types-as-facts per the scriptc mine).
3. Pass catalog table: each classic SSA pass mapped to the sema fact that turns it from analysis into lookup (aliasing -> exclusivity, vectorization legality -> noalias + purity, const-prop/licm -> purity + freeze, bounds-check elision -> typed bounds).
4. Layout freedom section: default Jet layout is guarantee=physical-layout-unspecified, so field reorder and AoS-to-SoA of default-layout aggregates are legal transforms; #Layout(columnar) (D-SOA1) stays the only user-facing spelling.
5. Amendment path: sema-fact channels enter the frozen TIR contract via an #668 amendment — no third lens, no parallel IR. State the exact amendment.
6. Rejected alternatives with reasons (at minimum: annotate-LLVM-harder, a separate optimizer IR, doing nothing and trusting rustc).
7. Autovectorization boundary vs D-SIMD3: the ratified default auto-vec (#2261) lives in today's AOT path; state how the self-hosted backend inherits, not duplicates, that mechanism (I8).

Close: mint implementation cards per doc section and link them here; meet blank rows 1-4 with evidence 'empty placeholder row — superseded by the appended criterion' per the 2026-08-19 repair note.
Owned paths: the design doc only. Non-goal: any compiler code.

log.text: Prep: plan written. Exit is a committed design doc plus minted implementation cards (criteria 5-6); blank rows 1-4 close per the 2026-08-19 repair note. Card sits in the DEFERRED self-hosting milestone; ready for whenever the owner resumes.

video-mine follow-up (scriptc mine, 2026-08-21): two optimizer liberties worth designing in. (1) Types-as-facts: scriptc's whole memory win came from lowering typed source to real structs — Jet's sema facts are richer (effects, contracts, view/ownership) and the optimizer should consume them, not just types. (2) Semantic layout freedom: probed today, default Jet layout reports guarantee=physical-layout-unspecified — so field reorder and even AoS-to-SoA transforms of default-layout aggregates are already legal (audience C121 on the scriptc video spelled out why source without address guarantees permits SoA; Jet's no-address-observability default is stronger than JS's). Explicit #Layout(columnar) (D-SOA1) stays the user-facing spelling; this is about optimizer rights on unannotated types. Also worth a lane here: perf ADVISORIES from the same sema facts (allocation-in-loop, implicit copy in hot path) — the HW-crisis video's 'AI writes correct-not-best' problem wants the oracle to propose the optimization, not wait to be asked.

video-mine evidence (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kr9ai5zxAcY audience): baseline user expectation that 'most langs don't roll your code into sse2+ features' — autovectorization of ordinary code is table stakes for the performance-first positioning. #1143 covers explicit core.compute SIMD; this card's sema-fact-fed optimizer is where ordinary-code vectorization would land.
