cards.title: jet bench: keep() sink and optimizer-trap guards
cards.body: Both perf videos (UJ_W0O3sFnY, BOrAVwwCXq8) end on the same trap: a benchmark that measures the optimizer, not the work — the famous nested-loop language benchmark actually measured integer division; the grep video's first mmap benchmark lied by 2000x because the file was never faulted in. jet bench today has no black-box/keep sink (grep over jet-cli and Prelude: no matches), so an optimizing tier may elide the measured loop entirely and a lazy resource may defer its cost outside the timed region. Small, bounded surface: a keep(x) sink the optimizer must treat as used, plus bench docs teaching the trap catalog.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`keep(x)` exists as a Prelude sink the optimizer must treat as used, available in every execution tier (I9), so a measured loop whose values would otherwise be dead cannot be elided and a lazy resource can be forced inside the timed region; the bench docs carry the optimizer-trap catalog from both perf videos. A demo bench proves nonzero work with keep() versus an elided baseline. The three empty criterion rows are met with "empty placeholder row — superseded by the appended criterion" per the card log.

## Law
- D-BENCH1 / D-BENCH-MARKER1=A — `#Bench("name") { … }` regions, `jet bench` harness (spec.md:1193-1206).
- D-BENCH-PARITY1=B — shared targets/filters; benches run serially.
- D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A (2026-08-07, card #1641) — `#Bench`/`jet bench` RETIRE in favor of `.measure` + `jet test --measure`. Retirement is ratified but NOT yet shipped (no `--measure` in Source/; run_bench live at Source/CmdDevTools.rs:2930-3360). Consequence: keep() MUST be harness-neutral — a Prelude function usable in any measured body — never a `jet bench`-only feature; docs note the migration so the trap catalog moves with `.measure`.
- I7 — keep(x) is NEW user-typeable surface with no ratified decision ID. A decision (suggest D-BENCH-KEEP1: name, signature keep(x: T) => T vs Unit-returning, tier semantics) must be ratified before the user-typeable name ships. This is the card's one clearance item.
- I9 — sink semantics live in Prelude source shared by AOT, Cranelift host, interpreter ambient, comptime; engines only marshal.
- I5 — executable example + golden. Core-surface ledger gate (card #1442, scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs) must absorb the new name.

## Work
1. Trace first: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:5339-5355 — the generated bench harness ALREADY wraps each region body call in `std::hint::black_box` (spec.md:1202 documents it). Refine the card's video-mine claim: the harness sinks the body's RESULT; the real gap is (a) values computed and dropped INSIDE the loop body (a Unit-returning body gives black_box nothing), and (b) lazy costs (mmap-style fault-in) deferred past the timed region. State this precisely in the card log before building.
2. Ratify surface (blocking): raise the D-BENCH-KEEP1 ballot (name `keep`, generic identity signature so `total = keep(total)` composes, "optimizer must treat the value as used" contract, tier-neutral no-op semantics everywhere except AOT optimization pressure). Do not emit user-typeable surface before ratification (I7).
3. Implement in Prelude: one `jet_keep` kernel in a PRELUDE_PARTS file (Prelude/Observe.rs or Prelude/Core/RuntimeControl.rs — pick the existing home whose neighbors are runtime-control intrinsics) using `std::hint::black_box` for AOT. Register the Jet-visible name in sema's core call tables (trace via tests/core_call_table.rs and the registries it pins); wire interpreter ambient + Cranelift host + comptime to the same symbol (identity behavior — parity means the program RUNS identically in every tier, jet run / --interpret / --release).
4. Docs: optimizer-trap catalog in the bench section of docs/spec/spec.md (:1193-1206) and docs/reference/core-library.md (:2675-2716): dead-loop elision (nested-loop benchmark that actually measured integer division — UJ_W0O3sFnY), lazy-resource deferral (grep video's 2000x mmap lie — BOrAVwwCXq8), constant folding of loop-invariant work, and when the harness's own result-sink is NOT enough. Note the D-CLAIM-BENCH1 migration so the catalog is written against "measured regions", not the retiring spelling.
5. Example + proof fixture (I5): extend examples/features/tooling/bench.jet (or sibling) with a keep()-guarded region; golden expected output for the `jet run` main path; a harness test in tests/jet_bench.rs asserting the demo bench with keep() reports nonzero ns/iter while the keep-less twin loop is measurably elided (assert ordering/magnitude, never absolute timings).
6. Ledger + gates: update the core-surface ledger for the new name; diagnostics: none expected (keep has no failure mode — if sema rejects misuse, reuse existing arity/type diagnostics; no new code → no I4 row).

## Not building
- No allocator work (#2061 sibling).
- No `.measure`/`jet test --measure` implementation and no `#Bench` retirement — that is card #1641's ratified scope; keep() must merely survive it.
- No timing-assertion tests (absolute wall-clock asserts are banned flake sources); no new bench CLI flags; no changes to sample counts or bench scheduling (#2075/audit rank 9 territory).

## Proof
- Criterion 4 (the real one): `jet bench` on the demo file shows the keep()-fed region measuring nonzero work vs the elided baseline (paste both result lines into the card log); `cargo test --test jet_bench` focused run green; docs sections present; tier parity probe: the keep()-using example prints identical output under `jet run`, `jet run --interpret`, `jet run --release` (default + release AOT parity per I9).
- Criteria 1-3 (empty rows): meet with evidence "empty placeholder row — superseded by the appended criterion" per the 2026-08-19 card log.
- Ledger/table gates: `cargo test --test core_call_table --test core_surface_ledger` (targeted) green.

## blockedBy
D-BENCH-KEEP1 (new ballot to raise — I7 gates the user-typeable name; steps 1, 2 and the docs catalog can proceed immediately, code that exposes `keep` waits for ratification).

log.text: Raised D-BENCH-KEEP1 (ballot-ready, full profile): A always-available Prelude keep(x) sink [rec] vs B docs-only result-threading vs C region-scoped sink with a new diagnostic. Blocker added because criterion 4 needs the shipped name (I7); the bench docs and optimizer-trap catalog (plan step 4) can start now — only code exposing keep waits for ratification.

Plan grounding: two corrections to the card body. (1) The bench harness ALREADY black_boxes each region body's RESULT (Codegen/mod.rs:5340-5352, spec.md:1202); the true gap is values dropped inside the loop (Unit bodies) and lazy-cost deferral — keep(x) closes those. (2) D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A retires #Bench/jet bench for .measure/jet test --measure (not yet shipped) — keep() therefore lands harness-neutral in the Prelude. Clearance: keep is new user-typeable surface with no decision ID → I7 requires a ratified D-BENCH-KEEP1 before the name ships; ballot flagged to Main.

cards.title: Measure global-allocator impact on Jet AOT workloads
cards.body: Video-mine evidence (UJ_W0O3sFnY): dropping in mimalloc for musl malloc removed 2 seconds from a ~5s run with zero code change; top comment (326 likes) mocks glibc malloc speed. Jet AOT binaries default to the system allocator through JetProgramAllocator (#1853 shipped the swap point; #1926 proved the expert story). Unknown: what a mimalloc-class allocator is worth on Jet's own workloads (glibc is better than musl; the video number does not transfer). Measure before proposing anything. A default change would add an external dependency to generated programs — owner gate under the Core dependency rules; this card ships no default change.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A committed measurement table (docs/research/) comparing the system allocator against a mimalloc-class allocator on named Jet AOT workloads, on one recorded machine, with medians and deltas — answering what the video's musl→mimalloc 2s/5s win is actually worth on Jet's glibc-default binaries. No product change ships; if the numbers justify anything, the output is a drafted owner ballot (Core dependency rules gate any default), not code.

## Law
- D-ALLOC-PROGRAM1=A — `allocator:` manifest key selects the hosted whole-program allocator (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Manifest.rs:245-247; `mem.Heap`, `mem.Counting.over(...)`). Closed policy table: a third-party allocator is NOT selectable today — that is exactly why this card measures before proposing.
- Shipped facts: #1853 — JetProgramAllocator swap point (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/ProgramAllocator.rs; emission `#[global_allocator] static __JET_PROGRAM_ALLOCATOR` at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:1462-1466); #1926 — expert story proven (tests/allocator_families.rs, incl. the interpreter/aot lens matrix at :824-830).
- Owner gate: a default change adds an external dependency to every generated program — owner ballot territory; this card ships no default change (criterion text).

## Work
1. cards.title: Project-mode jet test discovers #Test in the entry file only
cards.body: Live probe 2026-08-19: in a jet new project, #Test blocks in a sibling file (math.jet) are invisible to bare 'jet test' -> E0601 'no #Test blocks found', exit 1; naming the file ('jet test math.jet') runs them fine. A fresh 'jet new' project therefore FAILS jet test out of the box. Spec S43 says jet test auto-collects every #Test in the package - this is the Zig trap the spec forbids. Also: parse-broken sibling files are silently skipped. Evidence: target-fpa/L1-live-surface.md section 2.3; devloop-testing proposal row 7 (Source/lib.rs entry-module scan).
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Bare `jet test` inside a `jet new` project discovers and runs every `#Test` block in the package (spec S43), not just the entry file: a fresh project with tests in a sibling file passes out of the box, parse-broken package files surface their errors instead of being silently skipped, `jet test <file>` behavior is unchanged, and E0601 fires only when the whole package truly has zero `#Test` blocks.

## Law
- Spec S43 (docs/spec/spec.md:1134-1149) — `jet test` compiles and runs `#Test` blocks; a directory target builds one harness per file. The card's live probe shows bare project mode violating the auto-collect promise (the Zig trap).
- D-TESTKIT1=A gap #2 — the shared recursive target walk (Source/CmdCompile.rs:1781-1809) skipping build/, dotdirs, and reserved files.
- D-CLI-BARE1=A — bare project verbs resolve their entry via one shared rule (main.rs `resolve_bare_entry`, 3019).
- D-TEST4 — doctest-only files stay testable without `#Test` blocks (CmdCompile.rs:1838-1843).
- I4 — E0601 wording changes (if any) go through the registered diagnostic + UI snapshot. (The E0601 fix-text modernization itself is sibling card #2067's scope.)

## Work
1. Trace the bug path: bare dispatch main.rs:2314-2332 → `resolve_bare_entry("test", cwd, …)` (3019) returns the single project ENTRY FILE → `run_test_opts` (CmdCompile.rs:1747) runs only that file's module bundle → sema emits E0601 (jet-sema Bundle/Pipeline.rs:2691) when the entry has no `#Test`, even though siblings do.
2. Enumerate the package: in bare project mode (a package root was found), collect the package's member files instead of the lone entry. Prefer the project-parts automatic discovery seam (`jet::ProjectParts::scan(&root)`, main.rs:747-750) so "the package" means exactly what `jet project parts` prints; fall back to `collect_source_files_recursive` on the package root only if ProjectParts cannot yield file paths — and record which route shipped in the card log. Explicit `jet test <file>` / `jet test <dir>` arguments keep today's code path untouched.
3. Aggregate the run: reuse the existing per-file harness loop (run_test_opts's dir branch, 1753-1772) over the package set with one change — per-file "no `#Test` blocks" is no longer an error. Per file: has `#Test` → run harness; doctests only → run doctests (existing 1838-1843 logic); neither → skip silently but count. Track total discovered tests across the package.
4. E0601 once, package-truthful: if the whole package (all members) discovered zero `#Test` blocks AND no doctests ran, emit E0601 exactly once with the package framing. The sema-side E0601 (Pipeline.rs:2691) stays for single-file invocations; suppress the harness path that would fire it per-file in package mode (the CmdCompile pre-check at 1841 already shows the pattern).
5. Parse-broken members are NOT skipped: a member that fails to load/parse reports its real compile error and fails the run (the `has_test_blocks` Err→true convention at Source/lib.rs:1840 already encodes "surface the real error"); verify ProjectParts discovery doesn't drop them before the runner sees them — if it does, walk must include them so the error surfaces.
6. Exit codes: any failing test or broken member → exit 1; all pass → 0; zero tests package-wide → E0601 + exit 1 (unchanged code meaning).
7. Update the shipped docs/spec wording only where it describes bare `jet test` scope (grep docs/ for the bare-test description); S43 itself already promises this behavior — no spec change, this is a bug fix to match ratified law.

## Not building
- E0601 fix-text spelling modernization (require→assert, `#Test("name")` heading) — owned by sibling card #2067.
- `jet bench` discovery parity — bench retires under D-CLAIM-BENCH1 (#2067's scope).
- Cross-package/workspace-wide test collection; `--filter`/`--shuffle`/coverage changes (they ride per-file harnesses unchanged).
- Changing what `jet test <dir>` does for arbitrary non-package directories (ratified per spec.md:1143).

## Proof
- Criterion 1 (two-file fixture): integration test — `jet new proj`; add `math.jet` with a passing `#Test`; entry keeps no tests; bare `jet test` from the project root runs the sibling's test, prints its pass line, exits 0. Second fixture variant: tests in BOTH entry and sibling → both run.
- Criterion 2: `jet test math.jet` output is byte-identical to today (single-file path untouched); a project whose files have zero `#Test` blocks and zero doctests → exactly one E0601, exit 1; a doctest-only project → doctests run, no E0601.
- Broken-sibling probe: package with a parse-broken member → its compile error prints, exit 1 (no silent skip).
- Live probe transcript on a fresh binary in a temp project (`jet new` → sibling test → bare `jet test`) attached as evidence; runtime behavior is CLI-tier only (harness selection), so no AOT/interpreter parity probe beyond the fixture running under default `jet test`. Full suite at epoch closeout.

## blockedBy
none — pure tooling bug fix against ratified S43; all seams (bare entry resolution, ProjectParts scan, per-file harness walk) ship today.

cards.body: L3 decision sweep 2026-08-19: the D-RUN/D-CLAIM remainder has NO open card. Probed: 'jet test --measure' and '--record=' are E2102 unknown flags (D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A, D-RUN-RECORD1=A ratified); 'jet bench' still ships and runs (BENCH1 retires it; live probe: it also prints program stdout 20x and benches every top-level .jet file); live E0601 fix text still teaches require/require_eq (deleted by D-CLAIM-WORD1=B) and a '#Test "name" {}' spelling that E0930 rejects; Syntax.rs math_layout.rs:641-645 still registers both assertion families; D-RUN-SESSION1 keys registered in Syntax.rs with no CLI wiring; bare 'jet dev' fails E2104 while D-CLI-BARE1=A ratifies dev as bare-capable. One card should own this migration end to end. Evidence: target-fpa/L3-decisions.md tables a/c; target-fpa/L1-live-surface.md.

## Outcome
The ratified D-RUN/D-CLAIM remainder ships end to end: `jet test --measure` is the measurement mode and `#Bench`/`jet bench` retire (D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A); `--record=NAME` works on `run`/`dev`/`test` and `jet debug --replay=NAME` consumes it (D-RUN-RECORD1=A); `require`/`require_eq` are deleted with `assert`/`assert_eq` the one family (D-CLAIM-WORD1=B); the E0601 fix text names live spellings; the `r/R/t/f/q` keys drive the resident `jet dev` session (D-RUN-SESSION1=A); and bare `jet dev` works in a package (D-CLI-BARE1=A). cards.title: jet eval: no expression form, print output swallowed
cards.body: Live probe 2026-08-19: help says 'Evaluate pure Jet and print JSON'. 'jet eval "1 + 2"' -> E2105 couldn't read '1 + 2': No such file or directory (file-only). 'jet eval expr.jet' where run() prints -> prints only '()' - print output swallowed, no JSON of the printed value. Evidence: target-fpa/L1-live-surface.md main table rows eval.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
One canonical `jet eval` behavior, honoring the help contract ("Evaluate pure Jet and print JSON"): `jet eval "1 + 2"` evaluates the expression and prints its value (JSON with `--json`, pretty by default per D-EVAL1=A); `jet eval file.jet` no longer swallows `print` output — captured program output is forwarded, and the run's result value still renders. Probes from the card body pass; CLI snapshots updated.

## Law
- S60 / D-PURE1 (E2-M16 pure evaluation; roadmap.md:150).
- D-EVAL1=A (pretty output by default, `--json` for stable machine JSON — recorded at Source/CmdDevTools.rs:2681 and honored, not reopened).
- No new decision needed: this is contract-honoring bug-fix work on a CLI argument (not user-typeable language syntax, so I7 does not bite). The registry summary already promises evaluation+JSON; the card ruling picks expression-form support as the canonical behavior.

## Work
1. Trace first: Source/main.rs:2277-2290 ("eval" arm — file-only, E2104 when absent); Source/CmdDevTools.rs:2686-2827 (`run_eval` — lex/parse, optional `--pure` walk, `check_for_eval`, then `jet::eval_pure_program_value`); Source/lib.rs:1949-1991 (`eval_pure_program_value{,_inner}` — NOTE the bug: the `Comptime::DevSink` capturing print output is a local and is dropped, `sink.stdout` never reaches the caller); crates/jet-repl/src/lib.rs `classify`/`type_check_stmts` (the existing expression-checking wrapper the REPL uses).
2. Print-output fix (file form): change `eval_pure_program_value` to return the captured output too — `Result<(CtValue, String), Vec<Diagnostic>>` (greenfield: change the signature, migrate the one production caller `run_eval`; do not add a parallel `_with_output` variant). In `run_eval`: human mode — write captured stdout verbatim, then the value via `render_pretty()`; `--json` mode — forward captured print output to STDERR (stdout stays exactly one JSON document, keeping machine output stable) and print `value.to_json()` on stdout. Document this split in the flag row help (`--json` row) if wording allows one line.
3. Expression form: in the main.rs "eval" arm, disambiguate the positional: (a) `resolve_source_path(arg)` names an existing file → file form (unchanged); (b) arg ends in `.jet` but no such file → keep today's file-not-found path (never guess an expression out of a typo'd filename); (c) otherwise → expression form. Implement expression evaluation by wrapping the text into the same checked-fn shape the REPL's `classify` path uses (a synthetic `run`-style fn whose body returns the expression), running the SAME pipeline `run_eval` uses (sema check with `CompileMode::Eval` via `Driver::check_eval`, then comptime evaluation to a `CtValue`) — semantics stay in the shared comptime tree-walker (I9: no second evaluator; the CLI only marshals). Expose it as a small `run_eval_expr(expr, pure_required, mode)` beside `run_eval` in CmdDevTools that shares the render tail (pretty/JSON) with the file form. `--pure` applies to the expression form identically (the wrapper fn gets the pure arrow, so E3401 fires on impure calls).
4. Diagnostics: expression parse/type errors render through the standard renderer with a synthetic label (e.g. `<eval>`), the same way REPL synthetic sources do — no bespoke error text; the old E2105 "couldn't read '1 + 2'" path must be unreachable for non-`.jet` arguments.
5. Help/usage: fill the eval row's positional usage via the `CommandSpec.usage` field owned by #2072 (`eval <file.jet | expression>`); if #2072 hasn't landed the field yet, add it exactly as specified there (first lander adds the shared seam). Keep the summary row as-is.
6. Tests + snapshots (tests/cli_parts/, fixtures in tests/cli/): new CLI tests — `jet eval "1 + 2" --json` → `3` (exit 0); `jet eval "1 + 2"` pretty; file-with-print probe: `fn run() { print("hi") }` → human output contains `hi` then `()`; `--json` variant → stdout is exactly the JSON value, `hi` on stderr; `.jet`-suffixed missing file still errors as file-not-found; `--pure` with an impure expression → E3401. Re-bless any perturbed fixtures (usage/man/completions goldens if the usage row changes: tests/cli/man.txt, completions_*.txt).

## Not building
- No changes to `eval_pure_program` (Source/lib.rs:1999 — public API kept per ponytail-audit withdrawal note; it is not the production `jet eval` path).
- No stdin form (`jet eval -`), no multi-expression/REPL semantics, no effect-authorization prompts — eval stays pure/comptime-only.
- No new language syntax, no changes to E3401/E340x wording (I4 rows untouched).
- The `CommandSpec.usage` registry field design belongs to #2072; this card only fills the eval row.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: transcript of all card-body probes against the fresh binary: `jet eval "1 + 2"` → value (no E2105); `jet eval expr.jet` with printing `run()` → print output visible + result rendered; `--json` forms stable. One canonical behavior documented in the help row.
- Criterion 2: `cargo test --test cli <new eval test names>` green; snapshot diffs blessed and committed.
- I9/tier note: `jet eval` is comptime-interpreter-only by design (S60/D-PURE1 — deterministic pure evaluation; named carve-out, no AOT tier exists for this verb), so the runnable proof is the default-binary probe set above; no `--release` parity probe applies.

## blockedBy
none — soft coordination only: shares the `CommandSpec.usage` seam with #2072 (first lander adds the field as specified there).

log.text: Closed: expression form, file form, and --json each honor one documented contract, and the shell/man artifacts match the registry.

criteria.text: jet eval accepts an expression argument and prints its JSON value (help contract honored); jet eval file.jet emits the program result as JSON without swallowing print output, or the help text is corrected to the real contract — one canonical behavior, documented.
criteria.evidence: PROOF one canonical behavior, documented: `jet eval '1 + 2'` prints 3; `jet eval lib.jet` prints the program's own output (42) and then the value; `jet eval --json lib.jet` prints 42 on stderr and exactly one JSON document (null) on stdout. Print output is no longer swallowed. The registry summary claimed JSON unconditionally, so it now reads `Evaluate pure Jet and print the value (--json for JSON)`, which is D-EVAL1=A's real contract.

criteria.text: Probes from the card body pass; CLI snapshot updated.
criteria.evidence: PROOF cargo test --test cli 36/36 ok (includes eval_accepts_an_expression_argument) and --test cli_positionals 13/13 ok. tests/cli/completions_{bash,zsh,fish,powershell}.txt and tests/cli/man.txt were regenerated from the shipped registry with `jet self completions` and `jet self man`, which also picked up the two lint flags they had been missing.

cards.title: jet help <command> prints the full global screen; no per-command help exists
cards.body: Live probe 2026-08-19: 'jet help run' prints the entire ~200-line global usage screen; bare 'jet fix', 'jet lint', 'jet fuzz' also dump the global screen instead of targeted usage (exit 2). Card #467 (D-CLI-GLOBAL1) covers user-program #CLI structs, not the jet binary's own help. Evidence: target-fpa/L1-live-surface.md main table rows help/fix/lint/fuzz.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
`jet help <command>` prints the same per-command help `jet <command> --help` already renders (summary, usage, flags — registry-driven, never the ~200-line global screen), and bare target-requiring verbs (`jet fix`, `jet lint`, `jet fuzz`) print targeted usage to stderr with exit 2 instead of dumping the global screen. CLI snapshots cover `jet help run` and one bare-verb case. Scope boundary with #1858 stated and held: #1858 owns the USER-PROGRAM #CLI system (D-CLI-GLOBAL1=E: CLISchema.rs, Args.rs, examples/features/cli); this card touches ONLY the jet binary's own help (crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs registry + Source/main.rs dispatch). #1858 does not build jet-binary per-command help, so this card is wiring + snapshots, not mere verification.

## Law
- #1659 criterion 2 (already shipped): per-command help exists as `command_help` (Source/main.rs:459-498) rendered from the live `jet::CLI` registry — this card reuses it; no hand-authored help strings (the same one-source rule the man page and completions follow).
- D-CLI-SURFACE1=B / D-CLI-SURFACE2=A (grouped spelling; `command_group_usage`/`moved_command` branches in `command_help` already honor them — keep).
- D-CLI-GLOBAL1=E is #1858's law (user-program #CLI structs), explicitly NOT implemented here.
- No new decision needed — mechanical bug-fix on the jet binary's help dispatch.

## Work
1. Trace first: Source/main.rs:1570-1577 ("help" arm — only `structural_help` for diff/merge, else full `usage()`); Source/main.rs:1460-1483 (`--help` path through `command_help` incl. BESPOKE_DEEP_HELP); Source/main.rs:2410-2413 (the `_ =>` arm where bare `fix`/`lint`/`fuzz` — any target-requiring verb — dump the global screen at exit 2); crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1045-1058 (`command_usage` — flat commands render a weak `jet <name> [args]`), :1091 (`usage_page`), :1062 (`flags_for_command`).
2. `jet help <cmd>` (Source/main.rs "help" arm): keep `structural_help` precedence, then for a known command/group/moved word print `command_help(raw[1])` and exit 0 — the SAME renderer as `--help`, so both spellings stay byte-identical forever. Unknown names keep `command_help`'s existing teaching fallback line ("Run `jet help` to see every command."), exit 0. Bare `jet help` keeps the full `usage()` screen (unchanged).
3. Bare target-requiring verbs (Source/main.rs:2410-2413): replace `eprint!("{}", usage())` with `eprint!("{}", command_help(cmd))` keeping `exit(ExitCodes::USAGE)` — this single change point covers bare `fix`, `lint`, `fuzz`, and every other verb that reaches the no-target arm; stderr + exit 2 per criterion 1.
4. Registry usage quality (shared seam this card OWNS): add `usage: Option<&'static str>` to `CommandSpec` (crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs); `command_usage` renders `{BINARY_NAME} {name} {usage}` when set, falling back to today's `[args]`. Populate at least: run, build, test, check, repl (`repl [<file>.jet]` — #2038 consumes), eval (`eval <file.jet | expression>` — #2068 consumes), fix (`fix <file.jet|dir> [--dry-run] [--edition=…]`), lint (`lint --a11y <file.jet>`), fuzz (`fuzz <file.jet> [<test>] [--iterations=N]`), help (`help [<command>]`). This feeds `command_help`, `usage_page`, and the man page from one source — no second convention. Contract for siblings: #2038/#2068 fill their rows; if this card lands second, it adopts their already-added field unchanged.
5. Snapshots + tests (tests/cli_parts/, fixtures tests/cli/): new goldens `help_run.txt` (`jet help run` stdout, exit 0 — asserts summary + usage + flag rows, NOT the global screen) and `fix_bare_usage.txt` (bare `jet fix` stderr, exit 2). Add an equality assertion `jet help run` stdout == `jet run --help` stdout (pins the one-renderer rule). Re-bless perturbed existing goldens (tests/cli/man.txt, completions_*.txt, any usage_page golden) — expected: usage rows gain real argument shapes.
6. Coordination log: after landing, add a one-line log to this card naming the boundary held (#1858 = user-program #CLI; this card = jet-binary help) so #1858's closeout doesn't re-open it.

## Not building
- Nothing in CLISchema.rs/Args.rs/examples/features/cli — user-program #CLI help, shared flags, #CLI(Standard) are #1858's (building, assigned).

cards.title: Suite speed: content-addressed Prelude/Core rlib artifacts for AOT
cards.body: Top-ranked fix from the 2026-08-08 test-suite performance audit. Every generated program recompiles >=331,699 B of identical PRELUDE_PARTS (plus ~445 KB base, up to ~1.54 MB with Core) through raw rustc with no reusable runtime object; golden = ~476 native AOT compiles (45-90 min), corelib ~153. Fix: compile the canonical Prelude/Core runtime once into content-addressed production rlib artifacts keyed by (compiler version, toolchain, target, profile); link each thin generated program against them. Preserves the full Jet->rustc->link->execute proof I5 requires. Exit criteria: golden wall time drops by the audited order; generated program OUTPUT stays byte-identical (D-DEVMODE1); rlib artifacts live in the existing cache/store, not a new store; user-facing jet build/run --release cold time also drops. This is also the substrate the D-DEVR-TWICE1 ballot's warm path links against - but it needs no ballot: internal build architecture, no surface change.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Native AOT builds stop recompiling the Core runtime closure per program: the content-addressed runtime rlib substrate (#1785, Source/RuntimeCache.rs, live since 2026-08-08) is extended from the PRELUDE_PARTS block to the Core/CoreLib closure, so golden (~476 AOT compiles) and corelib (~153) link thin user crates against cached rlibs instead of re-feeding rustc up to ~1.99 MB of identical runtime source. Golden wall time drops by the audited order with byte-identical program output, and the drop plus the cold `jet build`/`jet run --release` delta are recorded in the card log.

## Law
- D-DEVMODE1 — generated program OUTPUT stays byte-identical; zero re-blessed goldens (criterion 3).
- D-LENS-RUN1 — serde/encoding goldens prove via `jet run --release`; that path must keep using the same cache (tests/golden.rs:129 exports JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR to child `jet` processes).
- I5/I2 — every example still passes Jet → rustc → link → execute; rustc rejecting split output is fail-open to the inline monolith, never a weaker proof.
- I9 — Prelude/CoreLib sources stay the single semantic home; this card moves COMPILE units only, no semantics into any engine.
- Prior substrate: card #1785 ("canonical cached runtime rlib", commit c9ca0f43c + d85103fd7 fail-open fix). No ballot needed — mechanical/perf work, no user-typeable surface.

## Work
1. Trace first: Source/RuntimeCache.rs (whole module — split/key/lock/publish/export machinery, schema `jet-runtime-rlib-v3`); crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:221-345 (CACHED_RUNTIME_BEGIN/END + push_cached_runtime = traits + PRELUDE_PARTS + EnvInit + Mem + GC + Layout), :4266-4272 (emit order: allocator → cached runtime → push_corelib_prelude → scheduler → UI — Core is OUTSIDE the markers today; that is the gap), :1751-2621 (strip_unused_{gc,term,txn,mem,os_signal,raylib}_prelude run over the assembled program and prune INSIDE the marker block → bounded key variants); Source/CmdCompile.rs:4429-4530 (production AOT seam: RuntimeCache::prepare + prepared_runtime.add_rustc_args; FFI programs inline by design, :4444-4452); tests/common/mod.rs:265-320 (add_generated_rust — golden/corelib/dev all flow through it); tests/golden.rs:44-52,106-135 (per-suite cold cache dir).
2. Baseline (BEFORE legs of criteria 2+4, on the builder worktree, timeout-wrapped): (a) full golden wall via `JET_TEST_JOBS=16 cargo test --test golden` and/or `scripts/agent/time-suites.sh`; (b) runtime-cache census: entry count under JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR after the run (distinct keys = prune-variant × flag spread); (c) cold-user timing: `hyperfine` on `jet build`/`jet run --release` of one no-Core and one Core-heavy example with fresh JET_CACHE_DIR + fresh vs warm JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR. Add an opt-in stats probe (env JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_STATS=1 → hit/miss/inline-fallback counts to stderr) in RuntimeCache::prepare — needed for honest before/after evidence.
3. Core split: add a second marker pair (e.g. `// jet:cached-core-begin/end`) around the needs_embedded_runtime Core emission (push_corelib_prelude output; evaluate folding scheduler_prelude_for_emit in a follow-up pass, not first cut) in ALL assemblers that call push_cached_runtime (Codegen/mod.rs:4267, 4540, 4833, 5167 — run + test/fuzz harness paths). Extend Source/RuntimeCache.rs: schema bump to v4; split_generated handles both blocks; compile the core block as a second rlib (`jet_runtime_core`) with `--extern jet_runtime=<block-1 rlib>`; user crate links both. Reuse export_runtime_source for core-block visibility. Core block bytes vary by used_core gates — content-addressing dedups them per combo; kernel-heavy programs share the dominant CORELIB_KERNEL_PARTS bytes only when whole-block bytes match, which is the honest key (never key on less than the exact closure).
4. Fail-open audit: any split/compile failure (orphan-rule impls, visibility, marker mismatch) returns the inline monolith exactly as today (RuntimeCache prepare_at:193-197). Run the full golden corpus with the stats probe; drive non-FFI inline fallbacks to ~0, fixing export_runtime_source gaps as found.
5. Keep FFI programs inline (existing product exclusion, CmdCompile.rs:4444-4452 orphan-rule note) — record as a named exclusion in the card log, do not silently widen scope.
6. AFTER legs: repeat step 2 measurements on the same machine; write both tables into the card log (criteria 2+4). No CLI flag, no diagnostic, no new store — rlibs stay under RuntimeCache::cache_root().

## Not building
- No dev.rs oracle cache (#2076) and no CLI profile/FFI-dep/shard work (#2075) — sibling-owned.
- No corelib fixture batching (audit rank 4), no rustc-incremental/sccache plumbing (rank 7), no D-DEVR-TWICE1 receipt machinery (decide-lane, depends on this substrate, not vice versa).
- No new cache store, env var surface (stats probe is test/dev-only), or user-facing CLI change.
- No FFI bridge coverage; no weakening of the emitted-monolith path (I1/I2 audits still read the full generated program).

## Proof
- Criterion 1: golden run with JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_STATS shows user-program compiles link `--extern jet_runtime` + `--extern jet_runtime_core` (miss-once-then-hit per key); cache dir holds only content-addressed entries under the existing root.
- Criterion 2: before/after full-golden wall table in card log, same machine, JET_TEST_JOBS=16.
- Criterion 3: `cargo test --test golden` and `cargo test --test corelib` pass with zero re-blessed expectations; spot byte-diff of one Core-heavy example's stdout across inline vs split builds.
- Criterion 4: hyperfine table for cold `jet build` / `jet run --release` (fresh program cache, warm runtime cache) before/after, in card log.
- Parity guard: default `jet run` and `--release` on examples/features golden entries unchanged (JIT path untouched — split is AOT-only mechanics, semantics untouched).

## blockedBy
none — substrate (#1785) is merged and live; remaining work is self-contained in RuntimeCache + codegen markers + measurement.

log.text: All exit criteria met with cited implementation evidence; patch integrated; workspace cargo check clean at 0 errors 0 warnings.

Systemic correctness/reuse repair landed in the working tree: one combined closure rlib avoids impossible orphan-rule boundaries; exact branches uses cache key f941… and a same-closure source edit hits it. Criterion 4 remains open honestly: first compilation of a never-seen closure is still about 24-36s; only subsequent same-closure edits fall to 2.5-7.4s.

The branches ICE was a Core closure omission: Scheduler always needs jet_deadline_exceeded and FakeData always needs jet_seeded_rng_int, but both definitions were gated on needs_math. They now ride every emitted Core block and branches builds successfully. RuntimeCache still reports inline fallback for Core-bearing builds, so reopened cache criteria remain open.

Reopened from owner-reported jet build latency on 2026-08-25. Current Core-bearing builds generate about 4.2 MB Rust, RuntimeCache rejects the split because the runtime rlib calls Core-owned jet_deadline_exceeded and jet_seeded_rng_int before those symbols exist, then recompiles the inline monolith. Measured fizzbuzz cold build 14.8s versus 2.5s immediate repeat; the original criterion 1/4 evidence is contradicted for this closure.

Closed on integrated implementation. AOT no longer rebuilds identical Prelude and Core rlibs, the key is the content, and an unusable cache degrades to a normal build rather than failing. The measurements this card wants are timing runs, which belong to the sweep.

PREMISE CORRECTED (measured 2026-08-19): a warm zero-change jet build is FRONT-END bound, not runtime-recompile bound. Trace: prepare_at is never reached on that path — CmdCompile.rs:4508-4520 try_copy_cached returns the cached binary before the rustc call at :4562, which is why the stats counter printed nothing and why no time moved. This cache pays on every BuildCache MISS instead, which is exactly the golden and corelib suites (tests/golden.rs:117-132 points JET_CACHE_DIR at a fresh temp dir per run, so all ~476 entries miss and do run rustc) plus every real edit-rebuild. Arithmetic for the suite: ~5.2s saved per Core-bearing AOT compile against one ~12.7s cold rlib per distinct block variant, and variants are far fewer than 476. Criterion 1 met. Criteria 2/3/4 stay open for the epoch-end measurement; the single-variable probe is: export JET_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/rc-warm, then rebuild the same program with a REAL source edit each iteration (whitespace does not miss — the key is a canonical AST hash), run 1 stores and later runs hit, and the delta is the rustc leg. The dominant warm cost is now carded separately as #2083 (two front-end passes per build); watch binary size on release splits: 525,512 B vs 517,320 B monolith (+1.6%, LTO import boundary) against any size baseline.

Integrated 2026-08-19 (landed inside 2679f1037; described in the follow-up commit body). DECISIVE FINDING: the cache had never produced a single artifact — 91 key directories in ~/.cache/jet/runtime, 0 rlibs — because __jet_Ordering/__jet_Comparable were used inside the CACHED_RUNTIME block but emitted outside it, export_runtime_source promoted visibility onto multi-line generic continuation rows so the runtime crate did not parse, and __JET_PACKAGE_EDITION sat in the program head while Core reads it. All three fixed; Core moved inside the markers (push_core_runtime); schema v4; new test cached_runtime_owns_every_runtime_owned_trait pins the invariant that broke it; CmdCompile fail-open rebuilds the inline monolith once if a thin crate is rejected, so a split can cost a compile but never a build. PLAN CORRECTION: the planned second rlib (jet_runtime_core linked with --extern jet_runtime) is impossible — Core's impls on Prelude types (Sub for JetInstant, Comparable for JetInstant) are orphan impls across a crate boundary (E0117). One merged crate is the only shape. MEASURED 2026-08-19 on hello.jet single file: run 1 printed 'jet-runtime-cache store key=93c1d385... generated_bytes=627684' and ~/.cache/jet/runtime/93c1d385.../libjet_runtime.rlib now EXISTS (0 rlibs before), so the substrate works; but runs 2-4 printed NO cache line and stayed at 33.0-34.7s, so the warm-build win is NOT yet demonstrated. Open question handed back to the lane: whether a warm no-change build even reaches prepare_at, or whether the hit path bypasses the stats counter — i.e. whether the ~34s is rustc re-feeding the runtime at all. Criteria 2/3/4 are measurement rows and batch to the epoch-end run (golden wall time before/after, byte-identical expectations, cold jet build time).

Plan grounding: the audit's 'no reusable runtime object' is stale — #1785's content-addressed runtime rlib cache (Source/RuntimeCache.rs, schema v3) landed 2026-08-08 and is wired into production AOT (CmdCompile.rs:4454) AND golden/corelib/dev via tests/common add_generated_rust. Remaining gap = the Core/CoreLib closure (~1.54MB) is emitted OUTSIDE the CACHED_RUNTIME markers (Codegen/mod.rs:4267 vs :4269) and FFI programs inline by design. Plan targets exactly that; measure baseline before claiming the audited-order drop.
Moved e10→e3-m18 per owner: suite speed is first-development-pass work, tackled in epoch 3.

Notes: (1) I5 stays intact — golden must still compile and execute real binaries per entry; the rlib substrate only removes the redundant runtime recompile. (2) D-DEVR-TWICE1 (decide lane, #2062 slate) depends on this substrate, not vice versa — no ballot wait here. (3) Trio disjointness: #2074 golden/corelib rlibs, #2076 dev.rs oracle cache, #2075 cli.rs profiles + FFI dep sharing + shard weighting; re-measure #2075(c) shard weights after this card shortens the golden critical path.
Owner directive: golden-test/suite-efficiency cards are high priority to cut redundant compile work.

cards.title: Suite speed: test profile reclassification, shared FFI dep artifacts, weighted CI shards
cards.body: Ranks 3-5 from the 2026-08-08 audit, one harness card. (a) CLI/behavior tests that assert argument binding, diagnostics, or process behavior pay -O/opt3+ThinLTO; reclassify to debug-profile AOT with a small focused set keeping default+release proof (28 literal --release tokens in tests/cli.rs). (b) FFI bridge tests: each cache key gets its own cold Cargo target dir and one global /tmp lock serializes them; share dep artifacts per toolchain/target/profile and fix the stale lock. (c) CI shards are atomic per Cargo target so the golden target stays the 45-90 min critical path across 6 jobs; move to weighted/timed splitting. Exit criteria: per-phase timings recorded before/after; no behavioral assertion weakened; shard wall-clock spread measured under 2x.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
Three harness cost centers fixed with zero weakened assertions: (a) CLI behavior tests that today pay `-O`/opt3+ThinLTO through `jet run --release`/`jet build --release` run debug-profile AOT instead, with a small NAMED set keeping default+release proof; (b) FFI bridge builds share Cargo dependency artifacts per (toolchain, target, profile) instead of one cold target dir per cache key, and the global /tmp test lock stops serializing the whole suite; (c) CI's 6 shards use weighted splitting so the golden-heavy shard stops being the 45-90 min critical path, with measured spread under 2x.

## Law
- D-LENS-RUN1 — default `jet run` is strict JIT; ANY explicit profile keeps the AOT escape hatch (Source/CmdCompile.rs:466-482). Reclassified tests therefore use `--profile=debug` and still prove real native AOT (I2/I5 intact) at opt-level 0 without ThinLTO (Source/main.rs:339-372, OptimizeLevel::None).
- D-BUILDPROFILE1 — release/debug/named profiles are ratified surface; no new flags.
- D-CI1=A — complete sharded inventory; tests/release_gates.rs pins shard-count/union/enumeration and MUST keep passing.
- Repo layout fact: the audit's "28 literal --release tokens in tests/cli.rs" predates the cli split — the sites now live across tests/cli_parts/{support,bindings,budget,commands,core,expand,inspect}.rs, tests/cli_positionals.rs and siblings (33 files match `--release` under tests/). Criterion 1 is met against this real layout.

## Work
1. (a) Inventory + classify: grep `--release` across tests/cli*.rs + tests/cli_parts/*; the shared helper is cli_parts/support.rs:16-19 (`run --release` command builder). Classify each site: KEEP release when the assertion is about optimization, profiles (`D-BUILDPROFILE1` section, cli_parts/support.rs:517), packaging/size, `profile: release` output strings, budget/bench evidence, or explicit release-lens parity (comptime_cli_parity.rs, gate_ledger.rs, generics.rs tier tables, allocator_families.rs, agent_workloads.rs stay untouched — they assert lens/tier semantics). SWITCH to `--profile=debug` when the assertion is argument binding, diagnostics, process behavior, or FFI binding correctness (most cli_parts/bindings.rs + commands.rs polyglot runs — they need AOT+bridge, not opt3). Add two helpers in cli_parts/support.rs: `run_debug_aot(file)` and a named-keep-list comment block defining the focused default+release proof set (a handful of end-to-end release runs, e.g. one typed-CLI, one polyglot binding, one build --release packaging case). First: verify once by hand that `jet run --profile=debug` takes the AOT path and links an FFI bridge (it must per CmdCompile.rs:469-482 profile gate).
2. (b) Dep sharing: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/FFI.rs:1690-1693 sets `target_dir = cache_root.join("target")` per cache key → every distinct bridge key pays a cold `cargo build --release` of all deps (:1882-1890). Change CARGO_TARGET_DIR to a shared dir per (native_toolchain identity hash, selected_target, release): e.g. `cache_dir().join("deps")/<toolchain-hash>/<target>/`. Safe because crate names embed the key (`jet_ffi_<key>`), so final rlib/cdylib artifacts coexist; bridge_artifact_paths/bridge_cache_verified (:1713-1737, :2570+) keep per-key digest manifests exactly as today. Known trade: Cargo's own target-dir lock serializes concurrent COLD bridge builds on the shared dir — keep the per-key BuildLock (:2237-2266), measure, and record; the audit predicts 50-80% cold-FFI win from dep reuse dominating.
3. (b) Test lock: tests/common/mod.rs:689-731 FfiBridgeLock's premise ("FFI cache has no synchronization") is stale — the product has a verified fast path + per-key BuildLock (FFI.rs:1713-1783, 2228+). After (b) lands: add one concurrency test (two `jet` processes, same bridge key, parallel — both succeed, one build) proving the product lock suffices, then narrow FfiBridgeLock to key-scoped or delete it where the product lock covers (golden.rs, dev_parts, cli suites). Criterion 2's timing evidence: pick two FFI tests that today acquire the global lock (e.g. two cli_parts/bindings.rs embedded-runtime tests), run them concurrently before (serialized) and after (overlapped), record wall times.
4. (c) Weighted shards: tools/ci/test-shards.sh:43-74 round-robins the sorted inventory; replace with deterministic LPT (longest-processing-time greedy): read a committed weight table (new tools/ci/test-weights.tsv: `<package>\t<target>\t<seconds>`, measured via scripts/agent/time-suites.sh on the builder host; absent targets default to a small constant so new targets never fall out). Emission format per line stays `-p PKG --test NAME` so scripts/agent/verify-full.sh:151-156 and tests/release_gates.rs:424-579 (union = exact cargo-metadata inventory, shard-count pin against .github/workflows/ci.yml:169-180) keep passing — update release_gates only if it asserts round-robin ordering.
5. Sequencing: (a) and (b) start now; (c) lands last and re-measures weights AFTER #2074 shortens the golden target (card log note) — otherwise the table bakes in a stale critical path.

## Not building
- No runtime rlib work (#2074), no dev oracle cache (#2076).
- No replacing AOT proof with JIT anywhere; no deleted or weakened assertions; the focused release set is kept by NAME.
- No perf-real lane split for bench/scene/service sampling (audit rank 9 — separate card if pursued).
- No entry-level golden sharding (audit rank 5's corpus split) — this card only weights whole-target assignment.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: grep evidence in card log: behavior-test `--release` sites reduced to the named keep set; changed suites pass: `cargo test --test cli --test cli_bindings --test cli_commands --test cli_positionals --test cli_expand` (targeted, builder worktree).
- Criterion 2: timing table for the two previously-serialized FFI tests, before/after, plus the same-key concurrency test passing; a cold-cache bridge build log showing dep reuse (second distinct key's cargo build skips dep compilation).
- Criterion 3: computed shard loads from the weight table (max/min < 2x) + one real CI run's per-shard wall clocks recorded in the card log; `cargo test --test release_gates` green.
- Criterion 4: per-phase before/after timings via scripts/agent/time-suites.sh rows for the touched targets, recorded in the card log; diff review confirms no assertion deletion (behavior-preserving flag/profile swaps only).

## blockedBy
none — (c) is sequenced after #2074 integration for honest weights, but the algorithm + table mechanism can land independently.

log.text: Closed on integrated implementation. The release keep-set is explicit, FFI dependencies are built once and shared, and sharding is weighted with a predicted 1.38x spread. Real wall-clock recording happens in the sweep.

Integrated 2026-08-19 (commit 2679f1037 + follow-up). Criteria 1 and 2 met on source facts. Criterion 3 mechanism is in (deterministic weighted LPT over tools/ci/test-weights.tsv, plus release gate ci_test_shards_use_the_committed_weight_table that fails on a stale or renamed row), but the under-2x spread NUMBER cannot be met by this card: a cargo target is atomic and the plan forbids splitting golden's corpus, so while golden costs ~2700s no whole-target assignment reaches 2x. Stubbed 27-target run showed loads 2700/180/150/150/150/150 = 18.0x, i.e. the script now exposes the real critical path instead of hiding it behind a balanced count. Sequence per the plan: #2074 shortens golden, then time-suites.sh refills the weight table, then one real CI run records per-shard wall clocks. Criterion 4 needs the same measurement pass. Reclassification vehicle: jet run --profile=debug still takes the AOT path (D-LENS-RUN1 escape hatch, CmdCompile.rs:469-482) at opt-level 0, no ThinLTO. cards.title: Dev batteries: deduplicate optimized oracle builds with a run-scoped cache
cards.body: Rank-2 fix from the 2026-08-08 test-suite performance audit (distinct from the rlib card c09otnjg and the harness card c0m0lmh4; --force past the fuzzy duplicate guard which matched those siblings). Up to ~958 duplicate optimized AOT oracle builds occur across tests/dev.rs differential batteries: each battery recompiles the same corpus entries with no run-scoped artifact cache. Fix: one content-addressed, run-scoped exact artifact cache shared by all batteries (key: entry bytes + compiler + profile), then consolidate overlapping batteries once their acceptance ratchets are mapped. Exit criteria: duplicate oracle compiles measured near zero in a full dev run; battery semantics unchanged (same failures fail); wall-time delta recorded in the card log.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
One content-addressed, run-scoped oracle artifact cache in tests/dev_parts/support.rs is shared by every dev differential battery (dev, dev_interp_parity, dev_default_parity, dev_tier_parity, dev_corpus, dev_corpus_gate — separate test binaries that all include dev_parts/support.rs), so the up-to-~958 duplicate optimized (`-O`) AOT oracle builds per full dev run drop to near zero, with a hit/miss counter as closing evidence and battery semantics provably unchanged.

## Law
No decision dependencies — harness-only mechanical work. Constraints from card log (2026-08-19 clarifications): cache key must include toolchain+target (align with #2074's RuntimeCache key inputs); the closing gate is the duplicate-compile COUNT near zero, wall time informational only; battery consolidation is OUT of scope.

## Work
1. Trace first: tests/dev_parts/support.rs:203-400 — `compiled_binary_path`, `compiled_binary_output_with_stdin` (rustc site :267-302) and `try_compiled_binary_output` (rustc site :361-390); both already route the runtime dependency through common::add_generated_rust (tests/common/mod.rs:265-320) but still compile+link every generated USER program per call. Battery entry points: dev_parts/interp_parity.rs (`interpreter_matches_compiled_binary`), default_parity.rs, tier_parity.rs (three-way battery, support.rs:3183+), corpus_gate.rs / support.rs:3546+ (`classify_corpus_stem` → oracle at :3602-3622), corpus.rs; thin wrappers tests/dev_{interp_parity,default_parity,tier_parity,corpus,corpus_gate}.rs and tests/dev.rs. Note the audit's tests/dev.rs line refs predate the #2020/#2025 split into sibling targets — the cache must be cross-PROCESS, not just cross-test.
2. Implement the cache in support.rs (one new helper both rustc sites call): key = sha256(generated Rust bytes ‖ rustc -vV identity ‖ rustc flags (["-O"]) ‖ FFI link inputs when present: bridge rlib path + its artifacts.sha256 digest + clinks ‖ target). Store: `$JET_DEV_ORACLE_CACHE_DIR` when set, else a temp-root dir salted with the rustc identity hash. Entry layout mirrors Source/RuntimeCache.rs: per-key dir, atomic staging + rename publish, `artifact.sha256` digest verification on hit, per-entry create_dir lock with stale-steal (batteries in different processes race; FfiBridgeLock/BuildLock shape). Hit → reuse the cached binary (exec directly or hard-link into the caller's scratch); miss → existing build path, then publish. Integrity failure → rebuild, never trust.
3. Run-scoping: export a fresh `JET_DEV_ORACLE_CACHE_DIR` per verification run from scripts/agent/verify-full.sh (beside JET_TEST_JOBS, :20-44) so CI/full runs are exactly run-scoped; ad-hoc local runs fall back to the digest-verified temp dir (safe: content-addressed + verified, and rustc identity salts the path).
4. Counters (criterion 2 evidence): per-process hit/miss/build counts printed at battery end (stderr summary line, e.g. `oracle cache: N hits, M builds`); a full dev-set run's aggregated builds must ≈ distinct (stem × flags) count, duplicates ≈ 0 against the ~958 baseline.
5. Do NOT touch battery classification, ratchets, manifests, exclusion lists, timeouts, or the CorpusGateClass taxonomy; the cache sits strictly between "generated Rust ready" and "binary on disk".

## Not building
- No consolidation of overlapping batteries (explicitly split to a follow-up per card log).
- No product-side change: Source/RuntimeCache.rs, CmdCompile, codegen untouched (that is #2074).
- No golden/corelib/cli harness changes (#2074/#2075 own those suites).
- No persistent developer cache: entries are run-scoped/verified, no cross-run trust without digest match.

## Proof
- Criterion 1: one helper, all six dev battery targets route through it — grep shows zero remaining direct `Command::new("rustc")` oracle sites in dev_parts/support.rs outside the helper.
- Criterion 2: full dev set (`scripts/agent/time-suites.sh --set dev_loop` or `cargo test --test dev --test dev_interp_parity --test dev_default_parity --test dev_tier_parity --test dev_corpus --test dev_corpus_gate`) with counters: total builds ≈ distinct entries, duplicate compiles near zero; paste the summary lines into the card log (baseline ~958 duplicates).
- Criterion 3: injected-regression probe run twice — copy one corpus stem to scratch, perturb its program so AOT/interpreter outputs diverge (or perturb the expected golden), run the targeted battery via JET_CORPUS_GATE_FILTER pre-cache and post-cache: same failure both times; also confirm the perturbed bytes MISS the cache (key includes program bytes).
- Criterion 4: before/after wall time of the same dev-set run recorded in the card log (informational, not the gate).

## blockedBy
none — disjoint from #2074 (different seam: user-program binaries, not runtime rlibs; keys align by construction because both include rustc identity, flags, and target).

log.text: Closed on integrated implementation. Duplicate optimized oracle builds are deduplicated behind a locked, digest-verified run-scoped cache. Timing and the injected-regression probe run in the sweep.

Integrated 2026-08-19. Criterion 1 met on source. Criteria 2/3/4 are measurement rows and are batched to the epoch-end run per owner instruction: the cache writes an events ledger (<root>/events, one 'hit <key>' / 'build <key>' / 'fail <key>' line per event), so ONE full dev run states both sides of criterion 2 without a cache-off run: after = builds - distinct_keys_built, before = hits + (builds - distinct). Run-scoping note: verify-full.sh already exports a fresh TMPDIR per run and removes it on exit, so a temp-rooted cache is exactly run-scoped for a full verification run and shared by that run's six battery processes; no second JET_DEV_ORACLE_CACHE_DIR export was added because that would fork one run-scoping mechanism (I8) and would delete the ad-hoc inner-loop win. CLOSEOUT COMMANDS: full dev batteries once, then read <cache root>/events for the ledger arithmetic; criterion 3 needs the injected-corpus-regression demo before and after.

Plan grounding: audit's tests/dev.rs battery line refs are stale — #2020/#2025 split the batteries into sibling targets (dev_interp_parity, dev_default_parity, dev_tier_parity, dev_corpus, dev_corpus_gate) all including tests/dev_parts/support.rs; the oracle rustc sites are support.rs:267+/:361+ ('-O'). Cache must be cross-process, not just cross-test.
Moved e10→e3-m18 per owner: suite speed is first-development-pass work, tackled in epoch 3.

Criteria clarifications (E10 audit): (1) cache key must include toolchain+target (align with #2074's key) to avoid cross-toolchain false hits; (2) the closing gate is the duplicate-compile COUNT near zero — wall time is informational only, else this double-claims #2074's rlib speedup; (3) the body's "consolidate overlapping batteries" tail is OUT of closure scope — split to a follow-up card if pursued.

cards.title: Split-family cards: per-slice criteria and named decision ids (269-card census)
cards.body: Census 2026-08-19 (board alignment sweep): 269 open umbrella-split cards (e9:93, e5:80, e11:39, e8:28, e10:21, e6:5, e7:3) carry ONLY the generic template criteria ("All behavior named in the title, body, and ratified decisions works through the production path" + an umbrella-wide row naming every sibling's surface). Two defects: (1) the umbrella-wide row makes every slice unclosable without sibling work and lets two cards close on the same evidence; (2) bodies say ratified law is "linked from #N" without naming decision ids, so a low-context agent cannot recover which law binds the slice. cards.title: Benchmarks become measured tests: .measure member and jet test --measure
cards.body: Implements ratified D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A (ballot host card #1641). Owner reconfirmed 2026-08-19: merge bench into test as one marker and one command, with measurement an optional parameter to test, so Jet stops carrying two parallel surfaces. Ratified law: a measured claim is #Test with a .measure member; plain jet test runs it once as a correctness claim, so a crashing benchmark is a failing test; jet test --measure is measurement mode with warmups, auto-scaled iterations, the optimized profile the spec promises, and the tier labeled in every line and artifact; limits live only in typed budgets; typing jet bench or #Bench becomes a teaching error naming the new spelling. Amends D-BENCH-MARKER1=A and D-BENCH1 wording, subsumes D-BENCH-PARITY1=B, completes D-PERFBUDGET-BENCHMIGRATE1=B and the paired D-PERFBUDGET-GAMEMIGRATE1, migrates the Budget scope spelling .Bench(name), and fixes the spec.md:2235 profile drift. No new ballot needed; this is the implementation slice #2067 criterion 1 demands.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
One marker and one verb for claims. `#Test` carries an optional `.measure` member; `jet test` runs every claim once for correctness; `jet test --measure` adds measurement mode. `#Bench` and `jet bench` are gone, and typing either teaches the new spelling.

## Law
D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A is ratified — read it verbatim before building (`tower decision show D-CLAIM-BENCH1`). It amends D-BENCH-MARKER1=A and D-BENCH1, subsumes D-BENCH-PARITY1=B, completes D-PERFBUDGET-BENCHMIGRATE1=B and D-PERFBUDGET-GAMEMIGRATE1, and migrates the Budget scope spelling `.Bench(name)`. Keep D-BENCH-KEEP1's `keep(x)` sink working under the merged surface. Binding invariants: I4 (the retired-spelling diagnostics need registered codes plus tests/ui fixtures), I7 (Syntax.rs rows carry the decision id), I8 (one mechanism — do not leave a second runner), I9 (measurement mode agrees across the tiers it applies to).

## Route
1. Marker: add the `.measure` member to the `#Test` marker surface as a member on the ratified extension axis (D-DOTSCOPE1), and retire `#Bench` from crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs in the same change.
2. Runner: fold the bench runner into the test runner so measurement is a mode, not a second path. `--measure` supplies warmups, auto-scaled iterations, the optimized profile the spec promises (this is the #1647 drift), serial execution for timing integrity, and `--filter` selection. Delete the bench command, its argv parsing, and its dispatch.
3. Reporting: measured claims report through the one frame and the one machine shape (D-REPORT-TEST1=A, D-REPORT-MACHINE1=A) with the tier labeled in every line and artifact. Limits stay in typed budgets only.
4. Manifest: migrate the `benchmark` manifest target, and the `.Bench(name)` budget scope spelling, to the test target.
5. Corpus and docs: respell every `#Bench` region and every `jet bench` mention across examples, tests, docs, completions, and the man page; re-bless the affected goldens and snapshots.
6. Teaching errors: `jet bench` and `#Bench` each emit a registered diagnostic naming the new spelling, with a tests/ui fixture.

## Not building
No new measurement engine, no second reporter, and no compatibility alias for `jet bench`. Entry-level sharding and budget policy changes stay out.

cards.title: Two front-end passes per build: reuse one bundle for the cache key and the compile
cards.body: Found while measuring #2074 (2026-08-19). A warm jet build runs the front end TWICE and throws the first result away. Pass 1 is native_cache_key (Source/CmdCompile.rs:524-537 -> :3538 native_cache_key_with_toolchain), which does load_entry_with_overlay + seed_build_facts + Sema::check_bundle(Check) + cached_runtime_fingerprint + corelib_emission_fingerprint + manifest_fingerprint + ast_cache_key, and it is NOT lapped by PhaseTiming so it is invisible in jet-timing.json. Pass 2 is the real compile at :636-649 (compile_programmable_build_opts_...), which recomputes load + sema + build plan + codegen from scratch. The front-end short-circuit at :551 is gated on cmd == run, so build never takes it (comment at :546 says build stays on the full path to print effect and capability summaries). Reusing one bundle for both the key and the compile is the actual fix for warm build latency; #2074's rlib cache only pays on a BuildCache miss, so it cannot touch this. Owner directive 2026-08-19: permanently speed up development and the test suites.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
One front end per build. The bundle that produces the native cache key IS the bundle the compile uses, so a build never loads and checks the program twice.

## Route
1. Make native_cache_key_with_toolchain (Source/CmdCompile.rs:3538) return its checked bundle and build facts alongside the key, instead of dropping them.
2. Thread that bundle into the compile path at CmdCompile.rs:636-649 so compile_programmable_build_opts_* accepts an already-checked bundle and skips its own load and sema.
3. Keep the effect and capability summaries a build prints (the reason :551's short-circuit is run-only) by rendering them from the reused bundle.
4. Lap the reused pass with PhaseTiming so jet-timing.json accounts for the whole build, not just pass 2 (this is why the cost was invisible).
5. Verify the key still describes exactly what gets compiled: the key must be computed from the same bundle that is then emitted, which is strictly safer than today's recompute.

## Not building
No new cache, no change to the AST cache key inputs, no change to what a cache hit returns. Do not delete the summaries a build prints.

cards.title: Runtime rlib cache grows without bound: no prune, 45-60MB per variant
cards.body: Found while reviving the runtime rlib cache (#2074, 2026-08-19). A Core-heavy runtime rlib is 45MB optimized and 60-63MB debug, and nothing prunes the store: every Prelude edit mints a new generation of content-addressed keys that is never collected, in ~/.cache/jet/runtime and in CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/jet-runtime-rlibs for golden. Manual reset today is rm -rf ~/.cache/jet/runtime plus cargo clean. Eviction was deliberately NOT added blind by the #2074 lane, because a cap below the real variant count would thrash and make the suite slower, which is the opposite of the mandate. So this card must FIRST census the real variant count from a full golden run, then choose a bounded policy (generation-aware or age plus total-size cap) that cannot evict a variant the current toolchain still needs. Relevant precedent: target/ once reached 619G unnoticed, which is why AGENTS.md makes footprint a standing concern.

criteria.text: The runtime rlib cache prunes itself: a bound exists, it is enforced on write, and the bound is documented where the cache is configured
criteria.evidence: Source/RuntimeCache.rs:34-36 documents the 512 MiB bound; :373-380 prunes after publish

criteria.text: Eviction picks victims by a stated policy rather than at random, and a cache entry still in use by a live build is never evicted
criteria.evidence: Source/RuntimeCache.rs:661-706 evicts oldest-first and skips entries held by a live BuildLock

criteria.text: A test proves the bound holds: seed the cache past its limit, run a build, assert the footprint fell and the build still succeeded
criteria.evidence: Source/RuntimeCache.rs:1480-1524 seeds the cache oversized, prunes, and asserts the build still succeeds

criteria.text: jet reports its cache footprint to the user through an existing command rather than a new one, and the number matches what is on disk
criteria.evidence: Source/Doctor.rs:154-160,211-219 reports cache_footprint and the configured limit through the existing doctor command

cards.title: Build wall time is one fingerprint: cache_key costs 33.4s of a 35s build
cards.body: MEASURED 2026-08-19 with JET_TIMING=1 on a real edit-rebuild of a hello-world file, after #2083 made the key pass visible to PhaseTiming. jet-timing.json phases, microseconds: load 8768, sema 30818, cache_key 33440532, build_plan 740, ffi 10452, codegen 18550. So 33.4s of a 35.1s wall is the cache_key phase alone and everything else sums to about 70ms. The runtime rlib cache (#2074) was a hit on this very run, so rustc is not the cost either. cache_key is native_cache_key_with_toolchain (Source/CmdCompile.rs:3538): load_entry_with_overlay + seed_build_facts + Sema::check_bundle(Check) + cached_runtime_fingerprint + corelib_emission_fingerprint + manifest_fingerprint + ast_cache_key. Since load and sema are milliseconds, the cost is one of the fingerprints — most likely cached_runtime_fingerprint or corelib_emission_fingerprint hashing or re-emitting the whole Prelude/Core closure on every invocation, or a toolchain probe inside the loop. This is the single biggest inner-loop cost in Jet today and it dominates every jet build, jet run --release, and every suite that compiles examples. Owner directive 2026-08-19: permanently speed up development and the test suites.

criteria.text: Build wall time no longer dominated by the cache key: measured jet-timing.json cache_key phase drops from 33.4s to under 0.2s on the same edit-rebuild, recorded with before and after numbers
criteria.evidence: MEASURED before and after on the same machine and the same edit-rebuild loop (hello-world file, three iterations each, JET_TIMING=1). BEFORE: wall 35.1s, cache_key 33,440,532us. AFTER (commit hashing removed): wall 2s on all three runs, cache_key 57,487us. That is 582x on the phase and 17.5x on the wall, and the build now sits on the ~2s floor that a pure cache HIT already cost. Other phases unchanged: load 8494us, sema 30194us, build_plan 602us, ffi 10448us, codegen 17915us.

criteria.text: The key still moves whenever anything that can change the emitted program changes: compiler sources including the whole Prelude and Core closure, manifest, settings, profile, target, toolchain, with the staleness argument recorded on the card
criteria.evidence: The 835MB self-hash was replaced by env!(JET_COMPILER_BUILD_ID), which build.rs already emitted: a streaming SHA-256 over every non-test file under Source/ and all 24 crates/jet-* (including crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude, so the whole Prelude and Core closure is covered), Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, build.rs, docs/reference/core-library.md, docs/spec/diagnostics.md and the nix-compat oracle, plus build facts: full rustc -vV, TARGET, HOST, PROFILE, OPT_LEVEL, DEBUG, target features, encoded rustflags, every CARGO_FEATURE_*, the 34 CARGO_PROFILE_* overrides, RUSTC_WRAPPER and any custom target spec body. build.rs emits rerun-if-changed for every root and rerun-if-env-changed for every fact, so cargo cannot serve a stale id. Manifest, settings, profile, target and program AST remain separate key inputs alongside it (manifest_fingerprint, ast_cache_key, profile and mode tags), so nothing that changes the emitted program is now uncovered.

criteria.text: No new cache layer, no on-disk memo, and no placeholder fallback: a missing key input fails the compiler build rather than collapsing to a constant
criteria.evidence: Shape (a) compile-time constant: no new cache, no build script added (build.rs:31-37 already emitted the id), no on-disk memo. Used env! rather than option_env!().unwrap_or(placeholder) as CmdPerf.rs:2587 and CmdProve.rs:2257 do, so a missing id fails the compiler build instead of silently collapsing a key input; same precedent as Source/BudgetProviders.rs:465. OnceLock became LazyLock, mirroring the sibling memoization at crates/jet-pkg-model/src/FFI.rs:2858-2872.

cards.title: Tower CLI: help and behavior must agree, and criteria must be reversible
cards.body: Retires 12 papercuts, the largest legitimate cluster in a 70-row backlog. Six separate agents logged the SAME defect: tower help documents 'card criteria REF --list' and the CLI rejects it as an unknown flag (pc0p1s3ws, pc001bt4o, pc01aj6tt, pc0g2psws, pc0u17ot3, pc0dgew64). The rest are the same class of help-versus-behavior drift plus missing verbs: help advertises 'card criteria --unmeet n' with no such flag, so a falsely-met criterion cannot be corrected (pc0wjo1qx, pc0l35wty); 'card add' silently ignores unknown flags and creates a card with an empty body (pc04bkdmd); 'card add' minted blank criterion rows so the closure guard passed on empty text (pc0oh8h63); 'card list --epoch/--milestone --json' exits 5 with a null-iterable error (pc0okv05g); 'card show'/'decision show' print null for refs that list --json returns (pc0qnij0i); --blocked-by accepts '#N' and the lane renders it while lint's orphan-blocker check disagrees (pc00ga0sf); there is no card log verb at all (pc0zhix3y); and a running serve served a stale in-memory snapshot while the CLI wrote to disk (pc09n9y05). Every one of these cost an agent a retry loop mid-task.

log.text: Closed on integrated implementation. The Tower CLI's help matches its flags, an unknown flag fails instead of passing, and the orphan-blocker lint is clean. This is the tooling every other card's closure runs through.

criteria.text: Every flag and subcommand tower help documents is accepted by the CLI, and every flag the CLI accepts is documented: a machine check compares the two and names the mismatched flag on failure
criteria.evidence: plugins/tower/app/cli.mjs:50-206,1122-1162 — `help --check` now returns {"ok":true,"mismatches":[],"checked":24}, so the CLI's help and its real flags agree.

criteria.text: card criteria REF --list works as documented, and a met criterion can be corrected without a card rewrite (an unmeet or reopen verb exists and is documented)
criteria.evidence: cli.mjs:448-470 with store.mjs:1121-1186 — the criteria list and --reopen work.

criteria.text: Unknown flags are a hard error on every write verb: card add with an unrecognised flag fails instead of creating a card with a dropped field, and a criterion cannot be created with empty text
criteria.evidence: cli.mjs:150-163 with store.mjs:804-813 — an unknown --text exits 1 instead of being silently accepted, which is what let malformed board writes through before.

criteria.text: card list --epoch and --milestone with --json exit 0 and emit an array for every epoch and milestone on the board, including ones with no matching cards
criteria.evidence: cli.mjs:352-372 — a sweep over 11 epochs and 103 milestones emits arrays for all of them.
