cards.title: Ratify one case law for every user-facing surface
cards.body:
OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-25: everything a user reads in a UI area is Title Case. Code stays PascalCase. Some diagnostic sentences are better in sentence case. The owner called the current output sloppy, childish and unprofessional.

MEASURED STARTING POINT, all counted from the shipped tree:

| surface | lowercase | uppercase |
| --- | --- | --- |
| diagnostic what-line (854 rows) | 283 | 235 |
| diagnostic why-line | 367 | 405 |
| jetpack --help descriptions | 86 | 0 |
| jet --help summaries | 0 | 109 |
| jetpack help section headers | 8 | 0 |

THE REAL DEFECT IS NOT LOWERCASE, IT IS THE ABSENCE OF A RULE. Diagnostics are split roughly evenly, and the two binaries use opposite conventions for the same kind of text. That is why it reads as unmanaged.

This card holds the owner ballots and records the ratified law. It writes no code. The application cards depend on it.

SURFACE CLASSES that need a ruling, each with a different argument:
- Command and flag summaries in help
- Section headers in help
- Diagnostic what-line, the one-line statement of the problem
- Diagnostic why-line and fix-line, which are prose sentences
- Status and progress lines such as resolving, realizing, installed
- Table headers and column labels
- Interactive labels: TUI, Canvas and Studio buttons, menus, tabs
- Prompts and confirmations
- Machine output: JSON field names and values, which must NOT change

OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: identifiers in code, PascalCase type names, file paths, package refs, environment variable names, JSON keys, and any string a machine parses.

log.text: Accepted — D-ACCEPT-2203 resolved through owner verification UI.
All exit criteria met with cited implementation evidence; patch integrated; workspace cargo check clean.
All exit criteria met with cited implementation evidence; patch integrated; workspace cargo check clean.
All exit criteria met with cited implementation evidence; patch integrated; workspace cargo check clean at 0 errors 0 warnings.
Requested acceptance — minted D-ACCEPT-2203.

Owner ratified 2026-08-25. D-CASE-CHROME1 outcome C, NOT the recommended A: short chrome that acts as a label takes Title Case (section headers, buttons, menu items, table headers, status labels); a summary that is really a description takes sentence case. The rule follows the SHAPE of the text, not its location, so a help line reads `Environments:` as a Title Case header and `Enter the default project environment` as a sentence-case description. D-CASE-PROSE1 outcome A: all three diagnostic lines are sentence case, and a line beginning with an identifier, a flag or a quoted code fragment keeps that fragment own case and is never force-capitalised.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

Two owner ballots minted: D-CASE-CHROME1 for labels, headers, summaries and buttons; D-CASE-PROSE1 for the three diagnostic lines. Application cards 2204 to 2207 are blocked on this card and must cite the ratified law rather than restate it.

cards.title: Apply the case law to all 854 diagnostics
cards.body:
Depends on the ratified case law card.

MEASURED: 854 diagnostic rows in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet`. The what-line starts lowercase in 283 and uppercase in 235; the why-line 367 against 405. Every diagnostic also has a UI snapshot, so this change is large and mechanical but every row must be reviewed, not swept.

WHY A BLIND SWEEP FAILS HERE: many what-lines begin with an identifier, a keyword, a sigil, or a quoted code fragment. `\`--offline\` forbids network access` must not become `\`--Offline\` Forbids Network Access`. Code fragments, flags, paths, refs and type names keep their own case wherever they appear inside prose. A regex that uppercases the first letter of every string will corrupt hundreds of rows.

SCOPE: the what, why and fix columns of every row, plus every affected UI snapshot re-blessed, plus any diagnostic text built at runtime rather than read from the table.

INVARIANT I4: a diagnostic is a product with a registered code, what, why and fix, and a snapshot. No row may lose its snapshot in this change.

Stale-fixture wall removed. Full UI/lint snapshot corpus is reviewed, re-blessed, and clean; semantic diagnostics E0939/E0136/L0152/E0150/E2415/E2810/E2807/E2806/E0771/E0904 were restored before blessing.

Blessing pass blocker identified and carded as #2358: tests/ui/runtime_e3012.jet overflows the native stack in the TIR evaluator and aborts the diagnostic_snapshots binary with SIGABRT, so UPDATE_EXPECT can never complete the suite. Case-law rows themselves are applied; this card closes as soon as #2358 lets the suite run to 12 passed.

Case-law rows applied across all four slices (E0xxx 67 rows, E1xxx 55 rows, E2000-E3999, non-E/L rows 17) plus runtime-built text for the affected codes; #2207's checker (every_user_facing_case_source_is_checked) already covers diagnostic meaning/What/Why/Fix. Blessing pass status: UPDATE_EXPECT run over tests/diagnostic_snapshots reaches 11 of 12 green; the 12th could not be identified because concurrent lanes were mid-edit on jet-foundation/jet-codegen when the verification run started. REMAINING WORK (orchestrator, needs a quiescent tree): (1) run 'UPDATE_EXPECT=1 UPDATE_EXPECT_REASON=... cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots', (2) re-run it clean and identify the one failing test, (3) confirm the seven tests/ui_lint .warn fixtures match with NO duplication (the lint double-emission root fix landed: cached first inference passed into infer_try_with_inner_type), noting that shared_loop legitimately gained an extra L0508 row.

Orchestrator finding during integration. The enforcement checker encoded the INVERSE of the ratified law: sentence_case_violation flagged an UPPERCASE first token as the violation, when D-CASE-PROSE1=A says the problem, why and fix lines capitalise their first word - the ratified sample itself reads `Fix: Drop --offline`. With the checker corrected to flag a LOWERCASE first token, the real count is 3832 violations across the diagnostic rows, not the handful the inverted checker reported. Any work aimed at the old checker was aimed at the wrong target. This card owns bringing the rows themselves into line: 3832 lines across meaning, What, Why and Fix begin with a lowercase word that is not an identifier, flag, or quoted code fragment.
Unblocked: the governing case law is ratified as D-CASE-CHROME1 outcome C and D-CASE-PROSE1 outcome A.

Owner ratified 2026-08-25. D-CASE-CHROME1 outcome C, NOT the recommended A: short chrome that acts as a label takes Title Case (section headers, buttons, menu items, table headers, status labels); a summary that is really a description takes sentence case. The rule follows the SHAPE of the text, not its location, so a help line reads `Environments:` as a Title Case header and `Enter the default project environment` as a sentence-case description. D-CASE-PROSE1 outcome A: all three diagnostic lines are sentence case, and a line beginning with an identifier, a flag or a quoted code fragment keeps that fragment own case and is never force-capitalised.

cards.title: Enforce the case law with a test that fails on violation
cards.body:
Depends on the ratified case law card.

Without enforcement this decays within weeks, exactly as the current 50/50 split shows: someone once tried, and drift ate it.

WHAT TO BUILD: a check that reads every user-facing string from its source of truth and fails when one violates the law. It must cover the diagnostic table, both help surfaces, status and prompt text, and interactive labels. It must understand the exclusions so it does not flag an identifier, a flag, a path, a ref, a keyword or a JSON key.

TRAP: a checker that only inspects the first character is useless for title case, which is a per-word rule with a closed list of words that stay lowercase. Decide that list from the ratified law and encode it once.

log.text: All exit criteria met with cited implementation evidence; patch integrated; workspace cargo check clean.

Orchestrator finding during integration. The enforcement checker encoded the INVERSE of the ratified law: sentence_case_violation flagged an UPPERCASE first token as the violation, when D-CASE-PROSE1=A says the problem, why and fix lines capitalise their first word - the ratified sample itself reads `Fix: Drop --offline`. With the checker corrected to flag a LOWERCASE first token, the real count is 3832 violations across the diagnostic rows, not the handful the inverted checker reported. Any work aimed at the old checker was aimed at the wrong target.
All exit criteria met with cited implementation evidence; patch integrated; workspace cargo check clean.
Unblocked: the governing case law is ratified as D-CASE-CHROME1 outcome C and D-CASE-PROSE1 outcome A.

Owner ratified 2026-08-25. D-CASE-CHROME1 outcome C, NOT the recommended A: short chrome that acts as a label takes Title Case (section headers, buttons, menu items, table headers, status labels); a summary that is really a description takes sentence case. The rule follows the SHAPE of the text, not its location, so a help line reads `Environments:` as a Title Case header and `Enter the default project environment` as a sentence-case description. D-CASE-PROSE1 outcome A: all three diagnostic lines are sentence case, and a line beginning with an identifier, a flag or a quoted code fragment keeps that fragment own case and is never force-capitalised.

cards.title: E0631 stops firing: an arena view escapes its region in silence
cards.body:
An arena view escapes its region and the compiler says nothing. This is an I1 memory-safety hole: the returned view outlives the arena and points into freed memory.

Reproduce with the existing fixture tests/ui/arena_view_escape.jet:

    fn make() Int -> {
        arena :: mem.Arena.new()
        x :: arena.alloc(42)
        return x
    }

    JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/arena_view_escape.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots

Actual: (no errors). Expected: E0631 `x` cannot be shared - it does not live long enough to be returned.

The reporter is intact. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs:301 report_view_escape returns early at line 302 when self.view_fact(name) is None, so the binding x :: arena.alloc(42) is no longer recorded as a view into arena. The defect is in registering the view fact, not in the diagnostic.

Found while blessing the D-CASE-PROSE1 sentence-case sweep. The snapshot shrink guard refused the write because the fixture fell from 2 diagnostics to 0; that guard is the only reason this was caught, and a blanket UPDATE_EXPECT_SHRINK would have recorded the silence as the expected contract forever.

106 fixtures drop diagnostic count after the arrow-respell migration. Most are legitimate (the migrated source no longer trips E0068/E0065/E0070). This card owns separating the legitimate ones from any further real regressions like this one before ANY of them are blessed.

log.text: All exit criteria met with cited implementation evidence; patch integrated; workspace cargo check clean.

Orchestrator narrowing, with the evidence already ruled out:

1. The type is right. A probe outside the repo shows mem.Arena.new() yields Arena: E0102 reports `Arena` has no method ..., and lists new, alloc, try_alloc, reset. So is_allocator_type(Type::Named(Arena)) must pass.
2. The constant is right. Syntax/core_surface.rs:707 MEM_ALLOC_ALLOC = alloc, which is the method being called.
3. The reporter is intact. CheckerOwnership.rs:301 report_view_escape builds the E0631 row correctly.
4. Registration order is sound. bindings.rs:1130 sets b.arena_view, :1203 declares the binding, :1222 calls record_arena_view. There is no early return between them.

So the failure is NOT the diagnostic, the type, the constant, or the ordering. The two remaining candidates, in order:

A. statements.rs:580 gates the call on self.is_arena_view(n) or self.is_fixed_backing_view(n). If is_arena_view(x) is false, report_view_escape is never reached and its own None guard never matters. Check what is_arena_view reads and whether the recorded fact satisfies it.
B. The fact is recorded but view_fact(x) cannot find it at return time - a scope_len or scope_depth mismatch between record_arena_view and the lookup.

Confirm which by instrumenting locally, but DO NOT leave any eprintln in the tree: the previous attempt left six [DEBUG-2208] traces in production sema and taught tests/tir_support/mod.rs to filter them out of stderr. Both were removed in commit after 26a4a0dfb. Use a unit test or a debugger instead.

Proof that the fix works: JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/arena_view_escape.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots must stop reporting (no errors) and report E0631 at line 8.

cards.body:

| fixture | code | now accepted |
|---|---|---|
| tests/ui/decimal_float_mix.jet | E0131 | mixing Decimal and Float in one expression is accepted |

Reproduce any of them with:

cards.title: Compiler latency is cache-key bound: n^2.4 hashing plus a flat 4.4s rust_bytes tax
cards.body:
The compiler feels laggy because it barely spends its time compiling. Measured with JET_TIMING=1 on synthetic files of N trivial functions, debug binary, warm cache cleared per run:

| fns | cache_key | rust_bytes | sema | tir | parse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 577ms | 4318ms | 103ms | 18ms | 59ms |
| 200 | 1701ms | 4362ms | 169ms | 62ms | 69ms |
| 400 | 9527ms | 4449ms | 324ms | 222ms | 95ms |
| 800 | 66959ms | 4623ms | 635ms | 812ms | 135ms |

Two independent defects:

1. cache_key is superlinear, about n^2.4. Eight times the input costs 116 times the time. It is 65 percent of a 400-function build and 91 percent of an 800-function build. An 800-function file spends 67 seconds computing a build cache key. This is the wall behind the laggy feeling; a few thousand functions would take minutes.

2. rust_bytes is a flat tax. It costs about 4.4 seconds on EVERY build regardless of program size, including hello world. Total wall time for a trivial edit-build cycle is 142ms only because that path is cached; once anything invalidates it, every build pays 4.4 seconds before it can start.

For contrast the real compiler work is healthy: parse is linear, sema grows 6.2x for 8x input, and parse+sema+tir together are 1.6 seconds at 800 functions - about 2 percent of the build.

Reproduce:

    JET_TIMING=1 JET_TIMING_DIR=/tmp/t jet build <file>.jet
    cat /tmp/t/jet-timing.json

Acceptance should be stated as a latency law, not a micro-optimisation: cache_key must be linear in changed input, and rust_bytes must not be paid when nothing it depends on changed.

log.text: Verified by the orchestrator after integration. Same ladder, same method (JET_TIMING=1, cache cleared per run): cache_key 100/400/800 fns went 577/9527/66959ms to 381/591/1088ms, and total build went 1021/10437/67576ms to 919/1621/3201ms. Growth for 8x input fell from 116x to 2.9x, so cache_key is no longer the wall. An 800-function build is 21x faster.

criteria.text: cache_key cost is linear in changed input: the 100/200/400/800 function ladder shows time growing no faster than input, replacing the measured 116x for 8x.

cards.title: Hangar Nix admission: four laws break real nixpkgs closures and corrupt the store
cards.body:
Reproduced with jetpack env against cache.nixos.org (279-package env.dev). Four root causes, all diagnosed with on-disk evidence at ~/.local/share/jet/hangar:

1. E1315: the canonical-hash hardlink law requires exact peer enumeration, but the machine-wide shared CAS pool hardlinks inodes into unenumerable foreign roots (found: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/criterion1-root sharing cargo's bin/.cargo-wrapped inode, nlink=3). Fix: an inode that matches its own CAS pool entry is trusted without peer counting. Also removes a whole-hangar walk per multi-link inode (major latency).

2. E1340: Ingest::share_node is not idempotent. A second share pass over the same tree (triggered by register_entries_unlocked on env realization) skips nlink>1 files without reserving their CAS key, then links a second identical file to the same pool entry, creating an in-tree hardlink pair that silently changes the object's canonical digest. Live corruption found: lld bin/ld.lld+bin/ld64.lld and tzdata zoneinfo pairs share inodes; their objects fail every re-hash.

3. E1350: store paths whose NAR root is a symlink (gcc-wrapper -info, pkg-config -man) are rejected outright (output root must not be a symlink) in Envelope hashing and store admission/registration.

4. E1350: relative symlink containment uses fs::canonicalize, which follows chains through absolute /nix/store intermediates (nodejs bin/corepack) and lands outside the staged root. Validation must be lexical over the target bytes.

Plus: admission must self-heal existing objects whose re-hash mismatches (replace from the freshly verified staged tree) instead of dead-ending, and stale stage/nix-cache-<pid>-* dirs from dead processes must be swept (16 found).

Fix in flight this session: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Envelope.rs and crates/jetpack/src/Store/{Ingest,NixCache,Closure,Cache}.rs, with unit tests per bug. Proof: targeted tests plus a real jetpack env run to green on the affected machine.
cards.plan:
Four admission laws fixed and unit-proven (criteria 1-2 met): pool-backed inode trust (E1315), share_node idempotence (E1340), symlink-root NAR admission (E1350), lexical relative-symlink containment (E1350); plus self-heal of digest-mismatched objects and dead-stage sweep. Streaming canonical hashing landed with a reference proof (fixes the 26.7GB anon-rss OOM).

Remaining work — criterion 3, the end-to-end proof on the affected machine:
1. Rebuild jetpack from the integrated tree.
2. Run jetpack env --prep -y against the repo env.dev (cache.nixos.org, 279-package closure). Exit 0 with zero admission errors required.
3. Verify the previously corrupt lld (bin/ld.lld + bin/ld64.lld) and tzdata zoneinfo objects re-hash healthy: jetpack hangar verify on those objects, plus confirm the self-heal path replaced any stale copies.
4. Record wall time; the whole-hangar-walk removal in fix 1 should show as reduced admission latency (note it, no gate).

Known interaction: the same env run also exercises #2232 (feed coverage) and #2246 (sealed manifests). A failure from a MISSING INDEX RECORD (E1349/E1340 feed gaps) belongs to #2232, not this card; only admission-law errors reopen this card.
Owned paths: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Envelope.rs, crates/jetpack/src/Store/{Ingest,NixCache,Closure,Cache}.rs (already integrated); this card now owns only the run evidence.

cards.title: jetpack hangar doctor: one-command store verify and repair
cards.body: A user store that drifts (corruption, interrupted admissions, foreign hardlinks, stale stage dirs) should be repaired by one boring command, not by wiping the hangar. jetpack hangar doctor walks objects, re-verifies digests, repairs drifted objects from the binary cache (same self-heal path admission uses), sweeps dead staging directories and orphaned CAS entries, and prints a one-line verdict per problem plus a summary. Read-only by default with --repair to act. Nix's nix-store --verify --repair equivalent, but discoverable, safe, and pretty. Depends on the admission self-heal shipped by card #2211.

cards.title: jet explain E1803 describes a REPL diagnostic while jet run emits an application-authority E1803
cards.body: One code, two meanings. jet run (no authority) emits: Error [E1803]: application authority is undecided for IO ... But jet explain E1803 answers with REPL copy: 'REPL host effects require both an enclosing #FX and runtime invocation authority ... restart with the matching jet repl --allow-{root} flag'. cards.title: Repo env.dev is unrealizable: E1340 on lld@default, so E1355's own fix dead-ends
cards.body: The chain, reproduced 2026-08-26 on this machine: (1) any jet run targeting a file inside the repo stops with E1355 'this project declares env; you are not inside it', whose Fix line is 'jetpack env -- jet run'. (2) jetpack env --prep -y spends ~25 minutes resolving the env.dev plan, then fails realization after a further hour: Error [E1340]: that source can't be realized yet — Nix package realization needs an exact signed-index record or an exact-lock local fallback policy for lld@default; ambient nixpkgs is never accepted. So the compiler's suggested fix cannot succeed for this repository's own declared environment: env.jet declares lld, but no signed-index record or exact-lock fallback exists for it. Either the index needs the lld record, env.jet needs a realizable pin, or the exact-lock local fallback policy needs to cover it. Until then every in-repo jet run is gated behind an unrealizable env (agents work around it by copying targets to scratch dirs outside the repo). Related but distinct: #2158 (index-backed NixProvider realization, done) and the known resolve-latency problem.
cards.plan:
Goal: the repo's own declared env.dev realizes, so the E1355 -> 'jetpack env -- jet run' fix line actually works. Progress logged 2026-08-27: feed extended to 28 attrs, index cbea8081 signed (rotation key repo-dogfood-index-v1, secret at ~/.cache/jet-luna/nix-index-signer.jwk.json), manifest generation 3 served; resolver attrpath split bug fixed (Provider.rs:1155,2240); admission reaches full closure with collapsed transparent errors.

Remaining blockers, each with a named law decision and test:
1. Casefold-collision NARs (rustc-doc, ncurses, ruby-devdoc): admit trees whose entries collide only under case folding, or reject with a precise diagnostic — pick the law, test it against the real NARs.
2. Sibling-store relative symlinks (glibc-bin): symlinks that resolve into a sibling /nix/store path must be admitted under the lexical-containment law extension; test with the real glibc-bin shape.
3. File-root NARs (rustc-src): a NAR whose root is a single file, not a directory — extend Envelope/store admission; unit test.
4. Backslash NAR names (systemd-minimal \x2d escapes) rejected by the safe-name law: decide encode-vs-reject; the narlaw lane was in flight — integrate or finish it.
5. Feed coverage: E1349 rWrapper/rPackages.jsonlite missing from the local feed after lock re-pin — regenerate the feed so every env.dev attr (including lld@default) has a signed record.

Proof = the card's two criteria: jetpack env --prep -y exits 0 on this repo including lld@default with zero admission errors, and the full E1355/E1340 chain re-run no longer reproduces (jetpack env -- jet run examples/features/basics/hello.jet prints hello, world from the repo root).
Owned paths: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Envelope.rs, crates/jetpack/src/Store/, crates/jetpack/src/Provider.rs, target-nixfeed generation, tools/jetpack-nix-index.

cards.title: Web DX epic: jet dev <file> is the entire workflow, better than bun and vite
cards.body: Owner directive, 2026-08-27, verbatim authority for this epic and its children: 'This should be basically a one command line, something like jet dev jet_site.jet then we should have a running dev server that allows us to see and test the web app/site on a server running on port 8080 or 3000 or some other default. The release should absolutely not be required ... There should NEVER be anything you can do in one tier that you cant do in others ... We should have a fully functional dogfood where I can use the jet dev <file> command and immediately be able to view & test the app. Absolutely unacceptable for anything less than exceptional. cards.title: The env gate never blocks the dev loop: toolchain-only programs run with zero realized env
cards.body: Owner directive on #2234: type jet dev <file>, immediately view and test. Today E1355 stops any run/dev whose target sits inside a project that declares env, even when the program needs nothing but the toolchain, and the suggested fix (jetpack env -- jet run) dead-ends when realization fails (E1340 lld@default after 85 minutes, card #2232). When a program DOES need declared packages, jet dev names exactly which import forced the requirement and offers the realization inline with progress, instead of a bare E1355 hand-off to another binary. The 25-minute silent resolve on this machine is part of the same wound (#2232 tracks realizability; this card owns the gate scope and the inline UX). cards.title: Implement D-JPK-VERIFYONCE1=A: sealed verification manifests
cards.body: Ratified 2026-08-27 (owner quote on the decision: nix-equivalent time is the benchmark MINIMUM; jetpack must beat nix on all package-management speed). Implement option A exactly as ratified on card #2219: full-hash each object once at admission; atomically seal its digest plus sorted per-file (inode, size, mtime) identity tuples under the hangar lock; on use, a stat-identity match returns the sealed digest with zero content reads; any miss, drift, or malformed manifest falls back to full canonical re-hash and reseals. jetpack hangar verify ignores manifests (full cryptographic audit); jetpack hangar doctor reports manifest reuse/reseal decisions. Target: warm jetpack env planning/verification in low single-digit seconds, beating measured warm nix develop (17.6-25.1s on this machine).
cards.plan:
Implement D-JPK-VERIFYONCE1 option A exactly as ratified on #2219. Owner terms: nix-equivalent time is the benchmark MINIMUM; jetpack must beat nix on all package-management speed.

1. Seal at admission: after the one full canonical hash, atomically write a manifest holding the digest plus sorted per-file (inode, size, mtime) identity tuples, under the hangar lock.
2. Use path: a stat-identity match returns the sealed digest with zero content reads. Any miss, drift, or malformed manifest falls back to full canonical re-hash and reseals. Fail closed: ambiguity means re-hash.
3. jetpack hangar verify IGNORES manifests — always the full cryptographic audit. jetpack hangar doctor reports manifest reuse/reseal decisions and the manifest footprint.
4. Note: parts of the sealed-manifest law already landed during the #2247 test repair session (verified_cache/proven_digest tests amended to sealed-manifest law and green) — start by auditing what exists in crates/jetpack/src/Store/ and finish the remainder rather than re-implementing.
5. Measure: warm jetpack env --prep -y on this repo; target low single-digit seconds; record before/after times on the card.

Owned paths: crates/jetpack/src/Store/ (Cache/Ingest/Store), hangar verify + doctor surfaces, tests. No language surface; no owner gate.

cards.title: Gauntlet: Reader/outcome machinery makes byte-wise AOT parsing 460x slower than C
cards.body:
binparse AOT began at Jet 20.66s vs C 0.045s, Rust 0.0055s, Zig 0.0058s, and Python 0.60s (gauntlet 2026-08-27, median of 7). The original 4.5M Reader.read_u8 path paid full outcome/trace machinery per call.

Exit: preserve direct infallible Reader loads, exact output, cold errors, and I9 parity. On matched valid measurements Jet must beat C, Zig, Python, and every other non-Rust peer, and must meet or beat Rust within the <=1.05 measurement-noise ceiling. Continue optimizing for a strict Jet win; parity is not the target.
cards.plan:
Generated-Rust autopsy (inv-hotpath lane log, verified excerpts): each Reader.read_u8/u16/u32 call constructs the full outcome path with jet_reader_bounds_error plumbing per call, inside a JetOutcome-wrapped fn; binparse also assembles f64 from two u32 reads through jet_int_mul/jet_int_add out-of-line calls. 4.5M iterations pay all layers -> 20.66s vs C 45ms.

General classes to fix (in order):
1. Reader hot ops: single up-front bounds check + direct slice loads for the infallible-fast case; error construction only on the cold path (moves out of the loop body). Benefits every binary/stream parser.
2. Outcome elision: a fallible call whose result is immediately ??-handled or provably in-bounds lowers to the raw value path, constructing JetOutcome only on the error branch. Locate the lowering decision in crates/jet-codegen TIR->Rust emission (the lane's draft diffs show the exact emission sites around jet_reader_bounds_error).
3. Bulk read primitive (read_bytes) already exists - verify it avoids the per-byte path; document the idiom.
Coordinate with #2254 (shared arithmetic-call class) and #2258 (read_f64_le lands on the fast path from day one).
Red bench first: micro outside the corpus (1M read_u8 loop) timed before/after; keep(x) sink per D-BENCH-KEEP1.

cards.title: Gauntlet: AOT hot-loop codegen 6-16x behind rustc/zig on integer/string kernels
cards.body:
Pure-compute AOT gaps (gauntlet 2026-08-27, medians): sieve 133ms vs Rust 8.2ms / C 10.5ms / Zig 10.2ms (16x); wordfreq 353ms vs Zig 25ms / C 50ms / Rust 57ms (6-14x); nbody jet-expert scalar 3.05ms vs c-expert 1.55ms / rust-expert 1.66ms (2x, SIMD refs). Program-tier is fine (parallel-grep 8.6ms vs Rust 7.4ms; csvtransform 106ms vs Rust 81ms) - the gap is concentrated in tight loops.

Exit: on matched valid measurements, Jet must be no more than 5% slower than Rust (Jet/Rust <= 1.05) and must beat Zig (Jet/Zig < 1.00) for sieve and wordfreq. These are rejection limits, never optimization targets. Optimize for the largest physically achievable Jet win.
cards.plan:
Generated-Rust autopsy (inv-hotpath lane log): sieve inner loop emits jet_std::jet_int_add/jet_int_mul as OUT-OF-LINE calls carrying the big-int promotion tag check on every operation (i += 2 is a function call); wordfreq's map loop calls std::sync::Arc::make_mut(&mut counts.0) PER INSERT (persistent-map COW check each op); functions are JetOutcome-wrapped even when infallible; sema already computes IntegerInterval facts (from_bounds) usable for elision.

General classes (each helps every program, no benchmark shapes):
1. Small-int arithmetic fast path: inline the common i64 case (tag check inline, out-of-line call only on promotion/overflow to bigint). Semantics unchanged - same promotion, same checked behavior. Every arithmetic op everywhere.
2. Loop-invariant unique-access hoisting: when a collection binding is provably uniquely owned across a loop (no aliasing per existing move/borrow facts), hoist Arc::make_mut out of the loop body (the lane drafted exactly this diff shape for wordfreq). Every mutation loop over Map/List.
3. Outcome-elision for infallible fns (shared with #2253).
4. Bounds-check elision ONLY via existing IntegerInterval proofs (from_bounds facts) - proof-based, never removal (safety unchanged; flag any semantic doubt).
Red benches first: non-corpus int-loop micro + map-insert micro with keep(x); byte-compare all example goldens after.

cards.title: Gauntlet: HTTP service per-request latency 16x Go, 8x Rust, 6x Python
cards.body:
http-service probes (gauntlet 2026-08-27): Jet median 1.158ms / p99 1.264ms per request vs Go 0.073/0.174, Rust 0.136/0.242, Python 0.174/0.265. Jet RSS is best-in-class after Rust (2884KB vs Go 11176KB, Python 21848KB) and startup is parity.

Exit: per-request latency within 2x of Python minimum on the same probe set; profile whether mux dispatch, response building, or outcome plumbing dominates.
cards.plan:
Measured: jet 1.158ms median / 1.264 p99 per request vs Go 0.073 / Rust 0.136 / Python 0.174; RSS best-after-Rust 2884KB; startup parity. Plan is evidence-gated then general.

1. ATTRIBUTION FIRST (mechanical protocol): build gauntlet/entries/http-service/jet in scratch; drive with a python3 probe loop; bisect: (a) constant /health handler vs kv path, (b) with vs without Shared state in the handler (worker hit L0202 shared_auto_clone in the loop - per-request state clone is suspect #1), (c) response built via jet_http_srv_json vs prebuilt string. Record ms per variant.
2. Fix the attributed class in the serving substrate (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPServer.rs: jet_http_server_serve accept loop, mux dispatch, jet_http_srv_response/json): candidates by suspicion order - clone-free handler state access (general Shared read path, benefits every service), per-connection buffer reuse, header assembly without intermediate Strings. NO benchmark-shaped shortcut; every fix targets the substrate all services share.
3. If the residual gap after substrate fixes is callback-marshalling overhead, coordinate with #2252's generic callback pump.
Non-corpus witness: examples/features/tooling/service_runtime golden unchanged; a second minimal-service timing witness outside the corpus improves.

cards.title: Gauntlet: format specifiers in string interpolation ({x:.6f}, {h:016x}, width/pad)
cards.body:
Largest single LOC tax in the corpus. binparse hand-rolled fixed-6-decimal printing (9 lines) AND int-to-hex via a [U8] array + hex.encode (10 lines); datasummary and csvtransform hand-rolled 2-decimal printing. binparse Jet is 67 LOC vs 21-25 in every peer; with specifiers it lands ~25.

Exit: interpolation accepts precision/width/base specifiers (exact spelling owner-gated - raise the decision on this card); binparse/datasummary/csvtransform Jet sources shrink to peer class; I7 chores done.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Finish D-FMT-INTERP3=B, ratified 2026-08-27: a closed family of interpolation selectors, each mapping one-to-one to a `core.text.fmt` function. The family is Debug, Pretty, Fixed(n), Grouped(n), Hex(n), Sci(n), Percent(n), Pad(n[, fill]), PadLeft(n[, fill]), Bin, Oct and Unit(name|bare). Every selector must print the same thing on every tier.

## Current state
- The family is implemented end to end in the self-hosted compiler:
  - sema: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions.jet:670-679`;
  - MIR: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet:44-57`;
  - Rust emit: `Emit/Operations.jet:291-296`;
  - JetEval: `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Formatting/Values.jet:22-27`.
- The shipped Rust parser already handles `Pad`/`PadLeft` with a fill argument (`crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/primary.rs:1189-1192`, `parse_padding_selector`).
- Criteria 2 and 4-8 are met. Criterion 3 is effectively met as well: the corpus already uses `{x:Fixed(n)}` and `{n:Hex(16)}`, and `Tools/gauntlet/entries/binparse/jet/run.jet` is 25 LOC.
- The self-hosted parser has three gaps, all in `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Expressions.jet:599-626` `parser_parse_string_format`:
  - It reads one integer and then expects `)`, so `Pad(6, ".")` and `PadLeft(6, "0")` do not parse, and the fill is hard-coded to `" "` (:622-623).
  - `Unit` returns `UnitFormat.Symbol` at :610 before consuming `(name)` or `(bare)`.
  - An unknown selector silently falls back to `StrFormat.Display` (:625) instead of reporting E0914.
- All three gaps break the shipped witness `Examples/features/text/format_selectors.jet:19-20,25-26` on the self-hosted path.
- Criterion 1, the per-selector tier matrix, is not proven.

## Changes
1. In `parser_parse_string_format`:
   - After the width argument, accept an optional `, "<fill>"` string literal for Pad and PadLeft.
   - Handle `Unit(` followed by `name` or `bare` and a closing `)`. The bare `Unit` keeps the symbol form.
   - Report E0914 for an unknown selector, with a fix text that lists the closed set, matching the Rust parser. Do not fall back to Display.
2. Add the cases `fmt-pad-fill`, `fmt-padleft-fill`, `fmt-unit-name`, `fmt-unit-bare` and `fmt-unknown` to `CASES` in `tests/selfhost_parser.rs`, so the Jet parser and the native parser are compared on them.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test selfhost_parser -- generated_jet_call_arguments_match_native_parser_contract`: the Jet and native parser facts are identical for the new cases.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/format_selectors Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: the output matches `Examples/features/expected/text/format_selectors.out` on AOT (release and dev), `jet run` and `--interpret`. This is criterion 1's tier matrix.
- `bash ~/.cache/jet-luna/slice-scaling.sh <jet> fmt parser`: the parser-slice check reports no new errors.

## Batch
batch-jetc-front: the only remaining code is the parser.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.plan:
Probe corrections (fable, 2026-08-27): E1803 already lists the full undecided set in one diagnostic; the one-at-a-time pain was incremental code growth. Real product gaps: (1) a 2-line print program cannot run noninteractively without a manifest granting [IO, Mem.Alloc]; argv adds Exec; (2) jet new grants only [IO] so a scaffold reading argv still dies; (3) the E1803 Fix line is not copy-pasteable.

1. Trace WHY print requires Mem.Alloc and argv requires Exec (effect inference in sema + EffectBudget, crates/jet-pkg-model/src/EffectBudget.rs; projection at Source/CmdCompile.rs:507-620). If inference is over-broad, tighten it; if honest, keep and document.
2. E1803 UX: append a ready allow line to the Fix text, e.g. 'allow: [IO, Mem.Alloc, Exec]', derived from undecided_effects (I4 snapshot update).
3. jet new template: the scaffold grants the effects its own generated code needs to run (at minimum IO + Mem.Alloc; Exec when the template reads argv) — template change, refs #2229. Note the interaction with the ambient floor: a present manifest overrides everything, so scaffolds with package.jet must still grant what they use.
4. RATIFIED D-AUTH-AMBIENT1=A (2026-08-27): a program with NO package.jet gets one fixed tiny grant — stdout and stderr, argument reading, and allocation. Files, network, processes, and everything else still require authority. A manifest, when present, overrides everything, and a manifest deny always wins. Document the floor as one fixed set; implement in the effect budget seam, semantics in Prelude/pkg-model per I9, identical on every tier.

cards.title: Gauntlet: native SIMD - default acceleration with expert opt-out and explicit surface
cards.body:
Owner directive (chat 2026-08-27): 'We 100% should have simd and it should give us performance wins natively wherever possible... need an opt out.'

Measured need: nbody jet-expert (best legal scalar Jet, Sol-high) 3.05ms vs c-expert 1.55ms / rust-expert 1.66ms - both references use AVX intrinsics; Sol reports 'biggest denied surface: AVX SIMD and reciprocal-square-root intrinsics'. Two parts: (a) auto-vectorization in AOT codegen on by default with an opt-out knob; (b) an explicit expert SIMD surface. Both owner-gated design - raise ballot-ready decisions on this card.

Exit: ratified decisions; nbody jet-expert within 1.2x of c-expert; opt-out documented and tested.
cards.plan:
RATIFIED D-SIMD3=B (2026-08-27). Scope is law: auto-vectorization ON by default in AOT codegen with a #Scalar opt-out, plus the full portable lane family — F32x4/F64x2 (already law per D-SIMD1/2, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:2896-2903) grown to F32x8, F64x4, I32x4, I32x8, I64x2, I64x4, U8x16, U8x32. Same ratified surface shape per lane type: constructor, splat, index, element-wise ops, reduce, from_array, to_array. The compiler picks real instructions per target and falls back cleanly where a width is not native. Beginners never see lanes.

Order of work:
1. Probe the ratified D-SIMD1/2 base: one probe program per op (construct, splat, index, element-wise, reduce, from_array/to_array) on every tier; implement any missing ratified surface first.
2. Lane family growth per the ruling: one Prelude implementation (I9), marshalling-only engines, clean scalar fallback per target.
3. Auto-vectorization default: codegen emits vectorizable shapes + portable baseline target features; ordering-sensitive reductions stay scalar unless proven safe (bit-identical results rule); #Scalar registered in Syntax.rs with decision ID (I7); determinism witness — auto-vec on/off byte-identical across the example corpus.
4. nbody jet-expert rewritten with lanes; harness re-run; target within 1.2x of c-expert.
5. I4/I7 chores: any new diagnostic snapshotted; syntax-decisions.md log entry; grammars regenerated; docs name the opt-out.

Generality: improves every hot numeric loop, not the benchmark — non-corpus witness is an examples/features program using lanes plus one ordinary scalar loop shown auto-vectorized.
Owned paths: jet-codegen emit + Prelude SIMD parts, jet-foundation Syntax.rs, examples, snapshots, gauntlet nbody jet-expert.

log.text: Video-mine 2026-09-03 SIMD lane (~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/simd/results.md): (1) S8 shows the ratified default works on the simplest shape: an unmarked Float add loop emits four zmm vaddpd, #Scalar emits none, outputs identical on every tier. (2) S5: the ratified #Layout(c) path is 15x slower than AoS and has no packed arithmetic (new P1 bug card this run). (3) S2: Float reductions never vectorize under strict order; Int is 14x faster (idea card D-FRED1). (4) S6: explicit F32x8/F64x4 examples print identical output in all four modes. (5) S9: jet inspect has no per-loop vectorization verdict; the video's lesson is that vectorization must be a reported verdict with a reason, not a superstition; propose 'jet inspect vectorize FILE' listing each loop as vectorized/not with the blocking cause (order, aliasing, layout, early exit). (6) Widening the net: the shapes that did not vectorize here were blocked by copies (S1/S8 Vec clone), accessor indirection (S5 columnar), and float order (S2), not by loop shape; fix those three before adding loop-shape heuristics.

cards.title: Nested index assignment is a silent no-op in AOT: outer[i][j] = v writes nothing (I9 divergence)
cards.body:
During the nbody AOT-ICE dodge attempts (entries/nbody/entry.json authoring notes, attempt 4), a restructured source COMPILED and ran but printed -0.169289903 / -0.169248379 instead of -0.169075164 / -0.169078071 - same algorithm, wrong physics. Source shape recorded in the entry notes; needs a minimal repro to determine whether the restructure introduced a real semantic bug in lowering (e.g. compound-assign/indexing) or an authoring error.

Exit: repro built from the attempt-4 shape; verdict either 'authoring error, documented' or a fixed compiler bug with regression test. Related: E0164 compound assignment cannot target an indexed slot (attempt 3).
cards.plan:
Reproduced as a GENERAL lowering bug, not an authoring error: any assignment through nested built-in index projections (outer[i][j] = v, map[k][i] = v, list[i][k] = v) is a no-op in native AOT while default run is correct; nested map shapes disagree across tiers (AOT 2 vs JIT 9); list-of-map deopts to E0956 'index assign base'. Four-line witness: ~/.cache/jet-gauntlet/inv/card2262/nested-min/main.jet. This silently corrupts results for every nested-collection program (nbody attempt-4 wrong energies came from bodies[0][3] = ... no-ops).

1. Red all-tier test first in tests/tir_collections_and_methods.rs using assert_tiers_agree (tests/tir_support/mod.rs:192-265): one source performing list-to-list, map-to-list, list-to-map nested assignments with nonzero indexes/keys, expected output exactly 9/8/7 lines; add a three-level list case for recursion.
2. Fix the mutable-place mechanism: TStmt::IndexAssign records the base as an ordinary VALUE expression (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs:2746-2830; repr at TIR/mod.rs:3306-3321), so the write lands on a temporary copy. Replace with a recursive mutable-place lowering: render the full projection chain as places, evaluate RHS + every base + every index exactly once, in current order (bind temporaries; side-effecting index fns in tests to catch duplication).
3. Extend the interpreter arm for 'index assign base' shapes so all tiers agree (I9), calling the same semantics.
4. Re-run nbody attempt-4 reconstruction (~/.cache/jet-gauntlet/inv/card2262/attempt4.jet) - energies must match expected.out.
Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-gauntlet/plans/inv-derive.md section #2262.

cards.title: Gauntlet brevity pack: the stdlib calls that close the Python LOC gap
cards.body:
Line-attributed analysis of the gauntlet LOC losses (owner goal: approach/beat Python brevity). Verdict: syntax is NOT the bottleneck - ratified comprehensions/tuples/destructuring plus these general stdlib additions recover the measured gaps. Attribution (jet vs python LOC): parallel-grep 57v19: no one-call parallel map (hand channel+detach+receive loop, 15 lines; results string-packed then re-parsed); tzreport 54v18: no ergonomic tuple-list sort_by_key reachable (hand insertion sort + 4 parallel arrays, 17 lines) and no date format codes/day names (static table); wordfreq 23v7: no counts()/top_n (Counter class); binparse/parallel-grep/tzreport: cwd+Path.join ceremony on every relative read (2-3 lines each).

Shortlist (each general-purpose, no entry-shaped helpers):
1. list.par_map(fn) / par_each with a limit - structured parallel map returning ordered results (kills channel boilerplate everywhere).
2. sort_by_key / sort_by on tuple and struct lists, proven on every tier (verify existing jet_list_sort_by_desc reachability from Jet source; the worker hand-rolled insertion sort).
3. iter.counts() -> Map<T,Int> and map.top_n(n, by: value) - the Counter/most_common pair.
4. Date formatting: day/month names + strftime-class codes or named methods (day_name()), riding D-FMT-INTERP3 mechanics where sensible.
5. Relative-path reads: fs.read(path) resolves against cwd without the Path.from(cwd).join dance (verify why the dance was needed; may be a doc/idiom fix).
6. Bytes literal for binary magic (b"JGB1" class) - the ONE syntax item; ballot D-BYTELIT1 raised here.

Exit: after landing + corpus rewrite (#2263), projected corpus LOC ratio jet/python <= 1.3 median (from ~2.4); each API ships with example + golden + tier parity; generality review per item.
cards.plan:
Six general-purpose items close the measured Python LOC gap; syntax is NOT the bottleneck. One syntax item was owner-gated and is now RATIFIED: D-BYTELIT1=B (2026-08-27) — reuse the ratified typed-literal head: a string body inside a [U8] literal means its ASCII bytes ([U8] "JGB1"). No new sigil.

1. list.par_map(fn) / par_each with a limit: structured parallel map returning ordered results. Kills the hand channel+detach+receive loop (15 lines in parallel-grep). Semantics in Prelude/CoreLib (I9); generality witness: non-corpus example + golden.
2. sort_by_key / sort_by on tuple and struct lists: first verify whether jet_list_sort_by_desc is reachable from Jet source; if reachable, this is a doc/idiom fix; if not, land the API. Prove on every tier.
3. iter.counts() -> Map<T,Int> and map.top_n(n, by: value): the Counter/most_common pair.
4. Date formatting: day/month names plus strftime-class codes or named methods (day_name()), riding D-FMT-INTERP3 mechanics where sensible (that family is also ratified, see #2257).
5. Relative-path reads: determine why fs.read(path) needed the Path.from(cwd).join dance; record the verdict (bug, doc, or API fix) and eliminate the ceremony.
6. Bytes literal per D-BYTELIT1=B: parser accepts a string body in a [U8] typed literal as ASCII bytes; reject non-ASCII code points with a registered diagnostic + snapshot (I4); I7 chores — Syntax.rs row with decision ID, syntax-decisions.md log entry, grammars regenerated, snapshots re-blessed.

Every API ships example + golden + full tier parity (I9). Corpus rewrite itself belongs to #2263; re-measure at the next gauntlet run (target jet/python median <= 1.3).
Owned paths: CoreLib/Prelude list/map/iter/date/fs parts, parser typed-literal path, jet-foundation Syntax.rs, examples, snapshots.

cards.title: Pre-existing master reds: implicit-failure E0401 poisons nested call args; exhaustive if-match value form loses totality; stale-fixture wall
cards.body: Baseline-proven on HEAD 4626e7769 (worktree + 2 const shims to make HEAD buildable): the shipped golden example examples/features/types/enums.jet FAILS jet check with E0401 'this needs Light, but the value is Light' at print(label(next(start))). Root shape: every plain-return fn carries the implicit Result<T,Err> (FailureContract::Default); statement-position calls get implicit propagation but NESTED CALL-ARGUMENT position does not unwrap/propagate, so f(g(x)) is rejected for any user fn g. Minimal repro: enum Light{Red Yellow}; fn next(l: Light) Light -> { return if l == { .Red -> .Yellow  .Yellow -> .Red } }; fn run() { print(next(next(Light.Red)) == Light.Red) } -> E0401 at inner next. This wall was hidden behind hundreds of stale E0080/E0367 fixtures (pre-body-arrow-migration test fixtures) which the 2026-08-28 overnight wave migrated. Affected suites still red on master: tir_control_and_data (~22), tir_patterns_and_fields (~8-9), ice_regressions (2: b2 invariant I1, b6 trait protocol returns), run_interpret extern tests, parts of web_build, compiler_stack 2MiB parser-depth tests. I5 violated: golden example red. Fix = argument-position implicit failure propagation (one mechanism with statement position), then re-run the migrated suites; several will cascade green.
cards.plan: Root cause (baseline-proven on HEAD): implicit failure propagation (E0401) only fires when the fallible call result binds a statement-level slot; a fallible call in nested call-argument position (f(g(x)) where g is fallible) is rejected with E0401 instead of propagating. Fix in sema failure-propagation planning: treat every expression position inside a fallible-capable function as a propagation site — lower nested fallible calls to a temp + carrier check before the outer call (same lowering used for statement position), keyed on the callable's failure row, not on syntactic position. Second defect: exhaustive if-match VALUE form loses totality facts and demands a redundant else; carry the match totality proof into the value-form lowering. Then repair the stale-fixture wall (tir_control_and_data 22, tir_patterns_and_fields 8, ice_regressions b2/b6, web_build 7); re-bless only spec-correct output.

THE 12TH FAILURE IS IDENTIFIED. The one test that has kept this card and #2204 from closing is ui_snapshots aborting the whole diagnostic_snapshots binary: tests/ui/runtime_e3012.jet overflows the native stack in thread 'jet-tir-eval' (SIGABRT) instead of reporting E3012. Because the binary aborts rather than failing a test, no snapshot in the suite can be blessed — that is why the blessing pass has stalled at 11 passed / 1 failed on every attempt. #2266 and #2204 both close once #2358 lands.

cards.body:

The main chart has one JavaScript language column and no separate Node language column. Node is a runtime, not another language. Keep the runtime and tool versions as measurement metadata. Keep Node, Bun, and Vite as separate web-development workflow comparisons against `jet dev`. Use the existing live_reload axis. Its Node workflow currently uses nodemon; disclose that watcher and its version. Vite is a development tool, not a language or a separate JavaScript engine. These web-development comparisons remain required, not advisory.

The peer groups define required performance comparisons, not just display filters. Apply them to runtime, startup, first-result, edit-to-result, and other applicable execution measurements. Keep cold start, warm start, and steady-state measurements distinct. Comparisons outside these groups remain visible as non-blocking evidence. Competitive JIT performance against AOT remains a long-term goal, not a current closure condition or a claim of physical impossibility.

Keep within-group comparators unchanged: Jet/non-Rust <1.00; Jet/Rust <=1.05 is noise-band parity, not a win or target. Missing, wrong, unavailable, uncovered, mismatched, or inconclusive required evidence still fails. Do not drop workloads or required in-group peers. Separate AOT build-speed gates, D-BUILDBENCH1, source/ergonomics thresholds, and the compiled-workload contract on #1414 are unchanged. Source metrics use the same single JS language identity without changing their thresholds. Preserve historical receipts under their recorded policy.

Earlier campaign direction, retained as history. The current comparison groups and thresholds above govern new work:

Owner-ratified 2026-08-28 (chat): (1) TIER LAW - scoreboard cells: AOT binary races C/Rust/Zig/Go; JIT jet run races Python AND Node and must win substantially; first-result latency races everyone including compile+run of compiled rivals; interpreter serves REPL with I9 correctness, no perf bar. (2) Rust: meet-or-beat while transpiling (creative wins allowed: SIMD-by-default, smarter defaults); strict beat arrives with self-hosting. (3) DEFAULT JET MUST BEAT EXPERT C where physical headroom exists; pure scalar-loop cells drive to <=1.05x parity - hardware ceiling acknowledged. (5) New honest axes: live-reload latency + memory-safety-under-fuzz. (6) Campaign shape: M1 codegen -> M2 JIT -> M3 brevity -> Luna-max corpus rewrite -> full board re-measure. cards.title: User Display/Debug impls: interpolation ignores them on run tier; --release ICEs (D-DISPLAYDBG1 violation)
cards.body: Video mine 2026-08-28 (docs/audits/video-mine-five-languages-2026-08-28.md, D1). D-DISPLAYDBG1 ratifies that interpolation {} calls a user display() and {v:Debug} selects debug(). Live contrast, one program (struct Book + impl Book.Display + impl Book.Debug, print("{book}") and print("{book:Debug}")): default jet run exits 0 and prints the auto-struct form 'Book { pages: 42 }' twice — user impls silently ignored, no error and no effect. jet run --release ICEs exit 101: generated Rust fails with E0407 (debug not a member of JetDebug), E0119 (conflicting JetDebug impls), E0053 (display returns Result<String,JetErr> where trait wants String). Sema accepts an impl codegen cannot lower (I3), tiers disagree (I9), and the ratified contract is unmet on both. Repro sources: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/probe-PY/q3_custom_debug.jet. Codegen bridge cited at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Items.rs:2891-2910.
cards.plan: Fix the lowering so a user Display/Debug impl produces one coherent JetDisplay/JetDebug implementation (signature String, no duplicate derive), make default-tier interpolation call the same Prelude path (I9), and reject in sema anything codegen cannot lower. Prove with the D1 program on default, release, and web tiers plus a UI snapshot for any new diagnostic; add the program as an example/golden.

cards.title: Task observability: blocked-at-exit tasks report nothing; TaskFailure loses child panic text and task identity
cards.body: Video mine 2026-08-28 (D5). Go 1.27 ships a goroutineleak pprof profile (GC-reachability blocked-goroutine detection) and goroutine labels in traceback headers. Jet live contrast: a task blocked forever on a full channel hangs until external timeout with no Jet report (probe task_blocked.jet, exit 124 from external timeout); a panicking child's 'child boom' text and any task identity are absent from the parent TaskFailure diagnostic (task_panic.jet, exit 70). docs/spec/architecture.md:200-204 documents non-detection of wait cycles; Prelude/Observe.rs already keeps a bounded payload-free task registry (parent/state/wait/deadline) but has no name/label field and no at-exit report. This is verdict-fidelity work: the runtime knows the task is parked and still says nothing.
cards.plan: 1) Add a name/label field to the existing bounded task registry (Prelude/Observe.rs) settable at spawn (task.spawn(name: ...) optional label; I7 for any new user-typeable key) and carried into traceback/failure paths. 2) At-exit report: when the scheduler reaches exit with tasks still parked (blocked on channel/wait), print one bounded diagnostic block per parked task (name, state, wait target, spawn site) through a registered diagnostic row + snapshot (I4); exit code unchanged. 3) TaskFailure fidelity: parent-visible failure carries the child's panic text and task identity (name or id) in the registered TaskFailure diagnostic; never a bare 'task failed'. 4) Witnesses: task_blocked.jet and task_panic.jet as examples with goldens (stderr goldens), identical across tiers (I9); scheduler changes live in the shared Prelude scheduler only. Non-goals: no GC-reachability leak profiler (Go's goroutineleak analog) - carded separately if wanted.

cards.title: Go 1.27 stdlib parity pack: cut_last, Int Euclidean div/rem, Unicode 17, JSON map-order pin, test-server and fake-time assessments
cards.body: Video mine 2026-08-28 (surface-coverage gaps, each verified by exact-name negative probe or source pin). MODEL MAPPING (verified live): DateTime=Instant(+civil UTC reads); LocalDate=PlainDate (weekday/iso_week/day_of_year/quarter/add_days/add_months/diff_days/replace-with-clamping/format all shipped, tier-parity proven); LocalTime=PlainTime; ZonedDateTime=ZonedDateTime (offset_seconds/is_dst; add_duration absolute vs add_period calendar already matches Temporal's hybrid law; DST fall-back+spring-forward verified identical on both tiers); Duration(exact ns)+Period(calendar y/m/d) is CLEANER than Temporal's mixed 10-field Duration (their balancing/serialization criticisms don't apply); injectable seeded Clock beats untestable Temporal.Now; comptime-validated DateTime{"..."} literal has no Temporal analog. Jet has no implicit coercion, so Temporal's valueOf()-throws defense is structurally unnecessary.
cards.plan:
Gap families, each landing with example+golden on default AND release (zero E0956 anywhere in the family):
G1 ordering/equality on all six time types (#2282). G2 render/selector tier parity (#2281). G3 default-tier ctor arms (#2252 slice: from_unix_ms/new/parse/datetime/local_time).
G4 difference family: until/since-class methods with largest_unit/smallest_unit/rounding mode (nine named modes)/increment on DateTime, ZonedDateTime, LocalDate; Duration gains total_in (fractional), round, abs, negated, sign; Period totals take an explicit anchor date.

G6 transition queries next_transition/previous_transition (TZif data already internal in Prelude Time.rs), start_of_day, hours_in_day.
G7 epoch family: from_unix_s/us/ns and to_unix_s/us/ns (closes Temporal's own gap, their v2 issues #33/#40).
G8 ISO week-date parse/construct (Temporal gap); year-month/month-day partial types get a written do/defer verdict.
G9 formatting completion: finish the pattern token grammar (unknown tokens like VV XXX currently print literally - must implement or reject with a diagnostic); deterministic built-in day/month names (no Intl dependency - beats Temporal's split); strict parse diagnostics per garbage class.
G10 with-family: spec the verified clamping default (replace(2023,2,29) -> 2023-02-28) plus a reject option; ZonedDateTime gains with_time/in_zone (same-instant projection).
G11 Duration.in rename (#2283).
NON-GOALS: non-ISO calendars (D-TIME-CALENDAR1 stands), Intl locale engine, user zone/calendar protocols (written verdict only).
Semantic laws go into the spec: month 1-based, clamp default, disambiguation default, total order, round-trip serialization. Beginner pass: now/today/parse/add stay one-liners; expert pass: every option is an explicit named parameter, no policy jargon in defaults. cards.title: Core-call registry totality: kill the unconditional ALL claim and reconcile every tier's real dispatch arms
cards.body: Harness hardening 2026-08-28 (owner directive: default-tier breakage must be structurally impossible). Root cause of the whole E0956-divergence class, with evidence: CoreCallRecord::new hardcodes coverage: CoreCallCoverage::ALL (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:493-529, the assignment at :523), so every row CLAIMS every tier; the registry guard (:4312-4334) validates declared bits only; the actual ambient dispatcher (crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs:3830-5269, delegated enc_stream/mod.rs:1075-1082) is hand-written match arms ending _ => None. A row can pass all validation and still have no evaluator arm - the claim is a lie by construction. A reconciliation helper core_call_mismatch ALREADY EXISTS (core_calls.rs:4556-4583) but nothing feeds it the real arm set. Tier consumers to reconcile: ambient interpreter, TIR eval (jet-codegen TIR/eval/exprs.rs:5093-5116), comptime (jet-comptime Methods/core_calls.rs:50-87), JIT lower (jet-jit jit/lower.rs:675-704), AOT emit (TIR/emit/core_calls.rs:658-711).

Expect RED on first run - the current liars are exactly the #2252 backlog; the test IS the enumeration. 3) Remove the unconditional ALL: rows declare true coverage, and a claimed-but-unimplemented tier is unrepresentable in a green tree. 4) Assess (written verdict) the endgame: one macro/table generating both the registry row and the dispatch arm so divergence cannot be expressed. cards.title: Impl-shape x interpolation conformance matrix: every sema-admitted Display/Debug shape gets a three-tier golden
cards.body: Harness hardening 2026-08-28. The Display/Debug defect class (#2273 user impls, #2281 core types) escaped because sema admission and per-tier lowering are three independent seams with no shared contract test: sema admits via trait registry (jet-sema Sema/Diagnostics.rs:1610-1758), AOT emits bridges (jet-codegen Codegen/Items.rs:2725-2910), the TIR evaluator does its own name lookup (TIR/eval/exprs.rs:5824-5848, 10838-10859), and the JIT searches func_ids separately (jet-jit jit/lower_ctx.rs:10795-10945). No golden covers the two-impl shape; examples/features/types/display_debug.jet has Display only; the one manual-Debug test (tests/auto_derive_policy.rs:422-495) never runs AOT. The admitted shape space is closed and small - the matrix is bounded, not bloat.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Every sema-admitted Display/Debug impl shape renders byte-identically in every interpolation context on default run, release (AOT) and the forced interpreter (I9). The admission ratchet keeps the closed matrix complete. The self-hosted compiler is the system under test; the retained AOT emitter and JIT must agree with it.

## Current state
- tests/impl_shape_matrix.rs (9 rows; impl_shape_matrix_covers_all_contexts_and_resolution_seams) and Examples/features/traits/impl_shape_matrix.jet exist. The admission ratchet (criterion 2) is met.
- 2026-09-22 bounded run: 12/13 pass. The release golden assertion at tests/tir_support/mod.rs:406 fails because a nested DebugOnlyOwner in a list renders structurally (`DebugOnlyOwner { value: 3 }`) instead of through the user Debug impl. Tuple formatting also reads a moved SSA temp.
- Seams: Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/AutoDerives.jet:234; Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet:1037-1085 (derive/user-impl selection); the retained emitter crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs (AOT Rust emission is retained host, Docs/spec/architecture.md:118-123); Compiler/JetEval/Source/Formatting/Values.jet:16-17 and Numeric.jet:11-35; the JIT resolution in crates/jet-jit.

## Changes
1. Emission (MIRRust.rs and its Jet port Emit/Types.jet + AutoDerives.jet): when an owner has a user Debug impl, nested renders (list/map/tuple elements) call that impl's bridge, never a structural derive. Tuple formatting reads the checked borrowed place, not a moved temp.
2. JetEval Formatting/Values.jet: `.Debug`/`.Display` resolve the same user impl by checked impl identity, not by name lookup.
3. crates/jet-jit: share that resolution (checked impl id from MIR), with no separate func_id search by spelling.
4. JetSema: the trait registry enumerates admitted shapes for the ratchet. Add a plain-enum row once #3586 lands.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test impl_shape_matrix` passes (both tests).
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=traits/impl_shape_matrix cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes. `Tools/agent/jet-env target/debug/jet run --interpret Examples/features/traits/impl_shape_matrix.jet` matches the same golden.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- Self-hosted cell: the harness fixture row passes (see add_criteria).

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: emission and evaluator formatting. It shares the retest with #3586.

## Dependencies
None. The self-hosted cell needs the compiler-bootstrap-host harness building (#218 stream).

cards.title: Datetime accuracy harness: differential + property stress vs independent oracles, in the suite forever
cards.body: Owner directive 2026-08-28: 'we need to stress test the date stuff for accuracy not just look at what it should do and say were good to go.' Shape-review is not proof. This card owns a PERMANENT accuracy harness for core.time: the same computations executed by Jet and by independent references (Python zoneinfo/IANA tzdata; RFC 3339/ISO 8601 law for parse edges), diffed line-by-line, plus property laws (parse-format round-trip identity, diff_days antisymmetry, add_days composition, clamping table). Families: epoch round-trips incl. negative timestamps and 1900/2000/2100/2400 century-leap edges; civil fields (weekday/iso_week/day_of_year) vs isocalendar; calendar arithmetic incl. end-of-month clamping; DST transitions for hostile zones (Australia/Lord_Howe 30-min DST, Asia/Kathmandu +05:45, Pacific/Apia 2011 skipped day, Pacific/Chatham) at transition +/-1s; zoned absolute-vs-calendar arithmetic incl. fall-back ambiguity pick; malformed-input law table (leap seconds, 24:00, +24:00 offsets). A first prototype run is executing now (lane DTACC); its mismatch table seeds this card's fixture set. Every mismatch found becomes either a Jet fix or a documented, spec-cited semantic difference - never silently accepted.
cards.plan: Permanent differential + property harness for core.time, in the suite forever. 1) Oracle corpus: a checked-in generated table (tool under tools/, deterministic seed) of test vectors produced from Python zoneinfo/IANA tzdata + RFC3339 law at generation time; vectors committed so CI needs no Python. Families per card body: epoch round-trips (negative timestamps, 1900/2000/2100/2400 leap edges), civil fields vs isocalendar, calendar arithmetic incl end-of-month clamping, DST transitions (Lord_Howe, Chatham, Casablanca, Sao_Paulo historical), offset parse edges. 2) Property laws as tests: parse-format round-trip identity, diff_days antisymmetry, add_days composition, clamping table - run on default AND release. 3) Differential runner: one test binary walks the vector table, executes the same computation through the Jet Prelude time kernel, diffs line-by-line; failures name the vector. 4) Regeneration: tool re-run refreshes vectors with a diff review; drift between generated and committed fails. Depends on #2289 fixes landing first (known weekday/add_months defects would flood the diff).

cards.title: Datetime accuracy defects: weekday() rotated on every date; negative add_months uses truncated division; +24:00 offset accepted
cards.body: Differential accuracy run 2026-08-28 (500+ oracle-diffed cases vs Python zoneinfo/IANA; full report ~/.cache/jet-luna/mine-2026-08-28/artifacts/jet-dtacc.md; owner directive: prove accuracy, not shape). Verified first-hand: (1) WEEKDAY ROTATED, 150/150 random dates wrong: 2024-02-29 (Thursday) gives weekday()=2, 2026-08-28 (Friday) gives 3 - the value is iso_weekday-2, matching no convention on earth while docs say 0=Sunday (Thursday should be 4); iso_weekday() is correct everywhere. (2) NEGATIVE add_months WRONG via truncated-not-floored division: time.new(2024,2,29).add_months(-12) returns 2024-01-29 (minus ONE month; correct is 2023-02-28 with clamp); -1 and -25 happen to be correct, making the bug data-dependent and extra-silent. (3) parse_rfc3339 ACCEPTS RFC-invalid offset +24:00 ('2024-01-01T00:00:00+24:00' -> 2023-12-31T00:00:00Z; RFC 3339 offset hour is 00-23, Python rejects). (4) INVESTIGATE: fall-back overlap resolution is internally inconsistent across zones - America/New_York resolves the ambiguous local time to the earlier (DST) instant while Europe/London, Australia/Lord_Howe, Pacific/Chatham resolve to the later (standard) instant; a uniform policy (then explicit options, #2284 G5) is required. CLEAN BILL elsewhere: 150 epoch round-trips incl. negative timestamps, all 177 DST-transition lines (Lord Howe 30-min, Apia skipped day, +/-1s edges), add_days/diff_days, day_of_year/iso_week/leap/quarter, and 0 default-vs-release diffs on the tier-control set.
cards.plan: Fix weekday() to the documented Sunday=0 mapping (or re-ratify the mapping and fix to it - spec and impl must agree either way); replace truncated with floored divmod in add_months (property test: add_months(d,n) == n applications of +/-1 with clamp-at-each-step semantics documented, plus oracle-diff over negative deltas); reject +24:00 offsets in parse_rfc3339 with a registered diagnostic + snapshot; unify overlap resolution to one policy and document it (options ride #2284 G5). Each fix lands with its DTACC fixture as a permanent regression test on all tiers; harness ownership is #2288.
cards.checkSteps: weekday matches spec mapping on the 7-day calibration table;negative add_months oracle-diff clean over 200 random deltas;+24:00 rejected with snapshot;overlap policy uniform across all zones;fixtures in suite

log.text: ROOT CAUSE PROVEN (investigator, generated build/f2_max.rs:62628-62630): the map stores raw i64 keys, and extremes route through jet_int_from_i64 which packs out-of-63-bit values as JET_INT_BIG_TAG + a FRESH ARENA ID per call (CommonTypes.rs:1758-1770). insert() and get() each pack the same semantic value into DIFFERENT raw keys, so the BTreeMap (Core.rs:1549-1581) never matches. Additional cross-tier seam: comptime map folding serializes CtValue::Int keys as raw '{}i64' literals (foundation AST/comptime.rs:1905-1939; CtKey::to_value 1404-1407) — i64::MIN becomes the literal -9223372036854775808i64 which is INVALID RUST (unary minus on a too-large literal), while the runtime IntLit emitter (emit/expressions.rs:1301-1321) routes extremes through jet_int_from_i64. Likely the #2308 Int-key assignment ICE feeder too. Fix must normalize key serialization with the same representation as the runtime path.

Seams located: the bigint sentinel is the collision — CommonTypes.rs:1738-1777 packs out-of-63-bit Ints with JET_INT_BIG_TAG = i64::MIN + arena id, and the Int literal emit path (expressions.rs:1301-1321) routes i64::MAX/MIN through jet_int_from_i64, so extreme keys enter maps in tagged/untagged mismatched forms; map key emit (expressions.rs:3804-3828, 3831-3861) operates on raw i64 with no semantic key adapter, while comptime CtKey keeps raw i64 (comptime.rs:1311-1369) — hence default finds the key and release loses it. cards.title: Freestanding profile: core/alloc/hosted Prelude closure split with target capability facts
cards.body: Follow-up of #2046 (docs/research/embedded-freestanding-profile.md). Implement the research direction once the owner rules on the ballot-ready decisions in that doc: split the emitted Prelude closure into core/alloc/hosted parts, add target capability facts (MMIO, clock, entropy, scheduler, byte sink), and make sema admit a reachable closure only when layer+capabilities are present. I9: one semantic Prelude, target-selected providers; a separate freestanding Prelude implementation is prohibited. Blocked on the owner decisions listed in the doc's final section.
cards.plan:
Ratified law (all eleven decisions are ratified; no owner question remains): D-FREESTAND-SELECT1 = B (`--freestanding` is rejected; a named typed profile is required; the error names the typed route; no second `no_std` flag), D-FREESTAND-PRELUDE1 = A (Core: allocation-free carriers and operations; Alloc: owned String, Vec, map, allocating encoders, owned Path; Hosted: filesystem, network, process, terminal, ambient time, OS scheduler), D-FREESTAND-FACTS1 = A (a closed, registered fact menu: runtime layer, allocator, startup entry, vector table, panic report, memory, linker, IO read and write, wall and monotonic time, zone data, sleep, crypto entropy, scheduler, sockets, filesystem, browser DOM, GPU, FFI, MMIO, volatile; each present fact names a provider and its digest), D-FREESTAND-ALLOCAPI1 = A (Core returns fixed values, views, or caller-owned buffers; owned outputs live in Alloc), D-FREESTAND-SINK1 = B (`IO.Read`, `IO.Write`, and `Panic.Report` are target facts; the shared Prelude serializes and preserves call order; sink failure enters the runtime failure path), D-FREESTAND-TIME1 = A (pure calendar needs no provider; `Time.Wall`, `Time.Monotonic`, `Time.ZoneData`, `Time.Sleep` are separate services), D-FREESTAND-SCHED1 = A (cooperative, interrupt-driven, board-runtime, or no-scheduler mode; one task contract; no-scheduler rejects task APIs), D-FREESTAND-START1 = A (entry, vectors, ABI, and startup provider are typed facts; Jet generates startup glue and linker input; expert overrides hashed), D-FREESTAND-WASM1 = A (browser, WASI, and no-OS Wasm are three profiles; no implicit providers), D-FREESTAND-ARTIFACT1 = C (source closure is the authority; a linked artifact is an optional cache projection with the full identity key), D-FREESTAND-DIAG1 = B (E3301, E3303, E3304, E3305 name the selected profile and layer; new E33xx rows per new fact family). Read each with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json`; research: docs/research/embedded-freestanding-profile.md. Criterion 1 (sema admission with registered pre-codegen diagnostics) is already met.

Actual: admission exists, but the eight capabilities are not all typed providers with validated contracts, the tiers do not all route through target-selected marshalling, provider facts are not in artifact identity or the dossier, and the five witnesses do not exist.

cards.title: Regex value fidelity: replace all-vs-first tier fork; zero-width splits lose characters; byte spans; ReDoS
cards.body: Silent-data sweep 2026-08-28 (REGEX lane). (1) VERIFIED FIRST-HAND: method-form Regex.replace replaces ALL matches on default, only FIRST on release ('X' vs 'X ab', SWEEP-REGEX/f4_method.jet) — silent value fork. (2) split with zero-width/empty patterns LOSES characters on both tiers: split("") on 'abc' gives [,,,,] dropping a,b,c (python ['','a','b','c','']; Rust regex also keeps fields); 12 mismatched cases incl. limit variants (f5.jet f5_007/009/010/011/025/033-037). (3) match spans are UTF-8 BYTE offsets while String slicing is codepoint-indexed (f6.jet f6_018/022) — composing regex spans with s.slice silently corrupts; one unit must win or spans must be typed. (4) (a+)+$ on 26 a's + X hangs >10s on both tiers (f2_path.jet) — backtracking engine, ReDoS class. (5) Dialect pins needed (document, not bugs): ASCII-only \\d/\\w, $ absolute-end, split omits captured groups. Clean: 34/35 captures, 49/50 replace, quantifiers 38/39.
cards.plan: (a) One replace contract (replace_all vs replace_first as separate named methods; method form means ONE thing on every tier). (b) Fix split zero-width advancement to retain fields (differential fixtures vs python + Rust regex). (c) Spans: pick codepoint offsets to match String API (or a typed ByteSpan unusable as codepoint index). (d) Engine: linear-time engine or step budget with loud error — no input may hang matching. (e) Document the dialect pins. All behind differential fixtures on all tiers.

log.text: Int-key map ICE ROOT CAUSE FOUND (investigator, from generated build/f5_int_map_only.rs:62797): emitted 'let mut ints: JetMap<i64,String> = JetMap::<String,i64>::new();' — REVERSED constructor generics. Mechanism: sema CheckerInfer/expr.rs:4381-4457 elaborate_typed_lit rewrites a typed EMPTY map literal ([Int:String]{}) to a bare Expr::MapLit(vec![]) (4453-4455), dropping the head type; lower/expressions.rs:5567-5584 then applies the empty-MapLit FALLBACK (Type::String, Type::Int) (5573-5580); the Let annotation keeps the true type (statements.rs:2581-2589) so annotation and initializer disagree and rustc rejects. Consequence: EVERY empty typed map literal whose type differs from the hardcoded (String,Int) fallback ICEs on release — the String-key tests match the fallback by luck, which is why the suite is green. Fix: preserve the typed-literal head type through elaboration (or thread b.ty into empty MapLit lowering). This likely also explains other 'generated Rust did not compile' map ICEs in the cluster.

STRUCTS lane adds: struct-key map lookups ICE on release too (SWEEP-STRUCTS/f5_map.jet, default correct) — joins the Int-key assignment ICE family. Investigator note on the Int-key repro (HASH/f5_int_map_only.jet): plain flat emission looks valid in source (jet_map_insert(&mut m, (1i64).clone(), ...)); the repro assigns ints[1] twice (insert then overwrite) before read — fixer should diff the generated .rs of exactly this shape; candidates remain emit/statements.rs:1947-1993 + Core.rs:1679-1685, with comptime key serialization (comptime.rs:1905-1939) as the alternate root.

Seam for the Int-key map assignment ICE (HASH/f5_int_map_only.jet): emit/statements.rs:1947-1993 emits jet_map_insert(&mut base, key.clone(), v) whose helper (Prelude/Core.rs:1679-1685) requires M: DerefMut<BTreeMap<K,V>> — trait-bound mismatch against the JetMap impl (Core.rs:1578-1581). Test suite has only String-key map compile witnesses (TIR/tests.rs:2393-2415, tests/hardening.rs:140-157); no flat Int-key witness — exactly the #2286 conformance-corpus gap class.

cards.title: Stdlib API-shape policy: option parameters on one root method vs sibling methods
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-08-28: instead of sibling methods sharing one signature shape (replace/replace_first), prefer ONE root method with a great default for the common operation plus an optional customization parameter (enum such as .First/.All) — small namespace, one method to find, options discoverable in the signature; siblings stay when signatures genuinely differ. The mechanism is already ratified: D-CALLPOS1=A gives defaults-after-supplied-arguments and named-args-to-deconflict; parameter defaults spell Type{default}; zero new syntax. Full study: docs/audits/optional-args-stdlib-2026-08-28.html (sibling-cluster inventory: replace family, from_bytes pair, 24-method byte codec matrix on #2310, ratified zip verbs D-ZIPLEN1=D tension, trim trio, sort_by/min_by boundaries). Ballot D-STDLIB-OPTPARAM1 on this card; open ballots D-REGEXREPL1 (#2304) and D-BYTESDECODE1 (#2297) gain matching options and resolve consistently with this pick; #2310 implementation waits for it.
