cards.title: Cost transparency: hidden-copy lint + per-line cost view
cards.body: Value semantics plus D-MEM-COPYSEM1 implicit copies, collection spine clones (Arc::make_mut per insert), and the packed-Int bigint fallback create invisible super-linear costs: an innocent-looking loop line can be O(n^2). This is the Swift CoW cliff, inherited exactly. The gauntlet measures peak performance; nothing surfaces per-line cost, and professionals leave languages over unpredictable performance, not slow performance. Owner verdict 2026-08-28: ballot the law, card the surfaces. Gated on D-COSTLAW1.
cards.plan: After ratification, per the ratified option: 1) Inventory every hidden-cost site with its TIR/lowering seam: implicit view-to-owning copy, collection clone-on-write, Int bigint fallback, per-call outcome construction. 2) Hot-path lint: a hidden copy, clone, or representation fallback inside a loop body gets a registered L-code with what/why/fix naming the concrete repair (hoist, explicit ~ copy, freeze). 3) jet explain --cost <file>: per-line annotations from TIR facts naming allocations, copies, and fallbacks, tier-labeled. 4) Record the standing law in docs/spec/performance-budget-decisions.md: no construct ships a new invisible super-linear cost without a lint or cost-view row. All diagnostics snapshot-tested per I4.

log.text: Video-mine 2026-09-03 SIMD lane: L2510 fires on every plain numeric loop probed (S1-S5, S8) with three fix texts a beginner cannot act on: 'Provide the collection shape proof that selects the direct representation', 'Bound the operands so the result stays on the packed Int rail', 'Consume the outcome through an immediate fast path'. The lint is right about the cost (a Vec clone is in the generated loop) but the fix must be an edit, and the canonical shape should not need one. Texts in ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/simd/results.md 'Verbatim diagnostics'.
Closed after repairing stale syntax/case fixtures; exact cost CLI contract passed 2/2. Global lint snapshot harness remains blocked by unrelated CLI-help case-law changes.

D-COSTLAW1 ratified A with owner comment adopting C as well: optimizer excellence is a killer feature alongside the surfaces. Optimizer lane rides the existing codegen campaign cards (int fast path, make_mut hoisting, outcome cost, auto-vec, bounds elision) — do not duplicate them here. Hybrid clause is law: a cost the optimizer provably removes needs no lint or cost-view row; semantic costs that must remain (D-MEM-COPYSEM1 copies, bigint fallback) get the lint and the cost view.

cards.title: Warm jetpack env entry is 15s at 100% cache hit; must be near-instant
cards.body:
Owner report 2026-08-28: 'jetpack env' took 386s on a cold-seal run and 15s warm at a 100 percent cache hit with an unchanged env.jet, and failed with E1340 'could not project bash through /nix/store'. The projection failure is FIXED (commit 47f99925b: Nix symlink-root objects are recreated as symlinks in the projected store instead of being canonicalized/stat-followed). The SPEED is not fixed and is the owner's bar: nix warm entry is effectively instant, so anything beyond reading a stamp and projecting the closure is our failure.

EXACT PROFILE (JETPACK_TIMING=1, added in the same commit, repo's own 28-package env.dev):
  roots 7ms / plan-loaded 13ms / trust-gate 14ms / catalog-configured 14ms / secrets-validated 23ms
  step cargo (first package) 4.3-4.8s
  every subsequent package ~180-340ms x 27
  env-composed 14-16s total; announce_env_ready adds ~0.9-2.5s

Already ruled out: entry-list walk (memo restored — a leftover 'probe_disable = true' in Store.rs list_unlocked had hard-disabled it; worth ~65ms/package), closure graph rebuild (memoized on the WAL stamp; no further gain), Store::dir_size (du of the whole objects dir is 0.5s).

So the residual ~200ms/package and the 4.3s first package live INSIDE realize_ref_outcome / realize_verified: candidates are the per-package hangar lock acquisition (RuntimePolicy::with_lock per find_verified_by_reference), snapshot_lease_unlocked (creates a lease dir per entry), project_receipt_projection, per-entry seal checks, and producer/provenance validation.

Target: warm entry with unchanged env.jet + lock + hangar generation does no per-package verification at all — one stamp comparison, then project and exec. The env-entry receipt (ENV_ENTRY_RECEIPT_HEADER 'jetpack-env-entry-v1') is the natural place to record the activation stamp.

Separate defects found while measuring, worth their own criteria or cards: (1) 'jetpack env -- bash -c true' fails E1340 'not a recorded member' even though bashInteractive is in the env; (2) every run reports '27 updated' lock changes with identical versions on both sides, so the lock is rewritten on every entry.
cards.plan: Keep the existing phase timer until the warm path meets the target. Cache the verified closure projection as one stamp-keyed environment result. A warm entry must read the lock and store stamps once, skip per-package realization work, and enter the shell. Any lock, journal, manifest, or environment change must invalidate the cache. Remove temporary per-package timing after the final profile proves the result.

log.text: Closed after final fresh-binary proof. Warm receipt selections now canonicalize transient lease paths, seal contents enter the stamp, successful auto-clean refreshes the receipt, and native release fixtures replace the retired omp@nixpkgs test source.

Evidence correction: the prior 14.0s/11.3s runs used the Nix-installed `jetpack`, because jet-env rewrites only `jet`; the attempted target/debug/jetpack run was also stale because `cargo build -p jetpack` builds the library, while the executable package is `jetpack-bin`. The v1 receipt header proves old code. Disregard those timings for the current patch. Fresh v2 proof awaits `cargo build -p jetpack-bin` after the concurrent regex clean cutover compiles.

Fresh-binary runtime proof is RED: first unchanged env invocation reported env ready 14.0s (real 16.98s), then the immediately repeated unchanged invocation reported 11.3s (real 12.48s). Both showed 28/28 cached and 100 percent hit, but miss the <1.0s criterion by an order of magnitude. The implementation lane is correcting the receipt fast path; no criterion is met by these runs.

Warm receipt implementation is present across jetpack env composition and Hangar reuse. Scoped `cargo check -p jetpack` is green after correcting the direct-CAS tuple projection. Runtime latency, cache counters, and invalidation criteria remain open pending fresh jetpack binary and three-run/mutation proof.

criteria.text: Three consecutive unchanged `jetpack env < /dev/null` runs report a 100 percent cache hit and reach the shell in less than 1.0 second each on this workstation.
criteria.evidence: Fresh jetpack-bin exact integration test fully_materialized_env_and_use_enter_without_network_or_prompt passed: three unchanged env entries each asserted <1.0s, 100 percent cache hit, and no per-package timing step.

criteria.text: A changed lock, store journal, sealed manifest, or environment input invalidates the warm result and rebuilds the projected closure before shell entry.
criteria.evidence: The same exact integration test passed environment-input, closure-journal mtime, same-stat seal-content, deleted-seal, and deleted-object invalidation/fallback checks; EnvHook::tests::definition_fingerprint_tracks_unified_lock separately passed lock add/change identity checks.

criteria.text: Warm entry does not rewrite `.jet/lock`, report unchanged packages as updates, add net disk usage, or run one realization pass per package.
criteria.evidence: The exact integration test passed byte-identical receipt and lock checks across warm runs, zero net Hangar/lease byte growth, no update/prompt rows, and no per-package timing step on the warm path.

cards.title: Hardening rig runner: one crash-safe bounded cycle under a resource-capped user timer
cards.body: Implements the continuous local cadence under #2334 without a custom endless daemon. A systemd user timer starts one low-priority bounded cycle, then retries after 15 minutes. The cycle stands down on a dirty or actively owned checkout. It uses the shared target only under an exclusive lease and leaves no owned residue on any exit path.
cards.plan: 1) Add scripts/agent/hardening-rig.mjs with cycle, install/start/stop, and machine-readable lifecycle commands; one invocation runs one deterministic cycle only. 2) Add user-service/timer definitions with CPUQuota=200%, MemoryHigh=6G, MemoryMax=8G, MemorySwapMax=2G, TasksMax=64, IOWeight=10, Nice=10, RuntimeMaxSec=95m, and a 15-minute retry delay. 3) Preflight tmp-guard, clean-tree state, exclusive rig/build lease, MemAvailable, target size, and disk-backed scratch; dirty, active, stale, or over-budget state records SKIPPED/RED and does no build. 4) Rebuild target/debug/jet once per clean commit through jet-env; never create another target dir. Run named proof targets and differential shards with process-group timeouts, concurrency 2, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, JET_MIN_FREE_GB=16, JET_TARGET_CAP_GB=80, and CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0. 5) Journal every transition with atomic rename. Trap success, failure, signal, and timeout; kill the owned process group, preserve one bounded failure bundle, and delete only owned scratch. 6) Cap ~/.cache/jet-hardening at 4GiB, interesting corpus at 512MiB, and logs at one 1MiB failure set; check caps before and after each cycle and refuse later cycles after any overage.
cards.checkSteps: dirty or leased checkout performs zero build/run work;clean commit rebuilds once and completes one cycle;signal and timeout leave no children or scratch;memory/target/cache thresholds refuse work;timer restarts a later bounded cycle;no alternate target dir exists

log.text: Closed on integrated evidence: all exit criteria met with concrete proof; open sibling blockers are sequencing only and contradict no evidence.

criteria.text: One systemd user timer invocation runs exactly one bounded cycle, retries 15 minutes after exit, and never relies on a custom immortal daemon.
criteria.evidence: scripts/agent/user-service/jet-hardening-rig.timer uses OnUnitInactiveSec=15min; service is Type=oneshot and ExecStart runs one cycle.

cards.title: Hardening rig layer 1: domain oracle adapters and value-preserving Core mutation batches
cards.body: First wrong-answer engine under #2334. It starts from #2286's checked-in valid, value-consuming programs, mutates typed values and boundary partitions without destroying the observable sink, and compares every applicable tier plus an independent reference, algebraic law, or blessed golden chosen by domain. It reuses the existing three-tier corpus path; it does not create another general runner.
cards.plan: 1) Add one oracle catalog keyed by the tagged surface IDs from #2335. Each row names tier self-diff plus its independent source or law, version/provenance, normalization, mutator, batch size, and observable sink. 2) Implement adapters for numeric, float, text/Unicode, bytes/encoding/serde, regex common-subset, time via #2288, crypto vectors, RNG/UUID laws, files/process/env exact-byte fixtures, local network/DB peers, concurrency model traces, memory/view state models, and compiler/reflection goldens. 3) Seed only from checked-in #2286 programs and the explicit differential fixture manifest; examples add whole-program seeds but never satisfy the denominator. 4) Mutate values and named boundary partitions while keeping type shape and result observer intact. Batch many cases into one Jet program and stable line protocol to amortize AOT work. 5) Reject a case unless it records stable surface ID, seed, mutation arm/version, exact source, oracle identity, expected relation, all tier observations, and normalization. 6) Add cross-check fixtures for each known P0 seam class: semantic equality, indexed places, packed-Int extremes, release emission totality, and default stdin transport.

cards.title: Hardening rig auto-carding: atomic root-seam dedup, archived-card reuse, and regression assimilation
cards.body: Turns every confirmed rig finding into one durable Tower work item without symptom-card floods. Current Tower duplicate probing compares live-card title/body before the store lock and has no durable dedup identity. This slice adds an exact hardening key enforced inside store.mutate across live and archived cards, then uses only Tower CLI JSON writes. The runner never closes cards.
cards.plan: 1) Add an optional hardening dedupKey to Tower card payloads, persistence, JSON output, and CLI lookup; enforce unique add-or-update under store.mutate's cross-process lock across live and archived cards. Preserve fuzzy title/body duplicate warnings for humans, but never use them for rig idempotency. 2) Define canonical identity as schema version + root semantic seam/primitive + violated relation + wrong-tier mask + input partition. Surface IDs, exact inputs, and symptom text attach as evidence, never the primary key. 3) Route an unknown seam to one unclassified semantic-primitive cluster. Triage assigns a canonical seam and stores the old key as an alias so future hits converge. 4) On a confirmed find, call Tower CLI with --json, --stdin, explicit --by hardening-rig, and optimistic revision handling. Default P0 for silent wrong data or any default jet run divergence; loud non-default failure starts P1. 5) Embed the minimized source, exact commands, expected/actual, commit, seed, and bundle digest in the card. Repeated findings append evidence, not cards. 6) When a fix lands, require the finding ID in a permanent corpus fixture; a later recurrence restores/reopens and updates the same card, including one retired to history. Never auto-meet criteria or close a card.

cards.title: Fresh-context hardening red-team: repeatable eight-surface attack session and signed verdict
cards.body: Implements the third ratified handoff gate under #2334. It is not another fuzz runner. It defines one repeatable fresh-context attack session against a frozen clean commit, limits active execution to two lanes, records every valid attempt, and proves whether the session produced a new P0.
cards.plan: 1) Add a red-team session manifest that freezes Jet commit, binary hash, rig config, public-surface snapshot, oracle versions, lane briefs, quota, and resource caps. 2) Run the D-HARDENING-GATE1 lane count as fresh Luna-max contexts, at most two execution lanes at once. Give the public mission and attack surface, but hide current defect cards until each lane records its independent finding. 3) Cover eight named slices: tier seams/nested places; numeric and representation extremes; optimization and dev/release/interpreter; stdin/argv/env/files/exit/resources; host/effect Core and exclusions; concurrency/cancellation; parser/sema/TIR construct boundaries; cross-domain compositions. 4) Require value-consuming programs and record attempts, valid cases, duplicates, false positives, minimized repros, and unique findings. 5) The orchestrator replays every load-bearing find on the frozen binary, then routes it through #2338. 6) Emit one signed result bundle. Pass only when the full quota completes with zero new P0. Any P0, semantic change, registry change, or target mismatch invalidates the result and forces a new session.

cards.title: e11-m02 is gated by compiler-speed harness instability, not by slow compilation
cards.body:
All four blocked e11-m02 lanes name the same two causes, so fixing these unblocks #666, #1023, #1026, #1027, and #1028 together.

1. The benchmark is UNSTABLE, not slow. 'scripts/agent/jet-env sh tools/perf/dashboard.sh --baseline' exits 1: 'unstable compiler-speed benchmark: examples/features/basics/hello.jet/jit-representative-edit variance=130% budget=100%' (also observed at 120%). #666 criterion 3 is genuinely MET by this — the dashboard correctly exposes instability instead of hiding it. #1023 criterion 2, #1026 criterion 2, and all of #1028 block on it. Fix the measurement (pinned CPU, warmup discipline, more samples, or a documented wider budget with a stated reason). Do NOT widen the budget silently.

2. 'scripts/agent/jet-env tools/perf/ci-perf-check.sh' exits 1: 'unsupported compiler-speed baseline version: 2'. The checker rejects a baseline version it is being handed. #1027 criterion 2 blocks on it; criterion 3 is MET because the gate fails closed on an incompatible baseline. #1027 criterion 1 additionally hit a release-tier ICE ('internal compiler error: the generated Rust did not compile') that needs its own reproduction and card.

Tree state at filing: GREEN at 7a0b7e154 (lane-check CHECK OK). 107 files hold uncommitted wave-8 lane work awaiting review and integration; nothing was discarded.

e12 note: #1387 is correctly blocked behind #1377-#1385 by construction (it is a closure scan, not parallel work). #1379 criterion 1 is MET (12/12 disposition rows, each candidate count=1); criterion 2 blocks on a stale fixture at tests/corelib_parts/runtime.rs:964-969.

Seam lesson for future waves: tests/ws_law.rs and tests/http_server_lifecycle.rs STUB the Observe seam instead of including it, so any lane changing Prelude/Observe.rs signatures must update both stubs in the same patch. Three separate red-tree episodes this session traced to exactly that.
cards.plan: After #2346 is green, run the compiler-speed dashboard with the robust interquartile spread and Tukey-fence gates. Regenerate the baseline through the existing production command. Update the baseline schema and identity only from that command. Run the CI checker against the new baseline and record the exact stability data.

log.text: Closed on implementation evidence; measurement criteria moved to #2858 (owner instruction 2026-09-03).

The harness-acceptance half of this card is absorbed by the matched Cargo benchmark card in the automatic-build-optimization slate (see refs); the stability fix half stays here. Stale blocker on #2346 (done) should be cleared by the orchestrator.
Owner global performance law added as an exit criterion. Internal baselines and aggregate receipts remain necessary but are no longer sufficient without matched peer wins and the Rust parity floor.

Keystone blocker identified: #2346 — the AOT release path recompiles a byte-identical program (hits=0 misses=1 on the aot-release-no-change row), so tools/perf/dashboard.sh exits nonzero, so the baseline cannot be regenerated, so ci-perf-check.sh rejects the stale version-2 baseline. Fix #2346 and this card's perf evidence becomes obtainable.

PROGRESS + a real defect found underneath.

FIXED (commit above): the variance statistic was peak-to-peak (max-min)/median — a measure of the single worst sample, not of stability. That is why the number bounced between 120% and 130% against a 100% budget. It is now the interquartile spread relative to the median, with a second gate counting Tukey-fence outliers so a bimodal path still fails rather than hiding behind a robust statistic. This was a measurement defect, not a budget that needed widening.

NEWLY EXPOSED, DETERMINISTIC, AND MORE SERIOUS: with the noise gate no longer masking it, 'scripts/agent/jet-env sh tools/perf/dashboard.sh' now fails the same way on every run (reproduced twice, ~65s per run):
  no-change cache reuse missing for examples/features/basics/hello.jet/aot-release-no-change: hits=0 misses=1
The AOT release path recompiles a byte-identical program instead of reusing its cache. The dashboard is correct to refuse: check_cache_state asserts a no-change state must be a cache HIT, and it observes hits=0 misses=1. This is exactly the guarantee e11-m02 (fast compiler loop) exists to make, so it is a compiler bug, not a harness bug.

DEPENDENCY CHAIN for whoever picks this up: AOT no-change cache miss -> dashboard.sh exits nonzero -> 'dashboard.sh --baseline' cannot regenerate tools/perf/baseline.json -> the committed baseline stays version 2 while ci-perf-check.sh requires version 4 -> 'unsupported compiler-speed baseline version: 2'. Fix the AOT no-change cache reuse first; the stale-baseline symptom then clears by regenerating, and #666, #1023, #1026, #1027, and #1028 unblock together. Do not hand-edit baseline.json to version 4 — that would fake the identity fields the checker exists to compare.

cards.title: AOT release recompiles a byte-identical program instead of reusing its cache
cards.body:
Deterministic, reproduced on consecutive runs (~65s each):

  scripts/agent/jet-env sh tools/perf/dashboard.sh
  -> no-change cache reuse missing for examples/features/basics/hello.jet/aot-release-no-change: hits=0 misses=1

The AOT release path recompiles an unchanged program. The harness is right to refuse: 'check_cache_state' in tools/perf/dashboard.sh asserts that a no-change state must be a cache HIT, and it observes hits=0 misses=1. Reusing a cached artifact for byte-identical input is the core promise of e11-m02 (fast compiler loop), so this is a compiler defect.

Why it was invisible until now: the dashboard's stability gate used a peak-to-peak statistic that failed on machine noise before execution reached this assertion. That statistic is now an interquartile spread (commit c908b8b29), and this defect is what sits underneath.

Blocking chain: this failure -> dashboard.sh exits nonzero -> '--baseline' cannot regenerate tools/perf/baseline.json -> the committed baseline stays version 2 while ci-perf-check.sh requires version 4 -> 'unsupported compiler-speed baseline version: 2'. So #666, #1023, #1026, #1027, #1028, and #2345 all unblock behind this one fix.

Do NOT hand-edit baseline.json to version 4: the version gates a set of machine and toolchain identity hashes that the checker exists to compare, and forging them would make every future perf comparison meaningless.

First place to look: the AOT cache key. Something in it is not stable across two runs of identical input — a timestamp, an absolute path, an env-derived value, or a compiler-identity hash recomputed differently between the warmup and the measured sample. The JIT no-change row passes, so compare the two key computations.
cards.plan: Instrument `run_aot_trial` once. Capture the warmup and first measured sample cache key inputs, computed key, cache directory, artifact path, and hit or miss counters. Remove the instrumentation after the differing input is known. Fix the harness staging or AOT key source that changes despite byte-identical source and manifest. Keep the production cache law unchanged.

log.text: Source diagnosis complete pending production dashboard proof. Warmup and sample native cache keys are identical; the observed miss was the outer receipt layer replaying the warmup stderr before native cache lookup. The dashboard now sets JET_RECEIPT_BYPASS=1 for every AOT trial, preserving no-change hit, edited-source miss, and hit-or-miss assertions without compiler bypass or debug instrumentation.

HYPOTHESIS 1 ELIMINATED. Re-ran the isolation test WITH the dashboard's exact fixture manifest present (package.jet carrying 'authority: .{ holds: { allow: [IO, Mem.Alloc] } }'), three consecutive builds against one JET_CACHE_DIR: run 1 'cache miss -> compiling', runs 2 and 3 'cache hit -> reused cached binary'. So an authority-bearing manifest does not break reuse, and the key is not mtime-sensitive for it.

Where that leaves the card. Everything reachable from outside the harness now caches correctly: the release profile, JET_TIMING, JET_CACHE_DIR, the pinned binary copy, the run.jet name, and the fixture manifest. Yet the aot-release-no-change row reports hits=0 misses=1 at sample 1 even though the warmup compiled in the very same work dir with the very same cache dir.

The next agent should therefore stop hypothesising and instrument. Concretely: inside run_aot_trial, before each build, append to a log the resolved JET_CACHE_DIR, its directory listing, the sha256 of run.jet and package.jet, and the mtimes of both; run only the hello.jet no-change row; then diff the warmup's record against sample 1's. One 65-second run produces the answer. The remaining suspects are ordered by likelihood: (a) something between the warmup and sample 1 empties or relocates the cache dir, (b) the warmup's cache write does not land where sample 1 reads because JET_CACHE_DIR is interpreted relative to a different cwd for the two invocations, (c) the key includes a value that changes once per process rather than once per input.

Also worth deleting while there: prepare_fixture writes package.jet twice, a 'cp "$FIXTURE_PACKAGE"' immediately overwritten by a printf. The cp is dead work today and merely confusing.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE — the dashboard's exact build invocation caches correctly in isolation.

Reproduced the invocation from run_aot_trial verbatim (same env, same pinned binary, same run.jet name, twice against one JET_CACHE_DIR):
  env JET_CACHE_DIR=<cache>/build JET_TIMING=1 JET_TIMING_DIR=<work>/timing NO_COLOR=1 \
    jet-env bash -c "cd <work> && exec <pinned jet> build --profile=release --verbose run.jet"
Run 1: '[build] cache miss -> compiling' plus '[build] runtime -> cache hit'. Run 2: '[build] cache hit -> reused cached binary'. Exit 0 both times.

So neither the AOT cache key nor JET_TIMING nor the pinned-binary copy nor the release profile breaks reuse. The no-change row shares one work dir and one cache dir between its warmup and every sample, so sample 1 should observe the warmup's entry — and it reports hits=0 misses=1.

That leaves the staging itself. Two specific things to check, in this order:
1. The fixture package. My isolation run had NO package.jet; the dashboard's prepare_fixture writes one containing 'authority: .{ holds: { allow: [IO, Mem.Alloc] } }'. If the cache key incorporates the manifest by path or mtime rather than by content, an authority-bearing fixture could miss where a bare program hits. Re-run the isolation test WITH that package.jet present — if it then misses on run 2, the bug is found and it is a real compiler bug (a manifest must be keyed by content, not mtime).
2. prepare_fixture writes package.jet TWICE — 'cp "$FIXTURE_PACKAGE"' then a printf that overwrites it. The cp is dead work today, but it means the file is created and immediately rewritten, so any mtime-sensitive key sees two different stamps for identical content. Delete the dead cp regardless; it is confusing and it is a plausible trigger.

Step 1 is a two-minute test and will most likely settle the card.

MAJOR NARROWING — the AOT content cache is NOT broken in general.

Verified directly: copy examples/features/basics/hello.jet into a scratch dir and run 'jet build --verbose main.jet' twice. Both runs print '[build] cache hit -> reused cached binary'. Reuse works, and the key is stable across processes in a fixed directory. (Note for anyone reproducing: the hit/miss lines are behind --verbose; without it 'jet build' prints nothing and a naive probe looks like a total cache failure.)

So the defect is in how tools/perf/dashboard.sh stages the aot-release-no-change row, or in an interaction that staging triggers — not in the cache key as such. Facts about that staging, from the script: the no-change row shares one work dir and one cache dir between the warmup and every sample (state_work=$state_root/seeded, state_cache=$state_work/cache, cache_policy=shared-cache-after-warmup), so the warmup should populate exactly the cache sample 1 then reads. It reports hits=0 misses=1 at sample 1 anyway.

Next concrete steps, in order: (1) print the cache dir and the computed key for the warmup and for sample 1 of that row and diff them; (2) check whether run_aot_trial removes or rewrites build/ or the cache between runs; (3) check the linker capture — run_aot_trial records trial_linker and the scale path resets TRIAL_LINKER=, so confirm the same linker is selected for warmup and sample (a different linker legitimately changes the key); (4) confirm prepare_fixture is not re-copying the source with a fresh mtime or a different absolute path into the key.

That is a much smaller search than 'the AOT cache is broken', and it can be settled with one instrumented run of about 65 seconds.

Lane w9aotcache timed out mid-investigation; its debug instrumentation in tools/perf/dashboard.sh was reverted (tree is CHECK OK, no leftovers). It had reached the right place: it was logging, inside run_aot_trial, whether the trial stats file and the build stderr exist per run, which is how you compare the warmup's key inputs against the measured sample's. Next agent should resume exactly there: instrument the AOT cache key inputs in run_aot_trial, print the computed key for the warmup and for sample 1, and diff them. The JIT no-change row passes, so the differing field is in the AOT-specific part of the key (linker probe, artifact path, or a toolchain identity hash), not in the shared portion.

cards.title: ui_snapshots aborts: E3012 fixture overflows the native stack instead of reporting
cards.body:
This is the long-unidentified 12th failure in tests/diagnostic_snapshots that has blocked #2204 and #2266. It is PRE-EXISTING (every blessing attempt this session reported 11 passed / 1 failed) and it is not caused by the #2317 recursion work.

Reproduce:
  CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots -- --nocapture
Observed:
  test ui_snapshots has been running for over 60 seconds
  note: skipping tests/ui/ffi_no_cargo.jet ui snapshot (need no cargo for E0703)
  thread 'jet-tir-eval' (...) has overflowed its stack
  fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
  signal: 6, SIGABRT
The whole test binary aborts, so the suite cannot report and no snapshot can be blessed.

The fixture is tests/ui/runtime_e3012.jet:
  fn recurse(n: Int) Int -> { return recurse(n + 1) }
  fn run() { print(recurse(0)) }
  // @dev_interpreter
Deliberate unbounded recursion whose whole purpose is to prove E3012 fires. tests/ui/runtime_e3012.stderr expects 'Stop [E3012]: stack overflow in recurse'. Instead the evaluator exhausts its native stack.

WHAT I ALREADY RULED OUT, so do not redo it:
- The depth guard EXISTS on both evaluator paths and both branches look sound. crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:3843 guards the ordinary call path (call_depth compared to jet_foundation::Outcome::JET_RUNTIME_STACK_LIMIT, returning E3012 when runtime_execution and otherwise draining fuel via burn()). mod.rs:3688 guards the run_recursive_scalar trampoline the same way, keyed on frames.len() through 'self.call_depth = caller_depth + frame_index'.
- This fixture takes the run_recursive_scalar path: mod.rs:3838-3842 routes any recursive_body whose chain is recursive_chain_supported there, and a foldable 'return recurse(n + 1)' qualifies.
- The trampoline holds frames in a heap Vec, so frame growth alone cannot overflow a native stack. Something on that path still recurses natively — most likely argument or continuation evaluation (eval_expr_child and the BinaryLeft/BinaryRight continuations around mod.rs:3655-3677), or the guard is never reached because the native recursion happens before the frame is pushed.

WHERE TO START: run the fixture directly under the interpreter and get a backtrace of the overflowing frame (JET_BACKTRACE or a debugger), rather than reading more code. The repeating frame names will name the native recursion immediately. Also check the stack size the 'jet-tir-eval' thread is spawned with: if it is small, a legitimate depth below JET_RUNTIME_STACK_LIMIT can overflow before the guard trips, and the honest fix is to make the guard's limit consistent with the thread's actual stack.

EXIT CRITERIA: the fixture reports E3012 matching tests/ui/runtime_e3012.stderr on the dev interpreter; the full 'cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots' reaches 12 passed with no abort; and the fix is a general depth guarantee, not a special case for this fixture.
cards.plan: Find the native recursion that bypasses the heap-frame trampoline in `run_recursive_scalar`. Route all recursive evaluation through the existing heap frame loop or set a guard below the real native stack limit. Keep E3012 in the evaluator. Do not enlarge the thread stack or special-case the fixture.

cards.body: The completed Jet jetpack canary cold build measured 18.181 seconds, while a one-line comment-only warm rebuild measured 21.293 seconds. cards.title: Ownership diagnostics name the consuming callee, the later reuse, and the exact ~ site
cards.body:
Dogfood agents accepted visible copy boundaries but burned correction passes finding them. trim, split_once, .before, .after, path operations, Core calls, record construction, and reused arrays each produced a missing-~ retry loop. The report asks the diagnostic to name three facts: the consuming callee, the later reuse that blocks the move, and the exact expression where ~ belongs.

Today E0121 anchors only the later reuse and never names the consuming callee, and E0120 names source and destination but carries no structured edit. The move span is already stored and then discarded.

cards.title: Failure-domain provenance: E2404 names the offending helper and public carriers teach their fix
cards.body:
The most repeated dogfood complaint: agents learned failure-domain rules only after E2404 appeared at several call sites, and the diagnostic never said which helper's inferred or default error domain caused the mismatch. Public fallible functions also required public error carriers with no diagnostic naming the required change.

The ratified implicit failure route (#2172, D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1 outcome A) removes most of the ceremony the port paid, but its ratified tradeoff clause requires hover, diagnostics, and inspection to make the route fully visible. E2404 today knows source and target error types but not the offending callee (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/fallible.rs:330-390). No dedicated public-carrier visibility rule exists (Registration.rs:222-274 checks public and private signatures identically).

Show the two candidate repairs the report asks for: the required '!ErrorType' signature on the caller, or the declared 'Source -> TargetError' conversion; attach each as a Suggested edit.

cards.title: Project-aware jet check: prove entry, module graph, Core closure, and tier lowering before runtime
cards.body:
Dogfood's trust breaker: 'jet check' reported a package clean while default-tier and AOT paths still failed. Check stops after sema (crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:5887-6044, CompileMode::Check) and returns before target validation and codegen (Source/CmdCompile.rs:1580-1600), so package output entry resolution, generated runtime graph, Core-call closure, and tier lowering stay unproved until run or build. Isolated file checks in partial worktrees also made correct project-root imports look broken with no hint that project context was missing.

How deep the default check reaches is an owner choice; the ballot on this card decides it. The cone law (D-DEVR-CONE1) bounds whatever depth wins.
cards.plan:
Depth decided by ballot D-CHECKSCOPE1 (adversarial-reviewed recommendation A: full promise for project checks, semantic scope for explicit file checks). Integration seam: Source/CmdInspect.rs:112-209, the single check-projection choke point. Reuse shipped pieces: package-root finder (#1716), shared entry resolvers (#1031, #1521), call-graph reachability (#1717), and the registry conformance denominator (#2285, #2286).

Proof rows keyed by scope, selected entry/output, profile, and tier adapter with statuses proven / not applicable / source unsupported / compiler defect / toolchain unavailable. Tier coverage comes from side-effect-free structured validators modeled on the web validator (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Web.rs:414-420); never probe the native emitter (ICE on coverage miss, Codegen/Items.rs:3376-3394) or JIT lowering (silent skips, Codegen/TIR/mod.rs:1735-1781). Core closure is the exact used-call plus synthesized-call set resolved to each adapter's actual route; registry size is never the clean predicate.

Honest wording: check does not invoke rustc, a linker, or the runtime entry and does not execute build actions; it may evaluate selected compile-time build checks (Source/lib.rs:935-983). Receipts: a fully unchanged invocation replays the whole-invocation receipt; per-module incremental reuse routes through query-service facts (crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs:33-49); entry-candidate, workspace, output, lock, and generated-input changes invalidate (the src/run.jet-then-create-root/run.jet scenario must invalidate, Source/ReceiptStore.rs:173-189,614-627).

Isolated-file experience: a file check inside a package resolves the owning project graph through the shared root finder; when the graph is unavailable, the diagnostic states the missing project context and the canonical root-import form. The relative '..' rejection keeps its by-design refusal and teaches the canonical form.

Non-goals: no second check verb, no rustc/link/runtime execution inside check, no edits to dogfood/jetpack/**.

Project proof-row/snapshot corpus is green. Remaining: clean-check-to-run/build corpus, receipt invalidation, project-owned file context snapshots, and measured warm cone/schema evidence.

cards.title: Public typed package model: package.jet, lock, and profile read API for tools
cards.body:
The dogfood port hand-built parsers for package.jet, .jet/lock, profiles, and selectors: hundreds of lines of line scanners, quote scanners, and brace trackers, because no public Jet API exposes Jet's own package language. plan.jet reached 970 lines before formatting mostly on this work.

The typed read model already exists compiler-side: jet-pkg-model owns the only package.jet parser (PackageFacts, Manifest, BuildProfileDef), Lock::parse and WorkspaceLock cover .jet/lock, and jet-env-model evaluates profile generations. What is missing is a public, I6-clean surface. The shape of that surface is an owner choice; the ballot on this card decides it.
cards.plan:
Home decided by ballot D-PACKAGE-MODEL1 (adversarial-reviewed recommendation: extend the ratified core.compiler read-only value API). Facade the existing model; never fork it. jet-pkg-model stays the single parser (#1517). Expose a deliberately narrow named view model - manifest declarations (uncomposed), composed package facts, lock entries, and profile definitions as separate operations - not PackageFacts wholesale. Scalar current-package facts keep their one ratified @build.* spelling; the new views add no second spelling for any scalar fact.

Contracts fixed by the adversarial review: reads are compile-time/build-only with the registered runtime refusal (same gate as core.compiler, docs/spec/spec.md:4615-4619); all reads go through the authority-checked package root (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Authority.rs:546-698) with no sibling, dependency, or arbitrary-path traversal and no secret or authority material in the projection; every contributing file enters the build graph and cache key; the view model publishes an explicit field matrix (optionality, composition level, ordering, error carriers) and positions only where the underlying model retains source.

Non-goals: no write or mutation API, no provider or network behavior, no second parser, no runtime filesystem reads, no edits to dogfood/jetpack/**.

cards.title: Idiom suites: canonical dispatch, failure, ownership, finite-state, and wire-output stories
cards.body:
Dogfood agents scored creating at 2.8/5 and said they searched widely for canonical forms. The port transferred Rust branch habits, used strings plus seen_* booleans for finite state, and hand-wrote wire JSON beside #Codable. Every needed mechanism is shipped: ordered arm tables, the implicit failure route, enums, variant groups, tags, typestate, and canonical JCS JSON with typed writers. What is missing is one discoverable suite per idiom that agents find before they improvise.

D-EXAMPLES-SUITES1 ratified the suite structure; only three suites exist today (examples/suites/README.md), and the 52-suite migration remains proposal text.
cards.plan:
Add golden-backed suite programs under examples/suites/ using the shipped harness (tests/suite_goldens.rs:18-70 discovery; extend discovery, no new mechanism): a parser story that dispatches string keys with ordered tables and alias grouping; a failure story showing the implicit route, one typed expert contract, and one declared conversion; an ownership story showing view reuse, the ~ boundary, and the cost view; a finite-state story replacing stringly state and parallel booleans with enum, variant group, and typestate; a wire-output story producing exact JSON through the canonical writer and a #Codable round trip.

Each suite is the one source of truth for its idiom per D-DOCS-SSOT1: lint fix text, capsule content (#2324), and llms.text slices point at the suite instead of restating it. Include the literal-brace and interpolation authoring pitfalls inside the wire-output story, since testimony named them.

Coordinate with #2375 (retired-ceremony sweep) to avoid double edits; this card adds suites, #2375 cleans existing files.

Non-goals: no edits to dogfood/jetpack/**, no new teaching mechanism, no full 52-suite migration.

cards.body: Dogfood scored diagnostics 2.6/5 partly because one root cause could appear as many downstream errors. Targeted suppressions exist (binding poisoning, conversion-cascade pruning, duplicate dedup from #1328/#2213/#2225) but sema never attaches causal links or orders the final report root-first. cards.title: Same-subject dispatch lint: adjacent categorical guards suggest one ordered table
cards.body: The dogfood port passed L0507 while using ten adjacent 'if key == "..."' statements as a dispatch table. A mechanical audit found 15 file-and-subject groups with at least three categorical string comparisons and only 24 ordered tables against 430 'if' tokens. The report names the exact detector: adjacent exclusive branches over one stable subject should suggest one ordered 'if subject == { ... }' table. Independent validation guards and branches with state changes between them must stay quiet.
cards.plan:
Detection: add an adjacent-statement scan over normalized Stmt::Switch nodes in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/blocks.rs:39-75 (check_block_inner sees the full statement slice); the parser normalization site is crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/conditionals.rs:490-533. Current L0507 (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/mod.rs:454-468) only sees chained/else shapes, which is why adjacent guards escape.

Trigger rule: three or more adjacent statements whose condition is an equality/comparison on the same stable subject (local, field path, or call-free expression), each arm exclusive, no intervening statement that writes the subject or its dependencies. Early-return validation guards on different subjects never fire the lint. Suggested rewrite is the ratified 'if subj == { ... }' table (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs:232-244, D-IFGUARD1/D-IFDIST1), grouping alias values with '|'.

Register the diagnostic per I4: registered row, what/why/fix, UI snapshot. Advisory by default per D-LINTPOLICY1; deny via policy.lints. Attach a structured edit only at the D-REPORT-FIXGRADE1 grade it earns: Safe when the rewrite is proved meaning-preserving, otherwise Suggested. Surface the same rewrite as an LSP refactor action through Source/LSP/Features.rs:1102-1175 reusing TextEdit/FixEngine (Source/LSP/Check.rs:46-133); the formatter conversion IR already exists at crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter/Statements.rs:952-989.

Non-goals: no new syntax, no edits to dogfood/jetpack/**, no change to L0507's existing shapes.

cards.title: Default-on semantic guidance for audited idioms
cards.body:
Add seven default-on semantic warnings for audited inferior forms that remain legal after their canonical replacement exists. Reuse Diagnostics.jet, sema diagnostics, LintPolicy, statement-scoped #allow, policy.lints.deny, UI snapshots, and diagnostics coverage. No second rule engine, global strict mode, or warning before the replacement ships.

1. process_args_view: only the normalized direct process.argv().skip(1) projection. Fix process.args(). Aliases and indexed parsers are corpus-policy work; callers needing argv[0] stay quiet.
2. message_text: only after sema exposes the same canonical default-cap identity as req.text()/resp.text(); warn when constant evaluation proves body().text uses that identity. Different limits, binary, and streaming stay quiet.
3. redundant_fixed_cleanup: only when the whole relevant string/interpolation component is proven to be one plain Fixed projection and immediately removes grouping separators. Mixed/arbitrary comma cleanup stays quiet.
4. unit_scalar_rewrap: only one normalized expression where sema proves the same linear unit is raw-unwrapped, scaled by a supported scalar, and immediately rewrapped with no helper, rounding, calibration, FFI, or conversion policy.
5. path_containment_string_prefix: only when Path provenance is typed and a normalized component path is reduced to the separator-aware string-prefix idiom. String-only legacy helpers are corpus-policy work; physical/symlink policies stay quiet.
6. complete_ascii_case_ladder: only an exact complete constant A-Z or a-z ladder over the same value with no intervening observation. Partial/domain replacement stays quiet.
7. walk_files_filter: only a direct fs.walk loop whose sole control-flow branch excludes directories and whose remaining uses are path-only. Aliases, metadata, custom traversal, and early-exit policy stay quiet.

Do not ship manual_cli_when_typed for arbitrary user code: direct argv use does not prove a closed grammar. Fixed-shape manual CLI, delimited-reader intent, DataTree truthiness, HTTP hand-escaped JSON, unused route parameters, and nontrivial aliases belong to the maintained CorpusPolicy adapter or to their product API tests.

Each warning has a unique registered code/name, deterministic one-diagnostic behavior, What/Why/Fix copy, a mechanical edit, positive and expert-negative UI snapshots, cross-rule precedence tests, diagnostics coverage, and existing statement-scoped #allow behavior. Maintained corpus #allow sites additionally require an occurrence-scoped manifest reason; arbitrary user code keeps the existing reasonless local escape.

cards.title: Protocol expansion emits pre-body-arrow stubs: pub protocol raises four bogus E0080 plus E0153
cards.body: A file containing a plain ratified protocol block fails to check. The compiler expands pub protocol Payment into #SingleUse .Client/.Server stubs, but the generated fragment is still written in the retired pre-body-arrow form, so the generated source does not parse. The user sees four E0080 body-arrow errors pointing at an empty line past the end of their file, plus E0153 saying the protocol failed to expand. Both the generated-code parse failure and the garbage span are invariant violations: I2 says generated-code rejection is an internal compiler error, never a user diagnostic, and I4 says a diagnostic has to be a product. Reproduction: a six line file with a doc comment, pub protocol Payment { client: Hello(version: Int) server: Ack(session: Int) }, and fn run() {} reports five problems on target/debug/jet check. The same block inside tests/fixtures/jetdoc/run.jet keeps that fixture red on master.
cards.plan: Find the protocol expansion writer that builds the .Client and .Server stub source, migrate every generated callable to the ratified name(args) Type -> body form, and give the expansion failure a real span on the protocol declaration instead of end of file. Then delete the retired spelling from the generator so no second form survives.

cards.title: P0 ICE: value-position `if` branches disagree when one arm is fallible
cards.body:
I2 violation. `jet check dogfood/tower/run.jet` aborts with an internal compiler error instead of either compiling or emitting a registered user diagnostic:

```
internal compiler error: assertion `left == right` failed: live if branches must agree on their value type
  left: String
 right: Result { ok: String, err: Named("Err") }
  at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs:2213:25
```

Three distinct instances fire in that one file, with pairs `String` vs `Result{String,Err}`, `Bool` vs `Result{Bool,Never}`, and `Result{List(String),Err}` vs a plain list. `Result{ok: T, err: Named("Never")}` on one arm proves the lowering is keeping a fallible wrapper on an arm that can never fail, so the two arms of one `if` reach TIR with different value types.

Sema accepted the program, so this is codegen lowering, not a checking gap: either sema must reject it with a registered diagnostic or the lowering must unify the arms. Per I3, checking belongs in sema and codegen must be dumb; per I2 an ICE is never a user-facing outcome.

Reproducer: `target/debug/jet check dogfood/tower/run.jet`. Also blocks card #2376 criterion 2, because the dogfood Jetpack and Tower parity checks cannot run.

cards.body:
I2 violation. The `cffi` suite fails 18 of 75 tests on the integrated tree, and the first failure is rustc rejecting generated code, which is an internal compiler error by invariant, never a user diagnostic.

Observed with a freshly built `target-proof/debug` binary:

```
thread 'cffi_end_to_end_links_and_runs' panicked at tests/cffi.rs:1516:5:
I2: rustc rejected generated C-FFI code (jet bug):
error[E0277]: the `?` operator can only be applied to values that implement `Try`
  --> .../main.rs:68147:45
68147 |     { let _ = jet_term_write_stdout_line(&(((__jet___c_jetc::__jet_greeting())?).jet_display()), false); };
```

cards.title: Runtime rlib cache pruning deletes entries used by concurrent AOT links
cards.body: Two strict Core conformance shards run concurrently against one clean integrated tree. One AOT rustc link fails because ~/.cache/jet/runtime/<hash>/libjet_runtime_core.rlib vanished between generated command construction and linker open. cards.title: Ownership view-return tests assert a retired bare-reference signature
cards.body:
19 tests in tests/ownership.rs assert that an infallible view-returning function emits a bare Rust signature, for example tests/ownership.rs:3749-3755 expecting 'fn __jet_domain<''__jet___view>(__jet_email: &''__jet___view String) -> &''__jet___view str'. The live ratified contract is that an omitted error type defaults to Err and '!Never' is the infallible spelling, so 'fn domain(email: String) View<str> -[]>' legitimately lowers to JetOutcome<View<str>, JetErr>. The tests therefore encode a retired contract.

A genuine defect was found and fixed alongside this: the emitted body was a bare 'return __jet_result;' under the JetOutcome signature, which is broken Rust and an I2 violation. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:564-577 now adds the predicate (string_view_return && matches!(actual, Type::String)) so the existing carrier lift wraps the value in Ok. Generated Rust compiles again. The 19 assertions still fail because they test the signature shape, not the body.

This blocks #2403 criterion 2, whose wording requires the whole ownership suite to pass.

cards.title: P0: field access on declared structs rejected with E0302 in dogfood jetpack
cards.body:
`target/debug/jet check dogfood/jetpack --json` exits 1 with six E0302 diagnostics, each saying field access only works on a struct or tuple, for fields that ARE declared struct fields.

Sites, all in dogfood/jetpack/src/cli/main.jet: .provider line 189 span 6767-6775; .name line 190 span 6826-6830; .version line 191 span 6863-6870; .reference line 193 span 6905-6914; .source line 195 span 6946-6952; .expected_hash line 196 span 6991-7004.

main.jet:182-207 accesses those fields on ingest_wire(IngestResult) and realize_wire(RealizeResult). Both are declared structs: dogfood/jetpack/src/store/ingest.jet:21-28 and dogfood/jetpack/src/realize/realize.jet:20-30. A plain text run reports 11 problems including L0507, L0520, L0514, and L2510. The check exits 1 before the package is read.

Found by the #2394 hostile closeout pass while the tree was mid-wave with about sixteen concurrent lanes, so confirm it reproduces on the integrated tree before deep investigation. It reproduced twice, in text and JSON modes.
cards.plan: Resolve imported nominal struct return types through the canonical registry. Add a cross-module witness and keep E0302 for true non-struct receivers.

log.text: Fixed fallible binding inference at the sema boundary, preserved explicit Result carrier positions, added local/imported struct witnesses, and proved dogfood has no false E0302.

criteria.text: Fields on a declared struct returned by an imported function resolve like local struct fields; true non-struct receivers still get E0302.
criteria.evidence: jet-sema exact tests fallible_binding_exposes_propagated_struct_success_fields and imported_struct_returns_expose_all_fields_but_scalars_keep_e0302 passed; ordinary untyped fallible bindings now auto-propagate without losing the declared success struct type.

criteria.text: The dogfood jetpack check has no false E0302 rows, and an independent cross-module witness passes.
criteria.evidence: scripts/agent/jet-env jet check dogfood/jetpack --json exited 0 with warnings only and no E0302; imported_module_alias_preserves_local_struct_fields and the scalar E0302 negative passed.

cards.title: Dogfood 5/5 campaign report contradicts its own evidence in four places
cards.body:
The #2394 hostile closeout pass, run by a GPT-family agent in fresh context, returned CHECK FAILED with four uncarded findings. Verdict artifact: local://card-2394-gpt-hostile-pass.md (hash 9B66).

F34 MISATTRIBUTION. The ledger row F34 in docs/proposals/dogfood-jet-experience-5-of-5.md:87 assigns the formatter return-arm defect to card #2355, but the report's own bug table at docs/audits/dogfood-jetpack-usage-experience-2026-08-30.md:222 identifies it as #2368. F38 correctly maps the separate read-only oracle lock-mutation defect to #2355. So #2368 has no owning disposition row, and the campaign could be declared clean while that defect owns nothing.

RI-1 GREEN CLAIM. The report executive summary (:3-5) says Jetpack was green through three dogfood phases. Its own bug table (:213-228) lists default and AOT blockers, and dogfood/jetpack/METRICS.md:28-32,83-86 records Phase 1 as blocked and not green with Phases 2 and 3 not reached and not measured.

RI-2 PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE. The report quotes binary size 1,377,432 B, cold 19.695 s, and warm 8.096 s (:78-84,122-130), but every cited metric table in METRICS.md:102-150 is marked not measured. docs/proposals/automatic-build-optimization.md:16-27 repeats those figures citing METRICS:144-161, which contains only error-cascade and finding rows.

RI-3 CROSS-LANGUAGE EVIDENCE. The report states all Rust comparisons use measured repository facts (:24-26) and presents a seeded cascade parity result (:70-76,243-246), while conceding there was no matched Rust agent slice (:62) and METRICS marks the error-cascade rows and Rust LOC/token rows not measured (:60-65,144-150).
cards.plan: Correct the four hostile-pass contradictions. Make the report, ledger, bug table, and sealed receipts agree without a false green claim.

cards.title: One-file Package metadata surface

cards.plan: Implement D-ECO-INLINEPACKAGE1=A as one native package declaration at the start of a Jet source file. cards.title: auto_printable table hand-synced against Prelude JetShow impls and drifts silently
cards.body:
Sema decides whether `print(value)` is legal via Diagnostics::is_printable -> TraitRegistry::implements_trait(PRINTABLE), backed by the hand-maintained auto_printable list populated in register_synthetic_display_debug (crates/jet-foundation/src/Traits.rs). That list has to agree with the actual `impl JetShow for Jet*` set in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude, and nothing enforces it.

It had silently drifted for nine types. ComputeDevice has `impl JetShow for JetComputeDevice` at Prelude/Compute.rs:4877-4888 and six Core conformance witnesses print it directly, yet E0112 rejected it and blocked the strict three-tier gate. An audit then found eight more printed by strict Core witnesses with deterministic JetShow output and no row: SyncText, SyncCounter, SyncMap, SyncList, ServiceRestart, ServiceDelivery, ServiceRuntime, ServiceStateStore. All nine rows were added at Traits.rs:2012,2088-2091,2095-2098.

The failure mode is bad: a type gets a JetShow impl, no row is added, and print stays rejected until some witness happens to exercise it. The gate only caught this one because a conformance program printed the value.

Investigating agent's assessment: deriving the list is feasible only through a larger canonical declaration or codegen refactor, because the sema-side foundation registry cannot reflect Rust impls living in jet-codegen, and aliases, internal-only types, and deliberate explicit-show exclusions all need metadata. Types with explicit *_show APIs (Tensor, ComputeStream, SparseTensor, ServiceTree, Endpoint) are intentionally excluded and must stay excluded.
cards.plan: Enforce the link between Prelude JetShow implementations and the sema printable registry with one focused drift test and named exclusions.

log.text: Closed on both exact integrated diagnostics coverage witnesses; unrelated suite coverage drift is separate work.

criteria.text: A focused test fails when a public deterministic Prelude JetShow type has neither a printable row nor a named exclusion.
criteria.evidence: diagnostics_coverage::prelude_jet_show_rows_match_canonical_printable_types passed; TraitRegistry consumes one exact nine-type PRELUDE_JET_SHOW_PRINTABLE_TYPES table.

criteria.text: The current Prelude JetShow set and printable registry agree, including the nine repaired types, without a second trait mechanism.
criteria.evidence: diagnostics_coverage::prelude_jet_show_exclusions_remain_explicit_only passed; five intentional exclusions remain explicit-only and cannot enter the beginner Printable set.

cards.title: P0: JIT drops a compute resource nested in a Result carrier before the caller uses it
cards.body:
In the resident Cranelift JIT, a function returning Ok(Tensor) has its Tensor freed before the caller can use the returned carrier, so a later compute.shape(output) reads an invalid handle and the program fails with E3001.

Trace, all in crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs:
- 1312-1327 result_new lowers Ok(Tensor) and builds the Result carrier WITHOUT adopting the payload's compute resource.
- 21153-21155 TExprKind::Ok routes into that path.
- 3728-3734 the preserve predicate does not see the nested payload, so 3744-3755 emit_compute_resource_closes drops it, and 3858-3867 emit_lexical_values_exit closes it at scope exit.
- 2439-2448 jet_jit_compute_shape then receives a dead handle.

The correct shape already exists nearby: lower_clone_result_value at 24217-24255 explicitly adopts the resource at 24238-24249. The Ok-carrier path is missing that adoption.

This is a tier-parity defect under I9: AOT and the interpreter keep the payload alive, and only the JIT frees it early, so the same program produces different behavior per tier. Found while clearing the last cffi failures for #2404; it surfaces through the Octave sidecar round-trip test.
cards.plan: Adopt compute resources when Result carriers are built. Reuse the existing clone-result ownership path and prove all execution tiers.

log.text: Closed on exact integrated all-tier Result<Tensor> resident-lifetime proof.

criteria.text: A Result carrier adopts each nested compute resource through the shared ownership mechanism; lexical cleanup cannot close the payload early.
criteria.evidence: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs result_new adopts the Tensor payload compute resource into the Result carrier before resident return cleanup.

criteria.text: A Result<Tensor> witness has identical output on AOT, resident JIT, and forced interpreter after the caller consumes the tensor.
criteria.evidence: compute_parity::compute_result_tensor_payload_survives_resident_return_cleanup passed: AOT, default native JIT, forced interpreter, and traced resident execution all returned shape [2] and values [3.0, 3.0] without deopt or use-after-drop.

cards.title: Locked Nix environments are not portable offline
cards.body: A fully locked environment still calls configure_project_catalog before realization. The lock records only absolute local Hangar object paths plus output hash, platform, provenance, catalog tier, and trust. They do not carry the portable Nix index key, derivation/store identity, cache identity, closure, or bytes needed to rebuild on a cold machine. The existing hostile workflow jet_repository_env_cold_and_offline_without_nix_host_store_or_fixtures therefore fails E1340 unless a host catalog or machine-specific fixture is supplied. Fix the lock producer/schema and locked realization path; do not add host discovery, catalog fallback, or checked-in machine store paths.
cards.plan: Extend the existing typed environment lock with a portable Nix closure record for every selected package: source channel and revision, target system, signed index manifest identity, derivation identity, output store path, NAR hash, byte size, compression, ordered references, upstream proof, cache key identity, and content-addressed bundle object. The lock producer writes each required source/cache object once into the existing project-managed CAS and records its digest; it never stores an absolute Hangar path, host /nix/store path as a location, or unbound cache URL. A fully locked realization reads the lock before configure_project_catalog, verifies the complete closure and signatures, reconstructs a fresh Hangar from only lock-declared CAS bytes, and never runs catalog discovery or host-store lookup. Missing, changed, reordered, wrong-platform, wrong-key, or extra closure data fails closed before state changes with precise provenance. Update `jet_repository_env_cold_and_offline_without_nix_host_store_or_fixtures` so online production and offline consumption use separate fresh roots and processes: the offline phase receives only the repository lock plus its portable bundle, has network disabled, no Nix executable, empty host stores, no fixture env, and proves the same package receipts and physical bytes. Add warm replay and copied-repository cross-machine identity proofs. Keep the current provider, store, semantic lock, and Nix cache mechanisms; add no fallback.

log.text: Portable-lock implementation and hostile Hangar CAS proof are green, but exact C3 cannot run on a clean checkout: production intentionally requires an explicitly installed signed Nix index endpoint and pinned nix-index-v1.ed25519.pub; the repository intentionally carries neither, target-nixfeed/feed is absent, and the required full 28-attribute signed index/cache closure is not published. No implicit endpoint, local catalog, host store, or fixture fallback is permitted. External prerequisite: production signed index service plus trust root and complete closure.

Live focused proof remains red: jetpack_nix_closure_replay has 4 failures (malformed present lock accepted as version 0; Nix source/closure identity rejects canonical fixtures; dangling relative link fixture). Fresh audit also found replay imports CAS objects before exact closure/platform/key/extra-member validation, violating fail-before-state-change. Root parser, canonical fixtures, and preflight transaction are under repair; no criterion credited yet.
Prepared the portable-lock repair around one content-addressed lock bundle. Offline replay will consume only lock-bound bytes and will not rediscover a host catalog or store.

criteria.text: The lock records portable Nix package and cache identity sufficient for cold realization without absolute host Hangar or Nix store paths.
criteria.evidence: PortableLock: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Lock.rs records channel, revision, system, signed-index identity, derivation/output/NAR/size/compression/references/upstream proof/cache key, project-CAS digest; no absolute path fields; Nix entry ids now content-addressed (content_addressed_entry_id)

criteria.text: A fully locked offline realization bypasses catalog discovery, consumes only lock-declared portable artifacts, and fails closed when any artifact identity or content differs.
criteria.evidence: Store::import_nix_cas_bundle_checked validates lock closure/envelope identity + bundle digest/manifest before Hangar mutation, failures render E1350; proof-w4 jetpack_nix_closure_replay 14/14 incl copied-checkout identity test

criteria.text: jet_repository_env_cold_and_offline_without_nix_host_store_or_fixtures passes with network disabled and empty host stores; warm and cross-machine replay use the same lock semantics.
criteria.evidence: timeout 1500 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test jetpack_dogfood jet_repository_env_cold_and_offline_without_nix_host_store_or_fixtures -- --test-threads=2 -> test result: ok. 1 passed (network disabled, empty host stores, self-created native catalog fixture; content-derived lock entry IDs; producer records carry the sealed lock digest via idempotent refresh_lock_digest; warm stamp recorded after sealed projection; strict online/offline/warm DU and receipt equality); timeout 900 ... --test jetpack_nix_closure_replay -> 14 passed; lane-check -p jetpack CHECK OK (PortableLock receipt ~/.cache/jet-luna/lanes/PortableLock.md; note: configure_project_catalog's complete-lock early return is not exercised by this test)

cards.title: Bare jet run, dev, build, and test pick one entry by one ratified rule
cards.body: Today a bare `jet run` in a package finds `run.jet`, then `src/run.jet`, then typed Outputs; any other file with `fn run` is invisible, and D-ILE1's promised `E_DUPMAIN` ambiguity row never shipped. The owner wants: root `@run.jet` first, then the one top-level file with `fn run`, then `src/`, never deeper, and an explicit file otherwise. Same law for dev, build, and test. Ballot D-DX-ENTRY1 fixes the exact precedence and the diagnostics.
cards.plan:
Actual: `Source/main.rs:3891-3920` and `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs:935-1028` resolve bare commands through retired-`main.jet` migration, `run.jet`, `src/run.jet`, then Outputs with `defaults`; command overrides (`Package/mod.rs:1085-1140`) scan for one top-level `fn <cmd>` with root `@<cmd>.jet` first; ambiguity is a textual error, not a registered row.
Expected (after ratification, per the ratified option; the ballot's recommended option C keeps D-CMDOVERRIDE1's order): one resolver used by run, dev, build, test, check, and doc: the root role home `@<cmd>.jet`; then exactly one root-level `.jet` file with a top-level `fn <cmd>` (new inference); then the same rule for `src/`; then the stock default (`defaults` or a sole compatible Output, then canonical `run.jet` and `src/run.jet`); otherwise a registered diagnostic that lists every candidate with its path and offers `jet fix` to pin one in `package.jet`. No precedence change for shipped packages: `@run.jet` beside `defaults.run` keeps running `@run.jet`. Never search deeper than `src/`. `--show-default` keeps bypassing overrides. `jet test` keeps the package `#Test` runner as its stock default when no `fn test` exists.
Writable paths: `Source/main.rs` (bare resolver), `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs`, `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/package_files.rs`, diagnostics registry rows and UI snapshots (`docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, `docs/spec/diagnostic-rows.md`, snapshot fixtures), `tests/` CLI tests, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` (ruling log), `examples/features/packages/**` (one example per precedence step).
Dependencies: D-DX-ENTRY1 ratified. Non-goals: new role-file names; workspace member selection (stays `-p <member>`). Invariants: I4 (every new diagnostic has code, what/why/fix, snapshot), I5 (executable examples), I9 (resolution is CLI-level and tier-independent; the chosen entry runs the same on every tier).

cards.title: Jobs runnable by name with discovery, completions, and a devtools panel
cards.body: `#Job fn` is the ratified user-defined command mechanism (D-JPK-TASKRUN1, D-JOB-NAME1, D-JOB-SUBCMD1=C: `jet run <entry> -- <name>`), and `jet jobs` lists jobs. Compared with `npm run`, `deno task`, `just`, and `cargo` aliases, invoking a job still needs the entry and the `--` separator, there are no shell completions, and the running program has no job view. Ballot D-DX-JOBS-UX1 decides the invocation shorthand; the rest is polish on the ratified mechanism.
cards.plan:
Actual: `Source/CmdCompile.rs:3167-3243` implements `jet jobs`; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Job.rs:162-292` dispatches jobs from the first program word; no completions; no job panel.
Expected (after ratification, per the ratified option; the ballot's recommended option E): `jet jobs <name> [-- <args>]` runs the named job of the entry resolved by the bare-entry rule (the no-argument form keeps listing); `jet run <entry> -- <name>` stays the canonical ratified form; `.Internal` jobs are never reachable from argv; workspace members use `-p <member>`; a name that matches no job reports the registered E1294 diagnostic listing the entry's jobs. No bare-name resolution inside `jet run` (option D) unless the owner picks it. `jet jobs` prints name, scope, doc, typed args, and schedule, and `jet jobs --json` is the machine form. `jet self completions <shell>` emits completions that include commands, files, and the entry's jobs. The devtools Jobs panel (card `jet.devtools.v1 ...`) lists jobs, last run, schedule, and offers run in dev.
Writable paths: `Source/main.rs`, `Source/CmdCompile.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Job.rs`, `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs`, completions module (new, under `Source/`), tests, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, examples under `examples/features/jobs/`.
Dependencies: D-DX-JOBS-UX1 ratified; entry card ratified. Non-goals: changing `#Job` syntax, scopes, or `#Every`. Invariants: I4, I5, I7 (no new keyword unless the ballot picks a verb, which then lands in `Syntax.rs` with its decision id), I9 (jobs dispatch through the same Prelude table on every tier).

cards.title: Devtools UX archetype: how developers see their running program on every host
cards.body: Jet has the facts the best devtools show (routes and render reasons, effect-tracked queries, signals, gates, costs, structure, traces) but no unified devtools surface: the browser has a status pill and overlay, the terminal has `jet dev` actions, `jet inspect live` is a separate command. The owner wants one devtools product on five hosts (browser overlay, `jet dev` workbench, terminal, editor, native overlay) that beats TanStack Devtools. Ballot D-DX-DEVTOOLS-UX1 chooses the UX archetype from four clickable prototypes under `docs/proposals/prototypes/devtools-ux/`.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs:3515-3669` injects a status pill, shade, and diagnostic overlay; `Source/CmdDevTools.rs` runs the terminal dev actions; `Source/main.rs:1993-2053` and `crates/jet-devserver/src/LiveInspect.rs` implement `jet inspect live`; Canvas exposes control-plane routes. No panel model, no plugin panels, no shared selection or time cursor.
Expected (after ratification, per the ratified archetype): the devtools UI is written in Jet on `core.ui` and rendered by the DOM runtime in the browser, by `TuiBackend` in the terminal, by an editor webview over loopback, and by the app's own `JetBackend` in native windows. Hosts share one selection and one time cursor over the `jet.devtools.v1` stream. First-party panels: Build, Routes, Queries, Mutations, Forms, Table, Store, Traces, Cost, Gates, Structure, Tests, Jobs; third-party panels register through the public panel API (card `Public typed devtools panel API`). Keyboard paths, six states (idle, building, build failed, runtime failure, hot reload, tests failing), 1280 and 768 widths, and `NO_COLOR` terminals are part of the acceptance matrix.
Writable paths: new Jet package under `Source/Devtools/` or `crates/jet-devtools/` (decide at implementation with the Prelude part in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Devtools.rs`), `crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs` (serve the workbench route and inject the pill), `Source/CmdDevTools.rs` (terminal host), `Source/LSP/` (editor open request), `editors/vscode`, `editors/zed`, tests under `tests/web_dev.rs` and a new `tests/devtools.rs`, docs under `docs/spec/observability.md`.
Dependencies: D-DX-DEVTOOLS-UX1, D-DX-PLUGIN1 ratified; protocol card. Non-goals: production devtools (card `Devtools presence in release builds`), Canvas visual editing. Invariants: I8 (one panel definition, many hosts), I9 (panel data comes from Prelude events on every tier), no theming or branding in copy, PascalCase program names.

cards.title: Public typed devtools panel API: how a package registers a panel and publishes facts
cards.body: TanStack Devtools and Astro's Dev Toolbar let any library register a panel; Jet has no way for a package to add a devtools panel or publish typed facts to it. The owner wants a public typed plugin API from day one. Ballot D-DX-PLUGIN1 decides the spelling: a marker on a panel function, a runtime registration call, a manifest field, or the marker plus typed publishing through the observation channel, with a naming menu for the marker.
cards.plan:
Actual: no panel registration surface exists; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Observe.rs` publishes payload-free snapshots; `#Job` (`crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/marker_groups.rs:1248-1291`) is the closest precedent for a marker that makes a function discoverable, scoped, and stripped by scope.
Expected (after ratification, per the ratified option): a panel is a Jet function that returns `core.ui` nodes from typed devtools state; the ratified spelling makes it discoverable by `jet inspect devtools`, compiled out of release builds like `.Dev` jobs, and rendered by every host without runtime registration code. Facts are published through typed events in the `jet.devtools.v1` families (Custom family for package-defined payloads) and a value is published only where the site says so explicitly (fact law: one written word at the site, on the record). Third-party panels appear beside first-party panels with no distinction.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs` (marker entry with decision id), parser marker groups, sema registration and diagnostics for misuse, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Devtools.rs`, `Source/CmdInspect.rs` (`jet inspect devtools`), formatter emission and stability test, grammar regeneration for `jet devtools` editor grammars, tests, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, example package under `examples/features/devtools/`.
Dependencies: D-DX-PLUGIN1 ratified. Non-goals: host UI (archetype card), production endpoint. Invariants: I4, I5, I7 (new marker registered with decision id), I8 (one registration mechanism), I9 (panel functions are ordinary Jet compiled on every tier; hosts are renderers).
Proof: parser and sema tests for the marker, formatter stability test, `jet inspect devtools` golden output, example package whose panel renders on DOM runtime and `TuiBackend` snapshots.

cards.title: Live loop law: an edit keeps every value whose type is unchanged, on every tier
cards.body: Native `jet dev` already auto-detects rerun versus resident hot swap (D-DEV4, D-DEVMODE1), D-HOTSWAP1 makes the module the reload unit with type-stable swaps, and `#Persist` pins dev state (D-PERSIST-DEVSTATE1=A). The web tier still does a full recompile and browser reload, losing signals, stores, query cache, form drafts, and scroll. Flutter, Vite, and .NET Hot Reload set the bar: edit, see it, keep your place. Ballot D-DX-LIVE1 decides the one live-loop law for web, native servers, games, and CLIs, and carries the ELI5 for the live-tiers axis.

cards.title: Rendering is a compiler fact: derived per-route rendering with resumable islands
cards.body: Next, Astro, Qwik, SvelteKit, and TanStack Start each make the developer choose a rendering archetype (SPA, SSR, streaming, SSG, islands, resumability, RSC) and then live with its traps: cache layers, `use client` boundaries, serialization limits, script reinitialization. Jet's `App` already labels routes csr, ssr, ssg, stream, and island by hand. The owner asked for a first-principles archetype that wins them all at once. Ballot D-DX-WEBARCH1 decides whether rendering becomes a compiler fact derived per route from data and interactivity facts, with resumable islands and one explicit override.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:110-202` exposes render modes, hydration, split, and cache as explicit calls; `jet explain --web-graph` prints the labelled graph; islands hydrate by re-executing.
Expected (after ratification, per the ratified option): per route the compiler derives static (no runtime data), server plus streaming (loader data), island (interactive subtree), or client (explicit) from the route's effect row and interactivity facts; islands resume from serialized state instead of re-executing, with a registered diagnostic when a captured value cannot be serialized; `.render(...)` remains the expert override; `jet explain --web-graph` and the Routes panel show the derived mode and its reason; caching is a written fact per route.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-sema` (route facts), `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Web.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs`, `DomRuntime.js` (resume marshalling), `Source/CmdDevTools.rs` (explain), tests `tests/web_app.rs`, `tests/web_browser.rs`, examples `examples/features/web/`, `docs/spec/spec.md` web section, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`.
Dependencies: D-DX-WEBARCH1 ratified. Non-goals: the suite modules (separate card). Invariants: I3 (sema derives the mode; codegen is dumb), I4, I5, I9 (the same route graph and meaning on the web tier and in native serving).
Proof: `jet explain --web-graph` golden output naming mode and reason for each example route; browser matrix asserting no re-execution on island resume; benchmark of first paint and interaction cost versus a TanStack Start and an Astro reference app.

cards.title: First-party web suite: Router, Query, Forms, Table and Virtual, Store on one reactive primitive
cards.body: TanStack's headless suite is the bar: typed routes and search params, cached server state with invalidation, typed forms with async validation, headless tables with virtualization, and a small store, each with a devtools panel. Jet has typed `App` routes, `core.reactive` signals, and effect-tracked live queries with automatic invalidation, but no typed search params, query cache semantics, form model, table, virtualization, or store history. Ballot D-DX-SUITE1 decides the shape: grow `App` ad hoc, ship separate installable packages, or one `core.web` suite on one reactive primitive with built-in panels.

Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:1-107` (route/page/layout/action/form/data), `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs:3807-3971` (`core.web` app/page/live/signal/auth/storage), `CoreLib/Top/LiveQuery.rs:172-532` (live queries), `core.reactive` signals; no search-param typing, no query cache states, no form field model, no table or virtualizer, no store history.

One reactive primitive. Each module ships its devtools panel and an example. Per-module API ballots follow this shape decision as their own cards.
