cards.title: jet.devtools.v1: one observation protocol in the Prelude feeding every devtools host
cards.body: The devtools need one typed event stream and one query surface that every tier emits identically. Today the facts are spread across `Observe.rs` snapshots, `LiveInspect`, `.jettrace`, WebHost status endpoints, and Canvas control-plane routes. This card unifies them into a versioned protocol with event families for build, route, query, mutation, form, table, store, trace, cost, gate, structure, test, job, frame, request, and custom payloads, with a bounded time-travel ring in dev.

Existing producers (Observe, LiveInspect, perf, WebHost status, Canvas) publish through it; `jet inspect live`, `jet perf attach`, and the hosts consume it. cards.title: User operator hooks give the wrong value on jet run, an ICE on AOT, and E0956 on jet eval
cards.body:
Actual: `impl Money.Add { fn add(self, rhs: Money) Money -> … }` then `print(a + b)` prints `Money { cents: 0 }` under `jet run` (expected 7), `jet build` stops with an internal compiler error (generated Rust does not compile, exit 101), and `jet eval` reports E0956. `print(a.add(b))` prints 7 on `jet run`. The repo's own executable spec `examples/features/operators/user_defined.jet` shows the same defect: `jet run` prints `0,0 1,2 true true false` (expected `4,6 4,6 true true false`; both `a + b` and `+=` are silently wrong) and `jet build` ICEs. Two more accepted operator shapes fail only on `jet eval`: `1 + 2.5` (AOT/JIT print 3.5) and `#Comparable` `Score{points: 2} < Score{points: 5}` (AOT/JIT print true).

Mechanism (HEAD 8b9933668): `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:2399-2419` emits the synthetic `Add/Sub/Mul/Div` traits as `fn add(&self, rhs: &Self) -> Self`; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/functions.rs:963-991` lists Display/Debug/Equatable/Comparable/Close as raw protocols but not the arithmetic traits, so the user body lowers with the fallible carrier while the trait wants raw `Self` (AOT type mismatch); `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs:19822-19862` consumes the first result slot directly (JIT reads the wrong slot). Evaluator seams: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs:5887-5892` and `:7737-7809`; `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Builtins.rs:655-681`.

Implementer note: `tests/golden.rs` is AOT-only and should already be red on `user_defined.jet`; `tests/dev_parts/routine.rs:5625-5648` covers the JIT output. Confirm on a clean master build before changing code.

Non-goals: no reflected dispatch, no mixed-type operands (D-OPMIX1 design card), no weakening of E0360/E0109/E2511.

Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-xUBIbhPC_rQ/ (p4_money_add_ok.jet, p2_numeric_widen.jet, p5_score_compare_ok.jet); second-reader rerun 2026-09-01; mine report docs/audits/video-mine-never-operators-supply-chain-2026-09-01.md. Source: Indently, "NotImplemented" is Awesome in Python (video mine).

cards.title: Divergence does not flow through calls; `Never` in a success position is an ICE (D-NEVER1=C incomplete)
cards.body:
Actual: (1) `fn impossible() Never -> panic("stop")`: `jet build` ICE exit 101 ("codegen reached a construct the typed IR does not cover: the return type `Never`", `Codegen/Items.rs:3391`); `jet run` accepts the uncalled function (prints 1, exit 0, L0104) and reports E0956 when it is called. (2) `if stop -> { process.exit(3) } else -> { 5 }` fails E0124 (`Never` vs Int) on both tiers although `core.process.exit` is typed `Never` (`fixed_sigs.rs:791-794`) and works as a statement. (3) D-NEVER1 option C's own ratified sample, `fn stop(message: String) { panic(message) }` used as `return if found -> { "Ada" } else -> { stop("name missing") }`, fails E0124 `String` vs `Unit`. (4) The E0124 fix line reads "make both branches produce `Never` (or the same type)".

Expected under D-NEVER1=C: one compiler-only bottom fact that flows from `panic`, `return`, `break`, `next`, Never-typed Core calls, and calls to user functions whose every path diverges, into `if`, match, and `??` value joins on every tier; `Never` written in a success return or parameter position is one registered diagnostic on every tier (never an ICE) unless D-NEVER2 rules otherwise; E0124 never asks the user to produce `Never`.

Mechanism (HEAD 8b9933668): `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs:208-210` (Never as the failure-domain name), `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/mod.rs:356-370`, `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:2816-2834` (join handles equal, numeric, and Todo only) and `:2989` (fix text), `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/types.rs:115-120`, `subset/entry.rs:65-72`, `Codegen/Items.rs:3378-3395`.

Non-goals: no public bottom type, no change to `!Never`, no change to the E0073 loop-value rule, no change to process exit status. Design follow-up is the D-NEVER2 card.

Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-wpqiH56ITZo/P3_never_return.jet, P3_never_return_called.jet, P4_process_never_branch.jet; ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-main/never_c_sample.jet; mine report docs/audits/video-mine-never-operators-supply-chain-2026-09-01.md. Source: Let's Get Rusty, Rust just introduced a new "never" type (video mine). Refs #1291, #1842.

cards.title: extern rust bridge builds crates with host cargo outside the ratified sandbox (the arrayref vector)
cards.body:
Actual (HEAD 8b9933668): `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/FFI.rs:2209-2229` runs `Command::new("cargo") build` directly for the generated bridge crate; `:2703-2725` accepts any `name@version`; `:3439-3457` writes plain `[dependencies]` registry lines. No sandbox, trust, lock, integrity, advisory, or maturity step touches this path, and `which cargo` under jet-env is the plain toolchain binary. `extern rust "base64@0.22"` compiles and runs on `jet run` and `jet build`. A transitive crate's `build.rs` or proc-macro therefore executes on the host before Jet can say anything. That is the 2026-08-20 `arrayref 0.3.10` / `proc-macro1` compile-time backdoor (RUSTSEC-2026-0260; Rust Foundation post 2026-08-20). E0704's copy says "crates that need … a build script aren't supported yet" (`FFI.rs:2275-2276`), but cargo runs the script before E0704 can fire. On `jet run` an unresolvable crate reports E0956 "report this as a compiler bug" while `jet build` reports E0704, so a user error gets compiler-bug copy on one tier.

Expected (ratified): `docs/spec/spec.md:3020-3035`: Core Cargo actions run inside the same Bubblewrap boundary as every other executable action, and host Cargo is never an unsandboxed fallback (D-JPK-SANDBOX2, D-JPK-BUILDSCRIPT1, E1275/L0205). Bridge crates pass the same lock (E1217), integrity (E2604), advisory (E2603), and maturity (E2609, D-JPK-FRESHNESS1=D) gates as any dependency, with a receipt visible to `jet inspect audit` and `jet inspect sbom`.

Non-goals: keep the S50 inline `extern rust "crate@version"` spelling; never execute the incident packages; keep imported `build.jet` inert (`crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:2796-2799`, `:3592-3598`, proven inert by probe).

Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-uQV6hYwyjMY/ffi-base64-project, ffi-project; second-reader source check 2026-09-01; mine report docs/audits/video-mine-never-operators-supply-chain-2026-09-01.md. Source: Low Level, "a lot of people are upset" (video mine). Refs #427, #398.
cards.plan:
Actual: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/FFI.rs:2209-2229 runs `Command::new("cargo") build` on the host for the generated bridge crate; `:2703-2725` accepts any `name@version`; `:3439-3457` writes plain registry `[dependencies]` lines. No sandbox, lock, integrity, advisory, or maturity step touches the path, so a transitive `build.rs` or proc-macro runs on the host before Jet can refuse (the arrayref incident, RUSTSEC-2026-0260). E0704 says build scripts are unsupported, but cargo has already run them. `jet run` reports E0956 for an unresolvable crate while `jet build` reports E0704. Expected (docs/spec/spec.md:3020-3035, D-JPK-SANDBOX2, D-JPK-BUILDSCRIPT1): the bridge cargo build runs only inside the same Bubblewrap boundary as every other executable action (E1275 or L0205 when the sandbox is unavailable), bridge crates pass the lock (E1217), integrity (E2604), advisory (E2603), and maturity (E2609) gates, a receipt is visible to `jet inspect audit` and `jet inspect sbom`, and both tiers report the same E0704 for an unresolvable crate.

Steps:
1. Measure step 0 from the old plan and record it in the log: does a registry-backed `jet fetch` provision the signed advisory feed so `jet inspect audit` runs with zero configuration? If not, `jet inspect audit` on a bridge crate reports E2611 (missing advisory DB) exactly as it does for any dependency today; no ballot is needed, the existing default stands.

cards.title: Diagnostic copy contradicts ratified law: E0041, E2511, E0301, E0907, E0109, and the core-library concurrency page
cards.body:
Five diagnostics teach something Jet no longer does or never did. Copy is the product (I4).

- E0041 (`mutex()`): Why says "Jet avoids shared mutable state: tasks communicate by sending messages, not sharing memory". Jet ships `Shared<T>`, `SharedGuard<T>`, and `Condition` (`docs/spec/spec.md:587-640`, D-SHAREDGUARD1). Copy at `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/direct_calls.rs:932-968`; rows `docs/spec/diagnostics.md:1307-1309`. Expected: raw mutex vocabulary points to channels first (beginner) and names `Shared`/`Condition` as the expert route.
- E2511 (`Vec3 * Float`): Why says operator overloading is "blessed on the closed built-in math family ONLY"; D-OPDEF1=A ships user hooks. `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:2950-2952` repeats the stale claim. Expected: state the same-lane rule, name the `splat` route, and acknowledge user hooks.
- E0301 (`impl Int.Mul { … }`): says "`Int` names a type that doesn't exist … define `struct Int` first". Expected: built-in types do not take user impls, with the route (named method, or the D-OPMIX1 outcome).
- E0907 (`fn mul(self, rhs: Int)` under `Mul`): "impl methods must match the trait signature exactly" without showing the expected signature. Expected: show `fn mul(self, rhs: Money) Money`.
- E0109 (`3 * money`): fix "make both sides the same type" is not actionable for a user type. Expected: name the owning type's hook or a named method.
- `docs/reference/core-library.md:2912-2915` says "no mutex API" without pointing at `Shared`/`Condition`; add the cross-link and a `Shared`/`Condition` example under `examples/features/`.

Non-goals: no new APIs; the E0704 copy belongs to the extern-rust bridge card.

Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-kHpEolpE3pU/mutex_invalid.jet; ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-main/op_hetero.jet, op_reflected.jet, op_extend_int.jet, lane_scale.jet; mine report docs/audits/video-mine-never-operators-supply-chain-2026-09-01.md. Sources: Semicolon (Condvar) and Indently (NotImplemented) video mines.

E2511 (`Vec3 * Float`) says overloading is blessed on the built-in math family only while D-OPDEF1 = A ships user hooks (docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:2950-2952 repeats it). E0301 (`impl Int.Mul`) says `Int` does not exist. E0907 does not show the expected signature. E0109 (`3 * money`) says make both sides the same type. docs/reference/core-library.md:2912-2915 says "no mutex API" without pointing at `Shared` and `Condition`. cards.title: Lint: unbounded loop polling Shared state (busy-wait), with a fix to Condition or channel receive
cards.body:
Actual: `loop flag.ready == false {}` against a `Shared<Flag>` compiles with zero diagnostics and burns a core (AOT witness: user+sys 0.49 s of a 0.50 s producer delay). The idiomatic forms, `guard.wait(condition, predicate)` (`docs/spec/spec.md:635-640`) and channel receive, park the task and complete the same producer/consumer program.

Expected: a registered advisory lint for an unbounded loop whose condition reads `Shared` state and whose body has no blocking call, with a fix pointing at `Condition` or a channel receive, a `jet fix` safe fix where the rewrite is mechanical, and deny/allow through the existing lint policy. Runtime behavior is unchanged; deliberate spin code stays legal. Sibling of L0202/L0206 (`docs/spec/diagnostic-rows.md:195-199`). Structural prevention over prose warnings (owner guidance 14).

Non-goals: no universal CPU threshold; finite loops, loops that mutate the polled state, and loops with a blocking call or sleep are not flagged; no new runtime API.

Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-kHpEolpE3pU/busy_spin.jet, condition_basic.jet, channel_basic.jet; mine report docs/audits/video-mine-never-operators-supply-chain-2026-09-01.md. Source: Semicolon, Rust Condvar Explained (video mine).

cards.title: Design: named non-returning contract (`Never` in return position), ballot D-NEVER2
cards.body:
D-NEVER1=C (2026-08-04) ratified a compiler-only bottom fact and wrote: "Experts who need a named non-returning contract would need a later ballot." This card carries that ballot.

Evidence now on the table: Rust merged `!` stabilization for 1.100 after ten years and five attempts (rust-lang/rust PR #155499, with `Infallible = !`), driven by library signatures and generic code; Jet users can already write `Never` because it is the failure-domain name in `Int !Never`, and writing it as a return type today is an ICE; the C sample itself does not compile yet (bug card "Divergence does not flow through calls"). The bottom-fact bug card is independent of this ballot and is not blocked by it.

Evidence: mine report docs/audits/video-mine-never-operators-supply-chain-2026-09-01.md. Source: Let's Get Rusty, Rust just introduced a new "never" type (video mine).
cards.plan:
Ratified law: D-NEVER2 = B (2026-09-02). A function may write `Never` as its return type; the compiler checks that every path stops. Functions without the word keep the inferred bottom fact of D-NEVER1 = C. No new spelling: `Never` is already TYPE_NEVER in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs as the failure-domain name; the return position gains a ratified meaning under this id. Read the picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show D-NEVER2 --json` for the exact rules and the worked code.

Actual: writing `Never` as a return type is an ICE; divergence does not flow through calls (the separate bug card named in the body). Expected: the forms and checks below on every tier.

Rules to implement, in the ratified words:
- Legal forms: `fn usage() Never`, `fn serve(addr: String) Never !NetError`, and the function type `fn() Never`. Illegal: `Never` as a parameter, field, stored value, or generic argument; each is a registered diagnostic with its span.
- Sema requires every path of a declared function to diverge. Three exits are errors with their span: falling off the end, a bare `return`, and `return value`. `return Err(e)` is valid. A bare `loop { }` with no `break` satisfies an expected `Never` (narrow amendment of the E0073 loop-value rule for that case only).
- Calls: a completed call to `fn f() Never !E` has failed, so `f() ?? x` yields `x` and the success side is eliminated. A function value typed `fn() Never` rejects a returning function at the assignment. A trait method declared `Never` binds implementations to the same check.
- A public function that always stops without the word gets an advisory lint (a registered L-code with a fix that adds `Never`).
- ApiFreeze serializes both the declared and the inferred fact.

Steps:
1. Register the new diagnostics (declared-Never path returns; `Never` in an illegal position; the advisory lint) per docs/spec/diagnostics.md "Adding a diagnostic", with what, why, and fix from the ballot's worked code, in crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs and docs/spec/diagnostic-rows.md.
2. Parser: accept `Never` in the return slot of a function declaration and a function type (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Types.rs and Items/functions_params.rs); reject the illegal positions.
3. Sema: the divergence check on declared functions, the `??` elimination, the function-value assignment check, and the trait-method binding (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/, beside the existing D-NEVER1 bottom-fact code; find it with `grep -rn "NEVER1" crates/jet-sema/src`). ApiFreeze carries both facts.
4. Backends: AOT emits `-> !` or an uninhabited carrier for a declared `Never` function; JIT and interpreter need no new arm beyond accepting the type (every path already stops). No `jit_gaps` entry.
5. Syntax.rs: add the D-NEVER2 entry to the TYPE_NEVER row (I7); `jet self devtools grammars`; add the ratified rule to docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md.
6. Fixtures: tests/ui/ snapshots for each new diagnostic; a tier-parity test in tests/tail_return_parity.rs or a new tests/never_return.rs (register in tests/suites.txt) with the ballot's worked program (`usage`, `count`, `run_then_stop`, `serve`) printing byte-identical output on AOT, default `jet run`, `jet eval`, and `--interpret`. Example under examples/features/functions/ with golden output.

Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test never_return --test diagnostic_snapshots --test syntax_reconciliation --test golden -- functions` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet check` on the ballot's `almost` and `keep` programs prints the two new diagnostics.

Writable paths: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/{Types.rs,Items/functions_params.rs}, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/ (divergence and call checks, ApiFreeze), crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/ (declared-Never emit), crates/jet-foundation/src/{Syntax.rs,Registry.rs}, tests/never_return.rs, tests/ui/, tests/suites.txt, examples/features/functions/, docs/spec/{syntax-decisions.md,diagnostics.md,diagnostic-rows.md}, generated grammar files. Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: the worked program runs on AOT, default `jet run`, `jet eval`, and `--interpret` with identical output; web is not applicable (no browser surface in the program).

Non-goals: no requirement to write `Never` (option C was not picked); no change to the failure-domain meaning of `Never`; the "divergence does not flow through calls" bug keeps its own card.

cards.title: Design: mixed-type operands for operator hooks and lane types under one rule, ballot D-OPMIX1
cards.body:
D-OPDEF1=A hooks are same-type only: the synthetic traits are `fn add(&self, rhs: &Self) -> Self` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:2399-2419`). Live today: `impl Money.Mul { fn mul(self, rhs: Int) Money }` is rejected (E0907), `3 * money` is E0109, `impl Int.Mul` is E0301, and the blessed lane family rejects `Vec3 * 2.0` (E2511; D-SIMD2/D-LINALG1 same-lane rule, `splat` for scalars). The most common operator uses in money, physics, and graphics code are mixed-type: value times count, vector times scalar, scalar times vector.

Python solves operand ownership at run time (`__radd__` plus the `NotImplemented` sentinel: order-dependent, and silently `False` when misused). Rust solves it statically (`Mul<Rhs>` plus the orphan rule). Jet has neither. This card carries ballot D-OPMIX1: one static rule for mixed-type operands across user hooks and Core lane types. The operator ABI bug card is independent of this ballot.

Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-main/op_hetero.jet, op_reflected.jet, op_extend_int.jet, lane_scale.jet; mine report docs/audits/video-mine-never-operators-supply-chain-2026-09-01.md. Source: Indently, "NotImplemented" is Awesome in Python (video mine).
cards.plan:
Ratified law: D-OPMIX1 = D (2026-09-02). A typed right side on operator hooks (`impl Money.Mul<Int>`), plus one mirror rule: when the left operand is a plain number (`Int`, `Float`, `Decimal`), the symbol is `+` or `*`, and the right type declares that hook for the number, the compiler swaps the sides and calls the hook. Nothing mirrors for `-` or `/`, and nothing mirrors when neither side is a plain number. The package that defines the right type may write an explicit hook on the number type (`impl Int.Sub<Money>`); an explicit hook always beats the mirror. Core declares `Vec3.Mul<Float>` and `Vec3.Div<Float>` and writes `Float.Div<Vec3>`; `2.0 * v` comes from the mirror. `jet inspect types` lists the mirror row under the owning type. Read the picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show D-OPMIX1 --json` for the resolution order, the coherence rule, and the worked program; #2434 (diagnostic copy) is a live lane on E0907, E0109, E2511, and E0301 copy, so land this card after it and re-touch only the rows this card changes.

Actual: hooks are same-type only (`fn add(&self, rhs: &Self) -> Self`, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:2399-2419); `impl Money.Mul { fn mul(self, rhs: Int) Money }` is E0907; `3 * money` is E0109; `impl Int.Mul` is E0301; `Vec3 * 2.0` is E2511. Expected: the ratified matrix on every tier.

Rules to implement, in the ratified words:
- Spelling: `Mul<Int>` on an impl header is the one new spelling. Syntax.rs entry under D-OPMIX1 (I7); amends the D-OPDEF1 same-operand clause in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md.
- Coherence: a hook on a built-in left type is legal only when its concrete right type is local to the declaring package; a generic or foreign right type stays E0902, whose what, why, and fix gain this case.
- Resolution order: built-in numeric widening (D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1) first; then (left, symbol, right), an explicit hook wins; if absent and left is `Int`, `Float`, or `Decimal` and the symbol is `+` or `*`, look up (right, symbol, left) and call it with the sides swapped; operands are evaluated left to right, once; the literal rule applies to the mirrored key; two fitting hooks ask for the type. The mirror returns the forward hook's declared result type. Compound assignment never mirrors (`n *= price` with `n: Int` stays rejected). Chains follow precedence: `2 * price * 3` is `(2 * price) * 3`.
- Generic bodies: a bound `T: Mul<Float>` admits only hooks that return `T`; `x * 2.0` and `2.0 * x` both have type `T`.
- The mirror is a sema resolution rule, not a marker; every tier sees the same resolved call (I9).

Steps:
1. Parser and sema: accept the typed hook header (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/enums_traits.rs or type_methods_fields.rs); synthesize the operator traits with a right-type parameter (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs:2399-2419 and the sema trait registration); implement the resolution order and the mirror in the binary-operator checker (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/, find it with `grep -rn "E0109" crates/jet-sema/src`); widen E0902 coherence for the local-right-type case.
2. TIR: the mirrored call lowers as the forward hook with swapped, once-evaluated operands, so AOT, JIT, and interpreter need no new arm beyond the typed trait shape. No `jit_gaps` entry.
3. Core lane types: declare `Vec3.Mul<Float>`, `Vec3.Div<Float>`, and `Float.Div<Vec3>` in the Prelude math part (find the lane family with `grep -rn "E2511" crates/`); `Vec3 * 2.0` and `2.0 * v` resolve; `v * m` stays E2511 with the ratified copy.
4. Diagnostics: E0907 shows the expected signature; E0109 and E2511 name the mirror rule and the explicit-hook route; E0902 gains the built-in-left case; snapshots re-blessed one at a time.
5. `jet inspect types` (Source/CmdInspect.rs) lists `Int * Money -> Money  mirror of Money.Mul<Int>` under `Money` and the explicit hook in its place when one exists.
6. Fixture: one operator matrix test (new tests/operator_matrix.rs, registered in tests/suites.txt) with the ballot's worked program on AOT, default `jet run`, `jet eval`, and `--interpret`, byte-identical output; the error lines of the worked program become tests/ui/ snapshots. Example under examples/features/operators/ with golden output. Syntax.rs entry, `jet self devtools grammars`, syntax-decisions.md rule.

Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test operator_matrix --test impl_shape_matrix --test diagnostic_snapshots --test syntax_reconciliation --test golden -- operators` green.

Writable paths: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/ (operator checking, trait registration, coherence), crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs (synthetic traits), the Prelude math and lane parts under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/, crates/jet-foundation/src/{Syntax.rs,Registry.rs}, Source/CmdInspect.rs, tests/operator_matrix.rs, tests/impl_shape_matrix.rs, tests/ui/, tests/suites.txt, examples/features/operators/, docs/spec/{syntax-decisions.md,diagnostics.md,diagnostic-rows.md}, generated grammar files. Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: the matrix fixture runs on AOT, default `jet run`, `jet eval`, and `--interpret`.

Non-goals: no reverse hook lint or fix (option E was not picked); no mirror for `-`, `/`, or two non-number types; no bound spelling for a third result type (a separate ballot); the operator ABI bug keeps its own card.

questions.text: How can we eliminate/mitigate the tradeoff for option D? Seems like the best option but I think with a bit more thought we can eliminate the downside.
questions.answer: Done in option D. The downside was the hand-written second hook plus the reading cost of a hook living on Int. Both are removed. (1) When a package declares an Add or Mul hook whose right side is a built-in number and writes no reverse hook, a lint fires at that declaration; its fix writes the one-line delegating reverse hook with the forward hook's own result type. Plain `jet fix` reports it as skipped because it changes the package's public surface (api-changing class, per D-REPORT-FIXGRADE1); `jet fix --all` or the editor's code action applies it, and the author owns the line. Sub and Div get no fix because their reverse needs its own body (`2.0 / v` is a reciprocal, not a delegation). (2) `jet inspect types` lists both directions under the Money row, so nobody hunts for a hook on Int. This keeps D's core property (every direction is a real function, no trusted symmetry claim, no rewrite) and drops the boilerplate. The rival-family pass on this revision found two facts the ballot had wrong, now fixed in D: today's coherence rule rejects every operator impl with a non-local left type, so D explicitly amends E0902 to allow a built-in left type when the right type is local; and a generic body cannot spell `2.0 * x` because S45 has no bound on a concrete left type, so generic code writes `x * 2.0`. Residual: one visible delegating line per reversed scalar hook, and the forward-only rule inside generic bodies.

cards.title: Test loop: watch mode with failed-first rerun, output capture control, cache bypass, filter expressions, doctests in the normal loop
cards.body: Cargo test, Go test, Bacon, cargo-watch, and cargo-nextest show a correction loop that stays quiet until output is requested, can rerun fresh, includes documentation tests, watches dependencies, focuses failures, and selects tests structurally. This card covers the census features Explicit test-output capture control, Deterministic test-cache bypass, Documentation tests in the normal test loop, Background checker TUI with ordered errors and job switching, Failure-focused rerun, Dependency-aware test predicates, and Dependency-aware watch. It keeps Jet's existing test, filter, and dev surfaces while routing new flags and job behavior through D-DX-TESTUX1.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:817-822` registers `jet test` and its positional filter; `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1550-1557` exposes filter, shuffle, serial, measure, and record but no output-capture or explicit fresh-cache control. `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:963-968` exposes `jet doc`, while `diagnostic-rows.md:358` documents top-level `#Test` collection and no shipped doctest runner is evidenced. `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:867-872` and `:1483-1485` expose `jet dev`/watch behavior, but the census finds no persistent checker TUI, job switcher, failure-focus action, or structured dependency predicate.
Expected: after owner ratification, one normal `jet test` loop keeps passing output quiet, offers an explicit capture control, bypasses only test-result caching while reusing build artifacts, runs checked documentation examples with source identity, preserves the simple substring filter, and adds structured predicates without hiding package authority. `jet dev` or its test watcher keeps a persistent checker surface, orders actionable failures first, remembers the failing test for a focused rerun, and returns to the full suite without losing the watch graph or last-good result.
Decision: author D-DX-TESTUX1 before implementation; the ballot chooses capture and quiet-default policy, fresh-test semantics, doctest inclusion, failure-focus behavior, and structural filter controls without inventing syntax here.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs`, the existing test-runner/watch implementation, `tests/`, and the test-loop specification or command reference.
Dependencies: D-DX-TESTUX1; preserve the existing `jet test`, `--filter`, `jet dev`, and dependency-aware watch contracts.
Non-goals: do not make passing tests noisy, delete build caches for a fresh test, replace the compiler build graph, or run documentation generators as hidden test side effects.
Invariants: failed runs remain nonzero and source-local; capture, cache freshness, filter selection, doctest selection, and watch/job state are independently observable; focused reruns retain package and authority context; a failed rebuild leaves the last-good execution visible.
Proof command: `scripts/agent/jet-env jet --help` plus the targeted test-loop tests and a PTY smoke of the watcher.

cards.title: Diagnostics rendering parity measured against rustc, miette, Zig, and Go
cards.body: rustc, miette, Zig, and Go provide reference behaviors for stable codes, source labels, narrated fallback, editor protocol, and machine-readable events, while Jet's E0113 probe already shows a source-local What/Why/Fix path. This card covers the census features Statistics-driven benchmark history and named baselines; Workspace-wide command with shared lock and target cache; Named feature flags with additive defaults and explicit activation; Machine-readable build and diagnostic event stream; Contextual inlay hints for inferred types and argument names; Automatic imports and completion actions; Editor lightbulb assists and local refactoring; Run, benchmark, related-test, and rename actions at cursor; One-command interactive flamegraph profiling; Multi-file and multiline labels with width-aware rendering; Build-script options appear in generated help; Go test filter, list, and package-aware execution; Machine-readable interleaved build and test events; Multi-module workspace with use/sync commands; Interactive profile analysis with top/list/web/disasm views; Official LSP with diagnostics, completion, analysis, and refactoring; Named background processes and task execution in the development environment; Built-in LSP with one semantic source of truth; and Package/workspace authority and reproducible environment boundary. It measures before changing behavior so every loss has a reproducible rendering, an evidence locator, and a separate follow-up card rather than an unsupported parity claim.
cards.plan:

cards.title: Job graph: dependencies, freshness, bounded parallel runs on #Job metadata
cards.body: Bacon, just, mise, and devenv make project work discoverable through named jobs, dependency graphs, freshness checks, bounded parallelism, grouped output, and process lifecycle controls. This card covers the census features Project command runner with recipes, static errors, listing, and completion; Validated recipe parameters with defaults, variadics, regex, and generated usage; Declarative task graph with parallel dependencies and source/output freshness; Watch and inspect task execution with explicit output modes; and Named background processes and task execution in the development environment. Jet's existing #Job registry and build graph remain the authority, while D-DX-JOBGRAPH1 decides whether new user-task metadata belongs on that graph.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:794` lists jobs, `:867-872` exposes dev/watch, and `:389-394` exposes the compiler build graph; these are not yet a user-task graph with freshness or bounded parallel execution. `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1483-1485` exposes watch controls, while `:452-465` and `:978-985` expose environment actions; the census finds no recipe registry, task dependency listing, output grouping, source/output freshness registry, or named process lifecycle proof.
Expected: after D-DX-JOBGRAPH1, #Job declarations can name typed dependencies, inputs, outputs, freshness rules, bounded parallel limits, output grouping, watch behavior, and cancellation semantics without weakening the core job contract from #2422. The graph validates unknown and cyclic dependencies before execution, reports why a job is fresh or stale, schedules independent jobs within the configured bound, preserves package authority and evidence identity, and exposes a readable graph/status view. If project recipes and named processes are included, their arguments, usage, start/stop state, and CI checks use the same typed job records instead of opaque shell aliases.
Decision: author D-DX-JOBGRAPH1 before implementation; it decides whether non-build tasks join the typed graph, what metadata is required, and how bounded parallelism, output grouping, freshness, watch, and process lifecycle are surfaced.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs`, the existing #Job and build-graph implementation, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/`, `tests/`, and the job or package specifications.
Dependencies: core jobs card #2422 and ballot D-DX-JOBGRAPH1.
Non-goals: do not replace the compiler build graph, make arbitrary shell execution the default, silently infer dependencies from log text, or broaden this card into directory environment activation.
Invariants: #Job identity, package authority, effects, and evidence remain explicit; dependency cycles and unknown names fail before side effects; freshness uses declared source/output facts; parallelism is bounded and cancellable; grouped output remains attributable to a job; watch reruns only stale work; a failed job never reports the graph as successful.
Proof command: `scripts/agent/jet-env jet --help` plus the job-graph and PTY lifecycle tests.

cards.title: Explicit source generation loop with audit trail
cards.body: Go generate keeps source-adjacent generation explicit, ordered, and separate from build and test, while Jet currently exposes emit/eval without a source-driven generation command. This card covers the census feature Explicit source-driven code generation and binds each generated input to package authority, provenance, and a reproducible receipt. D-DX-GENERATE1 must choose the user-facing surface before any syntax or generator mechanism is implemented.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1130-1145` exposes emit/eval but no source-driven generation command; `docs/spec/architecture.md:92` describes a typed `BuildRecipe` rather than directive execution. The census marks Explicit source-driven code generation as a real gap and requires generation to remain explicit, source-ordered, and absent from implicit build/test side effects.
Expected: after owner ratification, a source-adjacent declaration names an authorized generator and its inputs, and an explicit invocation produces deterministic source files plus an audit receipt containing generator identity, source location, inputs, outputs, package authority, and toolchain/provenance facts. Preview or dry-run output must show the planned writes before mutation; rerunning unchanged inputs is a no-op or an identical receipt; build and test never invoke generation implicitly.
Decision: author D-DX-GENERATE1 before implementation; the ballot chooses whether Jet supports source-driven generation, the declaration and invocation surface, authority requirements, ordering, preview behavior, and receipt format without inventing syntax here.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs`, the existing emit/eval and package/provenance implementation, `crates/jet-codegen/src/`, `tests/`, and the generation or architecture specifications.
Dependencies: D-DX-GENERATE1; preserve the package authority and reproducibility boundaries in `docs/spec/architecture.md:91-96,266-289`.
Non-goals: do not execute arbitrary directives during build or test, hide shell commands behind a compiler hook, overwrite user source without an audit record, or make generated output a substitute for typed package declarations.
Invariants: invocation is explicit and reviewable; generator identity, inputs, outputs, order, authority, and toolchain are recorded; no partial output survives a failed generation; unchanged inputs are reproducible; build/test remain free of generation side effects; generated files remain attributable to their package and workspace.
Proof command: the explicit-generation CLI smoke test and the source-generation audit tests.

cards.title: Mobile dev loop design: doctor, device inventory, one-command run, reload semantics, inspector, structured logs
cards.body: Flutter, Expo, and React Native shorten the first path with SDK/editor quick start and DartPad, First-run project scaffold, Toolchain doctor, Device and emulator inventory, Real-device first setup and Expo Go, and One command to start and target a device. Development-client launcher and network inspector, State-preserving hot reload, Explicit hot restart and full restart boundaries, Reload failure and recovery diagnostics, Fast Refresh error recovery, and Default Hermes engine and release bytecode define safe edit and runtime boundaries. Widget tree selection and inspector, Frame timeline and jank diagnosis, Third-party DevTools extension tabs, Custom inspector tool scaffold, and Integrated console and source debugger define one inspection loop. The design reuses Jet's `core.ui`, Canvas, and authority model; it ballots the contract before #480, then waits for mobile targets and device evidence.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Deliver the ratified D-DX-MOBILELOOP1=A mobile dev loop as one NativeDevHost session under `jet dev`. This covers doctor, device inventory, one-command run, checked live edits, pixel inspector, and the typed devtools stream. The work starts only when native mobile is promoted.

## Current state
- Blocked: #480 (E3-UL9 mobile native UI + store pipeline) is `frozen`, and D-VERDICT-480-1 defers native mobile until the owner explicitly promotes it. D-DX-MOBILELOOP1=A does not lift that.
- Retained host anchors exist: `crates/jet-devserver/src/NativeSwap.rs`, `crates/jet-devserver/src/WatchService.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Ui.rs` (JetUiNode render path), `Source/CmdDevTools.rs`, and `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs`. All sit inside the retained host boundary (dev server, CLI host, Prelude UI), so none needs retargeting to Compiler/.
- No `tests/mobile_*.rs` exists yet.

## Changes (after #480 is promoted)
1. Doctor and inventory: extend the existing doctor handler with SDK/toolchain, simulator/emulator, physical pairing, transport, permission and signing readiness. Add the ratified device inventory. By default, select only one trusted local simulator/emulator. Physical and network devices need a qualified explicit ID, and ambiguity stops. Missing prerequisites fail before build with a registered diagnostic, and secrets never reach output.
2. Session: attach `jet dev` target selection to #480's NativeDevHost. Report checking, waiting, building, connecting, ready, reconnecting, rejected and stopped. Record target, session, revision, runtime, build and codegen identity.
3. Live edits: route through NativeSwap/WatchService and classify each edit as compatible, incompatible or native-affecting. Preserve only declared, checked live values. A restart or rebuild reports its reason, the discarded values and the reconnect path.
4. Inspector: a selected pixel resolves to its canonical JetUiNode, source span, geometry and temporary-layout flag. Frame/jank facts link to source, labelled debug or release-like.
5. Devtools: publish console, source, frame, request and custom facts through `jet.devtools.v1`. Use authority-scoped removable subscriptions, and a reconnect exposes gaps. Production compiles these channels out, following D-DX-PLUGIN1=D and D-DX-DEVTOOLS-UX1=D.
6. Authority: the probe stays fail-closed with E1803 and `authority.holds` remediation.
7. Measure cold and warm loop timings per device class. Migrate every mobile caller and delete temporary duplicates.

## Proof
Once #480 lands, run `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test mobile_loop_contract`, then `mobile_live_loop`, `mobile_runtime`, `mobile_inspector` and `mobile_devtools_extensions`. Each passes on at least one real simulator/emulator class, with unavailable classes reported as unavailable. Then run `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx/mobile/probes/ui_probe.jet`: it exits with E1803 naming the required effects and `authority.holds`. Criterion 6 cites the stale `scripts/agent/jet-env` path; use `Tools/agent/jet-env`.

## Batch
`batch-deferred`: owner-deferred mobile (e13) behind frozen #480.

## Dependencies
#480 (frozen; needs owner promotion under D-VERDICT-480-1).

Planned proof only; not run during preparation. Rebuild before compiler/runtime smoke. Run repository commands through scripts/agent/jet-env. Use exact narrow criterion evidence; broad suites remain milestone-gated.

7. `scripts/agent/jet-env jet --help` and generated completion/man output — only the ballot-selected public command and flags appear; no stale `jet mobile` or nonexistent `jet inspect dev` surface remains if Option A wins.
8. Record benchmark observations under `docs/benchmarks/dx/` — every supported target class and profile has cold/warm and reconnect evidence, while unsupported hardware is explicitly marked unavailable.

cards.title: Mobile scaffold, build profiles, signing, and destinations
cards.body: Flutter, Expo, Xcode, Android Studio, and Kotlin Multiplatform show why First-run project scaffold and Cloud build profiles and signing belong to one checked mobile workspace with an explicit destination. File-based typed universal routing makes targets and deep links visible; Network request recorder and query filters, Dev Menu, LogBox, and device shortcuts, Network panel with explicit limits, Components inspector and React Profiler, and Performance timeline and heap tooling keep diagnosis near the running app. Jet already has package and build facts, a typed UI tree, Canvas source projection, and fail-closed authority diagnostics, but no mobile artifact or signing path. D-DX-MOBILEBUILD1 separates the manifest and provenance ballot from target-backed implementation, which waits for #480.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Keep the mobile scaffold, profile, signing-reference, destination, artifact and provenance plan ready without starting native mobile work. Apply D-DX-MOBILEBUILD1=A only after the owner promotes #480.

## Current state
- #480 (native mobile UI and store distribution) is frozen by owner verdict D-VERDICT-480-1 (Tower log 2026-09-11). Jet has no mobile artifact or signing path.
- The existing seams are the package target model, `BuildProfile`/`TargetProfileSelection`, `BuildRecipe`, the output envelope, the artifact store (`Jetpack/Store/Source/ArtifactStore/`) and provenance.
- None of the criteria's proof files (`tests/mobile_build.rs`, `mobile_routes.rs`, `mobile_devtools.rs`, `mobile_perf.rs`) exist yet.

## Changes (after promotion only)
1. `package.jet` profiles own the mobile target, backend, signing reference, generated-native owner, toolchain and destination. CLI flags select declared facts and cannot invent or override them. There is no `mobile.jet` and no second loader.
2. Build and record one artifact with source, package, target, profile, backend, recipe, toolchain, generated-native hash, artifact hash and external signing identity reference. A missing SDK, account, destination, signer, entitlement or generated output stops before publication with redacted facts only.
3. Consume #2443's devtools/session identity. Dev Menu, LogBox, network capture (bounded and redacted), typed-tree inspection, profiling and heap data are development-only; production has no mobile devtools path under D-DX-PROD1=B.
4. Cut over scaffold, build, inspect, run, route, devtools, perf and ship to one provenance chain.

## Proof
After promotion: `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test mobile_build`, `--test mobile_routes`, `--test mobile_devtools` and `--test mobile_perf`, plus real Android and iOS artifact, signing and destination evidence. Preparation must not install, sign, upload or run a device. All six criteria stay open and unweakened.

## Batch
batch-deferred: owner-frozen dependency.

## Dependencies
#480 (frozen by owner verdict), and #2443's dev-loop identity.

cards.title: Reactive notebook: dependent-cell rerun, typed controls, rich outputs, delete-cell scrubbing
cards.body: Jupyter's one kernel and rich cell outputs are useful, while marimo and Pluto make dependency order and deletion visible instead of relying on notebook history. The census features Reactive dependent-cell execution, Delete-cell state scrubbing, and Persistent kernel after browser close define the loop Jet must close; Function arguments automatically become interactive controls supplies typed controls and Multiline code, markdown cells, and rich attached output keeps explanation beside results. Jet should keep one typed evaluator, make stale and effect decisions explicit, and reconnect only with identity and authority checks.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-repl/src/Notebook/document.rs:145-176` computes closure keys and transitive invalidation; `crates/jet-repl/src/Notebook/kernel.rs:32-35,338-381` has rerun decisions and stale IDs; `tests/notebook.rs:44-131,192-321` covers ordered state cells, MIME projections, and cache behavior; `crates/jet-repl/src/Notebook/trust.rs:1-40` has MIME/trust primitives. The live census records `Source/CmdDevTools.rs:466-471` as a dev snapshot rather than a reconnectable resident kernel, `docs/spec/architecture.md:451-466` as compiler invalidation rather than user-facing cell execution, and `docs/spec/roadmap.md:288-297` as having no namespace cleanup contract. `docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:304-306` is the existing notebook/UI target and `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:6027-6047` records notebook source and trust constraints.
Expected: after owner ballot D-DX-CELLS1, checked cell definitions form a dependency graph; a defining edit reruns only affected descendants or marks them stale under the selected lazy policy, typed arguments expose safe controls, rich results stay attached to their cells, and deletion scrubs bindings before dependents rerun or report stale/error. One bounded kernel survives browser reconnection with source/build identity and authority checks.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-repl/src/Notebook/{document.rs,kernel.rs,protocol.rs,trust.rs}`, `Source/CmdNotebook.rs`, and notebook integration tests.
Dependencies: author and ratify D-DX-CELLS1; reuse the existing notebook protocol and trust/quarantine contracts; do not invent a second evaluator.
Non-goals: implicit global mutation tracking, hidden namespace history, release-time reactive execution, or a new package/environment manager.
Invariants: source remains canonical; each definition has one owner; stale output is never presented as current; controls and rich outputs carry typed effect/trust status; reconnect cannot bypass authority.
Proof command: `cargo test --test notebook` and the bounded headless probe `scripts/agent/jet-env jet notebook --headless`.

cards.title: Run a notebook or typed function as a local app
cards.body: marimo turns a notebook into a local app, Streamlit turns a script into a local server, and Gradio maps a typed function to controls and outputs. The census features Run a notebook as a web app with layouts and galleries, Script-to-local-web-app launch, and One-call interface for arbitrary functions set the target. Jet should reuse the notebook kernel and trust receipts so a local app is a projection, not a second evaluator.

Each client receives an isolated typed session with ordered callbacks; reconnect, reset, local/public bind, and data movement are explicit and machine-readable.
Writable paths: `Source/CmdNotebook.rs`, `crates/jet-repl/src/Notebook/{kernel.rs,protocol.rs,trust.rs}`, the devserver app host, and notebook-app integration tests.

Invariants: typed function signatures remain the input/output contract; loopback is the default bind; every session has an identity and authority boundary; source and build identity are visible; cache data and shared resources are separate.

cards.title: Lazy table plans on every tier with plan and streaming inspector
cards.body: Polars makes a table pipeline lazy, checks schema before processing, and exposes optimizer and streaming plans. The census features Lazy query execution with schema checks before processing, Automatic query optimization and explainable pushdown, and Streaming collection and physical-plan graph inspection are gaps above Jet's typed `DataLazyFrame` and bounded `DataStream`. This card closes the execution gap while preserving the shared `DataStats.rs`, typed schema, limit, and structured-error contracts.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:780-797` defines a bounded pull `DataStream`, while `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:844-856` defines `DataLazyFrame` with only filter and sort operations. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/data_calls.rs:461-466` rejects lazy, plan, collect, and readers in the default evaluator; `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:3881-3891` ratifies lazy plans without the execution path. The shared-kernel baseline is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/DataStats.rs:44-105` with coverage in `tests/dataflow_stream.rs:53-181`.
Expected: typed scans and transformations build a lazy logical plan, perform schema preflight, optimize to an explainable physical plan, and collect either bounded in memory or in streaming batches with explicit fallback. AOT, default `jet run`, the interpreter, and the web tier where applicable marshal one semantic implementation and agree on rows, schema, limits, errors, and plan facts under I9.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/data_calls.rs`, the shared data Prelude, the inspect/devtools projection, and data parity tests.
Dependencies: none; this card is ready under the ratified data contracts and must not wait for an owner syntax ballot.
Non-goals: a full SQL console, a plugin ABI, unbounded memory use, or replacing the existing bounded reader stream with an opaque fallback.
Invariants: one semantic implementation serves every applicable tier; schema errors occur before processing; limits and hostile-input errors remain structured; logical, physical, and fallback choices are inspectable; streaming never silently becomes an unbounded collect.
Proof command: `cargo test --test dataflow_stream --test data_hostile` plus the I9 parity test.

cards.title: Data loaders with deterministic snapshots and invalidation
cards.body: Observable Framework's polyglot loaders turn ordinary files into deterministic snapshots, invalidate only affected routes, and make archive members addressable. The census features Polyglot data loaders produce static snapshots, File-routed loader cache and archive attachments, and Static site architecture keeps viewer data access local and precomputed define the required source, cache, and credential boundaries. Jet should add these facts to its existing watch graph without hiding a second data store.
cards.plan:
Actual: `docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:590-595` lists SQL, Arrow, Parquet, and streaming gaps; `docs/plans/epoch-3/universal-language-core.md:312-318` covers invalidation inputs but not loader outputs or archive members. `Source/CmdNotebook.rs:39-105` has the local notebook server but no loader publication path; `crates/jet-repl/src/Notebook/document.rs:179-214` has closure-keyed notebook output caching, not loader snapshots; `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:6027-6047` establishes source, cache, and trust constraints.
Expected: after owner ballot D-DX-LOADERS1, a typed loader declaration identifies its source files, archive members, parameters, and credential scope; the loader writes a deterministic snapshot with provenance and content identity. The incremental graph runs only referenced loaders, invalidates affected snapshots on source or input changes, isolates secrets, and exposes local preview, stale, error, and cleanup status.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-devserver/src/WatchService.rs`, `Source/CmdNotebook.rs`, `crates/jet-repl/src/Notebook/document.rs`, the typed data Prelude, and loader integration tests.
Dependencies: author and ratify D-DX-LOADERS1; reuse the existing watch graph, notebook source/cache law, trust/quarantine receipts, and typed data limits.
Non-goals: arbitrary polyglot execution without an explicit bridge, remote warehouse access by default, publication adapters, or a hidden data database behind an inspector.
Invariants: source and declared inputs are canonical; snapshot identity is deterministic; credentials never enter snapshot bytes or logs; archive members are first-class dependencies; stale data is visible and cannot masquerade as current; cleanup removes unreferenced artifacts.
Proof command: `cargo test --test data_loaders`.

Jet already has `jet prove` capture and replay identity plus named `jet dev --record=<name>`, but it has no bounded timeline that can scrub, jump, skip, and report first divergence. cards.body: Pharo's `Live object inspector and Do it`, CIDER's `Source-buffer definition evaluation`, Portal's `Tap stream data inspector` and `Return selected inspector value to REPL`, and Godot's `Debugger evaluator REPL` make a paused value a direct question surface. cards.title: Reverse step, watchpoints, and fix-and-continue in jet debug
cards.body: rr's `Reverse execution with data watchpoints`, Redux DevTools' `Jump, skip, and reorder history`, and Pharo's `Debugger-driven method creation` show three ways to move from a bad value to its cause or a checked fix. Jet's debugger has source-level `step`, `next`, `continue`, and `finish`, and replay artifacts have ordered frames, but no reverse search, watchpoint history, or fix-and-continue path. This card chooses those controls and their authority boundary before implementation.
cards.plan:
Actual: `docs/spec/roadmap.md:288-297` explicitly defers reversible execution and a standing variable history; `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:5397-5400` records source stepping and locals only; `docs/spec/proof-replay-decisions.md:116-142` defines replay frames and identity but not reverse indexing; `crates/jet-debug/src/lib.rs:87-115` models post-statement `RecordedAct` data and forward resume verbs.
Expected: Author D-DX-DEBUGBACK1 with `tower-ballot` to choose whether reverse, watchpoint, and fix-and-continue extend existing `jet debug` verbs or use a separate command surface. After the choice, index replay frames by source place and writes, let a watchpoint stop at prior writes, and allow a checked fix to resume only from a valid paused state; show the first unavailable reason when recording or indexing cannot support it.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-debug/src/lib.rs`, `Source/ProveReplay.rs`, `Source/CmdProve.rs`, `crates/jet-devserver/src/Canvas/debug_source_git.rs`, `crates/jet-canvas/src/js/input-events.js`, `tests/debug.rs`, and `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`.

Non-goals: No native CPU reverse execution outside recorded Jet runs, unbounded watch history, automatic source edits, or production reverse debugger.
Invariants: Reverse answers point to an exact sequence and source span. Missing or unsupported effects give an explicit unavailable result. A fix compiles and checks before resuming; a failed fix leaves paused history unchanged. Watchpoint scope and authority cannot escape the selected session.
Proof command: `cargo test --test debug` with the ratified `jet debug` transcript.

cards.title: Web module swap: preserve signals, stores, query cache, form drafts, scroll, and focus
cards.body: Vite's `Native-ESM dev server with module-level HMR` and Jet's `State-preserving hot swap` set the web loop target: update the changed module while keeping user state. Jet currently performs a full JS/WASM recompile and browser reload, although `Dependency-aware invalidation and warm reload` and `Last-good program after failed reload` already provide safe watch semantics. This card adds a `DomRuntime` swap path for signals, stores, query cache, form drafts, scroll, and focus, with a visible restart fallback.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs:5-10` says JS/WASM saves require a full recompile; `Source/CmdDevTools.rs:602-691` shows whole change rendering and transaction; `docs/reference/dev-dx-benchmark.md:12-29` measures Jet at 561.5 ms versus Vite at 54.9 ms for warm reload. The existing native path uses `Source/CmdDevTools.rs:625-675` for last-good transaction and `:696-707` for typed `#Persist`; `Source/CmdCompile.rs:6549-6695` and `crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs:3515-3669` perform web rebuild and page reload.
Expected: `DomRuntime.js` receives a module-level change and updates only the affected module; unchanged signals, stores, query-cache entries, form drafts, scroll, and focus retain identity. Server functions rebind, semantic diagnostics remain checked, and unsupported or layout changes announce a restart with kept and reset values; last-good output remains until a valid artifact is ready. Only the DOM runtime marshals web state, and the existing dev status reports the changed closure and tier.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js`, `Source/CmdCompile.rs`, `Source/CmdDevTools.rs`, `crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs`, `crates/jet-devserver/src/WatchService.rs`, `tests/web_dev.rs`, and `docs/reference/dev-dx-benchmark.md`.
Dependencies: `#2426` live-loop law; preserve the current dependency-aware watch, last-good transaction, and semantic diagnostics.
Non-goals: No native swap changes, unchecked TypeScript-like fast path, state preservation across type or layout changes, or release hot-module transport.
Invariants: Preserve values only when type and module identity permit. Server and client bindings and source revisions stay aligned. A failed build never replaces the last-good artifact. State and diagnostic payloads stay local, dev-only, and typed.
Proof command: `cargo test --test web_dev` and `scripts/agent/jet-env full node scripts/benchmarks/dev-dx.mjs`.

Jet already has `Type-stable module hot swap and layout restart`, but no restart trigger policy or `jet explain --reload`; `Method add/delete without restarting REPL` also lacks stale-reference semantics. This card keeps native server listeners and in-flight connections through safe swaps and reports every reset.
cards.plan:

Expected: Native `HotReplaceTxn` keeps listener handles, active connections, and typed `#Persist` state for type-compatible module edits; server and connection replacement is one commit. Unsupported edits produce a restart decision with reason, affected and reset values, source dependency, and `jet explain --reload`; `--restart`, `--swap`, and `--watch=off` remain explicit overrides. Removed definitions invalidate stale references and fail closed rather than calling old code.
Writable paths: `Source/CmdDevTools.rs`, `Source/CmdCompile.rs`, `crates/jet-devserver/src/WatchService.rs`, `crates/jet-devserver/src/Session.rs`, `crates/jet-devserver/src/lib.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DevServer.rs`, `tests/http_server_lifecycle.rs`, `tests/debug.rs`, and `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`.

Invariants: Listener identity and accepted connections stay valid on a successful compatible swap. Every reset or restart has a machine-readable reason and source identity. Failed compile or migration leaves the last-good session serving. Removed definitions cannot be called through stale references. Force flags do not hide diagnostics.

cards.title: Guided input: typed prompts and forms with validation and accessible non-TTY mode
cards.body: Bubbles' `Unicode text input with paste and scrolling` and Huh's `Interactive forms with pages and typed fields` plus `Field validation and accessible form mode` provide reusable guided input; Gum's `Shell-composable interactive commands` and `Environment-driven presentation customization` cover small scripts. cards.title: Human output primitives: capability detection, adaptive tables, progress, and a strict machine-output separation
cards.body: Rich's `Console capability detection, renderables, JSON, logging locals, and status`, `Adaptive tables with wrapping and borders`, and `Multi-task, transient, indeterminate, and custom-column progress`, together with Indicatif's `MultiProgress, non-terminal hiding, templates, and iterator adapters`, define the missing human-output layer. Jet already exposes `--json` and `--color` in the `jet --help` probe and has explicit NO_COLOR policy, while the E2102 probe demonstrates the exact diagnostic surface that must remain stable. This card adds typed renderables, width-aware tables, and bounded progress without allowing human presentation to contaminate machine output.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:155-207` proves JSON and terminal-aware color detection; `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1643-1671` contains help-only tables; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:579-604` implements NO_COLOR and terminal style policy; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:612-649` implements a line-oriented iterator progress path, not multi-task progress. `jet-help.txt:147-165` exposes `--json` and `--color`, and `jet-arg-error.txt:1-4` is the real exact diagnostic baseline.
Expected: add typed human renderables, adaptive tables with Unicode-visible-width measurement, and bounded single- and multi-task progress with known, indeterminate, transient, and custom-column states. TTY capability, TERM, NO_COLOR, and explicit `--color` precedence select ANSI or plain rendering; `--json` writes only the machine schema, progress stays off redirected streams, and logs/status use a separate channel. Existing help, E2102 diagnostics, and job output remain stable consumers of the canonical command registry.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs` and adjacent Prelude output modules, `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs` and output rendering modules, tests under `tests/cli_parts/`, and the relevant output sections under `docs/spec/`.

Non-goals: the general widget kit (card 01), guided prompts (card 02), TUI snapshots and recordings (card 04), dynamic completion (card 05), or native style reload (card 06). Invariants: human and machine streams are separate; `--json` and non-TTY output are deterministic and ANSI-free; NO_COLOR uses presence semantics; explicit color overrides are documented; progress never corrupts stdout or a pipe; E2102 remains narrow and exits 2.
Proof: `tests/cli_parts/output_modes.rs`.

Jet already advertises `--record` and `--update-snapshots`; the current `Help/Interactive` and `tests/cli_parts/core.rs` prove real-terminal and process-level paths, while `jet-jobs-project.txt` captures scoped job output. Actual: `jet-help.txt:257` advertises `--update-snapshots` and `jet-help.txt:276` advertises named `--record`; `crates/jet-cli/src/Help/Interactive.rs:79-112` proves only a real raw-terminal interaction path; `tests/cli_parts/core.rs:678-750` proves process-level help, jobs, and error assertions; `docs/spec/spec.md:4095-4105` has no terminal replay readiness contract. cards.title: Router: typed params, typed search params, loaders with preload and abort, pending and error boundaries
cards.body: TanStack Router and React Router v7 show why the census features Inferred typed route tree and type-safe navigation, File-based route generation with code-route escape hatch, Typed JSON-first search parameters, Route loader lifecycle with preload and abort context, Route data cache, stale-while-revalidate, and invalidation, and Pending and error elements at route boundaries belong to one route contract. Jet's App graph records route strings and zero-argument handlers, so links, URL state, loader cancellation, freshness, and boundary state are not typed or inspectable. The card extends the existing graph instead of creating a second route registry and keeps beginner conventions with an explicit code escape hatch.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:53-107` registers routes, pages, and layouts with string paths and zero-argument handlers; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:105-107` records only `.routes(root)`; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:53-167` has no typed URL-search state; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:17-25` stores cache policy strings; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:43-67` has no pending, not-found, or error boundary fields. `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:5837-5878` keeps the App graph and optional route conventions as the current authority.
Expected: after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies the `core.web` suite shape, add a Router module whose typed params, typed JSON-first search state, loader data, preload, abort, freshness, invalidation, pending, not-found, and error facts extend the existing App graph. A file convention may generate a checked view of that graph, but it must not create a second runtime registry; `jet explain --web-graph` and the Router panel show the same route contract.
Decision: D-DX-ROUTER1. The plan lane authors this API ballot after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies.
Prior-art signatures to compare (verbatim from `report.md` §API shapes):
```tsx
export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts')({
  loader: () => fetchPosts(),
})

const posts = Route.useLoaderData()
const routeApi = getRouteApi('/posts')
const data = routeApi.useLoaderData()
```
```tsx
export const Route = createFileRoute('/posts')({
  loaderDeps: ({ search: { offset, limit } }) => ({ offset, limit }),
  loader: ({ deps: { offset, limit } }) => fetchPosts({ offset, limit }),
})
```
```tsx
router.invalidate()
```
Recorded complaints to repair from `report.md` Avoid list: "Copy a file convention without a typed graph"; "Treat URL search as untyped strings"; and "Build a query cache with no invalidation story". The route API must retain graph authority, type URL state, and expose cache identity and invalidation causes instead of hiding stale data.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs`, `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs`, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, `tests/web_app_graph.rs`, `tests/web_browser.rs`, and `tests/web_app.rs`.
Dependencies: #2428 and D-DX-SUITE1; preserve D-WEBAPP1, D-WEBAUTHOR1, and the existing `App` graph.
Non-goals: no second route registry, untyped URL strings, framework-specific component markup, or RSC/island architecture in this card.
Invariants: route facts remain statically checked; loader capabilities and abort behavior are explicit; cache keys are serializable and inspectable; existing route, render, and diagnostic behavior stays compatible.
Proof command: `cargo test --test web_app_graph` plus `scripts/agent/jet-env jet explain --web-graph examples/features/web/web_app.jet`.

cards.title: Query: live queries by default, explicit keys, mutation lifecycle with optimistic rollback, targeted invalidation, cache states
cards.body: TanStack Query supplies the census features Server-state query cache with dedupe and background refresh, Mutation lifecycle with optimistic and rollback hooks, Targeted query invalidation, Suspense queries and render-as-you-fetch, Offline-first query and mutation modes, and Query and mutation devtools. Jet already has effect-tracked live queries and Browser storage, but it lacks a typed query-key cache, mutation state machine, offline queue, and cache inspector. This card keeps live queries as the default and adds explicit keys for outside sources, so fresh, stale, pending, error, paused, and invalidated states have one explainable authority.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:17-25` stores only opaque cache strings; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:69-94` registers action, form, and data handlers without typed results or mutation state; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:156-158` has no invalidation operation; `docs/spec/spec.md:1964-1980` provides Browser storage but no query persistence or queue; `docs/spec/spec.md:4280-4305` documents the dashboard without a query, mutation, or cache panel. DESIGN current-state `D-LIVEQUERY1=A` makes effect-tracked live queries and `app.subscribe`/`app.invalidate` the existing reactive foundation.
Expected: after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies the `core.web` suite shape, add Query on the live-query mechanism. DB-backed queries invalidate from effect footprints; non-DB sources use typed explicit keys with `app.subscribe` and `app.invalidate`; queries expose dedupe, fresh/stale/fetching/error states, bounded retention, targeted background refresh, optimistic mutation context with rollback, and explicit online/always/offlineFirst pause and replay policy. The Query panel is dev-only, shows key, age, observers, status, invalidation cause, and mutation state, and is absent from release output.
Decision: D-DX-QUERY1. The plan lane authors this API ballot after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies.
Prior-art signatures to compare (verbatim from `report.md` §API shapes):
```tsx
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider, useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
const queryClient = new QueryClient()
function Example() {
  const { isPending, error, data } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['repoData'],
    queryFn: () => fetch(...).then(res => res.json()),
  })
}
```
```tsx
const mutation = useMutation({
  mutationFn: (newTodo) => axios.post('/todos', newTodo),
})
mutation.mutate({ id: new Date(), title: 'Do Laundry' })
```
```tsx
queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
useSuspenseQuery({ queryKey: ['repoData'], queryFn: fetchRepo })
```
```tsx
useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos, networkMode: 'offlineFirst' })
```
Recorded complaints to repair from `report.md` Avoid list: "Build a query cache with no invalidation story"; "Hide optimistic writes and retries"; and "Add a devtool that ships to production". The query contract must show invalidation and paused work, make rollback observable, and compile the inspector out of release builds.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Observe.rs`, `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs`, `docs/spec/observability.md`, `tests/web_browser.rs`, `tests/web_app.rs`, and `tests/web_app_graph.rs`.
Dependencies: #2428 and D-DX-SUITE1; use D-LIVEQUERY1=A, `core.reactive`, `core.ws`, and the `jet.devtools.v1` observation path from DESIGN.
Non-goals: no normalized global cache, hidden retries, implicit offline policy, production Query panel, or replacement of effect-tracked DB invalidation with manual keys.
Invariants: DB query invalidation follows the recorded effect footprint; explicit keys are typed and deterministic; optimistic updates have a typed rollback boundary; offline pause and replay are visible; cache payloads remain private unless published at the site.
Proof command: `cargo test --test web_browser` plus `cargo test --test web_app_graph`.

cards.title: Forms: fields derived from struct types, sync and async validation, progressive enhancement through action
cards.body: TanStack Form and SvelteKit show the value of the census features Headless typed form state and field subscriptions, Sync and async validation with debounce, Standard Schema adapters and server field errors, and Progressive form actions. Jet's `.form` is an action alias with no field state, validator, structured error, or progressive submission contract. The card keeps markup and styling in the application while the type system owns fields, validation, submission state, and the `action` boundary.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:78-85` implements `.form(name, handler)` as a no-argument action alias; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:69-94` has no typed action result or field-error return; `examples/features/web/web_app.jet:10-24` demonstrates an action without a form input/result contract; `docs/spec/spec.md:4280-4305` documents the dashboard without a form inspector. The census records no Standard Schema adapter or field-state API.
Expected: after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies the `core.web` suite shape, add headless Forms derived from a struct type, with typed field registration and subscriptions, blur/submit synchronous validation, cancellable debounced asynchronous validation, structured form and field errors, and submission state. A form posts through `action` as ordinary HTML before JavaScript loads and gains pending, result, and revalidation behavior after hydration; the Form panel is dev-only and release-excluded.
Decision: D-DX-FORM1. The plan lane authors this API ballot after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies.
Prior-art signatures to compare (verbatim from `report.md` §API shapes):
```tsx
const form = useForm({
  defaultValues: { firstName: '', lastName: '' },
  onSubmit: async ({ value }) => { console.log(value) },
})
<form.Field name="firstName" validators={{
  onChange: ({ value }) => value.length < 3 ? 'Too short' : undefined,
  onChangeAsyncDebounceMs: 500,
  onChangeAsync: async ({ value }) => await checkName(value),
}} children={(field) => (
  <input value={field.state.value} onBlur={field.handleBlur}
    onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)} />
)} />
<form.Subscribe selector={(state) => [state.canSubmit, state.isSubmitting]}
  children={([canSubmit, isSubmitting]) => <button disabled={!canSubmit || isSubmitting}>Save</button>} />
```
Recorded complaints to repair from `report.md` Avoid list: "Couple form state to markup"; "Hide optimistic writes and retries"; and "Add a devtool that ships to production". The form contract must stay headless, make asynchronous and server failures explicit, and keep the inspector out of release builds.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js`, `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs`, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, `tests/web_browser.rs`, `tests/web_app.rs`, and `tests/web_app_graph.rs`.

Non-goals: no prescribed HTML or CSS, no untyped `FormData` escape hatch, no external schema runtime requirement, and no production form inspector.
Invariants: struct fields are the source of truth; field and form errors are typed and addressable; async validation can be cancelled; native form submission remains valid without JavaScript; browser-only effects remain capability checked.

cards.title: Table and Virtual: headless typed table, server pagination, viewport virtualization
cards.body: TanStack Table and TanStack Virtual set the bar with the census features Headless typed table core, Stable generic row accessors, Controlled and manual sorting state, Client/server pagination with row counts, and Headless list/grid virtualizer. Jet has no row model or viewport windowing surface, and its web page renderer currently emits a body string. This card keeps markup, styles, and accessibility in the application while one typed model scales from local rows to server pages and renders only the visible window.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:204-217` emits a complete HTML body string and has no table model; the census found no typed row/column, sorting, pagination, or virtualizer API in Jet web sources. `docs/spec/spec.md:1964-1980` supplies typed Browser events and storage but no data-view model.
Expected: after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies the `core.web` suite shape, add headless Table and Virtual modules over `List<T>`. The table owns typed columns, stable row accessors, controlled client or server sorting, filtering, page index/size, row counts, and accessible navigation state; the virtualizer owns measured or estimated viewport windows for lists, grids, horizontal content, and streams while the renderer owns markup and styles.
Decision: D-DX-TABLE1. The plan lane authors this API ballot after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies.
Prior-art signatures to compare (verbatim from `report.md` §API shapes):
```tsx
type ColumnSort = { id: string; desc: boolean }
type SortingState = ColumnSort[]
const table = useReactTable({
  columns,
  data,
  getCoreRowModel: getCoreRowModel(),
  getSortedRowModel: getSortedRowModel(),
})
```
```tsx
const rowVirtualizer = useVirtualizer({
  count: 10000,
  getScrollElement: () => parentRef.current,
  estimateSize: () => 35,
})
rowVirtualizer.getTotalSize()
rowVirtualizer.getVirtualItems().map((virtualItem) => ...)
```
Recorded complaints to repair from `report.md` Avoid list: "Ship table virtualization as a styled widget" and "Treat URL search as untyped strings". The table must preserve renderer ownership and tie sort/page state to typed route search or loader dependencies rather than hiding state in markup.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs`, `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs`, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, `tests/web_browser.rs`, `tests/web_app.rs`, and `tests/web_app_graph.rs`.
Dependencies: #2428 and D-DX-SUITE1; use `List<T>`, `core.reactive`, the existing App graph, and the shared `core.ui` backends described by DESIGN.
Non-goals: no styled table component, CSS system, framework-specific row renderer, hidden global cache, or untyped accessor escape hatch.
Invariants: row and column types are checked; data and column identity is stable or explicitly changed; client and server sorting share one state shape; page totals are explicit; virtualization never changes logical keyboard or accessibility order.
Proof command: `cargo test --test web_browser` plus `cargo test --test web_app_graph`.

Table and Virtual landed. Typed columns retain row and cell metadata; a literal column name is checked in sema against the declared row schema and a missing field emits registered E2475 with an actionable rename-or-declare Fix. One JetWebTableState drives local and server sort, filter, and pagination, and state boundary changes invalidate the page generation and page-key registry, reusing card #2473's keyed live-query generation rather than a second staleness rule.
