cards.title: Store: signals plus transactions with history
cards.body: TanStack Store demonstrates the census features Framework-agnostic reactive store and Derived stores, subscriptions, batching, and actions with a small renderer-independent API. Jet has `core.reactive` signals and effect-tracked live queries, but no public store with derived values, cleanup-safe subscriptions, batch updates, or history. This card makes one typed Store usable by DOM, native, and headless modules without turning server state into a second local-state model.
cards.plan:
Actual: DESIGN current-state `core.reactive` provides `Signal<T>`, `Computed<T>`, and `Effect`, while D-LIVEQUERY1=A provides effect-tracked live-query invalidation; `docs/spec/spec.md:1964-1980` documents Browser effects and storage but no public renderer-independent store; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:33-200` records web graph facts but no store state or history.
Expected: after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies the `core.web` suite shape, add a typed Store over the one `core.reactive` primitive. Store values and derived stores support `setState`, cleanup-safe subscribe/unsubscribe, batched updates, named actions, transactions with diffs, and a bounded monotonic history that the Store panel can scrub in development. Query remains the authority for server state; Store owns local and UI state and can feed every `core.ui` backend.
Decision: D-DX-STORE1. The plan lane authors this API ballot after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies.
Prior-art signatures to compare (verbatim from `report.md` §API shapes):
```ts
import { createStore } from '@tanstack/store'
const countStore = createStore(0)
countStore.setState(() => 1)
const { unsubscribe } = countStore.subscribe(() => console.log(countStore.state))
```
```ts
const count = createStore(0)
const double = createStore(() => count.state * 2)
```
Recorded complaints and traps to repair from `report.md`: the rendering matrix warns against "Treating server state as local state; shipping all code up front"; the Avoid list requires "Ship table virtualization as a styled widget" to remain a general warning against coupling headless state to a renderer. Store and Query must have separate authorities, and Store must not impose a framework runtime tax.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Observe.rs`, `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs`, `docs/spec/observability.md`, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, `tests/web_browser.rs`, and `tests/web_app.rs`.
Dependencies: #2428 and D-DX-SUITE1; preserve `core.reactive`, D-LIVEQUERY1=A, `jet.devtools.v1`, and the shared `core.ui` backends from DESIGN.
Non-goals: no second reactive primitive, server-state cache replacement, renderer-specific component store, implicit cross-process persistence, or unbounded history.
Invariants: derived values update from declared dependencies; subscriptions can always clean up; a batch emits one coherent transaction; history is bounded and deterministic; store values remain typed and payload publication stays explicit.
Proof command: `cargo test --test web_browser` plus `cargo test --test web_app`.

log.text: Closed on source completeness plus three-tier execution evidence. Store surface: shared Prelude/CoreLib/Top/WebStore.rs kernel with signal-backed bounded history, named transactions, and changed-field projection; JIT registers jet_jit_web_store_transaction against the same kernel. Tier parity required four repairs beyond the surface itself: WebStore/WebStoreTransaction/WebStorePatch/WebStoreInspection had no Rust root spellings so AOT ICEd at MIRRust.rs:901, fixed by a generic renderer that preserves type arguments plus a closed set of 12 Query/Store carrier spellings in Codegen/Context.rs; the interpreter reported core.web.store.with_history unsupported because the runtime pure-forwarding group in impure.rs lacked a core.web arm while all 41 store rows were already TypedIntrinsic; the standalone AOT bundle referenced jet_foundation::App::APP_SERVER_FUNCTION_MIDDLEWARE from included Prelude source, fixed by one dependency-free AppMiddleware.rs shared by all hosts and emitted from both app-prelude emitters; and the declared borrow masks disagreed with their callee signatures, measured across the whole surface as 83 divergences in 185 sema_web_call rows and corrected at the Core.jet source with regenerated tables.

Store landed. Typed WebStore state rides one canonical JetSignal read and write path with signal, state_signal, derived selectors, subscriptions, and staged transactions that publish once; a signal read inside a transaction sees that transaction's staged writes while a read outside sees only committed state. JetShared from card #2949 is the sole owner-bound optimistic revision and snapshot authority, so there is no second revision counter: transact and navigation call Shared replace which advances the revision on every committed write including equal values, optimistic capture stores an owner-bound snapshot, and rollback uses try_replace so a stale optimistic result is rejected rather than applied. A re-entrant per-store publication gate serializes transaction, update, batch, set, optimistic, navigation, and rollback paths to one publication per operation, with typed diffs and deterministic unsubscribe handles. History is bounded at 1000 with monotonic event-sequence labels, branch-aware back, forward, jump, and restore, non-mutating scrub and inspection, and UTF-8-safe metadata bounds. Sema-owned Store identity, kind, and history facts sit beside the query facts and the projection stays payload-free. cards.title: Server functions and progressive actions: typed RPC boundary with serializability checks and CSRF policy
cards.body: TanStack Start, Next App Router, and SvelteKit show the census features Type-safe server functions and RPC, Composable request and function middleware, and Progressive form actions. Jet's action, form, and data registrations accept zero-argument handlers and opaque security strings, so typed inputs, results, middleware, CSRF, and no-script submission are absent. This card makes the server boundary a checked part of the App graph and keeps ordinary HTML forms useful before hydration.
cards.plan:
Actual: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:69-103` registers action, form, and data handlers without typed input, output, validator, client stub, or CSRF contract; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:141-167` stores security names without middleware order, context, or validator execution; `examples/features/web/web_app.jet:10-24` has an action but no FormData/result boundary.
Expected: after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies the `core.web` suite shape, add a typed server-function boundary with method, input, output, error, validator, serializability, capability, and same-origin CSRF facts. Composable request and function middleware supplies ordered auth, context, CSP, logging, and observability; a native form posts without JavaScript and gains pending, result, and dependent-data revalidation after hydration.
Decision: D-DX-SERVERFN1. The plan lane authors this API ballot after D-DX-SUITE1 ratifies.
Prior-art signatures to compare (verbatim from `report.md` §API shapes):
```tsx
import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start'
export const getServerTime = createServerFn().handler(async () => new Date().toISOString())
export const saveData = createServerFn({ method: 'POST' }).handler(async () => save())
export const getUser = createServerFn({ method: 'GET' })
  .validator((data: { id: string }) => data)
  .handler(async ({ data }) => findUserById(data.id))
await greetUser({ data: { name: 'John' } })
```
```tsx
const logging = createMiddleware().server(({ next, context, request }) => next())
const fn = createServerFn().middleware([logging]).handler(async () => value)
```
Recorded complaints and traps to repair from `report.md`: "Hide optimistic writes and retries"; "Two module graphs and cache layers are difficult"; and "Add a devtool that ships to production". The boundary must expose mutation state and retry policy, keep server/client authority explicit without a hidden second graph, and exclude its inspector from release output.
Writable paths: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js`, `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/fixed_sigs.rs`, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, `docs/spec/observability.md`, `tests/web_browser.rs`, `tests/web_app.rs`, and `tests/web_app_graph.rs`.
Dependencies: #2428 and D-DX-SUITE1; preserve D-WEBAPP1, the Browser effect boundary in `docs/spec/spec.md:1964-1980`, and the existing App action/form graph.
Non-goals: no handwritten endpoint registry, untyped serialization fallback, disabled CSRF by default, arbitrary server code in the browser, or RSC architecture decision.
Invariants: server calls have checked input/output/error types and explicit effects; non-serializable values fail before transport; middleware order is observable; CSRF policy is explicit; native forms work without JavaScript; auth and secrets never enter client payloads.
Proof command: `cargo test --test web_browser` plus `cargo test --test web_app_graph`.

cards.title: Streaming and pending boundaries, islands with explicit hydration timing
cards.body: Next App Router, Astro, Qwik, and Fresh show different ways to deliver a static shell, defer slow work, and hydrate only explicit islands. cards.title: Style live reload for terminal apps
cards.body: Textual's `CSS live reload in --dev` shows that a style-only edit can become visible in the terminal without restarting application state, while Lip Gloss's `Declarative terminal styles and color profiles` supplies reusable capability-aware values. Jet's `jet dev` already exposes rebuild and reload status with last-good recovery, but the checked `docs/spec/spec.md` surface does not define style-only reload for a native TUI; its `--swap`, `--restart`, `--watch`, and `--color` controls are the existing policy hooks. This card applies D-DX-LIVE1 to terminal style edits without adding a second renderer.

cards.title: DX benchmark matrix: time to first run, edit to see, error to fix, test loop, build, against each ecosystem's best loop
cards.body: The existing `scripts/benchmarks/dev-dx.mjs` measures Jet, Bun, and Vite from empty projects, including first-page readiness and warm reload. This card extends that proof to the peer loops named by the `Cargo scaffold to run`, `marimo`, `Textual`, `TanStack Start`, `Flutter`, `Unity`, `Godot`, `Bevy`, `Phoenix`, `Rails`, and `Jet today` census findings. cards.plan: Actual: no proof-domain census.json or report.md exists; the current web benchmark is `docs/reference/dev-dx-benchmark.md:48-101` with runner `scripts/benchmarks/dev-dx.mjs:14-20,258-375,401-454`, and it already measures fresh directories, browser markers, ten reloads, medians, and JSON. `~/.cache/jet-luna/dx/DESIGN.md:9-15,56-63` is the current-state authority. Exact peer loops: web-tooling: Vite = `npm create vite@latest app -- --template vanilla --no-interactive; cd app; npm install; npm run dev`; Bun + Vite = `bun create vite app --template vanilla --no-interactive; cd app; bun install; bun run dev`; TanStack Start = define Router routes and `createServerFn().validator(...).handler(...)`, call the function from a loader/component/form, let middleware supply auth/context/CSP, send an SSR or streaming shell, and use typed client RPC stubs. Web frameworks: TanStack Router = type a route file, let the generator update the route tree, write `loader` and `loaderDeps`, use typed params/search, navigate or prefetch, and see pending/error components and cached data; TanStack Query = create `QueryClient`, declare `useQuery({queryKey,queryFn})`, render pending/data/error, call `useMutation`, invalidate the affected key, and inspect query/mutation state in Devtools; TanStack Form = call `useForm({defaultValues,onSubmit})`, add `form.Field`, edit and blur, run sync or debounced async validators, submit, and map server errors to fields; TanStack Table and Virtual = keep stable `data` and `columns`, call `useReactTable`, wire sorting and pagination, feed a page or row model, configure `useVirtualizer`, and render virtual items; Next = put a page/layout in `app/`, fetch in server components, add a `'use client'` island, add `loading.tsx` or `Suspense`, submit a `'use server'` action, and revalidate; Astro = render static HTML, add `client:visible`, defer with `server:defer`, use content collections, and opt into `ClientRouter`; Qwik = mark components and handlers with `component$` and `$`, serialize state/listeners, download an event handler chunk, and resume; SvelteKit/SolidStart/React Router/Fresh = place load code or a loader, submit an action/fetcher, use generated params/data types, choose CSR/SSR/SSG/streaming/islands, and hydrate only islands where needed. Mobile: Flutter = run doctor or use DartPad, run `flutter create`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`, `flutter run`, edit and hot reload, inspect widgets, profile, and build; Expo/React Native = run `npx expo start`, choose A/I/W, use Expo Go or a development build, edit JS/TS for Fast Refresh, inspect with Dev Menu/LogBox/DevTools, and build with EAS; SwiftUI/Xcode = `swift package init`, `swift build`/`swift run`, add `#Preview`, use Canvas and preview variants, run on a destination, inspect with sanitizers/Instruments, and distribute with Xcode Cloud; Android Studio/Compose = choose a template, sync Gradle, select an AVD/device, run once, edit with Compose Live Edit, use `@Preview` and Layout Inspector, profile, and assemble/install a signed bundle; Kotlin Multiplatform = use the wizard, select Android and iOS, run each app, use desktop/JVM Compose Hot Reload, build Android with Gradle, and hand off iOS through Xcode. Systems: Cargo scaffold = `cargo new app`, edit `src/main.rs`, run `cargo run -- arg`, inspect output or diagnostics; Cargo tests = run `cargo test`, narrow by a filter, pass harness controls after `--`, and use `--no-capture`; Rust diagnostics = read code, span, caret, What/Why/Fix, `rustc --explain`, and JSON edits; rust-analyzer = use inlay hints/completion, a lightbulb assist, cursor test action, and rename; Bacon = start `bacon test`, keep the pane alive, focus failed tests with `f`, and return with Esc; Zig = `zig init`, `zig build --help`, `zig build`, `zig build run` or `zig build test`, and `--watch`; Go evidence = `go test -run`, `-list`, `-json`, coverage or profiles, and `-count=1`; Go fuzz = write `FuzzXxx`, add seeds, run `go test -fuzz`, and use `go test -race`; profile = capture Criterion/flamegraph/pprof, rank hot functions, inspect source/call graph/disassembly, change code, and compare a named baseline; environment = enter a project, load direnv or devenv, run named tasks, watch outputs, and inspect the environment. Games: Unreal = launch/open, click Play or Simulate, pause/Frame Skip/Eject and keep with K, use the tilde console and `stat unit`, capture `stat startfile` or Insights, and Package Project; Unity = open, click Play, edit Inspector values and let Asset Database refresh, inspect Console/Inspector/Error Pause, use Profiler or Frame Debugger, and Build Profiles; Godot = create/import, run F6 or F5, pause with F9 and advance with F10, inspect Remote Scene and Evaluator, use Visual Profiler and monitors, and export presets or headless CLI; Bevy = `cargo new`, `cargo add bevy`, add an App, `cargo run --example breakout`, enable asset reload/dynamic linking/hotpatching, inspect through RemotePlugin or WorldInspector, add diagnostics plugins, and release-build with target/features/locked/timings/json. Backend: Phoenix = generate schema or HTML, run `mix phx.server`, let LiveReloader reload, open `/dashboard`, then inspect request logs/Telemetry/Ecto stats; Laravel = install Telescope and migrate, serve the route, inspect `/telescope`, `/horizon`, and `/pulse`, use `php artisan tinker`, and repeat Artisan jobs; Rails = generate scaffold, migrate, run server/dev, use reload and Turbo, inspect the error page or console, use `bin/rails console --sandbox`, and inspect Active Job/Solid Queue; Spring = generate with start.spring.io, run `./gradlew bootRun`, let DevTools restart and LiveReload, inspect `/actuator` and `/error`, and keep exposure explicit; Aspire = `aspire run`, open its tokenized dashboard, inspect resources/endpoints/logs/actions, filter traces/metrics, and export bounded telemetry; Django/Erlang = run `manage.py runserver`, run migrations and system checks, inspect Debug Toolbar, attach Observer, and inspect system/load/process/table/trace views. Data: Jupyter/IPython/JupyterLab/ipywidgets = run `jupyter notebook`, edit a cell and press Shift-Enter, use completion/magics/widgets, save `.ipynb`, and export with nbconvert; marimo = `marimo edit`, build the cell DAG, edit or run a cell for dependent reruns or stale marking, inspect/delete cells, and `marimo run` or export; Observable = edit a loader in local preview, let snapshots push over a socket, route generated files/attachments, compose Plot marks, and build static output; Pluto = edit a Julia cell, rerun affected cells, reorganize under single-definition rules, and embed package manifests; Livebook/Kino = execute `.livemd` cells, use Smart Cells/Kino controls, inspect stale annotations, collaborate, and manage packages; Polars = `scan_csv`, chain lazy expressions, `collect` or streaming collect, inspect optimizer rules and `show_graph`, and add plugins; DuckDB = launch `duckdb`, use multiline SQL and dot commands, pipe or export results, and open `duckdb -ui`; pandas = derive a frame or column, mutate the owned object, and observe copy-on-write boundaries; Streamlit = `streamlit run`, interact with widgets for reruns, preserve `session_state`, cache data/resources, and observe code-change invalidation; Gradio = wrap `gr.Interface`, use `Blocks` events, launch or hot reload, and call clients or a share URL; Quarto = render with nbclient, use widgets, publish HTML/PDF/Word, and retain provenance. CLI/TUI: Bubble Tea = declare Init/Update/View, route events through messages, return slow work as `tea.Cmd`, render View, and iterate in one process; Lip Gloss = create `NewStyle`, set color/padding/borders/width/joins, compose blocks, and adapt to terminal capability; Bubbles = select a widget, wire Update messages, render, and remap keys; Huh = declare Form/Groups and fields, attach Validate, call `Form.Run`, and use accessible mode; Gum = pipe `gum choose`/`input`/`write`/`confirm` into the next command; VHS = `vhs new`, write tape actions, render an artifact, and review it; Wish = wrap Bubble Tea in SSH middleware, connect, receive an isolated PTY, apply auth, and close; Ratatui = `cargo generate`, choose a template, call `ratatui::init`, draw widgets with constraint Layout, and restore; Ink = install `ink` and `react`, call `render(<App />)`, use hooks and React DevTools, and assert `lastFrame` or `waitUntilExit`; Textual = `textual run`, add `--dev`, save CSS, use `textual console`, serve in a browser, exercise Pilot, and compare SVG snapshots; clap = derive a command, inspect help/values/suggestions, generate completion/man, and test captured output; Typer = annotate a function, run it, install/show completion, and generate docs; oclif = generate/init, use `bin/dev.js`, add commands/hooks, test with `runCommand`, and ship `bin/run.js`; Cobra = create a root, add nested commands/flags, use generated help/completion/man/Markdown, and use aliases or a generator; Rich = create Console and print renderables/tables/JSON/logs/status; Indicatif = create ProgressBar/MultiProgress, update it, set templates, and finish/reset. Live: Elm = edit Model/Msg/update/view, trigger input, produce a new Model, inspect history, rewind, replay, and optionally swap code; Redux = wire DevTools, dispatch an action, inspect/jump/skip/reorder/export, edit a reducer with HMR, and enable trace when needed; Replay.io = record a browser run, reopen it, add a console expression at an execution point, and inspect React props/state/definitions; Pharo = edit and Accept into the image, evaluate in a Playground, inspect an object, mutate and update, and create a missing method in Debugger; Clojure/CIDER/Portal = keep one REPL, evaluate a buffer or s-expression, send values with `add-tap`/`tap>`, inspect and return values, and isolate nREPL sessions; Erlang/Elixir = start a node, load modules, coexist old/current versions, use `code_change`, inspect with Observer, install a relup, and consume structured Mix events; Swift Playgrounds/Xcode Previews = edit SwiftUI in a playground, add `#Preview`, name variants/devices/data, share setup with `PreviewModifier`, and use Canvas; Julia Revise = load Revise, edit/save, let the next REPL command revise methods, add/delete methods, and debug at current source locations; Live Share = host a session, join, co-edit, co-debug, share a terminal/localhost, and enforce access controls; rr = record, replay, set breakpoints/watchpoints, reverse-cont, and rerun deterministically; Jupyter and marimo use the data loops above. Time to first run starts immediately before the first setup command and ends at the first verified marker: DOM marker plus click for web, ready line or first frame for mobile/games/CLI, health response for backend, output cell/query/app marker for data, and stdout or event marker for systems/live; unavailable SDK, device, GUI, or network paths are recorded as unavailable with a reason, never as zero. Test loop starts the fixed test command or native watch/Pilot harness after warm readiness and ends at the first complete verdict, plus failed-first-to-green when the tool supports it; record filter, capture mode, exit, and raw events. Build starts the clean build/export/package command and ends when the expected artifact exists with hash and size; repeat a warm build and report both wall times. Each domain emits the five named metrics with the same fields and preserves command transcripts. Non-goals: no runtime feature implementation, no new API or command choice, no marketing rank, no source-only latency claim, no visual acceptance, and no fabricated mobile or GUI result. questions.text: We need to support safety by default with expert opt out. Since we are also looking for interoperability to gain market share, I want to ensure we support things like c strings. I believe there's a new null terminated string type planned for c++29, I think we should consider whether that should be standard in strings in jet for compatibility/safety
questions.answer: Two different axes are in play, so here is each. (1) This ballot only spells a literal; the value is an ordinary String either way, so the C-string question does not change the recommendation. I added a scope note to the ballot saying so. (2) C++29: P3655 is std::cstring_view (renamed from zstring_view), a borrowed, non-owning view that guarantees NUL termination; it targets C++29 and its construction rules are still being designed. std::string itself has guaranteed a trailing NUL since C++11, which is why c_str() is O(1). (3) Jet today: String lowers to Rust String (length-prefixed UTF-8, interior NUL allowed). At a C boundary (S59) every crossing allocates a NUL-terminated copy through CString::new; a literal with an interior NUL is E3211 at compile time, and a runtime interior NUL is a boundary stop. C-returned strings are copied into an owned String. Compatibility exists; the costs are one allocation per crossing and no borrowed view type. (4) My recommendation: do not make NUL termination the standard String representation. Length-prefixed is the safety property (no strlen scans, no over-read, interior NUL representable) and it is what every Core API and Rust interop assume. Instead: (a) add a typed borrowed view for the boundary, Jet's counterpart of cstring_view, so C-owned strings are checked once at entry and converted explicitly, never implicitly; beginners never see it, experts get it through c.* bindings; (b) keep String as is; (c) the C++ trick of keeping a trailing NUL in every String buffer, which makes String-to-C zero-copy when there is no interior NUL, is only worth taking when Jet's runtime owns String layout (the memory slate), and it should be measured against the FFI hot paths (per-frame raylib calls) rather than assumed. (a) is a new public type and needs its own ballot; you bounded this round, so I did not raise it. Say the word and I will raise D-CSTR1 with the full passes.

questions.text: what about --save instead of --keep and ../saved/.. instead of ../kept/,,
questions.answer: Adopted. Option D now reads `jet prove TARGET --save ARTIFACT`, `--unsave <id>`, and `.jet/records/saved/<artifact_id>`; the claim is still named `replay <id>`. I chose --unsave over --forget so the pair is discoverable from either word. While there, the tradeoff pass fixed the real weakness of a saved claim: it used to go stale on any edit. A saved claim now re-binds by a per-function anchor (the function that made the request, the record kind, and its order within that function), so an edit anywhere else keeps the claim alive; only a change of shape or name in that function reports diverged (E3623) or vacuous, each naming --unsave or a fresh capture. The saved-claim comparator is defined (no-fault for a recorded crash, same-output for a recorded clean run), which the rival pass showed was missing. Also corrected in the lesson: D-RUN-RECORD1 already ratified --record=NAME on run, dev, and test, and jet debug --replay=NAME as a second consumer.

questions.text: I dont know enough about this, but wouldnt it be possible for this kind of thing, since we already have the proof/record keeping and mostly deterministic, to allow for all NONDETERMINISTIC data to be captured during a run, then provide that data so it can be replayed deterministically?
questions.answer: Yes, and it is already the ratified design. D-JREPLAY1's capture records every nondeterministic input a run consumed (the safe form: clock reads; the sensitive form after consent: randomness, stdin, and network requests and responses), and replay re-executes the program deterministically, feeding those recorded values back at each request and failing with E3623 if the program asks for anything the recording does not hold. Everything else is deterministic by Jet's determinism law, so nothing else needs recording. What backward stepping needs beyond that is only a way to reach an earlier point: a jump to event N is re-execution from the start with the recorded values, and back 3 from event 11 is jump 8. Checkpoints only make long jumps fast. So the ballot no longer waits on a shipped release: card #2461 (ready to implement, blocked by #2429) is scoped to build scrub, jump, and skip, and option B now gates reverse step (#2463) on two facts proved in the repo, that every replay fixture jumps to every event with a byte-identical locals snapshot on both adapters and that the debug adapter suite is green. B names the two ratified clauses it amends (the D-TIMETRAVEL1 prerequisite wording and D-RUN-RECORD1's reverse-step deferral); the Epoch 6 slot stays for checkpoint runtime support.

cards.title: Claims: one evidence report, two producers, evidence that rises (slate 2)
cards.body: Implementation card for docs/proposals/claims-one-ladder.md. Ballots D-CLAIM1 (recommended C), D-GRADE1 (D), D-GRADE-POLICY1 (A). Depends on #2509 (contracts fail on every tier) landing first. Gated on its ballots on card #2500. Phase A work is internal and may start before ratification; every user-facing criterion waits for its ballot outcome. cards.plan:
Ratified law (2026-09-02): D-CLAIM1 = C (one evidence report; `jet test` runs examples, doctests, property tests, and generated contracts; `jet prove` stays the umbrella and adds solver evidence only under `--lens solver`; `jet fuzz` folds into `jet test --grade=generated --iterations=N`), D-GRADE1 = D (every evidence record is producer, outcome, count; the report shows the strongest rung by the order proved, generated(n), examples(n), checked, unchecked; gates are not claim evidence), D-GRADE-POLICY1 = A (`policy: .{ claims: .{ min: <rung> } }` in package.jet, tighten-only), D-LEDGER1 = D (one typed ledger over three stores; evidence records live in the run-evidence store), D-CLI-ONE1 = A (`jet inspect claims` is the view). #2509 (contracts fail on every tier) is done, so the contract example runs on every tier today. Read each picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json` before you start; the reviewed design is docs/proposals/claims-one-ladder.md.

Actual: `jet test` and `jet prove` render separate reports; a #Post on a pure function gets no generated evidence unless the author writes a property test; `jet fuzz` is a separate command; there is no claim floor in package.jet.

Expected: one evidence report shared by both commands, generated evidence for free on effect-free contracts, and a package floor that a diagnostic enforces.

Slices, in order. Each slice is one worker brief and leaves scripts/agent/lane-check.sh clean.

Slice 1, evidence records (internal). Reuse the ratified ProofReport evidence item shape from D-PROVE-SEM1 (kind, producer, outcome, count, facet) in Source/CmdProve.rs and the test runner (Source/ main test path; find it with `grep -rn "fn run_tests\|Test runner" Source/`). Records go into the ledger's evidence store (D-LEDGER1 = D: the run-evidence store, one typed query beside crates/jet-foundation/src/Facts.rs and Registry.rs; do not fold FactRegistry into Registry). One renderer prints the report for both commands. A claim keeps every record it earned; the summary shows the strongest rung by the narrow order.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test prove --test cli_commands` green (add `--test claims_report` with one program that has an example, a doctest, a property test, and a contract, and assert the same report text from `jet test` and `jet prove`).

Slice 2, generated contracts. For a callable whose inferred row is `-[]>` and that declares #Pre and #Post, `jet test` generates inputs from #Pre through the existing property generator, default budget 1,000 per contract, settable per package. Report "not generated" with the reason for an effectful callable, a #Pre that names another function, or a parameter type with no generator (E0613). Keep a failing generated input and replay it first on the next run (store it beside the property-test seeds). A false "generated" record must be impossible: the record is written only after the run.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test claims_report -- generated` covers the four cases (generated, effectful, cross-function #Pre, no generator) and the replay-first rule.

Slice 3, command surface (D-CLAIM1 = C). `jet prove --lens solver` adds `proved` rows for the implication #Pre implies #Post; a proved claim erases its runtime check on every tier (D-PROVE-SEM1). `jet fuzz` prints its replacement `jet test --grade=generated --iterations=N` and exits non-zero. Lenses stay presentation views. Update crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs, Source/main.rs, docs/reference/cli.md, and the help snapshot tests.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env jet fuzz` prints the replacement; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test prove` green.

Slice 4, evidence words, the view, and the floor (D-GRADE1 = D, D-GRADE-POLICY1 = A, D-CLI-ONE1 = A). Every report and `jet inspect claims [TARGET]` (Source/CmdInspect.rs; add the `claims` plane if #2505 has not yet added the plane grammar) print `proved`, `generated(n)`, `examples(n)`, `checked`, `unchecked`. Read `policy: .{ claims: .{ min: <rung> } }` from package.jet (crates/jet-pkg-model, the D-PACKAGE-POLICY-SCOPE1 field set) as a tighten-only floor; a claim below the floor is a new registered diagnostic (docs/spec/diagnostics.md "Adding a diagnostic") whose fix names the command that raises it when a generator exists, or the property test to write when one does not; one UI snapshot per fix shape.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots --test claims_report --test pkg` green; example under examples/features/contracts/ with golden output on AOT, default `jet run`, and `jet run --interpret` (I9).

Writable paths: Source/CmdProve.rs, Source/CmdInspect.rs, Source/main.rs, the test runner under Source/, crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/{Facts.rs,Registry.rs}, crates/jet-pkg-model/src/, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/ (contract eligibility only), tests/claims_report.rs, tests/prove.rs, tests/ui/, examples/features/contracts/, docs/reference/cli.md, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/diagnostic-rows.md. Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: a proved claim erases its runtime check on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`; the golden example proves it on all three.

Non-goals: no new lens; no solver change; no `max` policy field; gates such as #Unsafe never appear as claim evidence.

cards.body: Implementation card for docs/proposals/shapes-one-fact.md. Ballots D-SHAPE-ONE1 (recommended C), D-SHAPE-PROJECT1 (A). env.decode<T>(prefix:, file:, allow:) is already shipped and shares one codec with json; this card adds only what is missing. Database rows and FFI layout are out of scope until their own probe. Gated on its ballots on card #2500. Phase A work is internal and may start before ratification; every user-facing criterion waits for its ballot outcome. cards.plan:
Ratified law (2026-09-02): D-SHAPE-ONE1 = A (every projection reads the same field facts: the text formats, env, args, database rows, and FFI layout), D-SHAPE-PROJECT1 = A (`args.decode<T>()` anywhere through the core.args builder; `Config.merge(flags, settings)` applies flag, then env, then default), D-CLI-ONE1 = A (`jet inspect shapes` is the view). #2510 (json.decode on a computed text) is done. Read each picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json`; the reviewed design is docs/proposals/shapes-one-fact.md. The owner picked A over the recommended C, so database rows and FFI layout join now; the card body's "out of scope" sentence is superseded by that ratification.

Actual: crates/jet-foundation/src/JSON.rs holds a second tree (JSONValue) beside DataTree; EncodingFormat is a closed five-entry enum for twelve codecs; three error types carry the L0520 flag; one shared #[Rename] cannot name a legacy column; args decode only at the entry function; core.db maps rows with its own field logic; #Layout and #ABI read their own field facts.

Expected: one field-fact registry that every projection reads, declared format rows, one EncodingError, `args.decode<T>()` anywhere, per-format renames, and `jet inspect shapes` listing every fact a type carries and which projection honors it.

Slices, in order. Each slice is one worker brief and leaves scripts/agent/lane-check.sh clean.

Slice 1, one tree and declared formats (internal). Move every JSONValue caller to DataTree and delete the second tree in crates/jet-foundation/src/JSON.rs. Declare the format rows in the Prelude (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/, beside the encoding traits in CoreLib/Top/EncodingTraits.rs) and generate EncodingFormat from them (this is the D-OPENTABLE1 twin rule; coordinate with #2507 and use its generator if it has landed, else a checked-in generated file with a drift test). Replace the three L0520-flagged error types with one EncodingError.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test encoding_parity --test encoding_corpus --test encoding_types_single_home --test encoding_edition` green; every encoding example under examples/features/serde/ prints byte-identical output on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`.

Slice 2, migration verbs. `migration T { add … remove … change … }` (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/SchemaMigration.rs) ship with one example each under examples/features/serde/ and golden output on every tier (D-MIGRATE2A, D, E); only `rename` has an example today.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden -- serde` green for the three new examples.

Slice 3, args anywhere (D-SHAPE-PROJECT1 = A). Add `args.decode<T>()` to core.args (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/ core.args part and its host in crates/jet-jit/src/Args.rs) with the same signature family as `env.decode`. It lowers through the same builder that `fn run(args: T)` uses (the D-CLI builder floor, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:183-196), so `--help` and every diagnostic are byte-identical. Add `Config.merge(flags, settings) T ![FieldError]` with the order flag, env, default; a present but invalid value is a FieldError, never absent. Register the new rows in the core surface ledger (docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json through its generator; tests/core_surface_ledger.rs pins it).
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli_bindings --test cli_positionals --test env_overlay --test core_surface_ledger` green; an example under examples/features/cli/ decodes outside `run` with golden `--help` output identical to the entry-function form, on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`.

Slice 4, one fact for every projection (D-SHAPE-ONE1 = A). Extend the #[Rename] marker signature (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/markers.rs, Prelude/Markers.jet per D-MARKSIG1) to per-format names: `#[Rename("x", env: "Y", db: "col_x")]`. Every text projection, env, args, core.db row decode and encode (crates/jet-jit/src/DB.rs host and its Prelude part), and the FFI layout reader (crates/jet-jit/src/Layout.rs, Prelude/Layout.rs, #Layout and #ABI) read the shared field facts from crates/jet-foundation/src/Facts.rs; a projection that does not understand a fact ignores it. Migration stays scoped to #PublishedSchema types. `jet inspect shapes [TARGET]` (Source/CmdInspect.rs; add the plane if #2505 has not landed) lists each type's facts and, per fact, the projections that honor it.
Proof: one fixture type with a per-format rename decoded through json, env, args, a core.db row, and read through #Layout, with golden output on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test marker_rule_signatures --test marker_registry_coverage --test golden` green.

Writable paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/{JSON.rs,Facts.rs,Syntax/markers.rs}, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/ (encoding, args, db, layout, markers parts), crates/jet-jit/src/{Args.rs,DB.rs,Layout.rs,Encoding.rs}, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/SchemaMigration.rs, Source/CmdInspect.rs, tests/encoding_*.rs, tests/cli_*.rs, tests/golden.rs, examples/features/{serde,cli,ports}/, docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json (generated), docs/reference/core-library.md. Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: every projection is Prelude code with tier hosts as marshalling only; prove each example on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`.

Non-goals: no automatic database table migration (a field diff cannot name a table; that needs a table identity contract and is not part of the ratified projection list); no change to the FFI ABI itself, only to where its field facts are read; no new format.

cards.title: The live tier: swap by default, keep the pinned world (slate 4)
cards.body: Implementation card for docs/proposals/tier-live-dev.md. Ballots D-LIVE1 (recommended A), D-LIVE-PERSIST1 (A). #Persist stays: D-PERSIST-DEVSTATE1=A makes it the one writable module binding. The default does not flip until the long-lived edit proof is green on every engine. Gated on its ballots on card #2500. Phase A work is internal and may start before ratification; every user-facing criterion waits for its ballot outcome. Full I9 tier parity, I4 snapshots, and I5 examples are required for each criterion. Revised 2026-09-01 after the beginner (rli5) and rival-family adversarial passes; the proposal document carries the reviewed design and the ballot recommendations.
cards.plan:
Ratified law (2026-09-02): D-LIVE1 = A (`jet dev` swaps on save by default; #Persist values are kept; a layout change to a pinned type still triggers the announced restart; one line per save names swapped, kept, migrated, or restarting; `jet dev --restart` and `dev: .{ swap: false }` refuse swap), D-LIVE-PERSIST1 = A (a pinned #PublishedSchema value migrates in place through its migration step function; otherwise the announced restart with the migration block to write; a renamed binding resets), D-CLI-ONE1 = A (`jet inspect build --live PID` is the view). Precondition written into D-LIVE1: the default flips only after a long-lived edit proof is green on the JIT and interpreter engines. Read each picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json`; the reviewed design is docs/proposals/tier-live-dev.md.

Actual: `jet dev` (Source/CmdDevTools.rs run_dev, run_dev_inner; hot swap through jet::Sema::HotSwap::type_stable_check at CmdDevTools.rs:884 and the InterpreterBackend or CraneliftBackend hot_swap at :966-971) reruns by default and swaps only with a flag; the execution tier is a closed enum in Source/CmdCompile.rs so `jet run --interpret --release` is E2102; the watcher compares size and mtime; a pinned value whose type changed restarts without consulting the migration block; `jet inspect live PID` is the view.

Expected: swap on save by default with one honest line per save, kept pinned state, in-place migration for published types, and a view that lists the pinned values of a running session.

Slices, in order. Each slice is one worker brief and leaves scripts/agent/lane-check.sh clean.

Slice 1, the precondition proof and the internal fixes. (a) Make the execution tier a ledger value (a fact in crates/jet-foundation/src/Facts.rs read by Source/CmdCompile.rs) instead of the closed enum, so `jet run --interpret --release` composes instead of E2102. (b) Watch stamps (Source/CmdDevTools.rs watcher and crates/jet-jit/src/Watcher.rs) include a content digest so a same-size same-mtime edit is seen. (c) Long-lived edit test: tests/dev_live_swap.rs runs a program with a loop whose callers are mid-execution, edits a function while it runs, and observes the swap line and the kept #Persist value on the JIT engine and on `--interpret`, with identical program meaning under `jet run` and `jet build` (I9). Register the new test file in tests/suites.txt.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_live_swap --test dev_tier_parity --test dev_interp_parity` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret --release examples/features/devloop/persist.jet` exits 0.

Slice 2, migration of pinned values (D-LIVE-PERSIST1 = A). When the changed type is #PublishedSchema and a migration block covers the change, the pinned value migrates in place through the same step function decode uses (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/SchemaMigration.rs step functions applied to the resident value in the JIT runtime, crates/jet-jit/src/lib.rs RESIDENT_RUNTIME, and the interpreter). cards.title: The verdict loop: repair coverage by ratchet, one status object (slate 5)
cards.body: Implementation card for docs/proposals/verdict-loop.md. Ballots D-VERDICT-LOOP1 (recommended D), D-CLI-ONE1 (A). The ratified jet.report/v1 line and the five safety classes (D-REPORT-MACHINE1, D-REPORT-FIXGRADE1=D) are unchanged; this card adds a status object around them, a reason field, and a per-plane coverage ratchet. Gated on its ballots on card #2500. Phase A work is internal and may start before ratification; every user-facing criterion waits for its ballot outcome. Full I9 tier parity, I4 snapshots, and I5 examples are required for each criterion. Revised 2026-09-01 after the beginner (rli5) and rival-family adversarial passes; the proposal document carries the reviewed design and the ballot recommendations.
cards.plan:
Ratified law (2026-09-02): D-VERDICT-LOOP1 = D (a typed `no_fix_reason` field, mutually exclusive with `fix_edits`, joins the report object under a version bump to jet.report/v2; a per-plane coverage baseline never decreases; a new row in an open plane with neither fails the registry today; edit coverage and reason coverage are reported apart; one `jet.status/v1` object wraps every command's `--json` output on pass and fail), D-CLI-ONE1 = A (`jet inspect <plane>` for types, rights, claims, shapes, structure, build, and gates at file, package, `--live PID`, and `--replay ARTIFACT` scope; facts, authority, unsafe, guarantees, report, and dossier retire and print their new home; task actions keep their names). Read each picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json`; the reviewed design is docs/proposals/verdict-loop.md.

Actual: crates/jet-foundation/src/Report.rs renders one `jet.report/v1` envelope per command, but infrastructure failures (E2105 on `jet test --json`, `jet prove --json`) print no envelope; `jet check --json` on a passing file prints nothing structured; `inspect compiler check` reports ok around an inner error; Report.with_fields takes strings; the parser table in Source/main.rs is a second copy of crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs; 679 registry rows have no fix_edits and no reason; `jet inspect` has six ledger-view names.

Expected: one status object on every `--json` path, a reason field that keeps reason rows from counting as repairs, a coverage ratchet per plane, and one `jet inspect <plane>` grammar.

Slices, in order. Each slice is one worker brief and leaves scripts/agent/lane-check.sh clean.

Slice 1, the status object (internal). Add `{ schema: "jet.status/v1", action, ok, reports: [...] }` in crates/jet-foundation/src/Report.rs as the envelope clause of D-REPORT-MACHINE1 and emit it from every command's `--json` path in Source/main.rs and the Cmd*.rs files, including infrastructure failures (E2105 on `jet test --json` and `jet prove --json`), `jet check --json` on a passing file, and `jet fix --json`. `inspect compiler check` reports the inner error, never ok around it. Report.with_fields takes typed fields. Generate the Source/main.rs parser table from crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs with a drift test (tests/cli_surface.rs).
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test report --test cli_surface --test cli_commands` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet check --json examples/features/basics/hello.jet` prints one `jet.status/v1` line with `ok: true` and an empty `reports` array; `JET_STORE_DIR=/nonexistent scripts/agent/jet-env jet test --json <file>` prints a `jet.status/v1` line carrying E2105.

Slice 2, the reason field and the ratchet (D-VERDICT-LOOP1 = D). Bump the report object to jet.report/v2 with the optional typed `no_fix_reason = { kind: behavior | design | ambiguous, next: <text or link> }` in crates/jet-foundation/src/{Registry.rs,Diagnostics.rs,Report.rs}; a row may carry `fix_edits` or `no_fix_reason`, never both. The registry guard (tests/diagnostics_coverage.rs) fails a new row in an open plane with neither. Add a per-plane coverage baseline file (tests/diagnostics_coverage_baseline.txt, one row per plane: plane, edit-covered count, reason-covered count, total) that the guard reads; a decrease fails the guard. Classify the 679 uncovered rows plane by plane and record the split on this card. `jet inspect build --coverage` reports edit coverage and reason coverage as two numbers.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostics_coverage --test diagnostic_gate` green; the log records the per-plane split.

Slice 3, one inspect grammar (D-CLI-ONE1 = A). In Source/CmdInspect.rs and crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs: `jet inspect <plane> [TARGET] [--live PID | --replay ARTIFACT]` for types, rights, claims, shapes, structure, build, and gates; TARGET defaults to the current package; `--live` and `--replay` are exclusive (E2102). Fold table: facts to types, authority to rights, unsafe to gates, guarantees to rights, report to build, dossier to build, `live <pid>` to `--live PID`. Each retired name prints its new home for one edition and exits non-zero. Task actions (schema, codemod, sbom, bind, logs, info, outdated, digest, env, expand, output, provenance, semindex, impact, graph, query, explain-build, compiler, audit, live) keep their spelling. Regenerate help, man, and completions; update docs/reference/cli.md. The rights, claims, and shapes planes may print their skeleton (plane name plus the existing view's rows) until #2501, #2502, and #2503 fill them.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli --test cli_commands --test cli_surface --test help_pty` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet inspect authority` prints "use jet inspect rights" and exits non-zero.

Slice 4, the closed loop. tests/verdict_loop.rs (register it in tests/suites.txt): a program with one rights conflict goes emit (`jet check --json` reports E0712 with one needs-review edit), fix (`jet fix --json` applies the safe classes and lists the grant as skipped), decide (the test applies the named manual edit: move the call out of the #FX block), and re-run to an empty `reports` array, using only `jet.status/v1` objects; the needs-review grant is never applied by `jet fix`.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test verdict_loop` green.

Writable paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/{Report.rs,Registry.rs,Diagnostics.rs}, crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs, Source/main.rs, Source/CmdInspect.rs, Source/CmdReport.rs, Source/CmdDossier.rs, Source/CmdProve.rs, Source/CmdStatus.rs, Source/CmdGates.rs, Source/CmdUnsafe.rs, tests/diagnostics_coverage.rs, tests/diagnostics_coverage_baseline.txt, tests/verdict_loop.rs, tests/cli*.rs, tests/report.rs, tests/suites.txt, docs/reference/cli.md, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/diagnostic-rows.md. Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: not a runtime change; the status object is CLI output. The closed-loop test runs `jet check` and `jet fix` only.

Non-goals: the five safety classes stay (D-REPORT-FIXGRADE1 = D); the one-object-per-line law stays; no new plane beyond the seven; `jet explain` stays.

cards.title: Records: one index, one identity, safe capture by default in dev (slate 6)
cards.body: Implementation card for docs/proposals/records-one-receipt.md. Ballots D-RECORD1 (recommended B), D-RECORD-SPELL1 (D), D-TIMETRAVEL2 (B). Every ratified artifact keeps its bytes and codec (the jet-receipt-v2 receipt store of D-DEVR-TWICE1, .jetproof, .jetproof-replay); the safe and sensitive replay split of D-PROVE-REPLAY1 is unchanged; this card adds an index, one identity key, and a dev-tier default. Gated on its ballots on card #2500. Phase A work is internal and may start before ratification; every user-facing criterion waits for its ballot outcome. Full I9 tier parity, I4 snapshots, and I5 examples are required for each criterion. Revised 2026-09-01 after the beginner (rli5) and rival-family adversarial passes; the proposal document carries the reviewed design and the ballot recommendations. jet build --verify is proposed, not shipped; the opt-in --record=NAME capture on run/dev/test is shipped and stays.
cards.plan:
Ratified law (2026-09-02): D-RECORD1 = B (one index under .jet/records over the ratified formats with one identity key: target inputSha256, tool, engine; cross-links from a proof to the replay it consumed and the receipt it produced; `jet dev` captures the ratified safe replay by default within a retention budget of 256 MB and 200 records; the sensitive form only after one typed consent `capture sensitive` per session; release never captures without the flag; `jet build --verify` rebuilds from receipt inputs), D-RECORD-SPELL1 = D (`jet prove TARGET --save ARTIFACT` copies the replay under .jet/records/saved/<artifact_id> and lists it as a claim named `replay <artifact_id>` that runs first on every `jet prove` of the target; `--unsave <id>` removes it; anchors survive edits elsewhere; verdicts passed, failed, diverged E3623, vacuous), D-TIMETRAVEL2 = B (jump ships with the recorder on #2461; reverse step waits on two fixture facts; nothing to build here), D-CLI-ONE1 = A (`jet inspect build <target>` renders the index). Read each picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json`; the reviewed design is docs/proposals/records-one-receipt.md. Criterion 4 on this card says `--keep`, `--unkeep`, and `.jet/records/kept/`; the ratified spelling is `--save`, `--unsave`, and `.jet/records/saved/`, and the ratified spelling wins.

Actual: receipts (Source/ReceiptStore.rs, jet-receipt-v2), .jetproof, and .jetproof-replay artifacts each live in their own store with no shared index or identity; `jet dev` never captures; a replay can be consumed by `jet prove --replay` but never kept as a claim; no `jet build --verify`.

Expected: one index, one identity key, safe capture by default in dev, saved replays as claims, and a rebuild check from a receipt.

Slices, in order. Each slice is one worker brief and leaves scripts/agent/lane-check.sh clean.

Slice 1, the index (internal). Write .jet/records/index.jsonl, one line per artifact, `{target, tool, engine, kind, id, consumed: [...], produced: [...]}` keyed by target.inputSha256 and report_id or artifact_id; one changed source byte changes target; a different engine is a second row. Every writer (Source/ReceiptStore.rs, Source/CmdProve.rs for .jetproof and .jetproof-replay, the evidence and trust record writers) appends its row. The receipt and proof codecs gain the link fields under a version bump; bytes of existing artifacts do not change. `jet inspect build <target>` (Source/CmdInspect.rs) renders the index; sensitive records are listed only after the ratified authentication. Register a new test file tests/records_index.rs in tests/suites.txt.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test records_index --test receipt_store --test prove` green: one build, one prove, and one replay produce three linked rows and `jet inspect build` prints them.

Slice 2, `jet build --verify <id>`. Rebuild from an indexed receipt's inputs (Source/CmdCompile.rs, sharing the D-BUILD-NOCHANGE1 contract) and compare bytes; report identical bytes or the first differing input. Prove native byte identity on this machine, or card the divergence with the exact input that differs.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test records_index -- verify` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet build --verify <id>` on a hello build prints `identical`.

Slice 3, safe capture by default in dev (D-RECORD1 = B). In Source/CmdDevTools.rs run_dev: capture the ratified safe form (clock only) on every run within the budget (256 MB and 200 records by default, oldest evicted, settable under `dev: .{ records: .{ budget: … } }` in package.jet); print the capture line on start and the replay id on a fault; when the program reaches randomness, raw input, or the network, show the ratified preflight once per session and ask for the phrase `capture sensitive`; consent is a digest over target, capture mode, authorities, hosts and streams, byte limit, disclosures, and destination, and any change asks again; a session without a terminal prints `capture: skipped (<effect> at <file>:<line>); no terminal to consent` and continues; `records: .{ capture: off }` and `jet dev --no-capture` refuse; release never captures without the flag; `jet prove --capture`, `--record`, and `--capture-sensitive` keep E3627. Snapshot every line. Measure on gauntlet/entries how often the safe form suffices and record the count on this card.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev --test diagnostic_snapshots --test records_index -- capture` green.

Slice 4, saved replays (D-RECORD-SPELL1 = D). `jet prove TARGET --save ARTIFACT` and `--unsave <id>` in Source/CmdProve.rs and crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs; `jet prove --replay` accepts an index id or a path; a saved claim carries producer replay in the evidence report and runs before doctests; the anchor is (function stable id, record kind, ordinal within the function) stored at save time; verdicts passed, failed, diverged (E3623, register the row per docs/spec/diagnostics.md, snapshot), vacuous; two saves of one artifact are one claim; every verdict except passed names `--unsave` or a fresh capture. Update docs/reference/cli.md.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test prove -- save` covers the four verdicts and the one-claim rule.

Slice 5, the D-TIMETRAVEL2 facts. No code here. When #2461 ships jump, record on this card the three gate facts (default safe capture shipped, E3623 divergence under one in a thousand on the corpus, `jet debug` adapter suite green) with the command that produced each.

Writable paths: Source/ReceiptStore.rs, Source/CmdProve.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs, Source/CmdDevTools.rs, Source/CmdInspect.rs, Source/main.rs, crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs, crates/jet-pkg-model/src/ (policy fields), crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs, tests/records_index.rs, tests/receipt_store.rs, tests/prove.rs, tests/dev.rs, tests/ui/, tests/suites.txt, docs/reference/cli.md, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/diagnostic-rows.md. Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: a saved replay claim must give the same verdict on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`; the prove test runs the replay on all three.

Non-goals: no format change to .jetproof or .jetproof-replay; the D-PROVE-REPLAY1 safe and sensitive split stays; no backward stepping; no new command.

cards.title: Open tables: Core is Jet, declared once, bootstrapped in order (slate 7)
cards.body: Implementation card for docs/proposals/open-tables.md. Ballot D-OPENTABLE1 (recommended D: tables with a Jet twin are generated under a drift guard; tables with no twin keep their Rust home under a second-copy guard). Syntax.rs stays the ratified hand table for keywords and sigils; the parser needs it before any Prelude file is read. Generated Rust is checked in and diffed against the declarations. Core roots stay closed to user packages. Gated on its ballots on card #2500. Phase A work is internal and may start before ratification; every user-facing criterion waits for its ballot outcome. Full I9 tier parity, I4 snapshots, and I5 examples are required for each criterion. Revised 2026-09-01 after the beginner (rli5) and rival-family adversarial passes; the proposal document carries the reviewed design and the ballot recommendations.
cards.plan:
Ratified law (2026-09-02): D-OPENTABLE1 = D (every table with a Jet twin is generated from it with a drift guard that fails the build on a hand row: effect roots and leaves, marker sites, fact reads, encoding formats, taint sinks, transaction irreversibility, the Core dispatcher, ambient routes, the export classifier; tables with no twin keep their Rust home under a guard that fails when a second copy appears: the lexer keyword map, the CLI inventory, the report enums, the tier list; @irreversible is declared on FS.Write, Net, Exec, and FFI; precondition: a derivability census of the 622 dispatcher rows lists every row the generator cannot derive before the dispatcher switches), D-CLI-ONE1 = A (`jet inspect structure --core` is the view). Generation is a workspace build step over committed declarations, checked in like the embedded Prelude; Syntax.rs stays the hand table for keywords and sigils. Read each picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json`; the reviewed design is docs/proposals/open-tables.md. #2513 (core.services and core.task drift) is a live implementation lane on the same rows; read its result before slice 1 and do not redo its rename.

Actual: effect roots live in two hand enums (crates/jet-foundation/src/Effects.rs and BuildEffects.rs); the Core dispatcher rows (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs CORE_CALLS) and docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json disagree on names; crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreModuleExports.rs is a hand table; the transaction checker keeps a private irreversible table; the derive registry (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration/Derives.rs) is a Rust table.

Expected: the Prelude declares the twins once, generated Rust is checked in and diffed against the declarations, and a census names every dispatcher row the generator cannot derive.

Slices, in order. Each slice is one worker brief and leaves scripts/agent/lane-check.sh clean.

Slice 1, the census (internal, no product change). Write scripts/agent/core-dispatcher-census.mjs: read CORE_CALLS in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs (do not edit that file; another lane owns core_calls.rs and core_call.rs, read them only) and docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json, and print every dispatcher row with its derivability class (declared in the ledger, name drift, adapter-only, undeclared). Record the counts on this card. Each undeclared row becomes a declared fact in the Prelude Core module declaration (slice 2) or a card before the dispatcher switches.
Proof: `node scripts/agent/core-dispatcher-census.mjs` prints the table and exits 0; the log carries the four counts.

Slice 2, bootstrap steps 1 to 3 (generated tables with a twin). Declare effect roots, leaves, and the lexical reservations in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Effects.jet with `@irreversible` on FS.Write, Net, Exec, and FFI. Add a generator (a workspace build step, for example crates/jet-foundation/build.rs or a checked-in `scripts/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs` run by `jet self devtools grammars`) that writes crates/jet-foundation/src/Effects.rs and BuildEffects.rs from the declaration, and writes CoreModuleExports.rs, the dispatcher rows that the census could derive, and docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json from a Prelude Core module declaration. The generated files are checked in; a test diffs them against a fresh generation and fails on drift (tests/core_call_table.rs and tests/core_surface_ledger.rs are the pins to extend). Rows the generator cannot derive keep their argument adapter as hand marshalling code and only the row that names the adapter is generated; the diff lists every underived row until the count is zero. core.tasks is the canonical spelling; the core.task alias row and dispatcher row are deleted (with #2513).
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_call_table --test core_surface_ledger --test core_call_witness --test effects` green; `node scripts/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs` exits 0; the drift test fails when one generated row is edited by hand (prove once, then revert).

Slice 3, guards for tables with no twin. Add one test per table that fails when a second copy appears: the lexer keyword map (crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Tokens.rs against crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, tests/syntax_reconciliation.rs is the pin), the CLI inventory (crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs against Source/main.rs, shared with #2505 slice 1), the report enums (crates/jet-foundation/src/Report.rs), and the tier list (Source/CmdCompile.rs; #2504 slice 1 turns it into a ledger value).
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test syntax_reconciliation --test cli_surface --test report` green.

Slice 4, step 4 (D-OPENTABLE1 = D). The sema derive registry (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration/Derives.rs) becomes a Prelude declaration using the same template mechanism user code uses (D-ONCE-DERIVE1); the transaction checker (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Effects.rs, D-TXN rules) reads @irreversible from the declaration instead of its private table (shared with #2501 slice 2; whichever lands first does it, the other reuses it). `jet inspect structure --core` (Source/CmdInspect.rs) lists the declared home of every Core module and root.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test shared_transaction --test auto_derive_policy --test structure_fact_plane` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet inspect structure --core` prints one row per Core module with its declaration file and line.

Writable paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Effects.jet and a new Prelude Core module declaration file, crates/jet-foundation/src/{Effects.rs,BuildEffects.rs,CoreModuleExports.rs} (generated), crates/jet-foundation/build.rs or scripts/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs, scripts/agent/core-dispatcher-census.mjs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration/Derives.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Effects.rs (transaction checker only), Source/CmdInspect.rs, tests/core_call_table.rs, tests/core_surface_ledger.rs, tests/syntax_reconciliation.rs, tests/report.rs, docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json (generated), docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md (the D-OPENTABLE1 amendment notes to D-META-ONE1 and D-META-REG1). Read-only: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs and crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs (another lane owns them; generated rows for the dispatcher are written to a new generated file that core_call.rs includes, and that include line is the only edit, made after the owning lane lands). Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs or crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs.

I9: tables are compile-time facts; every tier reads the same generated rows. Prove one Core-calling example on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret` after slice 2.

Non-goals: Syntax.rs is not generated; Core roots stay closed to user packages; no bootstrap cycle (the lexer is not generated from the declarations it parses).

cards.title: The lexical space: reservations and three repairs (slate 8)
cards.body: Implementation card for docs/proposals/syntax-lexical-space.md. Ballots D-RAWSTR1 (recommended A), D-TRAILCOMMA1 (A), D-SEMI1 (A), D-MARKERSHAPE1 (B, the ratified law stands), D-MARKERARGS1 (A, #HTML only). Each ballot is independent. The phantom switch grammar is card #2512. Gated on its ballots on card #2500. Phase A work is internal and may start before ratification; every user-facing criterion waits for its ballot outcome. Full I9 tier parity, I4 snapshots, and I5 examples are required for each criterion. Revised 2026-09-01 after the beginner (rli5) and rival-family adversarial passes; the proposal document carries the reviewed design and the ballot recommendations.
cards.plan:
Ratified law (2026-09-02): D-RAWSTR1 = A (backtick raw `String` with the Markdown code-span rule: a run of N backticks opens, the next run of exactly N closes, other runs are content; no escapes, no interpolation, multi-line, bytes kept as typed including CRLF; one padding space stripped from each end when the content starts and ends with a space and is not all spaces; the empty raw String is written `""`), D-TRAILCOMMA1 = A (a trailing comma parses in every comma list: parameters, arguments, list and map literals, typed literal bodies, marker groups, effect rows, import lists, type arguments, loop headers; `jet fmt` writes it on a multi-line list and removes it on a one-line list; a comment after the last item counts as multi-line), D-SEMI1 = A (an explicit semicolon is E0373 with a behavior-preserving edit: a line break when code follows on the same line, removal at line end; the parser keeps the boundary so one file reports once; a corpus census first), D-MARKERSHAPE1 = B (no change to D-MARK-STACK1 and E0999), D-MARKERARGS1 = A (`#HTML(page: Path)`; `jet fix` rewrites `#HTML("x")` to `#HTML(Path{"x"})`). Each ballot is independent. Read each picked option with `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision show <id> --json`; the reviewed design is docs/proposals/syntax-lexical-space.md. #2512 (phantom switch) is a live lane; wait for it before slice 1's ledger table.

Actual: backticks lex as nothing; trailing commas are rejected in parameters, arguments, marker groups, effect rows, import lists, type arguments, and loop headers; E0373 today covers only a semicolon in a loop header (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs:1761); `#HTML` takes a plain string (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs:464-467).

Expected: the four ratified grammar changes, each with a Syntax.rs entry carrying its decision id (I7), formatter round trips, snapshots, examples, and regenerated grammars.

Slices, one ballot each. Each slice leaves scripts/agent/lane-check.sh clean and, because grammar changed, ends with `scripts/agent/jet-env jet self devtools grammars` and `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test syntax_reconciliation --test grammar`.

Slice 1, the ledger and the census (no grammar change). Render the lexical ledger table from docs/proposals/syntax-lexical-space.md into docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md as generated from crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs (extend tests/syntax_reconciliation.rs to pin the table). Run a census of every `.jet` file under examples/, tests/, gauntlet/, and docs/ for explicit statement-level semicolons (a small script under scripts/agent/) and record the count and file list on this card before slice 4 lands.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test syntax_reconciliation` green; the log carries the census count.

Slice 2, raw strings (D-RAWSTR1 = A). New token in crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Tokens.rs and the scan in Lexer/Strings.rs; the fence rule and the padding rule exactly as ratified; an unterminated fence is a registered diagnostic naming the opening line (docs/spec/diagnostics.md "Adding a diagnostic", snapshot); a teaching diagnostic for the rejected prefix forms (`r"…"`, `raw"…"`) with a snapshot; Syntax.rs entry under D-RAWSTR1 (I7); the value is an ordinary `String` in sema and every backend, so codegen, JIT, and interpreter need no new arm beyond the literal; crates/jet-parser/src/Formatter round trip (identical decoded bytes after reparse); amend S8 and S20 in docs/spec/spec.md; example under examples/features/strings/ with golden output on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`, including a CRLF case and a nested fence inside an ordinary string hole.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-lexer -p jet-parser --test fmt --test fmt_round_trip_regressions --test diagnostic_snapshots --test golden -- strings` green.

Slice 3, trailing commas (D-TRAILCOMMA1 = A). One parser change per row in crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/ (functions_params.rs, Expressions.rs for arguments and type arguments, marker_groups.rs, the effect-row parser, imports_policy.rs, Statements/control.rs for loop headers); a test per row in the parser crate; `jet fmt` writes the comma on multi-line lists and removes it on one-line lists, a trailing comment counts as multi-line (tests/fmt.rs). Syntax.rs entry under D-TRAILCOMMA1.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-parser --test fmt --test fmt_project --test grammar` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet fmt --check` on examples/ and tests/ reports no change.

Slice 4, the explicit semicolon (D-SEMI1 = A). Explicit and inserted terminators share TokKind::Semi (crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Terminators.rs); the E0373 row gains the statement-level case dispatched on a non-empty source span, with fix_edits: a line break when code follows on the same line, removal at line end; the parser keeps the boundary and reports once per file; two snapshots (mid-line and line-end). Apply the fix to every file the slice 1 census found. Syntax.rs entry under D-SEMI1.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-parser --test diagnostic_snapshots --test ui_fixes` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet check` over the census files is clean.

Slice 5, marker arguments (D-MARKERARGS1 = A; D-MARKERSHAPE1 = B needs no change). Change the marker signature to `HTML(page: Path)` in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Markers.jet and crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs (D-MARKSIG1); a malformed path fails at compile time with the Path grammar's diagnostic; `jet fix` rewrites `#HTML("x")` to `#HTML(Path{"x"})` (tests/ui_fixes.rs); one example under examples/features/web/ and one snapshot; E0999 snapshots unchanged. Syntax.rs entry under D-MARKERARGS1.
Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test marker_rule_signatures --test marker_declarations --test ui_fixes --test diagnostic_snapshots` green.

Writable paths: crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/{Tokens.rs,Strings.rs,Terminators.rs,Scan.rs}, crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/ and Formatter/, crates/jet-foundation/src/{Syntax.rs,Registry.rs,Syntax/core_surface.rs,Syntax/markers.rs}, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Markers.jet, tests/{syntax_reconciliation.rs,grammar.rs,fmt.rs,fmt_project.rs,fmt_round_trip_regressions.rs,ui_fixes.rs,marker_rule_signatures.rs}, tests/ui/, examples/features/{strings,web}/, docs/spec/{spec.md,syntax-decisions.md,diagnostics.md,diagnostic-rows.md}, the generated grammar files under editors/ or docs/ that `jet self devtools grammars` writes, scripts/agent/ (census script). Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs, or crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/math_layout.rs (owned by #2512 until it lands).

I9: raw strings are ordinary `String` values; the golden example proves byte-identical output on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`. The other slices are parse-time only.

Non-goals: no new marker stacking rule; no other backtick meaning; no change to S70 multi-line trimming outside a fence; the empty raw String stays `""`.

cards.title: package.jet authority.holds allow list does not refuse the package's own Net use on jet check or jet build
cards.body: Probe at commit 8b9933668: a package with `authority: { holds: { allow: [FS, Time] } }` whose run.jet declares `fn fetch(url: String) String -[Net]> { … http.get … }` and calls it from `run()` passes `jet check` (exit 0, only L0510 and L0520 warnings) and `jet build` (exit 0; the binary fails only on DNS). D-EFFBUDGET1 and D-AUTHORITY-MANIFEST1=A say the authority block holds package bounds and enforces the whole graph; the example examples/features/packages/effect_budget/package.jet describes dependency enforcement. Either the law scopes bounds to dependencies only (then the spec and the example must say so and jet check must report the package's own reach) or own-code enforcement is missing. Scratch: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/wla-verify/1-rights. Found by the whole-language audit (#2500).
cards.plan:
Actual: a package with `authority: { holds: { allow: [FS, Time] } }` whose own `fn fetch(url: String) String -[Net]>` calls http.get passes `jet check` and `jet build` (exit 0). Expected: the package bound covers the whole graph including the package's own code (D-AUTHORITY-MANIFEST1 = A makes the authority block the package bound; D-EFFBUDGET1 enforces it over the whole graph), so the program fails with the registered authority diagnostic naming `fetch` and `Net`, and passes once `Net` is in the allow list.

Steps:
1. Reproduce: copy ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/wla-verify/1-rights into a fresh scratch package and run `scripts/agent/jet-env jet check` there; confirm exit 0.
2. Find where the manifest bound is applied (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Effects.rs effects_uncovered callers and the authority checks in tests/authority_manifest.rs's subject; `grep -rn "holds" crates/jet-sema/src crates/jet-driver/src`). The bound is checked against dependency summaries only; extend the same check to the root package's own callable summaries (the inferred transitive row of every callable reachable from `run`).
3. Report the existing registered authority denial code (the one dependency violations use today; do not add a code) with the callable name and the effect; one UI snapshot under tests/ui/ from the probe program; a second fixture with `Net` added passes.
4. Spec: add one sentence to the D-AUTHORITY-MANIFEST1 entry in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md stating that the bound covers the package's own code; mirror it in the comment of examples/features/packages/effect_budget/package.jet.
5. Tier check: `jet build` and `jet run` both stop at the sema diagnostic; `jet check --json` carries it.

Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test authority_manifest --test diagnostic_snapshots` green with the new fixture; `scripts/agent/jet-env jet check <scratch probe>` exits non-zero naming `fetch` and `Net`.

Writable paths: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Effects.rs (bound application), crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs (if the bound is applied there), tests/authority_manifest.rs, tests/ui/, examples/features/packages/effect_budget/, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md. Do not touch crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs.

Non-goals: no new diagnostic code; no narrowing of the bound to dependencies (that would need its own ballot); no change to how leaves expand.

cards.title: Phantom switch grammar: Syntax::KW_SWITCH is the string "if" and Stmt::Switch has no live parse
cards.body: Lane A of the whole-language audit (~/.cache/jet-luna/wla/laneA.md:238-239,244) found a phantom source spelling. crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/math_layout.rs:353-384 defines KW_SWITCH whose value is literally "if"; source switch lexes as an identifier and checks with E0003 (probe p06). crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/statements.rs:184-189 keeps a Stmt::Switch variant that no parser path produces, while the ratified branch law says if is the one branching keyword. I7 says every user-typeable keyword lives in Syntax.rs with a decision ID; a keyword constant that is not a keyword and an AST variant with no grammar are dead weight that misleads the next reader. Fix: delete KW_SWITCH, TokKind::KwSwitch, and Stmt::Switch with every arm that matches them; confirm tests/syntax_ledger.rs and the grammar snapshot still pass; leave the E0003 behavior for a source switch unchanged.

cards.title: Core module name drift: dispatcher says core.services and core.task, ledger says core.service and core.tasks
cards.body: Lane F of the whole-language audit (~/.cache/jet-luna/wla/laneF.md:136-137) found two name drifts between the Core call dispatcher and the canonical surface ledger. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs CORE_CALLS carries 18 rows under core.services while docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json names the module core.service. The ledger alias table (core-surface-ledger.json:1-9) maps core.task to core.tasks while the dispatcher still has a core.task row. D-ONCE-LAW1=A says every truth has one home; today the dispatcher and the ledger disagree and an alias table hides it. Fix: the canonical spellings are the ledger's (core.service and core.tasks; docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json is the rendered inventory of D-CORE-TREE1); rename every dispatcher row and example to them, delete the core.task alias entry and dispatcher row, and add a test that fails when a dispatcher module name is absent from the ledger. Proposal docs/proposals/open-tables.md phase A generates these tables from one declaration; this card is the immediate drift fix and closes independently.
cards.plan:

Delete the `core.task` alias entry from the ledger through its generator, never by hand-editing the JSON.
