cards.title: jet-store: one machine-wide artifact store; BuildCache and RuntimeCache cutover
cards.body:
ACTUAL: BuildCache (~/.cache/jet/build, bin + bin.sha256, no bound: Source/BuildCache.rs), RuntimeCache (~/.cache/jet/runtime, 512 MiB FIFO: Source/RuntimeCache.rs), RunCache, ReceiptStore (<pkg>/.jet/receipts), the declared-action CAS (.jet/build-cache/cas, actions), package receipts, the FFI bridge cache, and the C bindings cache are eight file stores with eight key and integrity rules.

EXPECTED (per the D-BUILD-STORE1 outcome; recommended option E): one std-only crate crates/jet-store (path dependency, I6) with cas/<sha256> blobs, ac/<key> records (jet.store.v1), lto/<output-identity>/ cache dirs, a checksummed size-counted last-use journal, atomic temp+rename publish, verify-on-read, versioned records, in-flight per-key locks, cross-process live leases with crash recovery, pre-write admission against available space with a 2 GiB free-space reserve (statvfs available blocks; Windows volume API), and a default cap of min(20 GiB, 10% of the filesystem holding the store) that a host policy may lower. LRU pruning runs after a command; an entry that cannot fit safely is refused with a tool error naming the path. jet cache status (footprint, effective limit and its source, tiers) and jet cache prune [--to <size>] exist; jet self doctor shows the footprint row. BuildCache and RuntimeCache are deleted in the same change; their consumers write and read Link and runtime-unit entries in the store.

Writable paths: crates/jet-store/** (new), Source/BuildCache.rs (delete), Source/RuntimeCache.rs (delete; move rlib build logic into a store-backed executor), Source/CmdCompile.rs, Source/Cmd* for jet cache, Source/Doctor.rs, crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs, tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs, docs/spec/architecture.md (R8 wording).

Non-goals: RunCache and ReceiptStore cutover (next card), declared-action CAS move (compiler-nodes card). Invariants: I6 (no external deps), R8 (verified reuse; corrupt entries fall back to a rebuild).

Land crates/jet-store with unit tests for publish atomicity, verify-on-read, version refusal, journal integrity and compaction, LRU prune to a target, the adaptive bound, pre-write admission with the reserve, live leases across two processes, and the host override. 2. Route the final binary and the runtime rlibs through the store; keys unchanged in content, moved to the store's key domain. 3. cards.title: Hidden compile units, phase 1: partition, two-crate emission, Jet symbols, per-unit rustc
cards.body:
Current path: Driver lowers checked TIR once into canonical MIR, then calls MIRRust::emit_mir_program. That printer emits the user program and marked runtime/Core blocks; jet-store::runtime::prepare/split_generated extracts at most two local rlibs. This is not per-user-unit compilation.
Implement D-BUILD-UNITS1=A through the existing MIR/artifact contract. Partition the package module graph plus impl-placement edges; isolate the entry unit and name units deterministically from sorted module membership. Each unit has an interface crate (types, traits, generic bodies, impl forwarders and ratified typed declarations) and implementation crate (bodies and signature-keyed exported symbols). Dependent units take interface metadata; Link joins implementation rlibs. Entry globals, allocator, command schema and main stay in the entry implementation.
Owned paths: crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs; crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs; Codegen/TIR/{mir.rs,artifact_plan.rs} only for canonical producer/artifact changes; crates/jet-foundation/src/{MIR.rs,Names.rs}; crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/plan_impl.rs; crates/jet-store/src/runtime.rs; Source/CmdCompile.rs; existing build-graph/parity tests and the required unit-edit regressions. Do not revive emit_bundle_dbg_inner or the old TIR printer.
Non-goals: a new IR/backend, phase-2 generic placement (#2520), ThinLTO (#2522), public distribution (#2525). Preserve I1 under the exact D-BUILD-UNITS1 ruling, I2, I3 and I9. Units never cross package boundaries; sema still owns visibility and language checks.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-BUILD-UNITS1=A, hidden compile units phase 1. The checked package module graph (plus impl-placement edges) is partitioned into deterministic units. Each unit gets an interface crate and an implementation crate, rustc runs per unit, and a Link step joins the implementation rlibs. A body edit then recompiles one unit.

## Current state
- Neither emitter has a unit partition or iface/impl emission. `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Program.jet` prints one program crate. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs` `emit_mir_program` does the same.
- `crates/jet-store/src/runtime.rs` (`prepare`/`split_generated`) extracts at most two local rlibs (runtime and Core).
- `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet` builds the artifact plan (`jet_driver_artifact_plan`, around :2102) but carries no unit membership.
- `tests/units_incremental.rs` does not exist. `tests/dev_default_parity.rs` exists.
- The inline-monolith retry (split rejection rerun) is still in `Source/CmdCompile.rs`.

## Changes
1. Jet driver (`Pipeline.jet`, `Identity.jet`): compute unit membership from the checked module and impl graph. Isolate the entry unit, name units from sorted module membership, and record the result on the canonical MIR artifact records (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/MIR`). Add signature-keyed symbols `_JET_<pkg>_<module>_<item>_<abihash>`. The hash covers signature, rustc build, target features, panic strategy and layout flags.
2. Jet printer (`Emit/Program.jet`): print one iface crate (types, traits, generic bodies, impl forwarders, typed declarations) and one impl crate (bodies, exported symbols) per unit. Entry globals, the allocator, the command schema and `main` stay in the entry impl. The emitter does no semantic rechecking.
3. Host (retained):
   - Add Compile(unit.iface), Compile(unit.impl) and Link nodes in `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/plan_impl.rs` and `crates/jet-store/src/runtime.rs`.
   - Run rustc per unit in `Source/CmdCompile.rs` and delete the inline-monolith retry. A rejected unit becomes an ICE that names the unit and its generated path.
   - Add a single-crate fallback for targets that cannot honour the symbol contract, surfaced through `jet explain-build`.
   - Add MIR validation of the unit records.
4. Mirror: have the shipped Rust driver and MIRRust.rs consume the same projection, so the host tests exercise it. Do not revive the old TIR printer.
5. Tests: add `tests/units_incremental.rs` and extend `tests/dev_default_parity.rs`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test units_incremental`: passes. A leaf body edit runs exactly one Compile(unit.impl) and one Link. A signature edit recompiles only the importing units. Adding a module re-keys only the units whose membership changed. A skewed ABI record fails at link with an ICE that names the unit.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_default_parity`: every `Tools/perf/corpus.tsv` program and every `Examples/features/packages/**` example gives the same stdout, stderr and exit code on AOT release, AOT debug, `jet run` and `--interpret`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: no new JetDriver or JetCodegen errors.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: the unit projection is driver work. The printer and host nodes land in the same build.

## Dependencies
#2517 (persisted checks, D-INCR-UNIT1 layers 1-2). #2518 is done.

Out of scope: #2520 (generic placement), #2522 (ThinLTO), #2525 (public tier).

cards.title: Hidden compile units, phase 2: Jet-owned generic instantiation with deterministic placement
cards.body:
This is conditional phase-2 work after #2519, not a shipped phase-1 claim. The phase-1 design leaves generic bodies in interface units; rustc may instantiate the same concrete body in several users. Canonical MIR already owns resolved/instantiated generic-call meaning under D-TIER-FORM1.
Gate from automatic-build-optimization.md III.4: proceed only when phase 1 measures more than 15% of LLVM time in duplicated generic instances across units. A duplicate-symbol/object-size census or a high rank for generic-body interface churn cannot independently open this gate.
If triggered, reuse the existing checked demand/instance mechanism and place each demanded concrete instance once: the unit owning its most specific package-local type argument, ties resolved by the generic definition unit. Emit its non-generic symbol through MIRRust; interface units retain only the bodies/forwarders required by the approved contract. No parallel generic registry or emitter-owned semantic specialization.
Owned paths: the actual checked demand/instantiation producer in Codegen/TIR/mod.rs and its necessary lowering; canonical MIR/artifact instance records; Codegen/MIRRust.rs; active Driver/unit placement; focused generic edit/parity tests. Keep trait objects and generic language semantics unchanged.
cards.plan:
## Goal
This is conditional phase-2 work after #2519. Measure how much LLVM time goes to duplicated generic instances across units. If the share is conclusively above 15%, place each demanded concrete instance once. Otherwise, close as not-needed with the measurement.

## Current state
- In phase 1 (#2519, still ready and unimplemented), generic bodies sit in interface units, so rustc may instantiate the same concrete body in several users.
- Canonical MIR owns resolved and instantiated generic-call meaning (D-TIER-FORM1).
- The Jet instance producer is `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/TypeInstances.jet`.
- The owned paths named on the card (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs`, MIRRust.rs) are archived bootstrap code.
- The gate comes from automatic-build-optimization.md III.4. A duplicate-symbol or object-size census, or a high churn rank, cannot open the gate on its own.

## Changes
1. Measurement first, after #2519 lands:
   - Run the phase-1 corpus (`Tools/perf/corpus.tsv`) with rustc `-Z time-passes` or `-Z self-profile` per unit.
   - Alternatively, run a controlled A/B that eliminates duplicates, with the same toolchain, target, profile and corpus.
   - Record the numerator (LLVM time in duplicated instances), the denominator (total LLVM time), the identities and the uncertainty.
   - Keep LLVM time separate from parse, check and link time, and never convert object bytes into time.
2. Only if the share is > 15%:
   - Extend `TypeInstances.jet` and the unit placement in `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet` so each concrete instance is placed once, in the unit that owns its most specific package-local type argument. Ties go to the generic definition's unit.
   - `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit` prints one non-generic symbol per instance. Interface units keep only the required bodies and forwarders.
   - Host MIR validation checks the placement.
   - Keep caller specialization for tiny Core operations. Trait objects and generic semantics are unchanged.
   - Mirror the placement in the shipped path.
3. If the share is conclusively ≤ 15%, record not-needed with the evidence in the card log. An inconclusive result keeps the card open.

## Proof
- Measurement receipt at `~/.cache/jet-luna/perf/units-generic-share.json`, with the percentage, identities and uncertainty, is attached to the card log.
- If proceeding: `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test units_generics` passes. Every instance symbol appears in exactly one impl rlib, a generic-body edit recompiles only the owning units, and `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_default_parity` passes.

## Batch
batch-measure: the first and deciding deliverable is a measurement. Implementation, if the gate triggers, moves to batch-jetc-driver.

## Dependencies
#2519 (phase-1 units).

cards.title: Sealed package objects with payload: dependency packages as restorable unit sets
cards.body:
ACTUAL: #1422 delivered compiler package actions whose output is a jet.sealed-package.v1 text receipt (package, source digest, compiler, target, profile, dependency snapshots) at .jet/build-cache/package-artifacts/<pkg>.sealed (crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:3568-3594; plan_impl.rs:263-295). Dependency package code is still flattened into the program crate and recompiled per project.

EXPECTED (D-LIB-REUSE1 half one): a dependency package's sealed object is its unit set: interface records, unit.iface/unit.impl rlibs (release) or objects (fast lens), and generic templates as typed TIR instantiated at the use site. Identity is the ladder level 2 key (manifest, lock entry, module digests, policy, authority, dependency identities, compiler, target, profile). Restore from local, then team, then public tiers per the D-JPK cache slate; a restore skips recompiling that package and never skips checking the package being edited. The receipt-only artifact is deleted.

Writable paths: crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/{plan_impl.rs,plan_graph.rs}, crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs (package action runner), crates/jet-codegen (per-package emission roots), crates/jet-store (tier adapter use), tests/build_graph.rs, tests/build_entry.rs.

Non-goals: operating a public mirror; .jetlib loader changes. Invariants: hard rule (never split or merge package artifacts), D-JPK-CACHEAUTH1 verify-on-read, D-JPK-REPROCACHE1 quarantine.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the first half of D-LIB-REUSE1. Each dependency package becomes a restorable, sealed unit set: interface records, `unit.iface`/`unit.impl` rlibs (release) or objects (fast lens), and generic templates as checked IR that is instantiated at the use site. A restore skips recompiling an unchanged dependency but never skips checking the package being edited.

## Current state
- Package actions write a text receipt only:
  - format `jet.sealed-package.v1` (`crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:4065`);
  - path `.jet/package-artifacts/<pkg>.sealed` (`crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/plan_impl.rs:279`).
- Dependency code is still flattened into the program crate and recompiled for every project.
- `tests/build_entry.rs:629` `warm_dependency_cache_still_runs_frontend_diagnostics` exists. `multi_dependency_build_restores_every_unchanged_compiler_artifact` does not.
- The self-hosted driver has no per-package emission root.

## Changes
1. After #2519: `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet` emits each dependency package through its own Partition, Emit and Compile nodes. `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Program.jet` prints per-package roots. Generic templates stay as checked Jet IR for instantiation at the use site.
2. `Identity.jet` builds the unit-set manifest and its level-2 identity from:
   - the manifest and lock entry;
   - module digests;
   - policy and authority;
   - dependency identities;
   - compiler, target and profile.
3. Host (retained): restore through `crates/jet-store` tier adapters, local first and then bound mirrors, verifying digest and signature on read (D-JPK-CACHEAUTH1). A corrupt blob is quarantined and rebuilt with one note line (D-JPK-REPROCACHE1). An unbound mirror is never read or written. Package artifacts are never split or merged.
4. Delete the `jet.sealed-package.v1` format and the `package-artifacts` path in the same cutover (Rust `mod.rs:4065`, `plan_impl.rs:279`), migrating every caller. Mirror the per-package emission in the shipped driver so the tests exercise it.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_entry -- multi_dependency_build_restores_every_unchanged_compiler_artifact`: the second clean build of a three-package project runs zero Compile nodes for the two unchanged dependencies and links an identical binary.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_entry -- warm_dependency_cache_still_runs_frontend_diagnostics`: passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_graph -- corrupt_dependency_blob_is_quarantined_and_rebuilt`: passes.
- `rg 'sealed-package.v1|package-artifacts' crates Source Compiler` finds nothing.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: the package partition and identity live in the driver, and the store adapters land in the same build.

## Dependencies
#2519 (the unit boundary). Non-goals: operating a public mirror, and changes to the `.jetlib` loader.

cards.title: Release lens: per-unit bitcode and a store-managed ThinLTO cache at link
cards.body:
LLVM remains the optimized backend. The earlier 2026-09-01 receipt reported 28.7-30.5 s link phases on the 3349-line corpus program; it is historical evidence, not a current measurement. Implement per-unit LLVM rlib/bitcode and a store-managed ThinLTO cache using #2519 units and the existing jet-store, not a second compiler/cache route.
Preserve the approved release intent: compatible linker-plugin-LTO/embedded-bitcode/codegen-unit flags, a rust-lld matching the active toolchain, store-bounded link cache, and the existing fast-profile linker. Validate the actual flag combination on that toolchain. Do not silently change opt level, runtime semantics or target policy.
Owned paths: Source/{NativeLinker.rs,main.rs,CmdCompile.rs}, crates/jet-store, current unit/artifact identity records and focused compile/link behavior tests. #2525 owns fixed Core contents/public provenance. Local LLVM proof does not wait for a public mirror.
cards.plan:
## Goal
The release lens emits per-unit LLVM rlib/bitcode and links through a store-managed ThinLTO cache. A leaf body edit's link phase is under 3 s on the 3349-line corpus program, and a no-change build does zero ThinLTO codegen. Runtime cells and binary size (<= 2%) must not regress. LLVM stays the optimized backend.

## Current state
- One Rust crate per program; `Source/main.rs:561-562` adds `lto=thin` over the whole program at every link. `Source/NativeLinker.rs` (module at `Source/lib.rs:123`) and `crates/jet-store` own linking and the store.
- The 2026-09-01 receipt of 28.7-30.5 s link phases is history, not a current measurement.
- Compile units come from #2519, now retargeted to the self-hosted `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet` plus `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Program.jet` emission.

## Changes
1. `Source/CmdCompile.rs`/`main.rs`: compile each #2519 unit with `-C linker-plugin-lto` / `embed-bitcode` flags validated on the active toolchain. Discover the toolchain-matching rust-lld.
2. `Source/NativeLinker.rs`: pass `--thinlto-cache-dir` inside the jet-store root, with pruning bounded by jet-store policy.
3. Separate keys: the compile key covers source/dependency content, compiler/rustc/LLVM, target/ISA/ABI, panic/unwind and profile/codegen/bitcode/LTO. The final-link key covers ordered unit digests, native/FFI/model dependencies, linker path/version/args, and the link-only flags that `runtime_compile_flags` strips.
4. Tests assert observable reuse, not flag strings.
5. Measure clean, no-change and leaf-edit builds: link time, re-optimized module set, lld cache stats, runtime, RSS and bytes. Inspect LLVM/asm for cross-unit inlining, specialization and constant folding on bulk and tiny-generic fixtures (criterion 5).

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli_compiler_speed -- release_thinlto_cache_reuses_units` (new) passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_graph -- link_key_covers_link_only_flags` (new) passes.
- Perf report: leaf-edit link under 3 s and zero no-change cache misses.
- Fresh same-run gauntlet runtime cells pass the strict gate, and binaries stay within 2%.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: rustc emission/link and the store are retained host.

## Dependencies
#2519 (unit emission), a real prerequisite.

## Goal

cards.title: Prebuilt runtime and Core units with a public-tier seam
cards.body:
Current source has local content-addressed caching for at most two generated rlibs: shared runtime and a program-shaped Core closure. MIRRust emits flat Core symbols; Codegen::push_full_corelib_prelude_with_policy forces a broad closure. Fixed per-module Core artifacts and public distribution are not established by that mechanism. The prior 17-21 s cold-runtime receipt is historical, not a new measurement. #1025 remains absorbed here.
Implement ratified D-BUILD-PREBUILT1=D through #2519 typed units and #2522 LLVM/link identities. Fixed runtime/common/Core modules keep identical contents and keys across programs; resolved MIR calls select their transitive closure, and link-time dead stripping/ThinLTO preserves pay-for-what-you-call. A newly required module may compile or restore once; an unused module need not be built.
Retain the complete dossier: Jet/compiler/rustc/LLVM, target triple, ISA/baseline family, platform ABI (including deployment/libc/toolset constraints), linker/LTO, panic/unwind, target features, profile/codegen flags and dependency identities. Shared objects use the ratified family baseline; optional higher levels require CPU detection, while the root package keeps its ratified host-native policy. Freestanding uses its separate target-keyed projection of the same semantic source. Web/JIT/interpreter remain parity oracles, not alleged native-rlib consumers.
The public tier serves runtime/Core under the release root and reproducible third-party objects under separate registry-authorized builder roots, off unless host policy opts in. Preserve ordered mirrors, digest/signature/root verification, pinned runtime identity, expiry/checkpoints, revocation and quarantine. Missing/rejected remote artifacts compile the same authoritative source locally. The cold benchmark counts toolchain objects present equally on both sides and records local-compiled versus restored provenance.
Owned paths: active MIRRust/Core source-closure and Driver/artifact projection; crates/jet-store runtime/unit/tier materialization; Source/main.rs ISA policy and CmdCompile integration; existing peer-report and docs explanations where the contract changes. Non-goals: operating a mirror/builder service, new signing-key management, a new Core API/semantics/dependency, generic-placement redesign or a new backend.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-BUILD-PREBUILT1=D. Fixed runtime, common and Core modules become per-module units whose contents and keys are identical across programs. Resolved MIR calls select the transitive closure a program needs, and dead stripping keeps pay-for-what-you-call. A public-tier seam restores signed runtime and Core objects, and third-party objects when policy opts in. #1025 stays absorbed here.

## Current state
- `crates/jet-store/src/runtime.rs` caches at most two generated rlibs: the shared runtime and a Core closure shaped to the program. Its `target_dossier_source_invalidates_runtime_and_core_keys` test is at :998.
- The archived `MIRRust.rs` together with `Codegen::push_full_corelib_prelude_with_policy` forces a broad Core closure.
- The self-hosted producer already records the facts needed: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:2401-2545` gathers `prelude_calls`, `core_calls` and `used_core`, and sorts them at :2530.
- `tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs:995` `production_build_reuses_and_repairs_stdlib_objects` exists.
- The earlier 17-21 s cold-runtime receipt is historical, not a measurement.

## Changes
1. Compiler: make `used_core`/`core_calls` the authoritative per-program Core closure. Using #2519's unit/import contract, partition fixed Core and common roots from canonical MIR Core symbols. `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Program.jet` imports those symbols directly and never prints a program-shaped copy of Core.
2. Host (retained): add runtime/unit/tier materialization in `crates/jet-store`. Record the full dossier:
   - Jet, compiler, rustc and LLVM identities;
   - triple, ISA family baseline and platform ABI;
   - linker and LTO settings;
   - panic strategy and target features;
   - profile and codegen flags;
   - dependency identities.

   Separate the compile and link identities from #2522. The ISA policy lives in `Source/main.rs` and the integration in `Source/CmdCompile.rs`. Shared objects use the family baseline; the root package keeps host-native. Do not extend `push_full_corelib_prelude_with_policy`.
3. Public tier: restore runtime and Core under the release root, and third-party objects under registry-authorized builder roots only when host policy opts in. Verify digest, signature, root, expiry and revocation, and quarantine anything that fails. When a remote object is missing or rejected, compile the same source locally.
4. Kernel candidates (typed bulk DataStats after #3012; whole reader scans; fixed reductions after #2522) are kept only with matched inline, local-shared and prebuilt evidence.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli_compiler_speed -- production_build_reuses_and_repairs_stdlib_objects`, extended for shared and disjoint modules: shows zero repeated rustc for shared units and only the new closure for a disjoint module.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-store -- target_dossier_source_invalidates_runtime_and_core_keys`, extended so every input class forces a miss.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_graph -- public_tier_restore`: covers runtime restore, opt-in third-party restore, tamper quarantine and wrong-root refusal.
- Measurement: every corpus binary is within 2% of today's size, and baseline-ISA objects run under a CPU mask without AVX2.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: Core closure partitioning in the compiler and driver, plus host store materialization, in one build.

## Dependencies
- #2522 (compile/link identity separation).
- #2519 (units).

cards.title: Deterministic scheduler for compiler nodes: pools, critical-path priority, RAM cap, keep-going
cards.body:
ACTUAL: declared actions run in resource-compatible batches with sorted completion (execution_runtime.rs:428-547); compiler work is sequential outside the eight-worker lex/parse fan-out.

EXPECTED: all nodes run under D-BUILDSCHED1's scheduler with pools cpu (min(cores, RAM/1.5 GiB) for rustc), link (2), io, net; ready nodes ordered by longest remaining path (durations from the store) then key; independent subgraphs continue after a failure; dependents of a failed node are cancelled; diagnostics print in stable module order regardless of completion order; two runs with the same inputs schedule identically.

Writable paths: crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/execution_runtime.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs, tests/build_graph.rs.

Non-goals: remote execution. Invariants: deterministic outputs and diagnostics order.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Every build node runs under D-BUILDSCHED1=A's deterministic scheduler:
- the ratified pools are `cpu`, `memory`, `linker`, `console` and `gpu`;
- ready nodes are ordered by longest remaining path (stored durations), then canonical key;
- the rustc cpu cap is min(cores, available RAM / 1.5 GiB);
- keep-going: independent subgraphs continue and only dependents of a failed node are cancelled;
- diagnostics come out in stable module order.

## Current state
- `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/execution_runtime.rs:579-611` `execution_batches` packs actions into resource-compatible batches (limits from `plan.resource_pools()`, `action_pools` from `execution_helpers.rs`). There is no critical-path priority, RAM-derived cap or keep-going policy.
- D-BUILDSCHED1=A is at `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:5021-5023` (the old plan's `docs/spec/...:4880` is stale). The body's `io`/`net` pools are not ratified. Map RAM to `memory`, link to `linker` (capacity 2), and I/O/network to admission inside the existing pools.
- `tests/build_graph.rs:2590` `scheduler_records_parallel_ready_graph_pools_cancellation_and_metrics` and `:2674` exist. `schedule_is_deterministic`, `diagnostics_order_is_stable_under_delays` and `rustc_concurrency_respects_memory_cap` do not.

## Changes
1. `execution_runtime.rs`: replace batch packing with a ready queue over dependency edges. Priority is remaining critical path from stored durations (a missing duration counts as 0), then canonical node key. One admission function enforces the pool slots, with an injectable available-memory reading.
2. Failure: mark transitive dependents cancelled and keep running the rest. Sort completions and diagnostics by canonical module order.
3. `Source/CmdCompile.rs`: all compile callers go through this one scheduler; delete any sequential bypass.
4. Add the three named tests plus a keep-going/critical-path test to `tests/build_graph.rs`.

## Proof
`Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_graph -- schedule_is_deterministic diagnostics_order_is_stable_under_delays rustc_concurrency_respects_memory_cap scheduler_keep_going_cancels_only_dependents` passes. The run shows identical start logs across two runs of the 40-node fixture, and a 6 GiB injected reading gives cpu=4.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: build runtime and CLI.

## Dependencies
None real. The criteria use fixture graphs, and #2519's unit nodes will be scheduled by this same queue when they land, so #2519 is not a prerequisite.

cards.body:
ACTUAL: BuildProgress prints five fixed stage lines and 'Built <path> in <elapsed> ✓' to stderr without a TTY test (Source/CmdCompile.rs:18-76; labels at :1829-1831, :2255, :2408, :2771, :2864, :2898-2902).

EXPECTED (per the D-BUILD-UI1 outcome; owner direction 2026-09-01; mockups in docs/proposals/automatic-build-optimization/mockups/terminal.html): in a TTY a ≤ 8-line board redraws in place at ≤ 10 fps with stage rows (check/emit/compile/link; actions and fetch when relevant), a cpu row showing occupancy (cpu 2/16) and running processes, and a critical-path row whose time-left estimate appears only when recorded durations exist and is labeled est.; width rules at 100/80 columns; collapses to the receipt line; diagnostics and notes print above. Piped: one plain line per stage then the receipt. NO_COLOR removes color only; a non-UTF-8 locale or --ascii uses ASCII bars and [ok]/[x]. One renderer owns stderr: resize and SIGTSTP/SIGCONT handled, cursor restored on every exit path, plain-line fallback when cursor control is unsafe (TERM=dumb, no VT support). --json: NDJSON stage/node/receipt events under a versioned schema; --trace: the same events as Chrome Trace Event JSON. All note lines registered as product copy with snapshots (I4).

Owner look-and-feel check: open mockups/terminal.html; the board should read at a glance (what is running, what is reused, time left) and the receipt line should be the only thing left when done. Report taste, not mechanics.

Writable paths: Source/CmdCompile.rs (BuildProgress replacement), a new Source/BuildBoard.rs, crates/jet-cli (flags), tests/ui/** snapshots, tests/cli/** snapshots.

Non-goals: explain-build content (next card). Invariants: I4; stable diagnostics order.

cards.title: jet explain-build: why-ran, critical path, store panel, --why, and --html report
cards.body:
ACTUAL: jet explain-build explains declared targets, actions, and files from the pure BuildPlan projection (Source/CmdCompile.rs:137-307; plan_impl.rs:635-761); compiler work and rebuild causes are not visible.

EXPECTED (per the D-BUILD-UI1 outcome; mockup: docs/proposals/automatic-build-optimization/mockups/report.html): text output lists per node why it ran (changed input path and digest prefix), the critical path with durations, store hits/misses per tier and footprint, and unit detail rows under packages; --why <node> prints the full input diff; --json returns the graph record; --trace writes Chrome Trace Event JSON; --html [path] writes a self-contained dark page (header strip, per-lane timeline with critical path outlined, package/unit graph, sortable why-table with / j k Enter keys, store panel, reproducibility class per node) that renders from the embedded record serialized as escaped JSON (never HTML concatenation), carries a restrictive CSP meta tag, redacts secrets, and makes no network request; --open opens it. The LSP hover provenance reads the same record (D-BUILDQUERY1).

Owner look-and-feel check: open mockups/report.html; the timeline should make the slow chain obvious and the why-table should answer 'why did this rebuild' in one row.

Writable paths: Source/CmdCompile.rs (run_build_query), a new Source/ExplainHtml.rs (template, following CmdPerf's self-contained dark template conventions: Source/CmdPerf.rs:2027-2077), crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/plan_impl.rs, tests/cli/** snapshots.

Non-goals: live browser view. Invariants: I4 for text output; no network in the page; hostile-input safety.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Per ratified D-BUILD-UI1=A, `jet inspect explain-build` gains:
- why each node ran (changed input path and digest prefix);
- the critical path with durations;
- a store hit/miss and footprint panel;
- unit rows under packages;
- `--why <node>` (full input diff), `--trace` (Chrome Trace Event JSON), and `--html [path]` (a self-contained page).

All of these render from one graph record. The owner looks at the mockup `Docs/proposals/automatic-build-optimization/mockups/report.html`.

## Current state
- `Source/CmdCompile.rs:663-685` `run_build_query` emits only the BuildPlan projection. `:830` is the `jet.explain-build/v1` JSON with nodes. The command is nested under `inspect` (`crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:691`, D-BUILDQUERY1).
- Tests: `tests/build_entry.rs:694` `compiler_speed_explain_build_reports_release_nodes`; snapshots in `tests/cli_parts/surface.rs:2182` `explain_build_fact_golden`.
- There is no `Source/ExplainHtml.rs`, `--why`, `--trace`, `--html` or critical path. #2518 (compiler work as BuildPlan nodes) is done.

## Changes
1. `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/plan_impl.rs`: extend the node record with why-ran input and digest, duration, hit/miss/footprint, unit detail (present once #2519 lands; package rows until then) and reproducibility class. Keep the `jet.explain-build/v1` shape additive.
2. `Source/CmdCompile.rs`: text rows, `--why`, and a `--trace` export from the same record. There is no second timing path; PhaseTiming and BuildPlanReplay stay deleted.
3. New `Source/ExplainHtml.rs`, following the dark template at `Source/CmdPerf.rs:2027-2077`. The record is embedded as escaped JSON, never concatenated into HTML. It carries a restrictive CSP meta tag, stays under 250 KB, loads no external URL, and has sortable why-table keys (`/ j k Enter`). `--open` opens the page.
4. Snapshots in `tests/cli/`: a leaf-edit text report, JSON-equals-HTML-embedded bytes, and hostile strings (`</script>`, `javascript:`, bidi, controls).

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli_surface -- explain_build_` passes (text snapshot after a leaf edit showing the changed input, reused count and critical path; HTML size/CSP/no-URL; embedded JSON byte-equal to `--json`; hostile input DOM check). The existing `explain_build_fact_golden` is updated in place.
- Criterion 3 closes on the minted owner acceptance ballot with the captured report.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: CLI inspection tooling.

## Dependencies
None open. #2518 is done.

cards.title: Opt-in resident build session: jet dev --serve and automatic attach
cards.body:
ACTUAL: every command is a fresh process; jet dev is a foreground WatchSession loop with resident hot swap (Source/CmdDevTools.rs:409-596); it spawns a stdin thread and may bind Canvas/static web hosts (CmdDevTools.rs:348-361, :441-474; crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs:595-601) but accepts no build requests. D-JPK-NODAEMON1 forbids a resident background process and names the dev session as the process that may parent work.

EXPECTED (per the D-BUILD-SESSION1 outcome; recommended option A): jet dev --serve listens on a per-user, per-workspace endpoint (Unix-domain socket in a user-owned 0700 directory under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/jet/ or a private per-user fallback directory; Windows named pipe); jet build, jet run, and jet test in that workspace attach under --session=auto|off|required, submit a serialized request envelope (argv, cwd, env allowlist, terminal mode), and receive the same NDJSON events and exit status a fresh process would produce. The session authenticates the peer OS identity, requires a per-session nonce from the workspace's .jet/, rejects symlinked endpoints, allows one owner per workspace, refuses clients of a different Jet or protocol version (they run fresh), resets request-scoped state per request, binds each request to one source snapshot, re-verifies leaf digests, schedules deterministically, holds output-path locks, propagates Ctrl-C as cancellation, bounds its queue, and may pre-compile units affected by the last edit. Closing the dev terminal ends everything; nothing runs as root. Adoption gate: ship only if measured fresh-process overhead after memoized checks exceeds 100 ms or 20% of the median edit build on the corpus; record the measurement on this card first.

Writable paths: Source/CmdDevTools.rs, crates/jet-devserver/**, Source/CmdCompile.rs (attach), Source/Doctor.rs (session row), tests/cli_dev_session.rs (new).

Non-goals: a background daemon; lifecycle verbs. Invariants: byte-identical outputs to the fresh path; D-JPK-NODAEMON1 as amended by the ballot.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Per ratified D-BUILD-SESSION1=A, within D-JPK-NODAEMON1=A: an opt-in `jet dev --serve` session that `jet build`, `jet run` and `jet test` attach to under `--session=auto|off|required`. Outputs, NDJSON events and exit status are byte-identical to a fresh process. There is never a background daemon.

## Current state
- `Source/CmdDevTools.rs:409-596` is a foreground WatchSession with resident hot swap. It binds only Canvas/static web hosts (`:348-361`, `:441-474`; `crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs:595-601`) and accepts no build requests. There is no `--serve`, and `tests/cli_dev_session.rs` does not exist.
- Adoption gate: ship only if the measured fresh-process overhead after memoized checks exceeds 100 ms or 20% of the median edit build on the #2859/#666 corpus. Record that first.

## Changes
1. Measure the attach delta on the canonical corpus (criterion 1). This does not create a competing compiler-speed gate.
2. `crates/jet-devserver`: the endpoint is a Unix socket in a 0700 user-owned directory under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/jet/` (private fallback directory; a named pipe on Windows). It checks peer OS identity, requires a per-session nonce in the workspace's `.jet/`, rejects symlinked endpoints, allows one owner per workspace, refuses a mismatched Jet/protocol version (the client runs fresh), and bounds the queue.
3. `Source/CmdCompile.rs`: an attach client with a request envelope (argv, cwd, env allowlist, terminal mode). Any failure before side effects falls back to fresh. Requests are bound to one source snapshot and re-verify leaf digests. Ctrl-C propagates as cancellation, and output-path locks are held.
4. `Source/Doctor.rs` shows the session row only while a session runs. Closing the dev terminal removes the endpoint and all children.

## Proof
`Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli_dev_session` passes, covering:
- `attached_build_matches_fresh_build` (SHA-256 and NDJSON identical across success, warning, error and cancel);
- `stale_watch_stream_is_reverified`;
- `foreign_client_is_refused`;
- the endpoint-removed-on-close and second-serve-refused cases.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: CLI and devserver host.

## Dependencies
#2517 (persisted checks) and #2527 (shared event/board contract) are real.

cards.body:

cards.plan:
## Goal
Add the complete 30-case hostile invalidation matrix (proposal III.3) as one table-driven cross-tier suite, `tests/hostile_invalidation.rs`. Each case asserts the exact executed node set and identical stdout/stderr/exit on AOT release, AOT debug, default `jet run` and `jet run --interpret`. No performance assertions.

## Current state
- Cache behavior is tested piecemeal: `tests/build_graph.rs:3655` `per_package_dependency_artifacts_restore_and_invalidate`, `:3941` `compiler_package_identity_target_and_profile_force_rebuild_keys`, and others. `tests/hostile_invalidation.rs` and `tests/fixtures/hostile/` do not exist.
- The proposal is `Docs/proposals/automatic-build-optimization.md` (the card cites lowercase docs/). Criterion 1's `scripts/agent/jet-env` means `Tools/agent/jet-env`.

## Changes
1. Fixture `tests/fixtures/hostile/`: three packages with five modules each, plus `expectations.toml` holding the exact hit/miss node set per case, referenced from proposal III.3.
2. `tests/hostile_invalidation.rs`: one table covering:
   - comment, reformat, body, generic and signature edits;
   - module add/delete and impl move;
   - dependency bump; simulated rustc and Jet identity changes; profile, target and environment switches;
   - touch and `cp -p`; blob corruption; truncated record;
   - concurrent builds; injected disk-full; project move; generated-module change; remote tampering;
   - `--no-cache`; session versus fresh; unsupported-target fallback; store cap eviction; import cycle; harden-policy change.

   Each case reads the graph-record node oracle, not timestamps.
3. Shared helpers in `tests/common`. Register the target in `tests/suites.txt`.

## Proof
`Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test hostile_invalidation` passes 30 named cases, each with the exact node set and four-tier output identity.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: build-graph/store tests over the retained CLI host.

## Dependencies

Add hostile cases: (1) same-second double write with equal length, (2) compiler rebuilt with identical size and first 4 KiB (Source/RunCache.rs:88-132 hashes only a 4 KiB prefix plus metadata), (3) zero-mtime filesystem. Owner wants Zig-grade reliability where no `clean` is ever needed for correctness; today `jet clean` only prunes the package store (probe J13).

cards.body:
ACTUAL: web builds emit one wasm_rust string and run rustc once with --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --crate-type cdylib; web and cross builds never use the native cache (Source/CmdCompile.rs:6972-6997, :2109-2113).

cards.plan:
## Goal
Route web builds through the same build graph and store as native builds: wasm Emit/Compile units, a wasm-ld Link node, the no-change short circuit and memoized checks. Measure per-unit wasm ThinLTO before adopting it. The JavaScript runtime, public web syntax and I9 semantics do not change.

## Current state
- Web builds emit one wasm Rust string and run rustc once with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown --crate-type cdylib`. They never use the native cache. `Source/CmdCompile.rs:11259` `write_web_artifacts` is the publisher; the line numbers on the card have drifted.
- The self-hosted driver already selects the Web artifact: `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:1737-1741` (`MirArtifactKind.WebApplication`) and `:2138-2148` (`JetWebEmitConfig` → `jet_web_emit`). It emits one artifact with no units.
- The card names `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Web.rs` as an owned path. That file is archived; the Jet owner is `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Web/`.

## Changes
1. After #2519: in `Pipeline.jet` and `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Web/`, consume the canonical unit projection and emit one wasm Rust crate per unit. Each carries module membership, source closure, target triple, profile and web artifact names in the node receipt.
2. Host (`Source/CmdCompile.rs` `write_web_artifacts`):
   - Replace the one-shot rustc call with deterministic Emit, Compile and Link (wasm-ld) nodes through the existing store.
   - Publish `app.wasm` and the JS artifacts only after every node succeeds. On failure, keep the last known-good set and its receipt.
3. Key reuse on the full source/dependency closure plus target, profile, toolchain, linker and the relevant web flags. A body edit recompiles one unit and relinks.
4. Measure per-unit wasm ThinLTO with an identical corpus and toolchain. Adopt it only with complete measurements and no strict web-cell loss; otherwise record non-adoption.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_build -- web_graph`: covers four behaviours:
  - a no-change build restores from the store with zero rustc;
  - a body edit compiles one unit and relinks;
  - a target, toolchain or linker change invalidates the affected units;
  - an interrupted build leaves the previous set untouched.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_build`: the whole suite passes, and the web witnesses behave identically.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=web/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- The ThinLTO measurement receipt is attached to the card log.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: this is web unit orchestration in the driver, with the host publisher in the same build.

## Dependencies
#2519 (the unit graph and store contract).

Current native generation is Driver -> canonical MIR -> MIRRust::emit_mir_program. Active string interpolation is MirOperation::BuildString and already emits direct String::push_str construction; the old TIR-printer format! finding is not an active native opportunity. Emitter-side Rust format! calls used to construct source are not generated runtime macros.
Measure only live generated-code costs: imports/derives, type inference work, lint work and any other demonstrated macro expansion on the active path. Keep a lever only when it lowers measured user-unit rustc time without changing meaning or runtime/code-size outcomes. No guaranteed opportunity is inferred from a source grep.
Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs; typed TIR-to-MIR lowering only where a demonstrated operation shape must change; crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs and Source/CmdCompile.rs for the active generation/argument path; existing generated-artifact and semantic parity tests. Do not optimize the retired TIR emitter or its obsolete module layout.
Non-goals: semantics, a new backend, broad Core pruning (#2519/#2525), generic placement (#2520), or speculative scalar-carrier/CFG rewriting (measure first under #3011).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Cut the rustc time users pay on generated code (the user-unit crate) using levers that are measured to help: trimmed imports and derives, explicit types, lint attributes on the generated crate, and any other macro expansion shown to cost time. Keep a lever only if it reduces user-unit rustc time without changing meaning, runtime or code size. The combined goal is at least 10%.

## Current state
- The primary MIR-to-Rust printer is now `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/{Program,Functions,Operations,Types,Values}.jet`. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs` is the archived reference.
- Interpolation already lowers to `MirOperation.BuildString` with direct `push_str`, so the old `format!` finding is not a live opportunity.
- One observed candidate: every String literal prints as `"..".to_string()` (`Emit/Types.jet:1344,1389`). Shared with #2865.
- Nothing is measured yet. The matched Cargo build benchmark is #2530 (ready).
- The rustc argument path is `Source/main.rs` `rustc_args_for_target` plus `Source/CmdCompile.rs`.

## Changes
1. After #2530, and on the phase-1 unit baseline (#2519) if it has landed, profile the generated Rust with `-Z time-passes` or `-Z self-profile`. Separate Jet emission, rustc parse/typeck/LLVM, runtime/Core compilation and link time.
2. Change one lever at a time in the Jet printer. Change MIR lowering in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen` only where an operation shape has to change. A lint-cost lever (for example `#![cap_lints]` on generated crates, passed through the host rustc args) must never hide user diagnostics or a backend rejection.
3. Mirror each kept lever in MIRRust.rs only as far as the shipped binary needs to prove it.
4. For every lever, log to the card: before/after user-crate rustc wall time on the corpus, source/toolchain/target/profile identity, emitted item and byte counts, and a keep/drop decision.
5. Do not add tests that pin emitted strings.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_default_parity` passes after every kept lever.
- The matched Cargo build benchmark delivered by #2530 (it has no command yet), run on the corpus with the lever off and then on, shows a corpus median user-crate rustc time at least 10% below the phase-1 baseline, recorded in the perf report.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: no new JetCodegen errors.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: the levers live in the Jet printer. Each is proven by a timed measurement after the build.

## Dependencies
- #2530 (matched build benchmark).
- The baseline is best taken after #2519.

cards.title: Jetpack package jet build ICEs: generated Rust fails rustc with E0308 x33, E0382 x9, E0507 x7
cards.body:
ACTUAL (2026-09-01, commit 8b9933668, target/debug/jet): copy dogfood/jetpack to a scratch dir and run `jet build` from the copy root (package.jet selects src/cli/main.jet). After five lint warnings the build exits 101: `internal compiler error: the generated Rust did not compile.` Re-running rustc on the preserved build/main.rs yields 49 errors: E0308 x33 (mismatched nominal module types between manifest and ref ParseError; generated lines 89544, 89971-90231), E0382 x9 (DataTree value used after move, line 83698), E0507 x7 (move out of optional String, lines 95331-95342). Same in --verbose and plain modes. Card #2350 fixed a different exit-101 cause at 77df06cc6. Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-luna/abo/JetpackIce.md and the preserved generated file ~/.cache/jet-luna/abo/jetpack-ice-main.rs (session evidence; re-derive by copying dogfood/jetpack and building).

EXPECTED: jet build of the Jetpack package succeeds on every tier (AOT release, AOT debug, jet run, --interpret) with identical behavior; each of the three error classes is a sema or codegen defect fixed at its mechanism (nominal type identity across modules for error types; move analysis for reused values; optional String access), with a minimal example and golden per class added under examples/ or tests/.

Writable paths: crates/jet-sema/**, crates/jet-codegen/**, tests/**, examples/** for the minimal repros. Never edit dogfood/jetpack.

Invariants: I2 (rustc rejection is a compiler bug), I3 (fix in sema, never by rustc probing), I5, I9.
cards.plan: 1. Reduce each error class to a minimal Jet program from the source-map comments in the generated file. 2. Fix the mechanism in sema/codegen per class. 3. Add examples with goldens and run them on every tier. 4. Build the Jetpack copy on all tiers as the closing proof.

cards.title: jet build receipts never replay: identical invocations produce different receipt contexts
cards.body:
ACTUAL (2026-09-01, commit 8b9933668): two consecutive `jet build examples/features/time/datetime_accuracy_civil_arithmetic.jet` runs with an unchanged copied jet binary (SHA-256 cf196767d893f28a24de80dd76b4b97e7790b2ad421bc7a066fd9d244eb41065), receipts enabled, JET_RECEIPT_DIR under scratch, produced two receipt context files (35cbc60e1bb776ba65654466f9fdb95bcbdded466a8518e1a2c5dd94ce496bc1 and 086a403636c54f99d50d65d5b51f7e4969d2d6290a03e7bbff749cdfff94543f); the second run did not print `ok: build current (receipt ...)` and rebuilt (68.8 s). The receipt claim hashes verb, cwd, argv, the full environment, tool identities, terminal mode, and input digests (Source/ReceiptStore.rs:88-125, :1054-1166); something in that set differs between identical runs. Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-luna/abo/CargoPeer.md.

EXPECTED: an identical invocation replays. Find the varying claim component (diff the two context objects), remove it from the key or canonicalize it, and add a test that two sequential builds with identical inputs share one receipt context. This mechanism is replaced by the store's Receipt node (card 'checks'); the test written here carries over so the replacement cannot regress.

Writable paths: Source/ReceiptStore.rs, tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs or tests/build_entry.rs.

Invariants: replay only on byte-identical closure; I4 replayed diagnostics identical.
cards.plan:
Actual: two consecutive `jet build examples/features/time/datetime_accuracy_civil_arithmetic.jet` runs with the same binary, receipts enabled, and JET_RECEIPT_DIR under scratch produce two receipt context files; the second run rebuilds (68.8 s) instead of printing `ok: build current (receipt ...)`. The claim hashes verb, cwd, argv, the full environment, tool identities, terminal mode, and input digests (Source/ReceiptStore.rs:88-125 and :1054-1166); one component differs between identical runs. Expected: an identical invocation replays; two sequential builds with identical inputs share one context digest and the second prints the replay line and does no backend or link work.

Steps:
1. Reproduce: `export JET_RECEIPT_DIR=$HOME/.cache/jet-test-scratch/receipt-probe JET_STORE_DIR=$HOME/.cache/jet-test-scratch/receipt-store; rm -rf $JET_RECEIPT_DIR; scripts/agent/jet-env jet build <file>` twice; list `$JET_RECEIPT_DIR/contexts/`.
2. Dump both context objects (they are JSON; the store writes them under contexts/<sha>) and diff them. Record the differing component in the card log (expected candidates: a per-process environment variable such as a temp dir, a PID-derived value, a terminal-mode probe, or a timestamp in tool identity).
3. Fix the key in ReceiptStore.rs: remove the component from the claim when it cannot affect the output, or canonicalize it (for example, the environment is filtered to the variables the build reads, per the D-BUILD-NOCHANGE1 contract); never widen replay to a non-identical closure.
4. Test: tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs `second_identical_build_replays_receipt` (add it if absent, or in tests/build_entry.rs): two sequential builds share one context digest; the second prints `ok: build current (receipt <first12>)` and no rustc or link process runs (assert through the receipt's recorded work or a wall-time bound). This test carries over when the store's Receipt node replaces the mechanism.

Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cli_compiler_speed -- second_identical_build_replays_receipt` green; the manual reproduction now lists one context file.

Writable paths: Source/ReceiptStore.rs, tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs or tests/build_entry.rs. Do not touch crates/jet-store beyond reading its key contract.

I9: replayed diagnostics are identical to a fresh build (I4); replay only on a byte-identical closure.

Non-goals: no change to what a receipt records beyond the varying component; no store redesign.

log.text: Closed after integrated focused proof. Receipt replay now survives volatile shell temp-root changes without hiding semantic environment changes.
Prep: plan refreshed with the reproduction commands, the context diff step, the canonicalization rule, and the carry-over test. A live lane (Bug2536) is implementing.

criteria.text: The log records the exact claim component that differed between the two contexts and the fix applied.
criteria.evidence: Root cause: ReceiptStore::environment_identity_from hashed volatile per-shell Nix and temp variables (NIX_BUILD_TOP, TEMP, TEMPDIR, TMP, TMPDIR) plus JET_RECEIPT_BYPASS, so identical builds produced different context digests. The fix excludes only those non-semantic harness/temp variables while preserving the rest of the environment identity.

criteria.text: tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs::second_identical_build_replays_receipt passes: second build prints `ok: build current (receipt <first12>)` and performs no backend or link work.
criteria.evidence: Focused integrated proof: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet --test cli_compiler_speed second_identical_build_replays_receipt -- --nocapture; 1 passed. The test proves one context pointer, replay line with the first receipt prefix, unchanged rustc log, unchanged binary bytes and mtime.

cards.title: jet-store: a second live jet process fails with E2105 instead of waiting for the store lock
cards.body: After the #2516 cutover every jet invocation shares one machine-wide store. When two jet processes overlap (proof-w3 on 2026-09-02 ran three test suites in parallel), the second one fails its build with `Error [E2105]: couldn't store build cache artifact: store lock is owned by a live process: ~/.cache/jet/store/locks/store.lock` (seen in tir_control_and_data `comprehension_forms_example_matches_all_execution_tiers` and golden release runs). A machine-wide store must treat lock contention as the normal case: the second process waits (bounded, with a clear diagnostic only after the wait expires), it never fails on first contact. Publishing is already atomic; only the acquisition policy is wrong.
cards.plan: In crates/jet-store/src/lib.rs make lock acquisition wait with backoff up to a bounded deadline (config field with a sane default, honoring the existing lease/liveness check so a dead owner is reclaimed immediately); keep E2105 only for a genuinely stuck lock past the deadline and name the owner pid and the wait in the diagnostic. Add a jet-store test that runs two writers concurrently and proves both publish. Add a build_entry integration test that runs two `jet build` processes against one JET_STORE_DIR concurrently and asserts both succeed.

cards.title: Lambda capture analysis misses a `&` write-lend argument and reports E0121 on the captured binding
cards.body: Actual (2026-09-02, tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs `try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable`, fixture tir_try_sort_by.jet): `seen := 0` then `items.sort_by((n) -> stopping_sort_key(n, &seen))` followed by `print(seen)` at line 20 fails with `Error [E0121]: seen was consumed by the earlier consuming operation, so it can't be used here`. The lambda body lends `seen` for writing through the `&` call-site marker (D-MEM1 bare=read, `&`=write, `^`=take), which is a borrow, not a move; the capture collector classifies the capture as a consuming take. Direct `stopping_sort_key(n, &seen)` outside a lambda is accepted. Expected: a `&` argument inside a lambda body captures the binding by write lend; the binding remains usable after the call; output 31 on every tier.
cards.plan:
Actual: tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs `try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable` (fixture tir_try_sort_by.jet) fails with `Error [E0121]: seen was consumed by the earlier consuming operation, so it can't be used here` at the `print(seen)` after `items.sort_by((n) -> stopping_sort_key(n, &seen))`. The lambda body lends `seen` for writing through the `&` call-site marker (D-MEM1: bare read, `&` write lend, `^` take), which is a borrow, but the capture collector (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Captures.rs, consumed by CheckerOwnership.rs:4085 where E0121 is emitted) classifies the capture as a consuming take. The same call outside a lambda is accepted. Expected: a `&` argument inside a lambda body captures the binding by write lend; the binding stays usable after the call; output 31 on every tier; a true `^seen` capture followed by a later use still reports E0121.

Steps:
1. Reproduce: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_core_and_closures -- try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable`.
2. In Captures.rs, classify each captured use by the call-site marker of the use inside the body (`&` write lend, `^` take, bare read) instead of defaulting a captured write to take; keep D-CONC-FREEZE1 `^`-capture semantics unchanged; CheckerOwnership then sees a lend, not a move.
3. Regression: tests/ui/E0121_take_capture_in_lambda.jet (`^seen` inside a lambda, then a use) with a blessed snapshot proving the true take still reports E0121 with the registered text.
4. Spec: if the D-MEM1 row in docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md is silent on markers inside lambda bodies, add one sentence: a call-site marker inside a lambda body has the same meaning as outside; the capture takes the strongest marker used.

Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_core_and_closures -- try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable` green with output 31 on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` green with the new snapshot; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test sema_soundness_invalid --test single_use` unchanged.

Writable paths: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Captures.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs (only if the classification is read there), tests/ui/, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md. Do not touch codegen or the JIT (the fix is in sema, so every tier sees one verdict), crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: the fixture runs on all three tiers with byte-identical output.

Non-goals: no change to the `^` take-capture law or to E0121's text.

log.text: Closed after integrated three-tier closure test, retained E0121 take-capture snapshot, and explicit D-MEM1 lambda-marker law.
Prep: plan refreshed with the capture collector home (Sema/Captures.rs), the take-capture snapshot, and the D-MEM1 spec sentence. A live lane (Bug2758) is implementing.

cards.title: Native build ICE: HTTP handler closure captures a non-Send Cell (web server packages cannot build)
cards.body:
Root cause: A non-Send Cell capture is emitted into the Send+Sync HTTP handler closure.
Kind: rustc-rejected. Tiers: check pass; run pass; run --release fail; build fail.
Repro: ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects/web/pkg/minimal.jet
Command: JET_FFI_CACHE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects/web/ffi JET_STORE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects/web/store ~/Projects/Github/jet/scripts/agent/jet-env jet build --verbose pkg/minimal.jet
Observed: error[E0277]: `Rc<JetCellInner<i64>>` cannot be sent between threads safely      --> build/minimal.rs:81903:6 ... required for the cast from `Arc<{closure...}>` to `Arc<dyn Fn(JetHTTPRequest) -> Result<..., ...> + Send + Sync>`
Location: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/lambdas.rs:1188-1193; HTTP closure generated handler
Found by probes: area-web-G1. Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/defects.json (DEF-1).
cards.plan:
## Authority and ownership

D-LOCALCELL1=A and D-CONC-CROSS1=A are ratified. `Cell<T>` remains thread-confined and is never auto-promoted. Sema owns the common crossing rejection; HTTP lowering owns only valid `Shared<T>`/sendable closures and must never emit rustc-rejected captures. Endpoint-contract repair is a separate owner and is out of scope.

## Work

1. Reproduce the area-web-G1/minimal fixture and inspect the generated path, then trace the common `SendCrossing::HttpHandler` check from `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs` through `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/lambdas.rs`.
2. Ensure a handler capturing `Cell` is rejected in sema before TIR/Rust emission with registered E1102 and a UI snapshot; remove or avoid any late HTTP-only promotion or duplicate checker. Keep `tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.jet` and `http_route_unsendable_capture.jet` as the invalid probes.
3. Keep an explicit `Shared<T>` capture legal on the same HTTP handler path. Trace `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/lambdas.rs` and only direct HTTP route callers; do not change Cell semantics or absorb the endpoint-contract card.
4. Exercise invalid Cell and legal Shared cases on check/default run/`--release`/`jet build`; preserve exact output/error and rule out rustc E0277 or ICE. Update the registered diagnostic and UI golden only if the canonical wording changes.

## Proof

Run the focused UI and area-web-G1 probes plus default, release, and build smoke paths for the legal Shared handler. Assert canonical E1102 before generated-Rust failure for Cell and expected response for Shared; no HTTP-only auto-promotion, duplicate crossing rule, rustc E0277, or ICE.

## Scope

Do not invent D-WEB-SEND1, add an HTTP-specific sendability mechanism, or repair the separate endpoint contract.

The first legal Shared-handler proof stops in default JIT with ICE: checked TIR cannot lower to MIR at 853..856, missing checked function target route_error (tests/http_i9.rs:22). Current live work exposed that the old auto-promotion acceptance contradicts ratified Cell and common-crossing law; align the plan and two open criteria with the required sema rejection plus explicit Shared success. Acceptance conflict identified before any Cell lowering change: D-LOCALCELL1=A makes Cell and its guards thread-confined (docs/spec/spec.md:685-711; Prelude/LocalCell.rs:1-3). D-CONC-CROSS1=A applies the existing common sendability check to HTTP handlers (CheckerOwnership.rs:4858-4872; CheckerInfer/calls/lambdas.rs:343-357). tests/ui/local_cell_crossing.jet:22-27 already covers this exact invalid capture. A Cell holds changeable data for one thread. HTTP handlers can run on other threads, so Jet must reject a captured Cell before it builds the program. I removed the code that silently changed Cell into Shared. Next I am checking both paths: Cell should get a clear error; an explicitly written Shared value should work. This follows your existing D-LOCALCELL1 decision.

cards.body:
Root cause: Non-fallible user functions are represented as Result at the module boundary while callers still apply `?`, producing a Rust carrier mismatch.
Kind: rustc-rejected. Tiers: check pass; run pass (control); run --release fail; build fail.
Repro: ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects/storage/pkg/import_bool.jet

Observed: error[E0308]: mismatched types      --> build/import_bool.rs:23220:68 ... this expression has type `bool` ... expected type `bool` ... found enum `Result<_, _>`

Found by probes: prim-storage-G2, prim-dsl-G7. Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/defects.json (DEF-2).

1. Preserve one carrier decision from the checked callee signature through TIR lowering and MIR emission. The caller must consume that fact; it must not infer a Result carrier from syntax or re-decide the ABI.

Location: generated call build/set_ice.rs:79873; compute set lowering source not isolated

cards.plan:
## Authority and semantic resolution

D-BIND1 is ratified at `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:20-22`: `::` binds an immutable local and `:=` binds a mutable local. The historical ICE report must therefore close as an invalid-source diagnostic, not by making an immutable binding mutable. Current evidence records sema E0111 for the immutable fixture and the `::`→`:=` companion producing `[0.0, 3.0, 0.0, 0.0]`; preparation does not rerun that evidence.

## Owned paths

cards.title: Tensor elementwise map allocates per element: 256x256 takes 62 s in release, 512x512 never finishes
cards.body:
Root cause: CPU tensor binary mapping allocates fresh coordinate vectors and performs coordinate-based raw lookups for every output element, making a 2-D map scale far worse than the element count alone.
Kind: slow. Tiers: run --release: 256^2 completes; 512^2 exceeds 300s; prior 4096^2 run also exceeded 300s.
Repro: ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/arrays/map_256.jet
Command: scripts/agent/jet-env bash -c 'cd ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/arrays && time -p timeout 300 env JET_STORE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/arrays/store JET_FFI_CACHE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/arrays/ffi ~/Projects/Github/jet/target/debug/jet run --release map_256.jet --watch=off'
Observed: 256x256 output: shape:[256, 256] numel:65536 corner:3.0; real 62.43 user 92.49 sys 2.24. 512x512: timeout after real 300.03 (exit 124). Built-binary check: 256x256 real 41.63 user 43.60 sys 2.03; 512x512 timeout after real 300.01 user 505.79 sys 29.75.
Location: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Compute.rs:7223-7261
Found by probes: prim-arrays-G7. Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/defects.json (DEF-17).
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Close the tensor elementwise-map repair with fresh evidence:
- the 256² and 512² repros terminate;
- results stay identical on every tier;
- the canonical `tensor-map-4k` paired gauntlet cell meets the strict gate (Jet/Rust ≤ 1.05, Jet/every other peer < 1.00).

**History**
The old path allocated coordinate vectors and did raw lookups per element (DEF-17, probe prim-arrays-G7). 256² took 62 s in release, and 512² and 4096² exceeded 300 s.

**Current state**
- The repair is in HEAD. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Compute.rs:7597` `jet_compute_binary_contiguous` computes layout once and walks contiguous slices; `jet_compute_binary` (`:7697`) is the canonical fallback.
- The repros exist at `~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/arrays/map_{256,512,1024,2048}.jet`.
- The gauntlet entry is `Tools/gauntlet/entries/tensor-map-4k/` (jet, rust, python, c, zig, node; cell `numerics.tensor-map`).
- Goldens: `Examples/features/tooling/compute_tensor.jet` and `compute_ndarray.jet`, with `.out` files under `Examples/features/expected/tooling/`.

**Changes**
None planned. If the fresh run shows a remaining hot path (for example, validation repeated per scalar read), fix it in `Compute.rs` without a workload-specific fast path. Keep checked offsets, bounds, broadcast stride zeroing, f32 behavior, and chunk order.

**Proof** (fresh release binary)
- `cd ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/arrays && Tools/agent/jet-env bash -c 'timeout 300 target/release/jet run --release map_256.jet --watch=off'`, and the same for `map_512.jet`: both exit 0 well under the cap, printing `shape:[256, 256] numel:65536 corner:3.0` and the 512² equivalent.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_tensor cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_ndarray cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` pass. These cover default run, `--release`, and build.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry tensor-map-4k --jet-bin target/release/jet` reports Jet/Rust ≤ 1.05 and Jet/{python,c,zig,node} < 1.00 for every required metric. Record the ratios on the card and keep any loss open.

**Batch**
`batch-measure`: the code is landed, and only evidence runs remain.

**Dependencies**
None.

Overnight proof 2026-09-29: FAIL. FAIL on criterion 1 (performance gate): same host, same staged entry, outputs all == expected.out: Jet release AOT median 33 926 ms vs Rust (`Tools/agent/jet-env rustc --edition=2021 -O main.rs`) median 49.2 ms (5 runs) -> Jet/Rust ~= 690x (gate <= 1.05); Node (`node main.mjs`) median 211.9 ms -> Jet/Node ~= 160x (gate < 1.00). C and Zig peers not measured (gcc/zig not on PATH outside jet-env; not attempted). The gauntlet harness (`node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry tensor-map-4k`) was not run: it requires a release jet binary (target/release/jet), while only the debug snapshot is available to workers; the numbers above are a manual same-host replay of the entry's programs, not a harness receipt. Criterion 2 (goldens on default run / --release / build) not fully exercised: only the release-run and AOT outputs above were observed (all identical to the recorded outputs); no checked-in golden exists for the map_* repros. Phase 0 triage 2026-09-28 (toolwebmem1b, Opus 5.5): F_PROOF. The per-element allocation root is fixed in the Prelude compute kernel: layout is computed once and contiguous slices are used. What remains is the fresh-binary repro run and the tensor-map-4k paired gauntlet cell. Fresh workload and peer timing proof is unverified, but source evidence is sufficient to reject the original defect as still present. Fresh bounded build astra-wave-build3.json passes. 4K resident tensor-map workload now exits 0 with exact shape/checksum in 27,547 ms; prior run exceeded 240 s. Receipt ~/.cache/jet-luna/astra-wave-tensor-map-4k-default.json. Main moved full validation to public get/set boundaries; internal kernels already validate immutable inputs once. Bounds/overflow checks remain in scalar addressing. cards.title: Checker is superlinear on a bounded loop that pushes generic values: 10,000 iterations never finish checking
cards.body:
Root cause: Checking a statically bounded loop that pushes generic Embedding values grows superlinearly with the bound, making a 10,000-entry index exceed a one-minute check budget.
Kind: slow. Tiers: check: 1250 completes in 4.91s; 2500 in 20.66s; 5000 and 10000 exceed 60s.
Repro: ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/ai/embedding_10000.jet

cards.title: core.compute.fft is a naive O(n^2) DFT: 476 ms at N=4096 where a radix-2 library kernel takes 105 us
cards.body:
Root cause: core.compute.fft is implemented as a naive nested discrete Fourier transform, so doubling input length costs about four times rather than O(n log n).
Kind: slow. Tiers: run --release passes at 1024, 2048, and 4096; measured transform time scales approximately 3.8x then 4.1x per doubling.
Repro: ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/fft/compute_fft_4096.jet
Command: scripts/agent/jet-env bash -c 'cd ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/fft && time -p timeout 120 env JET_STORE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/fft/store JET_FFI_CACHE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/fft/ffi ~/Projects/Github/jet/target/debug/jet run --release compute_fft_4096.jet --watch=off'
Observed: Timing table (program ns): n=1024 30853298; n=2048 116669574; n=4096 476150738. All runs printed first:1.0 and completed.
Location: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Compute.rs:7603-7646
Found by probes: prim-numerics-perf-G2. Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/defects.json (DEF-19).
cards.plan:
## Current state and scope

This card remains the owner of the core.compute.fft performance loss. The 2026-09-08 log says the tree now contains radix-2 and Bluestein paths with a focused prime/composite regression; no timing or tier proof is claimed. Do not rename the old quadratic path, special-case the benchmark, or replace a current implementation without measuring the real production entry point.

## Owned paths

Own the FFT implementation in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Compute.rs and focused proof in tests/compute_extended.rs and tests/compute_parity.rs. Keep the rank-1 real tensor contract, CPU placement/error policy, empty input behavior, precision profiles, and all existing Core callers. Do not add a public syntax or a parallel numerical API.

## Ordered work

1. Trace `jet_compute_fft` and its f32/f64 dispatch from the current source, then map the radix-2 power-of-two path and Bluestein non-power-of-two path to the existing tensor storage and result conversion.
2. Exercise empty, singleton, power-of-two, prime, and composite lengths against an independent small-size DFT oracle and the existing expected values. Check finite results, output shape, precision policy, and error behavior.
3. Prove AOT release, default `jet run`, and `jet build` preserve the same spectrum and first-result output. Include the focused prime/composite regression; add other tiers only where the Core contract already applies.
4. Measure N=1024, 2048, and 4096 with length, precision, tier, warmup, samples, transfer policy, and exact-result identity recorded. Retain the existing target of N=4096 under 200 us only with matched production evidence; an external library number is not a Jet result.
5. Record the command and numbers in the card log. Keep timing closure separate from semantic/tier proof and do not claim a win from source inspection alone.

## Exit

Both existing criteria remain open until the real repro meets the target and all applicable tiers retain one meaning. Any numerical or performance loss stays open or is re-carded; it is not hidden by renaming the algorithm.

cards.title: Default evaluator E0956: core.log.set_trace_id has no arm when a service-state call forces interpretation
cards.body:
Root cause: The default TIR evaluator has no core.log.set_trace_id arm when a service-state call forces interpretation, although the native release backend accepts the same five-line program.
Kind: diagnostic. Tiers: default run fails E0956; run --release passes with no output; --interpret reports E2201 on the same unsupported evaluator path.
Repro: ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/backend/fallback.jet
Command: scripts/agent/jet-env bash -c 'cd ~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/backend && env JET_STORE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/backend/store11 JET_FFI_CACHE_DIR=~/.cache/jet-luna/dx3/_defects2/backend/ffi11 ~/Projects/Github/jet/target/debug/jet run fallback.jet --watch=off'
Observed: Error [E0956]: ``core.log.set_trace_id()`` isn't supported by the current evaluator yet   --> fallback.jet:4:14  Why: The canonical TIR evaluator doesn't cover this construct yet  Fix: Use a simpler form, or use `jet build` for the full evaluator
Location: crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/core_calls.rs:2666-2673; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/RingCsvLogTimeCrypto.rs:113-115

## Current state
- Fixed in tree (triage A_DONE): crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/core_calls/plain_calls.rs:263-266 and impure.rs:436-439 handle core.log.set_trace_id. The self-hosted registry routes it through the Ambient interpreter route (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1027, CoreValueSignatures.jet:1038-1039). Core/log/log.jet:105-107.
- Criteria 1-2 are met. Criterion 3 (probe area-backend-G5) is HTTP Connection: close / pooled keep-alive work. 728ee658d (2026-09-21) narrowed Connection token handling; the bounded area-backend load proof was never run.
- The original repro command used scripts/agent/jet-env; the current path is Tools/agent/jet-env.

## Changes
No code change. Evidence only:
1. Run the repro on all three tiers from a clean project directory (not a sibling of other scratch dirs; the frozen-binary attempt hit an unrelated E1334 authority-symlink check).
2. Pip moves criterion 3 to #3225 (HTTP client and shared-body lifecycle) if its scope covers server keep-alive, or to a new HTTP keep-alive card. Then close this card.

None.

cards.title: Signals and request deadlines as cancellation; closable child stdin
cards.body:
Probes area-backend (G3, G4), area-cli (G1): no typed signal subscription (E1004 core.process.signal), no request-scoped deadline middleware (E1004 core.http.server.timeout), and ProcessStdin has no close so a producer feeding an arbitrary child times out (E0102, 60 s). Law: cancellation is preemptive at wait points (D-CANCELMODEL1), #Context deadlines emit E3003 (D-DEADLINE1), on_interrupt is Ctrl-C only (D-OSFACTS1), graceful HTTP shutdown is shipped. Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/all-gaps.json.

Gate: D-FOUND-LIFECYCLE1. The card starts when the owner ratifies the ballot; no code before that.

cards.title: Operators between different types: typed right side and result on the existing hooks (amends D-OPDEF1)
cards.body:
Probe prim-units (G3): an operator implementation with a different right-hand type is refused (E0907 `div` doesn't match `Div`; E0360 no `/` for Meter), so every mixed operation becomes a named helper at every call site. D-OPDEF1 fixes same-operand-type hooks; this ballot amends it. Units already mix through #UnitFamily; vectors, matrices, money-times-rate, and durations-times-counts do not. Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/all-gaps.json.

Gate: D-FOUND-OPMIX1. The card starts when the owner ratifies the ballot; no code before that.

cards.title: Literals for library types: a literal capability on the existing context rule
cards.body:
Probe prim-exact-numerics (G4): a plain literal does not reach a library type (E0112 accept wants Rational but literal 1 is Int) and a suffix is refused (E0134 `rat`), so Rational and scaled Decimal values need a constructor at every call. Law: context selects a literal's type (D-LITCARRIER1); user-defined prefixes are deferred (D-UNIFYLIT1). Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/all-gaps.json.

Gate: D-FOUND-LITERAL1. The card starts when the owner ratifies the ballot; no code before that.
cards.plan: After ratification: a type adopts Literal.Int or Literal.Float through a compile-time constructor (@fn from_literal); the Float form receives the literal digits as text so exact types stay exact; the existing context rule picks the target; no new syntax; diagnostics for a lossy or out-of-range literal with snapshots; example with goldens on every tier. blockedBy: none (the ballot on this card is the gate).
